faqs.question: How much does IB math IA help cost in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Published UAE rates run from AED 33 to 65 an hour at the budget online tier, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 200 to 450 and above for IB specialists, and AED 650 for one provider's named premium tutor. Those are the providers' own figures, read in October 2026. The more useful number is the total: most exploration work is three to five sessions, so even at specialist rates it is closer to one month of tutoring than a term. We quote after a free trial lesson, once we have seen the state of the draft.

faqs.question: How many marks is the IB mathematical exploration worth?
faqs.answer: Twenty marks, which convert to twenty per cent of the final Mathematics grade at both Standard and Higher Level, on Analysis and Approaches and on Applications and Interpretation alike. The twenty marks are split across five criteria: presentation worth four, mathematical communication worth four, personal engagement worth three, reflection worth three, and use of mathematics worth six. The school marks the work and the IB moderates it externally. That split is worth knowing before writing, because fourteen of the twenty marks are not awarded for the mathematics itself.

faqs.question: Which exploration criterion do students lose most marks on?
faqs.answer: Reflection and mathematical communication, in our experience of drafts from this emirate, not use of mathematics. Reflection is worth three marks and is lost when a student narrates the process instead of evaluating the result, its limitations and what they would change. Communication is worth four and is lost to undefined variables, calculator syntax in prose and unlabelled graphs. Both are retrievable in an evening of careful rewriting, which is why a marking session on a mathematically sound draft is usually the best value hour in the task.

faqs.question: How long should the maths exploration be?
faqs.answer: Twelve to twenty pages is the recommended length, and it is a recommendation rather than a target. Drafts that run well beyond it tend to score lower, because the extra pages usually repeat mathematics rather than deepen it and presentation suffers under the weight. We regularly advise students to cut a twenty-six page draft back, which is a hard instruction to accept after weeks of work and almost always raises the mark. Check your own school's submission guidance too, since schools differ on how appendices and references are counted.

faqs.question: Can a tutor write or correct my child's exploration for them?
faqs.answer: No. The exploration must be the student's own work, and the IB treats a breach as malpractice affecting the whole Diploma rather than one subject. A tutor may teach the mathematics, test a topic, mark a draft criterion by criterion, point out that a paragraph narrates instead of reflecting, and demonstrate notation on an example the student is not using. A tutor may not supply text, run the student's calculations for them or choose the topic. Any provider offering a finished internal assessment is selling your child a risk to the award.

faqs.question: Is an HL exploration judged differently from an SL one?
faqs.answer: Yes, on criterion E. The criterion asks for mathematics commensurate with the level of the course, so an HL exploration needs to use HL content from the student's own route and use it to do real work. A technically flawless piece built on material met two years earlier cannot reach the top of a six-mark criterion at HL. At SL the equivalent test is whether the mathematics goes beyond a single procedure applied repeatedly. Everything else, including the other fourteen marks, is assessed the same way at both levels.

faqs.question: What makes a good exploration topic for a student in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: One where the student generates their own data, the mathematics sits at their course level, and the result could have come out differently. Local options are unusually strong: a trigonometric model of prayer-time variation across the year, an exponential fit to published district population figures, a route optimisation built from the student's own timed journeys between Khalifa City and the island, or queue modelling from their own counts at a Corniche attraction. Each gives personal engagement evidence that a borrowed data set cannot, and each has a context the student can describe first-hand.

faqs.question: My child's exploration mark came back at fourteen out of twenty. Is that fixable?
faqs.answer: Usually, and usually by two or three marks rather than six. Fourteen is a competent draft sitting below its ceiling, and in most cases the shortfall is in reflection and communication rather than in the mathematics. The diagnostic is quick: does the reflection evaluate or narrate, are all variables defined once and used consistently, is the aim stated in the opening paragraph, is every data source cited. Fixing those is a rewriting job the student can do in a few evenings with one marking session to confirm the direction.

faqs.question: Are sessions online, or does a tutor come to our home in Al Raha?
faqs.answer: Online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For exploration work the online format is the stronger one, because the document, the graphing output, the data spreadsheet and the criteria all need to be on screen together. A family in Al Raha also gets a tutor matched to their child's route and level rather than whoever covers maths within a reasonable evening drive, and pays no travel premium for the hour.

faqs.question: When should a DP student in Abu Dhabi start the exploration?
faqs.answer: Topic tested eight to ten weeks before the school's final deadline, with data collected around six weeks out and a full first draft four weeks out so a teacher's mark is still actionable. Schools in the emirate set their own internal dates but work back from the May session, which puts the exploration late in DP1 or early in DP2. Students who leave it later collide with paper revision, which is exactly what the school's scheduling was designed to avoid. The topic session is the cheapest intervention and the one most often skipped.

faqs.question: Does the exploration have to use data the student collected themselves?
faqs.answer: It does not have to, but original data makes criterion C substantially easier to evidence, because the decisions the student made are visible in the work. A published data set can produce a strong exploration if the student does something genuinely their own with it: cleaning it, questioning its collection method, comparing two sources that disagree. What scores poorly is a downloaded set run through a standard test with no commentary on where it came from. Either way, the source must be cited, including the software used to analyse it.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both the exploration and paper technique?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for many students that is the sensible arrangement, because the exploration is twenty per cent of the grade and the papers are the other eighty. A weekly slot can carry course content and past-paper technique with exploration work folded in at the topic, first-draft and post-marking points. It costs more in total than a short exploration block and buys more. If the papers are fine and only the exploration is weak, a short block is the better purchase and we will say so.

faqs.question: What if my child's topic was approved at a previous school?
faqs.answer: Raise it in the first session, because approval does not travel automatically. Abu Dhabi sees a steady flow of mid-year arrivals, and a topic signed off by one teacher may not suit another school's expectations or may duplicate work already being done in that class. The practical move is to write a one-paragraph proposal stating the aim, the data source and the mathematics involved, and take it to the new teacher before any further writing. Finding a mismatch in week one costs a session; finding it in the marked draft costs the draft.

faqs.question: How do exploration sessions work during Ramadan in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: They move later rather than stopping. School days shorten, households reorganise around iftar and the usual 5pm slot becomes unworkable, so we schedule post-iftar sessions instead. Keeping the cadence matters more in this task than in most, because the Ramadan weeks often sit directly on top of the exploration drafting window. For a student who is fasting, two shorter sessions a week usually work better than one long one, and draft marking between sessions carries the work forward without needing live time.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist on my child's route is available?
faqs.answer: We tell you rather than matching your child with a general maths tutor and hoping. Route and level matter here: an Applications and Interpretation HL exploration and an Analysis and Approaches SL one have different criterion E thresholds and different typical topics. If no suitable tutor is free in your window, the options are a later start with written draft feedback in the meantime, a tutor on a compatible evening schedule outside the emirate, or using the school's own clinic hours. A clear no is more useful to you than a poor match.

abu-dhabi/ib-math-ia-help.closingHeading: Price the task, not the hour
abu-dhabi/ib-math-ia-help.closingBody: The useful question is not what an hour costs in Abu Dhabi but how many hours your child's exploration actually needs, and that depends on whether there is a topic, a draft, and a teacher's comment naming a criterion. Send us those three facts and the school's deadline, and we will tell you the number of sessions before you pay for any of them. The first lesson is free and is spent on the real document, so you will know within an hour whether the shortfall is mathematics or writing, and roughly what it will take to close.

intro.heading: When budget is not the constraint, the constraint is information
paragraphs: Al Bandar is a waterfront community inside the Al Raha Beach development, close to several of the emirate's better-known Diploma schools, and families here are usually weighing quality rather than affordability. That sounds like an easier problem than it is. The published rates in this market span a factor of twenty, from AED 33 an hour at the budget end to AED 650 at the top, and almost nothing in the public record explains what separates them. In the absence of information, price becomes a proxy for quality, which is precisely the condition under which a market overcharges.

Here are the bands with their sources, because this page would be worthless without them. Budget online tutoring is advertised from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor working online runs roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200. Specialists are quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate showing AED 200 to 450 plus for exam-year specialists. Premium named or examiner-led provision reaches AED 500 to 650 and beyond, with BartyED publishing AED 650. In-home visits including travel are quoted at AED 180 to 500.

What a higher band reliably buys is narrower than the marketing suggests. It buys mark-scheme fluency: someone who can look at a student's working and say why a correct answer scored two out of four, which is a genuinely different skill from explaining the mathematics. It does not buy access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content, it does not buy an outcome, and it does not make a Standard Level student into a Higher Level one. Those distinctions are worth real money in a household that can afford either option, because the common error here is not underspending. It is spending the premium band on work the mid band does identically.

The second information gap is credentials. In a market where examiner-led is used as a selling phrase, a parent is entitled to ask what can actually be verified. Some claims are checkable in a minute: the MoHRE private tuition work permit, the route and level taught to examination, the component weightings, the Internal Assessment criteria by letter. Others cannot be independently verified by a parent at all, and a provider who presents the second kind as though it were the first is doing something worth noticing. This page sorts them.

One statement of model. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Al Bandar is one of the easier places in the emirate to arrange an in-home tutor, so the case for online here is not logistics: it is that the specialist you want for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level may not live within driving distance, and at the published bands you would be paying a travel premium on top. We publish no rate card. The trial lesson is free with no card required, and a quote follows the diagnosis.

sections.heading: The AED 650 question: auditing the premium band
paragraphs: The top of this market is quoted at AED 500 to 650 an hour and above, with BartyED publishing AED 650, against a mid band of roughly AED 150 to 300 where Unitors lists IB from AED 200. A household that can pay either rate deserves a straight answer about the difference, and the straight answer is that the premium buys one specific capability plus two things that are not capabilities at all.

The capability is mark-scheme forensics. Someone who has marked the paper can look at a student's script and say that the second line lost the method mark, that the final answer was penalised for form rather than value, or that the approach taken to an unfamiliar Paper 3 problem was reasonable but unrewardable. That is a different skill from explaining mathematics clearly, and it is the thing a student stuck between grade bands with secure content actually needs. In the final term of Higher Level, it is worth paying for.

The two things that are not capabilities are scarcity and reputation. A scarce specialism costs more because few people teach it, which is a real cost and not a quality signal. A recognised name costs more because the name is recognised. Neither improves the teaching, and neither buys access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content, which nobody can sell and nobody should imply. The table sets out where each band earns its difference, and the honest conclusion is that for most of a Diploma the mid band and the premium band do the same work.

sections.heading: What changes a grade against what changes the invoice
paragraphs: This is the distinction a well-funded household most needs, because almost everything on sale sounds like it belongs in the first column. The things that reliably change an IB maths grade are unglamorous: visible method, so partial credit is earned when the final answer fails; pacing, so the back of the paper is reached with time to think; non-calculator fluency for Analysis and Approaches; approach strategy for Paper 3 at Higher Level; and an exploration written to the criteria rather than written and then checked against them.

The things that change the invoice without reliably changing the grade are also identifiable. More hours of the same teaching the school already provides. A premium rate applied to Standard Level content coverage. Sessions in the week before papers, which produce calm rather than marks. A second subject bought when the losses in both are caused by the same algebra. And the switch to a new tutor late in Year 2, which starts the relationship over at the worst possible moment.

A household that can afford to ignore price is still better off knowing which column it is buying from, because the two columns compete for the same evenings. A student has a finite number of usable study hours and every hour spent on the second column is unavailable to the first. That, rather than money, is the real constraint in this community, and it is the reason this page argues for fewer, better-aimed hours instead of more.

sections.heading: Which credential claims can a parent actually verify?
paragraphs: In a market that sells examiner-led as a phrase, the honest division is between claims a parent can check and claims they cannot. Checkable in minutes: the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years, with no fee and a stated two-working-day completion time. Also checkable: which route and level the tutor has taught to examination and when, the component weightings, and the exploration criteria by letter with their mark allocations. Those four answers, given quickly and precisely, tell you most of what you need.

Not verifiable by a parent: current examiner status. A provider may describe a tutor as an examiner, and you have no mechanism to confirm it, which is why we do not use the term for anyone whose status we cannot evidence, and why examiner status should never be presented as implying access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content. Nobody has that access to sell. Equally unverifiable are self-published satisfaction percentages, student counts and star ratings; in the pages researched for this project one provider showed two contradictory review totals on a single page and another showed a perfect score from twenty reviews alongside a far larger claim about students taught.

Then there are claims that are checkable and usually false. Regulator approval is a specific thing: in Dubai a tutoring operation with premises and staff requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal; in Abu Dhabi private schools are regulated by ADEK, which supervises their licensing and accreditation. Neither body certifies online tutoring platforms, so ask for a permit number and the issuing body. For the record, IB Gram holds no licence, approval, certification or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International or Pearson, and has no office or centre in the UAE.

sections.heading: The cost of switching tutors mid-Diploma
paragraphs: Families in this belt switch tutors more often than families elsewhere, partly because they have more options and partly because expectations are higher. Switching is sometimes exactly the right decision and it is never free, and the cost is almost entirely about timing rather than about money. A new tutor spends the first two or three sessions learning the student: how they write, what they skip, which gaps are real and which are confidence. In Diploma Year 1 that cost is trivial. In the spring of Year 2 it is most of the remaining runway.

The honest guidance is to make the decision early and then stop making it. If after six sessions the tutor has not produced a specific account of what is costing marks, measured on timed questions, that is a switch worth making immediately. If the complaint is about manner rather than substance, and the student is making measurable progress, switching usually costs more than it returns. The hardest case is the competent tutor who is not quite right: the losses are gradual and invisible, and most families persist through politeness.

We build a review at six sessions into every arrangement precisely to remove the politeness problem, and we change the tutor at our cost when the match is wrong. The table below prices the switch by timing so a family can make the decision with its real cost visible rather than guessing. The one pattern to avoid entirely is switching twice in Year 2, which consumes the remaining weeks in two separate learning curves and tends to leave a student worse prepared than either tutor would have left them.

sections.heading: What the extra level costs: Higher against Standard
paragraphs: Parents in this community frequently ask whether to push for Higher Level, and the question has a support cost attached that rarely enters the conversation. Standard Level in Analysis and Approaches is two papers at forty per cent each, one of them without a calculator, with the exploration at twenty. Higher Level is three papers at thirty, thirty and twenty per cent, with the exploration again at twenty. Applications and Interpretation follows the same shape, with a calculator permitted throughout at Standard Level.

The extra paper is not simply more of the same. Paper 3 rewards sustained work on an unfamiliar problem, which cannot be drilled from a topic list and has to be built over months. That means a Higher Level student needs support spread across two years rather than concentrated before the papers, and it means the final-term work is forensic rather than instructional. Both of those push the cost up, and the second is the one place where the premium band genuinely earns its rate.

The decision should rest on evidence rather than ambition. A student whose algebraic fluency is secure and who enjoys unfamiliar problems belongs at Higher Level and will be fine. A student who is capable but needs structure and worked examples may well score better at Standard Level and arrive at university with a stronger transcript. A 4 at Higher Level is worth less to almost every application than a 6 at Standard Level, and no amount of expensive support changes the arithmetic of that. Check what the specific university programmes your child is aiming at publish, in the year they will apply, rather than inheriting a view about prestige.

sections.heading: The twenty marks that go cheap early and expensive late
paragraphs: The exploration is worth about a fifth of the maths grade, marked out of 20, and it is written at home across months. That makes it the one part of the grade whose cost depends almost entirely on when support is bought rather than at what rate. Supervision while the topic is being chosen and the mathematics written is inexpensive and decisive. Supervision in the fortnight before submission is expensive, stressful and mostly cosmetic, because the topic is fixed and the thinking has already happened.

In a community where premium rates are normal, this produces a specific and avoidable pattern: a family pays the top band in the spring of Year 2 for help that arrives after a fifth of the grade has been settled. The same household could have spent a fraction of that in Diploma Year 1, on the only occasion when the exploration could still be shaped. The marks are not more expensive later; they are simply no longer available.

The boundary on that help is fixed regardless of rate. A tutor teaches what each criterion rewards, works a comparable example on a different topic, and gives feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor does not choose the topic, supply text, or edit a draft until the thinking has stopped being the student's. One provider ranking for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price, and the malpractice consequences of that purchase fall on the candidate rather than the seller. No band of spending changes that boundary, and a provider who offers to cross it for enough money is selling the student's diploma.

sections.heading: Package terms, siblings, and what we will not claim
paragraphs: Monthly packages in this market sit around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits, and the headline is the least important part of any of them. Ask whether unused sessions roll over, how long the package remains valid, whether hours can move between subjects or between siblings, and what happens if the tutor changes mid-package. A package that cannot flex around internal deadlines, school assessment weeks, family travel and Ramadan is cheaper per hour and dearer per useful hour. We also do not state the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees on this page, because that would require a Federal Tax Authority citation rather than an assumption.

On measurement, the standard here is timed questions and marked work rather than impressions. A cold paper or a draft marked against the published criteria at the start, the same components re-measured after the block, and at six sessions a written statement of what has moved and which components are still costing marks. If the match is wrong we change the tutor at our cost. Nothing renews automatically, and a household that wants only the diagnosis can take it and stop.

And the claims we will not make, which matter more on a page about premium pricing than anywhere else. No grade or points promise: the Diploma is externally assessed, the maximum is 45 points with 24 required for the award, and the result belongs to the student on the day. No satisfaction percentage, score-improvement figure, student count or star rating, because none could be shown with a sample size, a date and a method. No examiner description for anyone whose status we cannot evidence, and no suggestion that any tutor has access to marking, boundaries or paper content. No accreditation from any regulator or board, and no UAE premises. On a page arguing that information is the real constraint in this market, those omissions are the point.

faqs.question: Is an AED 650 an hour IB maths tutor worth it for an Al Bandar family?
faqs.answer: For most of a Diploma, no. The top of this market is published at AED 500 to 650 and above, with BartyED at AED 650, while the qualified subject-tutor band runs AED 150 to 300 with Unitors listing IB from AED 200. What the premium reliably adds is mark-scheme forensics: reading a script the way a marker would and saying exactly where the marks went. That is worth paying for in the final term of Higher Level, when content is secure and the gap is technique. It adds little to Year 1 teaching.

faqs.question: What exactly does a higher hourly rate buy in IB mathematics?
faqs.answer: One capability and two things that are not capabilities. The capability is mark-scheme fluency, which is a different skill from explaining mathematics clearly: it is the ability to say that the second line lost the method mark, or that an approach to an unfamiliar Paper 3 problem was reasonable but unrewardable. The two non-capabilities are scarcity, which is a real cost but not a quality signal, and reputation. No band buys access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content, because nobody has that to sell.

faqs.question: Can I verify that a tutor is really an IB examiner?
faqs.answer: Not independently, which is why we do not use the term for anyone whose status we cannot evidence. A parent has no mechanism to confirm current examiner status, and the phrase should never be presented as implying access to marking, grade boundaries or paper content. What you can verify in minutes is the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which route and level the tutor has taught to examination and when, the component weightings for the course, and the exploration criteria by letter with their mark allocations.

faqs.question: Which activities actually move an IB maths grade?
faqs.answer: Visible method, so partial credit is earned when a final answer fails. Pacing, so the back of the paper is reached with time to think. Non-calculator fluency for Analysis and Approaches. Approach strategy for Paper 3 at Higher Level. And an exploration written to the criteria rather than written and then checked against them. What does not reliably move a grade is more hours of general content teaching, a premium rate applied to Standard Level coverage, or sessions in the week before the papers.

faqs.question: We are in Diploma Year 2 and considering a new maths tutor. Should we switch?
faqs.answer: Only on evidence, and the cost rises as the year progresses. A new tutor spends two or three sessions learning the student, which is trivial in Year 1 and most of the remaining runway in the spring of Year 2. Switch immediately if nobody has produced a specific account of what is costing marks, measured on timed questions. If progress is measurable and the complaint is about manner, switching usually costs more than it returns. Avoid switching twice in Year 2 entirely.

faqs.question: Should we push for Higher Level maths if we can afford the support?
faqs.answer: Support is not the deciding factor, and affordability can obscure that. Higher Level adds a third paper, and Paper 3 rewards sustained work on unfamiliar problems that has to be built over months rather than drilled. A student with secure algebraic fluency who enjoys unfamiliar problems belongs there. A capable student who needs structure and worked examples often scores better at Standard Level, and a 4 at Higher Level is worth less to almost every application than a 6 at Standard. Check what your target programmes publish.

faqs.question: When is the right moment to pay for exploration supervision?
faqs.answer: While the topic is being chosen and the mathematics written, which is usually Diploma Year 1 into the first part of Year 2. The exploration is about a fifth of the subject grade, marked out of 20 across five criteria, and produced at home over months. Bought early it is inexpensive and decisive. Bought in the fortnight before submission it is expensive and mostly cosmetic, because the topic is fixed and the thinking has already happened. The marks are not dearer later; they are simply no longer available.

faqs.question: Does paying more ever make an exploration eligible for more help?
faqs.answer: No. The boundary is fixed at every rate. A tutor teaches what each criterion rewards, works a comparable example on a different topic, and gives feedback on your child's own draft. Choosing the topic, supplying text or editing a draft until the thinking is no longer theirs crosses into malpractice, and the consequences fall on the candidate rather than on whoever was paid. One provider ranking for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price, which is a reason to avoid them at any budget.

faqs.question: Why would an in-home tutor cost more in Al Bandar when the drive is short?
faqs.answer: Because travel is inside the price even when the journey is modest. Published in-home rates across Abu Dhabi run AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. Short journeys from Khalifa City and the Al Raha belt put Al Bandar at the lower end of the in-home range rather than outside it, so the premium shrinks and does not vanish. The stronger argument for online here is breadth: the right Higher Level specialist may not live within driving distance.

faqs.question: Which package terms decide whether a monthly IB maths arrangement is good value?
faqs.answer: Four things the headline price does not cover. Whether unused sessions roll over. How long the package remains valid. Whether hours can move between subjects or between siblings. And what happens if the tutor changes mid-package. Market packages sit around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. A package that cannot flex around internal deadlines, school assessment weeks and family travel is cheaper per hour and dearer per useful hour.

faqs.question: My child has maths and physics tutors at the same premium rate. Is that necessary?
faqs.answer: Often not, and it is free to test. Where physics marks are being lost to algebra rather than to concepts, a mathematics repair block improves the physics grade and the second arrangement adds cost without adding gain. The test is a diagnostic session on the physics work that classifies the losses: if most of them are rearrangement, substitution and units rather than conceptual, the maths tutor is the physics intervention. That advice is worth less to us than two bookings, which is a reasonable reason to trust it.

faqs.question: Are the satisfaction figures and ratings on premium tutoring sites reliable?
faqs.answer: Treat them as unverifiable unless they carry a sample size, a date and a method. In the pages researched for this project, one provider displayed two different review totals on the same page, and another showed a perfect score from twenty reviews next to a far larger claim about students taught. Self-asserted rating markup is against Google's structured-data policy and is a consumer-protection exposure as a commercial representation. We publish no such figures, which on a premium-priced page is the more informative choice.

faqs.question: If money is not the constraint, what is?
faqs.answer: Hours. A Diploma student has a finite number of usable study evenings, and every hour spent on work that changes the invoice is unavailable for work that changes the grade. That is why this page argues for fewer, better-aimed sessions rather than more: visible method, pacing, non-calculator fluency, Paper 3 approach work and an exploration written to the criteria. A household able to buy any band still has to choose which column of work it is filling those evenings with.

faqs.question: Will you tell us if the mid band is enough rather than selling the specialist rate?
faqs.answer: Yes, in writing, as part of the plan. For most of a Diploma the honest answer is that the mid band does the same work, and the exception is forensic component repair in the final term at Higher Level. Saying so costs us revenue, which is exactly why it belongs on the page rather than in a conversation. We also publish no grade promises, no statistics we cannot evidence and no accreditation claims, because the argument here is that information is what this market is short of.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-bandar.closingHeading: Buy the diagnosis, then buy the right band

intro.heading: Three maths routes within a short drive, and what that means for Al Bateen families
paragraphs: Al Bateen and the districts around it contain IB continuum schools, British-track schools and American curriculum schools within a few minutes of each other. The practical consequence is that two children on the same street can be sitting Diploma Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Edexcel A-Level Mathematics, and AP Calculus respectively, and all three sets of parents will describe the problem as needing a maths tutor.

Those are not variations on one request. Diploma mathematics assesses five topic areas across two or three papers plus a twenty per cent independent exploration, and Analysis and Approaches sits Paper 1 without a calculator. A-Level mathematics is examined entirely by terminal papers, with pure mathematics split across two of them and statistics and mechanics in a third, and no independent written component. AP Calculus is a single-year course scored on a different scale, with a multiple-choice section that nothing in the other two routes resembles.

A tutor fluent in one can be close to useless in another, and the overlap in content makes that easy to miss. Calculus appears in all three. The way it is assessed, the notation expected, the proportion of marks available for method, the role of the calculator and the existence or absence of an independent component all differ. A family hiring on the word calculus will get somebody competent at calculus and possibly unfamiliar with the examination their child is actually sitting.

This matters for Al Bateen specifically because the district comparison that families here make most often is between schools rather than between tutors. Choosing between a school in Al Bateen, one in Khalidiyah and one in Al Mushrif frequently means choosing between these three routes without anybody framing it that way. The choice has consequences for university applications, for workload and for how much support the next two years will need, and it is usually made on the strength of a school tour rather than on a reading of what each examination asks a student to produce.

What follows sets the three routes side by side, explains which district tends to produce which, and then makes the argument this page exists to make: the tutoring answer is the same in all of them, because what determines whether an hour is worth paying for is the course and level the tutor has actually taught to an examination. IB Gram provides no home visits in Abu Dhabi; visiting tutors are a service offered only in India, and the same statement appears on every country page we publish. For a central household the practical gain is that the late-afternoon hour stays bookable, because nobody has to be anywhere by then, and that is the better hour for teaching something a student has not yet understood.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme mathematics
programmes.description: One course from four: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, each at Higher or Standard Level. Two papers at Standard Level and three at Higher, plus an independent exploration worth twenty per cent of the grade in every course, marked out of twenty against five criteria. Analysis and Approaches sits Paper 1 without a calculator; every Applications and Interpretation paper permits one.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session. No IB examination or results date appears on this page, because the IB's own site blocks automated verification and an unverified date acted on by a family is worse than none. Your school's IB coordinator holds the internal deadline calendar, which governs when exploration work is actually due and usually sits a term earlier than parents expect.

programmes.name: A-Level Mathematics
programmes.description: The British-track route, examined by terminal papers with pure mathematics across two of them and statistics and mechanics in another, depending on the board. There is no independent written component, so the whole grade is produced in the examination room. Further Mathematics is a separate qualification rather than an extension, which families frequently conflate with Higher Level Diploma mathematics.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs International A Level in June and November series, allocating each centre to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version. Pearson publishes its own series dates and provisional timetables ahead of each sitting, so any revision schedule should be built from the live official timetable for your child's centre rather than from a restated date.

programmes.name: AP Calculus and AP Statistics
programmes.description: The American route, taken as individual one-year courses rather than as a two-year programme, with AP Calculus available in two variants of differing scope and AP Statistics as a separate course. Assessment includes a multiple-choice section alongside free response, scored on a scale that is not comparable to an IB grade or an A-Level letter.
programmes.countryNote: AP examinations are sat in May. Students on this route in the island districts often take two or three AP courses alongside a school transcript, so the tutoring request is usually narrower than for a Diploma student: one course, one examination, one year, with less independent written work to manage.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Criterion-referenced assessment graded 1 to 8 against four criteria, with extended and standard streams in the upper years. Students arrive at any of the three post-16 routes strong on investigation and slower at routine manipulation under time pressure, because the programme credits reasoning quality over fluency.
programmes.countryNote: Because Al Bateen and its neighbours hold IB, British and American schools within a short drive, a student can move between systems at sixteen more easily here than in most of the emirate. abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-bateen.subjectsIntro: Diploma mathematics broken into what a tutor actually works on, with a note on which parts behave the same across all three post-16 routes and which do not.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebra, proof and calculus led, with Paper 1 sat without a calculator. Higher Level adds complex numbers, vectors and induction. The closest of the four Diploma courses to A-Level pure mathematics, though the exploration and the calculator-free paper make it a different examination.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics and modelling led, calculator permitted throughout, with matrices and graph theory at Higher Level. Closer in spirit to AP Statistics than to A-Level pure mathematics, and frequently chosen for the wrong reason by students avoiding algebra.

subjects.name: Calculus
subjects.levels: All four courses, and all three routes
subjects.description: The content that appears everywhere and is assessed differently in each route. Notation expectations, the proportion of marks for method, and whether a calculator is permitted all vary, which is why a calculus specialist is not automatically the right tutor.

subjects.name: Number and algebra
subjects.description: Sequences, series, logarithms, and at Analysis and Approaches Higher Level proof by induction and complex numbers. The topic where a weak pre-16 foundation surfaces first, usually as correct manipulation performed too slowly to finish a question.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.description: Central to Applications and Interpretation and lighter in Analysis and Approaches, with hypothesis testing at Higher Level. Marks are withheld when calculator output is reported without the justification that earns the method credit.

subjects.name: Geometry and trigonometry
subjects.description: Identities, triangle rules and radian measure, extending to three-dimensional vectors at Analysis and Approaches Higher Level. The usual failure is recognising which identity a question invites rather than recalling the identities themselves.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.description: Twenty per cent of the grade, marked out of twenty, with only six marks for the mathematics being right. The component that has no equivalent in A-Level or AP mathematics, and the one families moving between systems are least prepared for.

subjects.name: Paper 3 investigation
subjects.description: Two long structured problems in one hour, where an early error contaminates later parts. Nothing in A-Level or AP mathematics demands sustained reasoning on a single problem in quite this way, so it needs its own practice.

subjects.name: Calculator discipline
subjects.description: Writing the equation before the screen value, storing rather than retyping, rounding once, checking angle mode. The one body of work that transfers identically between Diploma, A-Level and AP mathematics, and the cheapest marks available in all three.

subjects.name: Command terms and notation
subjects.description: Show that, find, justify and hence mean specific things, and the expected notation differs between boards and routes. A reading skill rather than a mathematical one, and one that responds quickly to focused work.

sections.heading: Diploma mathematics, A-Level and AP side by side
paragraphs: The comparison below is the one families in these districts most need and least often see, because each school naturally explains its own route. Read across the rows rather than down the columns: the useful information is not which route is hardest but what each one actually asks a student to produce, since that is what determines the kind of support the next two years will need.

The structural difference that matters most is the independent component. Diploma mathematics carries an exploration worth twenty per cent of the grade in all four courses, marked out of twenty against five criteria, of which only six marks concern the mathematics being correct. Neither A-Level nor AP mathematics has anything equivalent. A student moving from a British-track or American school into the Diploma at sixteen meets a genre of assessed writing they have never attempted, and a student moving the other way loses a component they had been working towards.

The second difference is the calculator. Analysis and Approaches sits Paper 1 without one at both levels, which makes exact-value fluency an examination requirement rather than good practice. A-Level papers vary by board in what is permitted and provided. AP Calculus includes sections with and without calculator access alongside a multiple-choice format that neither of the other routes uses. A tutor who has taught one route will have habits built around its calculator rules, and those habits transfer badly. A tutor who has spent five years on A-Level papers will reach instinctively for the formula booklet, which is the right instinct in one route and a misleading one in another.

sections.heading: Why the tutoring answer does not change by district
paragraphs: Al Bateen, Khalidiyah, Al Mushrif and the Corniche draw on substantially the same tutor pool, because the drive between them is short enough that somebody serving one serves all of them. They send children to overlapping sets of schools. They face the same scarcity in the same courses. The differences between the districts are measured in minutes, and minutes are not what determines whether an hour of mathematics tutoring is worth paying for.

What determines it is three things, none of them geographic. Whether the tutor has taught your child's exact course and level to an examination, which for Diploma students means one of four courses rather than Diploma mathematics in general. Whether the plan is built from a marked script, so it targets the clusters where marks are actually being lost rather than working forward through a syllabus. And whether the slot holds every week, because each missed session costs the first part of the next one in recovery.

All three are available on identical terms whichever of these districts you live in, and all three are available regardless of how far away the tutor is. That is why the recommendation at the end of this page would be the same if you moved two streets. The one genuine advantage of a central address is that short commutes make a late-afternoon slot realistic, and that advantage is preserved rather than lost when nobody has to travel. The central address keeps its one real benefit and stops paying for the other one.

sections.heading: Siblings on different routes in one household
paragraphs: Because these districts hold IB, British-track and American schools within a short drive, a single Al Bateen family can genuinely have one child on Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level and another on A-Level Mathematics or AP Calculus. Parents in that position reasonably ask whether one tutor can cover both, and the honest answer is that it is usually the wrong economy even though it looks like the convenient one.

The reason is that the examinations ask for different things. A Diploma student needs criteria coaching for the exploration, practice at sustained multi-part reasoning for Paper 3 at Higher Level, and exact-value fluency if they are on Analysis and Approaches. An A-Level student needs the board's specific paper split, the formula booklet's contents committed to habit, and applied mathematics technique. An AP student needs the free-response rubric and multiple-choice strategy, which neither of the others uses at all.

The practical arrangement that works is two matches on one family schedule, often back-to-back on the same evening, with one point of contact for rescheduling. That costs about the same as one generalist covering both and wastes fewer sessions, because neither tutor is learning an unfamiliar examination while being paid. Review each child separately, since the two routes progress at different rates and a single review date hides whichever one is struggling. Ask each tutor which examination they taught most recently to a result, and expect two different answers rather than a reassuring claim to cover everything.

sections.heading: The marks that behave the same in every route
paragraphs: One body of work does transfer identically between Diploma, A-Level and AP mathematics, and it is the cheapest set of marks available in all three. These are the marks currently being withheld rather than missed: questions where the student reached a correct answer and the credit was not awarded, or where a correct method was recorded in a way the examiner could not reward.

The causes are the same wherever the student sits. An answer written straight from a calculator screen with no visible equation collects the answer mark and forfeits the method marks, which on a multi-part question are usually the larger share. Rounding at an intermediate step pushes a final answer outside tolerance. Retyping a previous result rather than storing it introduces silent transcription errors. An unlabelled graph fails a communication requirement. An answer given to the wrong accuracy or in the wrong form earns nothing despite being right.

All of that is a habit rather than knowledge, it takes four to six sessions to install and a few weeks to enforce, and it is measurable: take a marked script, count the marks withheld on questions where the final answer was correct, and that total is the ceiling on what this work can recover. For many students it exceeds the marks lost to genuinely unknown content, and almost nobody has pointed it out to them. It is also the first thing worth doing in any route, which makes it a sensible test of whether a prospective tutor is thinking about marks or about topics.

sections.heading: Reading a university requirement properly
paragraphs: The route comparison becomes a decision when university requirements enter it, and this is where families in these districts most often rely on hearsay. Requirements are published, they are specific, and they are not interchangeable between routes in the way that general equivalence tables suggest. Read the admissions pages of three or four target institutions, including the UAE universities on your child's list, before treating any two routes as substitutable.

What you will find falls into recognisable patterns. Some programmes name a specific Diploma course and level, most commonly Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level for engineering, mathematics and physics; where that appears, strong performance in Applications and Interpretation does not substitute. Some name a grade in A-Level Mathematics. Some accept a range of qualifications with a stated minimum in each. Some treat AP scores separately again, sometimes with a required number of AP courses rather than specific ones.

For UAE universities there is an additional process to understand rather than to assume. Ministry of Education equivalency for the British track requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. No IB points threshold is published on this page, because the source setting out those British and American track requirements states none, and an unsourced figure in front of a parent is the kind of error that gets acted on. Verify through the Ministry's own channel.

sections.heading: Moving between routes at sixteen
paragraphs: Because the districts around Al Bateen hold several systems within a short drive, a move at sixteen is more practical here than almost anywhere else in the emirate, and families do make it. What transfers between routes is less than it appears, and knowing precisely what has to be rebuilt is the difference between a short piece of catch-up work and a difficult first year.

Moving from IGCSE into Diploma mathematics, the content gap is early calculus, sequences and series, and the genre gap is the exploration, which is an entirely unfamiliar kind of assessed writing. Moving from IGCSE into A-Level, the content gap is similar and there is no genre gap, which is why that transition feels smoother even when the mathematics is no easier. Moving into AP Calculus, the gap is format: multiple-choice strategy and the free-response rubric rather than content.

Moving between post-16 routes mid-course is a different and harder proposition. A student switching from A-Level into Diploma mathematics in the second year arrives with no exploration started and twenty per cent of the grade unaddressed. A student switching the other way loses the exploration work they had done. Neither is impossible, both need the school's agreement, and both are far more manageable if the conversation happens at the end of the first year rather than in the second. Ask the school early, and ask specifically what the receiving course expects to already be in place. The answer is usually a short list, and a short list is a manageable piece of summer work rather than a crisis.

sections.heading: Testing a match, and the two questions behind it
paragraphs: A free hour over live video, with no card details and no commitment, answers more than any amount of reading profiles, provided you decide in advance what you are testing. Send the course and level, the school, a marked script and the state of any exploration under way. Then watch three things in the hour and ask one question afterwards.

Watch whether the tutor works from your material rather than from a generic topic. Watch whether they can classify every loss on the script as method, timing, fluency or reading, because those four need unrelated remedies. And watch whether they can name something the course does not assess, since somebody working from a specification can exclude things and somebody working from a general idea of mathematics cannot. Afterwards ask your child whether they followed it, which is the judgement that actually predicts whether the arrangement holds.

Two further questions belong to the provider rather than the tutor. What happens if the match is wrong, which tells you whether a replacement costs anything. And what will you refuse to do, which matters because the Diploma exploration is assessed work submitted with a declaration: no tutor may write, draft, rewrite or edit any part of it, at any price. At least one provider in UAE search results sells completed Internal Assessments, and the student carries all of that risk. It is also worth noting that private tutoring in the UAE requires a MoHRE private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, and that IB Gram holds no approval from ADEK, KHDA, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson.

sections.heading: What to do with all of this
paragraphs: The sequence is short. Establish which route and, for a Diploma student, which of the four courses and which level, in writing from the school. Read the published admissions requirements for three or four target universities, including UAE institutions, and see whether the route is actually substitutable for the programmes your child wants. Those two steps are free and they decide more than any tutoring arrangement will.

Then deal with the marks that are being withheld rather than missed, because they are the cheapest in every route: equation before screen value, round once, store rather than retype, label the graph, read the required form. Four to six sessions and a few weeks of enforcement. Measure the gain by counting withheld marks on a script before and after, which is a concrete number rather than an impression.

After that, take the single weekly hour and spend it on concepts and diagnosis rather than on practice the student could run alone. For a Diploma student, add exploration work scheduled from the school's internal dates rather than from the examination window, and start with the topic test because a topic that cannot reach the course level caps the mark permanently. None of that depends on living in Al Bateen rather than Al Mushrif, which has been the argument of this page from the beginning. The district decides which schools are convenient and therefore which route your child is likely to take. It does not decide anything about the hour you buy afterwards.

faqs.question: How does IB maths differ from A-Level maths for tutoring purposes?
faqs.answer: Most importantly, the Diploma carries an exploration worth twenty per cent of the grade and A-Level has no independent written component at all. That changes what support looks like: a Diploma student needs criteria coaching and a research-style conversation that an A-Level student never has. The calculator position also differs, with Analysis and Approaches sitting Paper 1 without one, and Higher Level adds a third paper demanding sustained reasoning on a single problem. A tutor fluent in one route has habits built around its rules.

faqs.question: Is AP Calculus easier than IB Higher Level maths?
faqs.answer: They are not comparable in a way that makes the question answerable, which is itself the useful answer. AP Calculus is usually a single-year course with a multiple-choice section and a free-response rubric, scored on its own scale. Diploma Higher Level mathematics is a two-year course with two or three papers plus a twenty per cent exploration and roughly 240 taught hours. Ask instead what each route requires for the programmes your child wants, by reading the published admissions pages rather than relying on an equivalence table.

faqs.question: Can one tutor teach my two children on different maths routes?
faqs.answer: It is usually the wrong economy. A Diploma student needs exploration criteria coaching and, at Higher Level, practice at sustained multi-part reasoning. An A-Level student needs the board's paper split and formula booklet in habit. An AP student needs the free-response rubric and multiple-choice strategy. Somebody strong at one often has no useful opinion about the others. Two matched tutors on one family schedule, back-to-back if that suits, costs about the same and wastes fewer sessions.

faqs.question: Which maths route should an Al Bateen family choose at sixteen?
faqs.answer: Work backwards from the universities rather than forwards from the school's recommendation. Read the published admissions requirements for three or four target institutions, including UAE universities, and note which name a specific Diploma course and level, which name an A-Level grade, and which treat AP scores separately. Where a programme requires Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, nothing substitutes for it. Where several routes are accepted, the choice becomes a question of which assessment style suits your child.

faqs.question: What transfers if my child switches from A-Level to IB maths?
faqs.answer: Most of the pure content transfers. What does not is the exploration, which is worth twenty per cent of the Diploma grade and would be starting from nothing, and the specific paper structure and calculator rules of the new course. A switch at the end of the first year is manageable with the school's agreement; the same switch in the second year leaves a student with a fifth of the grade unaddressed while everything else continues. Raise it with the school early and ask what the receiving course expects to be in place.

faqs.question: Which marks are easiest to recover whatever route my child is on?
faqs.answer: The ones already nearly earned. Take a marked script and count the marks withheld on questions where the final answer was correct: that figure is the ceiling on what technique work can recover. The causes are identical across Diploma, A-Level and AP mathematics: a screen value written with no visible equation, rounding at an intermediate step, retyping instead of storing a value, an unlabelled graph, an answer in the wrong form. Four to six sessions installs the habits and a few weeks enforce them.

faqs.question: Does living in Al Bateen help with finding a maths specialist?
faqs.answer: For mainstream requests, modestly: the district is central and reachable from Khalidiyah and Al Mushrif without a bridge crossing, so a local search returns results. For Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level the picture is the same as everywhere else in the emirate, because the number of people who have taught that course to an examination is small regardless of geography. A central address makes it easier to accept the nearest person who agrees, which is the specific risk here rather than an absence of options.

faqs.question: What does the IB maths exploration require that A-Level does not?
faqs.answer: A piece of independent mathematical writing worth twenty per cent of the grade, marked out of twenty against five criteria, of which only six marks concern the mathematics being correct. The remaining fourteen reward presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement and reflection. Nothing in A-Level or AP mathematics resembles it, which is why students arriving from those routes are least prepared for it and why the topic choice, made at the start, decides most of the eventual mark.

faqs.question: Why will nobody give me an IB score for Ministry equivalency?
faqs.answer: None appears here, deliberately. The source that documents the British and American track requirements states no IB threshold, and putting an unsourced figure in front of a parent is the kind of error that gets acted on. For the British track, the documented requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the count, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. Verify through the Ministry's own channel.

faqs.question: How many hours a week does a Diploma maths student need?
faqs.answer: One reliable hour suits most students across the two years, spent on concepts that have not landed and on diagnosis rather than on practice the student could run alone. Add density twice: before the school's internal exploration deadline, and in the weeks before the session. Higher Level candidates should also plan a short block of longer sessions for Paper 3, because one structured investigation takes more than an hour to attempt and review and cannot be squeezed into a weekday slot.

faqs.question: Do you send a maths tutor to the house in Al Bateen?
faqs.answer: No. There are no home visits anywhere in the UAE from IB Gram; visiting tutors are a service we offer only in India. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, on a shared whiteboard with your child's own material open, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time. For a central district the practical gain is that the late-afternoon hour stays available, which is the better slot for teaching something new, while the evening window costs the same if the week needs it.

faqs.question: What should the first paid maths session contain?
faqs.answer: Work on the marked script, not an introduction. If the first paid hour is spent discussing how mathematics is going, you have bought something the free trial should have covered. A prepared first session opens the script, classifies the losses as method, timing, fluency or reading, works on the largest recoverable cluster, and ends with a short set to attempt alone plus a written note naming the concept covered and the next target.

faqs.question: Does a maths tutor in Abu Dhabi need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced the MoHRE private tuition work permit, granted free of charge for two years, covering school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged fifteen to eighteen. Tutoring without one brings fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published so no figure appears here. The permit attaches to the individual rather than a platform, so ask the person teaching your child.

faqs.question: How much exploration help is allowed before it becomes malpractice?
faqs.answer: Yes, within limits that any provider should state before being asked. A tutor may teach what each criterion credits, stress-test a topic against the level required, question a method until the student finds its weakness, model a technique on entirely different data, mark drafts against descriptors and check referencing. A tutor may not write, draft, rewrite or edit any part of the submission, at any price or deadline. One provider in UAE search results sells completed Internal Assessments, and the student carries that risk alone.

faqs.question: Should I ask a neighbour whose child does A-Level for a recommendation?
faqs.answer: Ask, then check the route. A tutor who is excellent on A-Level pure mathematics may be an awkward fit for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, because the exploration, the calculator-free Paper 1 and Paper 3's sustained reasoning have no A-Level equivalents. If the neighbour's child is on the same course and level as yours, the recommendation is genuinely valuable. If they are on a different route, you are being recommended somebody for a different examination, which is easy to miss in these districts.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-bateen.closingHeading: Confirm the route, then the course, then the hour
abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-bateen.closingBody: An IB maths tutor in Al Bateen is worth hiring only once the route is settled, because Diploma mathematics, A-Level and AP Calculus assess genuinely different things and the districts here produce all three. Get the course and level in writing from the school, read the published admissions requirements for the universities that matter, recover the withheld marks first, and then take the free trial hour over live video with no card details. Ask your child afterwards whether they followed it.

intro.heading: Price the course, not the hour
paragraphs: Parents in Al Falah comparing IB maths tutors almost always start by comparing hourly rates, and the hourly rate is close to meaningless in this subject. The reason is structural. A Diploma maths course runs for twenty-four months, carries two or three written papers depending on the level, and includes an exploration written at home across months that is worth about a fifth of the final grade. A number per hour cannot describe a commitment shaped like that, and families who choose on the hourly figure routinely spend more in total than families who plan the whole course at a higher rate.

Here is the market, in AED, with sources named. Budget online tutoring is advertised from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor working online runs roughly AED 150 to 300, and Unitors lists IB from AED 200. Specialists are quoted at roughly AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate showing AED 200 to 450 plus for exam-year specialists. Premium examiner-led provision reaches AED 650 at BartyED. In-home visits including travel are quoted at AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate at AED 180 to 350. Monthly packages in the market sit around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits.

Those numbers become useful only once they are multiplied by a plan. Fortnightly support in one maths subject across two Diploma years is roughly forty hours. Weekly across the same period is nearer eighty. A single exam-term intensive is twenty to twenty-four hours bought at the worst possible moment, when a fifth of the grade has already been produced and cannot be revisited. The arithmetic routinely surprises families: the spread-out plan at the middle band often costs less than the panicked plan at the same band, and it buys supervision of coursework the intensive cannot touch.

The largest single cost variable is not the rate at all. It is the route. Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation are different courses with different demands, and a student sitting the wrong one needs more support for a worse result over two years. Getting that decision right in Year 11, or correcting it in the first weeks of Diploma Year 1, saves more money than any discount in this market. There is a comparison table below rather than a recommendation, because the right route depends on the student and on what the university they are aiming at publishes.

One statement of model before the detail. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. For Al Falah families delivery is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, which is also the cheaper half of the comparison above, since the in-home premium in a community this far from the island is largely a travel charge. We publish no rate card on this page: the trial lesson is free with no card required, and a quote follows the diagnosis so it is attached to a plan rather than to a price list.

sections.heading: What two Diploma years of maths support actually cost
paragraphs: The useful question is not what an hour costs but what the course costs, so here it is at the published mid band of AED 150 to 300 an hour, with the patterns Al Falah families actually buy. The figures are market rates from provider pages, not IB Gram prices; our trial is free and our quote follows a diagnosis.

Two things stand out when the arithmetic is laid out. The first is that fortnightly support across both Diploma years frequently costs less than a single twice-weekly final term, and buys supervision of the exploration that the final term cannot. The second is that the route decision block, at two to four hours, is by far the highest return per dirham in the list, because a student in the wrong route pays for two years of remedial support and still lands below where the other route would have left them.

The third observation is less comfortable. A weekly plan across two years in one maths subject is a substantial commitment at any band, and for many households it is not the right purchase. A fortnightly plan with two concentrated blocks, one around the exploration and one before the papers, achieves most of the effect at roughly half the hours. Families are rarely offered that option because it is worth less to the seller, which is reason enough to put it in a table. Read the totals as a range rather than a quotation: a student who needs only technique repair will sit at the lower end of each row, and one carrying real content gaps from Year 11 will sit above it.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation: the decision that moves the total
paragraphs: These are two different mathematics courses, not a harder and an easier version of one. Analysis and Approaches is built around algebraic technique, proof and calculus, and one of its papers is sat without a calculator. Applications and Interpretation is built around modelling, statistics and the interpretation of real data, with a calculator permitted throughout at Standard Level. A student with strong algebraic fluency and weak interpretive writing is a different proposition from a student with the reverse profile, and placing either in the wrong course is expensive in both money and grades.

The decision should be made against what the student's intended universities publish, and nothing else. Engineering and mathematics programmes commonly expect Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level; many business, economics and social-science programmes accept either route. The only reliable method is to read the published entry requirement for the specific programme, in the year the student will apply, rather than inheriting a reputation. Where a family is unsure, the safer route is the one the student can actually perform in, because a 4 in the prestigious course is worth less than a 6 in the appropriate one.

Where this becomes a cost question is in the support each route needs. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is the most expensive maths course to support in this market, because Paper 3 rewards extended problem solving built over months rather than drilled from a topic list. Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level is the cheapest to support well, because much of the work is method that transfers to independent practice once taught. Two to four hours spent settling this decision in Year 11 routinely saves twenty or more later.

sections.heading: The twenty marks you cannot buy back in the final term
paragraphs: The exploration is worth about a fifth of the maths grade and is marked out of 20 across five criteria. Presentation carries 4 marks for coherent organisation. Mathematical communication carries 4 for correct notation, defined variables and labelled graphs. Personal engagement carries 3 for genuine independent thinking. Reflection carries 3 for discussing what the results mean and what the limitations are. Use of mathematics carries 6, the largest single allocation, for mathematics that is relevant, correct and at a level appropriate to the course.

This is where IB maths budgets go wrong. A family that starts tutoring in Diploma Year 2 after poor mocks is buying paper technique, which is useful, while a fifth of the grade has already been decided by a document written without supervision. Six to eight hours spent while the exploration is being scoped and drafted is cheap and changes that fifth. The same six to eight hours bought in the fortnight before submission are expensive, stressful and mostly cosmetic, because the mathematics in the piece is already chosen and the reflection has already been skipped.

The boundary on that help is fixed and worth stating in a page about money, because the market sells across it. A tutor teaches what each criterion rewards, works a comparable example on a different topic, and gives feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor does not choose the topic, supply text, or edit a draft until the thinking has stopped being the student's. One provider ranking for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price; the consequences of that purchase fall on the candidate as a malpractice matter, not on the seller. Nobody should be paying for that, at any band.

sections.heading: Where IB maths money is wasted, specifically
paragraphs: The first waste is buying content teaching when the problem is paper technique. A student who understands the syllabus and scores 4 is usually losing marks to pacing, non-calculator arithmetic and unwritten method, not to gaps in knowledge. Twelve hours of re-teaching produces a student who understands the content slightly better and scores the same. Twelve hours of timed papers with the mark scheme read afterwards produces a different result, and a diagnostic session tells you which situation you are in.

The second is paying for two years of remedial support in the wrong route rather than two hours on the route decision. The third is buying group classes for a Paper 3 problem: extended problem solving at Higher Level cannot be taught at group pace, because the whole point is the individual student's approach to an unfamiliar question. The fourth is buying hours when what the student needs is papers; some students have never sat a full past paper under time, and that costs nothing but a weekend.

The fifth is the most expensive and the least visible: starting in Diploma Year 2. By then the exploration is written, so a fifth of the grade is settled, and the available work is narrower than the price suggests. None of these wastes is a sign of a careless parent. They happen because the market sells hours, and hours are easier to sell than diagnoses. The questions in the table below cost nothing to ask and remove most of the risk before any money moves.

sections.heading: What you can verify before you pay anyone
paragraphs: Almost everything that matters in this purchase is checkable in advance, and none of it requires you to know the mathematics. Ask what each component of your child's course is worth; a tutor who has planned the course answers immediately. Ask for the exploration criteria by letter and mark allocation. Ask which route and level they have taught to examination, and when. Ask what they will not do with coursework, and listen for a boundary rather than for reassurance.

Then the administrative checks. The UAE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years, with MoHRE listing a two-working-day completion time and no fee. Ask to see it, and treat a quoted permit fee as a signal about the provider. Ask who bears the cost of changing a tutor if the match is wrong. Ask how progress will be reported and in what units: an answer about confidence is not a measurement.

Finally, be sceptical about published numbers. Several providers in this market show satisfaction percentages, student counts and star ratings with no sample size, date or method attached, and in the pages researched for this project one showed two contradictory review totals on a single page. We publish none of those figures, for the same reason we would not accept them from anyone else. What we do publish is a free diagnostic trial with no card required, a written plan with the hours counted, and a six-session review measured on timed questions.

sections.heading: Why the in-home premium from Al Falah is a travel charge
paragraphs: In-home one-to-one in Abu Dhabi is quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, with Unitors listing IB from AED 200. The clearest evidence that the gap is travel rather than teaching is geographic: quotes sit lower in Khalifa City, where journeys are short and specialists are concentrated, and higher in the outer communities where the drive is long. Al Falah is one of those outer communities.

There is a second cost that never appears on an invoice. Choosing in-home from here means choosing among tutors willing to drive out towards the airport road at the evening peak, which is a much smaller group than the set of people who teach Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level well. For a Standard Level student the two groups may overlap enough to be irrelevant. For a Higher Level student with a Paper 3 problem, the local set is often empty, and the usual outcome is a competent generalist, which is the one substitution in this market that costs marks rather than money.

The honest counter-case deserves stating. A younger or distractible student is easier to supervise in the room. A tutor can see written working on paper without any equipment. Online needs a tablet and stylus or a phone propped over paper, and that is worth testing in a free trial rather than assuming. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, and home visits are a service available only in India, so if a physical presence is genuinely what your child needs, buy it locally with the premium understood. This page would rather say that than take a booking it is the wrong answer to.
