sections.heading: What we will not promise, whatever the budget
paragraphs: No grade and no points total. The Diploma is externally assessed, the maximum is 45 points with 24 required for the award, and the result belongs to the student on the day. Any provider promising a 7 is describing their marketing rather than their teaching, and in a market where several pages publish unverifiable success statistics it is worth saying plainly that we publish none: no satisfaction percentage, no score-improvement figure, no self-asserted rating, because we could not show you the sample size, the date and the method behind any of them.

No accreditation either. IB Gram holds no licence, approval, certification or partnership from the Department of Education and Knowledge, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge International or Pearson. It has no office, centre or branch in the UAE. Those claims are the most dangerous ones available to a page like this, which is exactly why they are ruled out here rather than left ambiguous.

And nothing that crosses the coursework boundary at any price. A tutor teaches, marks and gives feedback on your child's own work. A tutor does not produce it, does not supply submittable text, and does not edit a draft until the thinking is no longer the student's. We also do not publish or supply IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads; we cite them and link to the official source, because reproducing them is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure. What is on offer is a free diagnostic trial, an honest total, and a plan whose hours are counted before you commit to any of them.

process.title: Tell us the route, the level and the year
process.description: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, Standard or Higher, Diploma Year 1 or Year 2. process.title: Free trial lesson used as a diagnostic
process.description: A working session with no card required. The tutor pitches questions at the route and level, watches the method rather than the answers, and separates algebraic fluency from problem solving, which is the distinction that decides whether a route correction is worth discussing.

process.description: You receive the component priorities, the exploration timeline and the total hours the plan needs, placed across the months rather than averaged into a weekly habit. Counting hours at the start is what stops a household discovering in the spring that it has spent twice what it intended.

process.title: Sessions placed where they are worth most
process.description: Fortnightly through Diploma Year 1 with the exploration supervised while it is being drafted, concentrated blocks before internal deadlines, and twice weekly only in the final stretch after a diagnosis. Sessions move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan on request.

process.title: Review at six sessions, with a route check
process.description: The tutor reports what has moved on timed questions and whether the route and level still look right. If the match is wrong we change the tutor. In a two-year programme a polite mismatch can run for terms, which is the most expensive failure available here.

whyPoints.title: We price the course, not the hour
whyPoints.description: An hourly rate cannot describe a twenty-four-month commitment with a fifth of the grade written at home. The cost model here sets each realistic plan against its total hours so you can compare commitments rather than two numbers describing different things.

whyPoints.title: The route decision is treated as the biggest saving available
whyPoints.description: Two to four hours spent settling Analysis and Approaches against Applications and Interpretation routinely saves twenty or more hours of remedial support later. It is the cheapest purchase in the programme and the one almost nobody is offered.

whyPoints.title: Exploration supervision is placed early
whyPoints.description: Twenty marks across five criteria, written at home over months. Six to eight hours while the work is being scoped changes that fifth of the grade; the same hours in the final fortnight are stressful and mostly cosmetic.

faqs.question: What does an IB maths tutor cost for a family in Al Falah?
faqs.answer: Published Abu Dhabi bands run wide: budget online tutoring from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, a qualified online subject tutor at AED 150 to 300 with Unitors listing IB from AED 200, specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and premium examiner-led provision reaching AED 650 at BartyED. In-home visits including travel are quoted at AED 180 to 500. Those are provider figures, not IB Gram prices. The more useful number is the course total, which is why this page costs each plan in hours.

faqs.question: How much should we budget for two Diploma years of maths support?
faqs.answer: At the published mid band of AED 150 to 300 an hour, fortnightly support across both years is roughly forty to forty-four hours, or about AED 6,000 to 13,200 in total. A lighter structure of fortnightly sessions plus two concentrated blocks runs nearer twenty-eight to thirty-two hours. Weekly across two years is eighty or more hours and is only justified for a student well behind. The point of the comparison is that the spread-out plan often totals less than a panicked final term and also covers the exploration.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to start IB maths support in Diploma Year 1 or Year 2?
faqs.answer: Year 1, usually by a wide margin, and for a structural reason rather than a commercial one. By Year 2 the exploration is written or nearly written, so about a fifth of the grade is already settled and the available work narrows to paper technique. The same budget spent twelve months earlier buys both the papers and the coursework. Families most often start after poor Year 2 mocks, which is a reasonable trigger and an expensive moment, since the cheapest fifth of the grade has gone.

faqs.question: Which maths route costs more to support, Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation?
faqs.answer: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is the most expensive to support in this market, because Paper 3 rewards extended problem solving that has to be built over months rather than drilled from a topic list, and because one paper is sat without a calculator, which is a separate strand of work. Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level is the cheapest to support well, since much of it is method that transfers to independent practice once taught properly. Availability also differs, and a longer match time is part of the real cost.

faqs.question: How do we decide between the two IB maths routes without wasting two years?
faqs.answer: Buy two to four diagnostic hours in Year 11 or the opening weeks of Diploma Year 1. The session tests algebraic fluency separately from problem solving and interpretation, because a student strong in one and weak in the other belongs in a specific route. Then read the published entry requirement for the exact university programmes your child is aiming at, in the year they will apply. Engineering and mathematics commonly expect Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, while many business and social-science programmes accept either.

faqs.question: Why does the exploration matter so much to the budget?
faqs.answer: Because it is about a fifth of the subject grade and it is produced at home across months, so it is the part of the grade a final-term intensive cannot touch. It is marked out of 20 across five criteria: Presentation 4, Mathematical communication 4, Personal engagement 3, Reflection 3 and Use of mathematics 6. Six to eight hours of supervision while the topic is being chosen and the mathematics written is cheap and changes that fifth. The same hours a fortnight before submission are largely cosmetic.

faqs.question: Can I pay a tutor to write or finish my child's maths exploration?
faqs.answer: No, and you should not want to. A tutor teaches what each criterion rewards, works a comparable example on a different topic, and gives feedback on your child's own draft. Choosing the topic for them, supplying text or editing a draft until the thinking is no longer theirs crosses into malpractice, and the consequences fall on the candidate rather than on whoever was paid. One provider ranking for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price, which is a reason to avoid them rather than an option.

faqs.question: My child understands the content but scores 4. Is more teaching the answer?
faqs.answer: Usually not. That profile points to pacing, non-calculator arithmetic and unwritten method rather than to gaps in knowledge, and twelve hours of re-teaching tends to produce a student who understands slightly more and scores the same. Twelve hours of timed papers with the mark scheme read afterwards is the intervention that fits. A single diagnostic session tells you which situation you are in, and it is the difference between spending usefully and spending politely.

faqs.question: Are group IB maths classes good value for a Higher Level student?
faqs.answer: Not for a Paper 3 problem. Extended problem solving at Higher Level is about an individual student's approach to an unfamiliar question, and group pace cannot address that because the point is what this student does when they do not recognise the problem. Group teaching can work for content coverage at Standard Level, where the material is common and the gaps are shared. The sequence that avoids wasting money is a diagnosis first, then the format, rather than the format first.

faqs.question: Why is an in-home maths tutor more expensive in Al Falah than in Khalifa City?
faqs.answer: Because the price includes the journey. In-home one-to-one is quoted across Abu Dhabi at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, and the quotes sit lower in Khalifa City, where specialists are concentrated and drives are short, and higher in outer communities like Al Falah where the evening-peak run is long. That geographic pattern is the clearest evidence available that the premium is travel rather than expertise. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are available only in India.

faqs.question: Do monthly tutoring packages in this market work out cheaper?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the terms matter more than the headline. The packages seen in the market are around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. Before committing, ask whether unused sessions roll over, how long the package stays valid, whether the hours can move between subjects, and what happens if the tutor changes. A package that cannot flex around internal deadlines and school assessment weeks is cheaper per hour and more expensive per useful hour.

faqs.question: Does paying a premium rate improve my child's IB maths grade?
faqs.answer: It improves the match rather than the outcome, and nobody can honestly promise the outcome. What the higher bands reliably buy is someone who has taught and marked the exact route and level, who can say why a correct answer scored two out of four, and who can name the three components still costing marks. That raises the quality of the work and leaves the grade with the student on the day. We publish no score-improvement figures, because we could not show you the sample size, date and method behind one.

faqs.question: What should I ask an IB maths tutor before paying anything?
faqs.answer: Six things, none about price. What is each component of this course worth? Name the exploration criteria by letter with their mark allocations. Which route and level have you taught to examination, and when? What will you not do with the exploration? Do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is free of charge for two years? And how is progress reported, in what units? A tutor who answers all six precisely is a different proposition from one who answers on rate alone.

faqs.question: If our budget only covers a few hours, where should they go?
faqs.answer: It depends on the year. In Year 11 or early Diploma Year 1, spend them on the route decision, which is the highest-return purchase in the programme. In Diploma Year 1, spend them on exploration supervision while the topic is being chosen and the mathematics written. In Diploma Year 2, spend them on a diagnostic plus timed papers with mark schemes read afterwards. What not to do with a small budget is buy general content teaching, because that is the pattern most likely to produce no measurable change.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-falah.closingHeading: Count the hours before you compare the rates
abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-falah.closingBody: If you are weighing IB maths support for an Al Falah household, the first useful step costs nothing. Tell us the route, the level and the Diploma year, then take a free trial lesson with no card required. The tutor will pitch questions at that route and level, separate algebraic fluency from problem solving, and tell you which components are costing marks and whether the route still looks right. You will then have an honest total in hours as well as a rate, including the cheaper structures most providers do not offer. Lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. If the written diagnosis is all you want, take it and stop there.

intro.heading: The Al Ghadeer school run decides your maths timetable
paragraphs: A Diploma student living in Al Ghadeer does not go to school in Al Ghadeer. There is no IB World School in the community, so the family picks a direction: south down the E11 toward Khalifa City, Al Raha and eventually Abu Dhabi island, or north toward the Dubai side of the border. Either way the journey is long in the morning and worse at dismissal, and the honest consequence is that a 16:00 tutoring slot does not exist for this household. A lesson starting at 17:30 or 18:00 does.

That single fact reshapes everything else. A student arriving home at 17:00 after ninety minutes in a vehicle is not in a state to begin Analysis and Approaches Higher Level calculus at 17:05. They need twenty minutes and something to eat. So the usable weekday window is roughly 17:30 to 20:00, and inside that window sit dinner, Arabic homework, the school's own maths set, and whatever else was assigned. A tutor who ignores this books a slot the family cancels twice a month and then resents.

The scheduling shape that works from this corridor is specific. One weekday session, fixed, in the 17:30 to 19:00 band, plus a longer weekend slot used for the exploration and for timed paper work that cannot be rushed. Two weekday sessions works only in the run-up to a deadline, and families who commit to it in September abandon it by November. We would rather build the pattern that survives a whole term than the one that looks thorough on paper.

Maths is also the subject where this matters most, because maths rewards short frequent practice over long infrequent effort. A student who does forty minutes of focused question work four times a week will outperform one who does three hours on a Saturday, and no tutor can supply that frequency. What a tutor can do is make each of those forty-minute sessions target the right thing, and set the questions that fill the days in between, which means knowing whether this student is losing marks to algebraic slips, to notation, to misreading the command, or to genuinely not knowing the method.

The rest of this page is practical. There is a table of realistic session start times by school cluster and travel direction. There is the AA versus AI decision set out properly, because the wrong route choice in Year 11 is the most expensive maths mistake available in this market. There is a paper-by-paper account of where marks go at both levels, and the exploration criteria by letter with their mark allocations, which no competing page in this cluster publishes. Lessons are online, one-to-one, over live video; IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-ghadeer.programmesIntro: Maths support in this corridor divides cleanly by stage, and the stage determines both the content and the realistic length of a session after a long drive home.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Mathematics
programmes.description: MYP maths is assessed against four criteria, A to D, covering knowledge and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Schools often run a standard and an extended route from Year 9. A student strong on Criterion A and weak on Criterion D does not have a knowledge problem; they cannot transfer a method to an unfamiliar context.
programmes.countryNote: MYP Year 10 and 11 is where the Diploma maths route gets decided for a Al Ghadeer student, usually on the basis of the extended or standard set they are in and their Criterion A and D profile. Fixing algebraic fluency here costs a term. Discovering the gap in DP1 costs two years at specialist rates, and the commute means those years have fewer usable evenings than most families assume.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
programmes.description: The algebra-and-proof route. SL candidates sit two papers; HL candidates sit three, with Paper 3 asking extended problem-solving on unfamiliar ground. Calculus carries substantial weight at HL, and marks leak from notation, from not stating a domain, and from solutions that reach the right number without showing the reasoning that earns method marks.
programmes.countryNote: AA is the most requested and hardest-to-staff maths course in Abu Dhabi, and market specialist rates of AED 200 to 450 an hour reflect that scarcity rather than the difficulty of the topics. For a Al Ghadeer family the practical consequence is that the right AA HL tutor almost certainly does not live within driving distance of the border corridor, which is why the match is made over video.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
programmes.description: The modelling-and-statistics route, with the graphical calculator in constant use. SL candidates sit two papers, HL three. Statistics carries far more weight than most parents expect, and HL adds substantial content rather than simply harder versions of the same questions. Students lose marks by rounding too early and by reporting a result without commenting on the suitability of the model.
programmes.countryNote: AI is often chosen as the easier route and then found to be a different kind of difficult. A tutor who teaches AA by default will teach AI badly, because the examiner is rewarding interpretation and justified modelling rather than algebraic manipulation. Confirm which route your child is entered for before any booking: the two share a name and little else.

programmes.name: The Mathematical Exploration
programmes.description: A single piece of written mathematics, produced by the student, marked against five criteria from presentation through to reflection. It carries 20 marks and it is the most predictable place to gain or lose grade-level marks because the criteria are published and the deadline is set by the school rather than by the IB.
programmes.countryNote: The exploration is where honesty matters most. A tutor may teach the criteria, discuss whether a topic has enough mathematics in it, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not supply the mathematics, rewrite the draft or choose and execute the investigation. The consequence of a malpractice finding falls on the student, so the boundary is stated before any session is booked.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-ghadeer.subjectsIntro: Within IB maths, these are the areas Al Ghadeer families actually ask about, listed with where marks are lost rather than with what the syllabus is called.

subjects.name: Analysis and Approaches, Higher Level
subjects.description: Three papers plus the exploration. Paper 3 is the grade separator because it presents extended unfamiliar problems rather than recognisable question types. Proof, complex numbers and the harder calculus are where candidates stall, and notation errors cost marks even where the method is right.

subjects.name: Analysis and Approaches, Standard Level
subjects.description: Two papers plus the exploration. Most lost marks come from algebraic manipulation that is slow rather than wrong, from differentiating or integrating without stating what was done, and from calculus questions where the student can compute but cannot interpret the result in context.

subjects.name: Applications and Interpretation, Higher Level
subjects.description: Three papers with heavy statistics and modelling, plus the exploration. HL AI carries content many families do not anticipate, including hypothesis testing and matrices work. The calculator is essential and using it fluently is itself an examinable skill that needs deliberate practice.

subjects.name: Applications and Interpretation, Standard Level
subjects.description: Two papers plus the exploration. The characteristic error is a numerically correct answer with no comment on whether the model fits, and premature rounding that compounds through a multi-step question. Interpretation sentences earn marks and are the part students skip when short of time.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.description: Twenty marks across five criteria covering presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics. The commonest failure is a topic with too little mathematics in it, chosen late, which caps three criteria at once however well it is written.

subjects.name: Calculus
subjects.description: Differentiation and integration appear in every route at different depths. The repeated error is procedural fluency without meaning: a student who differentiates correctly but cannot say what the derivative represents in the question's context will lose the interpretation marks that follow.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.levels: HL and SL, heavier in AI
subjects.description: The AI routes carry substantial statistics and the AA routes carry some. Candidates lose marks by quoting a correlation coefficient without interpreting it, by confusing conditional probability with independence, and by using the calculator's output without stating the distribution assumed.

subjects.name: Algebra and functions
subjects.description: The foundation that decides everything above it. A Diploma student who is slow at manipulating expressions runs out of time on Paper 2 regardless of how well they understand the topic being tested. This is the single highest-return area for tuition in the MYP years.

subjects.name: Trigonometry and geometry
subjects.description: Identities and the ambiguous case cause most of the trouble in AA, while AI candidates more often lose marks on bearings, three-dimensional geometry and converting between units. Both routes reward a clear diagram, and students who do not draw one lose marks they could have kept.

subjects.name: Calculator technique
subjects.description: An examinable skill in its own right, particularly in AI. Knowing which function to use, how to store an unrounded value and when to show working alongside a calculator result separates candidates with identical mathematics. It is also the quickest thing to improve in a single session.

sections.heading: When a maths session can honestly start from Al Ghadeer
paragraphs: The useful question is not what time you would like the lesson, but what time your child is actually at a desk with the energy to work. From Al Ghadeer those are different numbers, and the gap between them is where cancelled sessions come from. A student at school in Khalifa City is home around 17:00 on a good day. A student on Saadiyat is home nearer 17:45. Add twenty minutes to decompress and eat, and the honest start times are 17:30 and 18:05.

The second constraint is what else is in the window. A Diploma student carries homework from six subjects plus Arabic, and in most Abu Dhabi schools the maths set is given on a fixed night. Putting the tutoring session on the same evening as the maths homework deadline is a common mistake: the lesson gets spent finishing an assignment rather than fixing a weakness. We ask which night the maths set is due and schedule away from it.

The third is the weekend. From a long-commute household the weekend is worth more than two extra weekday evenings, because it is the only time a student can sit a full paper under timing without the session running past bedtime. Families who use the weekend for timed papers and the exploration, and keep weekdays for short targeted work, get more from the same number of hours.

The table sets out the pattern we actually schedule by school direction. These are not promises about traffic, which nobody can make; they are the start times that have held for families travelling each of these routes.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation: getting the route right
paragraphs: This is the decision that most affects a maths grade and it is usually made quickly in Year 11, on the basis of which option the school is encouraging and what friends are choosing. The two courses share a name and very little else. Analysis and Approaches rewards algebraic fluency, proof and calculus. Applications and Interpretation rewards modelling, statistics and justified interpretation, with the graphical calculator used constantly.

The route also reaches forward into university admission. Degree programmes in engineering, mathematics, physics and economics at competitive universities commonly expect Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, and a student who takes Applications and Interpretation may find a course they want asks for something they do not have. That is not a universal rule and it varies by institution, which is precisely why the only safe method is to check the stated entry requirements for the actual universities on the list before the route is chosen.

The route choice also changes what a tutor needs to be. A teacher excellent at AA HL may be mediocre at AI SL, because the examiner is rewarding different behaviour. We match on route and level together for this reason, and we ask for the route in writing before the trial, since families sometimes report AA when the entry is AI.

If the route is already fixed and feels wrong, the honest position is that a change is a school decision with a deadline, and after that deadline the work is to maximise the grade in the course entered. That is still a lot of work worth doing; it is simply a different plan from the one a family hoped for.

sections.heading: Where IB maths marks actually go, paper by paper
paragraphs: Most maths tuition is sold as covering the syllabus, which is the least useful way to spend a limited number of evenings. The syllabus is not where marks are lost. Marks are lost in identifiable, repeated behaviours, and a tutor who can name your child's behaviour is worth considerably more than one who can name every topic.

The first is method not shown. IB mark schemes award method marks, and a student who writes a correct final answer with nothing between the question and the answer collects a fraction of what was available. This is the single most common loss we see in Al Ghadeer students, and it is fixable in about three weeks of insisting.

The second is premature rounding, which matters more in Applications and Interpretation than anywhere. A value rounded at the third step compounds into a final answer outside the accepted range, and the candidate loses marks for arithmetic they actually did correctly. The third is not answering the question asked: a correct calculation followed by no interpretation sentence, in a question that explicitly asked for a comment on the model, loses marks that required no further mathematics at all.

The fourth, and the hardest to train, is time. A student slow at algebraic manipulation runs out of paper time regardless of understanding. That is why algebraic fluency work in the MYP years has such a high return, and why a Diploma student with that gap needs drills rather than explanations.

sections.heading: The exploration: five criteria, twenty marks, one deadline that is not the IB's
paragraphs: Every IB maths student produces a mathematical exploration, and it is the most predictable part of the course. The criteria are published, the mark allocation is published, and the deadline is set by the school rather than by the IB. A student who starts it in good time and understands the criteria can secure marks that candidates of identical ability lose through rushing.

The commonest failure is the topic. A student picks something interesting that contains almost no mathematics, writes well about it, and caps several criteria at once because there is nothing for the mathematics criteria to reward. The fix is a conversation about mathematical scope before any writing happens, and it takes one session rather than ten.

The second failure is reflection treated as a conclusion. Reflection in this context means considering limitations, the validity of assumptions and what a different approach might have shown. A paragraph saying the investigation was interesting and could be extended earns very little. Students who understand what the criterion is asking for write something materially different.

The boundary matters here more than anywhere else in the course. A tutor may teach the criteria, discuss whether a topic carries enough mathematics, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not supply the mathematics, produce the write-up, or decide and execute the investigation. A malpractice finding falls on the candidate, and no arrangement with a tutor protects them from it.

sections.heading: What a long commute does to a revision plan
paragraphs: Two hours a day in a car is roughly ten hours a week, and from Al Ghadeer that is what a Diploma student schooling on the island spends. It comes out of the same budget as revision. Families who plan a mock-season revision timetable on the assumption of a normal evening will build something that collapses in the second week, and the student will conclude they cannot do maths rather than that the plan was impossible.

The practical adjustments are small and they work. The first is to use the journey: flashcards for formulae and command terms, or a recorded explanation of a topic the student got wrong, is genuinely useful passenger time and costs nothing. The second is to move the heaviest work to the weekend and keep weekday sessions short and single-focused. The third is to protect one evening entirely, because a student with no clear night will stop working properly on all of them.

There is a UAE-specific point to add. During Ramadan the school day shortens and the household rhythm changes, and families in this corridor often shift sessions to after Iftar. That works well and it needs to be planned rather than improvised, because a Diploma internal deadline does not move for it. We ask about it in advance and set the pattern rather than cancelling week by week.

The summer and winter breaks are the other lever. A student who uses two weeks of a long break on algebraic fluency arrives in the new term with the thing that was costing them paper time already fixed, and from a commuting household that is far easier to arrange than finding four extra weekday evenings in October.

sections.heading: Why a maths tutor who can reach you is not the same as one who can teach the paper
paragraphs: The pool of maths tutors willing to drive to the Al Ghadeer corridor is defined by the road network. The pool who can teach Analysis and Approaches Higher Level Paper 3 well is defined by their own mathematics and by what they have taught recently. Those two sets barely overlap, and choosing from the first while hoping for the second is how families end up paying specialist rates for approximate teaching.

What the market charges makes the point. In-home one-to-one visits in Abu Dhabi are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour, with Bestimate's table putting the usual band at 180 to 350 and independent tutors asking 200 to 500, read in October 2026. An online specialist sits at AED 200 to 450. The in-home figure includes the drive, and from the border corridor the drive is long. You are paying a premium that narrows your choice of teacher.

To be explicit about our own position: IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere else in the UAE. Tutors travelling to a family's address is a service we run only in India. For a Al Ghadeer family the lessons happen one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, with papers screen-shared and worked on together.

The practical gain is specific rather than philosophical. A student doing AI HL statistics gets somebody who teaches AI HL statistics, not a maths graduate who last saw hypothesis testing at university. And the session starts at the agreed minute, which from this corridor is not a small thing.

sections.heading: What the first six weeks of maths tuition should produce
paragraphs: A plan that cannot be checked is a plan nobody can hold a tutor to. Six weeks is long enough to see movement and short enough that a wrong diagnosis has not cost a term, so that is the review point we use. The first session is diagnostic: a real question from the right route and level, worked while the tutor watches what the student does when they are stuck.

Weeks one and two go to the behaviour rather than the content, because behaviour is faster to change and it earns marks across every topic. Showing method, not rounding early, reading the command term, drawing the diagram. Most students pick up measurable marks from these alone, which also matters for morale in a household where the evenings are short.

Weeks three to five go to the two or three topics the diagnostic exposed, worked through past-paper questions rather than through explanation. The test of whether a topic is fixed is a question the student has not seen, done under timing, marked against the published scheme. Week six is a full paper and a written review, which is the evidence a family uses to decide whether to continue, change focus or change tutor.

The table sets the shape out explicitly. It is deliberately modest: six weeks of one weekday session and a weekend slot is what a commuting household can sustain, and a plan built for an easier timetable is a plan that will not run.

sections.heading: Honest answers on availability, permits and what a tutor may not do
paragraphs: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is the hardest IB maths course to staff anywhere in this emirate, so availability is worth asking about before a family rearranges its week. For mainstream requests, AA SL, AI SL and AI HL, a free trial can usually be arranged within days. For AA HL, particularly mid-year, it can take longer, and we say so at enquiry rather than booking somebody approximately right and letting a parent find out in week three.

On permits, private tutoring in the UAE is regulated. The private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE free of charge for two years, and is open to school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged fifteen to eighteen. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any specific figure you are quoted with suspicion.

There is an Abu Dhabi caution on top. ADEK's professional ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct is reported to bar the same. So the convenient option, paying your child's own maths teacher, is the one to avoid. Verify the current wording on ADEK's own policy page.

On the exploration, the boundary is the same for every provider whatever they imply. A tutor teaches criteria and gives feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor does not supply mathematics for submission or produce the write-up. IB Gram holds no regulator permit, accreditation or partnership, and anyone claiming an ADEK or KHDA approval for private tutors is describing a scheme that does not exist.

faqs.question: What time can an IB maths tutor realistically start with a Al Ghadeer student?
faqs.answer: It depends on the direction of the school run. A student schooling in the border corridor can start at 17:00. One travelling to Khalifa City or Al Raha is usually home around 17:00, so 17:30 works. A student at school on Abu Dhabi island or Saadiyat is home nearer 17:45, which makes 18:00 the honest start. Add twenty minutes after arrival for food and decompression: a lesson beginning the minute the car stops is a lesson nobody learns anything in.

faqs.question: Which schools does the Al Ghadeer area feed for the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: None inside the community, which is the root of the scheduling problem. Families travel south toward Khalifa City, Al Raha and Abu Dhabi island, where the emirate's established Diploma provision sits, or north across the border. Students we support attend schools across that range. Because the direction varies household by household, the realistic lesson time does too, and that is why we ask which school before proposing a slot rather than after.

faqs.question: Should the maths session be on the same night as the school maths homework?
faqs.answer: No, and this is the most common scheduling mistake we see. If the school sets maths on a Tuesday for a Wednesday, a Tuesday session gets spent finishing the assignment instead of fixing the weakness it exposed. We ask which night the maths set is due and schedule away from it, which usually means the session lands one or two days after, when the marked work and the confusion are both available to look at.

faqs.question: Is one maths session a week enough for a Diploma student who commutes?
faqs.answer: One fixed weekday session plus a weekend block is the pattern that survives a term from this corridor. Two weekday sessions looks thorough in September and is abandoned by November, because a student losing two hours a day to the road does not have three usable evenings. Maths rewards short frequent practice, so the tutor's job between sessions is to set forty minutes of the right questions rather than to be present more often.

faqs.question: How do I know whether my child should be doing AA or AI?
faqs.answer: Start from the universities and courses actually on the list, because engineering, mathematics, physics and competitive economics programmes commonly expect Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level. Then look at the student: AA rewards algebraic fluency and proof, AI rewards modelling, statistics and justified interpretation with constant calculator use. A student who is quick with algebra and slow at writing interpretation sentences usually belongs in AA, and the reverse is also true.

faqs.question: Can a tutor who teaches AA also teach AI properly?
faqs.answer: Some can, many cannot, and the difference is not about ability. The examiner rewards different behaviour in each route, so a teacher who has spent years on AA proof and calculus will under-prepare an AI candidate for the statistics and for commenting on model suitability. We match route and level as a single unit for that reason, and we ask to see the route in writing, since families sometimes report AA when the school's entry says AI.

faqs.question: Where do IB maths candidates lose the most marks?
faqs.answer: Four places, in order of how often we see them. Method not shown, which forfeits method marks the mark scheme would have awarded. Premature rounding, which turns correct arithmetic into an answer outside the accepted range. Not answering the question asked, usually a correct calculation with the required interpretation sentence missing. And time, where a student slow at algebraic manipulation runs out of paper regardless of understanding. The first three are fixable within about three weeks.

faqs.question: How is the IB maths exploration marked for a Al Ghadeer student?
faqs.answer: Against five criteria worth 20 marks in total: presentation (4), mathematical communication (4), personal engagement (3), reflection (3) and use of mathematics (6). The deadline is set by your child's school, not by the IB. The commonest avoidable loss is a topic with too little mathematics in it, which caps several criteria at once no matter how well the piece is written, and the second is treating reflection as a summary instead of a critique of limitations.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the exploration without crossing the honesty line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the line is clear. A tutor may teach the five criteria, discuss whether a topic carries enough mathematics, and give criterion-by-criterion feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not supply the mathematics, produce the write-up, or decide and run the investigation. The student does the work and the thinking. A malpractice finding falls on the candidate rather than on whoever helped, which is why we state this before any session is booked.

faqs.question: Does the commute from Al Ghadeer really change the revision plan?
faqs.answer: Two hours a day is about ten hours a week, and it comes out of the same budget as revision. A mock-season timetable built on a normal evening will collapse, and the student will blame themselves rather than the plan. The adjustments that work are small: use the journey for formulae and command terms, move timed papers to the weekend, keep school nights short and single-focused, and protect one evening completely so the others hold.

faqs.question: Can maths sessions shift to after Iftar during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it works better when it is planned in advance rather than improvised. The school day shortens and the household rhythm changes, so a fixed post-Iftar slot holds more reliably than trying to keep the usual time. The thing not to assume is that internal deadlines move with it: an exploration deadline set by the school stands, so the plan for that month should front-load the work rather than hope for a quiet fortnight.

faqs.question: What does maths tuition cost in Abu Dhabi, and does the drive add much?
faqs.answer: Market rates read in October 2026 put an online IB specialist at AED 200 to 450 an hour, and in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 500 including travel, with Bestimate's table showing the usual in-home band at 180 to 350 and independent tutors asking 200 to 500. From the border corridor the travel component sits at the upper end of that premium. Those are market figures published by the providers themselves, not IB Gram's price list.

faqs.question: Will IB Gram send a maths tutor to our home in Al Ghadeer?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; tutors travelling to a family's address is a service we run only in India. Al Ghadeer students are taught one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, with papers screen-shared and worked through together. The practical benefit is that the tutor is chosen for the paper your child sits rather than from the small group of people willing to drive out to this junction at dismissal time.

faqs.question: How long does it take to find an AA Higher Level tutor for this area?
faqs.answer: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is the hardest IB maths course to staff in this emirate, so mid-year it can take longer than a few days, and we say so at enquiry. For AA Standard Level, AI Standard Level and AI Higher Level a free trial can usually be arranged within a week. We do not fill a slot with somebody approximately right, because a family that has rearranged its evenings around a booking deserves the match it was promised.

faqs.question: Do we need to check a maths tutor's permit in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: It is worth asking. The private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, issued through MoHRE free of charge for two years, and tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so a specific figure quoted at you is unverified. There is also an Abu Dhabi point: teachers are reported to be barred from paid tutoring of students at their own school, so avoid that arrangement and check ADEK's current policy.

intro.heading: What the Diploma maths syllabus actually contains
paragraphs: Families on Al Jubail Island send their children across a bridge to IB campuses on Saadiyat Island, Yas Island or along the Al Raha corridor, and when they look for maths help the search tends to be about reach rather than about content. That ordering is understandable and it is the wrong way round, because Diploma maths is a subject where the specific structure of the assessment decides the grade and a tutor either knows it or does not.

Both Diploma maths courses are built on five syllabus topics: number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus. Those headings are identical across Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, and the content underneath them is not. The Higher Level content in each course extends further again. A tutor who talks about maths in general rather than about these five areas and their Higher Level extensions is describing a different subject from the one your child is sitting. Ask any prospective tutor to describe the Higher Level extension content of your child's course without being prompted; a specialist can do it in two sentences and a generalist cannot do it at all.

On top of the content sit the components. Standard Level students sit two papers and the exploration. Higher Level students sit three and the exploration. Paper 1 is taken without a calculator in both courses and at both levels, which is the single most consequential fact in the subject and the one most often absent from a tutoring conversation in Abu Dhabi. The exploration carries 20% of the final grade and is marked against five criteria with published mark allocations that very few students have ever seen written down.

This page works through all of it: the five topics and where each course diverges, what each paper asks and how it should be practised, the exploration criteria letter by letter, the command terms that mark schemes treat as instructions, and how past-paper work should be structured in a Diploma year. The intention is that a parent finishes it able to ask a tutor precise questions and recognise a precise answer. None of it is secret and all of it is published, which is what makes it checkable.

On delivery, stated plainly: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, and visits to a family's address are a service we run only in India. Al Jubail Island lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. That also removes the real constraint from this address, which is not distance but the very small number of Higher Level maths specialists who would cross two bridges on a weekday evening for a single hour of teaching.

subjects.name: Topic 1: Number and algebra
subjects.description: Sequences and series, exponents and logarithms, binomial expansion, and at Higher Level in Analysis and Approaches, proof by induction, complex numbers and partial fractions. In Applications and Interpretation the emphasis shifts towards approximation, percentage error and financial applications.

subjects.name: Topic 2: Functions
subjects.description: Function notation, composite and inverse functions, graph transformations, quadratics and rational functions. Students lose marks reading graphs for information rather than sketching them, and the Higher Level Analysis and Approaches content extends into further rational and modulus work.

subjects.name: Topic 3: Geometry and trigonometry
subjects.description: Trigonometric ratios, identities and equations, with vectors added at Higher Level in Analysis and Approaches and three-dimensional work throughout. In Applications and Interpretation the topic carries more applied geometry, including Voronoi diagrams and matrix transformations at Higher Level.

subjects.name: Topic 4: Statistics and probability
subjects.description: Data presentation, regression, probability distributions and hypothesis testing, weighted far more heavily in Applications and Interpretation. Marks go to correct interpretation of output and to stating conclusions in context, which students routinely omit after getting the calculation right.

subjects.name: Topic 5: Calculus
subjects.description: Differentiation and integration with their applications, extending at Higher Level in Analysis and Approaches into implicit differentiation, further integration techniques and differential equations. In Applications and Interpretation the calculus is applied and technology-assisted rather than formal.

subjects.name: Paper 1, no technology
subjects.description: Sat without a calculator at both levels and in both courses. Exact-value trigonometry, surd and index manipulation, logarithm laws and by-hand differentiation are the recoverable marks, and almost all school practice happens with technology to hand.

subjects.name: Paper 2, technology permitted
subjects.description: A graphical calculator is assumed and rewarded, including numerical solving, intersections and distribution work. Method marks disappear into unshown working, and students lose marks writing calculator output without the reasoning the scheme pays for.

subjects.name: Paper 3, extended response
subjects.description: Two long investigative questions worth 20% of the Higher Level grade, each building a mathematical thread across many parts. It cannot be revised by topic; it is trained by sitting whole papers and dissecting how the questions are constructed and signposted.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.description: Independent mathematical writing worth 20% of the grade, marked against criteria A to E for presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. A tutor teaches the criteria and interrogates the mathematics; no tutor writes any of it.

subjects.name: Command terms in mathematics
subjects.description: Hence, hence or otherwise, show that, verify, justify and state each carry a specific obligation in a mark scheme. A student who treats them as stylistic rather than instructive loses marks on questions they can otherwise answer, and this is five minutes of work a session.

sections.heading: The five topics, and where the two courses diverge
paragraphs: Both Diploma maths courses are organised around the same five topics, which is why a parent can be told their child does IB maths and learn almost nothing. Number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus. The headings match; the contents do not, and the Higher Level extension in each course adds material the other course never touches.

Analysis and Approaches builds depth in algebra and calculus. Its Higher Level content includes proof, among it proof by induction, complex numbers, vectors, further integration techniques and differential equations. Applications and Interpretation builds depth in modelling and statistics. Its Higher Level content includes graph theory, matrices and more extensive statistical modelling, with technology assumed throughout rather than permitted at the edges.

This matters for tutoring in a very direct way. A tutor whose experience is Analysis and Approaches teaching an Applications and Interpretation student will often over-weight formal manipulation and under-weight the justification and interpretation that the second course's mark schemes pay for. The reverse error is just as common. The table sets the five topics against both courses so a parent can see at a glance what their child's course actually asks, and ask a prospective tutor to describe the Higher Level extension content without prompting. Keep the distinction in mind when reading a school report, too. A comment about progress in maths means something different in each course, because the two reward different habits of mind and a student can be strong in one sense and weak in the other.

sections.heading: Paper 1 without a calculator, and why it is the cheapest grade on the table
paragraphs: Paper 1 is sat without technology in both Diploma maths courses and at both levels. Almost every student in an Abu Dhabi IB cohort practises almost everything with a graphical calculator in hand, because that is how the lessons run and how the homework is set. The result is predictable: a student who is genuinely competent mathematically underperforms on a paper that tests the same mathematics by hand.

The recoverable ground is specific. Exact values in trigonometry, so that the common angles are known rather than derived. Surd manipulation and rationalising. Index laws with negative and fractional powers, applied at speed. Logarithm laws, including changing base. By-hand differentiation and integration of standard forms, including the chain rule applied without a prompt. Factorising and completing the square without reaching for a solver. None of this is advanced; all of it is motor skill, and motor skill is trained by short frequent repetition rather than by explanation.

Which makes the intervention unusually cheap. Six focused sessions on non-calculator fluency, interleaved with ten minutes of drilling at the start of every other session, will typically move more grade than six hours of general revision. It is also the easiest thing for a parent to check: ask your child to simplify a fractional negative index, or give the exact value of a standard trigonometric ratio, without a calculator, under a minute. The answer tells you whether this ground has been covered, whatever the last report said.
bullets: Exact trigonometric values known rather than derived

sections.heading: Paper 2 and the graphical calculator nobody was taught to drive
paragraphs: Paper 2 permits a calculator and assumes competence with it, and that assumption is where a second predictable set of marks disappears. Schools tend to treat calculator skill as something students absorb, and most students absorb enough to get an answer and not enough to get it quickly, accurately and with the working the mark scheme wants to see.

The specific skills are learnable in two or three sessions. Solving equations numerically and knowing which solution the context wants. Finding intersections, maxima and minima from a graph and reporting them correctly. Working with distributions, including inverse normal calculations, without guessing which function to use. Using regression tools and reading the output. Storing values to avoid rounding through a multi-step calculation. Setting a sensible window so a graph shows what matters rather than an empty rectangle.

Alongside that sits the writing problem. A Paper 2 answer consisting of a correct number and nothing else forfeits method marks, because the scheme pays for the reasoning as well as the result. In Applications and Interpretation this is even sharper: a modelling question rewards the justification of the choice of model and the interpretation of the result in context, and a student who produces perfect regression output with no sentence of interpretation leaves marks on the page every time. The calculator model matters here as well. Schools specify a permitted handset and a student who borrows a different one for revision learns a menu structure they will not have in the exam hall, which is a small thing that costs real minutes under pressure.

sections.heading: Paper 3 at Higher Level: how the question is built
paragraphs: Paper 3 exists only at Higher Level, carries 20% of the Higher Level grade, and is the component least amenable to ordinary revision. It consists of two long questions, each developing a single mathematical thread across many parts, from an accessible opening through generalisation to something genuinely demanding. You cannot revise for it by topic because its subject is the thread rather than the content.

What can be trained is the reading of it. Each part of a Paper 3 question is usually built on the previous one, and the word hence is doing load-bearing work: it instructs the student to use what they have just established rather than start again. Students who ignore that signal restart from first principles, run out of time and lose marks they had already earned the right to. Equally, the opening parts are deliberately approachable and are there to be banked, and a student who skips them because the question looks hard has given away the easiest marks in the paper.

The method is unglamorous and effective. Sit whole Paper 3 papers under timing, then dissect each question's architecture: where does the thread start, what does each part establish, where does hence appear, which part is the hinge, where was time lost. Three papers treated this way teaches a student to read the structure of an unfamiliar question, which is precisely the skill the component is designed to test. The table sets out the anatomy.

sections.heading: The exploration, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: The mathematical exploration carries 20% of the final grade at both Standard and Higher Level and is marked against five criteria, A to E, covering presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics. Twenty marks are available across them, weighted towards the mathematics itself. Most students write an exploration without ever having seen those five headings with their mark allocations beside them, which is an extraordinary thing to be true of a fifth of a subject grade.

Reading them changes behaviour. Presentation rewards a coherent, organised piece with a clear aim, not decoration. Mathematical communication rewards correct notation, defined variables and consistent terminology, which is a drafting discipline rather than a talent. Personal engagement rewards genuine independent thinking about a topic the student actually chose, which is why a borrowed topic reads thinly however well it is executed. Reflection rewards the student questioning their own results and limitations, and it is the criterion most often scored at zero because nobody told the student it existed.

Use of mathematics carries the largest allocation and depends almost entirely on the topic chosen, because a thin topic cannot support sophisticated mathematics no matter how well it is written up. That is the whole argument for interrogating the topic in the first fortnight rather than polishing the prose in the last. The exact mark allocations and the current criterion wording are published in the subject guide, so confirm them with your child's Diploma coordinator rather than relying on any tutoring website, including this one.

sections.heading: Command terms in maths are instructions, not style
paragraphs: Mathematics mark schemes treat a handful of words as formal instructions, and students who read them as prose lose marks on questions they can otherwise do. This is a short, cheap piece of teaching that almost never happens in a classroom because there is no time for it.

Show that requires a demonstration ending at the stated result, and the stated result cannot be used to get there; a student who works backwards from it earns nothing. Hence requires the use of the immediately preceding result. Hence or otherwise permits a fresh start but signals that the preceding result is the shorter road. Verify permits substitution to confirm, which is a lower bar than show that and students often do the harder thing unnecessarily. Justify requires a reason, not a restatement. State wants a short answer with no working, and a student writing a paragraph for one mark is spending time they will need at the end of the paper.

Write requires the answer in a particular form, usually specified. Find permits any valid method. Determine often expects a conclusion drawn from working. And in Applications and Interpretation, interpret and comment both require a sentence about the real-world meaning, which is where a student who has done the statistics correctly and written nothing in words loses the mark that distinguishes them. Five minutes a session on this, sustained across a term, is one of the highest returns per minute available in the subject.
bullets: Show that: demonstrate to the stated result, never from it
Hence: use the previous result; hence or otherwise: it is the shorter road
Verify: substitution is sufficient, so do not do more
State: a short answer, no paragraph for one mark
Interpret and comment: a sentence of real-world meaning is required

sections.heading: Past-paper work in Diploma maths, structured
paragraphs: Past papers are the most abundant and most wasted resource in Diploma maths. A student is given a stack, works through questions in a tired hour, checks answers against a solutions file, notes that most were right and learns nothing diagnosable. Structured properly, the same material is the strongest preparation available.

Four rules again. Papers are sat whole and under real timing, from the student's own course and level, which from an island address means weekend mornings rather than a late weeknight after two crossings. They are marked against the published mark scheme rather than against an answer key, because the scheme shows what the method marks pay for and an answer key does not. The session is spent on dissection, so the paper is done before the hour begins. And every error is logged in one place, categorised as content, technique, command term or timing.

After three papers the pattern is readable. A typical Higher Level student's log might show four marks a paper lost to unshown reasoning on Paper 2, two to a misread hence, one topic consistently weak, and the last long question unattempted. Those are four separate interventions and three of them are short. Attempting five further papers without that analysis would have produced five more scores and no information. The last point matters most at Higher Level, where Paper 3 cannot be practised in fragments at all. Store the log where the tutor can see it between sessions. A log that lives in a student's notebook tends to be rewritten each week from memory, which defeats the entire purpose of keeping one.
bullets: Whole papers, real timing, the student's own course and level
Marked against the published scheme, not an answer key
Session spent on dissection, with the paper already sat

sections.heading: Availability for Higher Level maths, said plainly
paragraphs: Content knowledge is useless if nobody with it is free, and this is where honesty matters more than marketing. Diploma maths at Standard Level, in both courses, is comfortably covered at Abu Dhabi evening hours. Higher Level is the tightest teaching skill in this market, and Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is the tightest of all.

The reason is structural rather than commercial. Higher Level cohorts at individual IB campuses are small, so the number of teachers who have taught the course repeatedly is small nationally, and the number free at 7pm Gulf Standard Time on a particular weekday is smaller again. Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level is scarcer still, because it is a newer course with fewer experienced teachers behind it. Exploration coaching in the autumn of Year 13 is in heavy demand across the whole emirate simultaneously.

So a request for a scarce combination gets one of three answers. A waiting time with a date attached. A named tutor who covers the course solidly but is not the deepest specialist available, with that limitation stated plainly so you can weigh it, which is usually reasonable for Standard Level and poor for Paper 3. Or an honest statement that we cannot cover it well at the hours you need. None of the researched competitor pages in this market discloses a coverage limit anywhere, and from an address where the local alternative is genuinely thin, a straight no in September is more useful than a yes that becomes a problem in February.

faqs.answer: It consists of two long questions, each developing a single mathematical thread across many parts, from an accessible opening through generalisation to something demanding, and it carries 20% of the Higher Level grade. What can be trained is reading the structure: banking the approachable opening parts, recognising that hence is a load-bearing instruction to use the previous result, slowing down at the hinge step, and managing time across two long questions.

faqs.question: What does the word hence oblige a student to do?

Hence or otherwise is different again: it permits a fresh approach while signalling that the previous result is the shorter road. Show that is stricter still, requiring a demonstration ending at the stated result without using that result to get there.

faqs.answer: Show that, where working backwards from the given result earns nothing. Hence, treated as a connector rather than an instruction. Verify, where substitution is sufficient and students often do something much harder than required. Justify, which needs a reason rather than a restatement. State, which wants a short answer and tempts students into writing a paragraph for one mark. And in Applications and Interpretation, interpret and comment, which both require a sentence of real-world meaning that students who have done the statistics correctly frequently never write.

faqs.question: Which exploration criterion carries the most weight, and which gets forgotten?
faqs.answer: Five criteria, A to E, covering presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics, with twenty marks available across them and the weighting tilted towards the mathematics itself. Use of mathematics carries the largest allocation and depends mostly on the topic chosen, because a thin topic cannot support sophisticated work however well written up. Reflection is the one most often scored at zero, simply because students were never told it existed. Confirm the current wording and allocations in the subject guide with your child's Diploma coordinator.

faqs.question: How early should the exploration topic be tested for depth?
faqs.answer: In the first fortnight, because the mark ceiling is set there. Use of mathematics is the heaviest criterion and it depends almost entirely on whether the chosen topic can support demanding work, and once a student has invested three weeks in a thin topic almost nobody changes it. Two short sessions testing two or three candidate topics against that question is worth more than six sessions polishing prose at the end, and costs a fraction as much. By the final week a tutor is reading a finished piece whose ceiling is already fixed.

faqs.question: Will a maths tutor travel to Al Jubail Island in the evening?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; visits to a family's address are a service we run only in India. Some Abu Dhabi providers will, and market rates for in-home one-to-one sit at AED 180 to 500 an hour because the figure absorbs a round trip across the water. From this address the harder problem is who agrees to it: the small group of tutors prepared to cross twice on a weekday evening very rarely includes a Higher Level specialist in your child's specific course.

faqs.question: Is Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level hard to staff in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: It is the tightest teaching skill in this market, and the reason is structural rather than commercial. Higher Level cohorts at individual IB campuses are small, so the number of teachers who have taught the course repeatedly is small nationally, and the number free at a particular weekday evening hour is smaller again. Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level is scarcer still, being a newer course with fewer experienced teachers behind it. A request in either gets a waiting time with a date, a named alternative with its limits stated, or an honest no.

faqs.question: How should past papers be used in a Diploma maths year?
faqs.answer: Whole papers, sat under real timing, from your child's own course and level, which from an island address means weekend mornings rather than a tired weeknight. Marked against the published mark scheme rather than an answer key, because the scheme shows what the method marks pay for. The session spent on dissection, with the paper already sat. And every error logged in one place, categorised as content, technique, command term or timing, then reviewed weekly. Three papers in, the pattern is readable and the remaining hours can be aimed properly.

faqs.question: My child is in AI SL and the statistics marks keep slipping. What is going wrong?
faqs.answer: Usually the interpretation rather than the calculation. Applications and Interpretation weights statistics heavily and its mark schemes pay for conclusions stated in context, not just for correct output. A student who produces an accurate regression line, a correct correlation coefficient or a valid hypothesis test and then writes no sentence about what it means in the real situation loses the mark that distinguishes a competent answer from a complete one. It is a writing habit rather than a mathematical gap, and three or four sessions of deliberate practice generally fixes it.

faqs.question: Which IB campuses do your maths students near Al Jubail Island attend?
faqs.answer: Families on and around the island travel to IB campuses on Saadiyat Island and Yas Island and along the Al Raha corridor. The names that come up include Cranleigh Abu Dhabi, West Yas Academy, Raha International School, Repton School Abu Dhabi and GEMS American Academy Abu Dhabi. Those names are given to describe the local education map and nothing more. IB Gram has no affiliation, partnership or endorsement relationship with any school listed, and none of them is a client of ours.

faqs.question: Can a tutor coach the exploration without crossing an academic-honesty line?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a boundary that should be stated before any money changes hands. A tutor may teach the five criteria and their mark allocations, discuss and press on candidate topics, teach mathematics the exploration needs, question a method, point at an unjustified step and give written feedback on a draft the student has written. No tutor may write any part of it, supply text to paste in, restructure the prose or produce mathematics for the student to transcribe. Bought-in work is malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student.

faqs.question: Does the MYP prepare a student properly for Diploma maths?
faqs.answer: Partly. The MYP criteria that matter most are the investigation of patterns and the application of maths to real-life contexts, which are the direct ancestors of the Diploma exploration, so a student who worked seriously at those arrives with a real advantage. What the MYP does less reliably is build the technical fluency a Diploma course assumes from week one: negative and fractional indices, surds by hand, rearrangement where the unknown appears twice, and exact-value trigonometry. Those gaps are best closed in the summer before Year 12 rather than during it.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-karamah.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach specific IB Mathematics courses to students across central Abu Dhabi island, including Al Karamah, Al Mushrif and Al Nahyan. Each profile names the course and level, which is the comparison that matters more than any district boundary.

intro.heading: Al Karamah, and the districts either side of it
paragraphs: Al Karamah runs inland along Karamah Street, between Al Mushrif to the south and Al Nahyan to the north-east, with Al Khalidiyah a few minutes west towards the Corniche. It is a mixed district: villas on some streets, mid-rise apartment blocks on others, and a school profile shared almost entirely with its neighbours. Families here compare notes constantly, which is why a tutor recommendation travels across three districts in a week.

The comparison those families make is usually about who someone found and what they paid. It is worth making the comparison properly, because some of the differences between these districts are real and some are illusions. The real ones are housing and commute. A villa in Al Mushrif has a study; an apartment in Al Karamah often does not, which changes whether a quiet hour has to be negotiated. A school run to Al Bateen is short; one to Khalifa City is not, and that sets the earliest workable session time.

The illusion is the in-home rate. Published in-home one-to-one rates across the emirate run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, and where a family sits in that band has almost nothing to do with their child's needs and almost everything to do with where the tutor happens to live. A tutor in Al Karamah quotes an Al Mushrif family a short hop; the same tutor quotes an Al Reem Island family a bridge crossing. The teaching is identical. The price is not, and the difference is road time.

What does not differ between any of these districts is the thing that actually decides a Diploma maths grade: whether the tutor knows the course. IB Mathematics is four separate courses, Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, each at Higher and Standard Level, and a tutor fluent in one is frequently no use in another. That is true on every street in central Abu Dhabi, which is why comparing districts is less useful than comparing tutors on course knowledge. The same holds for the recurring mark losses: method not shown where the scheme awards it separately, premature rounding, computed results left uninterpreted. Those are features of the assessment rather than of the postcode, and they respond to the same treatment wherever the student happens to live.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Every UAE session runs one-to-one online over live video with a shared screen. The rest of this page is a set of comparisons a family in Al Karamah can actually use: the four districts side by side, IB mathematics against the other post-16 routes, Higher against Standard Level as a decision, the provider models compared on their own published prices, and internal assessment compared across Diploma subjects so you can see where the maths Exploration sits.
