abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-karamah.programmesIntro: The programme comparison matters as much as the district one, because Al Karamah families often have children on different routes at the same time and assume the mathematics transfers between them. It does not, in either direction.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Mathematics
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each out of eight, with standard and extended strands in the upper years. Criterion C rewards communication and Criterion D rewards application to real contexts, so a correct answer with no visible reasoning sits in the middle bands however accurate it is.
programmes.countryNote: Compared with an IGCSE route, the MYP produces students who articulate mathematics well and have had less timed manipulation practice. Al Karamah families with one child in each system frequently notice the difference and misread it as ability rather than as training.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Mathematics
programmes.description: One of four courses, with the Exploration carrying 20 per cent at both levels. At Higher Level the papers split 30, 30 and 20 per cent across Papers 1, 2 and 3; at Standard Level, Papers 1 and 2 carry 40 per cent each. Analysis sits Paper 1 without a calculator; Applications is calculator-active throughout.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi IB schools sit the May session, with November as the alternative route. No IB examination or results date appears on this page, because ibo.org blocks automated verification and an unverified date a family plans around is worse than none at all.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A smaller set of DP courses alongside a career-related study and a reflective project. Where mathematics is carried inside the CP it is examined to the same standard as in the full Diploma, including the Exploration, so the comparison with a full Diploma student's support needs is closer than the programme titles suggest.
programmes.countryNote: CP cohorts across Abu Dhabi are small, so schools can struggle to staff individual subject help at depth. For an Al Karamah CP student the mathematics course is usually the component carrying the heaviest external examination weight.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: No external examinations and no mark schemes. Mathematically, what the later programmes assume is number fluency, comfort with multi-step reasoning and a willingness to explain a method aloud, none of which the Middle Years Programme teaches from scratch.
programmes.countryNote: Children transferring into an Abu Dhabi PYP school from a worksheet system usually find the inquiry structure unfamiliar before they find the mathematics hard. The first useful work is explaining reasoning, not more content.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-karamah.subjectsIntro: The entries below describe the components of Diploma mathematics that generate requests from central Abu Dhabi island, written so an Al Karamah family can compare what each actually demands.

subjects.name: Analysis and Approaches SL
subjects.description: Papers 1 and 2 at 40 per cent each plus the Exploration at 20. Paper 1 is non-calculator, so manipulation is tested directly. Compared with Applications SL it asks for less writing and far more algebraic accuracy, and it punishes a weak IGCSE foundation faster.

subjects.name: Analysis and Approaches HL
subjects.description: Papers 1 and 2 at 30 per cent each, Paper 3 at 20, Exploration at 20. Proof by induction, complex numbers in polar form and deeper calculus mark the step up. Compared with SL, the content is wider and the problem-solving demand sustained across longer questions.

subjects.name: Applications and Interpretation SL
subjects.description: Calculator-active, built on statistics, probability and modelling. Compared with Analysis SL, the arithmetic is easier and the writing harder: a computed value earns little without a sentence saying what it means in the context given.

subjects.name: Applications and Interpretation HL
subjects.description: Adds matrices, graph theory and numerically solved differential equations, with a data-rich Paper 3. Compared with Analysis HL it trades proof for technology-assisted analysis, which suits some students very well and is not a lighter course.

subjects.name: The Mathematical Exploration
subjects.description: An independent written investigation of roughly twelve to twenty pages, worth 20 per cent, marked out of 20 across criteria A to E with Use of Mathematics worth six. Compared with other subjects' internal assessment it is shorter than most and weighted the same.

subjects.name: Paper 3
subjects.description: Two extended problem-solving questions worth 20 per cent between them, each developing across several parts. Compared with Papers 1 and 2 it rewards reading the whole question first and recovering explicitly when an early part has gone wrong.

subjects.name: Proof and reasoning
subjects.description: Direct proof, proof by contradiction and induction at Higher Level. Compared with the IGCSE habit of verifying a result, establishing one is a conceptual shift that takes weeks rather than sessions and cannot be compressed into a revision block.

subjects.name: Statistics and modelling
subjects.description: Regression, correlation and model fitting. Compared with Analysis, the mathematics is more accessible and the marks sit in interpretation, which is why strong computational students can underperform here without understanding why.

subjects.name: Calculus across the four courses
subjects.description: Present everywhere at different depths, from basic rules in Applications SL to integration by parts and differential equations in Analysis HL. A tutor's ease at the top of this range is the clearest evidence of genuine Higher Level experience.

sections.heading: Four neighbouring districts, compared on what genuinely differs
paragraphs: Al Karamah, Al Mushrif, Al Nahyan and Al Khalidiyah sit within a few minutes of each other on central Abu Dhabi island, share most of the same schools, and receive noticeably different tutoring quotes. Setting them side by side shows which differences are real and which are artefacts of who happens to live where.

Housing is a real difference and it matters more than families expect. Villa districts give a student a door to close and a desk that is not the dining table. Apartment districts require the quiet hour to be arranged rather than assumed, particularly where siblings share a room. That affects which hour works and whether headphones are needed, and it is worth settling before the first session rather than discovering it during one.

Commute is the second real difference, and it is a function of the school rather than the home. A child at a campus in Al Bateen or Al Mushrif is home within twenty minutes of the bell from any of these four districts. A child bussed out to Khalifa City or Mussafah is not, and the forty to fifty minutes consumed in each direction is additional fatigue rather than neutral time. The earliest workable session hour therefore varies by school, not by district.

The in-home quote is the difference that looks real and is not. A tutor living in Al Karamah quotes a short hop to Al Mushrif and a bridge crossing to Al Reem Island, and bills accordingly within the published AED 180 to 500 band. The teaching is the same teaching. What varies is road time, which means two families with identical needs pay different amounts for an identical product depending on an accident of addresses.

sections.heading: Why the answer is the same in all four districts
paragraphs: Having set out what differs, the honest conclusion is that none of it changes the decision. The thing that determines whether maths support works is whether the tutor knows the specific course, and that is a question about a person rather than about a postcode. IB Mathematics is four separate courses. A tutor who has prepared Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level and can describe what Paper 3 rewards is useful to a student on that course and limited use to one on Applications at Standard Level, and that is equally true in Al Karamah, Al Mushrif and Al Nahyan.

The second constant is what actually moves marks. Across all four districts the recurring losses are the same: method not shown where the mark scheme awards it separately, premature rounding in Analysis, computed results left uninterpreted in Applications, an Exploration topic too simple for the course level. None of those is a local phenomenon. They are structural features of the assessment, and they respond to the same treatment regardless of which street the student lives on.

The third constant is the scheduling constraint. In every one of these districts the binding limit is the school day plus the commute plus homework, which leaves one or two genuinely usable evening hours. Online delivery means the tutor does not consume any of that budget travelling, and that is the same gain in a villa in Al Mushrif as in an apartment in Al Khalidiyah.

Which leaves the one difference worth acting on. If you insist on a tutor who arrives at an Al Karamah address, your available pool is whoever will make that journey on that evening, and the course match becomes whatever remains. That is a genuine cost, it falls hardest on students taking the less common courses, and it is the reason this page exists. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India.

sections.heading: IB mathematics compared with the other post-16 routes
paragraphs: Al Karamah families frequently have a choice to make at sixteen, or a sibling on a different route, and the comparison is rarely laid out clearly anywhere. Diploma mathematics, A Level mathematics and the IGCSE extension courses are assessed differently enough that a judgement about difficulty depends entirely on the student.

Diploma mathematics is compulsory: every Diploma candidate takes one of the four courses, which means the cohort includes students who would never have chosen mathematics at all. A Level mathematics is optional and self-selecting, so its cohort is narrower and stronger. That alone changes what a grade means and how a student experiences the room they are sitting in.

Structurally, the Diploma carries an internally assessed Exploration worth 20 per cent, which A Level mathematics does not. A Level compensates with a higher volume of examined content per subject and the option of Further Mathematics for depth. The Diploma spreads a student across six subjects with three at Higher Level, so the mathematics competes with five other courses and the core; A Level typically concentrates on three.

For an Al Karamah student the practical question is usually which structure suits them rather than which is harder. A student who writes well, works steadily and dislikes high-stakes finals benefits from the Exploration carrying a fifth of the grade. A student who performs best in examinations and resents coursework may prefer A Level. Both routes lead to the same universities, and both are recognised; what differs is where the pressure sits in the two years.

sections.heading: Higher against Standard Level: the decision, compared
paragraphs: This is the comparison that matters most and the one most often made on ambition. Higher Level mathematics is not Standard Level with extra chapters. It is a wider syllabus, an additional paper worth 20 per cent, and a sustained problem-solving demand that Standard Level does not test. Choosing it should follow evidence about the student rather than aspiration about the university.

The evidence available before the decision is better than families realise. A student's IGCSE or MYP performance in algebraic manipulation under timed conditions is a reasonable predictor for Analysis at Higher Level, because Paper 1 tests exactly that without a calculator. Comfort with interpreting data in writing is the equivalent predictor for Applications at Higher Level. Neither correlates particularly well with how much a student enjoys mathematics, which is the signal most families actually use.

The cost of over-reaching is specific. A student on Higher Level who cannot access the harder material spends two years losing marks on questions they cannot start, and the time consumed comes out of their five other subjects. The cost of under-reaching is also specific: some degree courses, particularly engineering, economics and the physical sciences, commonly specify Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and discovering that in DP2 means either a late change or a narrowed list of universities.

The practical sequence is to check the published entry requirements of three realistic target universities, sit a timed paper at both levels in the chosen course, mark both against the published scheme, and decide on what the scripts show. Done in Year 11 that process costs two or three sessions. Done in DP1 it costs a term of repair, and done in DP2 it may cost an option.

sections.heading: Provider models compared, on their own published prices
paragraphs: Every tutoring page compares itself favourably with an unnamed alternative. A more useful comparison is between the models themselves, using the rates the providers publish about themselves and naming the source, which is the only way a parent in Al Karamah can check anything.

The specialist agency model places a vetted tutor and charges a margin. Published figures include an agency quoting IB from AED 200 an hour and IGCSE from AED 150, and a UK-based agency quoting the equivalent of AED 270. The international marketplace model lists many tutors and lets a parent choose, with the lowest published rates in the set, from around AED 33 to 65 an hour at the budget end. The premium named-tutor model publishes rates of AED 650 and above. The in-home independent model is quoted at AED 180 to 500 including travel. Market monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year work.

What differs between the models is not only price. It is who carries the risk when a match is wrong. In a marketplace the parent carries it: choose badly and the remedy is to choose again and pay again. In an agency or platform model the provider should carry it, which means a rematch at no additional cost, and whether that is actually offered is the single most useful question to ask any of them. A tuition centre with premises carries a different obligation entirely, since a training institute in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit issued to the physical centre; no online service holds or should imply one, and IB Gram does not.

The second differentiator is disclosure. Three of six researched competitor pages publish no price at all, and two quote in US dollars, a currency no Al Karamah family transacts in. None of the researched pages in the Abu Dhabi cluster discloses a coverage limit, which means every one of them implies it can staff any subject at any level. That is not true of anybody, including us.

sections.heading: The maths Exploration compared with internal assessment elsewhere
paragraphs: Al Karamah families with a Diploma student usually understand that there is coursework and rarely understand how much of the grade it carries or how it compares across subjects. Setting the components side by side makes the planning problem visible, because they do not arrive evenly through the year.

The Mathematical Exploration is worth 20 per cent, runs to roughly twelve to twenty pages, and is marked out of 20 across five lettered criteria with Use of Mathematics worth six. By length it is among the shorter internal assessments; by weighting it sits at the standard level for the Diploma. A science Scientific Investigation also carries 20 per cent. Economics requires three separate commentaries of 800 words each. Business Management at Higher Level requires 1,800 words on a real organisation's issue. The Extended Essay is 4,000 words marked out of 34, with Critical Thinking alone worth 12, and the TOK essay is 1,600 words on a prescribed title.

Add those up for a student taking three Higher Levels and the picture changes. A DP2 student in the second term is frequently finishing an Extended Essay, two or three internal assessments and a TOK essay inside the same eight weeks that mock revision needs. That collision is the single most common cause of a Diploma underperforming its predicted grades, and it is a sequencing problem rather than an effort problem.

The planning answer is to move everything movable earlier. The Exploration can be drafted in DP1; the Extended Essay research can be substantially complete before DP2 begins. What cannot move is the examination window. Families who treat the internal components as the flexible part of the year, and start them when the school's deadline appears, end up with no flexibility left at exactly the point they need it most.

sections.heading: Comparing two children's mock results, and two schools'
paragraphs: Al Karamah parents compare a great deal, and two comparisons are worth doing carefully because both are routinely misread. The first is comparing siblings. The second is comparing schools.

Comparing two children's mock results tells you very little unless they are on the same course at the same level. A 5 in Applications at Standard Level and a 5 in Analysis at Higher Level are not the same achievement, because the courses differ in content and the Higher Level grade includes a Paper 3 the other child never sat. Comparing a Diploma grade with an IGCSE grade is less meaningful still. The only useful comparison is each child against their own earlier marked script, which is why a diagnostic at the start of a block matters.

Comparing schools is more tractable, because ADEK publishes inspection outcomes for private schools in the emirate and that is the one common scale across different curricula. The limitation is what a rating covers: leadership, teaching and provision across the whole cohort, which says nothing about whether a specific Higher Level class is well staffed this year. A strong school can have a weak department, usually after a mid-year staff change, and that situation generates a great many tutoring enquiries from families who cannot understand why their child struggles at a well-regarded school.

The questions that cut through both comparisons are the same three. What was the last assessment marked against. Has this class had a consistent teacher this year. Which syllabus topics remain to be taught this term. A school that answers those readily has given you more than any rating can. A school that cannot has told you something about why your child is unable to explain the problem either.

sections.heading: Starting now compared with starting next term
paragraphs: The final comparison is about timing, and it has a clear answer that most families act against. Starting earlier costs less in total, achieves more, and buys a better match, for three separate reasons that compound.

The first is market capacity. Between September and December there is availability across almost every Diploma maths course, and an Al Karamah family has a genuine choice of specialist and of hour. From January, as mock results land, demand rises. By February and March every DP2 cohort in the emirate wants examination-term support in the same weeks, and what remains is either less specialised or more expensive. That pattern repeats annually and is entirely predictable.

The second is what can still be fixed. Content gaps can be closed in the autumn because there is time to re-teach and then consolidate. By March the honest plan targets the highest-value accessible topics and says plainly that full coverage is not available, which is a worse conversation to have and a worse product to buy. Examination technique can be rebuilt late, which is why a March intensive is not worthless, merely narrower than families assume.

The third is the Exploration. Worth 20 per cent, it should be stress-tested and drafted in DP1 or early DP2, well before the mock season. A family starting support in February is starting after the single highest-value intervention has passed. One hour spent interrogating a topic in October changes a fifth of the grade; the same hour in March is spent repairing a topic that was never viable.

process.description: Send the exact course and level, Analysis or Applications, Higher or Standard, and whether Paper 3 is sat. That comparison decides whether a genuine specialist exists. Which of the central island districts you live in makes no difference to the match and never has.

process.title: Compare providers on the same five questions
process.description: Ask every provider, including us, the same things: is a rematch free, who verifies course experience, what is the published rate in dirhams, is there a trial, and what coverage limits exist. Identical questions make quotes comparable; different questions make them persuasive.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One session at no cost with no card required, built around past-paper questions rather than an introduction. You get a written read separating content gaps from process losses. If the fit is wrong we rematch, which is cheap in week one and expensive in week six.

process.title: Agree the sessions and the measure
process.description: A standing weekly hour in Gulf Standard Time, the number of sessions in the block, the weeks skipped for Ramadan or Eid, and the measure: a timed paper marked against the published scheme at the start and again at the end of the block.

process.title: Compare the two scripts, then decide
process.description: At eight sessions, put the first and last marked papers side by side. Continue, change focus, change tutor, or finish. A comparison of two scripts settles the question in minutes; an exchange of impressions never does, which is why the measure is agreed first.

whyPoints.title: The match is made on the course
whyPoints.description: An Al Karamah student is matched to a tutor who teaches their exact course at their exact level, drawn from the whole specialist pool rather than from the subset willing to drive inland on a weekday evening. That is the only comparison between providers that reliably predicts an outcome.

whyPoints.title: Provider models compared honestly
whyPoints.description: This page compares agency, marketplace, premium, in-home and centre models using their own published rates with the source named, rather than against an unnamed straw man. Three of six researched competitor pages publish no price at all.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits disclosed
whyPoints.description: Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level is thinner than Analysis, and February and March are tight across every course. We say which, give a date, or decline. No researched competitor page in the Abu Dhabi cluster discloses a coverage limit at all.

whyPoints.title: No travel in the price
whyPoints.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not visit UAE homes; home visits are offered only in India. Published in-home rates run AED 180 to 500 against AED 150 to 300 online, and that gap varies with the tutor's address rather than with your child's needs.

whyPoints.title: The internal assessment boundary is explicit
whyPoints.description: A tutor questions a topic, teaches criteria A to E and gives feedback on drafts the student wrote. Nobody supplies a topic, data or prose. Completed Internal Assessments are sold in this market, and the consequence of buying one falls on the student's Diploma.

whyPoints.title: Claims limited to what can be checked
whyPoints.description: Regulatory statements here come from u.ae, MoHRE and ADEK. No IB date is published, because ibo.org blocks automated verification. IB Gram claims no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from any regulator or examination board, because it holds none.

faqs.question: Is tutoring in Al Karamah different from tutoring in Al Mushrif next door?
faqs.answer: In two small ways and one large non-way. Housing differs: Al Mushrif is villa-heavy so a study is more likely, while Al Karamah mixes villas with apartment blocks where a quiet hour has to be arranged. In-home quotes differ, because they track the tutor's address rather than yours. What does not differ is the thing that decides the grade, which is whether the tutor knows your child's specific maths course at their specific level.

faqs.question: Why do two families on neighbouring streets get different in-home quotes?
faqs.answer: Because the quote prices a journey. Published in-home one-to-one rates across the emirate run AED 180 to 500 an hour, and where a family sits in that band depends on how far the tutor has to travel and at what time, not on the child's needs. A tutor in Al Karamah quotes Al Mushrif a short hop and Al Reem Island a bridge crossing, for identical teaching. That is the clearest argument available for taking travel out of the equation entirely.

faqs.question: How should we compare a sibling on A Level with one on IB maths?
faqs.answer: Carefully, and mostly not at all. Diploma mathematics is compulsory for every Diploma candidate, so its cohort includes students who would never have chosen the subject; A Level mathematics is optional and self-selecting, so its cohort is narrower and stronger. The Diploma also carries an Exploration worth 20 per cent that A Level does not. Comparing grades across the two tells you little. Compare each child against their own earlier marked work instead.

faqs.question: Which should our daughter take, Higher or Standard Level maths?
faqs.answer: Decide from a marked timed paper at both levels rather than from how much she enjoys the subject, which is the signal most families actually use and the weakest predictor available. For Analysis, timed manipulation under non-calculator conditions is the best indicator; for Applications it is comfort interpreting data in writing. Then check the published entry requirements of three realistic target universities, because engineering and economics routes commonly specify Analysis at Higher Level.

faqs.question: What should we ask every tutoring provider so the quotes are comparable?
faqs.answer: Five things, asked identically of each. Is a rematch free and how fast. Who verifies that the tutor has taught this exact course at this level. What is the published rate in dirhams rather than in another currency. Is there a trial, and does it require a card. And what subject-and-level combinations can you not staff. The last question is the most revealing, because nobody covers everything and the researched competitor pages in this market disclose no limits at all.

faqs.question: How does the maths Exploration compare with coursework in other subjects?
faqs.answer: It is shorter than most and weighted the same. Roughly twelve to twenty pages, worth 20 per cent, marked out of 20 across five lettered criteria with Use of Mathematics worth six. A science Scientific Investigation also carries 20 per cent. Economics requires three commentaries of 800 words each, Business Management at Higher Level 1,800 words, the Extended Essay 4,000 words marked out of 34, and the TOK essay 1,600 words. They do not arrive evenly through the year, which is the real problem.

faqs.question: Our son's school has a strong inspection rating and his maths is poor. Why?
faqs.answer: Because an inspection outcome describes a school across its whole cohort rather than one Higher Level class in one year. A well-regarded school can have a weak department, usually after a mid-year staff change, and mathematics shows it fastest because the later topics are taught last. Ask the school three questions: what the last assessment was marked against, whether the class has had a consistent teacher this year, and which syllabus topics remain to be taught this term.

faqs.question: Does a marketplace work out cheaper than an agency for IB maths?
faqs.answer: On the headline rate, yes: published marketplace figures start from around AED 33 to 65 an hour against agencies publishing IB from AED 200. What differs is who carries the risk when the match is wrong. In a marketplace the parent chooses, so choosing badly means choosing again and paying again. In an agency or platform model the provider should carry it through a free rematch, and whether that is actually offered is the question worth asking before any money moves.

faqs.question: Is it better to start maths support now or wait until after the mocks?
faqs.answer: Now, for three compounding reasons. Specialist availability is good from September to December and tight by February and March, when every DP2 cohort wants the same weeks. Content gaps can still be closed in the autumn and largely cannot by March. And the Exploration, worth 20 per cent, should be stress-tested early: one hour interrogating a topic in October changes a fifth of the grade, while the same hour in March repairs a topic that was never viable.

faqs.question: Are Applications and Analysis really that different, or is it marketing?
faqs.answer: Genuinely different. Analysis is built on algebra, calculus and proof, and its Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, so manipulation is load-bearing. Applications is calculator-active and built on statistics, probability and modelling, with matrices and graph theory at Higher Level, and its mark schemes award written interpretation. A tutor fluent in one may never have taught the other, which is why we match on the course name and level rather than on the word mathematics.

faqs.question: Does an apartment in Al Karamah make online lessons harder than a villa would?
faqs.answer: Slightly, and it is worth solving before the first session rather than during it. What a video lesson needs is a quiet hour and a screen the student can see properly, which in a shared room means headphones and an agreement with siblings. Villa districts tend to supply a door to close. It is a practical arrangement rather than an academic obstacle, and students in apartments across the island work perfectly well once the hour is protected.

faqs.question: What does Paper 3 add, and does our child sit it?
faqs.answer: Only Higher Level candidates sit it, in both courses, and it carries 20 per cent of the grade. It is two extended problem-solving questions, each developing across several parts so later answers depend on earlier ones. That dependency is the distinctive difficulty: an unflagged error early can cost marks through the rest of the question. The most valuable thing to learn for it is stating an assumption and carrying on explicitly when part (a) has clearly gone wrong.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover maths for two children in different districts of the family?
faqs.answer: Location is irrelevant, since the lessons are online, so the only question is whether the courses align. A specialist teaching Analysis at Standard Level can often also support an MYP extended mathematics student, because the content sits on one continuum. A tutor covering Applications at Higher Level for one child and Analysis at Higher Level for another is two different specialisms, and combining them means one child gets the weaker match.

faqs.question: Under what circumstances would you turn our money away?
faqs.answer: Several things. If the school's own clinic covers the gap, which costs nothing and is already paid for through fees. If the last assessment was never properly diagnosed, in which case a conversation with the head of department comes first. If the working environment is the real problem. And if the diagnostic shows the student simply needs supervised practice they could do alone. We would rather say that than sell a weekly habit that outlives the problem.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-karamah.closingHeading: Compare the course, not the postcode
abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-karamah.closingBody: If you are weighing up an IB maths tutor in Al Karamah against what a neighbour found in Al Mushrif or Al Nahyan, the comparison worth making is not about districts. Send the exact course, the level and whether Paper 3 is sat, along with the hours that genuinely work once the school run is counted, and we will say honestly whether a specialist in that course is free. Ask us the same five questions you ask everyone else. The first lesson is a free trial with no card required, and lessons run one-to-one online over live video in Gulf Standard Time.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-khalidiya.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed here teach IB Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, at both Higher and Standard Level. Each profile names the course and level, so an Al Khalidiyah family can check the match against their child's timetable before spending anything.

intro.heading: Start with the bill, not the brochure
paragraphs: Most tutoring pages discuss price last, vaguely, or not at all. Three of the six main competitor pages researched for Abu Dhabi and Dubai publish no figure whatsoever, and two of the remaining quote in US dollars, a currency no family in Al Khalidiyah pays anybody in. That silence is not an accident. A monthly number is harder to defend than a page of adjectives, and once a parent sees the number they start asking what it buys.

So here is the market, in dirhams, with sources. Budget online tutoring is advertised from around AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified subject tutors working online are quoted at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Specialist IB and IGCSE tutors sit at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. Premium named or examiner-track tutors reach AED 500 to 650 and more, with BartyED at AED 650. In-home one-to-one visits, travel included, are quoted at AED 180 to 500. Monthly, Bestimate's estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year work. Those are other providers' published rates, cited as the market rather than as our price list.

The more useful question for an Al Khalidiyah parent is where that money disappears. Four patterns account for most of the waste we see. Buying hours before anyone has diagnosed the problem, so the first month is spent discovering what a marked paper would have revealed in ninety minutes. Paying the examiner-track premium for a DP1 student who needs algebra consolidation, which is a Formula One mechanic changing a bicycle tyre. Paying the in-home travel premium, which adds no teaching. And buying a group class for a student whose gap is specific, where a shared pace means the one topic they needed is covered in four minutes.

Mathematics in the Diploma is also four courses, not one, and the course decides the cost of support. Analysis and Approaches is the algebra and proof route, with a non-calculator Paper 1 and, at Higher Level, a Paper 3 of two extended problem-solving questions. Applications and Interpretation is calculator-active, built on statistics and modelling, with matrices and graph theory at Higher Level. Higher Level in either course carries a third paper and a wider syllabus, which is a real difference in hours rather than a marketing distinction. A quote given before anyone has established the course and level is a guess.

One structural point before the detail. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Every session for an Al Khalidiyah family runs one-to-one online over live video with a shared screen. That removes the travel premium from your bill and removes the geographic limit from the pool of maths specialists available to your child, which is the part that actually affects the result.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-khalidiya.programmesIntro: The cost of maths support changes with the stage, because the thing being bought changes. Primary support buys fluency, middle-years support buys criteria literacy, and Diploma support buys examination technique against a published mark scheme. Paying Diploma rates for primary consolidation is one of the quieter ways families overspend.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: No external examinations, so there is no mark scheme to teach to. What is bought at this stage is number fluency, confidence with multi-step reasoning and the habit of explaining a method. Short blocks work better than standing arrangements, and the rate should sit at the lower end of the market rather than the specialist band.
programmes.countryNote: Al Khalidiyah families transferring into an Abu Dhabi PYP school mid-year sometimes buy a year of support when eight weeks of targeted work would have closed the gap. Ask any prospective tutor what they would stop doing once the gap is closed; the answer tells you whether the arrangement has an end.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight. In mathematics the recurring loss is Criterion C, communication, where a student with the right answer scores poorly for not showing reasoning. Support here is inexpensive relative to the Diploma and disproportionately valuable, because it prevents the DP1 collapse.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP extended mathematics strand feeds Analysis and Approaches; the standard strand feeds Applications and Interpretation. Settling that route in Year 10 is the cheapest intervention available to an Abu Dhabi family, because correcting a wrong course choice in DP1 costs a term of catch-up at Diploma rates.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Where the money concentrates. Six subjects with three at Higher Level, scored out of 45, with every subject carrying an internally assessed component. In mathematics the Exploration is 20 per cent of the grade and is produced during DP1 or early DP2, which means a fifth of the result is decided before revision begins.
programmes.countryNote: Two-thirds of the maths enquiries from Abu Dhabi island are DP1 students in their second term, which is after the first mock and before the Exploration. That is an expensive moment to start, because it is the point at which two needs compete. Starting a term earlier is cheaper and calmer.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Fewer DP courses alongside a career-related study and a reflective project. The DP mathematics course inside it is examined to the same standard as in the full Diploma, so the support needed is identical even though the overall programme is lighter. Budget for the course, not for the programme's reputation.
programmes.countryNote: CP students in Abu Dhabi are a small cohort, which means their schools sometimes cannot staff individual subject help at depth. For a CP student in Al Khalidiyah, maths support is usually the single highest-value purchase in the programme, because it is the component carrying external examination weight.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-khalidiya.subjectsIntro: An IB maths quote is only meaningful once the course, the level and the component are named. The entries below break the subject into the parts families actually pay to fix, with what each one demands and where it tends to go wrong.

subjects.name: Analysis and Approaches SL
subjects.description: Papers 1 and 2 at 40 per cent each, Exploration at 20. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, which exposes any weakness in algebraic manipulation immediately. The commonest losses are unsimplified surds, sign errors through long rearrangements, and differentiation applied without stating the rule used.

subjects.name: Analysis and Approaches HL
subjects.description: Papers 1 and 2 at 30 per cent each, Paper 3 at 20, Exploration at 20. Paper 3 presents two extended problem-solving questions that build across parts, so a single early error can cost a whole section. Proof by induction and complex numbers in polar form are the predictable trouble spots.

subjects.name: Applications and Interpretation SL
subjects.description: Calculator-active throughout, with statistics, probability and modelling at the centre. The course is not easier than Analysis, it is different: the writing demand is higher, because interpretation marks require a sentence about what a number means in context rather than the number itself.

subjects.name: Applications and Interpretation HL
subjects.description: Adds matrices, graph theory, complex numbers in applied contexts and differential equations solved numerically. Paper 3 is a data-rich extended investigation under timed conditions. Students who chose the course to avoid algebra are frequently caught by the volume of technology-assisted work it expects.

subjects.name: The Mathematical Exploration
subjects.description: A written investigation of around twelve to twenty pages, worth 20 per cent, marked out of 20 across five criteria. Use of Mathematics carries six of those marks. The commonest failure is a topic that is interesting but not mathematically rich enough to generate work at the right level.

subjects.name: Paper 3 problem solving
subjects.description: The component most often bought as a standalone block, because it is unlike anything in SL. Two long questions, each developing a situation across several parts, rewarding the ability to carry a result forward. It is teachable, but it needs full-length timed practice rather than topic exercises.

subjects.name: MYP extended mathematics
subjects.description: The feeder strand into Analysis and Approaches. Assessed against four criteria, where Criterion C rewards communication and Criterion D rewards applying mathematics to real contexts. A student strong on answers and weak on reasoning will score in the middle bands and then struggle with the Diploma's method marks.

subjects.name: Cambridge 0607 International Mathematics
subjects.description: The IGCSE course many Abu Dhabi IB schools use as a Diploma feeder, with a graphics-calculator requirement and an investigation paper. Students arriving in DP1 from 0580 rather than 0607 often need explicit work on calculator technique and on open-ended investigation.

subjects.name: University entry mathematics requirements
subjects.description: Engineering, economics and most physical-science degrees commonly specify Analysis and Approaches, frequently at Higher Level. Checking the published requirements of target universities before the DP1 course deadline costs nothing and prevents the single most expensive error in Diploma maths planning.

sections.heading: What IB maths support costs per month around Al Khalidiyah
paragraphs: Hourly rates are how tutors quote and monthly totals are how families actually budget, so the monthly view is the useful one. A weekly one-hour session at the budget end of the published market lands somewhere around AED 240 to 600 a month on Bestimate's estimates. A mid-market qualified subject tutor puts the same weekly session at roughly AED 600 to 1,200. Specialist examination-year support reaches AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above. Advertised packages confirm the shape: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits.

Read those three bands as three different products rather than three prices for the same thing. The budget band typically means a university student or a generalist working from textbook exercises, which is adequate for consolidating MYP arithmetic and inadequate for Analysis and Approaches HL Paper 3. The middle band buys someone who knows the course and the mark scheme. The specialist band buys depth in one course plus examination-term availability, which is genuinely scarce in February and March. Paying the top band for a problem the middle band solves is the commonest overspend in this market.

The in-home comparison is the clearest. Published in-home one-to-one rates across Abu Dhabi and Dubai run AED 180 to 500 an hour, against AED 150 to 300 for qualified online subject tutors. The additional money buys a car, a parking space and forty minutes of someone's evening. It does not buy better teaching, and in a dense part of the island it buys a cancellation risk as well. Every figure in this section is another provider's published rate, named so you can check it, and framed as the market rather than as an IB Gram price.

What we will not do is publish an invented price list to look competitive. The honest route to our number is a free trial lesson and a short conversation about the course, the level and the hours, because a quote given before those are known is a guess dressed as a figure.

sections.heading: The four places Al Khalidiyah families waste tutoring money
paragraphs: The first is buying hours before anyone has diagnosed anything. A family books twelve sessions, and the first three are spent working out what a marked timed paper would have shown in ninety minutes. The fix is to sit a paper first, mark it against the published scheme, and buy against what the script says. It feels slower and it removes a month of guesswork.

The second is paying for the wrong altitude of expertise. An examiner-track tutor at the top of the market is the right purchase for a DP2 student polishing Paper 3 technique in February. For a DP1 student whose actual problem is that quadratic manipulation from Year 10 never became automatic, it is a waste of two hundred dirhams an hour, because the work required is patient and elementary. Match the tutor to the gap, not to the aspiration.

The third is the travel premium. In-home rates run AED 180 to 500 against AED 150 to 300 online for a qualified subject tutor, and the difference funds a journey. In Al Khalidiyah, where a tutor is crossing dense island traffic in the late afternoon, that premium also buys variance: sessions that start late, sessions that move, and eventually a week with no session at all.

The fourth is a group class bought for a specific gap. Group tuition has a legitimate place and a genuinely lower price, and it is the wrong instrument when a student needs twenty minutes on integration by substitution. A shared pace means the one topic that mattered gets four minutes while the rest of the hour covers material the student already has. Families often discover this in month three, having paid for twelve hours to receive perhaps ninety minutes of relevant teaching.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation: the choice that changes the bill
paragraphs: Every Diploma maths budget starts with this choice, and families frequently make it on the wrong information. Analysis and Approaches is the algebra, calculus and proof route. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, which means algebraic fluency is not optional. Applications and Interpretation is calculator-active throughout, built around statistics, probability, modelling and, at Higher Level, matrices, graph theory and numerically solved differential equations.

Applications is not the easier course. It is the course with a different centre of gravity. Students who pick it to escape algebra are frequently caught by its interpretation demand: a correct number earns little unless the candidate writes what it means in the context given, and that sentence is marked. Students who pick Analysis because it sounds more rigorous and who have not consolidated manipulation from the IGCSE years spend DP1 paying someone to repair foundations.

The cost difference is real in both directions. An Analysis HL student usually needs Paper 3 support, which is a specialist component and is priced accordingly. An Applications HL student usually needs technology fluency and investigation practice, which is less scarce and therefore cheaper, but they need more written-interpretation coaching than families expect. A tutor who can describe this difference before quoting is a tutor who knows the courses.

The expensive mistake is choosing the course without checking university requirements. Engineering, economics and most physical-science degrees commonly specify Analysis and Approaches, frequently at Higher Level. Discovering that in DP2 means either a course change under deadline pressure or a narrowed university list. Checking the published entry requirements of three target universities costs nothing and happens before the DP1 deadline.

sections.heading: HL and SL weightings, and why Higher Level genuinely costs more to support
paragraphs: The weightings are public and they explain the price difference better than any sales conversation. At Standard Level, Papers 1 and 2 carry 40 per cent each and the Exploration 20. At Higher Level, Papers 1 and 2 carry 30 per cent each, Paper 3 carries 20 and the Exploration 20. The arithmetic matters: at HL a fifth of the grade sits in a component that does not exist at SL and that is unlike anything in it.

Paper 3 is two extended problem-solving questions, each developing a scenario across several parts. A candidate who makes an early error can lose a cascade of marks downstream, and the skill of carrying a result forward under time pressure is not built by topic worksheets. It needs full-length timed questions, marked and discussed, which is why HL support tends to be bought as a block in the months before mocks rather than spread thinly across two years.

The syllabus is also wider at HL, so more content has to be covered before technique work can begin. An HL student arriving in February with the last topics untaught is in a different and more expensive position than an SL student in the same month, because the SL student can spend the whole window on technique. That difference is the single clearest justification for a higher rate, and it is worth asking a tutor to explain it rather than accept it.

The practical consequence for budgeting is sequencing. An HL family who buys support from the start of DP2 at one session a week spends less in total, and more calmly, than one who buys three sessions a week in March. The second arrangement costs more per week, achieves less, and arrives at the point where syllabus gaps can no longer be closed.

sections.heading: The Exploration is a fifth of the grade: the criteria, by letter
paragraphs: No researched competitor page names a single IB assessment criterion, which is remarkable given that the Exploration carries 20 per cent of the maths grade. It is marked out of 20 across five criteria, and knowing the letters changes how a student spends their time. Criterion A, presentation, is worth four marks. Criterion B, mathematical communication, four. Criterion C, personal engagement, three. Criterion D, reflection, three. Criterion E, use of mathematics, six.

The distribution is instructive. Use of mathematics is the single largest criterion, which means a beautifully written investigation built on mathematics below the level of the course cannot score well, no matter how engaging it is. That is the most common reason an Exploration underperforms: the topic was chosen for interest and never stress-tested for mathematical richness. One session spent interrogating the topic before any work starts is worth more than three spent polishing prose afterwards.

Reflection and personal engagement together carry six marks and cannot be outsourced, which is a practical argument as well as an ethical one. A ghostwritten Exploration scores poorly on precisely those criteria, because the voice is generic and the reflection is decorative. Operations selling completed Internal Assessments exist in this market, one at a published fixed price. Buying one is academic malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student, whose Diploma can be withheld.

What a tutor may legitimately do is clear. Question the topic until the student's own idea is workable. Point out that a planned data set will not support the analysis. Teach what each criterion rewards. Give feedback on a draft the student has written. What a tutor must not do is choose the title, supply the data, draft paragraphs, or edit the work until the words are no longer the student's. The test is whether the student can explain every sentence and every decision as their own.

sections.heading: A two-year Diploma maths plan, costed stage by stage
paragraphs: The cheapest effective plan is spread, not intense. Set out across two years, Diploma maths support divides into four stages with different needs and different prices, and a family that buys in that order spends less than one that buys in a panic. Published market bands make the comparison possible even though our own numbers come after a trial lesson.

The first stage is the course decision, late in the MYP or at the start of DP1. The purchase here is diagnosis and advice rather than teaching: two or three sessions that establish whether Analysis or Applications fits, and whether Higher Level is realistic. It is the smallest spend in the plan and the one that prevents the largest later cost, because a wrong course corrected in DP1 means a term of catch-up.

The second stage is DP1 maintenance, one session a week in the mid-market band, which keeps content current and builds method-mark discipline while the pressure is still low. The third stage is the Exploration block, three to five sessions, concentrated and then finished. The fourth stage is the examination term, where rates are highest and availability is tightest, and where a family that has done the first three stages needs the least.

The alternative pattern, which is what most families actually do, is nothing for eighteen months followed by three sessions a week from February at the specialist band. That costs more per week, buys less, and arrives at the point where untaught syllabus content can no longer be recovered. The table sets both out so the comparison is visible rather than argued.

sections.heading: Who is free to teach which maths course, and what happens if nobody is
paragraphs: Availability is a cost question as much as a scheduling one, because scarcity is what moves a rate. Analysis and Approaches at both levels is the best-covered course in the whole IB catalogue, which is why it is also the course where a family has genuine choice and should not accept the top of the market by default. Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level is thinner, particularly for Paper 3 work, and that scarcity is real rather than manufactured.

The hour matters as much as the course. An Al Khalidiyah student who can work at seven or eight in the evening Gulf Standard Time has a wide pool, because several time zones overlap comfortably with an Abu Dhabi evening. A student who can only manage seven in the morning before school has a much narrower one, and narrow pools cost more. This is the one scheduling flexibility that translates directly into price, and families rarely realise it is available to them.

February and March are the tight months, every year, because every DP2 cohort wants examination-term support simultaneously. A family that arranges a specialist in October has a choice of tutors at the normal rate. A family that starts looking in February is competing for the remaining capacity. Nothing about that is unique to Abu Dhabi, and it is entirely predictable, which makes it manageable.

When we cannot staff a request properly, there are three honest answers and promising a match is not one of them. Offer a dated waiting slot. Offer a genuinely qualified alternative and state the limitation plainly. Or decline. No competitor page found in the Abu Dhabi cluster discloses a coverage limit at all, which is worth noticing when every one of them implies total coverage.

sections.heading: Five emirates, five regulators, and why cost context differs across the UAE
paragraphs: Tutoring prices in the UAE are discussed as though the country were one market, and schooling is not regulated that way. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Dubai sits with KHDA, which oversees the quality of private education there. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

This is not academic for a family budgeting an Al Khalidiyah education. Fee regulation differs by emirate, and so does the published evidence a parent can use. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. That is a Dubai measure, announced by the Dubai regulator. An Abu Dhabi family reading a Dubai figure and assuming it applies to them is working from the wrong market.

Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so in those emirates curriculum and fee approval both sit locally rather than federally. The federal baseline is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations.

A final note that belongs on a page about money. IB Gram claims no accreditation, licence, approval or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, because it holds none of them. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai would need a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute; an online matching service is a different legal animal and should not imply otherwise. Naming a regulator and explaining what it does is legitimate. Implying an endorsement is not.

process.title: Name the course, the level and the component
process.description: Not "IB maths" but "Applications and Interpretation HL, DP2, struggling with Paper 3". Those three facts determine whether a specialist exists and what the work costs. A quote offered before they are known is a guess, and quotes like that are usually revised upward later.

process.title: Sit a diagnostic before buying hours
process.description: One timed past paper, marked against the published scheme, locates the gap in ninety minutes rather than in a month of sessions. This is the single cheapest step in the whole process and the one families skip most often, which is why the first month so frequently feels unproductive.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One session with the matched tutor at no cost, with no card required, built around the diagnostic rather than a conversation. If the fit is wrong, say so and we rematch. Correcting a match in week one costs nothing; correcting it in week six costs a term.

process.title: Buy the smallest plan that fits
process.description: One session a week in the band that matches the gap, not the band that sounds most impressive. If the diagnosis says elementary consolidation, an examiner-track rate is money spent on reassurance. We will say so, even though the smaller plan is the smaller invoice.

process.title: Review at eight weeks and stop when done
process.description: Repeat the diagnostic paper, compare the two scripts, and decide: continue, change focus, change tutor, or finish. Finishing is a real outcome and we will name it. Tutoring that outlives the problem it was bought to solve is the most expensive habit in this market.

whyPoints.title: Every figure attributed, in dirhams
whyPoints.description: The rates on this page are other providers' published numbers, named so you can check them, in the currency you actually pay in. Three of six researched competitor pages publish no price at all and two quote in dollars, which is not a comparison a UAE family can use.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the gap, not to the aspiration
whyPoints.description: If the diagnostic says a DP1 student needs quadratic manipulation rather than Paper 3 technique, we match to a tutor at the rate that work deserves. Selling the specialist band for elementary consolidation is the easiest upsell in tutoring and the least defensible.

whyPoints.title: No travel premium, because there is no travel
whyPoints.description: Lessons run one-to-one online over live video. IB Gram does not visit UAE homes; home visits are offered only in India. Published in-home rates run AED 180-500 an hour against AED 150-300 online, and the gap funds a journey rather than a lesson.

whyPoints.title: Blocks that end
whyPoints.description: The Exploration block is three to five sessions and then stops. The examination intensive has a finish date agreed before it starts. An arrangement with no end point is a subscription, and families usually discover they have one when they stop looking at the invoice.

whyPoints.title: The academic-honesty line is published
whyPoints.description: A tutor questions a topic, teaches the criteria and gives feedback on drafts the student has written. Nobody drafts an Exploration. The market contains operations selling completed Internal Assessments, and the risk of buying one falls on the student's Diploma rather than on the seller.

whyPoints.title: Scarcity named rather than exploited
whyPoints.description: Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level is thinner than Analysis, and February and March are tight in every course. We say so, give a date, or decline, instead of filling a slot with someone who does not teach the course.

faqs.question: What should we budget per month for IB maths help in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Published market estimates for one weekly hour run roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 for a qualified subject tutor, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support. Advertised packages confirm the shape, with around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. Those are other providers' figures, cited as the market. Our own number follows a free trial and a conversation about the course and level, because quoting before that is guesswork.

faqs.question: Why would an online session cost less than a tutor coming to Al Khalidiyah?
faqs.answer: Because the in-home price includes a journey. Published in-home one-to-one rates across Abu Dhabi and Dubai run AED 180 to 500 an hour, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor. The difference funds a car, a parking space and roughly forty minutes of someone's evening in each direction. In a dense part of the island it also funds variance: late starts, moved sessions and eventually a missed week. None of that is teaching.

faqs.question: Is a top-band examiner-track tutor worth AED 650 an hour for our DP1 son?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly not at DP1. That band makes sense for narrow late-stage work, typically a DP2 student polishing Paper 3 technique weeks before the papers. If the diagnostic shows the real problem is algebraic manipulation that never became automatic in Year 10, the work needed is patient and elementary, and the mid-market band does it better because the tutor is not bored by it. Match the rate to the diagnosed gap. We will say when the cheaper option is the right one.

faqs.question: Does a group maths class save money for a student with one weak topic?
faqs.answer: Usually not, despite the lower headline rate. A group moves at a shared pace, so if your child's gap is integration by substitution, that topic gets a few minutes of an hour while the rest covers material they already hold. Families often work this out in month three, having paid for twelve hours and received perhaps ninety minutes of relevant teaching. Group classes are genuinely good value for broad revision across a whole cohort, and poor value for one diagnosed hole.

faqs.question: How much of the IB maths grade is decided before the exams?
faqs.answer: A fifth. The Mathematical Exploration carries 20 per cent at both Higher and Standard Level, and it is produced during DP1 or early DP2. It is marked out of 20 across five criteria, with Use of Mathematics worth six marks, Presentation four, Mathematical Communication four, Personal Engagement three and Reflection three. That means a student can walk into the examination hall having already secured or lost a significant slice of the result, which is the strongest argument for spending early rather than late.

faqs.question: Our daughter picked Applications to avoid algebra. Was that a saving?
faqs.answer: Rarely. Applications and Interpretation is calculator-active and built on statistics, probability and modelling, which suits some students very well, but it is not the lighter course. Its mark schemes reward an interpretive sentence saying what a number means in context, and students who chose it to escape algebra often need more written coaching than they expected. At Higher Level it adds matrices, graph theory and numerically solved differential equations. Check the published entry requirements of target universities too, since engineering and economics routes commonly specify Analysis.

faqs.question: What exactly does Paper 3 add at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent of the grade and a component with no Standard Level equivalent. Paper 3 is two extended problem-solving questions, each developing a situation across several parts, which means an early mistake can cost a cascade of marks downstream. The skill of carrying a result forward under time pressure is not built by topic worksheets; it needs full-length timed questions, marked and discussed. That is why Higher Level support is usually bought as a concentrated block before mocks rather than spread thinly.

faqs.question: When is the cheapest time in the two years to start maths support?
faqs.answer: Late in the MYP or at the start of DP1, and it costs the least because what you buy is small. Two or three diagnostic sessions establish whether Analysis or Applications fits and whether Higher Level is realistic. Correcting a wrong course choice in DP1 costs a term of catch-up at higher rates, and discovering it in DP2 may cost a university option. The most expensive pattern is eighteen months of nothing followed by three sessions a week from February.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Exploration without crossing a line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the line is specific. A tutor may question the proposed topic until the student's own idea is workable, warn that a planned data set will not support the analysis, teach what each criterion rewards, and give feedback on a draft the student wrote. A tutor may not pick the title, supply the data, draft paragraphs or edit the work until the words are theirs. The test: could the student explain every sentence and decision as their own? Reflection and engagement marks collapse otherwise.

faqs.question: Are the Dubai school fee figures relevant to an Abu Dhabi budget?
faqs.answer: Only as context, not as a number to plan with. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that Dubai private school fees would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under an incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. KHDA regulates Dubai. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with ADEK, which supervises licensing and accreditation in this emirate and handles fee matters separately. Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah approve fees through their own authorities. Reading a Dubai measure as a UAE-wide fact is a common budgeting error.

faqs.question: Which maths course is hardest to find a tutor for at short notice?
faqs.answer: Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level, particularly for Paper 3, and anything at all during February and March when every DP2 cohort wants the same weeks. Analysis and Approaches at both levels is the best-covered course in the catalogue, which means a family has real choice and should not accept the top of the market by default. If we cannot staff a request properly we give a dated waiting slot, state a limitation plainly, or decline.

faqs.question: Does moving the session later in the evening change what we pay?
faqs.answer: It changes who is available, which is what moves a rate. An Al Khalidiyah student who can work at seven or eight in the evening Gulf Standard Time draws on a wide pool, because several time zones overlap with an Abu Dhabi evening. A student restricted to seven in the morning before school draws on a narrow one, and narrow pools price higher. Flexibility on the hour is the one lever families rarely realise they hold, and it is worth more than negotiating.

faqs.question: How do we tell whether the money is working?
faqs.answer: By repeating the measure you set at the start. A timed past paper in week one, marked against the published scheme rather than impressionistically, and the same style of paper at week eight. Between them, a short written note after each session and an error log so the same mistake is not paid for twice. If the second script has not moved, either the plan targeted the wrong gap or the match is wrong. Both are fixable, and both are our problem to fix.

faqs.question: If we spend at the very top of the market, can a final grade be promised?
faqs.answer: No, and anyone who says otherwise is selling something they cannot deliver. A grade depends on the student's work across two years, on the Exploration, on three or two papers sat in one window, and on grade boundaries nobody controls. What tutoring can reliably do is close diagnosed content gaps, rebuild examination technique and recover the marks lost to process rather than ignorance, which for most students is a meaningful number. Promises beyond that are marketing, and the UAE market has plenty of them.

Send us the course, the level and the hours that work, take the free trial lesson with no card required, and we will tell you honestly whether the answer is a short Exploration block, one weekly session, or nothing at all. Lessons run one-to-one online over live video in Gulf Standard Time, and every rate quoted on this page names its source.

intro.heading: The Diploma day in Al Manaseer does not finish at half past three
paragraphs: Parents planning maths tuition for a Diploma student usually plan around the school day. In Al Manaseer that produces a timetable nobody can keep, because the Diploma day is longer than the school day and the difference lands exactly where a tutoring slot wants to sit. Creativity, Activity, Service is a programme requirement, not an optional extra, and in practice it means two or three afternoons a week committed to something that finishes after everyone else has gone home.

Al Manaseer itself sits on the western side of Abu Dhabi island, between Al Khalidiyah and Al Bateen with the Corniche a few streets north. Diploma students here mostly travel: to campuses in Al Bateen and on the western island, east into Al Mushrif, or further to Bloom Gardens, Al Reem Island and the Al Raha corridor. A school day ending at 3.20pm plus a 4.30pm finish at a training session plus a twenty-five minute drive puts a Year 12 student through the door at about 5.15pm, three days out of five.

That is why the useful question is not when does school end but when is the student actually free, fed and able to think. For most Al Manaseer Diploma households the honest answer is 7pm on CAS days and 6pm on the others, with one weekend morning available for anything long. A tutoring plan built on 5pm sessions will hold for a fortnight and then start shedding weeks, and the cost of that is not the missed hour. It is the loss of continuity in a cumulative subject during the one year that cannot absorb it.

In-home tuition struggles with this more than families expect. A tutor arriving at a flat in Al Manaseer for a 7pm start has crossed the island in the same traffic, and that journey reaches you either as a higher rate, with in-home one-to-one quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour in this market against AED 150 to 300 online, or as a two-hour minimum nobody needs at that time of night. A late slot is also the one most likely to be moved by a tutor with a long drive home.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Visits to a family's address are a service we run only in India. Every Al Manaseer maths lesson is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, which is precisely what makes a 7pm Tuesday slot stable across a whole Diploma year. The rest of this page is about what to put in that slot: where the maths marks actually sit, which deadlines collide and when, and what a session should look like for a student who got home at a quarter past five.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-manaseer.subjectsIntro: A maths tutor working with an Al Manaseer Diploma student is dealing with specific components rather than the subject in general. These are the ones that determine the grade.

subjects.name: Analysis and Approaches, Higher Level
subjects.description: Proof, complex numbers, vectors, differential equations and Maclaurin series on top of the full function and calculus toolkit. Three papers plus the exploration. The scarcest teaching skill in Abu Dhabi, and the course most exposed by a tutor who covers maths generally rather than this syllabus specifically.

subjects.name: Analysis and Approaches, Standard Level
subjects.description: Functions, trigonometry, sequences, differentiation and integration with a lighter statistics component. Two papers plus the exploration. The recurring problem is a student who chose this course for a prerequisite and whose instincts are applied rather than formal.

subjects.name: Applications and Interpretation, Higher Level
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics, graph theory, matrices and complex numbers in applied settings, with technology assumed throughout. Three papers plus the exploration. Marks go to justified modelling choices rather than to correct calculator output, which is the distinction students most often miss.

subjects.name: Applications and Interpretation, Standard Level
subjects.description: Statistics, financial maths, two-variable modelling and introductory calculus. Two papers plus the exploration. A serious course rather than a soft option, where the marks sit in interpreting regression and chi-squared results correctly.

subjects.name: Paper 1, non-calculator
subjects.description: Sat without technology at both levels, and the component Abu Dhabi students most consistently underperform because school practice is calculator-rich. Exact-value trigonometry, surds, logarithm laws and by-hand differentiation are trained motor skills, and they are the cheapest marks on the table.

subjects.name: Paper 2, calculator
subjects.description: Technology permitted, longer questions, and the component where method marks disappear into unshown working. Graphical calculator fluency is assumed, including solving numerically and reading intersections, and most students have never been taught it deliberately.

subjects.name: Paper 3, extended response
subjects.description: Two long investigative questions worth 20% of the Higher Level grade, built to test whether a student can follow an unfamiliar mathematical thread under pressure. It cannot be revised topic by topic; it is trained by sitting whole papers and dissecting how the questions are built.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.description: Independent mathematical writing worth 20% of the grade, marked against criteria A to E covering presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. A tutor teaches the criteria and questions the mathematics. No tutor may write any part of it.

subjects.name: MYP to Diploma bridging
subjects.description: The specific gap between a comfortable MYP 5 student and a functioning Analysis and Approaches student: indices and surds, confident rearrangement, factor and remainder work, and function notation the Diploma assumes from week one. Eight weeks of summer work prevents a year of catch-up.

subjects.name: Graphical calculator technique
subjects.description: Solving equations numerically, finding intersections, working with distributions and using regression tools accurately under time pressure. Schools often assume this is picked up, and the result is students losing Paper 2 marks to a tool they own but cannot drive.

sections.heading: The real Al Manaseer Diploma week, hour by hour
paragraphs: A workable maths slot for an Al Manaseer Diploma student is 6pm on a clear day and 7pm on a day with an after-school commitment. That comes out of adding up the day rather than from any view about when teenagers concentrate. The school day ends between roughly 3.00pm and 3.30pm. Creativity, Activity, Service, which is a Diploma requirement rather than an optional extra, commonly runs to 4.30pm or 4.45pm two or three afternoons a week. Then the drive, eight minutes from Al Bateen and up to forty from the Al Raha corridor.

The table sets out what that produces across a typical week. The point is the pattern rather than the precise minutes: a Diploma student in this neighbourhood has roughly two evenings that are genuinely free before six and three that are not, and which evenings those are changes each term as CAS commitments rotate. A fixed slot therefore needs to be placed at the time that works on the worst day, not the best one.

This is where a late online slot does something an in-home arrangement cannot. A tutor driving to Al Manaseer for 7pm is making the same island crossing the family just made and then making it again at eight, and a tutor with a long journey home is the one most likely to ask to move a late session. Market in-home rates of AED 180 to 500 an hour in the UAE exist because that time has to be paid for. Removing the journey entirely means the slot can sit at the hour the household actually needs and stay there for the year.
