sections.heading: Where the Diploma maths marks actually are
paragraphs: Families spend tutoring money on topics and the grade is decided by components. Knowing which component carries what is the difference between a plan that moves a grade and a plan that fills evenings, and it takes five minutes to establish.

At Standard Level there are two papers plus the exploration. At Higher Level there are three plus the exploration. The exploration is worth 20% of the final grade at both levels, which makes it the single largest assessed item in the subject and the one most students treat as an administrative task. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator at both levels and in both courses, which is the detail most often missed, because almost all school practice happens with technology to hand.

The consequence for an Al Manaseer student with one weekly hour is a question of allocation. A full term spent on content revision while Paper 1 technique and the exploration go untouched is a term spent on the smaller problem. The table lays out the components and what each actually needs, and the pattern that emerges is consistent: the cheapest marks in Diploma maths are in non-calculator fluency and in the exploration, and both are routinely left until the term in which neither can be fixed. Ask your child which paper is the non-calculator one and watch what happens. A student who hesitates has not yet been taught the shape of their own assessment, and that is a ten-minute conversation worth having before the next fifty hours of tuition are planned around it.

sections.heading: The exploration deadline lands in the most crowded month of the year
paragraphs: Diploma students in Abu Dhabi rarely fail maths because the mathematics defeated them. They lose marks because the exploration was written in the same fortnight as three other internal assessments, a university application and a mock timetable, and something had to give. The exploration is what gives, because it is the only one with no immediate external consequence and it is worth 20%.

The collision is predictable, which means it is avoidable. School-set internal deadlines for Diploma assessments cluster in the autumn and early winter of Year 13. The Extended Essay has its own milestones in the same window. University applications for overseas destinations sit there too, and UAE applications arrive on a different calendar again. Any family that writes these dates on one sheet in September can see the pinch point two months before it arrives.

The maths response to that is specific: get the exploration's mathematics done early, while it is still only competing with ordinary coursework. The mark is largely set by the topic chosen and the depth of mathematics available in it, both of which are decided in the first fortnight of the process. Two short sessions at that stage, interrogating two or three candidate topics for genuine mathematical depth, is worth more than six sessions in the week before submission. The table shows how the deadlines usually collide and where the maths hour should go in each phase. Put the sheet on a wall rather than in a phone. The point of writing the deadlines down is that two adults and a teenager can all see the same pinch point at the same time, which is what turns an argument in November into a plan made in September.

sections.heading: What a maths hour looks like for a student who got home at 5.15pm
paragraphs: A 7pm session on a CAS day is a different proposition from a 4pm session in a free afternoon, and a tutor who does not adjust for that is wasting the slot a family fought to protect. The student in front of them has been awake since six, sat a full Diploma timetable, spent ninety minutes at a commitment they are assessed on, and travelled across an island.

What works is narrow and specific. Open with three or four minutes of something already secure, to get the mathematics moving before anything unfamiliar arrives. One objective for the hour, named at the start, so the student knows what they are being asked to achieve. The tutor writing while explaining, on a shared screen the student can reopen in March, because retention from a tired listening session is poor and retention from a document is not.

What does not work is volume. Ninety minutes at seven in the evening produces less than sixty does, and a two-hour block after a CAS day is mostly endurance. If a household wants more time in the week, the better answer is a weekend morning for the long tasks rather than a longer weeknight. A tutor who proposes two hours on a Tuesday for a Year 13 with a Diploma timetable is either not paying attention or is selling hours, and either way the second hour is the most expensive unproductive time a family buys. The same applies to how the hour ends. Two minutes stating what was achieved and what the next session will do is worth more than two minutes of extra content, because it is the part the student can repeat to a parent afterwards.
bullets: Open with something secure before anything new arrives
One named objective per hour, stated at the start
The tutor writes on a shared screen the student keeps
Sixty minutes outperforms ninety on a CAS evening
Long tasks belong on a weekend morning, not a late weeknight

sections.heading: Bridging from IGCSE maths into Analysis and Approaches
paragraphs: A good proportion of Al Manaseer Diploma students arrive from IGCSE rather than from the Middle Years Programme, and the transition into Analysis and Approaches is steeper than their Year 11 grade suggests. An IGCSE Extended or Higher student who scored well can still be missing exactly the fluency the Diploma assumes from the first week, because the two qualifications reward different things.

The specific gaps recur. Index laws with negative and fractional powers, used confidently rather than recalled. Surd manipulation without a calculator. Algebraic rearrangement where the unknown appears twice. Factor and remainder work. Function notation, composite and inverse functions, treated as ordinary rather than as a new topic. Trigonometric exact values. None of these is advanced mathematics, and all of them are assumed background in a Diploma lesson in week three.

Which means the right time to address them is the summer between Year 11 and Year 12, not the autumn of Year 12 when the course has already moved on. Six to eight sessions over the summer, delivered online wherever the family is travelling, is the single highest-return maths purchase available to an Al Manaseer household. It is also the one most reliably cancelled, because summers are for travelling and nobody feels the cost until November, by which point the student is being taught new content on top of a foundation that was never finished. There is a useful diagnostic for this. Ask the student to simplify an expression with a fractional negative index, without a calculator, in under a minute. A Year 12 who cannot is not short of Diploma teaching; they are short of Year 10 fluency, and no amount of new content will fix that.
bullets: Negative and fractional indices used fluently, not recalled
Surds handled without a calculator
Rearrangement where the unknown appears more than once
Composite and inverse functions treated as routine
Exact-value trigonometry known rather than looked up

sections.heading: The exploration boundary, stated before anyone pays for anything
paragraphs: The exploration is 20% of the maths grade and the one place where buying the wrong kind of help can end a Diploma rather than improve it. The boundary comes from IB academic-honesty rules, it is not a matter of taste, and it should be said in plain language before a first session rather than discovered afterwards.

A tutor may teach the five criteria and what each rewards, with the mark allocations named. A tutor may discuss candidate topics and press hard on whether the mathematics inside them reaches the higher bands. A tutor may teach mathematics the exploration requires, which is often slightly beyond the taught course. A tutor may question a method, point at an unjustified step, ask why a model was chosen, and give written feedback on a draft the student wrote.

No tutor may write any part of the exploration, supply text to be pasted in, restructure a student's prose into their own, or produce the mathematics for a student to transcribe. Bought-in work is malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student rather than on whoever sold it. There is a visible market in completed Internal Assessments in this region, advertised at four-figure dirham prices. Any provider should be willing to state its position on this in writing, and a provider who will not is telling you something. Say the boundary to your child as well as hearing it from the tutor. A student who knows exactly which kinds of help are legitimate asks for them earlier and uses them better; one who is unsure tends either to ask for nothing or to accept something they should not have.
bullets: Criteria A to E taught explicitly with their mark allocations
Topic depth interrogated while the topic can still change
Written feedback on drafts the student has written
Nothing written, supplied or restructured on the student's behalf

sections.heading: Ramadan, travel and the weeks a Diploma cannot afford to lose
paragraphs: Three predictable interruptions hit an Al Manaseer Diploma year, and each one costs more than the sessions it removes because restarting a cumulative subject is slower than continuing it. Planning for all three in September is a twenty-minute job that saves a term.

Ramadan shortens the school day across the UAE and shifts household energy to the evening. A session that sat at 7pm often works better after iftar, and shorter more frequent sessions suit a shortened day better than one long block. For a Year 13 this is not a month to drop out of, because the gap between Ramadan and the May session is short and the exploration deadline may sit nearby. Agreeing the replacement slot in advance beats cancelling week by week.

The other two are travel and the winter break. Al Manaseer households travel, often between Abu Dhabi and somewhere else at short notice, and an in-home arrangement cancels every time. An online session follows the student, so the only adjustment is a time zone. The winter break lands shortly after mocks, which makes it either the most valuable fortnight of Year 13, spent dissecting scripts while they are still warm, or a complete loss. Which of those it becomes is decided in November, not in December. Book the winter-break sessions in November while there is still capacity. Every Diploma family in Abu Dhabi wants the same fortnight, and the specialists who are free in December are the ones nobody asked in November.
bullets: Move the slot after iftar during Ramadan rather than pausing
Online sessions follow the family when they travel
The fortnight after mocks is the highest-value break of Year 13
A cumulative subject does not forgive a four-week gap in the spring

sections.heading: ADEK, tutor permits and what to ask a maths tutor specifically
paragraphs: Private schools in Abu Dhabi are licensed and inspected by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Private tutoring is a separate matter, regulated federally: an individual giving private lessons in the UAE needs a private tuition work permit from MoHRE, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years.

Eligibility is broad. Registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18 may all apply, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Working without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since no fine schedule has been published, any specific figure quoted online is unverified. One restriction is worth naming in Abu Dhabi: ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a comparable condition.

For a maths tutor specifically, two further questions are worth more than the permit. Which course and level have you actually taught, named precisely as Analysis and Approaches Higher Level rather than as IB maths? And what do you do with the exploration? A tutor who answers the first question with a precise count of cohorts and the second with a clear account of the honesty boundary is demonstrating exactly what you are buying. For completeness, IB Gram holds no ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, Ministry, IB, Cambridge or Pearson accreditation, partnership or licence, and no school on this page is a client or a partner.

faqs.question: How late can a maths session start for a Diploma student living in Al Manaseer?
faqs.answer: Seven in the evening works for most households and is often the only hour that does. A Diploma day ends between 3.00pm and 3.30pm, Creativity, Activity, Service commitments commonly run to 4.30pm or 4.45pm two or three afternoons a week, and the drive back ranges from eight minutes within Al Bateen to forty from the Al Raha corridor. That puts a student home at a quarter past five or later on the busy days. The fixed slot should be placed at the time that works on the worst day of the week rather than the best.

faqs.question: Does CAS really affect how much maths tutoring is practical?
faqs.answer: More than families expect. Creativity, Activity, Service is a Diploma requirement rather than an optional extra, and in practice it commits two or three afternoons a week to something that finishes after the ordinary school day. Those commitments also rotate each term, so the evening that was free in September may not be free in January. The practical response is to place the weekly slot at the hour that survives a CAS day, and to review the slot each term rather than discovering in week three that it no longer fits.

faqs.question: Will a tutor travel to our building in Al Manaseer for Diploma maths?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Visits to a family's address are a service we offer only in India, and we do not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE. Other Abu Dhabi providers do, and market rates for in-home one-to-one sit at AED 180 to 500 an hour because the figure absorbs the journey. For a late Diploma slot that journey is also a stability problem, since a tutor with a long drive home is the one most likely to ask to move a 7pm session. Al Manaseer lessons run one-to-one over live video.

faqs.question: Which part of the maths grade should we be spending the weekly hour on?
faqs.answer: Start from the components rather than the topics. The exploration is worth 20% of the grade at both Standard and Higher Level, which makes it the largest single assessed item, and Paper 1 is sat without a calculator in both courses and at both levels, which is where Abu Dhabi students most consistently underperform because school practice is calculator-rich. At Higher Level, Paper 3 adds another 20% and cannot be revised topic by topic. A term of general content revision while those three go untouched is a term spent on the smaller problem.

faqs.question: Why does the exploration always get written in the worst week of the year?
faqs.answer: Because its deadline sits in the same window as several subject internal assessments, Extended Essay milestones and university applications, and it is the only one of those with no immediate external consequence. So it is the one that slips. The collision is predictable rather than unlucky: write every internal deadline on one sheet in September and the pinch point is visible two months ahead. The response for maths is to complete the exploration's mathematics early, while it is competing only with ordinary coursework rather than with everything at once.

faqs.question: How early should we interrogate the exploration topic?
faqs.answer: In the first fortnight of the process, because that is when the mark ceiling is set. Most of an exploration's mark comes from the topic chosen and the depth of mathematics genuinely available inside it, and once a student has invested three weeks in a thin topic almost nobody changes it. Two short sessions testing two or three candidate topics for real mathematical depth is worth more than six sessions the week before submission, and it costs a fraction as much. By the final week a tutor is reading a finished piece whose ceiling is already fixed.

faqs.question: Our child did well at IGCSE maths but is struggling in Year 12. What is missing?
faqs.answer: Almost always fluency rather than understanding. An IGCSE Extended or Higher student can score well and still lack what a Diploma lesson assumes in week three: negative and fractional indices used confidently, surds handled by hand, rearrangement where the unknown appears twice, factor and remainder work, composite and inverse functions treated as routine, and exact-value trigonometry known rather than looked up. None of that is advanced. All of it is assumed background. Six to eight sessions over the summer between Year 11 and Year 12 closes it far more cheaply than the autumn of Year 12 does.

faqs.question: Is sixty minutes enough for Higher Level maths, or should we book longer?
faqs.answer: Sixty is usually better on a weeknight, and the reason is the Diploma day rather than the subject. A student who has been awake since six, sat a full timetable, spent ninety minutes at a CAS commitment and travelled across the island is not going to produce two productive hours at seven in the evening. Concentration on abstract mathematics degrades noticeably after about seventy-five minutes. If more time is needed, a weekend morning for exploration work or a whole paper does far more than extending a late weeknight session.

faqs.question: What can a maths tutor legitimately do with the exploration?
faqs.answer: Teach the five criteria and what each rewards, with the mark allocations named. Discuss candidate topics and press on whether the mathematics in them reaches the higher bands. Teach mathematics the exploration needs, including material slightly beyond the taught course. Question a method, point at an unjustified step, ask why a model was chosen, and give written feedback on a draft the student wrote. What no tutor may do is write any part of it, supply text, restructure the prose, or produce mathematics for the student to copy. Bought-in work is malpractice and the student carries the consequence.

faqs.question: How do I check a tutor really teaches Analysis and Approaches rather than maths in general?
faqs.answer: Ask two precise questions and listen for precision back. First, which course and level have you taught, named as Analysis and Approaches Higher Level or Applications and Interpretation Standard Level rather than as IB maths, and how many cohorts? Second, which paper is sat without a calculator, and what does Paper 3 actually ask of a student? A tutor who answers those cleanly, and who can describe where students lose marks in each, is demonstrating the thing you are buying. General talk about experience and rapport answers a different question.

faqs.question: Should Diploma maths tutoring pause during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: It should move rather than pause. The school day shortens across the UAE and household rhythm shifts towards the evening, so a session that sat at 7pm often works better after iftar, and shorter more frequent sessions suit a shortened day better than one long block. For a Year 13 this is a poor month to drop out of, because the interval between Ramadan and the May session is short and an exploration deadline may sit nearby. Agreeing the replacement slot in advance works much better than cancelling week by week and intending to catch up.

faqs.question: Can lessons continue while we are out of Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for Al Manaseer households this is one of the stronger practical arguments for online delivery. Families here travel, sometimes at short notice, and an in-home arrangement cancels every time. A live video session follows the student, so the only adjustment is the time zone. Over a long summer most families thin sessions out rather than stopping, because the fluency a Diploma course assumes is the first thing to decay in a ten-week gap, and a Year 12 who stops entirely returns weaker in exactly the algebra the autumn will demand.

faqs.question: Which IB campuses do your Al Manaseer maths students attend?
faqs.answer: Diploma students from the western island mostly travel to IB campuses on Al Reem Island, Saadiyat Island and along the Al Raha corridor, with some at schools closer to Al Bateen. The names that come up include Repton School Abu Dhabi, GEMS World Academy Abu Dhabi, Cranleigh Abu Dhabi, Raha International School and the American Community School of Abu Dhabi. Those are given to describe the local education map only. IB Gram has no affiliation, partnership or endorsement relationship with any of them, and none is a client.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in Abu Dhabi need a licence, and does it say anything about quality?
faqs.answer: They need a permit, and it says nothing about quality. An individual giving private lessons in the UAE requires a private tuition work permit from MoHRE, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Registered teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18 may all apply, and MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day turnaround. Treat it as a legal floor. No UAE regulator approves individual tutors on teaching merit, so approved tutors claims deserve scepticism.

faqs.question: When will we know whether the maths hour is achieving anything?
faqs.answer: At six weeks, against school evidence rather than impressions. By then there should be a written gap list from the first session in syllabus language, saved worked solutions from every session since, practice chosen against named weaknesses rather than chapters, and at least one timed component attempted. Set those beside the most recent school assessment and the picture is usually clear. If none of those artefacts exists, nobody can tell you in March whether February's hours achieved anything, which is the position most families find themselves in.

intro.heading: The school run decides the maths lesson before anyone talks about maths
paragraphs: Al Maryah Island holds Abu Dhabi Global Market, The Galleria, Cleveland Clinic Abu Dhabi and a cluster of residential towers inside roughly half a square kilometre. What it does not hold is a school. Every child living here leaves the island each morning and comes back across a bridge each afternoon, and that single fact governs the shape of a tutoring week more than any argument about teaching method.

Work it through. A school on Al Reem Island finishing at 3.15pm puts a student back in a Maryah tower by around 3.45pm. The same finish time at a Saadiyat or Yas school, with a pickup queue and a longer run, lands between 4.15pm and 5pm. Add two afternoons of sport or music and the number of weekday slots where a sixty-minute maths lesson can start and finish before the evening collapses is smaller than parents assume when they begin looking.

An in-home tutor has to fit inside that same window having travelled from wherever they live, which in this emirate usually means Khalifa City, Al Reef or Mohammed Bin Zayed City. A forty-minute mainland run to the island at half past four is a guess rather than a schedule, and a session that starts fifteen minutes late still costs the full hour. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE — that is an India-only service — so the constraint is removed rather than managed. The tutor is present at the agreed minute and the student walks from the kitchen to a desk.

That matters more in maths than in most subjects, because maths tutoring works on momentum. A student who is tired, late and twenty minutes into a session before they have written anything will not get through a calculus problem properly, and the hour becomes revision of the previous week. Protecting the start time is a maths-specific gain, not a convenience argument.

There is a second timetabling point that only matters in maths. A maths lesson needs the student to write, which means a surface, a pen and a camera that can see the paper. A child who has just come off a bridge, eaten nothing and been handed a laptop on a sofa is not set up to do calculus. Thirty minutes between arrival and the session, and a table rather than a bed, are worth more than most of the things a tutoring page would sell you.

The rest of this page is the maths itself: the route decision between Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, what each paper is worth at Higher and Standard Level, the topics where marks reliably disappear, how the individual exploration is actually marked criterion by criterion, when in the two Diploma years each kind of work belongs, and what the Abu Dhabi market charges for each of those purchases in AED. Read it and you will know what to ask any maths tutor in this city before you book a single hour, including us.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-maryah-is.programmesIntro: Maths support looks different at each stage of an IB education, and the step a family on Al Maryah Island feels most is the one into the Diploma. These are the stages in play.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme mathematics
programmes.description: MYP maths is assessed against four criteria — knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts — each marked out of 8 and converted to a 1 to 7 grade by school-set boundaries. There are no timed external papers unless the school enters eAssessment, so students arrive in the Diploma fluent in investigation and inexperienced at speed.
programmes.countryNote: This is the step Al Maryah Island families most often fund. An MYP Year 11 student used to extended investigations meets DP1 papers sat under timing with a formula booklet and a graphic display calculator, and discovers the difference in October. Six to eight online sessions across the spring of Year 11 handles it cheaply; the same gap addressed in DP1 costs more and arrives later.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Every Diploma student takes one maths course from Group 5, choosing between Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, at Higher or Standard Level. Standard Level sits two papers; Higher Level sits three, with the extra paper consisting of extended multi-part problem solving. An individual exploration, the Internal Assessment, carries roughly a fifth of the final grade in every combination.
programmes.countryNote: Most Al Maryah Island Diploma students sit the May session, which is the one Abu Dhabi schools enter. IB exam and results dates are set and occasionally revised by the IB, and we do not publish them here — confirm every date with your school's IB coordinator. The dates that actually drive a maths term are your school's internal deadlines for the exploration, which usually fall well before anything external.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme with a DP maths course
programmes.description: A Career-related Programme student takes at least two Diploma courses alongside a career-related study, and maths is frequently one of them. The course is assessed identically to the full Diploma version, with the same papers and the same exploration, so nothing about the maths teaching changes.
programmes.countryNote: The tutoring need here is narrow: one maths course to a defensible grade, usually Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level, plus structural help on the reflective project. A single-subject request is exactly where a national online pool beats a local one, because one course a week is not enough work to interest a resident generalist.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-maryah-is.subjectsIntro: These are the parts of IB mathematics Al Maryah Island families ask about, with the specific place marks go in each. Both routes and both levels are covered.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL
subjects.description: Algebra, functions, trigonometry, calculus and proof at depth, with Paper 3 adding two long investigative problems. Marks go on structure: students who have practised only short questions lose the thread by part (c).

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches SL
subjects.description: The same analytical spine with less breadth and two papers. The commonest loss is differentiation and integration applied in context rather than performed in isolation, and poor presentation of working.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation HL
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics, graph theory and technology-led problem solving, with Paper 3 built around extended data-handling tasks. The calculator is central, and unexplained calculator answers earn a fraction of the marks available.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation SL
subjects.description: Statistics, financial maths, functions and modelling across two papers. Students lose marks by reporting a statistical result without interpreting it in the context the question established.

subjects.name: The Mathematics Internal Assessment
subjects.description: A personal exploration of twelve to twenty pages, marked on presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics. Weak explorations are usually weak on reflection and on mathematics appropriate to the level.

subjects.name: Calculus
subjects.description: Limits, differentiation, integration, kinematics and differential equations at HL. The reliable loss is chain, product and quotient rules in combination, and integration by substitution attempted without first naming the substitution.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.description: Distributions, hypothesis testing, correlation, regression and, at AI HL, more advanced inference. Marks go on using the right test and on stating hypotheses and conclusions in the context given rather than generically.

subjects.name: Functions and modelling
subjects.description: Transformations, exponentials, logarithms, rational and piecewise functions and fitting models to data. The common failure is finding a model with technology and never justifying why that model rather than another.

subjects.name: Proof and reasoning
subjects.description: Direct proof, contradiction, induction and counterexample. Induction questions are highly structured and highly learnable, and students who drill the structure recover marks quickly where they previously scored nothing.

subjects.name: Graphic display calculator technique
subjects.description: The calculator is examined, not merely permitted. Students lose marks through unset modes, unrecorded commands and answers given without the model that produced them. One session on technique often returns more marks than a topic re-teach.

sections.heading: What the Al Maryah Island school run leaves you to work with
paragraphs: A maths session is worth what the student brings to it, and what they bring depends on how long ago they got out of a car. The island's geography makes this unusually sharp: there is no school on Al Maryah Island, so the afternoon always contains a bridge crossing. The question is how long one.

From Al Reem Island the crossing is short and a student can be at a desk by four o'clock, alert. From Saadiyat or Yas the same bell lands them home between a quarter past four and five, after a queue and a longer drive, and the first twenty minutes of any lesson starting immediately is spent recovering. From the Khalifa City belt the day is effectively over before a session could usefully begin.

The practical answer is to set the slot from arrival time plus thirty minutes, not from the school's finish. That looks like a small scheduling nicety and it is worth real marks in maths, because maths is the subject where a tired start compounds: a student who mislays a sign in the first ten minutes spends the next thirty finding it. Across a term of weekly sessions, the difference between a well-placed slot and an optimistic one is several hours of usable teaching.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation
paragraphs: The most consequential maths decision in the Diploma is the route, and it is often made on a misunderstanding. Analysis and Approaches is not the clever course and Applications and Interpretation is not the easy one. They are different mathematics. AA is algebraic and proof-oriented, built on calculus and manipulation. AI is modelling and statistical, built on using technology to make sense of data. Both exist at Higher and Standard Level, and AI HL is a demanding course that many students find harder than AA SL.

The decision should be made on two things: what the student is good at, and what their intended degree requires. A student who enjoys a clean algebraic argument and dislikes open-ended data work belongs in AA. A student who reasons well about real quantities and finds abstract manipulation thankless belongs in AI. Both are respectable, and a grade 6 in the right route is worth more than a grade 4 in the prestigious one.

University requirements are the hard constraint. Engineering, physics, mathematics and economics programmes frequently specify Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and some will not accept AI for those courses at all. Business, social science, design and many life-science programmes accept either. Requirements vary by institution and change, so the correct action is to read the admissions page for the specific universities on the student's list rather than to rely on a general rule, including this one.
If the route is already fixed and wrong, say so early. A change in DP1 is a manageable piece of work; the same change in DP2 is not.

sections.heading: What each paper is worth, and what that changes
paragraphs: Students revise as though all marks are equal, and they are not. At Standard Level there are two papers and an exploration. At Higher Level there are three papers and an exploration, and the third paper behaves unlike anything else in the course: two long problems, heavily scaffolded, requiring a student to sustain a line of reasoning across many parts.

The practical consequence is about where revision time earns most. A Higher Level student who has never practised a complete Paper 3 under timing is leaving a meaningful share of the grade to chance, no matter how secure their topic knowledge is, because the skill being examined is endurance and structure rather than recall. Conversely a Standard Level student has no Paper 3 to worry about and should spend that time on calculator discipline and on presentation of working.

The exploration is the other underweighted component. It carries roughly a fifth of the grade in every route and level combination, it is marked internally against published criteria and moderated by the IB, and it is the one part of the course where a student has months rather than hours. Students who treat it as a side project lose marks that were entirely within their control.

Confirm exact weightings and component details against the current subject guide through your school, because the IB revises its courses on a cycle and published figures move. sections.heading: Where IB maths marks actually disappear
paragraphs: The useful diagnosis is not "weak at maths". It is a short list of repeating, nameable errors, and almost every student has four or five. A tutor's first job is to find them from marked scripts rather than to start at chapter one.

The most common, across both routes, is method marks lost to invisible working. A student reaches the right answer with three steps in their head and writes one line, and the mark scheme awards a fraction of the credit. This is free marks, it is pure habit, and it takes about three weeks of insistence to fix. The second is formula-booklet dependence without familiarity: the booklet is provided, but a student who does not know roughly where things are loses minutes per question hunting.

In Analysis and Approaches specifically, the recurring losses are calculus rules in combination — chain inside product, quotient with a trigonometric argument — and integration attempted without first naming the substitution. Proof by induction is worth separate mention because it is highly structured: students either score nearly everything or nearly nothing, and the fix is learning the structure rather than understanding induction more deeply.

In Applications and Interpretation, the recurring losses are statistical conclusions stated generically rather than in the context of the question, models produced by technology with no justification for the choice, and hypothesis tests run correctly but reported without hypotheses. All three are presentation failures rather than knowledge failures, which is why they respond quickly to targeted work.

sections.heading: The Mathematics exploration, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: The exploration is where the most tutoring confusion sits, so here is what it is and what help on it may look like. It is an individual piece of mathematical writing, typically twelve to twenty pages, on a topic the student chooses. It is marked against five published criteria covering presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection, and the use of mathematics, with the last carrying the most marks at both levels.

Weak explorations fail in predictable ways. The topic is too large, so the mathematics stays shallow. The mathematics sits below the level of the course, which caps the heaviest criterion regardless of how neat the rest is. Reflection is a concluding paragraph saying the student enjoyed the task rather than genuine commentary on what the mathematics showed and where it broke down. Notation is inconsistent. None of those are mysteries, and all of them are fixable at draft stage.

What a tutor may do: explain what each criterion rewards and in what proportion, question whether the chosen topic can carry mathematics at the right level, read the student's own draft and name which criterion it is underselling, teach correct notation and citation, and discuss the mathematics itself as mathematics. What a tutor may not do: choose the topic and hand it over, write or rewrite any part of the text, edit a draft to completion, supply data the student did not generate, or produce a model exploration for adaptation.

We explain that boundary to the student directly in the first session on the exploration, because the student signs the authenticity declaration and the consequence of a breach falls on them. It also produces better work: a student who has been questioned hard about their own mathematics writes a stronger reflection than one handed a polished paragraph.

sections.heading: Teaching maths over video into a Maryah tower
paragraphs: Maths is the subject most often assumed to need a person in the room, and in practice it adapts to video better than almost any other, provided one thing is right: the tutor must be able to see the student's handwritten working as it happens. A camera angled at paper, or a tablet and stylus, solves it. Without that the session degrades into dictation and nobody learns anything.

With it, video has genuine advantages for maths specifically. A shared whiteboard retains every derivation, so Tuesday's integration by parts can be reopened on Saturday instead of reconstructed from a notebook. The tutor can paste the exact past-paper question onto the board rather than describing it. Two routes can be shown side by side. And a student working on their own paper, in their own handwriting, is doing the thing the exam will ask of them rather than watching someone else do it.

An Al Maryah Island apartment supplies the rest. Fibre connectivity is standard in the island's towers, the building is quiet once the business district empties, and there is no visitor parking at The Galleria to arrange and no lift wait at five o'clock. What we ask for is a table rather than a bed, headphones, and that camera on the paper.

To be explicit, because this page targets a local maths-tutor search: IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. No tutor will travel to an Al Maryah Island address. sections.heading: What an IB maths tutor costs here, by what you actually buy
paragraphs: Rather than listing tiers, it is more useful to price the thing you are buying. The published market bands, read in October 2026, are these: budget online tutoring at AED 45 to 150 an hour, a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150 to 300, an in-home visit at AED 180 to 500, a named IB or A-Level specialist at AED 200 to 450 and above, and premium examiner-led provision reaching AED 650. Those are other providers' figures, not IB Gram's price list.

Map them onto maths purchases. A calculator-technique session or a working-presentation fix is short, defined and returns marks quickly — a handful of hours at the qualified band. A topic repair in calculus or inference is four to six sessions. Exploration coaching is three or four sessions spread across a term, timed to the school's internal deadline. Paper 3 work at Higher Level is a block in the final months. A full year of weekly route teaching is the largest commitment and the one that actually moves a grade.

The cheapest high-return item on that list is usually the presentation and calculator work, and it is the one nobody sells, because it is not impressive to advertise. The most expensive mistake is funding a full year of general maths hours when the real problem was four nameable errors and a calculator mode.

sections.heading: When in the term maths tutoring actually pays
paragraphs: Maths tutoring has a seasonality that families discover too late. The autumn term of DP1 is the cheapest and most effective moment to intervene, because the foundations being laid then are the ones every later topic sits on, and because the student has time to change a habit rather than patch a gap. Almost nobody buys tutoring then, because nothing has gone wrong yet.

The spring of DP1 is when the exploration should be chosen and begun, and three or four sessions placed there are worth more than ten placed in DP2 when the draft is due and the topic is already too small to carry the mathematics. Schools set their own internal deadlines for this, and those deadlines, not the external calendar, are what should drive the booking.

The autumn of DP2 is topic consolidation and the first serious past-paper work. The spring is paper technique, timing and error patterns, and at Higher Level it is when Paper 3 has to be practised as a complete paper rather than as questions. By the final four weeks the work should be nothing but timed papers and the correction of repeating errors; attempting to learn new content at that point is expensive and rarely recovers.

Ramadan falls inside the UAE academic calendar and shifts when revision realistically happens, and sessions commonly move to post-Iftar timing without losing the slot. Abu Dhabi schools enter the May session; IB dates are set by the IB and we do not restate them, so confirm every deadline with your school's IB coordinator and plan the maths term backwards from the school's own internal dates.

process.description: The test is external — the next school assessment or mock. If the same four errors are still there, we change the approach or the tutor rather than adding hours. That review is what keeps the spend a decision.

whyPoints.title: Route specialists, not maths generalists
whyPoints.description: AA and AI are different mathematics taught by different strengths. We match on the route and level your child sits, which is possible because delivery is online and the pool is not limited to people who can drive to Al Maryah Island.

whyPoints.title: Slots built from arrival time
whyPoints.description: We ask when your child is actually at a desk rather than when school ends, because on an island with no school the gap between those two is twenty minutes or an hour depending on the bridge.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis from marked scripts
whyPoints.description: The first session works from your child's own marked paper and produces a named list of repeating errors. Almost every maths problem is four or five nameable habits, not a general weakness.

whyPoints.title: A stated boundary on the exploration
whyPoints.description: We question, explain criteria and give feedback on the student's own draft. We do not choose the topic, write, rewrite or edit to completion, or supply a model exploration. The student signs the authenticity declaration.

whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no ADEK, KHDA, Ministry or IB approval or partnership, runs no UAE office, and publishes no self-generated success figures. Unsourced numbers are left off the page.

faqs.question: What time can an IB maths session realistically start on Al Maryah Island?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the school, because none of them are on the island. From a school on Al Reem Island, a 3.15pm finish puts a student at a desk by around four, so a 4.30pm maths slot works. From Saadiyat, with a pickup queue and a bridge, 5.30pm is the first honest option. From Yas Island or the Khalifa City belt, 6pm or later. We plan the slot from arrival time plus about thirty minutes rather than from the bell, because the first twenty minutes of a maths lesson started too soon are spent recovering from the car.

faqs.question: Is my child on the right IB maths route, AA or AI?
faqs.answer: Judge it on two things. Aptitude: a student who enjoys a clean algebraic argument belongs in Analysis and Approaches, one who reasons well about real quantities and finds abstract manipulation thankless belongs in Applications and Interpretation. And degree requirements: engineering, physics, mathematics and economics courses frequently specify AA at Higher Level, while business, social sciences and many life sciences accept either. Requirements vary by university and change, so read the admissions pages for the specific institutions on the list. A grade 6 in the right route beats a grade 4 in the prestigious one.

faqs.question: Should an Al Maryah Island student pick AI because it sounds gentler than AA?
faqs.answer: No, and the assumption causes real damage. AI is different mathematics, not reduced mathematics: modelling, statistics, inference and technology-led problem solving, with a Higher Level that many students find harder than AA at Standard Level. What AI asks for is comfort with real data, justified model choices and conclusions stated in context. What AA asks for is algebraic manipulation, calculus and proof. A student placed in AI because it sounded gentler, who then has to justify a regression model every other question, is not in an easier position.

faqs.question: What makes Paper 3 at Higher Level different from the other papers?
faqs.answer: It is two long multi-part investigations rather than a set of questions, and the skill it examines is sustaining a line of reasoning across many parts. Topic knowledge alone does not carry it: students who have practised only short questions lose structure around part (c) and never recover the thread. It has to be practised as a complete paper under timing, several times, which is why it belongs in a dedicated block in the final months rather than being folded into general revision. Standard Level students do not sit it and should spend that time on calculator discipline instead.

faqs.question: What share of the maths grade rests on the exploration rather than the papers?
faqs.answer: Roughly a fifth, in every route and level combination, and it is the component students most reliably under-invest in. It is an individual piece of mathematical writing, usually twelve to twenty pages, marked against five published criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection, and the use of mathematics. The last carries the most marks. Unlike a paper, the student has months rather than hours, which makes lost marks here entirely avoidable. Confirm the current weighting and criteria through your school, since the IB revises its subject guides on a cycle.

faqs.question: Why do explorations score badly even when they look neat?
faqs.answer: Usually for one of three reasons. The mathematics sits below the level of the course, which caps the heaviest criterion no matter how good the presentation is. The topic was too large, so nothing is explored in depth. Or the reflection is a closing paragraph saying the student enjoyed the work rather than genuine commentary on what the mathematics showed and where it broke down. All three are visible at draft stage and all three are fixable then. None of them are fixable in the week before the deadline, which is when most families first ask.

faqs.question: How far can a tutor go in helping with the Mathematics exploration?
faqs.answer: A tutor may explain what each criterion rewards, question whether the chosen topic can carry mathematics at the right level, read the student's own draft and name the criterion it undersells, teach notation and citation, and discuss the mathematics as mathematics. A tutor may not choose the topic and hand it over, write or rewrite any part of the text, edit a draft to completion, supply data the student did not generate, or produce a model exploration for adaptation. The student signs the authenticity declaration, so the boundary protects them rather than us.

faqs.question: On a marked IB maths script, which losses show up again and again?
faqs.answer: To invisible working, across both routes. A student does three steps in their head, writes one line, reaches the right answer, and the mark scheme awards a fraction of the credit available. It is pure habit and about three weeks of insistence fixes it. After that: formula-booklet unfamiliarity, which costs minutes per question; in AA, calculus rules used in combination and integrations attempted without naming the substitution; in AI, conclusions stated generically rather than in the question's context and models produced by technology with no justification for the choice.

faqs.question: Does online teaching work for maths, or does the tutor need to be in the room?
faqs.answer: It works, on one condition: the tutor must see the student's handwritten working as it happens, via a camera angled at paper or a tablet and stylus. Without that it degrades into dictation. With it, video has real maths advantages — a shared whiteboard retains every derivation so last week's integration can be reopened rather than reconstructed, the exact past-paper question can be pasted onto the board, and two approaches can sit side by side. The student also works on their own paper in their own handwriting, which is what the exam asks of them.

faqs.question: Will an IB Gram maths tutor travel to our Al Maryah Island address?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram runs no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Every UAE lesson is live one-to-one video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. We say so plainly because the search phrase includes a local tutor and a parent deserves the answer before enquiring. The practical upside on this island is that the tutor is selected for your child's maths route and level rather than for their ability to cross a bridge from the mainland by five in the afternoon.

faqs.question: What does an IB maths tutor cost in Abu Dhabi, in AED?
faqs.answer: Published market figures, read in October 2026: budget online tutoring at AED 45 to 150 an hour, a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150 to 300, an in-home visit at AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the rate, a named IB or A-Level specialist at AED 200 to 450 and above, and premium examiner-led provision reaching AED 650 at the top. On a monthly basis, Bestimate's 2026 estimates put mid-range weekly sessions at AED 600 to 1,200. Those are the market's figures, not ours; our number follows a free trial lesson and a consultation.

faqs.question: Which single piece of maths tutoring gives the fastest return?
faqs.answer: Almost always the dull one: fixing how working is presented, plus a session on calculator discipline. Between them they recover method marks the student is currently throwing away and marks lost to unset modes, unrecorded commands and answers given without the model that produced them. Two or three hours of work, and the gain shows on the next marked paper. Nobody advertises it because it is unimpressive. The expensive mistake is funding a year of general maths hours when the actual problem was four nameable habits and a calculator setting.

faqs.question: At which point in the Diploma should an Al Maryah Island family begin maths support?
faqs.answer: The autumn term of DP1 is the cheapest and most effective moment, because the foundations laid then carry every later topic and the student has time to change a habit rather than patch a gap. Almost nobody buys then, since nothing has gone wrong yet. The spring of DP1 is when the exploration should begin. DP2 autumn is consolidation and first real past papers; DP2 spring is timing, error patterns and, at Higher Level, complete Paper 3 attempts. The final four weeks should be timed papers only.

faqs.question: My child moved from MYP maths into DP1 and is struggling. What changed?
faqs.answer: The assessment model, not the content. MYP maths is marked against four criteria with extended investigations and no timed external papers unless the school enters eAssessment. DP maths is timed papers with a formula booklet and a graphic display calculator. A student fluent in investigation can be genuinely inexperienced at speed and at presenting working for a mark scheme, and they usually find that out in October of DP1. Six to eight sessions bridge it, and placed in the spring of Year 11 they cost less and arrive earlier than the same work done in DP1.

faqs.question: Can the maths slot move during Ramadan or an exam week in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Yes. Sessions commonly shift to post-Iftar timing through Ramadan and the slot is held rather than reassigned, which matters because Ramadan falls inside the UAE academic calendar and changes when revision realistically happens. Sessions can also pause across school examination weeks and resume afterwards, and they can follow a family that travels, since nothing depends on a tutor's driving route. An in-home maths tutor whose week is built around a fixed route across the island's bridges usually cannot offer any of that flexibility.

faqs.question: What should we send before the free IB maths trial lesson?
faqs.answer: The route and level — AA or AI, Higher or Standard — the school name, the last two marked maths assessments including the teacher's comments, and a draft of the exploration if one exists. Also the time your child is actually home, because that sets which slots are real. With that in hand the trial hour works on a real script, and at the end you can ask the tutor to name the four repeating errors they found. A route specialist will do that; a generalist will talk about the topic instead.

intro.heading: The cost of IB maths help in Al Muroor, before anyone talks about pedagogy
paragraphs: Most Al Muroor parents arrive at this search with a figure already in their heads, usually one quoted by a neighbour in the same building. The figures travel badly. A rate that made sense for a Grade 9 MYP maths top-up is the wrong anchor for Analysis and Approaches Higher Level in the second year of the Diploma, and a rate quoted for a group of three is not a rate for one-to-one work. The first job of this page is to separate the bands so you know which one your child's situation actually sits in. Get the band right and everything after it is easier to judge.

Across Abu Dhabi, published market rates split cleanly into four tiers. University-student and budget online tutors advertise from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour; EdFlik lists from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from about AED 33 to 52. Qualified subject tutors working online sit between AED 150 and 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A-Level tutors run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai rate table reaching AED 450 plus. Premium named or examiner-badged tutors are quoted up to AED 650, with BartyED at that figure.

The fourth band is the one that matters most on a page with the word home in its URL. An in-home one-to-one visit in the UAE is quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour once travel is built in, against AED 150 to 300 for the same calibre of teaching delivered online. The gap is not a quality premium. It is petrol, parking and forty minutes of a tutor's evening spent on Airport Road. You pay it, and your child receives nothing extra for it.

That is why IB Gram does not sell in-home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring at a family's address is a service we run only in India. For an Al Muroor family, every lesson happens one-to-one over live video, shared screen, with the same tutor each week. The practical consequence is that your shortlist is no longer limited to the Analysis and Approaches teachers who happen to live within a twenty-minute drive of Muroor Road, which in a subject this specialised is usually a shortlist of two or three.

The rest of this page spends its words on where money leaks out of a maths package: hours bought before anyone has diagnosed the gap, homework-supervision sessions dressed up as tuition, two-hour blocks that produce ninety minutes of value, and exploration support bought six weeks too late to influence the mark. Those four mistakes account for more wasted dirhams in central Abu Dhabi than any rate difference between providers.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-muroor.programmesIntro: IB maths in Al Muroor is taught across three programme stages, and the money behaves differently in each. Primary Years work is cheap and rarely urgent, Middle Years work is where a route choice is quietly being made, and Diploma work is where rates and hours both climb.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Maths in the PYP is embedded in transdisciplinary units rather than taught as a separate timetabled subject, so a parent often cannot see a gap until the child moves into the Middle Years. Number sense, place value, fractions and the early habits of mathematical reasoning are the real content. Tuition here is short, infrequent and inexpensive, and it is almost always about rebuilding confidence after a school move.
programmes.countryNote: Al Muroor families typically use primary schools in the neighbouring Al Mushrif and Al Nahyan districts, and a change of curriculum on arrival in Abu Dhabi is the common trigger. A child arriving from a CBSE or American primary into a PYP classroom meets a very different relationship with written method, and two or three sessions usually settles it.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP maths is assessed against four criteria, A to D, with criterion D asking students to apply mathematics to real-life contexts. Standard and extended strands run in parallel from around Year 9, and the strand a student sits in by Year 11 shapes which Diploma maths route the school will recommend. Tuition in MYP 4 and 5 is the cheapest intervention available with a real effect on the Diploma.
programmes.countryNote: Across Abu Dhabi island, the extended-strand decision is often made in the spring of Year 9, when a Muroor Road family is still settling into the school and not yet reading reports closely. A student held in the standard strand for two years can still reach Analysis and Approaches, but the catch-up is paid for later at Diploma rates rather than earlier at Middle Years rates.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Diploma maths is one of two courses, Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, each at Higher or Standard Level. SL sits two papers, HL sits three, and every student completes a mathematical exploration worth 20%. This is where hourly rates are highest and where hours are most often bought in the wrong order, because families start with revision when the problem is a two-year gap in algebraic fluency.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students in Al Muroor commute out to IB schools on Al Reem Island, Saadiyat Island and the Al Raha corridor, which pushes the realistic start of a weekday session past six in the evening. Online delivery is what makes a 7pm or 8pm Higher Level session possible at all without adding a tutor's drive time to the fee.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-muroor.subjectsIntro: A maths tutor for an Al Muroor Diploma student is rarely tutoring maths in general. These are the specific courses and components the money is actually being spent on, and the ones where the cost per mark gained differs most.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL
subjects.description: The algebra-heavy route, with proof, complex numbers, vectors and the full calculus toolkit including differential equations and Maclaurin series. Three papers plus the exploration. Marks are lost in Paper 1 because it is sat without a calculator and students have practised everything with one. This is the most expensive tuition in the subject and the one where an unqualified tutor is exposed fastest.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches SL
subjects.description: The same mathematical culture as HL with a narrower syllabus: functions, trigonometry, sequences, differentiation and integration, and a lighter statistics load. Two papers plus the exploration. The commonest failure is a student who chose AA SL for a university prerequisite and is really an AI student, spending sessions on binomial expansion they will never be fluent in.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation HL
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics, graph theory, matrices and complex numbers in applied contexts, with heavy expectation of technology use. Three papers plus the exploration. Students lose marks by writing calculator answers without the modelling justification examiners pay for. Fewer tutors in Abu Dhabi cover AI HL properly, which is exactly where a local-only shortlist breaks down.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation SL
subjects.description: Statistics, financial maths, two-variable modelling and an introduction to differentiation, all technology-assisted. Two papers plus the exploration. It is a serious course, not a soft option, and the marks sit in correct interpretation of regression and chi-squared output rather than in manipulation. Tuition here is often the best value in the whole Diploma.

subjects.name: Mathematical exploration (the maths IA)
subjects.description: A piece of independent mathematical writing worth 20% of the final grade, marked against criteria A to E covering presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics. A tutor may teach the criteria, question the mathematics and give feedback on drafts. No tutor may write any part of it.

subjects.name: Paper 1 technique, no calculator
subjects.description: At both levels Paper 1 is sat without technology, and it is the component Abu Dhabi students most consistently underperform because school practice is calculator-rich. Exact-value trigonometry, surd manipulation, logarithm laws and by-hand differentiation are the recoverable marks, and six focused sessions on them usually move more grade than six general revision hours.

subjects.name: Paper 3 extended response, HL only
subjects.description: Two long investigative questions worth 20% of the Higher Level grade, built to test whether a student can follow an unfamiliar mathematical thread under time pressure. It cannot be revised for by topic. It is trained by doing whole papers under timing and then dissecting the structure of the question, which is slow, specific work most generalist tutors never touch.

subjects.name: MYP extended maths, criteria A to D
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying maths in real-life contexts. Criterion B rewards generalisation and proof of a pattern, which is the skill the Diploma exploration later assumes. Students lose marks writing correct answers with no justification, and the fix is cheap at this stage.

subjects.name: MYP to Diploma bridging in algebra
subjects.description: The specific gap between a comfortable MYP 5 student and a functioning Analysis and Approaches student: fluency with indices and surds, confident rearrangement, factor and remainder work, and the function notation the Diploma assumes from week one. Eight weeks over the summer at mid-band rates prevents a year of Diploma-rate remediation.

subjects.name: University prerequisite planning for maths
subjects.description: Engineering, economics and medical routes each expect a particular maths course, and UAE and overseas admissions teams read AA and AI differently. Getting this right in Year 11 is free. Getting it wrong means a resit, an extra year, or a foundation programme, and those are the largest avoidable costs in this entire subject.

sections.heading: The four places maths money leaks in a Diploma year
paragraphs: Spending badly on maths tuition is not usually about paying too much an hour. It is about buying the right hours in the wrong order. Four patterns recur across central Abu Dhabi, and each has a specific cost attached.

The first is buying a package before anyone has diagnosed the gap. A ten-hour block looks like a saving against a single hour, but if six of those hours go on topics the student already holds, the effective rate on the useful four is more than double the sticker price. A single diagnostic session, with the student's last two school assessments in front of the tutor, costs one hour and routinely redirects the other nine.

The second is paying specialist rates for homework supervision. A tutor who spends an hour sitting beside a student working through set questions is doing something a quiet room and a worked-solutions file would do for nothing. The hour is only worth AED 250 if the tutor is teaching something the student could not have reached alone. The third is the two-hour block bought for convenience: concentration on abstract mathematics measurably degrades after about seventy-five minutes, and the second hour of a Thursday evening double is frequently the most expensive low-value hour a family buys all year.

The fourth is late exploration support. The mathematical exploration is 20% of the grade and its mark is largely determined by the topic chosen and the depth of mathematics available in it. Both decisions happen in the first fortnight. A tutor engaged in September can steer them. A tutor engaged ten days before the school deadline is reading a finished piece of work whose ceiling is already set, at the same hourly rate, for a fraction of the effect.
bullets: One diagnostic hour before any package, with recent school assessments to hand
Specialist rates for teaching, not for supervised silence
Sixty or seventy-five minutes beats two hours for abstract work
Exploration support in September, not in the week of the deadline

sections.heading: Online against in-home maths tuition on Muroor Road
paragraphs: This is the comparison most Al Muroor parents are really making, and it deserves honest numbers rather than a sales line. In-home tutoring is a real service that real families in Abu Dhabi buy, and it has genuine advantages: a young child stays in a familiar room, a parent can hear what is happening, and nothing depends on a connection.

It also carries costs that do not appear on an invoice. The travel premium is the visible one. The invisible ones are the shortlist and the schedule. A tutor who must physically reach a flat behind Muroor Road by 6pm can realistically serve a radius of a few kilometres, which for Analysis and Approaches Higher Level in Abu Dhabi narrows the field to a handful of people. If none of them is an AA HL specialist, the family quietly accepts a generalist and pays the specialist premium anyway.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Every Al Muroor lesson is one-to-one over live video, which means the match is made on subject and level rather than on postcode, and the hour you pay for is sixty minutes of teaching rather than forty minutes of teaching and twenty of someone else's commute. The table sets the two formats against each other on the terms that matter to a Diploma maths student. There is also a quieter advantage. An online session can be held when a family is travelling between Abu Dhabi and somewhere else, and Al Muroor households travel a great deal; a Year 13 maths programme that stops for three weeks in February does not recover by itself.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation: the choice that sets the bill
paragraphs: No single decision changes an Al Muroor family's tuition spend more than which maths course the student sits. The two courses are not a harder and an easier version of the same thing. They are different subjects with different assessment cultures, and a student placed in the wrong one needs support for two years rather than two terms.

Analysis and Approaches rewards algebraic fluency and formal method. Applications and Interpretation rewards modelling judgement and correct interpretation of technology output. A student with strong number sense and weak abstraction will fight AA HL every week for two years at specialist rates; the same student in AI HL is frequently a comfortable 6. The grade is not the only consideration, because university prerequisites differ, but the cost of fighting the wrong course is real and it is paid in hours.

Check the prerequisite before the preference, and check it against the actual universities on the shortlist rather than a general impression. Engineering and mathematics degrees commonly expect Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level. Business, economics, psychology and most health-science routes accept Applications and Interpretation, and many accept either. Where a family is undecided between a UAE university and an overseas one, the safe move is to read both admissions pages in Year 11 and keep the record, because this is also the conversation in which a school's blanket advice and a specific department's requirement sometimes disagree. One practical test, usable at a kitchen table: ask the student to explain why a method works rather than to perform it. A student who can justify is an Analysis and Approaches student; a student who can apply confidently but cannot justify is usually happier and better rewarded in Applications and Interpretation.

sections.heading: What a single maths session should actually produce
paragraphs: If you are paying AED 250 for an hour, you are entitled to know what the hour is supposed to leave behind. A good IB maths session is not a conversation about maths. It produces artefacts you can see, and a parent who checks for them twice a term will spot a drifting arrangement long before the report does.

By the end of a first session there should be a written gap list: the specific topics and skills the tutor believes are weak, in syllabus language, with the evidence that led to each. Not 'needs to work on algebra' but 'rearranges correctly but loses sign on expansion of a bracketed negative; cannot yet use the factor theorem unprompted'. That document is what the next eight weeks are purchased against, and if it does not exist, nobody can tell you later whether the money worked.

By the end of any session there should be worked solutions the student can reopen, a short set of practice questions chosen for a named weakness rather than a chapter, and one sentence about what comes next. Across a term you should expect timed component practice, not only topic work, because the Diploma is marked under timing. And you should expect to be told when tuition is no longer the right spend. A student who has closed the gap and now needs volume of past papers does not need a tutor every week, and a tutor who says so is worth more than one who does not.
bullets: A written gap list in syllabus language after session one
Saved worked solutions, not notes that leave with the tutor
Practice chosen against a named weakness, not a chapter number
Timed component practice built in before mocks
A clear statement when weekly tuition is no longer the right purchase

sections.heading: The exploration: what a tutor may do, and what no tutor may do
paragraphs: The mathematical exploration is 20% of the final maths grade, and it is the component where paying for the wrong kind of help can end a Diploma rather than improve it. The boundary is set by IB academic-honesty rules, it is not negotiable, and it is worth stating in plain language before any money changes hands.

A tutor may teach the assessment criteria and what each one rewards. A tutor may discuss candidate topics and press on whether the mathematics in them is deep enough to reach the higher bands. A tutor may question a method, point at an unjustified step, ask why a model was chosen, and give written feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may teach the mathematics the exploration needs, which is often mathematics slightly beyond the taught course.

No tutor may write any part of the exploration, supply text to paste, restructure the student's prose into their own, or produce the mathematics for the student to transcribe. Work bought in is malpractice under IB rules, with consequences that fall on the student rather than on whoever sold it. There is a real market in completed Internal Assessments in this region, advertised at four-figure dirham prices. Buying one risks the whole Diploma, and the pages selling them are the clearest reason a parent should ask any provider to state its honesty policy in writing before the first session. Say the boundary out loud with your child as well. A student who knows exactly what help is legitimate asks for it earlier and uses it better, and a student who is unsure tends either to ask for nothing or to accept something they should not.
bullets: Criteria A to E taught explicitly, with mark allocations named
Topic depth interrogated early, while the topic can still change
Written feedback on the student's own drafts
Nothing written, supplied or rewritten on the student's behalf

sections.heading: Counting backwards from the maths papers
paragraphs: Cost control in a Diploma maths year is mostly a scheduling problem. The hours are not expensive in the abstract; they are expensive when they are bought in the last six weeks, which is when every family in Al Muroor wants them and when the specialists with capacity are the ones nobody else booked.

Work backwards from the papers rather than forwards from today. Abu Dhabi IB schools sit the May session, and the school's own internal deadlines land months before it. Exploration topic approval and first drafts fall in the autumn of Year 13. Mock papers usually sit in the winter term. Predicted grades are issued off the back of those mocks, which makes the mock window the single highest-stakes assessment point of the year for university applications, and the one families routinely treat as practice.

For Cambridge IGCSE students in the same household, note that UAE centres sit the June and November series; the February and March series is offered in India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, with the November timetable ending on 19 November 2026 and November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026. Specific IB session and results dates change and are published by the IB, so confirm them with your child's Diploma coordinator rather than with any tutoring website, including this one. Book the specialist hours you expect to need in the winter term before the winter term arrives. Capacity in this market is consumed in the order it is requested, not in the order of need.

sections.heading: ADEK, your tutor's permit, and two things you can verify yourself
paragraphs: Private schools in Abu Dhabi are licensed and inspected by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and publishes its own inspection outcomes. ADEK is named by none of the tutoring competitors researched for this project, which is an odd gap given it is the body that actually governs the schools these students attend.

Private tutoring is separately regulated at federal level. Individuals offering private lessons in the UAE need a private tuition work permit from MoHRE, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered at government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Anyone tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so any specific figure you see quoted online is unverified.

Two things follow for an Al Muroor parent, and both are checkable. First, ask any tutor whether they hold a current private tuition permit, and understand that the permit is a legal clearance, not a teaching qualification or a regulator's endorsement of anyone's maths teaching. Second, note that ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction. A tutor who offers to teach your child privately while teaching them at school is offering something they should not, and that is reported policy worth verifying against the current ADEK document before anyone acts on it.
