sections.heading: What happens when no specialist is free
paragraphs: Every tutoring page in this market implies infinite availability. None of them has it. Analysis and Approaches Higher Level and Applications and Interpretation Higher Level are small, specialised cohorts, and the number of people who teach them well and are free at 7pm Gulf Standard Time in February is finite. Saying so is more useful to an Al Muroor parent than pretending otherwise.

When a request comes in for a course and level with no immediate specialist free, there are three honest answers and we will give you whichever applies. The first is a waiting time with a date attached. The second is a tutor who covers the course solidly but is not the deepest specialist available, named as such, usually a reasonable choice for SL work and a poor one for HL Paper 3. The third is that we cannot cover it well at the hours you need, which is sometimes the correct answer and always better than a bad match that burns a term.

The one thing that does not happen is a quiet substitution. You are told who is teaching your child, what they teach, and what their experience of the specific course and level is, before the trial lesson rather than after it. If the trial does not work, the match changes without an argument, because a mismatch identified in week one costs an hour and a mismatch tolerated to half term costs a grade. The same transparency applies to timing. If the only slot a specialist can hold is 8.30pm on a Tuesday, you are told that before you commit rather than discovering it in week three, because a slot a family cannot sustain is a slot that quietly becomes a cancellation habit.

The named tutor before the trial, not after it

faqs.question: What should I expect to pay an IB maths tutor in Al Muroor per hour?
faqs.answer: Published market rates in Abu Dhabi put a qualified subject tutor working online at AED 150 to 300 an hour, and an IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialist at AED 200 to 450 or more. Unitors publishes IB from AED 200, TutorChase quotes AED 270, and Bestimate's 2026 rate table reaches AED 450 plus. In-home one-to-one visits sit higher, at AED 180 to 500 with travel included. Which band you need depends on level, not age: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level in Year 13 belongs in the specialist band, and budgeting at the qualified-tutor band is the commonest way a family runs short in the spring.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to put my child in a group maths class instead of one-to-one?
faqs.answer: Per hour, yes. Abu Dhabi tuition centres commonly price a group of two to four at AED 80 to 180 a student against AED 150 to 300 for one-to-one online. Whether it is cheaper per mark depends entirely on whether everyone in the group is stuck on the same thing. A group working through a shared syllabus at a shared pace is good value. A group where one student needs non-calculator algebra and another needs exploration help is three students each receiving a third of a lesson, and families usually end up buying one-to-one hours afterwards anyway.

faqs.question: Do tutors come to apartments in Al Muroor for IB maths lessons?
faqs.answer: Some providers in Abu Dhabi do offer that, and market rates for in-home one-to-one sit at AED 180 to 500 an hour because the figure absorbs the tutor's journey. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; visits to a family's address are a service we run only in India. For an Al Muroor family every lesson is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. The practical gain is that the tutor is chosen for knowing Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level rather than for living near Muroor Road, and the hour you pay for contains no commute.

faqs.question: How many maths sessions does a Diploma student in central Abu Dhabi usually need?
faqs.answer: Most families start with one session a week and hold it for a term, which is enough to close a defined gap in algebra or calculus if the hours are aimed properly. A Year 13 Higher Level student with a wide gap and mocks approaching often needs two a week for six to eight weeks, then drops back to one. What matters more than the count is the order: a diagnostic hour first, then hours bought against a written gap list. Ten hours bought blind commonly deliver the value of four, which doubles the effective rate on the hours that worked.

faqs.question: My child is in AA HL and sinking. Is switching to AI HL a waste of the money already spent?
faqs.answer: No, and the question is worth asking early rather than late. Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation are different subjects, not difficulty settings. A student with strong number sense and weak abstraction can fight AA HL for two years at specialist rates and still land where AI HL would have put them comfortably. Check the prerequisite for the actual universities on the shortlist first, because engineering and maths routes usually expect AA. If the prerequisite allows AI, a switch made in Year 12 saves far more than it writes off, including in tuition hours.

faqs.question: Why does Paper 1 cost us so many marks when my child is good at maths?
faqs.answer: Paper 1 is sat without a calculator at both Standard and Higher Level, and most school practice is calculator-rich. A student can be genuinely strong mathematically and still lose a whole grade on exact-value trigonometry, surd manipulation, logarithm laws and by-hand differentiation, because fluency in those is a trained motor skill rather than an understanding. It is also the cheapest thing to fix. Six focused sessions on non-calculator technique typically move more grade than six hours of general revision, which makes it the highest-value hour available in either maths course.

faqs.question: Where is the line between exploration coaching and work a tutor must not touch?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor may teach the assessment criteria and their mark allocations, discuss and press on candidate topics, teach mathematics the exploration needs, question an unjustified step, and give written feedback on a draft the student has written themselves. A tutor may not write any part of it, supply text, or produce mathematics for the student to copy. Bought-in work is malpractice under IB rules and the consequences fall on the student. Ask any provider to state its honesty policy in writing before the first session; completed assessments are sold in this market.

faqs.question: When is the right month to start exploration support rather than exam support?
faqs.answer: Early in the autumn of Year 13, when the topic is still changeable. The exploration is 20% of the maths grade, and most of that mark is decided by the topic choice and the depth of mathematics available inside it, both of which are settled in the first fortnight of the process. A tutor engaged then can redirect a thin topic into a workable one for the cost of two short sessions. A tutor engaged ten days before the school deadline is reading a finished piece whose ceiling is already set, at the same hourly rate.

faqs.question: What time can lessons realistically start for a family living around Muroor Road?
faqs.answer: Six in the evening is the first comfortable slot, and seven is easier. Al Muroor children attend schools spread across Al Mushrif, Al Nahyan, Al Reem Island and the Al Raha corridor, so a 3.15pm finish regularly becomes a 4.45pm arrival once the car park and Airport Road are accounted for. Online delivery makes the later slot workable, because nobody is adding a tutor's drive to the end of that chain. Weekend mornings are the other good window and are usually the better one for long exploration sessions.

faqs.question: Do private maths tutors in Abu Dhabi need a permit, and how would I check?
faqs.answer: Yes. Individuals giving private lessons in the UAE need a private tuition work permit from MoHRE, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day turnaround. Ask the tutor directly whether they hold a current permit. Treat it as a legal clearance rather than proof of teaching quality, and remember no official fine schedule is published for working without one.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper tutor at AED 100 an hour a false economy for Higher Level maths?
faqs.answer: Often, though not always. The AED 45 to 150 band is populated by university students and generalist online tutors, and it is reasonable value for MYP homework support or for keeping a Standard Level student moving through routine practice. For Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level it usually is a false economy, because the specific skills in short supply are Paper 3 question structure, non-calculator fluency and exploration depth, and those need someone who has taught the course. Paying AED 250 for eight useful hours beats AED 100 for twenty supervised ones.

faqs.question: Which Abu Dhabi schools do your IB maths students near Al Muroor attend?
faqs.answer: Students we support in this part of the island come from campuses in Al Mushrif and Al Nahyan and from the IB and British-curriculum schools on Al Reem Island, in Bloom Gardens and along the Al Raha corridor, including Repton School Abu Dhabi, GEMS World Academy Abu Dhabi, Brighton College Abu Dhabi, The British School Al Khubairat and Abu Dhabi International School. Those names describe the local school map only. IB Gram has no affiliation, partnership or endorsement arrangement with any of them, and no school on this page is a client.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether the money we are spending on maths is working?
faqs.answer: Look for artefacts rather than impressions. After the first session there should be a written gap list in syllabus language with the evidence behind each item. After every session there should be saved worked solutions and practice chosen against a named weakness. Across a term there should be timed component practice, not only topic work. At six weeks the gap list should be revisited against school evidence and changed if the evidence says so. If none of that exists, nobody can tell you in March whether February's hours achieved anything.

faqs.question: What if no Higher Level maths specialist is free in the evening slot we need?
faqs.answer: You get told. Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level are small cohorts and the pool of people who teach them well at 7pm Gulf Standard Time is finite. The three honest answers are a waiting time with a date, a named tutor who covers the course solidly but is not the deepest specialist, with that limitation stated, or an admission that we cannot cover it well at the hours you need. What does not happen is a quiet substitution; you know who is teaching your child before the trial lesson.

faqs.question: Does the IB maths grade depend on which exam session my child sits?
faqs.answer: The grade depends on performance, not on the session, but the planning does change. Abu Dhabi IB schools sit the May session, and the internal deadlines that most affect the maths grade, exploration topic approval, first draft and final submission, fall months earlier in the autumn and winter. Mocks usually sit in the winter term and drive the predicted grades universities see. Specific IB exam and results dates are published by the IB and do change, so confirm them with your child's Diploma coordinator rather than with any tutoring website.

intro.heading: Which of the four maths courses is your child actually on?
paragraphs: Parents in Al Mushrif ring up about IB maths and are often surprised by the first question back, which is not about grades or availability but about which course. There are four. Analysis and Approaches at Standard Level, Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level and Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level. They share a name and very little else, and asking for an IB maths tutor without specifying is like asking for a science tutor without saying which science.

The split is substantive. Analysis and Approaches is the algebra, calculus and proof route, and its Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, which means manipulation fluency is load-bearing rather than optional. Applications and Interpretation is calculator-active throughout, built around statistics, probability and modelling, with matrices, graph theory and numerically solved differential equations added at Higher Level. Higher Level in either course carries a third written paper, Paper 3, worth 20 per cent, which has no Standard Level equivalent and which is unlike anything else in the Diploma.

The consequence for a search like yours is that geography is the least useful filter available. Somewhere within a short drive of Al Mushrif there is certainly a capable mathematician, possibly several. Whether one of them has taught Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level, can describe what Paper 3 rewards, and knows that the Exploration carries 20 per cent and is marked across five lettered criteria with Use of Mathematics worth six of twenty marks, is a separate and much narrower question. The pool of people who genuinely know a specific course at a specific level is small, and drawing a circle on a map makes it smaller.

There is an honest version of what that means. If you require a tutor who drives to an Al Mushrif address, your choice narrows to whoever will make that journey on that evening, and the course match becomes whatever remains. Drop the travel requirement and the choice becomes every specialist in that course who can work at your hour. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Every UAE session runs one-to-one online over live video with a shared screen, which for working through a Paper 3 question line by line is better than two people sharing one printed page.

The rest of this page is the information needed to make that match properly: what distinguishes the four courses topic by topic, four questions that establish whether a tutor knows yours, what Paper 3 actually demands, where marks go missing by topic, the real gap between MYP or IGCSE maths and the Diploma, what a school can and cannot provide one individual student, and the graphics-calculator skills that decide a surprising number of marks and that almost nobody teaches explicitly.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-mushrif.programmesIntro: Al Mushrif families reach Diploma mathematics through the Middle Years Programme or through an IGCSE route, and the two arrive with different strengths. Knowing which route a student came by is the fastest way to predict where the first few sessions have to go.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme Mathematics
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria, each out of eight, with the extended strand available in the upper years. Criterion C rewards communication and Criterion D rewards applying mathematics to real contexts, which means a student can reach the right answer and still score in the middle bands for not showing reasoning.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP extended mathematics strand is the natural feed into Analysis and Approaches, and the standard strand into Applications and Interpretation. Al Mushrif families who settle that route in Year 10 avoid the commonest and most expensive Diploma maths error, which is a Higher Level choice made on ambition rather than evidence.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme Mathematics
programmes.description: One of the four courses, taken as part of six subjects with three at Higher Level. Papers plus the Mathematical Exploration, which carries 20 per cent at both levels. At Higher Level the written papers split 30, 30 and 20 per cent across Papers 1, 2 and 3; at Standard Level, Papers 1 and 2 carry 40 per cent each.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi IB schools sit the May session, with November as the alternative route. No IB examination or results date is published on this page: ibo.org blocks automated checking, and an unverified date a family plans around is worse than none. Confirm with your school's IB coordinator.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Fewer DP courses alongside a career-related study and a reflective project. Where mathematics is one of the DP courses carried inside the CP, it is examined to exactly the same standard as in the full Diploma, including the Exploration, so the support required is identical.
programmes.countryNote: CP cohorts in Abu Dhabi are small, which means a school sometimes cannot staff individual maths help at depth. For a CP student the mathematics course is often the component carrying the most external examination weight in the whole programme.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: No external examinations and no mark scheme. What matters mathematically at this stage is number fluency, the willingness to explain a method, and comfort with multi-step reasoning, all of which the Middle Years Programme assumes rather than teaches.
programmes.countryNote: Al Mushrif children transferring into an Abu Dhabi PYP school from a worksheet-driven system often find the inquiry structure unfamiliar before they find the mathematics difficult. The first useful intervention is usually about explaining reasoning aloud rather than about content.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-mushrif.subjectsIntro: The entries below describe the parts of Diploma mathematics that actually generate tutoring requests from Al Mushrif, written by what each one demands rather than by chapter heading.

subjects.name: Analysis and Approaches SL
subjects.description: Papers 1 and 2 at 40 per cent each plus the Exploration at 20. Paper 1 is non-calculator, which exposes any weakness in algebraic manipulation within minutes. Unsimplified surds, sign errors through long rearrangements and differentiation applied without naming the rule are the standard losses.

subjects.name: Analysis and Approaches HL
subjects.description: Papers 1 and 2 at 30 per cent each, Paper 3 at 20 and the Exploration at 20. Proof by induction, complex numbers in polar form and the deeper calculus topics are where the course separates from Standard Level, and where a tutor without HL experience runs out of depth.

subjects.name: Applications and Interpretation SL
subjects.description: Calculator-active throughout, with statistics, probability and modelling at the centre. The demand students underestimate is written interpretation: a correct value earns little without a sentence stating what it means in the context given, and that sentence carries marks.

subjects.name: Applications and Interpretation HL
subjects.description: Adds matrices, graph theory, complex numbers in applied settings and differential equations solved numerically, with a data-rich Paper 3. Students who chose the course to avoid algebra are regularly caught by the volume of technology-assisted work and the writing it requires.

subjects.name: The Mathematical Exploration
subjects.description: An independent written investigation of roughly twelve to twenty pages, worth 20 per cent, marked out of 20 across criteria A to E. Use of Mathematics alone carries six marks, which is why a topic chosen for interest but not stress-tested for mathematical richness underperforms.

subjects.name: Paper 3 extended problem solving
subjects.description: Two long questions, each developing a scenario across several parts, where an early error can cascade. The skill is carrying a result forward under time pressure, and it is built by full-length timed questions rather than by topic exercises.

subjects.name: Proof and the toolkit
subjects.description: Direct proof, proof by contradiction and, at Higher Level, proof by induction. Students arriving from IGCSE have usually verified results rather than proved them, and the difference is conceptual rather than technical. It takes weeks to build and cannot be rushed in a revision block.

subjects.name: Statistics and modelling
subjects.description: Regression, correlation, hypothesis testing where the course includes it, and fitting models to data. The mathematics is usually accessible and the marks are lost on interpretation: stating what a coefficient means, or whether a model is appropriate for the data given.

subjects.name: Calculus across the courses
subjects.description: Differentiation and integration appear in all four courses at different depths, from basic rules in Applications SL to integration by parts and differential equations in Analysis HL. A tutor's comfort at the top of this range is the clearest signal of genuine Higher Level experience.

subjects.name: Technology and the graphics calculator
subjects.description: Required for Paper 2 in every course and throughout Applications. Graph intersections, numerical solving, statistical functions and distribution calculations save substantial time, and almost no school teaches them explicitly as a separate skill.

sections.heading: Four courses, and why "IB maths tutor" is not a specification
paragraphs: Begin with what distinguishes them, because the distinction decides who can teach your child. Analysis and Approaches is organised around algebraic technique, calculus and proof. Its Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, so a student with shaky manipulation has nowhere to hide. Applications and Interpretation is organised around data, modelling and interpretation, is calculator-active throughout, and asks students to say what results mean in context as often as it asks them to compute.

Level then changes the course again rather than merely extending it. Higher Level in either route adds Paper 3, two extended problem-solving questions worth 20 per cent between them, with no Standard Level counterpart. Analysis HL adds proof by induction, complex numbers in polar form and deeper calculus. Applications HL adds matrices, graph theory and differential equations solved numerically. A tutor comfortable with Applications SL statistics may have never taught graph theory, and saying so would be honest rather than disqualifying.

This is why Applications being described as the easier course is one of the most persistent errors in Diploma planning. It is not easier; it is differently difficult. Students who choose it to escape algebra are frequently caught by the interpretation demand, because the mark scheme awards a sentence about meaning and they have written only a number. Students who choose Analysis because it sounds more rigorous, without having consolidated IGCSE manipulation, spend DP1 repairing foundations under time pressure.

A practical note for Al Mushrif families: before committing to a course, check the published entry requirements of three universities your child might actually apply to. Engineering, economics and most physical-science degrees commonly specify Analysis and Approaches, frequently at Higher Level. That check costs nothing, takes twenty minutes and prevents the most expensive mistake available in Diploma mathematics.

sections.heading: Four questions that establish whether a tutor knows your course
paragraphs: Credentials are easy to assert in a message and hard to verify. Course knowledge is close to impossible to fake, because a tutor who has prepared candidates carries the structure of the papers the way a driver carries a familiar route. Four questions, asked in that order, sort a shortlist in a few minutes.

First, ask what the Exploration is worth and how it is marked. A genuine Diploma maths tutor will say 20 per cent, five criteria, twenty marks, and will know that Use of Mathematics carries six of them. A vague answer about coursework counting towards the grade means the published descriptors have never been in front of them. Second, ask what Paper 3 contains and whether your child sits it. The answer is two extended problem-solving questions, Higher Level only, 20 per cent. Someone who hesitates here has not taught Higher Level.

Third, ask which paper is non-calculator and why that matters. For Analysis the answer is Paper 1 and the reason is that it tests manipulation directly; for Applications there is no non-calculator paper, which itself changes how revision should be organised. A tutor who answers this without qualification for both courses has probably taught only one and should say so.

Fourth, ask what they will refuse to do. The right answer names the Exploration boundary without being prompted: question the topic, teach the criteria, give feedback on the student's own draft, and nothing else. Operations in this market sell completed Internal Assessments at a published price. A tutor who treats that line as obvious is telling you they have thought about the student's risk, which is the quality you are actually hiring.

sections.heading: The content that actually separates the routes
paragraphs: Course descriptions are written to sound comparable, which hides the real differences. Laid out topic by topic, the two routes diverge enough that a student transferring between them mid-course needs genuine bridging work rather than reassurance.

Proof is the clearest marker. Analysis expects direct proof and proof by contradiction, and at Higher Level proof by induction, which is conceptually unlike anything in IGCSE mathematics. A student arriving from a verification culture, where results are checked rather than established, finds induction baffling for several weeks and then straightforward. Applications does not carry this demand at all, which is a legitimate reason to choose it and a poor reason to assume it is lighter.

Statistics runs the other way. Applications treats data as the subject rather than a topic, with regression, correlation and modelling central, and it asks for interpretation in prose. Analysis includes statistics but does not build the course on it. A tutor strong in one route is frequently weak in the other precisely because the daily work is different: one spends its hours on manipulation and the other on reading what a result means.

Technology sits in between. Both routes require a graphics calculator for Paper 2, and Applications requires it throughout. The skills involved are specific and almost never taught as a separate strand: finding intersections, solving numerically, running statistical tests, computing from distributions. A substantial number of recoverable marks sit in calculator fluency, which is why it has its own section further down this page.

sections.heading: Paper 3: the Higher Level component with no Standard Level equivalent
paragraphs: Paper 3 is the component families know least and the one that most often prompts a late enquiry from Al Mushrif. It consists of two extended problem-solving questions, together worth 20 per cent of the Higher Level grade, and each develops a situation across several parts so that later work depends on earlier answers. Nothing at Standard Level prepares a student for it, and nothing in the topic exercises most students use for revision resembles it.

The distinctive difficulty is dependency. In an ordinary paper a wrong answer costs the marks for that question. In Paper 3 a wrong answer in part (a) can poison parts (b) through (e), which is why examiners allow follow-through credit and why students who do not know that lose marks they would otherwise keep. The single most valuable thing a tutor can teach for this paper is what to do when an early part has clearly gone wrong: state an assumption, carry on explicitly, and secure the method marks downstream.

The second difficulty is unfamiliarity of context. Paper 3 questions are built around situations a student has not met, which is deliberate: the paper tests whether mathematics learned in one setting can be deployed in another. That cannot be prepared by content coverage. It is prepared by sitting many full-length extended questions, discussing the opening moves, and building the habit of reading the whole question before starting part (a).

Practically, Paper 3 support works best as a short defined block rather than as a thread through two years. Six to eight weeks of two sessions a week, entirely full questions marked against the official scheme, placed before mocks rather than after them. Placed after mocks it becomes damage control; placed before, it changes the mock result and therefore the student's confidence for the rest of the year.

sections.heading: Where Diploma maths marks go missing, by topic
paragraphs: A grade is specific marks lost in specific places, and across Al Mushrif enquiries the places recur. Naming them converts a vague worry into a plan, and most of them are process rather than knowledge, which means they are faster to fix than families expect.

In Analysis, the heaviest cluster sits in manipulation under non-calculator conditions. Surds left unsimplified, sign errors carried through several lines, trigonometric identities applied in the wrong direction. The second cluster is method marks not earned because working was not shown: the mark scheme awards the approach separately from the answer, and a student who computes mentally and writes one number can lose most of a question while being entirely correct. The third is calculus notation, where a derivative is found correctly and then used without stating what it represents.

In Applications, the losses concentrate in interpretation rather than calculation. A regression line computed accurately and then not interpreted. A correlation coefficient stated without saying what it indicates about the relationship. A model fitted and never evaluated for suitability. These are writing marks inside a mathematics paper, and students who treat the subject as computation lose them consistently without understanding why.

Across both courses the Exploration produces its own pattern. Topics chosen for personal interest without being tested for mathematical richness score poorly on Use of Mathematics, which is the largest criterion at six marks out of twenty. Reflection written as description rather than evaluation loses Criterion D. Notation mixed between sections loses Criterion B. All three are preventable in one session at the planning stage and expensive to repair afterwards.

sections.heading: From MYP or IGCSE into Diploma maths: the honest gap
paragraphs: Al Mushrif students arrive in DP1 from two main routes, and each arrives with a predictable gap. Treating both as simply well prepared is why the first mock surprises so many families.

From the Middle Years Programme, the gap is usually technical rather than conceptual. MYP mathematics is assessed against criteria that reward reasoning, communication and real-world application, which builds genuinely useful habits. What it does not necessarily build is speed and accuracy in manipulation under timed conditions, because MYP assessment rarely demands it. A student who writes beautifully about mathematics can arrive at Analysis and Approaches and find Paper 1 brutal, and the repair is drill rather than discussion.

From IGCSE the gap inverts. A 0580 Extended or 4MA1 Higher candidate arrives with solid technique and little experience of proof, of radians, or of sustained multi-step problems. Proof is the real conceptual jump: IGCSE asks students to verify, the Diploma asks them to establish, and several weeks pass before the difference lands. A 0607 International Mathematics candidate arrives the other way round, comfortable with technology and investigation and thinner on manipulation.

The useful intervention is a short block in the summer between the two programmes rather than catch-up in the first term. Four to six sessions in July, aimed at the specific gap, cost less and achieve more than a term of DP1 repair, because the Diploma does not pause while a student consolidates. Families who skip it generally buy the same hours later, at a higher rate, under more pressure, and alongside the Exploration.

sections.heading: What a school can and cannot give one maths student
paragraphs: A fair version of this page has to say what the school already provides, because a parent who does not know that is likely to buy the wrong thing. A good Diploma maths department delivers the syllabus, sets and marks assessments, supervises the Exploration, runs mock examinations and usually offers some form of clinic or departmental help at no extra cost. Al Mushrif sits among some of the longest-established campuses in the emirate, and the teaching in them is generally strong.

What a class of twenty cannot provide is individual attention to one student's specific pattern of lost marks. A teacher marking twenty Paper 2 scripts can report a cohort trend; they rarely have time to sit with one student and work through why that student in particular loses accuracy marks in the third line of every long question. That diagnostic conversation is the thing one-to-one support actually sells, and it is worth distinguishing from content coverage, which the school is already doing and which you are already paying for through fees.

The Exploration is the second clear gap. School supervisors have a defined and limited role, correctly, and the number of supervision hours available per student is small. Interrogating a topic properly before work begins, and giving criterion-referenced feedback on a full draft, takes time most departments do not have across a whole cohort. This is why a short Exploration block is frequently the highest-value purchase in the two years.

Before buying anything, ask the school three questions. What was the last assessment marked against, and which specific marks were lost. Has this class had a consistent teacher this year. Which syllabus topics remain to be taught this term. Detailed answers may mean you do not need a tutor at all. Vague answers tell you something useful about why your child cannot explain the problem either.

sections.heading: The graphics calculator skills nobody teaches explicitly
paragraphs: A graphics calculator is required for Paper 2 in all four courses and used throughout Applications, and the skills it demands are specific, learnable and almost never taught as a separate strand. Students are shown the device in Year 12 and then expected to absorb its use alongside the mathematics. The result is a steady, invisible loss of marks to time and to avoidable error.

The clearest example is solving. A question that asks for the intersection of two functions can be answered in fifteen seconds with a graph and an intersect command, or in four minutes algebraically with several opportunities to slip. In a timed paper the difference compounds: four minutes saved on three questions is a question's worth of thinking time recovered. Students who do not know the command spend the time and often arrive at the same answer less reliably.

Statistics is the second area, and it matters most in Applications. One-variable statistics, regression lines, correlation coefficients and distribution calculations are all device functions, and a student computing them by hand is both slower and more error-prone. The mark is for the correct value and the interpretation, not for the arithmetic, so there is no virtue in the manual route under examination conditions.

The third area is judgement about when not to use it. Paper 1 in Analysis is non-calculator, so a student who has become dependent on the device for routine algebra is exposed. The right balance is deliberate: build manipulation fluency for Paper 1 and calculator fluency for Paper 2, and treat them as two distinct skills rather than as one subject with a tool attached. A tutor who teaches both explicitly is addressing a real and uncontested gap.

faqs.question: How do we find out which IB maths course our child is on?
faqs.answer: Ask the school, or look at the timetable and the course title rather than the word maths. There are four: Analysis and Approaches at Standard and Higher Level, and Applications and Interpretation at Standard and Higher Level. Also ask whether your child sits Paper 3, because that answer confirms the level immediately. A tutor who does not ask for this before a first session is treating four different courses as one, which is the commonest quality failure in Diploma maths tutoring.

faqs.question: Is Applications and Interpretation the easier of the two routes?
faqs.answer: No, it is differently difficult. Applications is calculator-active and built on statistics, probability and modelling, with matrices, graph theory and numerically solved differential equations at Higher Level. Its mark schemes award a written sentence saying what a result means in context, and students who chose it to avoid algebra are regularly caught by that writing demand. Check the published entry requirements of three target universities as well, because engineering and economics routes commonly specify Analysis and Approaches.

faqs.question: What is actually in Paper 3, and does everybody sit it?
faqs.answer: Only Higher Level candidates sit it, in both courses. It contains two extended problem-solving questions worth 20 per cent of the grade between them, each developing a scenario across several parts so that later answers depend on earlier ones. That dependency is the distinctive difficulty: an unflagged error in part (a) can cost marks through part (e). The highest-value thing to learn for it is how to state an assumption and carry on when an early part has clearly gone wrong.

faqs.question: Our son computes everything in his head and loses marks. Why?
faqs.answer: Because mark schemes in Diploma mathematics award the method separately from the answer. On a multi-step question a student who works mentally and writes one number can lose most of the available marks while being entirely correct. It is a habit rather than a knowledge problem, and it takes a fortnight of deliberate practice to change. A marked diagnostic script makes it visible immediately, which is usually the point at which a student starts believing it matters.

faqs.question: How much does the graphics calculator actually matter?
faqs.answer: More than most schools teach. It is required for Paper 2 in all four courses and used throughout Applications, and the skills are specific: graphing and intersecting to solve, regression and correlation menus, distribution functions, numerical integration. A question answerable in fifteen seconds with an intersect command can take four minutes algebraically with several chances to slip. The other half of the skill is judgement, because Paper 1 in Analysis is non-calculator and dependency on the device is a liability there.

faqs.question: What does the Exploration criterion for Use of Mathematics reward?
faqs.answer: Mathematics commensurate with the level of the course, and it carries six of the twenty available marks, which makes it the largest single criterion. That is why a topic chosen for personal interest and never stress-tested for mathematical richness underperforms: the writing can be excellent and the mathematics too simple for the course. One session spent interrogating the topic before any work starts is worth more than three spent polishing afterwards, and it cannot be recovered later.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Exploration without taking it over?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a specific boundary. A tutor may question the topic until the student's own idea is workable, warn that a planned data set will not support the intended analysis, teach what criteria A to E reward, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor may not supply the topic, the data or any prose, or edit the work until the words are no longer the student's. The test is whether your child can explain every sentence and decision as their own.

faqs.question: Our daughter came from MYP and is struggling with Paper 1. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: It is one of the two standard transition patterns. MYP mathematics is assessed against criteria that reward reasoning, communication and application, which builds genuinely useful habits but rarely demands speed and accuracy in manipulation under timed conditions. A student who writes well about mathematics can therefore find Analysis Paper 1 brutal. The repair is drill rather than discussion: short, frequent, non-calculator manipulation practice, which is dull and works within a term.

faqs.question: What should a student coming from Cambridge 0580 expect to find hardest?
faqs.answer: Proof, radians and sustained multi-step problems, in that order. IGCSE asks candidates to verify results; the Diploma asks them to establish them, and proof by induction at Higher Level is conceptually unlike anything in the IGCSE course. Several weeks pass before the difference lands and then it becomes straightforward. Four to six bridging sessions in the summer before DP1 cost less and achieve more than a term of catch-up alongside everything else the first year demands.

faqs.question: Does distance from Al Mushrif matter when choosing a maths tutor?
faqs.answer: Only if you require someone physically present, and then it limits you to whoever will drive inland on that evening, with the course match becoming whatever remains. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Sessions run one-to-one over live video with a shared screen, which for working through an extended question line by line is clearer than two people sharing one printed page.

faqs.question: Should we buy support for maths when the school's department is strong?
faqs.answer: Only for what the department cannot provide. A strong department delivers the syllabus, sets and marks assessments, supervises the Exploration and usually runs a free clinic, and you already pay for that through fees. What a class of twenty cannot do is sit with one student and work out why that student loses accuracy marks in the third line of every long question. Buy the diagnosis and the technique work, not a duplicate of the teaching.

faqs.question: Which of the four courses is hardest to find a specialist for?
faqs.answer: Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level, particularly for Paper 3, because the course is newer in many schools and the Higher Level content includes matrices and graph theory that fewer tutors have taught. Analysis and Approaches at both levels has the widest pool in the whole IB catalogue, which means a family there has genuine choice. When we cannot staff a request properly we give a dated waiting slot, state the limitation plainly, or decline rather than place someone adjacent.

faqs.question: When is the right time to buy Paper 3 support?
faqs.answer: Before the mock examinations rather than after them, which is the opposite of what most families do. Placed before, a block of six to eight weeks at two sessions a week changes the mock result and therefore the student's confidence for the rest of the year. Placed after, it becomes damage control against a score that has already affected predicted grades. The content is the same either way; the timing decides what it is worth.

faqs.question: Where should we get the May session window from, if not from this page?
faqs.answer: Because we could not verify them. The IB's own website returns an error to automated checking, so any session or results date here would come from a secondary source and be presented as fact. A wrong date that a family builds a revision plan around is worse than no date, especially inside an answer a voice assistant might read aloud. Abu Dhabi IB schools sit the May session, with November as the alternative; confirm the window with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-nahyan.tutorsIntro: Al Nahyan mathematics enquiries are most often triggered by a mock result. We ask for the script rather than the grade, classify the losses in the first session, and match to a tutor who teaches that course and that paper weekly.

intro.heading: The mock script is the most useful document in the Diploma
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi schools generally run Diploma mocks in the second-year winter. Most families read the result, note the grade, feel better or worse, and file the paper. Read that way a mock yields one number. Read properly, the same script tells you precisely which of four things is wrong, and the four have completely different remedies, different timescales and different costs.

The four categories are content not known, question wording misread, reasoning not shown, and time ran out. Go through the script mark by mark and sort every lost mark into one of them, then count. In Diploma mathematics the reasoning category is almost always larger than families expect, because marks are allocated to visible steps and a correct answer reached by an unjustified route collects a fraction of what it could.

That tally then dictates everything. A student with most losses in the timing column does not need more content teaching; they need marks-per-minute arithmetic and the discipline of abandoning a stuck question. A student with most in the reasoning column needs the habit of writing every line, which takes weeks to install rather than minutes to explain. A student with most in content needs a different plan again, and a shorter one than they hope, because only the topics that appear often enough to pay for themselves are worth the remaining hours.

The second thing this page covers is how to design the weeks after that diagnosis, because revision design is a genuine variable and almost nobody treats it as one. Interleaved practice, where topics are mixed, consistently outperforms blocked practice, where one topic is worked through at a time, even though blocked practice feels more productive while you are doing it. Students and parents both reliably choose the format that feels better, which is why the week has to be designed rather than allowed to emerge on its own.

Al Nahyan sits in the city east of Al Mushrif, with schools a short drive away in Al Mushrif, Al Bateen and the surrounding districts. Journeys are short, which means the constraint on a session is the rest of the week rather than the road, and the fortnight schools release students for mocks is unusually usable here because the commute disappears at the same moment the script arrives.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, or anywhere else in the UAE. In-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. What we deliver to Al Nahyan is one-to-one teaching over live video, which suits mathematics because every line of working stays visible on a shared whiteboard and is saved afterwards, so a worked solution can be reread rather than half-remembered. Over a term that accumulated record becomes a revision resource in its own right.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-nahyan.programmesIntro: Mathematics runs the whole length of the IB continuum. Each stage has a different diagnostic instrument, and knowing which one to read is most of the skill in deciding what to buy.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme mathematics
programmes.description: No external assessment, so the diagnostic is the teacher's own observation rather than a script. The risk is quiet: inquiry work builds reasoning well while arithmetic fluency drifts, and the drift surfaces two or three years later when every Middle Years problem takes three times as long as it should.
programmes.countryNote: Al Nahyan primary pupils attend schools a short drive away and are typically home early with the afternoon clear. Two short fluency sessions a week suit this age far better than one hour, and because nothing is urgent the work can be slow and thorough in a way it never is later.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Four criteria, each scored out of eight: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. The diagnostic here is the criterion-level score rather than the converted grade, and those four numbers per task identify the problem in minutes.
programmes.countryNote: Ask your Al Nahyan school for the criterion scores across the last two reporting cycles rather than the grade. They are recorded for every assessed task, the request is routine, and the pattern almost always shows one strand sitting three or four points below the others.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, at Standard or Higher Level. Standard Level runs two papers at forty per cent each with the exploration at twenty; Higher Level becomes thirty, thirty and twenty with the exploration at twenty. The mock script is the diagnostic that matters.
programmes.countryNote: Al Nahyan Diploma students attend schools in Al Mushrif, Al Bateen and nearby, several with study periods after a 15:30 finish. Both 17:30 and 19:30 work here, and during mock season the released days make a daytime session possible for the only time in the year.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme with a DP mathematics course
programmes.description: Where a school offers the Career-related Programme, a mathematics course inside it is examined on exactly the same papers with the same weightings and the same exploration. The diagnostic is therefore identical: a mock script read mark by mark, classified into the same four categories.
programmes.countryNote: Few Abu Dhabi schools run the Career-related Programme, so most Al Nahyan families are comparing Diploma mathematics with A Level Mathematics. If your child is on it, say so when booking, because a provider pricing it as something lighter has misunderstood what is being examined.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-nahyan.subjectsIntro: These are the areas a mock script usually implicates, with the category of error each tends to produce and how long removing it takes.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation
subjects.description: Produces reasoning and timing losses rather than content ones. A student who rearranges slowly loses minutes in every question, which then shows up as unattempted final parts. Two to three weeks of deliberate practice usually changes the shape of a whole paper.

subjects.name: Functions and graphs
subjects.description: Composite order reversed and domain or range ignored are the recurring errors, and both sit in the wording category: the question asked for something slightly different from what was answered. Fast to fix once named, and almost never named by the student.

subjects.name: Trigonometry
subjects.levels: Both courses; vectors at Analysis HL
subjects.description: Angle mode left in degrees for a radian question invalidates everything in that question, which registers as a content loss and is actually a calculator discipline. One of the cheapest single fixes available in the whole subject.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.levels: Heavier in Applications; present in both
subjects.description: Produces interpretation losses: a coefficient calculated correctly then described as evidence of causation, or a probability quoted without the condition it was calculated under. Self-contained enough to clear late in a plan.

subjects.name: Calculus
subjects.levels: Both courses; deeper at Analysis HL
subjects.description: Chain-rule errors inside composites and sign errors in definite integrals account for a large share of Higher Level losses. These are reasoning losses, visible in the working, and they respond to repetition rather than to re-explanation.

subjects.name: Proof
subjects.description: Marked on the validity of each step, so a right conclusion reached by an unjustified route scores poorly. Shows up unmistakably in the reasoning category and takes three or four sessions of structured practice to shift.

subjects.name: Paper 3
subjects.description: Sixty minutes, fifty-five marks, two extended problem-solving questions. The characteristic loss is timing: twenty minutes spent on one stalled part and whole later parts unattempted. It needs four or five timed attempts to build the parking reflex.

subjects.name: The exploration
subjects.description: Twenty marks across five criteria, with twelve to twenty pages recommended. Not diagnosed from a mock script at all, which is why it gets forgotten in a post-mock plan even though it is a fifth of the grade.

subjects.name: Calculator technique
subjects.description: Produces losses that look like content gaps and are not: a missed second root, a window set so an intersection is off screen, exactly rather than at most in a binomial question. Drillable in a handful of sessions on the school's own model.

subjects.name: Non-calculator arithmetic
subjects.description: Analysis forbids a calculator on Paper 1 at both levels, so slow mental arithmetic produces timing losses on that paper specifically. If the mock shows a split between Paper 1 and Paper 2 performance, this is usually the reason.

sections.heading: Reading a Diploma mathematics mock script properly
paragraphs: Take the script and a pen and go through it mark by mark rather than looking at the total. Every lost mark falls into one of four categories, and the point of the exercise is the count rather than the correction. Content not known. Question wording misread. Reasoning not shown. Time ran out. Twenty minutes of this produces more usable information than a term of general revision.

In Diploma mathematics the reasoning category is reliably larger than families expect. Marks are allocated to visible steps, particularly in proof work and across Paper 3, so a correct final answer reached by an unjustified route collects the answer mark and forfeits the method marks. Students read that as having got the question right, which is why the habit survives two years of practice.

The timing category is the one most often misread as a content problem. A student who routinely leaves the last part of a long question unattempted looks, on the total, like a student who does not know that material. They frequently do know it. The fix is marks-per-minute arithmetic and the discipline of abandoning a stuck question, which is two sessions of work rather than a term of teaching.

What the script will not tell you is anything about the exploration, which is a fifth of the grade and is not examined in a mock. That is why a post-mock plan has to be written deliberately rather than derived from the script alone. If the exploration is unfinished in the second-year winter, it belongs at the top of the plan regardless of what the mock says.

sections.heading: Interleaved against blocked practice, and why the better one feels worse
paragraphs: Revision design is a real variable and most families treat it as a non-question. The default is blocked practice: work through trigonometry, then work through calculus, then work through statistics. It feels productive, progress is visible within a session, and retention afterwards is poor. Interleaved practice, where topics are mixed within every session, feels worse while it is happening and retains considerably better.

The reason is mechanical rather than mysterious. In blocked practice the student knows which method applies before reading the question, because the last six questions used it. In an examination nothing announces the method, so selecting the right approach is itself an examinable skill, and blocked practice never exercises it. Interleaved sets force that selection every single question.

This has a direct consequence for how sessions should be structured, and it is the reason to design the week rather than let it emerge. A session that mixes four topics will feel less satisfying to everybody present, including the tutor, and will produce better scripts six weeks later. A parent watching a session and judging it by how smoothly it went is judging on the wrong signal.

Spacing belongs with it. Returning to material three and six weeks after it was first worked on, briefly, outperforms a single longer session at the time by a wide margin. In practice that means every session carries a short block of older material, and the student stops being surprised by topics they covered in October. None of this costs extra; it is a scheduling decision.

sections.heading: The calculator is a drillable skill with its own schedule
paragraphs: Calculator losses are the most commonly misdiagnosed category on a mathematics script, because they look exactly like content gaps. A plausible wrong number with correct method written above it is almost always a machine problem rather than a mathematics problem, and it is fixable in a handful of sessions. Nobody treats it as a scheduled piece of work.

The skills are finite. Solving an equation numerically and noticing a second root. Finding a graph intersection with a sensible window. Running a regression and reading its coefficient. Normal and inverse normal calculations in the right direction. Binomial probabilities, distinguishing exactly from at most. Numerical derivatives and definite integrals with the limits in the right order. Generating a sequence in a table. And angle mode, every time.

There is a practical complication in Abu Dhabi households. Schools standardise on a model, and students who own a different one follow video tutorials for a machine they do not have. The menus differ, and under examination pressure that difference costs real seconds. Settle on the school's model, learn that one properly, and make sure the tutor can work with it on screen.

For Analysis and Approaches students the mirror-image risk applies, because Paper 1 forbids a calculator at both levels. Two years of permanent access produces arithmetic that is competent only with support, and that shows on a script as a split between Paper 1 and Paper 2 performance. If the mock shows that split, non-calculator practice is the single highest-return item on the plan.

sections.heading: What to abandon, and when the decision is right
paragraphs: Every short plan requires something to be dropped, and dropping is the hardest instruction to follow because it feels like giving up. It is not. It is arithmetic. A topic that appears rarely and is genuinely not understood will consume hours that would produce more marks elsewhere, and the student who tries to cover everything thinly scores below the student who covers most things properly.

The decision rule is a two-by-two. A topic that appears often and is understood needs maintenance only. One that appears often and is not understood is the top priority, whatever it costs. One that appears rarely and is understood needs nothing. And one that appears rarely and is not understood should be abandoned deliberately, in writing, so the student stops feeling guilty about it every time they open a paper.

That last point about writing it down matters more than it sounds. An abandoned topic that has been explicitly abandoned stops consuming attention. An abandoned topic that nobody has acknowledged continues to generate low-level anxiety every week, and anxiety consumes hours as effectively as studying does. Making the decision explicit is itself a productive act.

The honest limit on all of this needs stating. Four to ten focused weeks with a well-designed plan can move a grade boundary and sometimes two in mathematics, which responds to technique work better than most subjects. It will not move four. No provider can guarantee a grade, a score or an improvement, including us, and anyone offering one is selling rather than teaching.

sections.heading: Four weeks out: what still works
paragraphs: With four weeks to the papers, the set of things that still change an outcome is small and specific, and most of what families instinctively do is outside it. Content teaching has very low returns at this point unless a topic is both frequent and entirely unseen. Re-reading notes has none. What works is pacing, the parking reflex, short daily recall and sleep, in roughly that order of neglect.

Pacing first, because it is the cheapest. Divide the marks by the minutes, write the rate at the top of the paper, and practise checking against it mid-question. A student with a rate can tell within a question whether they are behind and act. A student without one discovers the problem when the invigilator calls fifteen minutes with three parts remaining.

The parking reflex is second and is harder, because it is psychological rather than technical. Leaving a question with a mark or two taken and returning later is strictly better than spending eleven minutes on it, and in the moment it feels like failure. It takes four or five timed attempts to become available under pressure, which is why four weeks is enough to build it and two is not.

Then short daily recall rather than long evening sessions. Fifteen or twenty minutes on formulae, standard methods and the current error log, every day, beats three hours twice a week at this stage. And sleep, which parents are reluctant to treat as revision and which is the single biggest determinant of whether any of the above survives contact with an examination hall.

sections.heading: Al Nahyan: the schools, the commute and the usable hour
paragraphs: Al Nahyan sits in the city east of Al Mushrif, with most of the schools its students attend a short drive away in Al Mushrif, Al Bateen and the surrounding districts. By Abu Dhabi standards the journeys are short, which means the limiting factor on a mathematics session is what else is in the week rather than the road, and that is a better problem to have.

The practical range is narrow here. Students attending schools in Al Mushrif are commonly home between 15:15 and 15:45, which makes a 17:00 session realistic. Students travelling to Al Bateen or across a bridge are closer to 16:15 and do better at 19:30. Those attending schools out towards Khalifa City are the latest and almost always fix an evening slot for the whole year.

Mock season is where Al Nahyan has a real advantage. Schools across Abu Dhabi release students for parts of it, and because the commute from here is short, those released days are genuinely usable rather than theoretical. A daytime session with a rested student, working from a script marked three days earlier, is the single most productive hour available in the Diploma year.

For mathematics specifically, two shorter sessions a week work better than one long one, because accuracy consolidates in the gap between contacts. That is easier to schedule here than in the outer communities, and easier still on video, since two sessions a week means two journeys avoided rather than one. Supply the actual arrival time rather than the preferred start time when booking.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the spring break and the weeks that are not there
paragraphs: A plan built on calendar weeks rather than teaching weeks will break, and the gap between the two is substantial in the UAE. Most Abu Dhabi private schools run three terms with a winter break around the turn of the year and a spring break towards the end of March, and that spring break sits squarely inside the post-mock period this page describes.

Ramadan moves roughly eleven days earlier each year and currently falls in the spring, increasingly overlapping the run-up to the May session. Schools shorten the day, which frees the afternoon, but for mathematics specifically the freed afternoon is a poor window: arithmetic accuracy degrades faster than discursive work when a household is fasting and preparing. A post-Iftar slot, commonly 20:30 to 22:00, works considerably better.

Some families prefer to pause for the month and resume afterwards, which is a legitimate choice we would rather you made deliberately than drifted into. Paying for sessions nobody attends is the worst available outcome, and a month lost by accident at that point in the second Diploma year is expensive while a month paused on purpose is manageable.

Do the arithmetic before agreeing anything. Take the session month, subtract the spring break, subtract the weeks your school has reserved for study leave, subtract Ramadan if your household reduces sessions, and subtract travel you already know about. Most Al Nahyan families find the figure four to six weeks below their first estimate, and a ten-week plan with six real weeks in it fails predictably.

sections.heading: What it costs, and what we will not claim
paragraphs: Mathematics support costs more per grade point after the mocks than before them, which is market behaviour rather than a judgement. Demand concentrates in the spring, the formats families want are intensive, and specialists able to work on a named paper are among the scarcest people in this market. The same outcome bought in the first Diploma year costs materially less.

Al Nahyan sits close enough to most of the city's Diploma schools that families here compare tutors on price rather than on distance, so the published numbers are the useful ones. At the floor of the Abu Dhabi market, university-student tutors online advertise from around AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik on their own pages — one lesson a week for a month puts that at AED 132 to 260. A qualified subject tutor online sits at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200 and TutorChase quoting around AED 270, which is AED 600 to 1,200 a month on the same weekly rhythm. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, and premium named tutors have been quoted to AED 650 at BartyED — AED 2,600 a month for a single weekly hour, which is the figure worth holding in mind before a second-year panic sets the budget.

One band on this page we do not sell into, and it should be named. An in-home visit in Abu Dhabi is quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, with the tutor's journey priced inside the fee rather than billed beside it. IB Gram runs no home visits anywhere in Abu Dhabi; in-home tutoring is a service we operate only in India. So a family in Al Nahyan weighing a tutor at the door against a tutor on a screen is comparing our price with somebody else's, not with ours, and that is precisely why the bands above carry their sources. A quote — ours included — should be measurable against something a parent can go and read for themselves, not against a number we made up.

What we will not claim: no provider can guarantee a grade, a score or an improvement, including us. No regulator or examination board accredits IB Gram, we hold no ADEK, MoHRE or board approval, and there is no Abu Dhabi office. No tutor here writes an exploration, drafts it or edits it to completion; the work must be the student's own and the school supervisor signs it off.

process.title: Send the mock script, not the grade
process.description: A total tells us almost nothing. The script tells us whether the losses are content, wording, reasoning not shown or timing, and those four need different remedies over different timescales. Twenty minutes with the paper produces more usable information than any amount of conversation about how the subject is going.

process.title: Say which course and level
process.description: Analysis or Applications, Higher or Standard. Those four combinations are four different jobs, and for Higher Level students Paper 3 is a separate piece of work from Papers 1 and 2. A component-level request is matched faster because it is a narrower search.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One per family, before any payment and with no card details taken. Ask whether a calculator is permitted on Paper 1 in your child's course and what Paper 3 is worth. Published facts, so a specialist answers immediately. Then judge whether a specific diagnosis came out of the hour.

process.title: Design the week rather than letting it emerge
process.description: Two shorter sessions, interleaved topic sets, a short spaced block of older material each time, and daily recall of fifteen to twenty minutes. It will feel less satisfying than working through one topic at a time, and it produces better scripts six weeks later.

process.title: Write down what is abandoned
process.description: Rare topics that are genuinely not understood should be dropped explicitly rather than left hanging, because an unacknowledged gap generates weekly anxiety and anxiety consumes hours. Making the decision in writing is itself a productive act and students are visibly relieved by it.

whyPoints.title: The script read mark by mark
whyPoints.description: Every lost mark is classified as content, wording, reasoning not shown or timing, and the tally decides the plan. In Diploma mathematics the reasoning category is almost always larger than families expect, and it is the one a grade total hides completely.

whyPoints.title: Revision design treated as a variable
whyPoints.description: Interleaved practice outperforms blocked practice and feels worse while it is happening, which is why it has to be designed rather than left to the student. We mix topics in every session and build in spaced return to older material.

whyPoints.title: Calculator work scheduled, not assumed
whyPoints.description: A plausible wrong number with correct method above it is a machine problem, not a mathematics problem, and it is fixable in a handful of sessions. We drill the school's own standardised model rather than whichever one a video tutorial happens to use.

whyPoints.title: Abandonment made explicit
whyPoints.description: Every short plan requires something to be dropped, and an unacknowledged gap generates anxiety every week. We write down what is abandoned and why, which stops it consuming attention and lets the remaining hours go where the marks are.

whyPoints.title: Released mock days actually used
whyPoints.description: Abu Dhabi schools release students for parts of mock season, and because Al Nahyan journeys are short those days are genuinely usable. A daytime session with a rested student and a three-day-old script is the most productive hour in the Diploma year.

whyPoints.title: No guarantees and no claimed approvals
whyPoints.description: Four to ten focused weeks can move a boundary and sometimes two in mathematics. It will not move four. No provider can guarantee a grade including us, no regulator accredits IB Gram, and every figure here carries its source and date.

faqs.question: When is the best moment to bring in an IB maths tutor in Al Nahyan?
faqs.answer: The fortnight the mock script comes back, for three reasons. Every lost mark is visible and the student can still reconstruct their reasoning. Schools across Abu Dhabi release students for parts of mock season, so a daytime session becomes possible. And because Al Nahyan journeys are short, those released days are genuinely usable rather than theoretical. Two or three sessions in that window produce a plan for the remaining term that is based on evidence rather than guesswork.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a maths tutor to Al Nahyan homes?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Mathematics lessons here are one to one over live video with a shared whiteboard, which suits the subject because every line of working stays visible and is saved for rereading. In-home visits in Abu Dhabi are quoted in the market at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel priced into the figure.

faqs.question: How do we read a maths mock script rather than just the total?
faqs.answer: Mark by mark, with a pen, sorting every lost mark into one of four boxes: content not known, question wording misread, reasoning not shown, or time ran out. Then count the boxes. Twenty minutes of this produces more usable information than a term of general revision, because the four categories need completely different remedies over completely different timescales, and the tally almost always contradicts what the student assumed had gone wrong.

faqs.question: Why is reasoning not shown such a big category in DP maths?
faqs.answer: Because marks are allocated to visible steps rather than to final answers, particularly in proof work and throughout Paper 3. A student who reaches the correct answer by an unjustified route collects the answer mark and forfeits the method marks, then reads the question as one they got right. That misreading is why the habit survives two years of practice, and it takes three to six weeks to change because it is a habit rather than a piece of knowledge.

faqs.question: My son's totals look like a content problem, but is it really?
faqs.answer: Possibly not. The commonest misdiagnosis is a timing problem reading as a content problem: a student who routinely leaves the final part of a long question unattempted looks, on the total, like somebody who does not know that material. They frequently do know it. Look at where on the paper the losses sit. If they cluster at the end of long questions while earlier work is sound, the remedy is pacing and takes two sessions, not a term.

faqs.question: Is interleaved practice really better than working through one topic?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it reliably feels worse while you are doing it, which is why it has to be designed rather than left to the student. In blocked practice the student knows which method applies before reading the question, because the last six used it. In an examination nothing announces the method, so selection is itself an examinable skill that blocked practice never exercises. Mixed sets force that selection on every question.

faqs.question: How should spaced revision work across a Diploma maths course?
faqs.answer: Every session carries a short block of material first worked on three and six weeks earlier, briefly, before anything new. That outperforms a single longer session at the time by a wide margin and costs nothing extra, because it is a scheduling decision rather than additional hours. The visible effect is that a student stops being surprised in April by topics they covered in October, which is otherwise one of the most demoralising experiences of the second year.

faqs.question: Which calculator skills are worth drilling deliberately?
faqs.answer: Angle mode, checked monthly. Numerical equation solving with attention to second roots. Graph intersections with a sensible window. Regression and its coefficient, plus the interpretation. Normal and inverse normal in both directions. Binomial probabilities, distinguishing exactly from at most. Numerical derivatives and definite integrals with limits in the right order. Storing values rather than rounding mid-question. All finite, all drillable in a handful of sessions, and all producing errors that look exactly like content gaps.

faqs.question: Does it matter which calculator model my child uses?
faqs.answer: It matters more than families expect. Schools standardise on a model, and a student who owns a different one follows video tutorials for a machine they do not have. The menus differ and under examination pressure that costs real seconds repeatedly. Settle on the school's model, learn that one properly, and make sure any tutor can work with it on screen. For Analysis students remember Paper 1 forbids a calculator entirely at both levels.

faqs.question: Should we abandon topics my daughter has never understood?
faqs.answer: Some of them, deliberately, and in writing. The rule is a two-by-two: frequent and understood needs maintenance only, frequent and not understood is the top priority whatever it costs, rare and understood needs nothing, and rare and not understood should be dropped. Writing the decision down matters, because an unacknowledged gap generates low-level anxiety every week and anxiety consumes hours as effectively as studying does.

faqs.question: What still works when the papers are four weeks away?
faqs.answer: Pacing, the parking reflex, short daily recall and sleep, roughly in that order of neglect. Content teaching has very low returns unless a topic is both frequent and entirely unseen, and re-reading notes has none. Divide marks by minutes, write the rate on the paper, practise abandoning a stuck question and returning. For Higher Level students one final timed Paper 3 attempt belongs in week three rather than the last week.

faqs.question: Why practise abandoning a question rather than solving it?
faqs.answer: Because leaving a question with a mark or two taken and returning later is strictly better than spending eleven minutes on it, and in the moment it feels like failure, which is why it has to be trained rather than explained. It takes four or five timed attempts to become available under pressure. That is why four weeks is enough to build the reflex and two is not, and why it belongs on the plan rather than in a conversation.

faqs.question: Does the mock script tell us anything about the exploration?
faqs.answer: Nothing at all, which is the trap in a post-mock plan. The exploration is twenty per cent of the mathematics grade, marked out of twenty across five criteria, and it is not examined in a mock. A plan derived from the script alone will omit a fifth of the grade. If the exploration is unfinished in the second-year winter it belongs at the top of the plan regardless of what the mock result says.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan affect a maths plan in Al Nahyan?
faqs.answer: It changes the hour rather than the plan, and mathematics is affected more than most subjects. Schools shorten the day, which frees the afternoon, but arithmetic accuracy degrades faster than discursive work when a household is fasting and preparing, so that freed afternoon is a weak window specifically for this subject. A post-Iftar slot, commonly 20:30 to 22:00, works considerably better and is simple to staff on video because nobody is driving.

faqs.question: Can two shorter sessions a week be scheduled from Al Nahyan?
faqs.answer: More easily than in most of Abu Dhabi, because the journeys here are short. Students attending Al Mushrif schools are commonly home between 15:15 and 15:45, which makes a 17:00 session realistic alongside a later one in the week. Two contacts suit mathematics better than one long session, because procedural accuracy consolidates in the gap between them. On video it also means two journeys avoided rather than one, which matters across a term.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-nahyan.closingHeading: Send the script, not the grade
abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-nahyan.closingBody: The most useful thing you can send is the mock paper itself, with the course and level named. From it we will classify every lost mark into content, wording, reasoning or timing, tell you which category dominates, and design the remaining weeks around that rather than around a syllabus checklist. We will also tell you plainly what the time left can and cannot reach. Then your child meets a specialist in that course on a free trial lesson, live online, one to one, twice a week where the week allows.
