abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-raha-beac.tutorsIntro: These are the Mathematics specialists who take Al Raha Beach students: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, Applications and Interpretation at either level, MYP Extended maths, and the Exploration that sits behind the Internal Assessment. Each one works to your child's own school deadlines.

intro.heading: What you are actually paying for when you hire an IB maths tutor
paragraphs: Start with the arithmetic rather than the brochure. A family in Al Raha Beach booking one hour a week for a school year buys roughly 34 to 36 teaching hours. At the budget end of the Abu Dhabi market that is a commitment somewhere near AED 1,600 to AED 5,400 for the year. At specialist rates it is closer to AED 7,000 to AED 15,000. The number that matters is not the hourly figure on the quote. It is the total, and what share of that total is spent on teaching rather than on logistics.

The travel premium is the single largest avoidable cost in this market. Bestimate's Dubai and Abu Dhabi rate work puts in-home one-to-one tuition at roughly AED 180 to 350 an hour, and independent home tutors advertise AED 200 to 500. Online qualified subject tutors sit at roughly AED 150 to 300. Unitors publishes AED 200 as its own IB starting rate online. The gap between those two columns is not a difference in teaching quality. It is a car, a parking space in a villa community, and forty minutes of someone's evening.

The second avoidable cost is a mismatch between the tutor and the course. Al Raha Beach sits in the middle of a corridor of Diploma schools, and Mathematics splits four ways at Diploma level: Analysis and Approaches at Higher and Standard Level, Applications and Interpretation at Higher and Standard Level. A tutor comfortable with AA Standard Level is not automatically useful on AI Higher Level, where the toolkit paper and the statistics content look nothing like AA's calculus spine. Families pay for ten hours before discovering this, which is ten hours of the year gone.

The third is buying hours when the child needs a diagnosis. A student losing marks on Paper 2 because the graphical display calculator is being used as a last resort rather than a first tool does not need another twenty hours of content revision. They need two hours on calculator strategy and then a different plan. IB maths tuition in Al Raha Beach is worth buying when it is pointed at a named problem, and close to worthless when it is bought as general reassurance before an exam season.

So this page is written as a budget. It publishes the market bands with their sources, shows what the travel premium buys and does not buy, sets out where the money is usually wasted, and puts the AA against AI decision in a table because that decision changes the bill more than any discount will. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform with no affiliation to any school, authority or examination board named here. Lessons for families in Al Raha Beach are delivered as one-to-one online tuition; IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, and home tutoring is a service we run only in India.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-raha-beac.programmesIntro: Al Raha Beach families draw on the full IB continuum, and maths support looks different at every stage. The four programmes below set out where the maths load sits and what an Abu Dhabi student in that stage is usually asking for.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Maths in the PYP is embedded in units of inquiry rather than taught as a named timetabled subject, so a parent often cannot tell from a report card whether number fluency is secure. The transferable pieces are place value, fraction sense, the four operations with decimals, and reading a scale. A PYP student who leaves Year 6 shaky on fractions will meet the same gap again in MYP algebra three years later.
programmes.countryNote: Al Raha Beach children overwhelmingly attend PYP schools in the Al Raha and Khalifa City corridor, which means a short school run and a realistic 4.30pm start. At this stage the cheapest intervention in the whole of a parent's spending is twenty minutes of arithmetic practice twice a week rather than a weekly hour of formal tuition.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Mathematics runs as Standard or Extended, and the eAssessment at the end of MYP 5 is marked against four criteria: Knowing and understanding, Investigating patterns, Communicating, and Applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Extended is the route that keeps Analysis and Approaches Higher Level open. The criterion that consistently costs marks is Investigating patterns, because students find the rule and then stop before justifying it.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP to Diploma transition is where Al Raha Beach families usually first spend money on maths. A student arriving in DP1 from MYP Standard rather than Extended typically needs eight to twelve hours of algebraic fluency work before calculus is approachable, and that cost is far lower in the summer before DP1 than in the autumn term of it.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Diploma maths is compulsory, and the four routes carry very different loads. Analysis and Approaches is calculus-led and proof-heavy; Applications and Interpretation is statistics-led and modelling-heavy. At Standard Level there are two papers; at Higher Level there are three, with Paper 3 worth 20% and built from two extended problem-solving questions. The Internal Assessment, the Exploration, is 20% at both levels.
programmes.countryNote: This is where the money is either well spent or lost. Diploma families in Al Raha Beach commonly buy two years of weekly tuition when a targeted year would serve better: DP1 term two for the course foundations, then a Paper 3 and Exploration block in DP2. An online IB maths tutor in Abu Dhabi can be booked for a defined block rather than an open-ended retainer.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme pairs DP courses with a career-related study and a Personal and Professional Skills core. Maths usually appears as a single DP course alongside the career strand, most often Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level, because the modelling and financial mathematics content maps onto business and engineering pathways more directly than calculus does.
programmes.countryNote: CP cohorts in Abu Dhabi are small, which means in-area tutor supply for a CP maths course is thin and the travel premium on a home tutor is at its most pointless. One-to-one online lessons remove the supply problem entirely, because the pool is not limited to people who can reach Al Raha Beach by 5pm.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-raha-beac.subjectsIntro: Maths is the reason most Al Raha Beach families reach this page, so the grid below leads with the four Diploma maths routes and the Exploration, then covers the subjects whose grades move when maths improves.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL
subjects.description: Three papers, with Paper 3 at 20% built from two long problem-solving questions. The content spine is calculus, proof, complex numbers and vectors. Marks go on reasoning that is correct but unwritten, and on integration by substitution attempted without checking the limits.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches SL
subjects.description: Two papers, no Paper 3. Differentiation and integration of a narrower function set, plus binomial expansion, sequences and trigonometric identities. The repeated loss is in Paper 1 non-calculator algebra, where surd and index manipulation is the real obstacle rather than the calculus itself.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation HL
subjects.description: Statistics-led with a heavy modelling load: regression, hypothesis testing, matrices, graph theory and differential equations solved numerically. Paper 3 rewards a student who can interpret output and write a conclusion in context, and penalises one who reports a number without units.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation SL
subjects.description: Two papers with the graphical display calculator assumed throughout. Financial maths, normal distribution, chi-squared and bivariate statistics dominate. Students lose marks by rounding too early and by failing to state the hypotheses before running a test.

subjects.name: The Mathematics Exploration (Internal Assessment)
subjects.levels: HL and SL, 20% of the grade
subjects.description: A 12 to 20 page individual piece marked on presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics. The commonest failure is a topic so broad that the maths stays at course level. A tutor may question a draft and point at the criteria; the writing stays the student's own.

subjects.name: MYP Mathematics (Extended)
subjects.description: The route that preserves access to Analysis and Approaches Higher Level. Quadratics, surds, sequences, trigonometry beyond right-angled triangles and probability. The criterion worth targeting is Investigating patterns, where a general rule must be justified rather than merely stated.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Diploma Physics shares a border with maths: kinematics graphs, gradient and area interpretation, logarithmic plots in the nuclear and thermal topics, and uncertainty propagation. A student weak on rearranging formulae loses physics marks that look like physics gaps but are algebra gaps.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mole calculations, equilibrium constants, pH and the Arrhenius equation all sit on algebra and logarithms. The Chemistry Internal Assessment also needs a defensible treatment of uncertainty, which is where a maths-literate tutor adds more than a chemistry-only one.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Higher Level Economics carries quantitative questions on elasticity, tax incidence, and the calculation of national income figures. Diagram accuracy and the correct labelling of axes carry marks, and students who can differentiate find the marginal reasoning considerably easier.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Logic, binary and hexadecimal conversion, Big-O reasoning and the Higher Level abstract data structures topic all reward mathematical habits. The internal assessment is a solution developed for a real client, and the documentation is where marks are most often left behind.

The tutor works through a recent paper or two with your child, marks against the real criteria, and reports which losses are content, which are method and which are exam technique. sections.heading: What an IB maths tutor costs in Al Raha Beach, by the month
paragraphs: Hourly rates mislead parents because nobody buys one hour. The useful number is what leaves the account each month, and on a weekly one-hour schedule that is roughly four or five sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour tuition in this market run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Those are the brackets a family in Al Raha Beach should be planning against.

Against those monthly figures, the packages advertised in the emirate start to make sense. An online package at around AED 799 a month for eight sessions works out near AED 100 a session, which is budget-tier pricing bought in bulk. An in-home package at AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits is roughly AED 200 to 225 an hour, which is the in-home band with travel folded in. Neither is a bargain or a rip-off; they are different products.

The table below is the market, not an IB Gram price list. Read the right-hand column first. A family comparing AED 180 with AED 300 is comparing the wrong things if one figure includes a drive to Al Raha Beach and the other does not. The travel premium is real money and it buys physical presence, which is worth something to some students and nothing to others. What it does not buy is a wider choice of specialist, and at Higher Level that is usually the more valuable of the two.

sections.heading: Where families in this corridor waste money on maths tuition
paragraphs: The first waste is buying hours before buying a diagnosis. A parent sees a 4 on a report, books twenty hours, and the tutor spends six of them finding out what is wrong. Those six hours cost the same as the useful ones. Four deliberate diagnostic sessions at the front end change the shape of the whole year, because they turn a vague problem into a list: quadratic inequalities, the chain rule in composite functions, calculator-based solving on Paper 2.

The second is paying a specialist rate for work that does not need one. Catching up on MYP algebraic manipulation does not require a Higher Level Analysis and Approaches specialist at the top of the band. Interpreting a Paper 3 mark scheme does. Families who use one rate for everything either overpay on the easy work or under-resource the hard work, and the second is the more expensive mistake because it shows up in the final grade.

The third is the retainer that outlives its purpose. A weekly slot booked in DP1 term one often runs for two years because nobody cancels it, long after the original gap closed. The honest version of a tutoring plan has review points in it. At the end of each term, the question should be whether the named problem from the diagnostic is still a problem, and if it is not, the hours should move to the next one or stop.

The fourth is duplication. Several Al Raha and Khalifa City schools run their own after-school maths clinics at no extra charge, and a paid tutor covering the same ground in the same week is money spent twice. Ask the school what support already exists before buying, and point the paid hours at what the school does not cover: the Exploration, Paper 3, and the gaps that are personal to your child rather than general to the class.

sections.heading: Online against in-home maths tuition for an Al Raha Beach household
paragraphs: IB Gram delivers to Al Raha Beach as one-to-one online tuition over live video. We do not run home visits in the UAE; that is a service we offer only in India. Being plain about that is more useful than pretending otherwise, because it lets the comparison be made on the merits rather than on availability.

The case for online in this specific corridor is supply. Al Raha Beach is roughly equidistant from the island campuses and the inland Khalifa City cluster, which is pleasant for a school run and unhelpful for finding a tutor. The pool of people who hold a Mathematics degree, know Applications and Interpretation Higher Level, and can be physically present in Al Muneera at 5pm on a Tuesday is small. Remove the travel constraint and the pool is the pool of qualified Mathematics teachers, which is a different order of choice.

The case for in-home is real and worth stating. Some students, particularly younger ones and those with attention difficulties, work better with another person in the room. A physical presence makes it harder to disengage. Written work on paper is easier to supervise than work on a tablet. For a Year 7 student who needs supervision as much as teaching, that can matter more than specialist depth.

For Diploma maths specifically, the balance tips towards online, and the reason is the whiteboard. Mathematics at this level is worked out line by line, and a shared digital whiteboard with a screen-shared past paper and a recorded session is a better teaching surface than a kitchen table. The student can rewatch the worked solution. That is not available from a visit.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation: the choice that changes the bill
paragraphs: No tutoring decision costs an Al Raha Beach family more than the maths route chosen at the end of MYP 5. It sets two years of difficulty, determines whether Paper 3 exists, and narrows or widens the degrees your child can apply to. Getting it wrong and switching in DP1 term two is expensive in both money and time, because the content overlap between the two courses is smaller than the shared name suggests.

Analysis and Approaches is the calculus route. It rewards algebraic fluency and formal reasoning, and at Higher Level it includes proof, complex numbers and vectors. Applications and Interpretation is the statistics and modelling route, built around the graphical display calculator, regression, hypothesis testing and, at Higher Level, matrices and graph theory. A student who enjoys a clean algebraic manipulation and a student who enjoys interpreting a dataset are not the same student.

University prerequisites are where the real cost sits. Engineering, mathematics, physics and most economics degrees at competitive universities expect Analysis and Approaches, commonly at Higher Level. Many business, psychology, design and life-science routes accept either. Universities in the UAE and the wider Gulf vary, and the only reliable method is to read the prerequisite page for the specific programme and the specific intake year rather than relying on a general rule.

The practical advice is to spend money on the decision rather than on recovering from it. Two or three hours with a Mathematics specialist at the end of MYP 5, working through sample questions from both courses with your child, costs less than one month of remedial tuition in DP1. A Maths AA tutor in Abu Dhabi and a Maths AI tutor in Abu Dhabi are looking for different things in a student, and they will tell you honestly which way the evidence points.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in context: fees, exam entry and a two-year Diploma plan
paragraphs: Tuition is a small line next to school fees, which is exactly why it gets approved without scrutiny. Putting it beside the other numbers changes how carefully it is bought. A family already paying substantial annual fees for a Diploma place in this corridor is adding a few thousand dirhams, and the question worth asking is not whether it is affordable but whether it is the best use of that few thousand.

The emirate-level backdrop is relevant. In Dubai, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees would not rise for the following academic year under the emirate's economic incentives package. Abu Dhabi runs its own fee regime through ADEK, which governs when and how a school may apply for a tuition increase. Neither authority regulates private tutoring rates, which is why the tutoring market has a five-fold spread and school fees do not.

Exam entry is the cost parents forget. Diploma candidates sitting through their school pay registration through the school and it is usually folded into fees. A private candidate pays separately, and the figure depends on the number of subjects and the centre. Any family considering a resit outside their school should get that quote in writing before planning the tutoring around it.

Set against those figures, the table below sketches a two-year Diploma maths plan built the way this page argues for: a diagnostic block, a lighter maintenance year, an Exploration clinic, and an intensive before the exam series. The total is deliberately shown against the alternative of two years of unexamined weekly tuition, because the two are not far apart in cost and are very far apart in effect.

sections.heading: What a maths tutor may and may not do with the Exploration
paragraphs: The Mathematics Internal Assessment is 20% of the grade at both levels and it must be the student's own work. The boundary is not a matter of taste. The IB treats the submission of work that is not the candidate's own as malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student, including the loss of the Diploma. A page in this market that is vague about this boundary is doing families a disservice, and at least one site competing for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments outright.

What a tutor may do is substantial. They may discuss whether a proposed topic will support mathematics beyond course level. They may explain a criterion in the published guidance and point at where a draft fails to meet it. They may teach a technique the student has decided to use. They may ask why a step follows from the one before, which is the most useful question available and the one students answer least well. They may read a draft and respond with questions.

What a tutor may not do is write, rewrite, edit to completion, supply text, supply the maths, choose the topic on the student's behalf, or hand over a worked model to be adapted. IB Gram tutors do none of those things, and a tutor who offers to is a risk to your child's Diploma rather than a shortcut to it. If a provider's pitch includes a finished piece of work, that is the signal to stop the conversation.

Keeping a record helps. Schools ask candidates to account for how a piece of work developed, and a student who can point to dated drafts and a note of what was discussed in each session is in a far stronger position than one who cannot. Sessions on the Exploration are therefore organised around the student's own draft history, not around a tutor's template.

sections.heading: Is your tutor legally permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted, and it is permitted by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The permit is granted free of charge for two years. Anyone offering private tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and the published guidance does not set out a fine schedule, so no figure should be quoted to you as fact.

The eligible categories are wider than parents expect. They include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. The application route is MoHRE's own service, 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', which lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

One restriction matters specifically in Abu Dhabi. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a comparable restriction. This has been press-reported rather than read from the policy document itself, so treat it as the direction of travel and verify the current wording with ADEK. The practical consequence is clear enough: do not seek out your child's own class teacher as a paid tutor.

For an Al Raha Beach family the verification question is simple to ask and revealing to hear answered. Ask whether the tutor holds a MoHRE private tuition work permit, ask which category they hold it under, and ask whether they are employed at your child's school. A provider who cannot answer has not asked.

sections.heading: The exam calendar, counted backwards from the series
paragraphs: Tutoring money is spent well or badly depending on when it is spent, and the calendar is what decides that. Abu Dhabi Diploma candidates sit the May session. Cambridge IGCSE and O Level candidates in the UAE sit the June and November series; the February and March series is offered to India only and does not apply here. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Those are the fixed points everything else hangs from.

IB session and results dates are not restated on this page. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so rather than publish a date that might be wrong, the honest instruction is to take the exact exam window and results date from your child's IB coordinator or from ibo.org directly. What can be said safely is the shape: internal deadlines for the Exploration land well before the exam window, and mock examinations sit a term ahead of it.

Counting backwards is the useful exercise. If the Exploration draft is due to the school in the first half of DP2, the topic has to be settled in late DP1, which means the viability conversation belongs in DP1 term three and not in DP2. If Paper 3 is 20% of a Higher Level grade, the intensive work on it belongs in the twelve weeks before the series, not in the final fortnight when every other subject is also competing for time.

For Cambridge candidates, the zone detail is worth knowing. Every exam centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask your school which zone it sits in, then read that timetable rather than a general one.

sections.heading: Getting started, and what happens when no specialist is free
paragraphs: The honest version of starting is short. You tell us the board, the subject, the level and the component that is going wrong. We propose a Mathematics specialist and a time. The first lesson is a free trial with no card required, and after it you decide whether to continue. Nothing about that process requires anyone to travel to Al Raha Beach.

Matching for Diploma maths usually takes a couple of working days for Analysis and Approaches at either level, because the pool is deepest there. Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level takes longer, because fewer teachers have carried a cohort through the matrices, graph theory and numerical differential equations content. Specific pairings, such as Applications and Interpretation Higher Level alongside Physics Higher Level with the same tutor, take longer again.

When no suitable specialist is free, there are three honest answers and we give whichever is true. The first is a waiting time, with a date. The second is a tutor based outside the UAE who teaches the same syllabus over the same live video on Gulf Standard Time, which is how IB Gram serves many Gulf families and which we disclose rather than conceal. The third is that we cannot cover it well, in which case we say so instead of placing a generalist into a Higher Level seat.

What a family should expect in return is a record. After the diagnostic block you receive a list of named topics and components rather than a general impression, and after each term there is a review point where the plan either moves on or stops. That is also the mechanism that stops a retainer outliving its purpose, which this page has argued is where most of the wasted money in this market goes.

process.title: Tell us the component, not just the subject
process.description: Board, course, level and the thing that is actually going wrong: Paper 1 algebra, the Exploration topic, Paper 3 reasoning, calculator strategy. A request that names a component gets matched faster and more accurately than one that says a child needs help with maths.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One lesson, at no charge and with no card required, with the proposed Mathematics specialist. Watch for whether your child talks during it. A trial where the tutor explains for fifty minutes and the student says four words tells you something useful about the next thirty hours.

process.title: Buy a diagnosis before a block
process.description: Four sessions used as an investigation rather than as teaching, producing a written list of named topics and components. This is the step families skip and then pay for twice, because an undiagnosed problem absorbs the first six hours of any block of tuition.

process.title: Set the schedule around the school run
process.description: Al Raha Beach students mostly travel inland to school, so slots from 4.45pm work better than mid-afternoon ones. Lessons run over live video on Gulf Standard Time, so the only buffer needed is the walk from the car to the desk.

process.title: Review at the end of each term
process.description: The question is whether the named problem from the diagnostic is still a problem. If it is closed, the hours move to the next thing or stop. If it is not, the plan changes rather than continuing unchanged, and that is also when a different tutor can be requested.

whyPoints.title: The rates on this page carry their source
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here is attributed to the competitor page or rate study it came from, with the month it was read. No ranking page in this market cites a source for a single rate, and a number without a source is not information a parent can act on.

whyPoints.title: Specialist choice instead of catchment
whyPoints.description: Removing the drive to Al Raha Beach changes who can teach your child. An Applications and Interpretation Higher Level specialist is findable online and rarely findable within a twenty-minute radius of a specific Abu Dhabi community at 5pm on a weekday.

whyPoints.title: A boundary on assessed work that we state plainly
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, question and review. They do not write, complete or supply any part of an Exploration, Extended Essay or Theory of Knowledge essay. That boundary protects your child's Diploma, and it is the difference between a tutor and an essay service.

whyPoints.title: Delivery disclosed rather than implied
whyPoints.description: Lessons for UAE families are one-to-one online over live video. IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE. Where a tutor is based outside the emirate, we say so before you book rather than routing you to a number and hoping you do not ask.

whyPoints.title: A plan with an endpoint in it
whyPoints.description: Tutoring that is reviewed each term either closes a gap or changes shape. An open retainer does neither, and it is the most common way money is quietly wasted in this market. Review points are built into how a block is proposed.

whyPoints.title: Independent of every school and board named here
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no accreditation, approval or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and claims none. Schools appear on this page as local context, not as clients or endorsers.

faqs.question: How much should I budget for an IB maths tutor in Al Raha Beach for a full school year?
faqs.answer: Work from hours rather than from an hourly rate. One session a week across a school year is about 34 to 36 hours. At the budget online tier reported for this market, roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, that is around AED 1,600 to AED 5,400. At qualified subject-tutor rates of roughly AED 150 to 300 it is around AED 5,100 to AED 10,800. At specialist rates of AED 200 to 450 or more it rises further. Those bands come from published competitor pages and Bestimate's rate work read in October 2026. Ask any provider for the annual hour count, not just the rate.

faqs.question: Why does in-home maths tuition in Abu Dhabi cost more per hour than online?
faqs.answer: Because you are paying for travel. Market in-home rates in this emirate run roughly AED 180 to 350 an hour by Bestimate's figures, with independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to 500, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online. The difference covers the drive, the fuel and the time a tutor cannot sell to anyone else. That premium buys physical presence in the room, which genuinely helps some students. It does not buy a wider choice of specialist, and at Higher Level that trade is usually the wrong way round.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a maths tutor to my villa or apartment in Al Raha Beach?
faqs.answer: No. Tutoring for UAE families is delivered as one-to-one lessons over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. We state this before you book rather than after. For Diploma mathematics the online format has a practical advantage beyond cost: a shared digital whiteboard with a screen-shared past paper is a better surface for working a problem line by line than a kitchen table, and the session can be rewatched.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying a specialist rate for MYP maths, or only for the Diploma?
faqs.answer: Match the rate to the difficulty of the work. Rebuilding algebraic fluency in MYP 4 or 5 does not need a Higher Level Analysis and Approaches specialist at the top of the market band; a competent qualified teacher at mid-tier rates covers it well. Interpreting a Paper 3 mark scheme, or judging whether an Exploration topic will support mathematics beyond course level, does need that depth. Families who apply one rate to everything either overpay on the straightforward work or under-resource the hard work, and the second mistake is the one that shows in a final grade.

faqs.question: My child is choosing between Maths AA and AI next year. Can a tutor help us decide?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the cheapest useful thing you can buy at that point. Two or three sessions with a Mathematics specialist, working through sample questions from both courses with your child present, costs a fraction of a term of remedial tuition in DP1 after a wrong choice. Analysis and Approaches is calculus and proof led; Applications and Interpretation is statistics and modelling led with the graphical display calculator assumed throughout. The decision also depends on university prerequisites, so read the requirement page for the specific degree and intake rather than a general rule.

faqs.question: What is Paper 3 and why does it need its own block of tutoring?
faqs.answer: Paper 3 exists only at Higher Level in both Diploma maths routes and is worth 20% of the grade. It consists of two extended problem-solving questions that build across several parts, so a student has to sustain a line of reasoning rather than answer discrete items. It is also the component with the least practice material available, which is why schools often reach it late. Concentrated work across the twelve weeks before the exam series, one question worked slowly and a second worked under time, is a better use of money than spreading the same hours across two years.

faqs.question: Where exactly is the line between Exploration coaching and doing the work for my child?
faqs.answer: No, and any provider offering to should be avoided. The Exploration is 20% of the maths grade and must be the student's own work; submitting work that is not the candidate's own is malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student. A tutor may test whether a topic will support mathematics beyond course level, explain a published criterion, teach a technique the student has chosen to use, and read a draft and respond with questions. Writing, editing to completion or supplying a model to adapt all sit on the wrong side of that line.

faqs.question: Do private maths tutors in Abu Dhabi need a permit, and how do I check?
faqs.answer: Yes. The UAE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, free of charge for two years. Eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Ask the tutor directly whether they hold one and under which category. Working without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since no fine schedule is published, treat any specific figure quoted to you with scepticism.

faqs.question: Can my child's own school maths teacher tutor them privately for a fee?
faqs.answer: In Abu Dhabi you should assume not. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a comparable code of conduct. This has been reported in the press rather than read from the policy document, so verify the current wording with ADEK before relying on it. The practical position is straightforward: do not approach your child's class teacher as a paid tutor, and treat any provider marketing that arrangement as a risk.

faqs.question: Which schools near Al Raha Beach do the students you support attend?
faqs.answer: Students we support in this corridor come from the Al Raha and Al Raha Gardens campuses, the Khalifa City cluster and the island schools, including Raha International School, Al Yasmina Academy, Cranleigh Abu Dhabi, GEMS American Academy Abu Dhabi and Repton Abu Dhabi. Those names describe the educational context of the neighbourhood. IB Gram has no affiliation, partnership or endorsement relationship with any of them, and online delivery means a school's location has no bearing on which Mathematics specialist is available to your child.

faqs.question: What time can a maths session realistically start for an Al Raha Beach student?
faqs.answer: Most secondary students in Al Raha Beach travel inland to school rather than within the community, so the return leg lands later than the school bell suggests. A 4.45pm or 5pm start works reliably on a weekday; mid-afternoon slots rarely do. Because lessons run over live video, the only buffer needed is the walk from the car to a desk, which is typically ten to fifteen minutes rather than the half hour a visiting tutor would require. Families with two children usually take consecutive slots on the same evening.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a Diploma maths student usually need before the grade moves?
faqs.answer: There is no reliable general figure, and anyone offering one is guessing. What is predictable is the shape. Four diagnostic sessions identify which losses are content, which are method and which are exam technique. Content gaps in a named topic often close in three to six focused hours each. Method and exam-technique problems take longer because they are habits. A student losing marks through early rounding or through treating the calculator as a last resort can change that in a handful of sessions; rebuilding two years of missing algebra cannot.

faqs.question: Do Abu Dhabi IGCSE candidates sit the February and March Cambridge series?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge offers the February and March series to India only. Candidates in the UAE sit the June series and the November series, and November functions as the main resit route. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. One further detail matters: every Cambridge exam centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask your school which zone it sits in.

faqs.question: What happens if there is no Applications and Interpretation Higher Level specialist available?
faqs.answer: We tell you, with one of three honest answers. The first is a waiting time with an actual date attached. The second is a tutor based outside the UAE teaching the same syllabus over the same live video on Gulf Standard Time, which is disclosed before you book rather than hidden behind a phone number. The third is that we cannot cover it well, in which case we say so rather than placing a generalist into a Higher Level seat. Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level has the thinnest specialist supply of the four Diploma maths routes.

faqs.question: Is an online maths tutor based outside Abu Dhabi a problem for my child?
faqs.answer: It depends on two things: the syllabus and the clock. A tutor who has taught Analysis and Approaches Higher Level through to the exam series knows the same course your child's school teaches, because the course is set by the IB rather than by a country. Timing is the practical constraint, and it is solved by booking on Gulf Standard Time so lessons sit in your evening rather than someone else's. What does change is choice: the pool stops being people who can drive to Al Raha Beach and becomes qualified Mathematics teachers.

intro.heading: Three comparisons, only two of which matter
paragraphs: Al Raha Gardens, Khalifa City and Al Raha Beach sit within a short drive of each other on the inland side of Abu Dhabi, towards the airport road. They share schools, they share the same tutor supply, and their students finish the day within about forty-five minutes of each other. A parent comparing mathematics tutors between these three communities is running a comparison that cannot return a meaningful difference, and the time spent on it is time not spent on the decisions that do change a grade.

There are two comparisons worth the effort instead. The first is between the two IB mathematics courses, Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, which are different subjects wearing similar names and which open different university doors. The second is between Higher and Standard Level inside whichever course is chosen, where an entire extra paper appears and the prescribed teaching time rises from 150 hours to 240.

There is a third comparison many Abu Dhabi families face and few plan for: IB mathematics against A Level Mathematics, because the school cluster around Al Raha Gardens contains both systems. They assess completely differently. A Level Mathematics is examined entirely on timed papers with no coursework at all. IB mathematics carries an exploration worth twenty per cent, written over months and marked against five published criteria.

That difference is not a matter of difficulty. It is a matter of what kind of student thrives. A student who performs well under examination pressure and dislikes extended writing is better served by the A Level structure. A student who works steadily and writes well but underperforms in timed conditions gains real ground from a component worth a fifth of the grade that is not sat in an examination hall.

Al Raha Gardens has a local fact that shapes all of this. The school at the centre of the community runs the full IB continuum, so a great many students here are on the IB pathway by default rather than by decision, having joined in the primary years. The comparison with A Level therefore arrives late, often in Year 11, when a school change would be required to act on it. That is not a reason to avoid the comparison; it is a reason to make it a year earlier than feels necessary.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, or anywhere else in the UAE. In-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. What we deliver to Al Raha Gardens is one-to-one teaching over live video. abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-raha-gard.subjectsIntro: Below are the mathematics routes and components an Al Raha Gardens family is choosing between, each with the demand that actually decides a grade in it.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches SL
subjects.description: Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 2 with one, forty per cent each, plus the exploration at twenty. Most Paper 1 losses are arithmetic or sign errors in work the student understood, which makes non-calculator practice a mark-recovery exercise rather than a conceptual one.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL
subjects.description: Three papers at thirty, thirty and twenty plus the exploration. Proof, complex numbers and the depth of the calculus section carry the content; Paper 3 carries the format shock. Proof is marked on the validity of each step, so a right answer reached badly scores poorly.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation SL
subjects.description: A calculator is permitted on both papers, which makes calculator fluency examinable rather than convenient. Statistical tests, regression and modelling carry the content, and marks go on producing a correct output and then failing to say what it means in context.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation HL
subjects.description: Adds matrices, graph theory, differential equations and heavier statistics, with Paper 3 as an extended modelling investigation. The calculator demands are specific and substantial, and a student who has not drilled the menus loses time rather than understanding.

subjects.name: A Level Mathematics
subjects.description: Pure mathematics across two papers with an applied paper combining statistics and mechanics, all examined under timed conditions with a calculator permitted. No component is produced over months, so a student who writes well but examines poorly has nowhere to recover marks.

subjects.name: The IB mathematical exploration
subjects.description: Twenty marks across presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics, with twelve to twenty pages recommended. Six of the twenty marks are for engagement and reflection, which are written rather than calculated.

subjects.name: Paper 3, IB Higher Level only
subjects.description: Sixty minutes, fifty-five marks, two extended problem-solving questions that lead a student through unfamiliar territory in stages. It rewards reading every part first, carrying results forward unrounded, and parking a stalled part rather than fighting it.

subjects.name: Calculator technique
subjects.levels: Examinable in both IB courses and at A Level
subjects.description: Numerical solving, graph intersections, regression with its coefficient, normal and binomial work, numerical derivatives and definite integrals, and angle mode. Finite, drillable, and almost never taught systematically on the model the school has standardised.

subjects.name: Proof and reasoning
subjects.description: Direct proof, contradiction, induction and counterexample, each marked on structure. Three or four sessions on proof writing typically pay for themselves at Higher Level, because the marks are allocated to visible reasoning rather than to the conclusion reached.

subjects.name: Statistics and modelling
subjects.levels: Applications heavily; present in both routes
subjects.description: Distributions, hypothesis testing, correlation and regression. The recurring loss is interpretation: a coefficient calculated correctly and then described as evidence of causation, or a probability quoted without the condition it was calculated under.

sections.heading: IB mathematics against A Level Mathematics at sixteen
paragraphs: This is the comparison that genuinely changes a student's two years, and it is available to Al Raha Gardens families because both systems exist within reach. The structural difference is simple to state and large in effect. A Level Mathematics is examined entirely on timed papers with no coursework component at all. IB mathematics carries an exploration worth twenty per cent of the grade, produced over months and marked against five published criteria.

For a student who performs well under pressure and finds extended writing a chore, A Level is the kinder structure: everything they are good at counts, and nothing requires them to write about mathematics. For a student who works steadily, writes well and underperforms in examination halls, the IB structure hands back a fifth of the grade in a form they can control. That is not a small adjustment to a profile.

The breadth difference runs the other way. A Level students typically take three or four subjects; IB Diploma students take six plus the core, which means a mathematics-strong student at A Level can double down with Further Mathematics and Physics while an IB student must also carry a language, a humanity and Theory of Knowledge. Neither is better; they suit different students and different university plans.

Admissions is the piece to check rather than assume. Mathematics-intensive degrees commonly expect Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level from IB applicants, or A Level Mathematics with Further Mathematics from A Level applicants, and the stated requirement differs by institution and changes between cycles. Read the admissions page of each university you are considering, including the UAE institutions, rather than relying on a general rule.

sections.heading: Choosing between Analysis and Applications on evidence rather than instinct
paragraphs: Most families choose between the two IB mathematics courses on a feeling: which one the student says is easier, or which one a sibling took. There is a better method, and it takes about two hours of diagnostic work. Set short pieces of genuine material from each course and see where the student actually performs, then hold that against the university requirements they may need.

The signals are reasonably reliable. A student comfortable manipulating abstract expressions, who enjoys a proof and tolerates not seeing an immediate purpose, is pointed at Analysis and Approaches. A student who works well with real data, reads context carefully and loses patience with abstraction is pointed at Applications and Interpretation. Neither signal is about ability; both are about the kind of thinking the course rewards.

The non-negotiable input is the university requirement, and it has to be checked rather than assumed. Mathematics-intensive degrees commonly specify Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. Life sciences, business, psychology and much of the social sciences accept either, and some explicitly accept Applications at Higher Level. Requirements differ by institution and change between cycles, so read the admissions page for each course under consideration.

One caution for Al Raha Gardens specifically. Because many students here are on the IB pathway by default, having joined the continuum school in primary, the mathematics course decision arrives as the first real choice they have ever made inside the system. It deserves the two hours, and it is much easier to act on in Year 11 than in the second term of the Diploma.

sections.heading: Higher against Standard Level in whichever course you pick
paragraphs: The level decision is usually framed as a question of ability and is better framed as a question of workload and purpose. The prescribed teaching time rises from 150 hours at Standard Level to 240 at Higher Level, and that ninety-hour difference is additional content rather than deeper revision of the same material. A student moving up mid-course is taking on roughly a third more syllabus, not working harder at the same one.

The structural change is the arrival of Paper 3, a sixty-minute paper carrying fifty-five marks across two extended problem-solving questions. It is a fifth of the Higher Level grade and has no Standard Level equivalent, so it requires its own practice on its own past papers. Students who revise Papers 1 and 2 thoroughly and meet Paper 3 twice are the commonest Higher Level casualty.

The weighting shift matters for planning. At Standard Level the two papers carry forty per cent each, so an even split of practice is defensible. At Higher Level the split becomes thirty, thirty and twenty, with the exploration at twenty, which means Paper 3 deserves a fifth of the revision time. Almost nobody gives it that, because it is unfamiliar and therefore easy to defer.

The purpose test is the one to apply first. Higher Level mathematics is required or strongly expected for some degree routes and irrelevant to others. Taking it unnecessarily, at the cost of two other subjects and a great deal of sleep, is a common and avoidable mistake. Check the university requirement before the ability question, because if the requirement is not there the ability question does not need answering.

sections.heading: Where the two Diploma years actually go
paragraphs: Mathematics in the Diploma is taught across two years in a sequence most students never see written down, and seeing it changes how a family plans support. The first year covers the bulk of the core content, usually working through number and algebra, functions, and geometry and trigonometry, with statistics or calculus arriving depending on the department's preference and the course taken.

The exploration is the piece that collides with everything else. Most schools introduce it late in the first year or early in the second, with internal draft deadlines across several months. Twenty per cent of the grade is therefore being produced at the same time as new content is being taught and other subjects are running their own Internal Assessments. A student who defers the topic decision is the student who runs out of year.

The second year brings the hardest content, the mock cycle, and Paper 3 for Higher Level students. By the spring the useful work changes character entirely: content teaching has diminishing returns, and converting what is known into marks does not. Most families buy intensively at exactly this point, which is understandable and is also the most expensive hour in the whole plan.

The sequence suggests a cheaper and better shape. Two shorter sessions a week through the first year on the content as it is taught. A defined block on the exploration as soon as the topic can be narrowed. Diagnostic sessions on each mock script. Then intensive work only on named components in the final term. Because no IB session date in this project has been confirmed from ibo.org, which blocks automated checking, confirm every date with your school's Diploma coordinator.

sections.heading: The exploration compared with coursework you may have met before
paragraphs: Parents arriving from other systems compare the exploration with things that look similar and are not. It is not an IGCSE coursework piece, which tends to be tightly specified by the board. It is not an A Level component, because A Level Mathematics has none. It is a piece of individual mathematical writing on a topic the student chooses, marked out of twenty against five published criteria.

Those criteria are worth knowing precisely, because they explain most unexpected marks. Presentation carries four, mathematical communication four, personal engagement three, reflection three, and use of mathematics six, with twelve to twenty pages recommended. Six of the twenty marks therefore go to engagement and reflection, which are written rather than calculated, and which students treat as decoration around the mathematics.

Four of the five criteria are effectively decided by the topic. A question too broad to finish produces thin mathematics, disorganised presentation, shallow reflection and a struggle with communication, simultaneously. Narrowing is where the marks are won and it is the work students resist hardest, because a narrow question feels less impressive than a grand one and nobody has told them the grand ones score badly.

The boundary here is firm. A tutor may question the topic, challenge the mathematics chosen, explain each criterion and say why a section is weak. No tutor at IB Gram will write the exploration, draft it or edit it to completion. The school supervisor signs the work off and should know outside support exists; a tutor suggesting concealment is creating a risk that lands on your child rather than on them.

University-student tutors online advertise from around AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik on their own pages. A qualified subject tutor online sits at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200 and TutorChase quoting around AED 270. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above.

In-home one-to-one visits in Abu Dhabi are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel priced in, per the Bestimate rate table and published home-tutor rates. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. None of the figures above is our price list; they are the market, published so you can judge any proposal including ours.

For mathematics the allocation that works is frequency at the middle band rather than scarcity at the top. Two sessions a week with a qualified subject tutor through the first Diploma year will usually do more than a handful of premium hours in the final spring, because non-calculator arithmetic and Paper 3 technique are built by repetition. The exception is a narrow component review, where specialist rates are genuinely efficient.

And here is where the comparison ends. No provider can guarantee a grade, a score or an improvement, including this one, and anyone offering a guarantee is selling rather than teaching. No regulator or examination board accredits IB Gram, there is no Abu Dhabi office, and every figure on this page carries its source and date. faqs.question: Is an IB maths tutor in Al Raha Gardens better than one in Khalifa City?
faqs.answer: No, and the honest version is worth hearing. The two communities are a short drive apart, share schools and share tutor supply, and their students finish within about forty-five minutes of each other. Khalifa City has slightly more local supply because it is larger. Neither has meaningful depth in Higher Level mathematics specifically, which is the thing that decides a Diploma grade. Online delivery removes the journey and widens the pool to every specialist free at your hour.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a maths tutor to Al Raha Gardens villas?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Mathematics lessons here are one to one over live video with a shared whiteboard, which suits the subject well because every line of working stays visible and is saved afterwards. In-home visits in Abu Dhabi are quoted in the market at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel priced into the figure.

faqs.question: Should my child take IB maths or A Level Maths in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: It depends on how they perform under examination pressure. A Level Mathematics has no coursework at all, so the papers are the entire grade, which suits a student who examines well and dislikes extended writing. IB mathematics carries an exploration worth twenty per cent, produced over months and marked against five criteria, which hands back a fifth of the grade to a student who works steadily and writes well. Check the university requirement before deciding either way.

faqs.question: How do we choose between Analysis and Applications properly?
faqs.answer: With about two hours of diagnostic work rather than a conversation. Set short pieces of genuine material from both courses and see where the student performs. Comfort with abstract manipulation and proof points to Analysis; strength with real data, context and written interpretation points to Applications. Then check the stated entry requirement for the degree routes under consideration, because mathematics-intensive courses commonly specify Analysis at Higher Level and requirements change between cycles.

faqs.question: What actually changes between Standard and Higher Level maths?
faqs.answer: Prescribed teaching time rises from 150 hours to 240, which is additional content rather than deeper revision, and Paper 3 arrives: sixty minutes, fifty-five marks, two extended problem-solving questions worth a fifth of the grade. The weighting shifts from forty and forty to thirty, thirty and twenty, with the exploration at twenty throughout. The practical consequence is that Paper 3 deserves a fifth of the revision time and almost never receives it.

faqs.question: Does the exploration carry the same weight at both IB levels?
faqs.answer: Yes, twenty per cent at Standard and Higher Level in both mathematics courses, marked out of twenty across five criteria: presentation four, mathematical communication four, personal engagement three, reflection three and use of mathematics six, with twelve to twenty pages recommended. Six of those twenty marks are for engagement and reflection, which are written rather than calculated. Students treat that writing as padding and it is nearly a third of the Internal Assessment mark.

faqs.question: Why does my daughter get the answer right and lose the marks?
faqs.answer: Usually because the reasoning is not visible. In Higher Level proof work and in Paper 3 particularly, marks are allocated to steps rather than to conclusions, so a correct answer reached by an unjustified route collects a fraction of what it could. The other three common causes are sign errors in multi-step rearrangement, chain-rule mistakes inside composite functions, and angle mode left in degrees for a radian question, which invalidates everything in that question.

faqs.question: Can a student move from Standard to Higher Level mid-course?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is harder than it sounds. The ninety-hour difference in prescribed teaching time is additional content, so a student moving up has topics that were never taught rather than topics that were taught and forgotten. At Higher Level that includes proof and deeper calculus in Analysis, or matrices and graph theory in Applications, plus a whole new paper format. Ask the school what is possible and when, then get a diagnostic read on the untaught content before committing.

faqs.question: How much calculator work is examined in IB mathematics?
faqs.answer: More than most families expect, and the rules differ by course. Applications and Interpretation permits a calculator on every paper, which makes menu fluency examinable: numerical solving, graph intersections, regression with its coefficient, normal and inverse normal, binomial probabilities, numerical derivatives and definite integrals. Analysis and Approaches forbids it on Paper 1 at both levels, which exposes weak mental arithmetic. Drill the school's standardised model rather than whichever one a video tutorial uses.

faqs.question: When should the maths course decision be made in Al Raha Gardens?
faqs.answer: Year 10 or early Year 11, which is earlier than most families realise. The reason matters locally: because the continuum school at the centre of this community takes students from the primary years, many are on the IB pathway by default rather than by decision, and the mathematics course is the first genuine choice they make inside it. Acting on an A Level comparison later usually means changing school, which is a very different decision in the second Diploma term.

faqs.question: Is two sessions a week really better than one for Diploma maths?
faqs.answer: For most students, yes. The errors that decide mathematics grades are procedural, and procedural accuracy consolidates in the gap between contacts rather than within a session. Two shorter contacts halve that gap and double the number of times a recurring error gets caught and named. The exception is a student whose difficulty is genuinely conceptual, where one longer session gives room to build an idea. Marked work usually makes clear which case you are in.

faqs.question: What does Paper 3 require that Paper 2 does not?
faqs.answer: Format discipline rather than more content. Paper 3 leads a student through an unfamiliar investigation in parts, where early parts often generate results later parts need. It rewards reading every part before starting, carrying results forward unrounded, showing reasoning, and writing a sentence when a part asks for interpretation. The characteristic failure is spending twenty minutes stuck on part (b) and never reaching parts where marks were available independently. That is a trained habit, built over four or five timed attempts.

faqs.question: Can a tutor choose my son's exploration topic for him?
faqs.answer: A tutor can question a topic, narrow it, and say why it will not reach the available marks, which is the single most valuable thing anybody does on this component. What a tutor must not do is choose it for him, write the exploration, draft it or edit it to completion. The work must be his own, and the school supervisor signs it off and should know that outside support exists. A tutor suggesting concealment is creating a risk that falls on him.

faqs.question: What should we expect to spend on Diploma maths support here?
faqs.answer: At published market bands, a qualified subject tutor online runs roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, which is about AED 600 to 1,200 a month for one weekly session on Bestimate's mid-band estimate. Specialists sit at AED 200 to 450 and above, student tutors at AED 33 to 65, and premium named tutors have been quoted to AED 650. For mathematics, two middle-band sessions a week through the first Diploma year is usually better value than premium hours in the final spring.

faqs.question: What if you cannot staff Higher Level maths at our evening hour?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than substituting somebody who has not taught the course. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level in a fixed evening slot is one of the tightest combinations in this market, and Al Raha Gardens competes with Saadiyat, Al Reem and Yas families for the same 17:00 to 20:00 window. Standard Level requests usually match within days. Being told early leaves you time to look elsewhere, which beats discovering in session three that Paper 3 is unfamiliar to the tutor.

intro.heading: The comparisons that decide a maths grade, in the order they arrive
paragraphs: Families in Al Rawdah usually come to tutoring with the smallest question first: who is good, and how much. The decisions that move a Diploma mathematics grade sit upstream of that. Which course, AA or AI. Which level, Higher or Standard. Whether the Diploma is the right post-16 route at all when A-Level maths sits at the same schools. Each of those is a comparison with real consequences, and each is cheaper to get right in Year 11 than to compensate for in Year 13.

Take the level question. A 7 at Standard Level and a 4 at Higher Level are not close in effect, even though the Higher course looks more impressive on a form. The 7 protects the overall 45-point total, frees evenings for the subjects a university offer genuinely depends on, and leaves a student confident rather than permanently behind. The 4 does none of that. The only reason to take Higher Level mathematics is that the degree route requires it or the student is genuinely strong in it, and a tutor whose first instinct is to encourage the higher level is not acting in your child's interest.

The course question is sharper still, because the two courses are not a harder and an easier version of each other. Analysis and Approaches examines algebra, functions, proof and calculus, with a Paper 1 sat without a calculator. Applications and Interpretation examines modelling, data and statistics with technology permitted throughout. Both cover the same five named topics and diverge rapidly within them. By the end of DP1 an AA student has met implicit differentiation and complex numbers while an AI student has met chi-squared testing and the Poisson distribution, and no tutor can merge those two paths afterwards.

The third comparison is the one Al Rawdah families actually started with, and it is the least important: whether to hire somebody local. Al Rawdah sits between Al Mushrif and Al Karamah, minutes from the main school corridor, so local in-home tuition is genuinely available at published rates of AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included. The limitation is not price but pool size. The adults willing to drive here on a Tuesday evening are not the same set as the adults who have taught Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and for Paper 3 work that difference is the whole thing.

IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition into Al Rawdah over live video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not offer home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. For mathematics that arrangement is more than acceptable: the whiteboard is shared, graphs are plotted on the screen both people are reading, past questions are annotated live, and the session is recorded so a method can be replayed before the homework. What the format buys is the ability to choose a tutor by course rather than by distance.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-rawdah.programmesIntro: Three routes carry mathematics for a sixteen-year-old in Abu Dhabi, and the comparison between them is usually made on reputation rather than on fit. These are the differences that matter in practice.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Two courses, AA or AI, at Standard or Higher Level, each with five syllabus topics, a toolkit strand and a 20% Exploration. Standard Level is two papers at 40% each; Higher Level is three papers weighted 30%, 30% and 20%. Grades run 1 to 7 within a 45-point Diploma total that also carries Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students in Al Rawdah usually attend one of a modest number of schools offering the programme in Abu Dhabi, several of them off the island. The internal deadlines that drive the year, particularly the Exploration draft date and the mock window, are set by the school rather than by the IB, so ask for the written internal calendar early.

programmes.name: A-Level mathematics
programmes.description: Pure mathematics with mechanics or statistics as applied content, examined by written papers with no coursework. Narrower than the Diploma, which suits a student who wants depth in three subjects rather than breadth in six, and it does not carry an Exploration or a core.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, a student must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, plus five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3. The IB points threshold for equivalency is not published in that source, so verify it on moe.gov.ae before relying on any figure.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Four assessment criteria, each marked 0 to 8: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Strong on investigation, light on sustained timed algebra, which is the predictable shape of the gap when a student reaches DP1.
programmes.countryNote: For an Al Rawdah family comparing an IB continuum school with a British-curriculum school, this is the real comparison: a criterion-based middle school against a terminal-examination one. Both lead into the Diploma, and the practical difference shows up in the first term of DP1 rather than at the point of choosing.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-rawdah.subjectsIntro: Diploma mathematics splits into the components below. The comparison column matters: at Higher Level the same topic is examined with more depth and a different paper structure, and that is where tutoring hours go.

subjects.name: Number and algebra
subjects.levels: AA and AI, SL and HL
subjects.description: Sequences, series, exponents, logarithms and the binomial theorem, extending at AA Higher Level into proof by induction, complex numbers and partial fractions. The Higher Level extension is a different kind of work rather than more of the same, which is why a Standard Level tutor cannot simply stretch upwards.

subjects.name: Functions
subjects.levels: AA and AI, SL and HL
subjects.description: Domain and range, composites, inverses and transformations, with quadratic, rational and exponential models. AI leans on fitting a function to data; AA leans on manipulating it exactly. The recurring error in both is applying transformations in the wrong order.

subjects.name: Geometry and trigonometry
subjects.levels: AA and AI, SL and HL
subjects.description: Solids, the sine and cosine rules, radian measure and trigonometric equations, with vectors and compound-angle identities at AA Higher Level. Calculators left in degrees for radian questions invalidate every line that follows, which is a habit rather than a gap.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.levels: AA and AI, SL and HL
subjects.description: Data presentation, regression, probability rules and the binomial and normal distributions, extending at AI Higher Level into chi-squared testing, Poisson and hypothesis testing. This is where AI is genuinely harder than AA rather than lighter.

subjects.name: Calculus
subjects.levels: AA and AI, SL and HL
subjects.description: Differentiation and integration with kinematics and volumes of revolution, extending at AA Higher Level into implicit differentiation, Maclaurin series and differential equations. AI treats calculus more numerically. Most lost marks trace to a missing constant or a chain rule on the wrong inner function.

subjects.name: The Exploration
subjects.description: An individual investigation of roughly 12 to 20 pages, marked out of 20 across presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. Mathematics above course level scores badly because understanding cannot be shown, which surprises ambitious students.

subjects.name: Paper 1
subjects.description: Sat without a calculator in AA and with technology in AI. The comparison matters for preparation: AA requires paper fluency with surds, logarithms and radians, while AI requires knowing which calculator function to reach for quickly.

subjects.name: Paper 2
subjects.description: Calculator-permitted across all five topics, awarding method marks for a written setup even when the final value is wrong. Students who type into the calculator and record only the answer forfeit marks they had genuinely earned.

subjects.name: Paper 3
subjects.description: Two extended problem-solving questions crossing topics, present at Higher Level and absent at Standard. This single component is the strongest practical argument for matching a tutor to the exact level, because it cannot be prepared for by doing more short questions.

subjects.name: Graphical display calculator fluency
subjects.description: Solving numerically, finding intersections, evaluating definite integrals, running regressions and reading distributions on the specific model the school uses. Transfers from other systems often arrive without these skills and lose marks on questions they understand perfectly.

subjects.name: Mock papers and predicted grades
subjects.description: School mocks produce the predicted grade a university sees when it makes an offer. Preparing specifically for a school's own mock is bounded, legitimate work with an obvious end date, and it is often more consequential than the student believes at the time.

sections.heading: Answering the search, then naming the comparison that matters more
paragraphs: Directly: an IB maths tutor in Al Rawdah through IB Gram is a Diploma mathematics specialist matched to your child's exact course and level, teaching one-to-one over live video at an Abu Dhabi-friendly hour, with a free trial lesson first and no block of hours bought in advance. There is no travel and no tutor arriving at a UAE address, because in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India.

Having answered that, the more useful conversation is about the choices around the tutoring. Al Rawdah families comparing tutors by distance are comparing the least consequential variable available to them. The consequential ones are whether the student is on the right course, at the right level, with the Exploration under control, and whether the hours being bought are aimed at the topics an error log actually names.

There is a reason this ordering gets inverted. Distance and price are easy to compare; course fit is not, because it requires somebody to look at the student's work and say something uncomfortable. A first session that reports the student is on the wrong course is worth more than a term of competent teaching on the wrong course, and it is also the harder conversation to have, which is why many providers do not have it.

So the sections below work through the comparisons in the order they bite: level, course, Diploma against A-Level, the step up from IGCSE, cost by format, and the pool of available tutors. Each has a table, because a comparison without numbers is just an opinion with paragraphs attached.

sections.heading: Higher Level or Standard Level: comparing the cost of each in points
paragraphs: The level decision is usually framed as ambition against safety, which is the wrong frame. It is a comparison between two outcomes with different point totals and different time demands, and the right answer depends on what the university offer actually requires. A Diploma is marked out of 45 and a university looks at the total as well as the individual subject grade, so a level choice that costs two points in maths and two more in a subject starved of time is a four-point decision rather than a one-subject one.

Higher Level mathematics adds a third paper worth 20% of the grade, roughly 100 more teaching hours over two years in most school timetables, and a body of content the Standard Level student never meets: at AA that means complex numbers, induction, Maclaurin series and differential equations. The honest question is not whether the student could pass it but whether those hours produce more value in mathematics than they would in the subject the offer actually hangs on.

There are students for whom Higher Level is plainly right. They enjoy proof, they finish problem sets early, they ask why rather than how, and their target degree requires it. For those students the Higher course is the correct and enjoyable choice and tutoring is about depth rather than survival. The failure mode is the student who is capable and uninterested, pushed up by a school's grade profile or a family's expectation, who then spends two years behind.

If the decision is live, settle it on evidence. A short advisory block works sample Higher and Standard questions with the student and reports what happened: fluency, stamina, how they responded to an unfamiliar problem. Combine that with the actual entry requirements on the target universities' own admissions pages for the intake year in question, and the decision usually makes itself.
