process.title: Tell us where you are in the course
process.description: DP1 autumn, DP1 spring, DP2 before the exploration deadline, DP2 after the mocks. That single fact changes the recommendation more than the symptom does, because the same gap calls for fluency work in DP1 and triage in DP2.

process.title: Send the school's internal deadlines
process.description: The exploration deadline, the mock window, and the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge dates. These are set per campus, they sit well before external dates, and in most schools they cluster. The whole plan is drawn backwards from them.

process.title: Send one marked paper
process.description: A mock or a returned test with annotations. It tells a tutor whether the losses are clustered or structural, which determines whether a short repair block or a longer fluency programme is the right purchase at this point in the calendar.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: A full one-to-one session over live video at no cost and with no card details taken. Judge it on whether the tutor asked which route and level, which phase of the course you are in, and when the internal deadline falls, before discussing anything else.

process.title: Agree the block and its end date
process.description: A fluency block, an exploration block timed to the internal deadline, or an eight-week run-in. Each has a defined end. Agreeing the end at the start is what stops a two-year weekly arrangement forming by default and consuming the budget evenly.

process.title: Check the ranked list every fortnight
process.description: In any paper-based block the topic list should be shortening. That is the measurable test, and it is a better question than asking how revision is going. If the list is not moving after three sessions, the diagnosis was wrong and the plan should change.

whyPoints.title: Planned from your school's dates, not a generic timetable
whyPoints.description: Internal deadlines are set per campus and they are what a block has to be scheduled against. We ask for the exploration deadline, the mock window and the core dates before recommending anything, because a plan built on external dates is built on the wrong calendar.

whyPoints.title: The right intervention for the phase
whyPoints.description: Fluency work in DP1, exploration coaching before the internal deadline, timed-paper discipline after the mocks. The same symptom gets different treatment at different points in the course, and a tutor who does not ask the date will get one of them wrong.

whyPoints.title: Blocks with an end date
whyPoints.description: A fluency block, an exploration block and a run-in all finish. Agreeing the end at the start is the difference between buying tutoring and acquiring a subscription, and the flat two-year weekly arrangement is the most expensive pattern in this market.

whyPoints.title: Measured, not felt
whyPoints.description: A paper-based block produces a ranked list of topics costing the most marks, updated after each marked paper. If the list is not shortening, the plan changes. Comfortable sessions are the easiest thing in this market to keep paying for.

whyPoints.title: The exploration is coached, never written
whyPoints.description: A tutor explains the five criteria and their mark allocations, tests a topic the student proposed, teaches the techniques they chose and gives feedback on their own draft. No tutor writes, rewrites or supplies text for submission.

whyPoints.title: No dates we have not verified
whyPoints.description: This page publishes no IB session or results date. The IB's own site blocks automated access, nothing has been confirmed at source, and a date a family plans around has to come from the school's IB coordinator rather than a tutoring page.

faqs.question: When should an Al Reem Island family start IB maths tutoring?
faqs.answer: It depends what they are buying. A diagnostic session is worth having in the first term of DP1, because a gap identified then is cheap to close and a gap carried forward compounds. The fluency work that Paper 1 assumes belongs in DP1 spring. Exploration coaching belongs in the term before the school's internal deadline. Timed-paper work belongs in the eight weeks after the mocks. A flat weekly arrangement from the first week of DP1 spends evenly on a course that demands unevenly.

faqs.question: My child is in DP2 with eleven weeks left and real content gaps. What now?
faqs.answer: Triage, honestly described as triage. Rank the missing topics by the marks at stake rather than by difficulty, patch the top two or three, and spend the remaining time on paper technique, which converts existing knowledge into marks faster than new content does. Accept explicitly that some topics will not be rebuilt and decide which. A plan that pretends there is time for everything produces a student who has half-learned eight topics and cannot complete a paper.

faqs.question: How far ahead does the maths exploration need to start?
faqs.answer: Count backwards from the school's internal deadline, not the external one. Before submission there is a final criterion check, a session's work. Before that a complete draft, which takes the student two to three weeks if the mathematics is genuinely theirs. Before that the mathematics itself, worked and verified, around two weeks. Before that a tested, viable topic, one to two weeks of trial. And before all of it, twenty minutes reading the five criteria. That is most of a term.

faqs.question: Why do the Diploma internal deadlines all seem to land at once?
faqs.answer: Because in most schools they do. The maths exploration, the science investigations, the Extended Essay draft stages and the Theory of Knowledge essay are each set by their own department, and the departments converge on the same part of DP2. The collision is entirely predictable and entirely avoidable: ask for all of them in writing in the first term of DP2 and sequence the work. Families who meet them one at a time in January cannot sequence anything, and the maths exploration usually gives way.

faqs.question: What does an eight-week run-in actually contain?
faqs.answer: Sixteen sessions at two a week, which at ninety minutes each is roughly six full papers with their marking plus several targeted repair sessions. The loop is: sit a paper under genuine conditions, mark it together against the published scheme, name the specific reason for every lost mark, patch the two costliest topics, repeat. At higher level, Paper 3 needs its own allocated share or it gets squeezed out, which is the most common structural failure in a final-term plan.

faqs.question: Can sessions move during Ramadan for an Abu Dhabi Diploma student?
faqs.answer: Yes, and they should be planned to rather than improvised. Ramadan shifts roughly eleven days earlier each year, so it periodically sits inside the spring term and therefore inside the run-in. School days shorten, which changes arrival times home, and late-afternoon concentration drops. Put the timed papers in post-Iftar slots and the lighter review work in the shortened afternoons. Because lessons are over live video, moving a session costs nothing and requires no journey.

faqs.question: Should the run-in be booked before or after the mock results come back?
faqs.answer: Before. By the time mock papers are returned the calendar has closed in: there may be six usable weeks rather than eight, five other subjects are competing for the same hours, and the student is tired. Booking the run-in during the spring term as a deliberate decision is what makes eight weeks available. Assembling it reactively from the time that happens to be left is how a family arrives at the May session two papers short.

faqs.question: Does Paper 3 at higher level need separate preparation?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the component most often skipped. Paper 3 carries twenty per cent of the higher level grade and is an extended problem-solving investigation. The mathematics in it is familiar, which is exactly why students assume it needs no separate work, and the difficulty is structural: following the thread of a multi-part investigation under time pressure is a practised skill. Allocate it a defined share of the run-in rather than hoping general paper practice covers it.

faqs.question: Is it too late to fix non-calculator fluency in the final term?
faqs.answer: Partially. The arithmetic and algebraic automaticity that Analysis and Approaches Paper 1 assumes is built over months of short repeated practice, which is why DP1 spring is the right window for it. In a late run-in what can genuinely be improved is timing: measuring how long the paper actually takes without a calculator, adjusting question order, and deciding in advance which questions to attempt first. That is worth real marks. Rebuilding fluency from scratch in eight weeks is not realistic.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram teach at homes on Al Reem Island?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Abu Dhabi families are taught one-to-one over live video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time. On a calendar-led page the advantage is concrete: a late school finish moves a session instead of cancelling it, a family travelling over a half term keeps the plan with a time-zone adjustment, and no phase of a two-year plan is lost to a journey.

faqs.question: How long should each Diploma maths session be?
faqs.answer: Let the phase decide. The run-in needs ninety minutes, because the working unit is a paper sat under conditions plus the marking afterwards, and the marking is where most of the learning happens. Exploration coaching works well in sixty, since the material is the student's own draft. A DP1 fluency block works in forty-five or sixty, because non-calculator drills are more effective short and frequent than long and occasional. Choosing a duration before choosing a purpose wastes both.

faqs.question: What should I ask the school at the start of DP2?
faqs.answer: Five things in one email: the internal deadline for the maths exploration, the internal deadlines for the Extended Essay draft stages and the Theory of Knowledge essay, the mock examination window, which maths route and level your child is in, and whether the campus has any internal assessment deadlines in other subjects in the same term. Those five answers let a whole year be planned backwards in an afternoon, and they are the information most families acquire piecemeal and too late.

faqs.question: When should we stop paying for maths tutoring?
faqs.answer: When the block ends. A fluency block ends when the drills are automatic, an exploration block ends at submission, and a run-in ends at the examination. The measurable test inside a paper block is the ranked topic list: if it is empty and the scores have plateaued near the top of what the papers offer, the work is done. A weekly arrangement that drifts past its purpose is the most expensive pattern in this market, and it survives because comfortable sessions feel productive.

faqs.question: Where should an Al Reem Island family get the IB session and results dates from?
faqs.answer: Because none has been confirmed from the IB itself. The IB's own site blocks automated access, so no session or results date in this project has been verified at source, and a date a family builds a plan around has to be checkable. Secondary sources circulate figures that disagree with each other. The reliable route is your school's IB coordinator, who holds the campus's own calendar, plus the IB's published assessment pages. UAE Diploma schools sit the May session.

faqs.question: What does the summer between DP1 and DP2 get used for?
faqs.answer: Almost nothing, in most households, which is the quiet waste in the Diploma calendar. It is the best available window for two things: testing an exploration topic properly, so that DP2 autumn is spent on the mathematics rather than on choosing, and consolidating the fluency work that DP1 spring started. Both are low-pressure tasks that become high-pressure tasks in October. A short block of sessions across those weeks buys back a term of DP2 time.

intro.heading: The number first, then what it buys and where it leaks
paragraphs: Three of the six most visible competitors in this market publish no price at all, and one of them poses the price question in its own list of frequently asked questions and then declines to answer it. Two more quote in US dollars, a currency UAE families do not transact in. So the first job of this page is to publish the figures, with their sources and the date they were read, and then explain what each tier actually delivers for a Diploma mathematics student.

Read in October 2026, the Abu Dhabi market looks like this. Budget online tuition, often delivered by university students: AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor working online: AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. An in-home one-to-one visit with travel inside the rate: AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate quoting AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors AED 200 to 500. An IB, IGCSE or A-Level specialist: AED 200 to 450 and upwards, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. Premium named or examiner-led tuition: AED 500 to 650 and above, with BartyED publishing AED 650.

Monthly packages advertised in this market are AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work. None of these is an IB Gram price; ours is quoted after a free trial lesson, when the course, level and session length are known.

Al Samha sits in the north of the emirate, off the Dubai road, and that geography affects the cost in one specific way: in-home rates include a journey of forty minutes or more each way from the city, which is time nobody is taught in. Two families paying the same hourly figure, one in Al Mushrif and one out here, are therefore buying different amounts of teaching for it. Families out here are therefore paying a larger travel component than a family in Al Mushrif for exactly the same lesson, which is the clearest argument there is for choosing a format where the journey does not exist.

The rest of this page is about the part nobody publishes: where the money goes without producing marks. Six wastes recur, and most of them are things a provider could easily keep quiet about. Tuition here is delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; we do not offer home visits in the UAE, as in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-samha.programmesIntro: The cost of mathematics support changes sharply with the programme, because what has to be taught changes. These are the three stages an Al Samha family is likely to be budgeting for.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, at Standard or Higher Level, with five syllabus topics, a 20% Exploration and a third paper at Higher Level. This is the most expensive stage to support, because the specialism is narrow and Higher Level work needs ninety-minute sessions to be useful.
programmes.countryNote: The two-year nature of the Diploma is what makes budgeting matter. A weekly session from DP1 to the final papers is roughly sixty to seventy sessions. At the qualified online band that is a significant household commitment, and at the specialist band considerably more, which is why deciding what the hours are aimed at is a financial decision and not only an academic one.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Four criteria per subject, each marked 0 to 8, with no terminal external paper in the school-assessed route. The teaching need is general rather than course-specific, which means the budget tier can be genuinely sufficient where the aim is confidence and fluency.
programmes.countryNote: This is the stage where overspending is most common. A student needing arithmetic fluency and homework structure does not need a specialist rate, and the honest advice is often the budget tier or the school's own support. Paying specialist money at MYP 2 buys very little that the family could not get more cheaply.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Inquiry-led with no external examinations. Support is number fluency, confidence and reading, and most primary students do not need a paid tutor at all.
programmes.countryNote: If a provider is selling a long weekly commitment for a primary-aged child in this corridor, after a bus run that already tires them, ask what specific outcome it is aimed at and what would signal that it should stop. A short course of sessions with a defined end is defensible; an open-ended arrangement at this age usually is not.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-samha.subjectsIntro: Below is Diploma mathematics broken into the pieces a family is actually buying help with, each with a realistic number of sessions attached. Session counts make a budget possible; topic lists do not.

subjects.name: Algebraic fluency repair
subjects.description: Surds, index laws, rearrangement and standard form at speed, usually the gap a student arrives with from IGCSE. Four to six sessions in DP1 term one, and the cheapest intervention in the whole Diploma because it prevents compounding later.

subjects.name: Calculus foundations
subjects.description: Differentiation and integration from the beginning, including the chain rule and the constant of integration that students lose marks to for two years. Six to ten sessions, more at Higher Level where implicit differentiation and differential equations follow.

subjects.name: Functions and transformations
subjects.description: Domain, range, composites, inverses and transformation order, where horizontal shifts behave opposite to intuition. Two to four sessions usually fixes the recurring error, which is procedural rather than conceptual.

subjects.name: Trigonometry and radian discipline
subjects.description: The sine and cosine rules, identities and equations, plus the habit of checking calculator mode. A calculator left in the wrong mode invalidates every line after it, which makes this a two-session fix worth several marks a paper.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.levels: AA and AI, SL and HL
subjects.description: Distributions, regression and conditional probability, extending at AI Higher Level into chi-squared and Poisson work. AI students need more hours here than AA students, and budgets built on an AA assumption underestimate it.

subjects.name: Exploration coaching
subjects.description: Four to six sessions timed to the school's internal draft deadline, covering topic narrowing, level checking and criterion-level feedback on the student's own draft. The highest return per dirham in Diploma mathematics because a fifth of the grade is at stake.

subjects.name: Paper 3 preparation
subjects.description: Two extended problem-solving questions worth 20% of the Higher Level grade. Needs six to eight ninety-minute sessions to be done properly, which is the single largest line item in a Higher Level budget and the one most often omitted from it.

subjects.name: Calculator technique
subjects.description: Solving numerically, intersections, definite integrals, regressions and distributions on the model the school uses. Two sessions, permanently useful, and a common gap for students arriving from other curricula.

subjects.name: Mock preparation
subjects.description: Four to six sessions working the school's own paper styles before the mock window that produces the predicted grade. Bounded, dated and easy to budget for, which makes it one of the more defensible purchases of the year.

subjects.name: Method-mark discipline
subjects.description: Writing the setup before evaluating, so method marks survive a wrong answer. One session plus enforcement, and arguably the cheapest marks available anywhere in the Diploma.

subjects.name: Non-calculator fluency
subjects.levels: AA, where Paper 1 forbids a calculator
subjects.description: Exact-value work with surds, logarithms and radians, built in fifteen-minute timed blocks inside wider sessions rather than as separate lessons. Costs almost nothing extra and prevents arithmetic drag from eating a paper.

sections.heading: What it costs, in the three units families actually think in
paragraphs: Hourly rates make tutoring feel small, monthly figures make it feel real and two-year totals make it feel consequential. A Diploma runs two years, so all three units matter and only the first is ever published. The arithmetic is straightforward once the bands are in hand, and it is worth doing before committing rather than discovering in DP2.

At the qualified online band of AED 150 to 300 an hour, one session a week through a term is roughly twelve sessions. Across a full Diploma, from the start of DP1 to the final papers, a weekly session is in the region of sixty to seventy sessions. Bestimate's own monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work, give the monthly view. Multiply either by the months and the two-year picture appears.

The advertised packages anchor it further: AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, or AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Note what the second one means for an Al Samha family: eight hours of contact a month in the first case against eight hours in the second, at roughly double the price, with the difference being a tutor's journeys out to the northern corridor and back.

The point of laying this out is not to discourage spending. It is to make the spending deliberate. A family that knows a weekly two-year arrangement is a five-figure commitment at the specialist band will think harder about whether every one of those sessions is aimed at something, which is exactly the thinking that produces results. A family that only ever sees an hourly rate will not.

sections.heading: The six places the money leaks, named
paragraphs: Every one of these is something a provider could stay quiet about, and most do. They account for the majority of tutoring spend in this market that produces no measurable change, and recognising them is worth more to a family than any discount.

First, hours with no target. A weekly session that works through the textbook in order feels productive and changes nothing, because it is not aimed at the marks the student is actually losing. Second, the wrong course. A student on Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level who should be on Standard Level, or on AA when AI suited them, will absorb unlimited hours without the underlying problem moving. Third, paying for travel. In this corridor an in-home rate buys a journey of forty minutes or more each way, which teaches nothing.

Fourth, buying tier instead of fit. An examiner-led rate applied to a student whose real issue is calculator mode and missing method marks is an expensive route to a cheap fix. Fifth, parallel subjects. Three weekly tutors triples the cost and removes the evenings in which the student would practise any of the three, which in a corridor with a long bus run is close to self-defeating. Sixth, renewal by default: an arrangement with no review point and no exit criterion, continuing because nobody revisited it.

The protection against all six is the same and it is cheap: a diagnosis from a marked paper before any plan, a named target per block, a session count, and a review date with an exit criterion. That costs one free lesson and about ten minutes of conversation, and it is the difference between buying teaching and buying attendance.

sections.heading: What each tier actually delivers for a Diploma maths student
paragraphs: A rate band is only useful alongside what it buys. The honest mapping is less flattering to the top of the market than the top of the market would like, and more generous to the bottom than most agencies admit.

The budget tier, AED 45 to 150 an hour, buys supervision, structure and someone to keep a student working. For a Middle Years student needing fluency and routine that is often exactly right, and paying more buys nothing. It does not buy course-level expertise, so for Diploma content it is unsuitable: a tutor who has not taught the course cannot tell a student which of two plausible methods the mark scheme rewards.

The qualified tier, AED 150 to 300, buys someone who has taught the course and can mark against the scheme. This is the band most Diploma families should be in. It covers diagnosis, error logging, Exploration feedback, mock preparation and Standard Level content work. The specialist tier, AED 200 to 450 and upwards, buys depth at Higher Level: Paper 3 preparation, proof by induction, differential equations, AI statistics extensions. The premium tier, AED 500 to 650 and above, buys scarcity, and it is defensible only when the need is narrow and already identified.

The in-home column sits across all of these with a travel component added, and for Al Samha the travel component is large. What it buys is physical presence, which genuinely helps a younger or distractible student and helps a DP2 student working Paper 3 very little. That is the trade, stated plainly: presence against course expertise and about forty minutes of the hour.

sections.heading: Return on the spend: thinking in marks rather than hours
paragraphs: The only honest measure of tutoring value is whether marks move, so it is worth asking what each kind of work plausibly returns. Some interventions have a high and fast return; others are slow and necessary; a few have almost none and are bought anyway.

The fast returns are procedural. Method-mark discipline, one session plus enforcement, protects marks on every calculator paper. Calculator mode checking, effectively one session, protects whole questions. Transformation order and the constant of integration, two sessions each, remove recurring losses. Exploration coaching, four to six sessions, addresses 20% of the grade, over half of which sits in presentation, communication, engagement and reflection rather than mathematical difficulty.

The slow and necessary work is content. A Higher Level student who has not understood implicit differentiation needs sustained teaching over a term, and no amount of technique work substitutes for it. Paper 3 preparation sits here too: six to eight ninety-minute sessions, because the skill is stamina and structure across unfamiliar problems rather than recall, and it cannot be compressed into shorter sessions without losing the thing being practised.

The near-zero returns are the ones worth refusing. Re-teaching a two-year syllabus in the final eight weeks. General revision with no error log behind it. A second weekly subject bought when the student has no remaining evenings. And any arrangement that continues past the point where the log says the problem has gone. Declining those costs a provider money, which is precisely why so few pages list them.

sections.heading: The costs that are not in the quoted rate
paragraphs: Several real costs never appear on an invoice, and in this corridor they are larger than elsewhere. The first is the late start. A tutor driving to Al Samha in the late afternoon is subject to the same roads as everybody, so a booked hour can begin fifteen minutes late and still finish on time. Across a term that is several hours bought and not received, itemised nowhere.

The second is the lost session. When an in-home tutor cancels at short notice in mock week, the replacement needs to be free and willing to travel this far, which usually means the session is simply lost. Online arrangements refill most slots within the week. The difference does not show as money but as continuity, and continuity in an examination term is worth more than any individual lesson.

The third is package structure. Prepaid blocks that expire, minimum commitments bought before meeting the tutor, and cancellation terms that favour the provider all convert into money spent on nothing. Ask three questions before paying: does anything expire, what happens if we stop after one session, and who absorbs a late cancellation. A provider with clean answers to all three is unusual enough to be a signal.

The fourth is materials. Nobody should be charging for syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables: they are published by the IB and the examination boards and reproducing or redistributing them is a copyright matter. A legitimate provider cites and links them, or points to the school. If materials appear as a line item, ask what exactly is being sold.

sections.heading: The three options that cost nothing, tried first
paragraphs: A page about cost should start with the free options, and for Diploma mathematics there are three that genuinely work. They cost no money and, in this corridor, no travel time either, which makes them better value than anything on the rate table.

The first is the subject teacher and the department. Most schools run clinics or surgeries, often unadvertised, and the teacher who marks the work knows the gap already. For mathematics specifically, asking the teacher which two topics to prioritise produces a more accurate answer than any external diagnosis, because they have seen every piece of the student's work this year. For the Exploration, the supervisor's scheduled meetings are the single most valuable feedback the student will get and they are already paid for in the school fee.

The second is a classmate on the same course and level. Working a past paper together and then marking it against the published scheme is efficient and free, and explaining a method to someone else is among the most effective revision techniques known. The condition is the same course and level: an AA student and an AI student studying together will mislead each other within twenty minutes.

The third is self-marked past-paper work. Attempt a paper under timing, mark it strictly against the published scheme, and classify every lost mark by topic and type. Two cycles of that tell a family whether paid help is needed and for what, and the student keeps the skill afterwards. Recommending these three first costs us bookings, and it is the correct order because a family who gets a result from them will come back when the need is genuinely specialist.

sections.heading: Tutoring cost in the context of everything else a family pays
paragraphs: Families rarely judge tutoring against other tutors; they judge it against the school fee and the other costs of an academic year. Having both numbers in view at once makes the decision cleaner, so it is worth assembling the context even though the figures differ by family.

For a sense of the wider environment, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Abu Dhabi fees are regulated separately by ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Dubai's private school sector in 2024-25 enrolled 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula, with the International Baccalaureate accounting for 7% of enrolment, which is the clearest published indication of how small the Diploma cohort is relative to the whole market.

Against a school fee, a weekly qualified session at AED 150 to 300 an hour is a visible but secondary cost; a premium arrangement at AED 650 an hour for two years is not secondary at all. The useful exercise is to write down the annual school fee, the annual tutoring commitment at the tier being considered, and what each is expected to deliver. Most families have never seen the second number annualised.

One caution about the context: tutoring is not a requirement for progression, for Ministry of Education equivalency or for university admission, and any provider implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency about a regulatory process. Equivalency is run by the Ministry and the emirate attestation authority, should be verified on their own pages, and is not something a tutoring company performs or accelerates.

sections.heading: What cannot be bought, at any price
paragraphs: A cost page should end with the things no amount of money should purchase, because a family under deadline pressure is the one most likely to be offered them. The first is a grade. No tutor can guarantee an outcome that depends on a student's own work on a specific morning, and any guarantee offered should end the conversation.

The second is assessed work. No part of an Exploration, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or Personal Project may be produced for a student. A tutor may narrow a question, teach a technique the student applies, check that the mathematics sits at course level, and give criterion-level feedback on a draft the student wrote. One operator in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at a published price; submitting purchased work is malpractice under IB rules, the supervisor signs to authenticity, and the exposure falls on the student and can reach the whole Diploma.

The third is regulator approval. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and no UAE office. A tutoring business with premises in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval, a six-month completion window and annual renewal; that is a specific permit with a number, and it is not what an agency means when it advertises approved tutors.

The fourth is evidence that does not exist. A satisfaction percentage, an average tutor score or a success rate published without a sample size, a date and a method is a marketing device rather than a fact, and two pages in this market show review totals that contradict each other. The figures on this page are market rates from named published sources read in October 2026, which is a different kind of claim because you can go and check it.

process.title: Say what the budget is, and we will say what it buys
process.description: A straight conversation about tier and session count is more useful than a brochure. Tell us the course, the level and roughly what you can commit, and the answer will be what that buys and what it will not, including when the honest answer is the free options.

process.title: Diagnosis from a marked paper first
process.description: Before any plan, a recent marked paper is read against the published scheme and every lost mark classified by topic and type. That is what makes a session count possible, and a plan without it is a guess with an invoice attached.

process.title: Free trial lesson, no card required
process.description: One full lesson with the matched tutor, no hours bought in advance and nothing to cancel. It exists so that a family never pays for a block before knowing whether this tutor and this student work together.

process.title: A named target and a session count per block
process.description: Each block of work says what it is aimed at, how many sessions it should take, and how we will know it worked. Blocks end on the result rather than on a renewal date, which is the single biggest protection against drift.

process.title: Review, then reduce or stop
process.description: After six to eight weeks the error log is compared with where it started. When the logged failures have gone, the recommendation is fewer sessions or none. Continuing by default is the most expensive habit in this market.

whyPoints.title: The figures published with their sources
whyPoints.description: Three of six researched competitors publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars. Every AED band here names the company that published it and the month it was read, so a parent can verify rather than trust.

whyPoints.title: Two-year totals, not just hourly rates
whyPoints.description: A Diploma lasts two years, so a weekly arrangement is sixty to seventy sessions. Seeing that number before committing is what makes each session's purpose worth defining, and it is the number no tutoring page prints.

whyPoints.title: Six wastes named, including ones that cost us money
whyPoints.description: Hours with no target, the wrong course, paying for travel, buying tier instead of fit, three subjects at once, and renewal by default. Naming them reduces what families spend with us and is the honest thing to publish.

whyPoints.title: Free options recommended first
whyPoints.description: The maths teacher's two priorities, the Exploration supervisor's scheduled meetings, a classmate on the same course, and self-marked past papers. All free, all effective, and all better value than anything on the rate table.

whyPoints.title: No travel inside the price
whyPoints.description: From this corridor an in-home rate buys a journey of forty minutes or more each way. Online delivery removes it, which both lowers the cost per usable hour and widens the choice of tutor to people who have taught the course.

whyPoints.title: Blocks that end
whyPoints.description: Each block carries a target, a session count and an exit criterion, and the review is against an error log rather than a calendar. A provider that never reaches a point of recommending fewer sessions is selling attendance.

faqs.question: What does a Diploma maths tutor cost per hour around northern Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Market rates read in October 2026 put a qualified subject tutor working online at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 and upwards, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate estimating AED 200 to 450 plus. Budget online options start at AED 45 to 150. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 with travel included, and from this corridor that travel component is substantial. These are market figures from named sources, not IB Gram prices.

faqs.question: How much is two years of weekly maths tutoring, realistically?
faqs.answer: A weekly session from the start of DP1 to the final papers is roughly sixty to seventy sessions. At the qualified band of AED 150 to 300 an hour that is a substantial household commitment; at the specialist band it is considerably more. Bestimate's monthly estimates give the intermediate view: AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work. The useful exercise is to annualise it before committing rather than discovering the total in DP2.

faqs.question: Which single purchase gives the best return in Diploma maths?
faqs.answer: Exploration coaching, four to six sessions timed to the school's internal draft deadline. The Exploration is 20% of the grade in every course and level, and more than half its twenty marks sit in presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement and reflection rather than in mathematical difficulty. That makes it recoverable through process rather than through new content. The closest competitor for value is method-mark discipline, which is effectively one session plus enforcement.

faqs.question: Where do families most often waste money on maths tutoring?
faqs.answer: Six places recur. Hours with no target, working through a textbook in order. The wrong course or level, which absorbs unlimited hours without moving anything. Paying for a tutor's travel out to this corridor. Buying a premium tier when the real problem is calculator mode or missing method marks. Booking three subjects at once so the student has no evening left to practise any. And renewal by default, where an arrangement continues because nobody set a review date or an exit criterion.

faqs.question: Is the budget tier ever good enough?
faqs.answer: Yes, for the right job. At AED 45 to 150 an hour it buys supervision, routine and someone keeping the work moving, which for a Middle Years student needing fluency and structure is often exactly right, and paying more buys nothing. What it does not buy is course-level expertise, so for Diploma content it is unsuitable: a tutor who has not taught the course cannot tell a student which of two plausible methods the mark scheme actually rewards, and that judgement is the service.

faqs.question: Why do in-home quotes cost more out here than in the city?
faqs.answer: Because travel sits inside the rate and the journey from the city to this corridor is forty minutes or more each way, often into late-afternoon traffic. Published in-home bands are AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified tutor online. The gap widens with distance, and some tutors decline the trip entirely, which leaves a northern family with a shorter list of willing tutors than the search results suggested.

faqs.question: What costs are not shown in a quoted hourly rate?
faqs.answer: Four. Late starts, where a booked hour begins fifteen minutes late because of traffic and still finishes on time, which over a term is several hours paid and not taught. Lost sessions, which out here are hard to replace at short notice. Package expiry and minimum commitments bought before meeting the tutor. And materials charges, which should not exist at all, since syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes are published by the boards and reproducing them is a copyright matter.

faqs.question: Is a prepaid block of maths sessions better value than paying weekly?
faqs.answer: Ask what expires before deciding. Advertised packages in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions, and a package is good value only if the sessions are genuinely used and nothing lapses. Three questions settle it: does anything expire, what happens if we stop after one session, and who absorbs a late cancellation. Clean answers to all three are rarer than they should be.

faqs.question: What free help should we use before paying for maths tutoring?
faqs.answer: Three things. The maths teacher, asked by email for the two topics to prioritise, since they have seen every piece of your child's work this year. Every scheduled Exploration supervisor meeting, which is the most valuable feedback available and is already covered by the school fee. And a classmate on the same course and level, working a past paper together and marking it against the published scheme. Two cycles of self-marked papers will also tell you whether paid help is needed at all.

faqs.question: Does paying a higher rate get a better grade?
faqs.answer: Only if the higher rate buys something the student actually needs. A premium rate of AED 500 to 650 an hour applied to a student whose losses come from calculator mode and unwritten method lines is an expensive route to a cheap fix, and the result will be the same as a far cheaper session would have produced. Where the need is genuinely a Higher Level content gap, Paper 3 stamina or AI statistics extensions, the specialist tier is defensible because a generalist cannot close it.

faqs.question: Can we just buy eight weeks before the final exams and save the rest?
faqs.answer: You can, and it works for technique rather than content. Eight weeks will fix habitual losses, build method-mark discipline, train pacing and get whole papers completed under timing. It will not re-teach two years of mathematics, and a provider promising that is selling hope by the hour. The cheaper strategy is a short block early in DP1 to prevent the gap, because the same gap addressed in DP2 sits beneath a year of newer content and costs several times as much to clear.

faqs.question: After six weeks, what evidence should show the spend is working?
faqs.answer: By the error log rather than by how sessions feel. Before the first lesson, every lost mark on a recent paper is classified by topic and type. Six to eight weeks later a fresh paper is marked the same way and the two logs compared. If the logged failures have gone, the money worked and the recommendation should be fewer sessions. If the distribution looks identical, the diagnosis was wrong and the plan should be redone rather than continued at the same rate.

faqs.question: Is tutoring needed for Ministry of Education equivalency or university entry?
faqs.answer: No, and any provider implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency about a regulatory process. Equivalency is run by the Ministry of Education and the emirate attestation authority, should be verified on their own pages, and is not something a tutoring company performs, guarantees or accelerates. The published British-track requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one A-Level at E or two AS-Levels at the same grade.

faqs.question: Under what circumstances would you advise cancelling the sessions?
faqs.answer: A fresh marked paper showing the logged failures have gone, which is the stated exit criterion for every block. Also: a diagnosis that the real problem is the course or level rather than the teaching, a student too tired and over-scheduled to use another commitment, or a gap the school's own clinic can close for nothing. A provider that never reaches a point of recommending fewer sessions is selling attendance rather than teaching, and the willingness to finish is the signal worth looking for.

intro.heading: Thirty kilometres, and what it changes
paragraphs: Al Shamkha is a mainland district on the south-eastern side of Abu Dhabi, a settled villa community with its own shops and schools and a journey of roughly half an hour to the island on a clear run. In the late afternoon the run is not clear. That single fact is the reason this page exists, because it changes the answer to a question that families in Saadiyat or Al Bateen never have to ask: who is actually available to teach my child at five o'clock on a Tuesday.

The honest comparison is worth making directly. A family on Saadiyat Island looking for a Higher Level mathematics specialist has a reasonable chance of finding one living within fifteen minutes. A family in Al Shamkha looking for the same specialist is drawing from a far smaller set, because the tutor has to be willing to make a sixty-kilometre round trip for a sixty-minute lesson, and the ones who are willing charge for it. Market rates for in-home visiting in the emirate sit at AED 180 to 350 an hour in published survey data, with independent home tutors quoted from AED 200 to 500, and the upper end of those ranges is where a long journey lands.

The conclusion this page argues for is not that Al Shamkha families are disadvantaged. It is that the Saadiyat family and the Al Shamkha family should buy the same thing, and the Al Shamkha family simply notices it first. Diploma mathematics specialists are scarce by course and level rather than by district. A tutor who has taught Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level and marked Paper 3 work is rare everywhere in the emirate, and filtering that small set by driving distance makes it smaller still, regardless of where you start.

So the plain statement: IB Gram does not offer home visits in Al Shamkha or anywhere in the UAE, because home visiting is a service we run only in India. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. From a mainland address that is not a concession, it is the thing that puts an Al Shamkha household on the same footing as a household inside the school cluster, and it removes the half hour of travel risk that otherwise sits in front of every session.

The mathematics on this page is aimed at the decision that most changes a Diploma points total, which is not the choice of course but the choice of level. Higher Level mathematics carries two hundred and forty published teaching hours against one hundred and fifty at Standard Level, adds a third examination paper worth a fifth of the grade, and is the single most common cause of a Diploma student carrying a subject they cannot sustain. Getting that decision right in DP1 is worth more than any amount of tuition later.

The rest of the page is the detail: the commute arithmetic in a table, why the in-person pool thins with distance, the Higher and Standard Level comparison, what Paper 3 actually asks and how to practise it, a direct household-by-household comparison showing where the answer converges, what Diploma grades mean and why no page should publish a boundary, the market rates with sources, and the limits we work inside.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-shamkha.programmesIntro: Al Shamkha students reach Diploma mathematics by several routes, and from a mainland address the route often includes a school change. Each entry point leaves a different gap.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Two courses at two levels. Standard Level sits two papers plus the exploration across one hundred and fifty published teaching hours; Higher Level sits three papers plus the exploration across two hundred and forty. External papers carry eighty per cent of the grade, so examination technique is not a finishing touch but a substantial part of the qualification.
programmes.countryNote: For a household in Al Shamkha, the level decision interacts with the commute. A Higher Level student travelling an hour a day has materially less study time than the published hours assume, and that is a legitimate factor in the decision rather than an excuse. It is worth raising with the Diploma coordinator before choices are locked.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Four criteria, graded one to eight, with inquiry and reflection embedded. Students arrive in DP1 comfortable explaining a method and frequently slower at executing one, because criterion-referenced assessment rewards the explanation more generously than the speed.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP to Diploma step is the most common reason a mainland family books mathematics tuition in DP1 term one. The gap is almost always algebraic speed rather than comprehension, and it is diagnosable in a single trial lesson. Left alone it shows up as unfinished papers rather than wrong answers.

programmes.name: Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE mathematics
programmes.description: Terminal written papers, tiered Core and Extended or Foundation and Higher. Extended and Higher students arrive with sound manipulation and no exposure to proof, radians or calculus. Core and Foundation students arrive missing content the Diploma assumes, which is a different and larger problem.
programmes.countryNote: Where an Al Shamkha student moves school between Year 11 and DP1 — a common pattern for families whose local options stop at Year 11 — the handover of information between schools is imperfect. A marked IGCSE script in a parent's hand is often the only diagnostic record that travels with the student.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-al-shamkha.subjectsIntro: These are the components and topics where Diploma mathematics grades are decided, with the specific work each requires. The ordering reflects how much of the grade sits in each rather than how hard it feels.

subjects.name: Paper 3 extended problem solving
subjects.description: One hour, a fifth of the Higher Level grade, built from long scaffolded investigations. The deciding skill is using earlier parts in later ones and refusing to abandon a question. Students who have never sat one to time are improvising on the day with a fifth of their grade.

subjects.name: Calculus at Higher Level
subjects.description: The largest single content demand in the course. Marks go to notation, missing constants of integration, and failure to recognise which rule a composite expression requires. Volume of practice matters more here than any explanation.

subjects.name: Proof and reasoned argument
subjects.levels: Analysis and Approaches HL and SL
subjects.description: A style of writing rather than a topic. Students assert steps they believe obvious and stop once personally convinced rather than at the required conclusion. Both habits are correctable with marked written work and almost nothing else.

subjects.name: Statistical inference and modelling
subjects.levels: Applications and Interpretation HL and SL
subjects.description: The heart of the Applications course. Marks sit in interpretation rather than computation: a model applied beyond the range the data supports, or a correct result described in language that does not say what it means.

subjects.name: The mathematics exploration
subjects.description: Twenty marks across five published criteria, with reflection and personal engagement carrying three each and most often under-scored. The criteria can be read before the topic is chosen, which is the single most useful thing a DP1 student can do with an hour.

subjects.name: Graphic display calculator fluency
subjects.description: Recording the command used, working in the correct angle mode, and storing values rather than re-entering rounded ones. Entirely trainable in two or three sessions, and a steady source of lost marks until it is.

subjects.name: Radians and trigonometric work
subjects.levels: Analysis and Approaches HL and SL
subjects.description: Persistent error source well into DP2, particularly where a derivative is only valid in radians. Identity manipulation is pattern recognition, built by many short exercises rather than by long explanation.

subjects.name: Vectors, lines and planes
subjects.description: Scalar and vector products and the geometry underneath them. Students who compute without meaning attached stall on the reasoning parts rather than the arithmetic, which looks like a hard topic and is a translation problem.

subjects.name: Sequences, series and binomial expansion
subjects.description: Reliable marks for students who identify structure quickly and a reliable loss for those who try to spot patterns numerically. Higher Level extends into infinite series work that rewards algebraic confidence.

subjects.name: Timing and question selection under pressure
subjects.description: Not a topic, and worth more marks than several. Students routinely spend twelve minutes on a four-mark question and leave later marks unattempted. Four timed papers with a stopwatch usually fixes more than four content lessons would.

sections.heading: Al Shamkha against the island: the commute arithmetic
paragraphs: Begin with the numbers, because the rest follows from them. Al Shamkha sits on the mainland south-east of the city. A clear run to the island takes around half an hour; the late-afternoon run takes considerably longer and varies day to day in a way that cannot be planned around. For a student attending a mainland school the daily total on the road is commonly close to an hour; for one attending an island school it is more.

That hour comes from somewhere, and in practice it comes out of study time. The published teaching hours for a Diploma course assume a student with ordinary capacity to work outside lessons. A Higher Level mathematics student on the road for an hour a day has roughly five fewer usable hours a week than a classmate who walks to school, which over two years is a substantial quantity of the practice that Higher Level mathematics specifically requires.

The second consequence is the one this page is about. A visiting tutor making the trip is committing to a sixty-kilometre round journey plus traffic risk for a single lesson. Most Diploma specialists will not, and the ones who will price it accordingly: published in-home rates in the emirate run from AED 180 to 350 an hour in survey data and from AED 200 to 500 among independent home tutors, with long journeys at the upper end. So a mainland family pays more for a smaller choice of tutor, which is the opposite of what you want when the subject is scarce.

The table sets out the comparison across the districts an Al Shamkha family would reasonably consider. The last column is the practical one: what each situation does to a weekday session, which is the thing that determines whether a tuition plan survives past week six.

sections.heading: Why the in-person specialist pool thins with distance
paragraphs: Tutoring supply is not distributed like retail. A specialist in Higher Level Diploma mathematics is a person with a particular teaching history, and there are not many of them in any emirate. They cluster where the schools are, because that is where they taught or teach, and their availability is concentrated in the same late-afternoon hours every family wants.

Stack those constraints and the arithmetic becomes clear. Take the set of people who can teach Higher Level Analysis and Approaches and have marked Paper 3 work. Intersect it with the set willing to drive to Al Shamkha in the afternoon. Intersect that with the set free between five and seven on the specific weekday your household can hold. The result is frequently empty, and when it is not empty it is one person with no alternative if the match is wrong.

What families do next is the real problem. Faced with an empty set, most substitute: a general mathematics tutor who is available and nearby, or a university student at a lower rate. Published budget rates in the UAE start at roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, and at that level the lesson is usually a review of work already attempted. For a Standard Level student who needs supervision, that may be enough. For a Higher Level student with a Paper 3 problem, it is spending money on a different service and calling it the same thing.

Removing the travel constraint changes the arithmetic rather than the standards. The set of people who can teach the course becomes the set you choose from, and the remaining constraint is the hour of the day, which is negotiable. That is the whole argument for delivering this subject over live video, and it is stronger from Al Shamkha than from anywhere on the island — which is why we would rather make it here than bury it.

sections.heading: Higher or Standard Level: the decision that moves the points total
paragraphs: Course choice gets the attention; level choice does the damage. A student carrying Higher Level mathematics they cannot sustain loses points in that subject and in the two or three others that lose the study time it consumes. A student at Standard Level who could have managed Higher has usually lost nothing but a university prerequisite, which is recoverable in a way a wrecked DP2 is not.

The published difference in scale is the clearest guide. Higher Level mathematics is a two hundred and forty hour course; Standard Level is a hundred and fifty. That is not a small increment in difficulty, it is sixty per cent more teaching, and the extra content is the harder content. Higher Level also adds Paper 3, a third examination worth a fifth of the grade, while the exploration remains twenty per cent at both levels.

The right basis for the decision is evidence rather than ambition: how the student performed in IGCSE or MYP mathematics, how quickly they work rather than whether they understand, and whether they have the weekly hours. The commute belongs in that calculation for an Al Shamkha family, honestly rather than apologetically. An hour a day on the road is five hours a week, and Higher Level mathematics is the subject least tolerant of a thin practice schedule.

On universities, do not take a summary from anybody, including this page. Engineering, physics and some economics programmes commonly expect Higher Level mathematics, often in the Analysis course, but the authoritative statement is each institution's own published admission requirements, and they change. For families looking at the Emirates, read the current pages for Khalifa University, United Arab Emirates University, the American University of Sharjah, New York University Abu Dhabi and Zayed University directly. For Ministry of Education equivalency, no Diploma points figure should be quoted to you without a reference on the ministry's own site.

sections.heading: Paper 3: one hour, a fifth of the Higher Level grade
paragraphs: Paper 3 is the least prepared component in Diploma mathematics and the easiest to improve, which is an unusual combination. It runs for a single hour at Higher Level and carries twenty per cent of the grade, making it worth two-thirds of a main paper for a quarter of the writing. It consists of long scaffolded investigations rather than discrete questions, and it rewards something no other part of the course trains.

The skill is sustained work on one problem with earlier parts feeding later ones. A student who answers part (a), fails part (b) and stops has forfeited parts (c) through (f), several of which were answerable using the given result from part (b) whether or not they derived it themselves. That single behavioural rule — use what the question gives you and keep going — is worth more marks on Paper 3 than any content teaching.

Practising it requires actual papers sat to the clock, and there are fewer available than for Papers 1 and 2, which is part of why students skip it. The method that works is to sit a full paper under conditions, mark it against the published scheme, and then rework the point of failure rather than the whole paper. Three cycles of that typically changes a student's behaviour on the paper permanently, because the fault being corrected is a habit and not a gap.

For an Al Shamkha family this is also the most efficient use of a constrained week. A bounded block of three to five sessions on Paper 3 technique costs a fraction of a term's weekly tuition and addresses a fifth of the Higher Level grade. We would rather sell that than an open-ended arrangement, and where a student's Papers 1 and 2 work is sound we will say that a Paper 3 block is the whole of what they need.

sections.heading: The same answer either way: five households compared
paragraphs: This page began with a comparison and it is worth finishing it honestly, because the conclusion is not the one a page about a mainland district is expected to reach. The differences between an Al Shamkha household and a Saadiyat household are real, and almost none of them changes what the family should buy.

What genuinely differs is travel time, the cost of a visiting tutor, the size of the in-person pool, and in some cases the school's own Diploma provision. What is identical is the course, the examination structure, the exploration criteria, the Paper 3 problem, the hours the student needs outside lessons, and the scarcity of specialists by course and level rather than by postcode. The identical list is longer and it contains everything that determines the grade.

The table puts five households side by side. Read the third column first: it is the same in every row. A Higher Level Analysis student in Al Shamkha and a Higher Level Analysis student in Al Bateen need the same tutor, the same marked work, the same three cycles of Paper 3 practice and the same honest conversation about whether the level is sustainable. The Al Shamkha family simply reaches that conclusion sooner, because their alternative is visibly worse.

The practical upshot is a short instruction. Stop filtering by distance, which is costing you the thing you need, and start filtering by course, level and marking practice. Then solve the time of day, which is a solvable problem. That is the whole method, and it works equally well from a villa in Al Shamkha and an apartment on the Corniche.
