sections.heading: Where the marks sit: paper weightings at both levels
paragraphs: Students revise as though all components are equal. They are not, and the weighting tells a student where an hour of work returns the most. The structure is the same across both courses: Standard Level sits two papers plus the exploration, Higher Level sits three papers plus the exploration, and the exploration is worth a fifth of the grade in every case.

At Higher Level the arithmetic is worth sitting with. Each written paper carries thirty per cent and Paper 3 twenty, which means Paper 3 is worth two-thirds of a main paper despite running for a single hour. It is also the component students prepare for least, partly because there are fewer past examples and partly because its format rewards a skill — sustained work on one long scaffolded problem — that no other part of the course trains. A Higher Level student who has never sat a full Paper 3 to time is leaving a fifth of the grade to chance.

At Standard Level the two papers carry forty per cent each, so the external examination is the whole story apart from the exploration. The useful consequence is that timing practice matters more than breadth: a student who knows the content and runs out of time is losing marks that no further teaching will recover, and that is a fixable problem with four or five timed papers and a stopwatch.

The exploration is the component with the best return on effort anywhere in the course, because it is marked against published criteria the student can read in advance, in their own time, without exam pressure. Twenty marks, no invigilator, criteria available from the start. A student who treats it as a chore and writes it in a weekend is discarding the only part of the Diploma mathematics grade they fully control.

sections.heading: The exploration: twenty marks the student controls completely
paragraphs: The mathematics exploration is marked against five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection, and use of mathematics. Twenty marks in total, with use of mathematics carrying the largest single allocation and reflection and personal engagement carrying three each. Those three-mark criteria are where most Abu Dhabi explorations lose ground, because they reward something students do not think of as mathematics.

A typical failing pattern looks like this. The student picks a topic they half-like, executes the mathematics competently, presents it neatly, and submits. The mathematics scores well. Personal engagement scores low, because nothing in the piece shows why this student chose this question. Reflection scores low, because the piece records what was done rather than considering what the results meant, where the approach broke down and what a different method would have shown. Those lost marks required no extra mathematics at all, only a different conception of what the piece is for.

The practical advice is to read the criteria before choosing the topic, not after writing the draft. A topic that cannot support genuine reflection — one where the answer is known in advance and there is nothing to be surprised by — caps two criteria from the outset, no matter how well it is executed. Topic choice is therefore a mathematical decision and not an aesthetic one, and it is the single most useful conversation a tutor can have with a DP1 student.

The boundary is firm and we state it to the student directly. A tutor may teach the criteria, discuss topic viability, read the student's own draft, ask questions that expose an unsupported claim and point out which criterion a section is failing to address. A tutor may not supply sentences, restructure a draft into a finished piece, or produce any part of the exploration for submission. We decline that, because the entry belongs to the student and work they did not produce puts the whole Diploma at risk.

sections.heading: What a weekly Diploma maths hour should actually contain
paragraphs: A weekly lesson that consists of going through the week's homework feels productive and moves grades slowly, because it follows the school's agenda rather than the student's gaps. A lesson with a structure does better, and the structure is not complicated.

A workable shape for sixty minutes: ten minutes on the marked work set at the end of the last session, reviewing not the answers but the pattern of errors; twenty-five minutes teaching or repairing the diagnosed weakness, with the student working rather than watching; fifteen minutes on past-paper questions in that topic, under something close to exam timing; and the last ten setting written work for the week with an explicit instruction about what to show. At ninety minutes the proportions hold and the middle block doubles.

Two habits separate sessions that work from sessions that feel nice. The student should be writing for most of the lesson, because mathematics is not a spectator activity and watching a tutor solve a problem builds a false sense of competence that evaporates in an exam. And the lesson should end with something written down to be done, marked and returned, because the work between lessons is where the learning actually consolidates.

There should also be an error log, kept across every paper the student sits. One line per lost mark: the question, the topic, and the category — content not known, method known but misapplied, calculator or notation error, misread command, ran out of time. After three papers the pattern is unmistakable and the revision plan writes itself. Most students have never kept one, and it is the cheapest piece of exam preparation available to a Diploma mathematician.

sections.heading: Ramadan, holidays and the shape of the Abu Dhabi school year
paragraphs: A tuition plan that ignores the UAE calendar fails twice a year on schedule. The Abu Dhabi academic year runs with three terms and substantial breaks, and the sensible planning question is not how many lessons a student will have but which weeks are genuinely available for sustained work.

Ramadan is the clearest example, and it is handled badly by most providers. School days shorten, energy in the late afternoon drops, and the useful study window moves. For many families the answer is a post-Iftar session in the evening, which works well and requires nothing more than agreeing it in advance rather than discovering it in week two. For others it is a reduced cadence for the month with written work maintaining contact, picked up fully afterwards. Both are reasonable; the mistake is leaving the existing four o'clock slot in place and watching it fail.

The long summer break is the other structural feature worth planning around. For a student moving from IGCSE into DP1, those weeks are the most productive tuition window in the whole Diploma, because there is no competing coursework and the content taught then is absorbed rather than crammed. For a DP1 student heading into DP2, the same weeks are when an exploration can be properly thought about instead of rushed in a term already carrying the Extended Essay.

Term-time planning should work backwards from the school's internal deadlines rather than forwards from today. The exploration draft date, the final submission date and the mock window are the dates that govern a Diploma plan; the examination window itself is almost never the binding constraint. Get those three dates from the school at the start of the year, write them on the calendar, and build the tuition cadence around them.

sections.heading: What the travel premium buys, and what the market charges
paragraphs: Start with the premium rather than the base rate, because it is the figure that explains the rest of the market. A visiting tutor's hour in Abu Dhabi is priced at AED 180 to 350 in the Bestimate Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, with independent home tutors quoted from AED 200 to 500. Set against published online rates for a qualified subject tutor of roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour on agency rate pages read in October 2026, the loading is real and it is mostly a transport charge.

What that loading buys is physical presence in the room, which has genuine value for some students, particularly younger ones and those who need supervision rather than teaching. What it costs is twofold. There is the money, and there is the narrowing of choice: the set of tutors willing to drive into a north-island tower district at five in the afternoon is much smaller than the set who teach Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and for a Diploma mathematics student the second set is the one that matters.

The wider bands, all read in October 2026 and all belonging to the market rather than to us, run as follows. Budget online or university-student tutoring is advertised from AED 45 to 150 an hour. A qualified subject tutor online sits at AED 150 to 300. IGCSE and IB specialists are quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above in the Bestimate survey, and a premium named tutor has been advertised at AED 650 an hour. On a monthly basis for one weekly hour, the same survey estimates AED 240 to 600 at budget level, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

IB Gram does not publish a price list on this page and does not offer home visits in Al Zahiyah or anywhere in the UAE, since home visiting is an India-only service for us. What we do offer is a free trial lesson and a consultation in which the course, the level and the diagnosis get established first; the only condition attached is that the trial is one lesson and you decide afterwards.

sections.heading: What a Diploma maths tutor will not do
paragraphs: Three boundaries matter, and all three are places where providers in this market go wrong. The first is authorship. A tutor may teach the content, explain what each exploration criterion rewards, read a student's own draft and question it. A tutor may not supply sentences for submission, edit a draft into a finished piece, provide solutions to live assessed work or sit beside a student during an assessment. At least one site competing in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright for a four-figure dirham sum; the consequences of buying one land on the student, not the seller.

The second is board material. Specifications, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides belong to the IB and are published through the organisation's own channels and through schools. We do not reproduce or distribute them. A tutor works through them with the student from the official source, which is also the only way to be certain the version in use is current.

The third is what gets promised. No tutor can promise a grade, a points total or a particular university outcome, and a provider who does should be treated with real scepticism. Nor should any tutor be described as a current IB examiner unless that status can be evidenced, and examiner experience must never be used to imply access to marking, grade boundaries or unreleased papers. IB Gram holds no accreditation, licence or partnership from the IB, ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, and has no UAE office or centre.

There is one honest note about dates that follows from the same principle. Specific IB examination and results dates are not published on this page, because the organisation's own site is the only place to confirm them and we would rather state that than publish a date a parent acts on. The session UAE schools sit is the May one; for the exact windows, ask your school's Diploma coordinator or read the IB's own assessment pages.

faqs.question: What time can an IB maths lesson realistically start in Al Zahiyah?
faqs.answer: It depends on the school cluster and whether your child travels by bus. A short island journey supports a four o'clock start. Al Mushrif or Al Bateen pushes it to half past four. Saadiyat, Al Reem or the Khalifa City corridor puts it at five or later, and a school bus adds thirty to fifty minutes to any official finish. The reliable method is to record the actual arrival time for a week, take the latest, and add fifteen minutes for changing and eating.

faqs.question: Does an IB maths tutor visit homes in Al Zahiyah?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We deliver one-to-one Diploma mathematics tuition over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and we do not offer home visits in Al Zahiyah or anywhere else in the UAE, because home visiting is a service we run only in India. Independent tutors in the emirate do visit, and the market prices that at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour. For a Higher Level course the scarce resource is a specialist in that specific course, not somebody willing to drive.

faqs.question: Should my Al Zahiyah child take Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation?
faqs.answer: Decide by what they intend to study afterwards and how they think, not by which looks easier. Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-led, with Paper 1 sat without any technology. Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistics led, with technology permitted throughout, and its interpretation marks are harder than students expect. Engineering and physical science programmes commonly expect Analysis, often at Higher Level, but verify that on each university's own published admission requirements rather than any summary.

faqs.question: How much is Paper 3 worth at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent of the Higher Level grade, from a single sixty-minute paper. Each of Papers 1 and 2 carries thirty per cent and the exploration the remaining twenty. That makes Paper 3 worth two-thirds of a main paper for a sixth of the writing time, and it is the component students prepare for least because its long scaffolded format trains a skill nothing else in the course does. A Higher Level student who has never sat one to time is leaving a fifth of the grade unexamined.

faqs.question: How many marks is the mathematics exploration worth?
faqs.answer: Twenty marks, which is twenty per cent of the final mathematics grade at both Standard and Higher Level. They are split across presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics, with use of mathematics carrying the largest single allocation. Reflection and personal engagement carry three marks each and are where most explorations lose ground, because they reward something students do not think of as mathematics. The criteria are published and can be read before the topic is chosen.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with my Al Zahiyah child's exploration?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the criteria, discuss whether a topic can support genuine reflection, read your child's own draft, ask the questions that expose an unsupported claim and point at the criterion a section is failing. A tutor cannot supply sentences, restructure the draft into a finished piece, or produce any part of it for submission. We decline that. The entry belongs to your child, and material they did not produce puts the whole Diploma at risk rather than just that component.

faqs.question: What should a weekly Diploma maths lesson actually contain?
faqs.answer: A structure rather than a review of homework. A workable sixty minutes runs: ten minutes on the pattern of errors in last week's marked work, twenty-five teaching or repairing the diagnosed weakness with the student writing rather than watching, fifteen on past-paper questions in that topic under something close to exam timing, and ten setting written work with explicit instructions about what to show. Lessons that consist of following the school's homework feel productive and move grades slowly.

faqs.question: How do we handle tuition during Ramadan in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Agree the change in advance rather than discovering it in the second week. School days shorten and late-afternoon energy drops, so the two workable options are a post-Iftar evening session or a reduced cadence for the month with written work maintaining contact with the course. Both work. What fails is leaving an existing four o'clock slot in place and watching it get cancelled. We arrange the shift at the start of the month as a matter of routine rather than on request.

faqs.question: Is the summer break a good time to start Diploma maths tuition?
faqs.answer: For a student crossing from IGCSE into DP1 it is the best window in the whole two years. There is no competing coursework, so content taught then is absorbed rather than crammed alongside six new courses, Theory of Knowledge and an Extended Essay, and specialist availability is at its widest. For a DP1 student heading into DP2, the same weeks are when an exploration can be thought about properly instead of rushed during a term already carrying the Extended Essay.

faqs.question: Why does my child's grade not move even though they do the homework?
faqs.answer: Usually because the homework follows the school's agenda rather than the student's gaps, and because nobody is marking written work against a published scheme. Doing exercises in a topic already understood builds confidence and no marks. The diagnostic step is an error log kept across every paper: one line per lost mark, categorised as content, method, calculator or notation, misread command, or ran out of time. After three papers the pattern is obvious and the plan writes itself.

faqs.question: What does the travel premium on a home visit actually pay for?
faqs.answer: Mostly transport and waiting. A visiting tutor's hour is quoted at AED 180 to 350 in the Bestimate Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, with independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500, against roughly AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online on agency rate pages read in October 2026. The loading buys presence in the room, which genuinely helps some students. It also narrows your choice of tutor to whoever can reach a north-island tower by five o'clock.

faqs.question: When are the IB examinations, and why does this page not give dates?
faqs.answer: Because the organisation's own site is the only place those dates can be confirmed, and we would rather say so than publish a date you might act on. The session UAE schools sit is the May one, with a November session also available. For the exact windows and results dates, ask your school's Diploma coordinator or read the IB's published assessment pages. Any tutoring site quoting you a specific Diploma results date without citing the organisation is passing on something it has not verified.

faqs.question: How long does it take to fix a Diploma maths problem?
faqs.answer: It depends on the category, which is why the diagnosis comes first. Calculator and notation errors, early rounding and misread command terms often return marks within three or four lessons because each is one rule plus practice. A missing topic takes a few weeks of teaching. Weak algebraic fluency underneath everything takes a term or more, because it is a volume problem rather than a comprehension one. No tutor can promise a grade, and the review date exists so that an honest answer gets given at a fixed point.

faqs.question: Can a weekend session work instead of a weekday one for a Diploma student?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for some Al Zahiyah households it is the only honest answer. Where a mainland school plus two sibling collections makes the weekday arithmetic impossible, one longer weekend session beats a weekday lesson that survives on alternate weeks. Retention is slightly better with two shorter contacts a week, so we set written work across the week to maintain contact with the course, and review after a month to check that the single-session pattern is actually holding.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-baniyas.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Diploma mathematics at Standard and Higher Level in both courses. The first thing a specialist does is name the failure mode from marked work, because the five on this page need five different interventions and cost different amounts of time.

intro.heading: Name the failure before buying the repair
paragraphs: Most families arrive with a grade and a feeling: the mathematics is going badly. That is a symptom, not a diagnosis, and the gap between the two costs real money. Diploma mathematics fails in a small number of recognisable ways, and the interventions for them are not interchangeable. One takes three lessons. One takes a term. One is not a mathematics problem at all. Buying a general weekly arrangement without knowing which you have is how a household spends six thousand dirhams and finds the next report unchanged.

The five modes, briefly. Procedural faults, where a rule was never learned or is misapplied. Fluency faults, where the student understands but works too slowly to finish. Technique faults, where the content is known and the marks leak through notation, rounding, command words or calculator handling. Content gaps, where a topic genuinely was not learned. And load faults, where the student is competent and has too little time, usually because the level is unsustainable or the week is full. The table in the first section sets out what each looks like and what it costs to fix.

Baniyas is a large mainland district on the south-eastern side of Abu Dhabi, built out across eastern and western sides with numbered sectors, with Mussafah and Al Shawamekh nearby. The load fault is more common here than on the island for a mundane reason: an hour or more a day on the road is roughly five usable study hours a week, and Diploma mathematics is the subject least tolerant of a thin practice schedule. That is worth naming honestly rather than treating as an excuse, because it changes which repair is realistic.

On delivery, plainly: IB Gram does not offer home visits in Baniyas or anywhere in the UAE, because home visiting is a service we run only in India. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. For a diagnosis-led approach the relevant point is that the person who can identify a Higher Level failure mode from a marked script is a specialist in that course, and specialists are scarce by course and level across the whole emirate rather than by district.

The rest of this page is practical. The five failure modes with repair times. How to read a DP1 report comment and work out which mode it is describing. What changes between Paper 1 and Paper 2, because they are prepared for differently and most students prepare for both the same way. The Diploma's marking conventions, including exact form, follow-through and the requirement to record a calculator command. A comparison with the neighbouring mainland districts, which fail identically. An honest account of cadence and when to stop. What it costs to fix the right thing. And the boundaries we work inside.

Every AED figure on this page belongs to the market, is attributed to a named published source and was read in October 2026. No examination or results date for the Diploma appears here, because the organisation's own site is the only place to confirm one, and a date a parent acts on should not come from a tutoring page.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-baniyas.programmesIntro: The three Diploma mathematics configurations below behave differently under pressure, and the same failure mode has different consequences in each. Knowing the configuration tells a tutor how much room there is.

programmes.name: Analysis and Approaches, Higher Level
programmes.description: The most demanding configuration in Diploma mathematics: proof, calculus at volume, complex numbers, vectors in three dimensions, and three examination papers including the extended problem-solving Paper 3. Paper 1 is sat without any technology, which means manipulation by hand has to be genuinely fluent rather than merely correct.
programmes.countryNote: This is where the load fault most often shows up in a Baniyas household, because the course assumes study hours that an hour-a-day commute quietly removes. Where the diagnosis is load rather than ability, the honest conversation is with the Diploma coordinator about level, not with a tutor about more sessions.

programmes.name: Analysis and Approaches, Standard Level
programmes.description: Two papers plus the exploration, with Paper 1 again sat without technology. The content is narrower than at Higher Level and the demand for exact-form work and clean algebra is the same, which surprises students who expected the Standard Level route to be forgiving about arithmetic.
programmes.countryNote: Technique faults dominate at this level in the scripts we see: notation, rounding too early, command words misread, and answers given as decimals where an exact form was required. All of those are cheap to repair, which makes Standard Level Analysis one of the better returns on a short block of tuition.

programmes.name: Applications and Interpretation, both levels
programmes.description: Modelling, statistics, regression and financial mathematics, with technology permitted on every paper. Higher Level adds Paper 3. Marks sit in interpretation as much as calculation: a model applied beyond the range its data supports, or a correct result described in language that does not say what it means, both lose credit.
programmes.countryNote: The configuration most often chosen to avoid difficulty and least often understood. Calculator discipline becomes a graded skill rather than a convenience, and students who do not record the command they used lose marks on work that was entirely correct on the screen.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-baniyas.subjectsIntro: These are the specific places Diploma mathematics marks go in Abu Dhabi scripts, grouped by which failure mode each belongs to. The mode determines the repair time more than the topic does.

subjects.name: Rounding and exact-form discipline
subjects.description: A technique fault. Students round an intermediate value and carry the error forward, or give a decimal where an exact answer was demanded. One instruction enforced across four pieces of marked work ends it, which makes it the cheapest fix available.

subjects.name: Recording the calculator command
subjects.description: A technique fault with real cost. Work done correctly on the screen and not recorded on the page earns less than the same work shown. Two or three sessions of marked practice in which the command must appear is usually sufficient.

subjects.name: Command terms in a mathematics context
subjects.description: A technique fault. 'Show that' wants a derivation arriving at the printed result and gives nothing for substituting it back; 'hence' requires the previous part to be used; 'comment on' asks for interpretation rather than restatement.

subjects.name: Algebraic manipulation speed
subjects.description: A fluency fault, and the expensive one. The student understands each step and performs it slowly, so papers go unfinished. The repair is volume of short exercises over months rather than explanation, which is why it cannot be bought late.

subjects.name: Calculus technique and notation
subjects.description: A mix of content and technique. Missing constants of integration, wrong rule selected for a composite expression, and derivative notation used loosely. Each is specific and diagnosable from a marked script.

subjects.name: Proof as a style of writing
subjects.description: A content gap in most cases, because nobody taught it as a genre. Students assert steps they consider obvious and stop once personally convinced. Several weeks of marked written proofs is the realistic span.

subjects.name: Statistical interpretation and modelling language
subjects.description: A content gap disguised as a technique fault. The calculation is right and the sentence describing it does not say what the question asked. Responds to marked written interpretation rather than to more statistics teaching.

subjects.name: Paper 3 persistence at Higher Level
subjects.description: A technique fault worth a fifth of the Higher Level grade. Students abandon a long scaffolded question at the first part that resists, forfeiting later parts that were answerable from the given result. Three marked cycles usually changes the behaviour.

subjects.name: The exploration's reflection and engagement criteria
subjects.description: A content gap about what the piece is for. Technically immaculate explorations lose the three-mark criteria because nothing in them shows why this student chose this question or what the results actually meant.

subjects.name: Timing and question selection
subjects.description: Usually a fluency symptom rather than its own fault. A student spending twelve minutes on a four-mark question has a speed problem upstream, and timed papers reveal whether the cause is fluency or simply poor selection.

sections.heading: Five ways Diploma mathematics goes wrong
paragraphs: The table is the centre of this page. Each row is a failure mode with the symptom a parent actually observes, the underlying cause, a realistic repair span and the cadence that repair needs. Reading it against a marked script takes about half an hour and replaces a guess with a decision.

The two rows worth dwelling on are the cheapest and the most expensive. Technique faults are cheap: a student losing marks to early rounding, unrecorded calculator commands and misread command words is losing them for reasons that have nothing to do with mathematics, and three to five sessions of marked practice in which the required element must appear usually ends all three. On a paper where the content is broadly known, that is frequently a double-digit mark swing.

Fluency faults are the expensive ones and the reason timing matters. A student who understands every step and performs each slowly will not finish papers, and no amount of further explanation helps, because explanation is not the missing thing. Speed comes from volume of short practice spread over months. That is why fluency is a Year 9 to DP1 problem and an extremely difficult DP2 problem, and why a provider implying a six-week block can fix it is selling hope.

The fifth mode, load, is the one families resist most and it is worth stating directly. A competent student carrying three Higher Levels, the core, mandatory subjects and an hour a day on the road may simply not have the hours the course assumes. Adding a weekly tuition session to that week displaces the written practice that makes tuition work, so the intervention makes the problem worse. The honest response is a conversation with the Diploma coordinator about level or subject load, and we will say so rather than taking the booking.

sections.heading: Reading a DP1 report: which mode is the comment describing?
paragraphs: School report comments are written to be constructive, which makes them diplomatic, which makes them hard to use. They do nonetheless contain the diagnosis, and the translation is fairly reliable once you know what to look for.

A comment about needing to show more working, or about careless errors, is almost always describing a technique fault. That is the cheapest thing on the list and the easiest to misread as inattention. A comment about needing to practise more, or about not completing assessments in the time available, is usually fluency. A comment about struggling with a particular topic, named, is a content gap. A comment that praises effort and attitude while reporting a disappointing mark is frequently load, and occasionally a content gap the teacher is being gentle about.

The comment to take most seriously is any reference to pace in class — keeping up, or needing more time than the group. That is fluency, it is the most expensive mode to repair, and it is the one that compounds, because every later topic assumes the earlier manipulation. A DP1 report saying this in term one is an unusually clear signal and the best possible time to act on it; the same comment in DP2 term two is a much harder problem.

The way to confirm any of this is the script rather than the comment. Ask for the marked assessment, and go through it assigning every lost mark to one of five categories: content never learned, method known but misapplied, notation or calculator, command word misread, or ran out of time. Those categories map onto the five modes directly. Thirty minutes, no mathematics required of the parent, and the counts give you the answer the report was too polite to spell out.

sections.heading: Paper 1 and Paper 2 are prepared for differently
paragraphs: Most students revise for the papers as though they were one assessment of different lengths. In Analysis and Approaches they are substantially different instruments, because Paper 1 is sat without any technology and Paper 2 permits it. That single difference changes what a student should practise, and a revision schedule that ignores it wastes a measurable share of the time.

Without technology, everything has to be done by hand and expressed exactly. That means confident fraction and surd work, exact trigonometric values, algebraic manipulation at speed, and calculus performed rather than checked. A student who has done all their practice with a calculator to hand has been quietly outsourcing the skill Paper 1 examines, and will discover it in the examination hall.

With technology permitted, the skills shift to selection and recording. Which function on the device answers this question, whether the device is in the right angle mode, how to store an intermediate value rather than retyping a rounded one, and crucially how to record what was done so that the page shows a method. Marks are awarded for method on the page, not for the right number appearing on a screen, and this is where Applications candidates in particular lose work that was entirely correct.

The table sets the two out. The practical instruction is to timetable them separately in revision: distinct practice sessions, distinct past-paper work, and in the case of Paper 1 a hard rule that the calculator is out of the room. Students resist this and it is the single most useful change most Analysis candidates can make to how they revise.

sections.heading: Diploma marking conventions a student should know
paragraphs: Marking is a documented process and students who understand it write differently. Diploma mathematics mark schemes distinguish method from accuracy, allow credit to follow through an earlier error, accept answers within a stated tolerance, and require working for method marks. Almost no student has read one, and reading three changes the shape of their answers permanently.

Method marks reward a correct approach even where the arithmetic afterwards fails. The behavioural consequence is blunt: a student who writes nothing down and gets the wrong answer scores zero, where one who shows a correct substitution and slips at the last step keeps most of the marks. Accuracy marks require the right value in the right form, which is where exact form and rounding discipline earn their keep. Follow-through credit allows a correct later step built on an earlier wrong answer to score — but only when the working is visible, which is the whole argument for showing it.

Two conventions specific to this subject deserve naming. Answers are often acceptable within a stated tolerance, so a student who abandons a question because their value looks untidy may have been correct. And where a question gives a result for use in a later part, that result must be used even if the student's own earlier answer differed; students who stubbornly carry their own wrong value forward forfeit marks that were protected for them.

There is also the recording convention for technology. Work performed on a graphic display calculator earns marks when the page shows which command was used and on what, and earns far fewer when the page shows only an answer. This is the most common single avoidable loss in Applications and Interpretation scripts, and it is a habit rather than a skill. Three sessions of marked work in which the command must appear is usually sufficient to fix it for good.

sections.heading: Baniyas, Mussafah and Al Shawamekh: the same five failures
paragraphs: This page is written from a comparison angle, so it is worth testing whether the neighbouring districts differ in any way that changes the advice. They do not, and the pattern is worth stating because it saves families a great deal of thinking about geography.

What differs between Baniyas, Mussafah, Al Shawamekh, Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Al Shamkha is journey length, which local tuition centres are a plausible evening trip, and whether a visiting tutor will come at all. Published in-home rates in this emirate run from AED 180 to 350 an hour in survey data and from AED 200 to 500 among independent home tutors, read in October 2026, and the longer journeys sit toward the upper end of those ranges.

What is identical is the mathematics and the failure modes. The same five modes appear in marked scripts from every one of these districts, in roughly the same proportions, because they are properties of the course and of how students learn it rather than of where they live. Paper 1 permits no technology in Mussafah and in Al Bateen. The exploration is twenty marks either way. Higher Level Paper 3 is a fifth of the grade regardless of postcode, and students everywhere abandon it at the first part that resists.

The one district-linked effect worth naming is the load fault. Households with the longest journeys lose the most study hours, and Diploma mathematics is the course least able to absorb that loss. So in Baniyas and its neighbours, load should be actively considered as a diagnosis rather than assumed away, and the honest response to it is a conversation about level and subject combination rather than an additional tuition session. The table sets out the comparison plainly.

sections.heading: Cadence: how often, how long, and when to stop
paragraphs: Cadence follows the failure mode, and getting it wrong wastes money in both directions. A technique fault treated with a year of weekly lessons is an expensive way to fix something that needed four sessions. A fluency fault treated with a six-week block produces a disappointed family and a fair conclusion that tutoring does not work.

For technique and procedural faults, a short block with marked work each session is right, and it should end. Three to five sessions, a diagnostic set before and after, and no rolling commitment. If a second fault emerges, that is a second block rather than an open-ended arrangement, and the gap between them lets you see whether the first repair held.

For fluency and content faults, weekly lessons across a term with short daily written practice. The daily part is not optional and it is where the work actually happens: fifteen or twenty minutes of retrieval practice on six days outperforms two hours in one sitting, because the skill is recalled and rebuilt on six separate occasions. In a Baniyas household where the afternoon is consumed by travel, that twenty minutes has to be placed deliberately rather than hoped for.

When to stop is the question providers avoid. The answer is when the fault frequency in marked work has fallen and stayed down across two assessments, or when a review shows the diagnosis was wrong and needs redoing rather than extending. We set a review date at the start with the measure named, and the three honest outcomes are taper, change the cadence, or change the diagnosis. A review that produces a conversation about how the lessons feel has not happened, whatever it is called.

sections.heading: What it costs to fix the right thing
paragraphs: Lead with the cost per repair rather than with the hourly rate, because that is the number a diagnosis makes available. A technique fault costing three to five sessions is, at published specialist online rates of roughly AED 200 to 450 an hour read in October 2026, a few hundred to a couple of thousand dirhams for a repair that is often worth a double-digit mark swing. That is a defined purchase with a defined outcome, which is unusual in this market.

A fluency repair is a different order of commitment. On a monthly basis, the Bestimate Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table estimates roughly AED 600 to 1,200 a month for a weekly hour mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support. Across a term that is a substantial figure, and it is the correct purchase when fluency genuinely is the fault, because nothing cheaper addresses it. A family should know they are buying months rather than weeks before they start.

The rest of the market, for reference and all read in October 2026: budget online or university-student tutoring is advertised from AED 45 to 150 an hour; a qualified subject tutor online at roughly AED 150 to 300; in-home visiting at AED 180 to 350 in survey data and AED 200 to 500 among independent home tutors; and a premium named tutor advertised at AED 650. Packages seen include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

None of those figures is IB Gram's price list and all of them belong to the market. What a diagnosis changes is not the rate but the quantity: knowing the mode tells you whether you are buying four sessions or a term, which is a far larger determinant of total spend than the hourly figure. Our own arrangement starts with a free trial lesson and a consultation; the condition on the trial is that it is one lesson and you decide afterwards. On VAT treatment of tuition fees in the UAE we state no position, as that is a question for the Federal Tax Authority.

sections.heading: The exploration, board material and promises
paragraphs: The exploration deserves its own note because it is twenty per cent of the grade and because it is where the honesty boundary actually bites in mathematics. Five published criteria, twenty marks, with reflection and personal engagement carrying three each and most often under-scored. The criteria can be read before a topic is chosen, which is the single most useful hour a DP1 student can spend on the component.

What a tutor does with it: teaches the criteria by letter with their allocations, discusses whether a chosen topic can support genuine reflection at all, reads the student's own draft, asks the questions that expose an unsupported claim, and names the criterion a section is failing to address. What a tutor does not do: supply sentences, restructure a draft into a finished piece, or produce any part of it for submission. We decline that at any price. A provider in this market advertises completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; the consequence of buying one falls on the student's whole entry rather than on the seller.

On board material: specifications, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the organisation that publishes them and are available through it and through schools. We reference and link rather than reproducing, and a tutor works through them with the student from the official source. We also publish no grade boundary, because boundaries are set after each session in light of that session's papers and performance, and a fixed figure on a tutoring page is a fabricated certainty.

On status and promises: IB Gram is an independent online matching platform with no UAE office, centre or branch, holding no accreditation, licence, approval or partnership from the IB, ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson. Any paid private tutor in the Emirates needs a private tuition work permit issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. No tutor can promise a grade or a points total, we publish no rating or satisfaction statistic, and our tutors are not described as current examiners for any board.

faqs.question: How do I work out what is actually wrong with my child's IB maths?
faqs.answer: Read the marked script rather than the report comment. Assign every lost mark to one of five categories: content never learned, method known but misapplied, notation or calculator error, command word misread, or ran out of time. The counts map directly onto five failure modes with very different repair times, from three sessions for technique faults to a term or more for fluency. Thirty minutes, no mathematics needed of you, and it replaces a guess with a decision.

faqs.question: Which Diploma maths problem is cheapest to fix?
faqs.answer: Technique faults, by a wide margin. Rounding an intermediate value, giving a decimal where exact form was required, not recording the calculator command used, and misreading command words such as 'show that' or 'hence'. All four are habits rather than gaps, and three to five sessions of marked work in which the required element must appear usually ends them. On a paper where the content is broadly known, that is often a double-digit mark swing.

faqs.question: Why does more tutoring not help my Baniyas child who already works hard?
faqs.answer: That pattern usually indicates a load fault rather than a mathematics one. A competent student carrying three Higher Levels, the Diploma core, mandatory subjects and an hour or more a day on the road may simply not have the study hours the course assumes. Adding a weekly session to that week displaces the written practice that makes tuition work, so the intervention makes it worse. The honest next step is a conversation with the Diploma coordinator about level and subject load.

faqs.question: What does it mean when a report says my child makes careless errors?
faqs.answer: Almost always a technique fault, and it is the cheapest thing on the list rather than a character observation. It typically resolves into early rounding, exact form not given, working not shown so method marks were unavailable, or a calculator command not recorded. Each has a specific fix and all of them respond to marked practice in which the required element must be present. Ask for the script and check: the comment is polite, the script is specific.

faqs.question: Why should Paper 1 be practised with the calculator out of the room?
faqs.answer: Because in Analysis and Approaches no technology is permitted in Paper 1, and a student who has done two years of practice with a device to hand has been quietly outsourcing the exact skill that paper examines. Exact trigonometric values, surds, fraction work, manipulation at speed and calculus performed rather than checked all need to be fluent unaided. Separating the two practice streams is the single most useful change most Analysis candidates make to their revision.

faqs.question: What is follow-through credit in Diploma maths marking?
faqs.answer: It allows a correct later step built on an earlier wrong answer to earn marks, provided the working is visible. That is the whole argument for showing working: a student who writes nothing and reaches a wrong answer scores zero, while one who shows a correct substitution and slips at the last step keeps most of the marks. Related conventions matter too: answers are often acceptable within a stated tolerance, and a result given in the question must be used in later parts.

faqs.question: How long does a fluency problem in Diploma maths take to fix?
faqs.answer: A term or more, and there is no honest shortcut. Fluency means performing understood steps quickly enough to finish papers, and speed is built by volume of short practice spread across many days rather than by explanation. So the pattern is weekly lessons plus fifteen or twenty minutes of daily retrieval practice, which beats two hours in one sitting because the skill is rebuilt on six separate occasions. A provider promising to fix this in six weeks is selling hope.

faqs.question: Are tutoring needs different in Baniyas than in Mussafah or Al Shawamekh?
faqs.answer: No, and that is worth knowing because it saves a lot of thinking about geography. What differs between these districts is journey length, which centres are a plausible evening trip, and whether a visiting tutor will come, with published in-home rates of AED 180 to 500 an hour reflecting the distance. What is identical is the mathematics and the five failure modes, which appear in the same proportions everywhere because they are properties of the course.

faqs.question: How much does fixing one Diploma maths fault cost?
faqs.answer: A technique fault at three to five sessions, against published specialist online rates of roughly AED 200 to 450 an hour read in October 2026, is a few hundred to a couple of thousand dirhams for a defined repair. A fluency repair is months: the Bestimate Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table estimates AED 600 to 1,200 a month mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support. The diagnosis changes the quantity, which matters more than the rate.

faqs.question: When should we stop paying for maths tuition?
faqs.answer: When the fault frequency in marked work has fallen and stayed down across two assessments, or when a review shows the diagnosis was wrong and needs redoing rather than extending. That is why a review date and a named measure are set at the start. The three honest outcomes are taper the arrangement, change the cadence because the gap is larger than assumed, or change the diagnosis. A review about how the lessons feel is not a review.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks on correct calculator work?
faqs.answer: Because marks are awarded for method shown on the page, not for a correct number appearing on a screen. Work done on a graphic display calculator earns credit when the page records which command was used and on what, and earns much less when only an answer appears. This is the most common single avoidable loss in Applications and Interpretation scripts. It is a habit, not a skill, and three sessions of marked work in which the command must appear usually fixes it permanently.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the exploration in Baniyas?
faqs.answer: Within a stated boundary. A tutor teaches the five criteria by letter with their mark allocations, discusses whether a topic can support genuine reflection at all, reads your child's own draft, asks the questions that expose an unsupported claim, and names the criterion a section is failing. A tutor does not supply sentences, restructure a draft into a finished piece or produce any part of it for submission, and we decline that at any price regardless of the deadline.

faqs.question: What mark gives a 6 in Diploma mathematics?
faqs.answer: No figure can be given honestly. Grade boundaries are set after each examination session in light of that session's papers and candidate performance, and published afterwards; they are not fixed percentages and they move between sessions. Any site quoting you a fixed threshold is inventing a certainty. What is stable is the description of what each grade represents in accuracy, method selection and handling unfamiliar problems, and that is far more useful for choosing an intervention.

faqs.question: Does a short block really work better than a year of lessons?
faqs.answer: For the right fault, yes, and it costs a fraction as much. Technique and procedural faults are bounded problems: a named rule or habit, three to five marked sessions, a diagnostic set before and after, and then it ends. The gap before any further work lets you see whether the repair held. For fluency and genuine content gaps a block is the wrong purchase and a term is the honest answer, which is exactly why the diagnosis comes first.

intro.heading: Diploma mathematics is a two-year sequence, not a subject you revise
paragraphs: Both IB mathematics courses, Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, are organised into the same five topic areas: number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus. Standard Level is prescribed at 150 teaching hours and Higher Level at 240. That ninety-hour difference is additional content rather than deeper revision, and it is taught across two years in a sequence most students never see written down.

Seeing the sequence changes how support is bought. The first year covers the bulk of the core content. The exploration, worth twenty per cent of the grade, is usually introduced late in the first year with internal draft deadlines across several months. The second year brings the hardest content, the mock cycle and, for Higher Level students, Paper 3: sixty minutes, fifty-five marks, two extended problem-solving questions worth a fifth of the grade.

The commonest and most expensive mistake is to treat all of that as a single revision problem that can be solved in the second spring. It cannot. Paper 3 technique is built over months because it is a format discipline rather than a body of knowledge. Exploration marks are decided by a topic choice made early. Non-calculator arithmetic for Analysis Paper 1 has to be practised deliberately from the first term or it is simply absent when it matters.

There is also a dated decision almost nobody plans for: the level. Moving between Higher and Standard Level is possible within a window your school sets, and a student who moves late has topics that were never taught rather than topics taught and forgotten. Ask the school early what that window is, because the answer determines whether a struggling Higher Level student has an option or only a problem.

Because no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from ibo.org, which blocks automated checking, this page names the May session as the one UAE schools sit and publishes no specific IB date. Internal deadlines for the exploration are set by your school, so ask for the list in writing. Your Diploma coordinator holds the authoritative version for your child's cohort, and a date restated on any website, this one included, is a guide to structure rather than a source to act on.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, or anywhere else in the UAE. In-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. What we deliver to the Corniche is one-to-one teaching over live video, which suits mathematics particularly well: every line of working stays visible on a shared whiteboard and is saved afterwards, so a worked Paper 3 question can be reread rather than half-remembered. Over two years that accumulated record is worth more than most families expect.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme mathematics
programmes.description: No external assessment and therefore no calendar pressure, which makes this the only stage where fluency work can be slow and thorough. A child who understands place value but cannot recall multiplication facts finds Middle Years mathematics slow rather than hard, and the cost of that compounds for years.
programmes.countryNote: Corniche primary pupils attend schools a short drive inland and are usually home by 15:00 with the afternoon clear. Two short fluency sessions a week suit this age far better than one hour, and the whole year is available rather than only the gaps between deadlines.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Four criteria, each out of eight: knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Investigating patterns is where strong arithmetic students lose marks, because the criterion wants a generalised rule with a justification rather than the next term in a sequence.
programmes.countryNote: Middle Years students on the Corniche have the earliest home-by time in the household. Use the late afternoon rather than the evening, because criteria-based written work degrades badly when attempted late. The final Middle Years year is also when the Diploma mathematics course decision should be made.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, at Standard or Higher Level. Standard Level runs two papers at forty per cent each with the exploration at twenty. Higher Level becomes thirty, thirty and twenty across three papers, with the exploration at twenty, and adds roughly a third more content.
programmes.countryNote: Corniche Diploma students travel inland to schools in Al Bateen, Al Mushrif or Al Khalidiyah, and several run study periods after a 15:30 finish. That gives a workable 17:30 or 19:30. For Higher Level mathematics, two shorter sessions a week through the first year beats three a week in the second spring.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme with a DP mathematics course
programmes.description: Where a school offers the Career-related Programme, a mathematics course taken inside it is examined on exactly the same papers with the same weightings and the same exploration. The calendar is therefore identical even though the overall qualification differs, which matters when a provider prices it as something lighter.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-corniche.subjectsIntro: Below is what has to be secure by each point in the two-year sequence, and the component each piece of work serves.

subjects.name: Number and algebra
subjects.levels: Both courses; proof at Analysis HL
subjects.description: Should be automatic by the end of the first year, because almost every later question routes through manipulation. At Analysis Higher Level this area also carries proof, which is marked on the validity of each step and needs dedicated practice rather than absorption.

subjects.name: Functions
subjects.description: Transformations, inverses, composite functions and modelling, examined on both papers throughout. Composite order reversed and domain or range ignored are the recurring errors, and both are procedural rather than conceptual, so they clear in a week or two of deliberate work.

subjects.name: Geometry and trigonometry
subjects.levels: Both courses; vectors at Analysis HL
subjects.description: Identities, equations, three-dimensional work and, at Analysis Higher Level, vectors. The reliable loss is working in the wrong angle mode, which invalidates every answer in a question, and that is a calculator discipline rather than a mathematical one.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.levels: Heavier in Applications; present in both
subjects.description: Distributions, hypothesis testing, correlation and regression. Self-contained enough to be good late-calendar work, and the recurring loss is interpretation: a coefficient calculated correctly and then described as evidence of causation.

subjects.name: Calculus
subjects.levels: Both courses; substantially deeper at Analysis HL
subjects.description: Differentiation, integration, kinematics and, at Analysis Higher Level, techniques including substitution and parts. Chain-rule errors inside composites and sign errors in definite integrals account for a large share of Higher Level losses and need sustained practice.

subjects.name: The exploration
subjects.description: Twenty marks across presentation four, mathematical communication four, personal engagement three, reflection three and use of mathematics six, with twelve to twenty pages recommended. Four of the five criteria are effectively decided by how narrow the topic is.

subjects.name: Paper 3, Higher Level only
subjects.description: Sixty minutes, fifty-five marks, two extended problem-solving questions that lead a student through unfamiliar territory in stages. It rewards reading every part first, carrying results forward unrounded, showing reasoning and parking a stalled part rather than fighting it.

subjects.name: Non-calculator arithmetic
subjects.description: Analysis forbids a calculator on Paper 1 at both levels, so fraction arithmetic, surds, estimation and long multiplication have to be genuinely automatic. This must be practised from the first term; introduced in the second spring it reveals itself as a problem too late.

subjects.name: Graphical display calculator technique
subjects.description: Numerical solving, graph intersections, regression with its coefficient, normal and inverse normal, binomial probabilities, numerical derivatives and definite integrals. Finite, drillable and best done on the model the school has standardised rather than one from a video.

subjects.name: Proof and reasoning
subjects.description: Direct proof, contradiction, induction and counterexample, each marked on structure rather than on the conclusion reached. Three or four sessions on proof writing typically pay for themselves, and they belong in the first year rather than the second.

sections.heading: Where Diploma mathematics goes, term by term
paragraphs: Mathematics in the Diploma has a shape, and almost every student who feels behind is behind against that shape rather than against their own ability. The table below sets out the approximate sequence across the two years. Departments vary in the order they teach the five topic areas, so take the structure and write your school's actual sequence into it.

The pattern worth noticing is that the first year is where the course is winnable and the second year is where it is merely survivable. In the first year the deadline load is light, the content is the core of the course, and there is room to install the two disciplines the papers assume: non-calculator arithmetic for Analysis students and calculator menu fluency for Applications students. Neither can be retrofitted quickly.

The second year compresses the hardest content into the same months as the exploration's final deadlines, the mock cycle and, for Higher Level students, the first real encounter with Paper 3. A student who arrives in the second year with manipulation still slow is being asked to learn calculus while repairing algebra, which is why the first-year gap is the one that matters.

Use the table as an audit. If a topic area has had no attention in six weeks and appears on both papers, that is the gap to close first. And if the exploration topic is still undecided after the first summer, that is the single most urgent item regardless of what any grade currently says.

sections.heading: The exploration is a dated chain, not a single task
paragraphs: The exploration is twenty per cent of the mathematics grade, marked out of twenty across five criteria, with twelve to twenty pages recommended. Students treat it as one task to be done at some point. It is a chain of dependent steps with school-set deadlines, and the first step decides most of the mark, which is why a late start is almost impossible to rescue.

Four of the five criteria are effectively determined by how narrow the topic is. A question too broad produces thin mathematics, disorganised presentation, shallow reflection and a struggle with communication, all at once. Narrowing is therefore the highest-value work available, and it is the work students resist hardest, because a narrow question feels less impressive than a grand one.

The two criteria students neglect, personal engagement and reflection, carry six of the twenty marks between them and are written rather than calculated. They are earned by writing about the choices made, the approaches tried and abandoned, and what the result actually means and does not mean. Students treat that as padding around the mathematics, and it is nearly a third of the Internal Assessment mark.

The boundary matters here. A tutor may question the topic, challenge the mathematics chosen, explain each criterion and say why a section is weak. No tutor at IB Gram will write the exploration, draft it or edit it to completion. The school supervisor signs the work off and should know outside support exists; a tutor suggesting concealment is creating a risk that falls on your child.

sections.heading: Paper 3 needs months, not weeks
paragraphs: Paper 3 exists only at Higher Level, in both mathematics courses. It runs for sixty minutes, carries fifty-five marks across two extended problem-solving questions, and is worth twenty per cent of the grade. Nothing in the Standard Level course prepares anybody for its shape, and nothing in Papers 1 and 2 prepares a student for it either, which is why doing more Paper 2 questions is the commonest misallocation of Higher Level revision time.

The skills it rewards are specific and trainable, and they take repetitions rather than explanations. Read every part before starting, because part (a) frequently exists to generate a result part (d) needs. Carry results forward unrounded. Show reasoning, since marks sit on visible steps. Write a sentence in words when a part asks for interpretation. None of that is difficult to understand and all of it takes practice to do under pressure.

The characteristic failure is abandonment, or rather the lack of it. A student stalls on part (b), spends twenty minutes there, and never reaches parts (c) to (f) where marks were available independently. Teaching a student to park a part, state an assumption and continue is worth more on this paper than any additional content, and it takes four or five timed attempts to establish as a reflex rather than an idea.

That is why Paper 3 belongs in the plan from the first year rather than the second spring. Four or five genuine timed attempts spread across months, each marked line by line against the scheme, produces a different candidate from one who has seen the format twice in April. It is the clearest case in the whole Diploma for starting a component early.

sections.heading: The mock cycle as a mathematics diagnostic
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi schools generally run Diploma mocks in the second-year winter, and most families read the result as a progress report. Read that way, a mock yields a grade. Read as a diagnostic, the same script tells you which of four things is wrong, and the four have different remedies and different timescales. The difference between those readings is worth more than a term of general revision.

Go through it mark by mark. Every lost mark falls into content not known, question wording misread, reasoning not shown, or time ran out. Count the categories. In Diploma mathematics the reasoning category is usually larger than families expect, because marks are allocated to visible steps and a correct answer reached by an unjustified route collects a fraction of what it could, particularly in proof work and on Paper 3.

Timing is the category parents underestimate. A student who consistently leaves the final part of a long question unattempted is losing a grade boundary to pacing rather than to knowledge. Dividing marks by minutes to get a rate, writing that rate at the top of the paper, and practising the parking discipline are three cheap interventions that between them usually recover most of it.

For Corniche families mock season has a practical advantage. Schools across Abu Dhabi release students for parts of it, and because journeys from the waterfront inland are short, a daytime session becomes possible for the only time in the year. Three or four sessions in that fortnight, working from a fresh script, outperform twelve sessions in October working from a syllabus checklist.
bullets: Classify every lost mark: content, wording, reasoning, timing

sections.heading: The level-change window is a dated decision
paragraphs: Moving between Higher and Standard Level in mathematics is possible, and the window is set by your school rather than published. Most schools allow it early in the first year and progressively less easily afterwards, and the practical cut-off is usually long before a parent thinks to ask. That makes it a dated decision that quietly expires.

The content difference is what makes a late move hard. Prescribed teaching time rises from 150 hours at Standard Level to 240 at Higher Level, and that ninety-hour gap is additional content rather than deeper revision. A student moving up late has topics that were never taught, not topics taught and forgotten: proof and deeper calculus in Analysis, matrices and graph theory in Applications, plus an entirely new paper format.

The reverse move, from Higher to Standard, is easier and is sometimes exactly the right answer. A student carrying three Higher Levels and sleeping six hours is not short of teaching, and a well-timed move to Standard Level mathematics can rescue the whole Diploma rather than just one subject. That conversation belongs with the school, and it belongs in the first year.

The test to apply before the ability question is the purpose question. Higher Level mathematics is required or strongly expected for some degree routes and irrelevant to others, and requirements differ by institution and change between cycles. Read the stated entry requirement on each university's own admissions page. If Higher Level is not needed, the ability question does not need answering at all.

sections.heading: A ten-week conversion build for Papers 1 and 2
paragraphs: Ten weeks is the window most families arrive with, usually just after the second-year mocks. It is enough for a real change if it is spent on conversion rather than coverage. The decision that makes it work is to stop trying to learn the parts of the course never understood and to secure marks on the parts that were, which feels wrong and reliably raises the mark.

The build runs in four phases. The first two weeks establish a baseline with timed sections and produce the error list. Weeks three to five attack the two or three highest-frequency errors on it, which in Diploma mathematics are usually unshown reasoning, sign errors in multi-step rearrangement and angle mode rather than whole topics. Weeks six to eight rehearse full papers under timing. The last two reduce to pacing and short daily recall.

For Higher Level students, Paper 3 runs alongside rather than inside that structure, at roughly one timed attempt a fortnight across the whole ten weeks. It cannot be compressed into the final fortnight, because the parking discipline it requires is built by repetition and a student who meets it twice has not built anything.

Two things should be dropped deliberately. Topics that appear rarely and are not understood should be abandoned rather than learned badly, because the hours they consume are worth more on high-frequency marks. And re-reading notes should stop entirely at this stage, since it produces a strong feeling of progress with almost no measurable return. The honest limit is that ten focused weeks can move a boundary and will not move three.

sections.heading: Corniche timing, Ramadan and the weeks that are not there
paragraphs: A plan built on calendar weeks rather than teaching weeks will break. Most Abu Dhabi private schools run three terms with a winter break around the turn of the year and a spring break towards the end of March, and that spring break falls squarely in the weeks when a ten-week mathematics build should be at its most intense.

Ramadan moves roughly eleven days earlier each year and currently falls in the spring, increasingly overlapping the run-up to the May session. Schools shorten the day, which frees the afternoon, but the freed afternoon is a weak window for mathematics in particular, because arithmetic accuracy degrades sharply when a household is fasting and preparing. A post-Iftar slot, commonly 20:30 to 22:00, works considerably better.

On the Corniche the logistics argument for online delivery is strongest for mathematics, because mathematics wants two shorter sessions a week rather than one long one. Two visits a week means two rounds of visitor parking, reception and lift waits, and a tutor arriving ten minutes late twice a week is a meaningful share of what you are paying for. The hour starting on the hour matters more when there are two of them.

Count the real weeks before agreeing anything. Take the session month, subtract the spring break, subtract study leave, subtract Ramadan if your household reduces sessions then, and subtract travel you already know about. Most Corniche families find the usable figure four to six weeks below their first estimate, and a ten-week plan that is actually a six-week plan fails in a predictable way.

sections.heading: What each phase costs, and what we will not claim
paragraphs: Mathematics support costs more per grade point in the second-year spring than in the first-year autumn, which is market behaviour rather than a judgement. Demand concentrates before the session, the formats families want then are intensive, and specialists able to work on Paper 3 are among the scarcest people in this market. Buying earlier is cheaper for the same result.

Read the Corniche market from the top down, because the top is where Paper 3 help actually gets bought. The highest published Abu Dhabi quote is AED 650 at BartyED for a premium named tutor. Below that, specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above. A qualified subject tutor working online occupies roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200 and TutorChase quoting around AED 270 on their own pages. The floor is a university student teaching online, advertised from around AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik. The spread matters more than any single number in it: one hour at the ceiling buys between ten and twenty hours at the floor, and for a student who needs drilling rather than diagnosis, that trade is not obviously the right way round.

In-home visits in Abu Dhabi are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel priced in. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. For mathematics the allocation that works is frequency at the middle band through the first year rather than scarcity at the top in the second, because the disciplines the papers assume are built by repetition.

What we will not claim: no provider can guarantee a grade, a score or an improvement, including us. No regulator or examination board accredits IB Gram, we hold no ADEK, MoHRE or board approval, and there is no Abu Dhabi office. No tutor here writes an exploration, drafts it or edits it to completion. Every dirham figure on this page carries its source and the month it was read.
