process.title: Say which course, level and date
process.description: Analysis or Applications, Higher or Standard, and the date that is worrying you: an exploration deadline, a mock fortnight, the session month. Those three facts let us match from the component backwards and tell you what the remaining weeks can realistically reach.

process.title: Ask the school for the exploration deadlines
process.description: The internal draft dates are school-set and usually issued in writing. Most students never pass them on. Those dates plus the mock cycle are the whole planning input, and without them any schedule is guesswork dressed as a plan.

process.title: Send a marked mathematics paper
process.description: We classify every lost mark as content, question wording, reasoning not shown, or timing. In Diploma mathematics the reasoning category is usually larger than families expect, because marks sit on visible steps. The tally decides the plan and routinely contradicts the student's own guess.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One per family, before any payment and with no card details taken. Ask whether a calculator is permitted on Paper 1 in your child's course and what Paper 3 is worth. Those are published facts, and a specialist answers immediately without checking.

process.title: Set frequency, then review at the halfway point
process.description: Two shorter sessions a week usually beat one long one in mathematics, because accuracy consolidates between contacts. At the halfway mark, run a fresh timed section and compare the error list. If the recurring errors have not stopped, we change the tutor or the approach rather than adding hours.

whyPoints.title: Built backwards from dated components
whyPoints.description: Plans start from the exploration deadline, the mock cycle or the session month and work back in weeks. That is the difference between a schedule a Diploma student can hold in their head and a term of intentions that runs out of road in March.

whyPoints.title: Paper 3 treated as a months-long build
whyPoints.description: Sixty minutes, fifty-five marks, twenty per cent, and a parking discipline that takes four or five timed attempts to establish. We spread those attempts across months rather than compressing them into April, which is the commonest Higher Level planning error.

whyPoints.title: The exploration narrowed before it is written
whyPoints.description: Four of the five criteria are decided by how narrow the topic is, which makes narrowing the highest-value work on the component. We do it early, and we work explicitly on engagement and reflection, which carry six of the twenty marks.

whyPoints.title: The level-change window raised early
whyPoints.description: Moving between Higher and Standard is school-set and expires sooner than parents expect. We raise it in the first year, including the case for moving down, which sometimes rescues a whole Diploma rather than one subject.

whyPoints.title: No IB dates we cannot verify
whyPoints.description: ibo.org blocks automated checking, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. We name the May session and point you at your Diploma coordinator, who holds the authoritative dates for your cohort.

whyPoints.title: No guarantees and no claimed approvals
whyPoints.description: Ten focused weeks can move a boundary and will not move three. No provider can guarantee a grade including us, no regulator accredits IB Gram, there is no Abu Dhabi office, and every figure here carries its source and date.

faqs.question: When should an IB maths tutor in the Corniche start in the two-year course?
faqs.answer: The first year, and for a specific reason. That year carries a light deadline load, the core content and the two disciplines the papers assume: non-calculator arithmetic for Analysis students and calculator menu fluency for Applications students. Neither can be retrofitted quickly. A student arriving in the second year with manipulation still slow is learning calculus while repairing algebra, which is the position most families pay most to escape and could have avoided.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a maths tutor to a Corniche apartment?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Mathematics lessons here are one to one over live video with a shared whiteboard, which suits the subject because every line of working stays visible and is saved. The logistics point is sharper for mathematics than for other subjects: it wants two sessions a week, which doubles the parking and lift cost of any visiting arrangement.

faqs.question: Why can Paper 3 not be prepared in the final few weeks?
faqs.answer: Because its main requirement is a reflex rather than knowledge. Paper 3 runs sixty minutes for fifty-five marks across two extended problem-solving questions worth twenty per cent of the Higher Level grade, and the characteristic failure is spending twenty minutes stuck on one part and never reaching parts where marks were available independently. Learning to park a part, state an assumption and continue takes four or five timed attempts to become automatic. Two attempts in April builds nothing.

faqs.question: How much of the maths grade is the exploration, and when is it decided?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent, marked out of twenty across presentation four, communication four, personal engagement three, reflection three and use of mathematics six, with twelve to twenty pages recommended. Most of the mark is decided at the topic-narrowing stage, usually late in the first year, because a question too broad produces thin mathematics, weak structure and shallow reflection at the same time. A late start on this component is close to unrescuable.

faqs.question: Which exploration criteria do Corniche students lose most on?
faqs.answer: Personal engagement and reflection, which together carry six of the twenty marks and are written rather than calculated. They are earned by writing about the choices made, the approaches tried and abandoned, and what the result does and does not show. Students treat that as padding around the mathematics and lose nearly a third of the Internal Assessment mark to it. The fix is to keep notes on decisions as the work goes rather than reconstructing them at the end.

faqs.question: Can my son still move from Higher to Standard Level maths?
faqs.answer: Possibly, and the window is school-set rather than published, so ask now. Most schools allow it early in the first year and progressively less easily afterwards. Moving down is considerably easier than moving up and is sometimes exactly the right answer: a student carrying three Higher Levels on six hours of sleep is not short of teaching, and a well-timed move can rescue the whole Diploma rather than one subject. That conversation belongs with the school.

faqs.question: What makes moving up to Higher Level late so difficult?
faqs.answer: Untaught content rather than unrevised content. Prescribed teaching time rises from 150 hours at Standard Level to 240 at Higher Level, and that ninety-hour gap is additional material: proof and deeper calculus in Analysis, matrices and graph theory in Applications. On top of that sits Paper 3, an entirely new format worth a fifth of the grade. A student moving up in the second year is being asked to learn a third more course while revising the rest of it.

faqs.question: Is a calculator allowed on Paper 1 in my child's maths course?
faqs.answer: It depends which course. Analysis and Approaches forbids a calculator on Paper 1 at both Standard and Higher Level. Applications and Interpretation permits one on every paper. This single difference catches out more students than any content gap, because two years of permanent calculator access produces arithmetic that is competent only with support. If your child takes Analysis, deliberate non-calculator practice should be running from the first term rather than discovered as a weakness in the spring.

faqs.question: How do we read a Diploma maths mock script properly?
faqs.answer: Go through it mark by mark and sort every lost mark into four boxes: content not known, question wording misread, reasoning not shown, or ran out of time. In Diploma mathematics the reasoning box is usually larger than families expect, because marks sit on visible steps and a right answer reached by an unjustified route collects a fraction of what it could. The tally decides the plan and almost always contradicts what the student assumed had gone wrong.

faqs.question: Why do you recommend two shorter maths sessions a week?
faqs.answer: Because the errors that decide mathematics grades are procedural, and procedural accuracy consolidates in the gap between contacts rather than within a session. Two forty-five or sixty-minute contacts halve that gap and double the number of times a recurring sign error or chain-rule slip is caught and named. The exception is a student whose difficulty is genuinely conceptual, where one longer session gives room to build an idea properly.

faqs.question: Can ten weeks make a real difference to a Diploma maths grade?
faqs.answer: Ten focused weeks can move a grade boundary, and will not move three. The build that works runs in four phases: two weeks establishing a baseline and writing the error list, three attacking the highest-frequency errors, three rehearsing full papers under timing, and two on pacing and short daily recall. For Higher Level students a timed Paper 3 attempt runs alongside every fortnight. No provider can guarantee a grade, and anybody offering one is selling rather than teaching.

faqs.question: What should be dropped from a short maths revision plan?
faqs.answer: Two things, and both feel wrong. Topics that appear rarely and are not understood should be abandoned deliberately rather than learned badly, because the hours they consume are worth more on high-frequency marks. And re-reading notes should stop entirely at this stage, since it produces a strong sense of progress with almost no measurable return. Students who make both decisions explicitly score higher than students who try to cover everything thinly.

faqs.question: Does Ramadan affect maths tutoring differently from other subjects?
faqs.answer: Slightly, and in a way worth planning for. Arithmetic accuracy degrades more sharply than discursive work when a student is tired, so the freed afternoon that shortened Ramadan school days create is a poor window for mathematics specifically. A post-Iftar slot, commonly between 20:30 and 22:00, works considerably better and is easy to staff on video. Families who prefer to pause for the month can do that; the point is to decide in advance rather than lose the weeks.

faqs.question: Why does this page not give the IB maths exam dates?
faqs.answer: Because none has been verified for this project. ibo.org returns an error to automated checking, so no IB session date, results date or deadline here has been confirmed from the IB itself, and secondary sources disagree. A wrong examination date on a tutoring page is a family planning around guesswork. UAE schools sit the May session, and your school's Diploma coordinator holds the authoritative dates and the internal exploration deadlines for your child's cohort.

faqs.question: Do Corniche families struggle to book an HL maths slot in the spring?
faqs.answer: We tell you rather than substituting a generalist. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level in a fixed early-evening slot is among the tightest combinations in this market, and Corniche households compete with Al Reem, Al Bateen and Saadiyat families for the same window. Standard Level requests usually match within days. Being told early leaves you time to look elsewhere, which beats finding out in session three that the tutor is reading a Paper 3 question for the first time alongside your child.

intro.heading: Two addresses, one answer: the comparison parents actually make
paragraphs: Families on the mangrove channel compare before they commit, and the comparison usually runs along two axes at once. The first is geographic: is there somebody good on this side of the water, or do we look at Al Reem Island, Al Bateen, Saadiyat or the Khalifa City corridor? The second is academic: which Diploma maths course is my child actually on, and does that change who we need? The honest finding is that the second question matters and the first one barely does.

Here is why. Diploma mathematics is not one subject. It is two courses — Analysis and Approaches, and Applications and Interpretation — each offered at Standard and Higher Level, which makes four distinct syllabuses with different papers, different calculator rules and different university consequences. The pool of teachers who genuinely specialise in AA Higher Level Paper 3 is small in any single city, and it is not distributed by neighbourhood. Searching within a few kilometres of the promenade narrows that pool to almost nothing, while narrowing by course and level widens it enormously.

This is the reason IB Gram teaches UAE families online, one-to-one, over live video, rather than visiting homes. Home visiting is a service we run only in India. For a Diploma maths student the trade is a good one: screen sharing is a better medium for working through a Paper 2 question than a notebook on a kitchen table, because both people see the same working, graphs can be plotted live, and the whole session is reviewable afterwards. Nothing about graph sketching or calculus notation improves by having the tutor physically present.

The neighbourhood comparison is still worth making, because it changes one real variable: what time a session can start. A child at a school a few minutes along the inner island roads is home and settled far earlier than one crossing the Sheikh Zayed Bridge from Saadiyat or coming up the highway from Al Raha. For families with two children at different schools, the arrival times can be ninety minutes apart. That is a scheduling problem, not a tutoring problem, and online delivery is what makes two slots on one evening possible at all.

The rest of this page is the mathematics. What each paper is worth at each level. Where the twenty Exploration marks actually sit and what a tutor may and may not touch. The topics Abu Dhabi Diploma students lose marks in most reliably. What the Abu Dhabi market charges for specialist maths help, with the figures attributed. And a direct comparison of this pocket of the island against the neighbourhoods either side of it, so the geographic question gets a real answer rather than a reassuring one.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-eastern-mang.programmesIntro: Mathematics runs through the whole IB continuum, and the handover points are where families on this part of the island most often ask for help. Each stage below describes what the maths looks like and what a tutor is actually doing there.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Criterion-referenced rather than examined by a board, with four criteria covering knowledge, pattern investigation, communication and real-life application. Students can hold a strong MYP profile while carrying algebraic gaps, because investigation criteria reward process and reasoning. The fix in MYP 4 and 5 is fluency work: manipulation, indices, surds and functions practised until they are automatic.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi has several IB continuum schools, so a child here may do MYP and then Diploma on the same campus, or move from an MYP school on one island to a Diploma cohort on another. The second case is the harder one, because the receiving school's DP1 teaching assumes a baseline the MYP course never examined directly.

programmes.name: Diploma Year 1 mathematics
programmes.description: The year the course is chosen and most of the content delivered. AA or AI, Higher or Standard, is settled early and is awkward to change later. DP1 is also when the Exploration topic is usually proposed, which makes the spring of DP1 the cheapest moment in the whole Diploma to buy mathematics support: the content is still being taught and the Exploration has not yet become a deadline.
programmes.countryNote: Island families regularly discover in DP1 that the school's maths option block forces a choice they did not expect — AI Higher Level where AA Standard was wanted, or the reverse. Where the timetable is fixed, a tutor's job is to make the available route work for the degree the student is aiming at rather than to relitigate the choice.

programmes.name: Diploma Year 2 mathematics
programmes.description: Finishing the syllabus, submitting the Exploration and preparing for the May session papers. Three things compete for the same weeks: new content, the Exploration deadline and past-paper practice. Students who sequence them badly lose marks on all three. A tutor in DP2 is mostly a prioritisation engine, deciding what gets attention in which week and what is deliberately left alone.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi Diploma students sit the May session, with internal school deadlines for the Exploration and for the other Diploma core components typically clustered in the same term. IB Gram does not publish IB examination or results dates, because the board's own site cannot be verified by automated checks; ask your school's Diploma coordinator for the current dates.

programmes.name: University mathematics prerequisites
programmes.description: The point at which the AA or AI decision becomes visible. Engineering, physics, mathematics and many economics degrees typically specify Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level; other courses accept either route. The grade matters, but so does the course name on the transcript, and no amount of tutoring in DP2 changes a course chosen in DP1.
programmes.countryNote: For families staying in the UAE, the Diploma also feeds a Ministry of Education equivalency file. The Ministry's published British-track thresholds are sourced; no IB points figure in this project has been verified against the Ministry's own site, so we describe the process and point you to the official channel rather than publishing a number.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-eastern-mang.subjectsIntro: Requests for maths help from this pocket of the island arrive as a course name and a symptom. The list below separates the four Diploma routes and the components that generate the most questions, with the loss point named in each case.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL
subjects.description: The most demanding Diploma maths route. Three papers plus the Exploration, with Paper 1 sat without a calculator and Paper 3 presenting two extended problem-solving questions. Marks go on proof, calculus technique and the ability to keep going through a long multi-part question when the first part has not resolved cleanly.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches SL
subjects.description: Two papers and the Exploration, with Paper 1 non-calculator. The common profile is a student fluent in routine technique who stalls when a question combines two topics. Differentiation applied to a trigonometric or logarithmic function is the classic case, and it is a fluency problem rather than a comprehension one.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation HL
subjects.description: Calculator-permitted throughout, with heavier statistics, modelling and matrix content. The Higher Level Paper 3 rewards sustained modelling across a long context. Students lose marks by giving a numerical answer without interpreting it in context, which is precisely what the mark scheme asks for.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation SL
subjects.description: Often chosen as the lighter route and then underestimated. Statistics, financial mathematics and modelling carry the paper, and the technology demands are real: a student who cannot drive the graphing calculator efficiently loses marks to time rather than to understanding.

subjects.name: The Mathematical Exploration
subjects.description: Twenty per cent of the grade, marked out of 20 across five criteria. The two criteria students neglect are personal engagement and reflection, which together carry six marks and need evidence in the writing rather than good intentions. A tutor teaches the criteria and questions the reasoning; the student writes every word.

subjects.name: Paper 3 at Higher Level
subjects.description: A separate skill from Papers 1 and 2 and worth twenty per cent. Two extended questions that build, so an early error propagates. Practising it requires whole papers under timed conditions, not isolated questions, which is why it is usually the component most neglected until a mock exposes it.

subjects.name: The graphing calculator
subjects.description: A syllabus requirement rather than a convenience. Students who learned maths on a phone calculator arrive unable to find an intersection, a numerical derivative or a regression line efficiently. Two sessions of pure technology practice often recover more marks than two sessions of content.

subjects.name: IGCSE and MYP to Diploma bridging
subjects.description: A short, finite block over the summer before DP1 covering algebraic manipulation, functions, indices and the habit of writing full solutions. The students who need it most are usually the ones with strong prior grades from a course that rewarded process over fluency.

subjects.name: Physics and Economics mathematics
subjects.description: Diploma physics and economics both fail students on the mathematics rather than the subject: rearrangement, logarithms, gradients and interpretation of a calculated figure. Where that is the real problem, a maths tutor is the cheaper fix than a second subject tutor.

subjects.name: A Level and Further Maths transition
subjects.description: Relevant to island families who move between Diploma and British sixth-form routes mid-stream. The content overlap is substantial but the assessment style is not, and the adjustment is mostly in how much working a solution is expected to show.

sections.heading: What a search for an IB maths tutor in Eastern Mangroves is really asking
paragraphs: An IB maths tutor in Eastern Mangroves means a Diploma mathematics specialist teaching one-to-one. IB Gram supplies that to families on this part of Abu Dhabi island over live video. We do not visit homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is an India-only service for us. What the parent is usually trying to establish with a neighbourhood search is whether anybody competent is reachable, and the answer is better than the search implies, because reachability stopped being a function of distance once the lessons moved to video.

The question underneath it is more interesting. Diploma mathematics splits into four separate syllabuses, and the most common cause of wasted tutoring money in this subject is a tutor who knows mathematics but not the specific course. An AA Higher Level student needs somebody fluent in non-calculator Paper 1 technique and in Paper 3's extended problems. An AI Standard Level student needs somebody who can drive a graphing calculator at speed and who marks interpretation rather than arithmetic. A capable graduate tutor can fail both of them while being perfectly good at mathematics.

So the comparison that matters is not promenade against Al Reem, or island against mainland. It is specialist against generalist, and course-matched against subject-matched. A family here choosing from the whole pool of AA Higher Level teachers has a materially better chance of getting the right person than one choosing from the handful who happen to live within a short drive. That is the entire argument for online delivery in this subject, and it does not require anyone to pretend the in-home option has no appeal.
The one thing a neighbourhood comparison does settle is timing, and that is worth doing properly rather than waving away. The next section does it.

sections.heading: Eastern Mangroves against Al Reem Island: same answer, different reasons
paragraphs: Two families, two kilometres apart with water in between, ask the same question and need the same tutor for different reasons. The Eastern Mangroves family is close to the island school belt, so their constraint is a crowded 4pm to 6pm window shared with sport and siblings. The Al Reem family's constraint is a bridge: a crossing that takes ten minutes at eleven in the morning and thirty at four in the afternoon, which pushes their realistic session start later rather than making it impossible.

Neither constraint is solved by hiring somebody nearby. A tutor with a car in either neighbourhood still arrives inside the same traffic, and the arrival overhead lands on the family's hour rather than the tutor's. What does solve it is a fixed video slot chosen after the actual arrival time is known, which is a conversation that takes two minutes and which almost nobody has before buying tutoring.

The comparison below sets out the five neighbourhoods a promenade family realistically considers, with the practical variable in each. Note the last column: the subject-availability problem is identical everywhere, because Higher Level specialists in scarce subjects are scarce across the whole emirate, not scarce in particular postcodes. That is the sense in which the answer is the same either way.

There is one genuine local difference worth naming. Families on the island tend to have shorter commutes and therefore more scheduling choice, which means they can run two subjects on separate evenings. Families on the long highway runs usually have one usable weekday slot and should put their hardest subject in it, with the second subject at the weekend.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation
paragraphs: This is the decision that outlasts every tutor a family hires. The two courses share a core but diverge in emphasis: Analysis and Approaches leans on algebra, calculus and proof, with Paper 1 sat without a calculator; Applications and Interpretation leans on modelling, statistics and technology, with calculators permitted throughout. Both are offered at Standard and Higher Level, and both are respected qualifications. They are not interchangeable as university prerequisites.

The practical rule is to work backwards from the degree. Engineering, physics, mathematics and many quantitative economics courses commonly specify Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and a student who arrives with Applications at Higher Level can find a door closed that no grade reopens. Courses outside that group frequently accept either. Where a student is undecided at the point of choosing, the conservative route is the one that keeps more doors open, provided the workload is realistic.

The second input is the student rather than the destination. A student who enjoys structure, symbolic manipulation and proof will do better in Analysis and Approaches even at the cost of harder papers. A student who thinks in contexts and data, and who reaches for a graph before an equation, often scores higher in Applications and Interpretation and is happier doing it. A higher grade in the right course beats a lower grade in the prestigious one in almost every admissions scenario.

The third input is the school's option block, which overrides both of the above. If the timetable offers one route, the useful work is making that route serve the intended degree, which sometimes means adding a self-studied component or planning a different university route rather than fighting the timetable.

sections.heading: What each maths paper is worth, and why that changes the plan
paragraphs: Diploma mathematics is assessed on externally marked papers plus one piece of internally assessed work. The weightings are published and they are not evenly distributed, which means revision time should not be either. A student who spends every session on Paper 2 style questions while Paper 3 sits untouched is leaving a fifth of the grade to chance.

At Standard Level there are two papers, each carrying forty per cent, with the Exploration making up the remaining twenty. At Higher Level there are three papers at thirty, thirty and twenty per cent, with the Exploration again at twenty. The Higher Level Paper 3 is the component families most often discover late, usually when a mock paper produces a mark far below the student's usual standard. It is not harder content; it is a different task, built from extended questions where part one feeds part four.

The planning consequence is straightforward. Count the weeks available, allocate them by weighting rather than by comfort, and treat the Exploration as a scheduled project with its own deadline rather than as something that happens alongside. Students who protect two or three weeks for Exploration work in DP1 are not the ones asking for emergency help in DP2.

One further note on the Exploration: it is marked out of twenty, and the mark is converted according to the grade boundaries for the session. A strong Exploration cannot rescue weak papers, but a neglected one reliably costs a grade, which is a poor trade for a component the student controls completely.

sections.heading: The twenty Exploration marks, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: The Exploration is the part of Diploma mathematics most exposed to bad advice, so it is worth setting out exactly how the marks are distributed. There are five criteria. Presentation carries four marks, mathematical communication four, personal engagement three, reflection three, and use of mathematics six. Twenty in total, and twenty per cent of the final grade.

Students lose marks in predictable places. Personal engagement and reflection together carry six marks and are the two criteria most often treated as decoration: an introduction saying the topic is interesting, and a conclusion saying it was. Both criteria want evidence inside the work — a choice explained, an unexpected result examined, a method rejected and the reason given. Mathematical communication is lost to unlabelled graphs, undefined variables and notation that drifts. Use of mathematics is lost when the topic was never capable of carrying enough depth, which is a decision made weeks before any writing started.

The boundary around this work is firm, and worth stating plainly because this market contains providers who cross it. A tutor may teach the criteria, explain what the command words in them mean, interrogate a student's reasoning and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor does not write the Exploration, does not rewrite the student's sentences, and does not supply a topic with the mathematics pre-packaged. Crossing that line is academic malpractice and the consequence lands on the student.

The most useful intervention is also the earliest one: testing a proposed topic for mathematical depth before the student invests a month in it. A topic that cannot reach the level of the course caps the use-of-mathematics criterion no matter how well the writing goes, and that is six of the twenty marks decided before a word is typed.

sections.heading: Where Abu Dhabi Diploma students lose maths marks
paragraphs: Marked papers from Diploma students in this emirate show the same handful of patterns repeatedly, and almost none of them are about not understanding the mathematics. The largest single loss is unclaimed method marks: a student who can do the question writes three lines where the scheme rewards six, gets the final answer wrong because of one slip, and scores zero on a question they understood.

The second is calculator fluency, which is a bigger problem than its reputation suggests. Students who learned mathematics on a phone arrive at the Diploma without the habits the course assumes — finding intersections, numerical derivatives, definite integrals, regression lines and statistical distributions quickly and accurately. In Applications and Interpretation this is not a convenience, it is most of Paper 2. Two sessions on technology alone often return more marks than two sessions on content.

The third is the question that joins two topics. Differentiating a composite function involving a logarithm, or combining a sequence with a financial model, defeats students who are individually fluent in each component. This is a practice problem with a specific remedy: a diet of deliberately combined questions rather than the single-topic exercises textbooks are full of.

The fourth is Paper 3 at Higher Level, which students neglect because it feels unpractisable. It is practisable, but only in whole papers under timed conditions, with explicit coaching on what to do when part one has not resolved. Students who have never rehearsed carrying an unresolved result forward lose the entire back half of a paper to a single early error.
bullets: Write the method lines even when the final answer is wrong

sections.heading: What Diploma maths support costs around the island, and what travel buys
paragraphs: Published rates in this market, as at October 2026, give a usable picture. Qualified online subject tutors advertise from around AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level tutors are quoted from AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase listing around AED 270 and premium named or examiner-led tutors advertised as high as AED 650. In-home one-to-one visits, travel included, run from about AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table placing the common band at AED 180 to 350.

Set against those numbers, the travel premium is the interesting part of the comparison. The gap between a qualified online rate and an in-home rate is real money, and for that money a family gets a person in the room and loses the ability to choose from outside driving distance. For a general homework-support need that can be a fair trade. For AA Higher Level Paper 3, it is a poor one, because the pool of people who teach that component well is small and is not concentrated near any particular neighbourhood.

Monthly budgeting is the frame most families here actually use. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run from AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist examination-year support. Advertised packages in this market have included AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits.

IB Gram does not publish a tariff on these pages. The rate depends on level, subject scarcity and session length, and it is quoted after a free trial lesson so that both sides know what is being bought. Every figure above belongs to the provider or source named next to it.

sections.heading: Honest limits: what this page will not tell you
paragraphs: There are three things this page deliberately does not do, and each of them is something a competing page in this search result does. The first is publishing IB examination and results dates. The IB's own site cannot be verified by automated checking, and a wrong examination date is the single most damaging error a tutoring page can make, because a parent acts on it. Your school's Diploma coordinator holds the current dates; use those.

The second is claiming approval we do not hold. IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the International Baccalaureate or any examination board, and does not describe any school as a partner or client. Several pages competing for this query do one or both. A KHDA educational services permit is a specific instrument issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai, and implying one without holding it is a misrepresentation rather than marketing.

The third is promising outcomes. No tutor can guarantee a 7, a points total or a university place, and any page offering one is selling something it cannot deliver. What can be promised is specific and smaller: a specialist in the right course, a diagnosis from marked work, a plan with an end date, and an honest recommendation to stop when stopping is right.

The fourth, which belongs with the others, is pricing honesty. Every dirham figure on this page is attributed to the provider or rate survey that published it, with the date stated. Three of the six strongest pages for this cluster of searches publish no price at all, and two quote United States dollars to families who transact in dirhams.

process.title: Tell us the course, not just the subject
process.description: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, Higher or Standard, and the year group. Add a recent marked paper or the Exploration draft if there is one. Those three items decide which specialist is right, and they take a minute to send.

process.title: Free trial lesson on a real question
process.description: The trial is a lesson, not a consultation. It usually runs on a past-paper question from your child's own course so you can see the diagnosis being made. If the match is not right, we rematch rather than asking you to persist with it.

process.title: A scoped plan with a finish line
process.description: You get the number of sessions, the components in order, and the date the block ends. Where the Exploration is involved, the plan states explicitly what the tutor will and will not do with the student's draft before anything is written.

process.title: Weekly teaching with marked work between
process.description: Sessions run over live video at a fixed Gulf Standard Time slot, with screen sharing for working and graphs. Homework is short, targeted at the named error type and marked at the start of the following session rather than assumed.

process.title: Midpoint review against a second paper
process.description: A second timed paper on the same course, marked the same way, compared with the first by topic. The review says continue, change or stop. Stopping is a legitimate recommendation and we make it when the evidence supports it.

whyPoints.title: Matched by course and level, not by subject
whyPoints.description: AA Higher Level and AI Standard Level are different jobs. Tutors here are matched to one of the four Diploma maths routes, which is the difference between a tutor who is good at mathematics and one who is good at your child's examination.

whyPoints.title: Paper 3 treated as its own component
whyPoints.description: A fifth of a Higher Level grade sits in a paper most students never rehearse whole. We scope it separately, practise it under timed conditions and coach the recovery skill that keeps one early slip from costing the back half of the paper.

whyPoints.title: A stated boundary on the Exploration
whyPoints.description: The criteria are taught, the reasoning is questioned, the draft gets feedback, and the student writes every word. We put that in writing before the work starts, because the risk of the alternative falls entirely on the child.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling that respects an island commute
whyPoints.description: Sessions are set after the actual arrival time is known, with separate slots on the same evening for siblings at different schools. No travel means the hour you book is the hour your child is taught.

whyPoints.title: Attributed figures, not round numbers
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page carries the name of the provider or survey that published it and the month it was read. That is a deliberately higher standard than this search result currently sets.

whyPoints.title: Availability stated before you commit
whyPoints.description: Where no specialist is free for a scarce course and hour, you hear it immediately, with the options spelled out — a different slot, a dated wait, or a tutor whose location is disclosed before the trial rather than afterwards.

faqs.question: Is an IB maths tutor on Abu Dhabi island better than one teaching from elsewhere?
faqs.answer: Not for this subject. What matters is whether the tutor teaches your child's exact course — Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, Higher or Standard — and the pool of specialists in any one of those four routes is small in any single city. Restricting the search to a few kilometres around the mangrove channel shrinks it further for no gain, since the teaching happens over video either way. Choose by course, level and the component you need help with, and treat location as irrelevant.

faqs.question: My child is at a school on Al Reem Island. Does the plan change?
faqs.answer: Only the timing. A bridge crossing at four in the afternoon regularly turns ten minutes into thirty, so Reem families usually settle on a later weekday slot than families living beside the promenade. The mathematics, the specialist and the plan are identical, because the tutor is chosen by course rather than by catchment. Work out the real arrival time on a normal weekday first, then fix a slot fifteen minutes after it, and the session stops being a weekly negotiation.

faqs.question: Which Diploma maths course should my child take for an engineering degree?
faqs.answer: Engineering, physics and mathematics degrees commonly specify Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, so that is the safer route where the student can carry it. Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level is a strong qualification but is not accepted as a direct equivalent by every faculty, and no grade later fixes a course chosen in DP1. Check the published entry requirements for two or three target universities before the option block closes, and ask the school's university adviser to confirm what the school has seen accepted.

faqs.question: How much of the Diploma maths grade is the Exploration worth?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent at both Standard and Higher Level, marked out of twenty across five criteria: presentation four marks, mathematical communication four, personal engagement three, reflection three, and use of mathematics six. It is the only part of the grade the student controls completely and the only part with no time pressure on the day. A neglected Exploration reliably costs a grade; a strong one cannot rescue weak papers. Treat it as a scheduled project in DP1 rather than something that happens alongside revision.

faqs.question: What exactly is Paper 3 and why did my child's mock mark collapse on it?
faqs.answer: Paper 3 is sat only at Higher Level and carries twenty per cent. It presents two extended questions where later parts depend on earlier ones, so a single unresolved step early on can take out the rest of the question. Students who have only practised isolated exercises meet it for the first time in a mock and lose the back half of the paper. The remedy is whole timed papers plus explicit coaching on carrying an unresolved result forward and on flagging an assumption rather than stopping.

faqs.question: Where is the line between coaching the Exploration and doing it for my child?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor can test whether a proposed topic carries enough mathematical depth, teach the five criteria and what their command words mean, question the student's reasoning, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor does not write any part of the Exploration, does not rewrite sentences and does not hand over a pre-packaged topic. We set that out before the first session, because the consequence of crossing it falls on the student rather than on the tutor.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a maths tutor to an address at Eastern Mangroves?
faqs.answer: No, and the page would be dishonest if it implied otherwise. IB Gram makes no home visits in the UAE; in-home tutoring is something we offer only in India. Diploma mathematics for families here is taught one-to-one over live video with a shared screen, which suits the subject well: both people see the same working, graphs are plotted live, and the session can be reviewed afterwards. The trade is a tutor matched to your child's exact course instead of one matched to your postcode.

faqs.question: How many maths sessions a week does a Diploma student usually start with?
faqs.answer: One, in most cases. A single well-used hour with short marked homework between sessions moves more than two hours that leave no time for independent practice. Two sessions a week make sense in narrow circumstances: a student rebuilding a topic from scratch, a DP2 student working on papers and the Exploration at once, or a short block before mocks. Starting at one and reviewing after four weeks is cheaper and gives you evidence before you increase the commitment.

faqs.question: My child is fluent in class but slow in examinations. What fixes that?
faqs.answer: Usually calculator technique and question selection rather than content. Students who cannot find an intersection, a numerical derivative or a regression line quickly lose minutes on every question, and the deficit compounds across a paper. The second cause is attempting questions in printed order instead of banking the accessible marks first. Both are trainable in two or three sessions and both show up immediately in a timed paper, which is why the first session is a timed paper rather than a discussion.

faqs.question: What does specialist Diploma maths support cost in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Using published market figures as at October 2026: qualified online subject tutors advertise from roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, specialist IB and IGCSE tutors from AED 200 to AED 450 and above, and premium examiner-led tutors as high as AED 650. In-home visits including travel run from about AED 180 to 500. Those are other providers' published rates, not ours. IB Gram quotes after a free trial lesson, because the right figure depends on level, scarcity and session length.

faqs.question: Why does this page not list the IB examination dates?
faqs.answer: Because we have not been able to verify them from the International Baccalaureate directly. The board's site blocks automated checking, and a wrong examination date is the one error on a tutoring page that a parent will actually act on. Secondary sources circulate dates that differ from each other, which is exactly the situation in which publishing looks helpful and is not. UAE Diploma students sit the May session; for the specific dates, ask your school's Diploma coordinator or check the board's own site.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start maths tutoring in the second year of the Diploma?
faqs.answer: No, but what it can achieve narrows as the weeks go. Early in DP2 there is still room to rebuild a topic and to do the Exploration properly. By the spring the useful work is paper technique, method-mark discipline, calculator speed and Paper 3 rehearsal, which can move a grade for a student who understands the content but underperforms on the day. What a late start cannot do is teach a syllabus that was never covered, and a plan pretending otherwise wastes the weeks that remain.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover Diploma maths and the maths inside physics or economics?
faqs.answer: Often, and it is frequently the efficient choice. Diploma physics and economics both lose students marks on rearrangement, logarithms, gradients and interpreting a calculated figure rather than on the subject itself. A maths specialist who understands those applications can fix the underlying skill once instead of twice. Where the problem is genuinely subject content — a physics topic, an economics diagram — a second specialist is the right answer, and we will say so rather than stretching one tutor across both.

faqs.question: What should we watch for during the free trial lesson?
faqs.answer: Three things. Does the tutor ask to see marked work before teaching anything, or do they launch straight into explaining? Do they name your child's course and paper structure without being prompted, or do they talk about mathematics generically? And at the end, can your child state what their specific weakness is in their own words? A pleasant lesson where the child felt supported is not the same as a useful one. The diagnosis is the product, and it should be visible within the hour.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-hudayriyat-i.tutorsIntro: Each tutor below is listed against the specific IB maths course they teach rather than against a generic maths label. That distinction is the whole point of this page: AA Higher Level and AI Higher Level ask different things, and the tutor who can take a student through Maclaurin series is not automatically the tutor for Voronoi diagrams.

intro.heading: The honest answer to "is there anyone near me who knows this syllabus?"
paragraphs: Probably not, if near means within a short drive of Hudayriyat Island, and the course is Higher Level. This is the answer most tutoring pages will not give, so it is worth setting out the reasoning rather than just the conclusion. There are four separate IB mathematics courses, and the one a student is sitting determines which teacher is useful to them. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, which is the course that most often triggers this search, is taught by a comparatively small number of teachers in Abu Dhabi, almost all of them employed full time at an IB World School.

Hudayriyat Island compounds that. The island is reached by bridge from Al Bateen, residential handovers here are recent, and the school-age population arrived after the housing. There is no settled local teaching community on the island to draw from. So the pool of people who both teach AA HL and live close enough to Hudayriyat to come twice a week is, realistically, extremely thin, and in some subject-and-time combinations it is empty. A family that keeps searching for a nearby specialist is searching for something the geography does not contain.

The second reason the local search fails is structural. ADEK's professional-ethics expectations for private and charter school staff restrict teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation private tuition work permit carries a comparable bar on serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. The IB maths teachers physically nearest your child are frequently the ones who cannot lawfully be hired. The nearby pool is smaller than it looks even before the drive is considered.

What follows from this is not a sales argument but an arithmetic one. If the specialist pool for a specific course is small and scattered across the emirate, then the only way to reach a genuine AA HL or AI HL teacher is to stop filtering by distance. One-to-one lessons over live video do exactly that. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere else in the UAE — home visits are an India-only service — and on this particular search that limitation turns out to be the point rather than a compromise.

A word on what to expect from the market while you compare. Published UAE rates for a qualified subject tutor working online sit roughly between AED 150 and 300 an hour, with specialist IB and A-Level rates quoted from AED 200 to 450 and upward, and one premium examiner-led provider at AED 650. In-home arrangements are quoted from AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the rate. Those are figures read from other providers' published pages in October 2026. The relevant observation for this page is that the premium attached to specialist IB maths is not a travel premium; it is a scarcity premium, and travelling further does not reduce it.

The rest of this page is written to let you test a tutor rather than trust one. It sets out the difference between AA and AI, the papers and their weightings at both levels, where Higher Level students reliably lose marks, what the exploration is assessed on criterion by criterion, and the questions that separate a genuine IB maths teacher from a competent general mathematician in about ten minutes of conversation.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-hudayriyat-i.programmesIntro: An IB maths tutor is only useful if they know which point of the continuum the student is at. The four Diploma maths courses sit on top of several years of earlier IB mathematics, and most Higher Level problems that surface in Year 12 were planted in the Middle Years Programme.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Every Diploma candidate takes one of four courses: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, each at Standard or Higher Level. Standard Level is examined through two papers plus the exploration; Higher Level adds a third, shorter paper of extended problem-solving. The five topic areas are common to all four courses — number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus — but the depth and the balance differ sharply.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi IB schools sit the May session, which is the northern-hemisphere series. A November session also exists and is used by some candidates and schools. No IB session or results date appears anywhere on this page: ibo.org blocks automated checking, so nothing could be verified, and a date a family plans around has to come from the school's IB coordinator or ibo.org directly.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme mathematics
programmes.description: The five-year programme that feeds the Diploma, assessed against four criteria rather than by external paper. MYP mathematics rewards investigation and communication alongside technique, which is a genuine strength and also the reason some students arrive in Year 12 with weaker algebraic fluency than an IGCSE cohort. Extended mathematics in MYP years 4 and 5 is the honest preparation for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level.
programmes.countryNote: For a Hudayriyat Island family, the MYP years are the cheapest place to intervene. A student whose algebraic manipulation is shaky at the end of MYP 5 will meet that gap again in the first term of AA HL, under far more time pressure and at specialist tutoring rates rather than general ones.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Inquiry-led primary mathematics organised around number, pattern and function, measurement, shape and space, and data handling. There is no external examination. The transferable habit the programme builds — explaining a method rather than producing an answer — maps directly onto the communication criterion in the Diploma exploration years later.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi has a reasonable spread of PYP provision across the island and the Khalifa City corridor, so families moving to Hudayriyat usually have continuity options. Tuition at this stage is best spent on number fluency rather than on acceleration, because acceleration without fluency is what produces the Year 12 problems described further down this page.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The fourth IB programme, combining Diploma courses with a career-related study and a core of personal and professional skills. Mathematics appears where a student takes a DP maths course as part of the combination, most often Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level, which suits the applied and data-handling emphasis of the programme.
programmes.countryNote: CP provision in the UAE is much narrower than DP provision, so a family considering it should confirm directly with the school rather than assuming availability. Where a CP student is taking AI SL, the tutoring need is usually the technology component and the statistics topics rather than algebra.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-hudayriyat-i.subjectsIntro: An IB maths tutor for a Hudayriyat Island student is usually working on one of the areas below. They are listed by where the marks go missing rather than by syllabus order, because that is how a diagnostic session actually proceeds.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebra-and-calculus route, built for students heading towards mathematics, physics, engineering or economics at university. Higher Level is the most demanding of the four courses. Marks are lost on unstructured algebraic manipulation, on proof technique, and on the non-calculator paper where fluency rather than understanding is the binding constraint.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The modelling-and-data route, with the graphic display calculator assumed throughout both papers. Less algebraically demanding than AA and more demanding in interpretation: students lose marks by producing a correct statistical output and then failing to say what it means in the context of the question.

subjects.name: AA Higher Level: proof and complex numbers
subjects.description: Proof by induction, contradiction and counterexample, plus complex numbers in Cartesian and polar form with De Moivre's theorem. This content appears nowhere in Standard Level and nowhere in MYP, so it is new in every respect. It is the single most common reason an able AA HL student's grade stalls in the first year.

subjects.name: AA Higher Level: calculus extensions
subjects.description: Implicit differentiation, related rates, L'Hôpital's rule, Maclaurin series, improper integrals and first-order differential equations through separation of variables and the integrating factor. Paper 3 draws heavily here. Students who can execute each technique in isolation still lose marks when a question requires them to choose between three of them.

subjects.name: AI Higher Level: matrices and graph theory
subjects.description: Matrix algebra, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, transition matrices, and graph theory including adjacency matrices, minimum spanning trees and the Chinese postman and travelling salesman problems. Entirely absent from AA, which is why an AA-trained tutor is of limited use to an AI HL student.

subjects.name: AI: statistics and hypothesis testing
subjects.description: Regression, correlation, the chi-squared test for independence and goodness of fit, and at Higher Level the t-test, Poisson and binomial distributions and confidence intervals. The marks sit in stating hypotheses precisely, reading the p-value against the significance level, and writing a conclusion in context rather than in statistics vocabulary.

subjects.name: Functions and transformations
subjects.description: Domain and range, composite and inverse functions, rational functions, and the transformation sequences that appear in every paper. A student who cannot sketch a transformed function without a calculator will lose marks across the whole paper, not just on the function question, because sketches are how the harder questions are set up.

subjects.name: Geometry, trigonometry and vectors
subjects.levels: HL and SL · vectors AA HL
subjects.description: Trigonometric identities and equations at both levels, with three-dimensional vectors, lines and planes added at AA Higher Level. Vector geometry is where spatial reasoning and algebra have to work together, and it is the topic students most often decide to skip in revision, which is a mistake because it recurs in Paper 3.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration (internal assessment)
subjects.description: A piece of independent mathematical writing worth 20% of the final grade, assessed on five criteria totalling 20 marks: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection, and use of mathematics. The mathematics is only six of those twenty marks, which surprises most students and explains most low scores.

subjects.name: Calculator technique and the non-calculator paper
subjects.description: AA papers include a paper without technology; AI assumes the graphic display calculator throughout. Both demand specific discipline — the AA student needs arithmetic and surd fluency, the AI student needs to know which calculator function produces which output and how to present it. Neither skill is taught explicitly in most classrooms.

subjects.name: Paper 3 extended problem-solving
subjects.description: A shorter paper of two extended questions that build in stages, worth 20% of the Higher Level grade. It rewards reading ahead, recognising the structure of the problem, and persisting through an early part that is not yet obviously going anywhere. Practice on individual topics does not prepare a student for it.

subjects.name: Transition work: MYP or IGCSE into DP maths
subjects.description: The two most common gaps are algebraic fluency coming out of MYP and function language coming out of IGCSE. Both are closeable in a few weeks before Year 12 begins and expensive to close in the middle of it. For Hudayriyat Island families moving school or country, this is the highest-return tutoring block available.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-hudayriyat-i.regionsIntro: IB maths teaching in Abu Dhabi is spread thinly across these districts rather than concentrated in any one of them. Online delivery means the same tutor list serves every address below, which is the practical answer to a scarce specialist pool.

regions.name: Al Bateen
regions.note: Immediately across the Hudayriyat bridge and the first district most island families enter. IB Diploma provision sits here, so a Hudayriyat student may well be studying AA or AI within a few minutes of the crossing while their tutor options remain city-wide.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Its own island, its own bridge, and its own IB cohort. A tutor serving both Saadiyat and Hudayriyat in one evening crosses most of Abu Dhabi island in between, which is why an in-home specialist on two islands is close to impossible to arrange.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Dense towers with a substantial international cohort and a short drive to the central island campuses. Reem families searching for AA HL help are drawing on the same small teaching pool as Hudayriyat families, during the same spring term.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: At the eastern end of the city with its own campuses. The distance between Yas and Hudayriyat is the clearest illustration on this page of why proximity is a poor filter for a Higher Level maths specialist.

regions.name: Al Raha Beach and Al Raha Gardens
regions.note: The corridor along the Abu Dhabi–Dubai road, with heavy international enrolment and late-afternoon congestion. Sessions here start late for traffic reasons, which for a maths lesson is a real cost: tired students make arithmetic errors, not conceptual ones.

regions.name: Khalifa City and Al Reef
regions.note: Villa communities with large IB intakes and a well-known school-run bottleneck. The evening window is narrow, and an online slot that can start the moment the student is settled is worth more than a longer session that starts an hour later.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City
regions.note: Mainland and further from the island campuses than most families expect. For an in-home arrangement this is the kind of distance that eliminates specialist availability altogether rather than merely raising the price.

regions.name: Al Mushrif and the Corniche
regions.note: Established central districts with older campuses and a broad curriculum mix. Many island families were enrolled here before moving, so the IB coordinator who sets their internal deadlines sits in a district they no longer live in.

schoolClusters.note: The IB provision Hudayriyat families reach across the bridge and along the island. Diploma mathematics is taught at a handful of these campuses, and the teaching staff who cover Higher Level at each one are usually a small number of individuals, which is the supply picture behind this whole page.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation — the question that decides who can help
paragraphs: AA and AI are not two difficulty levels of the same course. They are different syllabuses with different content, different calculator rules and different university consequences. A tutor fluent in one can be close to useless in the other, and this is the single most common mismatch families in Abu Dhabi end up paying for. Before anything else, find out which course your child is enrolled in, at which level, and put that in the first message to any prospective tutor.

AA is the algebra-and-calculus course. It assumes manipulation as a working tool, examines a paper without technology, and at Higher Level adds proof by induction and contradiction, complex numbers, three-dimensional vectors, Maclaurin series and differential equations. AI is the modelling-and-data course. The graphic display calculator is assumed throughout both papers, and Higher Level adds matrices and eigenvalues, graph theory, and a considerably heavier statistical inference load including the t-test and Poisson distribution.

The university consequence is real and worth checking early rather than late. Engineering, physics, mathematics and many economics programmes commonly expect AA, often at Higher Level, while design, business, social science and life science routes are frequently satisfied by AI. Requirements vary by institution and by year, so the only sound method is to read the admissions pages of the specific universities on the student's list, including the UAE institutions, rather than relying on a general rule.

There is a practical tutoring consequence too. A student who has chosen AI because AA looked hard, but whose target degree expects AA, has a course-choice problem rather than a tutoring problem, and no number of sessions will substitute for the conversation with the school's IB coordinator. A good tutor will identify that in the first session and say so, which is worth considerably more than a term of competently delivered lessons in the wrong course.

sections.heading: The papers and the weightings, so you know what you are buying hours for
paragraphs: Standard Level is examined through two papers plus the exploration. Higher Level is examined through three papers plus the exploration. That third paper changes the whole shape of a tutoring plan, because it is the only component that tests extended, staged problem-solving rather than topic competence, and nothing in ordinary classwork prepares a student for it.

The arithmetic of the weightings is where families should start. At Standard Level, each written paper carries 40% of the grade and the exploration carries 20%. At Higher Level, the first two papers carry 30% each, the third carries 20% and the exploration carries 20%. Read that second row carefully: at Higher Level the exploration and Paper 3 together are 40% of the final grade, which is as much as both long papers combined. Most students spend almost none of their revision time on either.

Durations matter for the same reason. Standard Level papers run 90 minutes each. Higher Level Papers 1 and 2 run two hours each and Paper 3 runs an hour. A student who has never written for two hours continuously will lose marks in the final third of an HL paper for reasons that have nothing to do with mathematics, and timed practice is the only fix. This is one of the clearest arguments for booking exam-season work as a block rather than as more weekly sessions.

sections.heading: Ten minutes that tell you whether a tutor really teaches IB maths
paragraphs: Because the specialist pool is small, the market around it contains a lot of competent general mathematicians presenting as IB tutors. They are not frauds; they can genuinely teach calculus. What they cannot do is tell a student what the exploration's reflection criterion rewards, or why Paper 3 needs a different approach, or which parts of the Higher Level syllabus are new rather than extended. Those gaps cost a family a term before they become visible.

There is a short set of questions that separates the two groups quickly, and none of them require you to know any mathematics. Ask which course, at which level, the tutor has taught and for how long. Ask how many marks the exploration is worth and how they are distributed across the criteria. Ask what Paper 3 is and how long it lasts. Ask which Higher Level topics do not appear at Standard Level at all. A genuine IB maths teacher answers all four without pausing.

Then ask two harder ones. Ask what they would do with a student whose algebra is weak but who has chosen AA HL, because the honest answer involves the school and the course choice rather than more sessions. And ask what they will and will not do with the exploration, because the correct answer is a boundary rather than an offer, and a tutor who offers to help write it has told you something important about how they work.

Finally, ask what evidence sits behind any examiner claim. Several providers in this market describe tutors as examiners without anything verifiable attached, and the premium on the word is substantial. Which board, which component, which years. A tutor with genuine examiner experience answers that readily; one without it becomes vague, and vagueness at that question is a reliable signal.

How many marks is the exploration worth, and how are they split across the criteria?

sections.heading: The exploration: twenty marks, five criteria, and one boundary
paragraphs: The mathematical exploration is worth 20% of the final maths grade in all four courses, and it is assessed out of twenty marks across five criteria. Presentation carries four marks and rewards a coherent, organised, focused piece of writing. Mathematical communication carries four and rewards correct notation, defined terminology and consistent use of symbols. Personal engagement carries three and rewards evidence that the student actually thought about the topic. Reflection carries three and rewards discussion of the significance and limitations of the work. Use of mathematics carries six.

Set that distribution against how students behave. Most pour their effort into the mathematics, which is six of twenty marks, and treat the other fourteen as formatting. The highest-return hour of exploration tutoring available is almost always spent on reflection and communication, because those seven marks are the ones most frequently left on the table and the ones that respond fastest to specific feedback on a specific draft.

Topic choice is the other decisive factor, and it is decided before any tutoring can help. Mathematics that sits below the level of the course cannot earn the use-of-mathematics marks however well it is presented, and mathematics far above the course usually produces an exploration the student cannot discuss. A tutor earns their rate at the topic-choice stage by testing a proposal against the criteria early, which costs one session and saves a term.

The boundary is absolute. A tutor may explain what each criterion rewards in the IB's own language, may question whether the chosen mathematics earns credit at that level, may read the student's draft and say precisely where it falls short of a descriptor, and may ask questions that lead the student to notice a gap. A tutor may not write any part of the exploration, redraft a passage, supply a structure to fill in, or edit a draft to completion. Every word submitted must be the student's own, and IB academic-honesty rules make that an expulsion risk for the candidate rather than a problem for the tutor.

sections.heading: Where Higher Level students actually lose marks
paragraphs: The pattern repeats across Abu Dhabi IB cohorts and it is rarely about intelligence. In Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, the first collapse point is proof. Induction, contradiction and counterexample are new in every sense: not harder versions of Standard Level content but a different kind of mathematical activity, with conventions a student has never been taught. Able students lose marks because they produce a correct argument in a form the mark scheme does not recognise.

The second is multi-step algebra under time pressure on the non-calculator paper. A student who understands every individual technique still loses marks when a question requires four of them in sequence with no intermediate confirmation that they are on track. This is a fluency problem rather than a comprehension problem, and it responds to drilled practice, not to re-explanation. Many families buy the wrong remedy here and conclude that tutoring does not work.

In Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level, the equivalent failure is interpretation. A student runs a chi-squared test correctly, reads the p-value correctly, and then writes a conclusion in statistics vocabulary instead of in the context of the question. The marks are explicitly for the contextual statement. The same pattern appears with regression, with confidence intervals and with the t-test, and it is one of the fastest things to fix once it has been named.

Across both courses, Paper 3 is the component nobody practises. It is 20% of the grade, it is one hour long, and it consists of extended questions that build in stages. Students trained entirely on topic exercises meet it for the first time in the examination room. A handful of sessions on staged problems changes performance here more than the same hours spread across topics, which is why it appears as its own mode of work higher up this page.

sections.heading: Specialist availability in Abu Dhabi, stated plainly
paragraphs: This is the section competing pages omit. No provider found in this market discloses a coverage limit at all, and several conceal non-UAE delivery behind an overseas phone number. Being honest about availability is a better basis for a two-year relationship than pretending that every subject, level and time slot is always covered, so here is the actual position for IB mathematics in Abu Dhabi.

Standard Level teaching in both courses is reasonably covered, and a match is usually quick. Higher Level Analysis and Approaches is thinner, and the thinnest point is the combination of Higher Level, a specific weekday evening slot in Gulf Standard Time, and the spring term when the whole emirate wants the same hours. Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level is thinner still, because the matrices, graph theory and inference content narrows the pool further and AA teachers do not automatically cover it.

When a slot cannot be filled, we say so and give a realistic date instead of putting a general mathematician into an AA HL booking. Where no UAE-based specialist is available, the alternative is a tutor based elsewhere teaching the same IB course over the same video platform, with sessions timed to Gulf Standard Time, and that is disclosed before anything is booked. A parent is entitled to know who is teaching their child and from where.
