sections.heading: ADEK, the permit, and why the nearest teacher is often the one you cannot hire
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi's private schools are licensed and inspected by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Dubai's regulator is the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, Sharjah's is the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah has a Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. A Hudayriyat Island family sits inside the Abu Dhabi system, so inspection reports and school licensing come from ADEK.

Private tutoring is governed separately. The Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation issues a private tuition work permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time through the smart app, website and e-services system. Offering private lessons without the permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

The part specific to this page is the conflict rule. ADEK's professional-ethics expectations for private and charter school staff restrict teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. In a city where the AA HL teaching population is concentrated in a handful of campuses, that rule removes a meaningful share of the nearest specialists from a given family's options. It is a good rule, and it is also why the local search feels so unproductive.

IB Gram holds no ADEK permit, no KHDA permit and no accreditation from the IB, and nothing here should be read as implying otherwise. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a specific licence for a specific kind of entity. What a parent can reasonably ask for is the tutor's permit position, the exact course they teach, and a free trial lesson before any payment.

sections.heading: Starting from Hudayriyat Island, and what we will tell you if we cannot help
paragraphs: Send four things: the school, the exact course and level, the most recent internal assessment grade, and the time slots that genuinely work once the bridge and the school run are accounted for. The last of those matters more for maths than for most subjects, because arithmetic accuracy degrades with tiredness in a way that essay writing does not. A session at a time the student is alert for is worth more than a longer one at a convenient hour.

The first lesson is a free trial with no card required. Use it as a diagnostic rather than a demonstration: ask for a past-paper question worked through and marked live, and ask at the end what the tutor thinks the underlying problem is. If the answer is a course-choice conversation with the IB coordinator rather than a term of sessions, that is the most valuable thing the hour could have produced, and a tutor who says it is the one to keep.

Pricing is quoted after the trial against the actual plan — course, level, number of sessions, whether an exploration block or a Paper 3 block is included. Market context for comparison: specialist IB rates in this market are published between AED 200 and 450 and upward, with one premium provider at AED 650, and in-home arrangements from AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the rate. Those are other providers' figures read in October 2026, not ours.

Finally, the honest limits. We do not publish IB session or results dates anywhere, because none could be verified from the IB directly, and a date a family plans around has to come from the school's IB coordinator or ibo.org. We do not reproduce IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables; we reference them and link to the official source. And we do not produce any part of an exploration, under any deadline pressure, which is a boundary the student is told about in the first session.

process.title: Name the course, not the subject
process.description: Say AA HL, AA SL, AI HL or AI SL rather than IB maths. This single detail determines which tutors are relevant and which are irrelevant, and getting it wrong is how families end up with a competent teacher of the wrong syllabus. If you are unsure, the school's IB coordinator or the student's timetable will confirm it in a minute.

process.title: Take the free trial as a diagnostic
process.description: One session, no card required. Ask for a past-paper question worked and marked live, then ask the tutor what the underlying problem is. Fluency, concept, technique and course-fit problems need different plans, and a tutor who cannot distinguish between them after an hour of a student's work is not the right match.

process.title: Decide the shape before the volume
process.description: Weekly sessions, a Paper 3 block, an exploration clinic and a pre-Diploma bridging block do different work. Choose the shape that matches the diagnosis rather than defaulting to a weekly slot, because the most common waste in IB maths tutoring is a year of general weekly sessions aimed at a specific, nameable gap.

process.title: Fix a slot the student is awake for
process.description: Sessions run on Gulf Standard Time. For Hudayriyat Island families the honest options are usually straight after the commute across the bridge or well after dinner, and the second is better for mathematics. Timing is reviewed after a fortnight once the real pattern of the week is visible rather than the theoretical one.

process.title: Work to the school's internal calendar
process.description: The tutor plans from your school's scheme of work, mock timetable and internal exploration deadlines. Those deadlines are set by the campus your child attends, which for island families is frequently some distance from the address, and they are the dates that actually constrain the work.

process.title: Review against marked work at six sessions
process.description: Six sessions is enough evidence to judge. If marked problem sets are not improving, the options are a different tutor, a different shape of work, or a conversation with the school about level or course. Adding hours to a plan that is not working is the most expensive response available.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the course, not on a maths label
whyPoints.description: Tutors are listed against AA HL, AA SL, AI HL or AI SL, because those are four syllabuses rather than four difficulty settings. An AA specialist has no particular claim on matrices and graph theory, and an AI specialist has none on Maclaurin series. Naming the course up front removes the most common mismatch in this market.

whyPoints.title: The availability answer is honest
whyPoints.description: Higher Level specialists are scarce in Abu Dhabi and this page says so, by course and by level. When a slot cannot be filled we give a realistic date instead of putting a general mathematician into the booking, and if the available specialist is based outside the UAE, that is disclosed before anything is booked.

whyPoints.title: Paper 3 and the exploration treated properly
whyPoints.description: At Higher Level those two components are 40% of the grade and they are the two nobody revises. They appear here as distinct modes of work with distinct methods, because an hour on staged extended problems does more than an hour of additional topic revision in the term before the session.

whyPoints.title: A stated boundary on the exploration
whyPoints.description: Tutors explain criteria, test topic choice, question reasoning and mark the student's own draft. They do not write, redraft or complete any part of it, and the student is told so in the first session. IB academic-honesty rules put the consequence of a breach on the candidate, which is reason enough to be explicit.

whyPoints.title: No claims we cannot evidence
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no ADEK permit, no KHDA permit and no IB accreditation, and says so plainly. There is no self-asserted rating, no outcome percentage without underlying data, and no examiner claim without the board, component and years attached. Several providers in this market do all three.

whyPoints.title: Dates taken from the source, or not published
whyPoints.description: No IB session or results date appears on this page, because none could be verified from the IB. Cambridge and Pearson dates are quoted with their source where relevant. Where a figure or a rule comes from a regulator, it comes from ADEK, MoHRE or the Ministry rather than from a paraphrase.

faqs.question: Is there an IB maths tutor on Hudayriyat Island who teaches AA Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Within a short drive of the island, almost certainly not. Hudayriyat Island is reached by bridge from Al Bateen, the housing arrived before the school-age population, and there is no settled teaching community on the island to draw from. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is taught by a small number of people in Abu Dhabi, most of them employed full time at IB campuses elsewhere in the city. Online delivery removes distance as a filter, which is the only practical way to reach an actual AA HL teacher from this address. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

faqs.question: What is the difference between IB Maths AA and AI, and does it change who we need?
faqs.answer: It changes everything about who can help. Analysis and Approaches is the algebra-and-calculus course, examines one paper without technology, and at Higher Level adds proof by induction, complex numbers, three-dimensional vectors, Maclaurin series and differential equations. Applications and Interpretation assumes the graphic display calculator throughout and at Higher Level adds matrices and eigenvalues, graph theory and heavier statistical inference including the t-test. Neither set appears in the other course. A tutor who teaches AA HL well has no particular competence in AI HL content, so name the course and the level in your first message.

faqs.question: How many marks is the IB maths exploration worth, criterion by criterion?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent, in all four courses, assessed out of twenty marks across five criteria. Presentation carries four, mathematical communication four, personal engagement three, reflection three, and use of mathematics six. That last number surprises most students: the mathematics itself is less than a third of the available marks. Reflection and communication are where marks are most often left on the table, and they respond quickly to specific feedback on a specific draft. At Higher Level the exploration and Paper 3 together are 40% of the final grade, which is as much as both long written papers combined.

faqs.question: What is Paper 3 and why does nobody seem to prepare for it?
faqs.answer: Paper 3 is a one-hour Higher Level paper of two extended questions that build in stages, worth 20% of the grade. It exists in both AA HL and AI HL. Students neglect it because ordinary classwork and revision are organised by topic, and no amount of topic practice teaches the skill the paper actually tests: reading ahead, recognising the structure of a staged problem, and persisting through an opening part that is not yet obviously useful. A short block of full extended questions under timed conditions changes performance here more than the same hours spread across topics.

faqs.question: How do I check that a maths tutor genuinely knows the IB course?
faqs.answer: Ask four questions that need no mathematics from you. Which exact course and level have you taught, and for how long? How many marks is the exploration worth, and how are they split across the criteria? What is Paper 3, how long is it, and how do you prepare for it? Which Higher Level topics do not appear at Standard Level at all? A genuine IB maths teacher answers all four without hesitating. A competent general mathematician presenting as an IB tutor usually answers the first and becomes vague on the rest, which is exactly the information you need.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help my child write the maths exploration?
faqs.answer: A tutor can help the student write it; a tutor cannot write it. The permitted work is substantial: explaining what each criterion rewards in the IB's own language, testing whether a proposed topic uses mathematics at the level of the course, reading the student's draft and saying precisely where it falls short of a descriptor, and asking questions that make the student find a gap. What is not permitted is writing any part of it, redrafting a passage, supplying a structure to fill in, or editing to completion. Every submitted word must be the student's, and the consequence of a breach falls on the candidate.

faqs.question: My child is strong at maths but has stalled in AA HL. What usually causes that?
faqs.answer: Two things, in this order. Proof is the first: induction, contradiction and counterexample are new in kind rather than in difficulty, with conventions the student has never been taught, so able students produce correct arguments in a form the mark scheme does not reward. The second is multi-step algebra under time pressure on the paper without technology, where somebody who understands every individual technique still fails to chain four of them with no confirmation they are on track. The first needs teaching; the second needs drilled fluency. Treating the second as a comprehension problem is the common and expensive mistake.

faqs.question: Does a Hudayriyat Island family need AA or AI for a UAE university place?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the degree and the institution, and the only sound method is to read each named university's current admissions pages, including the UAE ones. The general pattern is that mathematics, physics, engineering and many economics programmes expect Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, while business, design, social science and life science routes are frequently satisfied by Applications and Interpretation. Requirements change year to year. If the target degree expects AA and the student has chosen AI, that is a course-choice conversation with the IB coordinator rather than a tutoring problem, and no number of sessions substitutes for it.

faqs.question: Why can't we just hire a maths teacher from my child's own school?
faqs.answer: Because the rules in this emirate restrict it. ADEK's professional-ethics expectations for private and charter school staff restrict teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Teachers tutoring outside school hours also need that permit. Since Abu Dhabi's AA HL teaching population is concentrated in a handful of campuses, this removes a real share of the nearest specialists from any one family's options, which is a large part of why the local search feels unproductive.

faqs.question: What do specialist IB maths tutors charge in this market?
faqs.answer: Published UAE figures put a qualified subject tutor working online at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with IB and A-Level specialists quoted from AED 200 to 450 and upward and one premium examiner-led provider at AED 650. In-home arrangements are quoted from AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the rate. Those were read from other providers' pages in October 2026 and are not IB Gram prices. The useful observation is that the premium on specialist IB maths is scarcity, not travel, so driving further does not reduce it. IB Gram quotes after a free trial lesson.

faqs.question: How many maths sessions a week does a Diploma student usually need?
faqs.answer: One a week through most of the two years, with a second added during the final term or for a specific block, is the shape most families settle on. The limiting factor is how much marked practice the student completes between sessions rather than contact hours, which is why problem sets are set and returned with comments. Where the diagnosis is a fluency gap rather than a conceptual one, short frequent practice beats longer sessions. Review against marked work at six sessions, and if nothing is moving, change the tutor or the shape of the work rather than adding hours.

faqs.question: Can my child get help before Year 12 starts, coming out of MYP?
faqs.answer: That is the highest-return block available and the one families most often skip. Four to eight sessions over the summer, aimed almost entirely at algebraic fluency, function language and notation conventions, decide how the first term of AA or AI feels. MYP mathematics rewards investigation and communication, which is a genuine strength and also why some students arrive with weaker manipulation than an IGCSE cohort. Closing that gap before Year 12 costs general rates; closing it in the middle of Year 12 costs specialist rates under time pressure, and competes with new content for the same hours.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram publish the IB exam and results dates for the May session?
faqs.answer: No, deliberately. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no IB session or results date in this project was verified from the IB itself, and publishing an unverified date that a family plans around would be worse than publishing nothing. Abu Dhabi IB schools sit the May session, and a November session also exists. For actual dates, ask your school's IB coordinator or read ibo.org directly. Cambridge and Pearson dates are a different matter and are sourced where this site uses them, including Pearson's November timetable and results timings.

faqs.question: What if no AA Higher Level specialist is free in the slot we need?
faqs.answer: We say so and give a realistic date rather than putting a general mathematician into the booking. Higher Level availability in Abu Dhabi is genuinely limited, and the tightest combination is Higher Level plus a fixed weekday evening slot plus the spring term, when the whole emirate wants the same hours. Where no UAE-based specialist is available for the course, the alternative is a specialist based elsewhere teaching the same IB course over the same platform with sessions timed to Gulf Standard Time, disclosed before anything is booked. No competitor page found in this market discloses a coverage limit at all.

faqs.question: Will an online tutor plan from our Abu Dhabi school's scheme of work?
faqs.answer: The school's. We ask which campus your child attends even though the lesson is online, because the internal exploration deadlines, the mock timetable and the order in which topics are taught all belong to that school. A tutor running their own sequence will be teaching differentiation while the class is being assessed on probability, which undermines the point of one-to-one work. Where the tutor thinks the school's order is creating a problem, they say so to you rather than quietly working around it, and the conversation that follows usually belongs with the subject teacher.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-hudayriyat-i.closingHeading: Stop filtering by distance and start filtering by course
abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-hudayriyat-i.closingBody: If the search for an IB maths tutor in Hudayriyat Island has not produced anybody who genuinely teaches your child's course, that is the geography talking rather than bad luck. Higher Level specialists are thin on the ground in Abu Dhabi and thinner within a radius of one island. Tell us the exact course and level, the school, the last internal grade and the slots that honestly work after the bridge crossing. The first lesson is a free trial with no card required, and the useful question to ask at the end is what the tutor thinks the real problem is. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-hydra-villag.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach Diploma mathematics at Standard and Higher Level in both courses. Matching happens against the course, the level and the point in the two-year programme the student has reached, because the same subject needs different work in DP1 term one and DP2 term two.

intro.heading: The same hour is worth different amounts in different terms
paragraphs: Diploma mathematics is a two-year course with a strongly uneven shape, and a tuition hour bought in the wrong term is worth a fraction of the same hour bought in the right one. In DP1 term one an hour can repair the fluency a student arrived with. In DP2 term two the same hour cannot, because fluency is built over months and there are no months left; it can only buy technique. Both are real gains. They are not the same gain and they should not cost the same amount of hope.

Hydra Village is a small gated villa community on the mainland side of Abu Dhabi, out near Al Shamkha and Al Reef, laid out in clusters with its own quiet internal roads and no school inside it. Every child here travels, mostly into the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor or onto the island, and the practical consequence is a late and slightly unpredictable afternoon. That matters for a calendar-led plan because the available weekly hours are fewer than a published school calendar implies, which makes placing them well more important rather than less.

The mathematics itself divides into three calendar problems. First, content: most of the syllabus arrives in DP1 and early DP2, and a gap opened there widens because later topics assume earlier ones. Second, the exploration: twenty per cent of the grade, with a chain of internal school deadlines running through the middle of the programme, and almost no household plans for it. Third, the run-in: the final six to eight weeks, which reliably improve timing, exact-form discipline, calculator recording and question selection, and reliably cannot teach a topic that was never taught.

On delivery, stated plainly: IB Gram does not offer home visits in Hydra Village or anywhere in the UAE, because home visiting is a service we run only in India. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. In a small community a long way from the schools, that is the difference between choosing a specialist in the exact course and choosing whoever is prepared to drive out through Al Shamkha at five in the afternoon.

What follows is the calendar in usable form. A term-by-term map of what DP1 and DP2 mathematics actually cover and what tutoring should be doing at each stage. The exploration deadline chain with the specific risk of arriving late at each point. What a mathematics mock does and does not predict. A six-week run-in plan organised by paper rather than by topic, because the papers are prepared for differently. The deadline on the level decision, which is earlier than families think. The summer between DP1 and DP2, which is the most under-used asset in the programme. And the boundaries we work inside.

No Diploma examination or results date appears on this page. The organisation's own site is the only place those can be confirmed, and a date a parent might act on should not come from a tutoring page. The session UAE schools sit is the May one; your school's Diploma coordinator holds the exact windows and every internal deadline that matters more than they do.

subjects.name: The exploration

subjects.description: The run-in's proper business. Full papers to the clock, exact answers where demanded, calculator commands recorded, and a hard rule that no question is abandoned before the given working is attempted.

sections.heading: DP1 and DP2 mathematics, term by term
paragraphs: Schools sequence content differently, so the table below is a typical shape rather than a universal one, and your school's scheme of work is the authority. What is consistent across schools is the distribution: most content lands in DP1 and the first half of DP2, and the back half of DP2 is examination preparation competing with the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and every other subject's internal assessment.

Reading the table, the useful question for a parent is which row you are currently in and therefore what is still possible. In the first two rows almost everything is possible, including repairing fluency. By the fourth row content gaps are expensive and fluency repair is effectively closed. By the fifth row the honest menu is timing, exact form, calculator recording, command words and question selection, which together still produce a worthwhile swing on a paper where the content is known.

The second use of the table is to notice where the exploration sits. In most schools the exploration chain runs through the middle rows, which is precisely when the content load is heaviest. Students therefore write it at the worst possible moment unless somebody has planned for it, and the planning consists of nothing more complicated than choosing a viable topic early and doing some of the thinking in the summer.

Finally, the right way to use any of this is against your own school's published calendar rather than against a generic table. Ask for the mathematics scheme of work and the internal assessment dates in the first week of the year. A household with those two documents and this table can place tuition hours where they are worth most, which is a bigger determinant of outcome than which tutor is chosen.

sections.heading: The exploration deadline chain
paragraphs: Twenty per cent of the mathematics grade sits in a piece of writing with no invigilator, criteria published in advance, and a chain of internal school deadlines that almost no household writes down. It is the most controllable component in the subject and the one most often produced in a panic.

The chain has recognisable stages and each has a specific risk attached to arriving late. Topic choice is the first and the most consequential, because a topic that cannot support genuine reflection or personal engagement caps two of the five criteria before a line is written, however good the mathematics. That is a mathematical judgement about the topic rather than a matter of taste, and it is the single most useful conversation a tutor can have with a DP1 student.

The middle of the chain is the draft and the feedback the school supervisor is permitted to give. A student who submits a draft that is really an outline receives feedback on an outline, which wastes the one formal opportunity available. A student who submits something close to complete receives feedback that can actually be acted on. The difference is a fortnight of earlier work, and it is worth more than any number of tuition hours spent afterwards.

The boundary throughout is firm and we say it to the student at the first session. A tutor teaches the criteria by letter with their allocations, discusses whether a topic can support them, reads the student's own draft, asks the questions that expose an unsupported claim, and names the criterion a section is failing. A tutor does not supply sentences, restructure a draft into a finished piece, or produce any part of it. We decline that at any price, and a provider in this market advertising completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750 is selling a risk that falls on the student's whole entry.

sections.heading: What a mathematics mock predicts, and what it does not
paragraphs: Mocks in mathematics are treated as forecasts and are better used as diagnostics. The grade on the front is a snapshot of a student's performance on a particular paper in a particular room on a particular morning, usually before the syllabus has been completely taught. Reading it as a prediction produces either complacency or despair, and neither is useful.

What a mock does reliably show is the pattern of lost marks, and that is genuinely predictive. A script where nine marks went to answers rounded at an intermediate step and six to unrecorded calculator work is describing a habit that will recur in the real papers unless something changes. A script where marks are spread thinly across every topic is describing something different and more serious. The categories matter more than the total.

What a mock does not show is how much the student will improve, because that depends on what is done next. It also systematically under-represents performance where the syllabus was incomplete at the time, which is common in mathematics because integration and the Higher Level extras often arrive late. A parent reading a disappointing mock in mathematics should ask the teacher directly which topics had not yet been taught, because that subtracts a predictable quantity from the apparent problem.

The practical routine is to read the script in the week it comes back. Assign every lost mark to a category: content never learned, method misapplied, notation or calculator, command word misread, exact form not given, or ran out of time. Count them. The two or three largest categories are the run-in plan, and everything else can be deliberately ignored. Narrow and well-aimed beats broad and reassuring when the weeks are finite, which in a Hydra Village household with a long daily journey they certainly are.

sections.heading: A six-week run-in organised by paper
paragraphs: Most run-in revision is organised by topic, working through the syllabus from the start and running out of time somewhere in the middle. Organising by paper works better, because the papers examine different things and because a student's faults are usually paper-specific rather than topic-specific.

In Analysis and Approaches the split is sharp. Paper 1 permits no technology, so its practice has to happen with the calculator out of the room: exact trigonometric values, surds, fraction work, manipulation at speed and calculus performed by hand. Paper 2 permits technology, so its practice is about selection, correct angle mode, storing values and above all recording the command used so that the page shows a method. Those are different practice sessions with different error logs and conflating them is why students arrive at Paper 1 having quietly outsourced its core skill for two years.

At Higher Level, Paper 3 needs its own allocation. One hour, a fifth of the grade, long scaffolded investigations, and a single decisive behaviour: use whatever the question gives you and keep going rather than stopping at the first part that resists. Three marked cycles — sit the paper, mark it against the published criteria, rework only the point of failure — usually changes that behaviour permanently. Students who have never sat one are improvising with twenty per cent of their grade.

The table sets out a six-week shape. The final week is deliberately light and contains no new content, because introducing anything in the last seven days produces anxiety rather than marks. And the whole plan assumes marked papers rather than self-assessed ones, because students reliably award themselves credit for answers that would earn none and overlook method marks they actually earned.

sections.heading: The level decision, and the date it closes
paragraphs: Choosing between Higher and Standard Level mathematics is treated as a preference and is in fact a deadlined decision, and the deadline is set by the school rather than by the family. Once the entry is made the decision is fixed, and before that there is a softer limit: moving between levels requires catching up content the other class has already covered, so a change needs teaching time as well as an administrative form.

The published scale of the difference is the clearest guide available. Higher Level mathematics carries two hundred and forty published teaching hours against one hundred and fifty at Standard Level, and it adds Paper 3, worth a fifth of the grade. That is not a modest increment in difficulty; it is sixty per cent more course, and the additional content is the harder content. The exploration remains twenty per cent in both.

For a Hydra Village household the commute belongs honestly in that calculation. An hour or more a day on the road is roughly five usable study hours a week, and Higher Level mathematics is the course least able to absorb that loss. Saying so is not an excuse; it is an input. A student who would manage Higher Level living beside the school may not manage it with a long daily journey and two other Higher Levels, and finding that out in DP2 term two is considerably worse than deciding it in DP1.

On universities, take nothing from a summary, including this one. Engineering, physics and some economics programmes commonly expect Higher Level mathematics in the Analysis course, and the authoritative statement in every case is the institution's own published admission requirements, which change. For families looking within the Emirates, read the current pages for Khalifa University, United Arab Emirates University, the American University of Sharjah, New York University Abu Dhabi and Zayed University directly. For Ministry of Education equivalency, no Diploma points figure should be quoted without a reference on the ministry's own site.

sections.heading: The summer between DP1 and DP2
paragraphs: This is the most under-used asset in the whole Diploma and it is free of the constraint that limits everything else: there is nothing competing for the time. No homework from six subjects, no Theory of Knowledge deadline, no Extended Essay milestone. A student working on mathematics in July is working on mathematics rather than triaging a week.

Three things fit the period particularly well. First, catching up content that DP1 left incomplete, which in mathematics is frequently integration or the Higher Level additions. Taught in the summer, that content is absorbed; taught in DP2 term one it is crammed alongside new material and the exploration. Second, the exploration itself: topic viability, the mathematics, and a genuine first draft can all be done without the school's own deadline bearing down. Third, Paper 3 exposure for Higher Level students, which otherwise waits until there is no room for it.

The practical obstacles are travel and willingness, and both are manageable. Lessons delivered over live video follow a family between countries, which is the specific reason online delivery suits a UAE summer: a household in Europe or South Asia for six weeks can keep a weekly session running on Gulf Standard Time or shift it to a local hour. For willingness, a bounded block with a stated end date is easier for a student to accept than an open-ended summer of tuition, and it is also what the work actually needs.

Specialist availability is wider in this period than at any other point in the year, which is the final argument for using it. In term time, demand concentrates in the same late-afternoon window every household wants and specialists in a given course and level fill first. In the summer that pressure lifts. Families who plan the summer in the spring get the person they want; families who decide in August get whoever is left.

sections.heading: Hydra Village logistics: a small community, a long afternoon
paragraphs: Hydra Village is a quiet, low-density villa community with no school inside it, which means every student here commutes and the afternoon is correspondingly long. The journey is mostly outward to the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor, and for families who have chosen an island school it is longer again. Published school finish times are therefore the least useful number in planning: what matters is arrival.

The method is unglamorous and it works. Record the actual arrival time for five consecutive days, take the latest of the five, and add fifteen minutes for changing and eating. That is the slot. From a mainland community a long way from the school cluster it will usually be five o'clock or later, and booking anything earlier produces a rescheduling habit that ends the arrangement by about week six — a failure that then gets attributed to the tutor.

A second feature specific to small communities is that the local in-person options are close to nonexistent. There is no tuition centre within the community and no reason for a Diploma mathematics specialist to live here. Published in-home visiting rates in the emirate run from AED 180 to 350 an hour in survey data and from AED 200 to 500 among independent home tutors, read in October 2026, with the longest journeys at the upper end. A sixty-kilometre round trip for a single lesson has to be paid for somewhere.

Set against published online rates of roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour for a qualified subject tutor, the loading is mostly transport. That is the straightforward case for live video from a community like this one, and it has a second benefit that matters for a calendar-led plan: a video session can move to a different evening in mock week, run at a different hour during Ramadan, and continue through a summer spent abroad. None of those is possible with a tutor who has to arrive at a gate.

sections.heading: Dates, boundaries and claims
paragraphs: A calendar page has to be careful about dates, so the omissions here are deliberate. No Diploma examination window or results date appears, because the organisation's own site is the only place to confirm one and automated access to it is blocked, which means any tutoring site quoting you a Diploma results date is passing on something unverified. The session UAE schools sit is the May one, and your school's coordinator holds the internal deadlines that matter more than the examination date does.

Nor does any grade boundary appear. Boundaries are set after each session in light of that session's papers and candidate performance and published afterwards; they move between sessions and a fixed figure on a tutoring page is a fabricated certainty. What is stable and more useful is the description of what each grade represents in accuracy, method selection and handling unfamiliar problems, because each description implies a different intervention.

On assessed work: a tutor teaches the exploration criteria, discusses topic viability, reads the student's own draft, questions it and names the criterion a section is failing. A tutor does not supply sentences for submission, restructure a draft into a finished piece, provide solutions to live assessed work or sit beside a student during an assessment. We decline that at any price. Board material — specifications, past papers, mark schemes and boundary tables — belongs to the organisation that publishes it; we reference and link rather than reproduce.

On status: IB Gram is an independent online matching platform with no office, centre or branch in the UAE, holding no accreditation, licence, approval or partnership from the IB, ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson. Any paid private tutor in the Emirates needs a private tuition work permit issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years. No tutor can promise a grade, and we publish no rating or satisfaction statistic.

faqs.question: When in the Diploma should a Hydra Village family start maths tuition?
faqs.answer: DP1 term one if there is any choice, because that is the only window in which an underlying fluency problem can genuinely be repaired. Fluency means performing understood steps fast enough to finish papers, and speed is built by short practice spread across months. By DP2 term two those months do not exist, so the honest menu narrows to timing, exact form, calculator recording and command words, which are real gains but different ones.

faqs.question: Does a maths tutor come out to Hydra Village?
faqs.answer: Independent tutors in the emirate do visit, and IB Gram does not. We teach one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and we do not offer home visits in Hydra Village or anywhere in the UAE, because home visiting is a service we run only in India. In a small community with no school inside it and no reason for a Diploma specialist to live nearby, published in-home rates of AED 180 to 500 an hour are largely paying for a long journey.

faqs.question: What time can a lesson realistically start from Hydra Village?
faqs.answer: Usually five o'clock or later, and the way to know is to measure rather than estimate. Record when your child actually walks in for five consecutive days, take the latest of those five, and add fifteen minutes for changing and eating. Published school finish times are the least useful number in this calculation because the journey out to the Khalifa City corridor or onto the island varies, and a slot booked too early becomes a rescheduling habit.

faqs.question: When should the maths exploration topic be chosen?
faqs.answer: In the second half of DP1, with a shortlist of three candidate questions tested for whether they can support genuine reflection. That matters because reflection and personal engagement carry three marks each of the twenty, and a topic with nothing to be surprised by caps both before a line is written. Choosing late also means rechoosing during the heaviest content term, which is how students lose weeks they later need for the mathematics itself.

faqs.question: Why organise exam revision by paper rather than by topic?
faqs.answer: Because the papers examine different things and students' faults are usually paper-specific. In Analysis and Approaches, Paper 1 permits no technology, so its practice must happen with the calculator out of the room: exact values, surds, manipulation at speed, calculus by hand. Paper 2 permits technology, so its practice is selection, angle mode, stored values and recording the command used. Those are separate sessions with separate error logs, and conflating them wastes the run-in.

faqs.question: How many Paper 3 papers should a Higher Level student sit?
faqs.answer: At least three full ones, marked against the published criteria, with only the point of failure reworked each time rather than the whole paper. Paper 3 is worth a fifth of the Higher Level grade in a single hour, and its decisive behaviour is using whatever the question gives you and continuing rather than stopping at the first part that resists. Three marked cycles usually changes that permanently; students who have never sat one are improvising with twenty per cent of the grade.

faqs.question: Is a disappointing maths mock a reliable prediction?
faqs.answer: Not of the final grade, and genuinely useful as a diagnosis. Mocks are often sat before the syllabus is complete, which in mathematics commonly means integration or the Higher Level additions were untaught, so ask the teacher which topics had not been covered and subtract that from the apparent problem. What is predictive is the pattern of lost marks: habits such as early rounding or unrecorded calculator work will recur in the real papers unless something changes.

faqs.question: What makes the summer before DP2 worth using?
faqs.answer: Nothing competes for the time. No homework from six subjects, no Theory of Knowledge deadline, no Extended Essay milestone, so content taught then is absorbed rather than crammed. Three things fit it especially well: catching up DP1 content such as integration, working through the mathematics behind the exploration and reaching a real first draft, and first exposure to Paper 3. Specialist availability is also at its widest, so families who plan in the spring get the person they want.

faqs.question: When does the Higher or Standard Level decision actually close?
faqs.answer: When the school submits the entry, and softly before that. Moving between levels requires catching up content the other class has already covered, so a change needs teaching time as well as a form. Higher Level is a 240 hour course against 150 at Standard Level and adds Paper 3, worth a fifth of the grade. Ask the Diploma coordinator for the entry date and how much of the Higher Level content has been taught, and work back from the earlier limit.

faqs.question: Can lessons continue if we travel for the summer?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is one of the practical advantages of live video delivery for a UAE household. A family in Europe or South Asia for six weeks can keep a weekly session on Gulf Standard Time or shift it to a convenient local hour, which keeps the summer catch-up window usable rather than lost to travel. A bounded block with a stated end date also tends to be easier for a student to accept than an open-ended summer of lessons.

faqs.question: How does the Hydra Village commute affect the level decision?
faqs.answer: It is a legitimate input rather than an excuse. An hour or more a day on the road is roughly five usable study hours a week, and Higher Level mathematics is the course least able to absorb that loss, because it assumes substantial practice outside lessons across 240 published teaching hours. A student who would manage Higher Level living beside the school may not manage it with a long journey plus two other Higher Levels, and discovering that in DP2 is far worse.

faqs.question: What should we ask the school in the first week of the year?
faqs.answer: For the mathematics scheme of work, the internal assessment dates, the exploration draft and final submission deadlines, and the mock window. Those four pieces of information let a household place tuition hours where they are worth most, which affects the outcome more than the choice of tutor does. Almost every disappointing tuition arrangement we see was built on a calendar nobody had looked at, and the calendar was available for the asking.

faqs.question: Why will you not tell us the Diploma results date?
faqs.answer: Because the organisation's own site is the only place it can be confirmed, automated access to that site is blocked, and a date a parent might act on should not come from a tutoring page. The session UAE schools sit is the May one, with a second session available. Your school's Diploma coordinator holds the exact examination windows, the upload deadlines and the results dates, and every internal deadline on the way there matters more to a plan than the examination date does.

faqs.question: What mark will my child need for a particular Diploma maths grade?
faqs.answer: No figure can be given honestly, because boundaries are set after each session in light of that session's papers and candidate performance and published afterwards. They move between sessions, so a fixed threshold on any website is a fabricated certainty. What is stable is the description of what each grade represents in consistency of accuracy, independent method selection and handling unfamiliar problems, and each of those descriptions implies a different and specific intervention.

intro.heading: Why the search for a local IB maths tutor in Khalifa City usually comes up empty
paragraphs: There are four DP mathematics courses, not one. Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation each run at Higher and Standard Level, and they diverge far enough that a tutor fluent in one can be close to useless in another. AA HL sits on proof, calculus and algebraic manipulation, with a no-calculator Paper 1. AI HL sits on modelling, regression, matrices and graph theory, with a graphic display calculator permitted throughout. A maths graduate who has never taught either will handle the content and miss the examination entirely.

That is the real reason a neighbourhood search disappoints. Khalifa City has plenty of people who can do mathematics to this level. The number who have taught AA HL to the exam, marked explorations against criterion E, and know why a Paper 3 investigation collapses in the last twelve marks is small in any single Abu Dhabi community, and it does not grow because you widen the search radius to Al Raha Gardens. Geography is the wrong filter. The course code is the right one.

The second thing families discover late is that the exploration carries twenty per cent of the grade in every one of the four courses, and it is assessed against five criteria lettered A to E with fixed mark allocations. A student can be strong in class, produce a technically correct exploration, and lose seven or eight of those twenty marks on presentation, reflection and personal engagement, which have nothing to do with mathematical ability. No amount of extra algebra practice recovers those marks. Reading the criteria does.

This page is written to be useful even if you never contact us or anybody else. It sets out exactly what each of the four courses assesses and in what proportion, where marks are actually lost in each paper, what the five exploration criteria credit and how many marks each is worth, and six questions you can put to any tutor in ten minutes to find out whether they know the syllabus or know mathematics. Those questions work on us as well as on anybody else, which is the point of publishing them.

On delivery, the position is unambiguous. IB Gram does not operate home visits in Abu Dhabi; visiting tutors are something we provide only in India. Every Khalifa City lesson is one-to-one over live video, on a shared whiteboard, timed to Gulf Standard Time so a session can begin at 16:00 after a Raha Gardens school run or at 20:30 in a household where both parents commute. No IB exam or results dates appear anywhere on this page, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and an unverified date in an answer a parent acts on is worse than no date at all.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-khalifa-city.programmesIntro: Three programmes matter for a Khalifa City family looking at DP mathematics: the Diploma itself, the Middle Years Programme that feeds it at the IB continuum schools in the corridor, and the British-track IGCSE route that a large share of students arrive from. Each produces a different starting point in Year 12.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Every Diploma candidate takes one mathematics course from four: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, at Higher or Standard Level. Five topic areas run through all four courses, with different depth: number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus. The examination structure differs by level, and the exploration is common to all four at twenty per cent of the final grade.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session, and Khalifa City students generally take their exploration deadline from the school's internal calendar rather than from any published board date. Ask the IB coordinator at your child's school for the written internal deadline schedule; it is the document that governs when exploration work has to be finished, and it usually falls a term earlier than families expect.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria, graded 1 to 8, with extended and standard mathematics streams in the final years. Students arrive in the Diploma strong on investigation and communication and often light on algebraic fluency, because MYP credits the process of mathematical reasoning more heavily than speed and accuracy in manipulation.
programmes.countryNote: The IB continuum schools in and around Khalifa City run MYP to Year 11, so a sizeable share of the corridor's Diploma cohort has never sat a terminal written mathematics paper before Year 12. That transition is the most predictable tutoring need in this area, and it is a short job if it is started in the summer rather than after the first Diploma assessment.

programmes.name: IGCSE and International GCSE mathematics
programmes.description: The British-track feeder, taught in the Khalifa City corridor as Cambridge 0580 or Pearson Edexcel 4MA1, with Additional Mathematics 0606 as an optional bridge. Extended or Higher tier is the realistic minimum for AA at either level, and students who took Core generally need a summer of catch-up before AA SL is viable.
programmes.countryNote: Khalifa City families moving from a British-track school into a Diploma school face a specific gap rather than a general one: trigonometric identities, sequences and series, and the early calculus that AA assumes from day one. Students who completed 0606 arrive with most of that gap already closed, which is the single best argument for taking it.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-khalifa-city.subjectsIntro: Mathematics is one subject on a timetable and five distinct bodies of work in an examination. The list below is how tutoring is actually organised, because a student losing marks in calculus needs nothing done about statistics.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebraic, proof-driven route. SL Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, which rewards manipulation fluency that no graphic display calculator can rescue. Higher Level adds complex numbers, vectors in three dimensions, proof by induction and substantially harder calculus.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The modelling route, with the calculator permitted in every paper. Statistics, regression and real-data interpretation carry more weight, and Higher Level adds matrices, graph theory and complex-number applications. Students who chose it to avoid difficulty are often surprised by the statistics load.

subjects.name: Number and algebra
subjects.description: Sequences, series, exponents, logarithms, and at Higher Level proof and complex numbers. The topic that most often exposes a weak IGCSE foundation, because almost everything later in the course assumes fluent algebraic manipulation rather than correct manipulation done slowly.

subjects.name: Functions
subjects.description: Transformations, composite and inverse functions, and graph interpretation. Marks go missing where a sketch is required before a calculation and the student calculates first, or where a domain restriction is ignored and an otherwise correct answer becomes invalid.

subjects.name: Geometry and trigonometry
subjects.description: Identities, non-right-angled triangles, radian measure and, at AA HL, three-dimensional vectors. The identity work is the usual failure point: students memorise the identities and cannot recognise which one a question is inviting them to use.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.description: Dominant in AI and lighter in AA, covering distributions, correlation, regression and hypothesis testing at Higher Level. Calculator competence matters more here than anywhere else in the course, and students lose marks for reporting an output without the working that justifies it.

subjects.name: Calculus
subjects.description: Differentiation, integration and applications, extending at AA HL into implicit differentiation, differential equations and Maclaurin series. The heaviest content block in AA and the usual reason an otherwise capable student stalls in Year 13.

subjects.name: Paper 3 extended investigation
subjects.description: Two long structured problems in one hour, worth twenty per cent of the Higher Level grade, requiring sustained reasoning across multiple parts where a mistake in part b can contaminate part e. Almost no student practises it enough, and almost no generalist tutor prepares for it specifically.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.description: A piece of independent mathematical writing worth twenty per cent of the grade, marked out of twenty against five criteria. Technical correctness earns six of those marks. The remaining fourteen come from presentation, communication, engagement and reflection, which is why strong mathematicians still lose them.

subjects.name: Toolkit and GDC fluency
subjects.description: The practical layer: knowing which calculator function answers which question type, and how to show working that earns method marks when the answer came from a screen. Underrated, quickly taught, and worth several marks across a paper in both AI papers and AA Paper 2.

sections.heading: Six questions that reveal whether a tutor knows the syllabus
paragraphs: Credentials do not answer the question parents are actually asking. A mathematics degree, twenty years of teaching, even a stack of good reviews, tell you nothing about whether this person has taught Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level to an examination. The fastest way to find out is to ask six specific things, in any order, and listen for whether the answers arrive immediately or get assembled. A tutor who teaches the course answers all six without pausing.

Ask which paper is sat without a calculator and in which courses. Ask what Paper 3 is, who sits it and what it is worth. Ask how many marks criterion E of the exploration carries and what it is called. Ask what the difference is between AA and AI in the statistics content. Ask what changes between Standard and Higher Level in calculus. Ask what a student most commonly loses marks for in Paper 2 despite getting the right answer.

The last one is the most revealing. A tutor who has marked these papers will say something about unsupported calculator output, or about answers given to the wrong accuracy, or about a correct final value with no visible method. A tutor who has not will talk about carelessness. Put the same six questions to us. Publishing them is only worth anything if we expect to be tested with them, and a family who asks them of three providers will have a clear ranking inside half an hour.

sections.heading: AA or AI: the choice that decides everything afterwards
paragraphs: The course decision is made in Year 11 or at the start of Year 12, often on incomplete information, and it is the decision tutoring can least easily undo. Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic route, with proof and heavy calculus, and it is the course most engineering, mathematics, physics and economics degrees expect. Applications and Interpretation is the modelling route, with regression, statistics and real data, and Higher Level adds matrices and graph theory that AA never touches.

Two misconceptions drive most of the bad choices. The first is that AI is the easy option. AI SL is less algebraically demanding than AA SL, but AI HL is a serious course with a substantial statistics and modelling load, and students who picked it as an escape route find that out in Year 13. The second is that the course can be swapped freely. Schools in the Khalifa City corridor will usually allow a move from Higher to Standard within the same route, and are far more reluctant about moving between AA and AI once teaching has started.

The practical test is to work backwards from the degree, not forwards from the student's current confidence. Check the published entry requirements of three or four target universities, including those in the UAE, and see which route and level they name. Where a requirement says Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, no amount of strong AI performance substitutes. Where it accepts either, the choice becomes a question of which paper style suits the student, which is a far lower-stakes decision.

sections.heading: What each paper is worth, and where the marks leak
paragraphs: Assessment weightings are published and almost nobody plans around them. At Standard Level both papers carry forty per cent each and the exploration twenty. At Higher Level the two long papers carry thirty per cent each, Paper 3 carries twenty, and the exploration twenty. That arithmetic has a direct consequence: a Higher Level student who ignores Paper 3 has written off a fifth of the grade, and a student who treats the exploration as a side project has written off another fifth before the examinations start.

Paper 1 losses have a recognisable shape. In AA, it is the no-calculator paper, so errors cluster in algebraic manipulation done under time pressure, in surd and exact-value work, and in abandoning a question that needed one more line of rearrangement. In AI, Paper 1 is short structured questions across the whole syllabus, and the losses come from answers reported without the working that earns method marks, or from rounding before the final step.

Paper 2 is where capable students lose the most unnecessary marks. The calculator is available, the answer is often correct, and the credit is still withheld because the examiner cannot see a method. Writing down the equation being solved before producing a screen value takes four seconds and protects several marks across a paper. Paper 3, at Higher Level, fails differently: the questions build, so an unnoticed slip early contaminates everything after it, and the skill being tested is partly the discipline of checking before moving on.

sections.heading: The exploration, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: The exploration is marked out of twenty against five criteria, and the mark allocation explains why strong mathematicians underperform on it. Criterion A, presentation, carries four marks. Criterion B, mathematical communication, carries four. Criterion C, personal engagement, carries three. Criterion D, reflection, carries three. Criterion E, use of mathematics, carries six. Only criterion E is about the mathematics being right. The other fourteen marks are about how the piece is built, explained, owned and interrogated.

Most lost marks are avoidable and predictable. Criterion A goes when the piece has no clear aim, wanders between topics or carries a structure the reader has to reconstruct. Criterion B goes when notation is inconsistent, when graphs arrive unlabelled, or when the student uses the calculator's syntax instead of mathematical notation. Criterion C goes when the topic could have been written by anybody. Criterion D goes when reflection is decorative, appearing once at the end as a paragraph saying the work was interesting.

What a tutor may do here is bounded, and the boundary is not a formality. Teaching what each criterion credits, stress-testing whether a topic can carry enough mathematics, questioning a method until the student finds its weakness, and marking a draft against the descriptors are all legitimate and all useful. Writing any part of the exploration is not, at any price. One provider in this search market advertises completed Internal Assessments for sale; that is academic malpractice under IB rules, and the student carries the consequence.

sections.heading: The honest answer about who is available
paragraphs: Every provider in this market implies unlimited supply. None of the competitor pages studied for this search discloses a coverage limit, and several route UAE parents to a foreign phone number without mentioning where the teaching happens. The honest position is more useful. Mainstream requests in Khalifa City staff quickly: AA SL, AI SL and AI HL are matched and trialled within a few days. AA HL is tighter, and AA HL combined with a specific exploration deadline in the same month is tighter still.

Where a specialist is not in the UAE, that is said before the trial rather than discovered afterwards, and the session is timed to Gulf Standard Time so it fits a Khalifa City evening rather than someone else's working day. Where nothing suitable is free, the choices are a short wait for the right person, a narrower piece of work with a different tutor while the specialist frees up, or a referral elsewhere. A fast general match is the one option that reliably wastes money, because the first four sessions get repeated later.

Availability also moves with the calendar. The weeks before the May session and the weeks around internal exploration deadlines are the tightest in the year, and the corridor's Diploma cohorts all hit them simultaneously. Booking a specialist a term ahead costs the same as booking one in the week of the mock results and gets a different person. That is the most practical scheduling advice on this page, and it applies whoever you end up using.

sections.heading: From MYP or IGCSE into Diploma mathematics
paragraphs: Khalifa City students arrive in Year 12 from two very different places, and the gap is specific enough to plan for. From MYP, the strengths are investigation, communication and willingness to reason about unfamiliar problems; the weakness is algebraic fluency, because MYP credits mathematical reasoning more than fast, accurate manipulation. From Cambridge 0580 Extended or Edexcel 4MA1 Higher, the strengths are exactly reversed: solid procedures, little experience of extended open investigation, and no exposure to anything resembling the exploration.

Both gaps are closable, and both close fastest in the summer before Year 12 rather than in the autumn after it. For MYP students the work is manipulation drill: indices, surds, rearrangement, algebraic fractions, and the trigonometric identities AA assumes from the first week. For IGCSE students it is early calculus, sequences and series, and a first attempt at a piece of open-ended mathematical writing so the exploration is not their first encounter with the genre.

Students who completed Additional Mathematics 0606 arrive with most of the AA entry gap already closed, which is the strongest reason to take it in Year 11 if the school offers it. Students who sat Core tier rather than Extended need honest advice rather than encouragement: AA SL is a stretch from Core, and AI SL is the more realistic route. That conversation is better had in Year 11 with a tutor who will say it than in Year 13 with a school that cannot change the entry.

sections.heading: What a Khalifa City week can actually hold
paragraphs: Scheduling kills more tutoring plans than teaching quality does. A Diploma student in Khalifa City is typically out of the house by 07:00, back between 15:10 and 16:00 depending on the school, and then carrying three to four hours of work across six subjects plus CAS commitments. Adding two mathematics sessions a week to that sounds decisive and usually produces two tired hours that achieve less than one alert one. Frequency has to be set against what the week genuinely has room for.

The pattern that holds across a full Diploma year is one fixed weekly hour, at a time that survives a bad week rather than a good one, with density added in two short bursts: the run-up to internal exploration deadlines, and the eight to ten weeks before the session. Online delivery makes both bursts easier, because there is no journey to negotiate and a cancelled slot can move to the following evening without anybody rearranging a drive across the emirate.

Two Abu Dhabi specifics are worth building in. Ramadan shifts household rhythms substantially, and a session that worked at 17:00 may work better after Iftar, which is a conversation to have before the month rather than during it. School examination weeks are better used for short technique reviews than for new content. Both of those are easy adjustments when nobody is driving anywhere, and they are the practical reason the format matters as much as the tutor.
