process.title: Name the course and the level
process.description: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, or Applications and Interpretation at Standard, and the Khalifa City school. Those words determine which tutors are candidates at all. The single most common cause of a wasted first month is a tutor teaching the right mathematics in the wrong course's style.

process.title: Send the marked script
process.description: The most recent marked mathematics paper, with the examiner or teacher annotations intact. It shows whether marks were lost to content, to method not shown, or to timing, and those three problems have three different remedies. A conversation cannot distinguish between them.

process.title: Take the free trial hour
process.description: One hour over live video, no card details, no commitment. The tutor works a problem your child is currently stuck on, on a shared whiteboard. You are testing whether the explanation lands and whether the syllabus knowledge is real.

process.title: Set the weekly slot and the bursts
process.description: One reliable hour a week, plus planned density before the internal exploration deadline and before the session. Agree the Ramadan arrangement at the same time rather than renegotiating it later, and agree what happens to the slot during school examination weeks.

process.title: Review against the paper
process.description: After four sessions, compare performance on the paper type that started the plan. If the lost marks are not coming back, the diagnosis was wrong and the plan changes. That review is included rather than something you have to ask for.

whyPoints.title: Matched by course, not by subject
whyPoints.description: A tutor is proposed for AA HL or AI SL specifically, because the four DP mathematics courses share a name and diverge in content, calculator access and paper structure. Matching on the word mathematics is how families end up practising the right topics in the wrong format.

whyPoints.title: Paper 3 is treated as a real component
whyPoints.description: Twenty per cent of the Higher Level grade sits in one hour of sustained multi-part reasoning that most students meet for the first time in the examination. It gets its own sessions, in longer slots, worked from past investigations rather than from general revision.

whyPoints.title: Exploration marks are chased where they actually are
whyPoints.description: Fourteen of the exploration's twenty marks sit outside technical correctness. Coaching starts from criteria A to E and their mark allocations, so the work goes into presentation, communication, engagement and reflection rather than only into the mathematics.

whyPoints.title: A boundary stated before you ask
whyPoints.description: No part of an exploration is drafted, written or edited to submission by a tutor. Criteria are taught, topics are stress-tested, drafts are marked against descriptors. The work stays the student's own, which is the condition on which the mark stands.

whyPoints.title: Availability disclosed in advance
whyPoints.description: Match times differ by course, and AA Higher Level is the tightest in this corridor. You are told that before the trial, along with where the tutor is based, rather than being given a general match and discovering the gap in session four.

whyPoints.title: Scheduled to Gulf Standard Time
whyPoints.description: Sessions are timed to a Khalifa City evening, with 16:00 starts for households with a short school run and 20:30 starts for those with a long commute. Ramadan timing is planned before the month rather than improvised during it.

faqs.question: How do I know an IB maths tutor in Khalifa City really knows the course?
faqs.answer: Ask six specific questions and listen for hesitation. Which paper is sat without a calculator, and in which courses? What is Paper 3, who sits it, and what is it worth? What is criterion E of the exploration called and how many marks does it carry? Where does AI statistics go beyond AA? What does Higher Level add to calculus? What loses marks in Paper 2 even when the answer is right? Somebody who teaches the course answers all six immediately. Somebody who knows mathematics but not the syllabus assembles answers as they go.

faqs.question: Which route should a Khalifa City student pick, AA or AI?
faqs.answer: At Standard Level, AA is more algebraically demanding, largely because Paper 1 is sat without a calculator. At Higher Level the comparison breaks down: AA HL is heavy on proof, calculus and vectors, while AI HL carries a serious statistics, matrices and graph theory load that students who chose it as an easier option find difficult in Year 13. The useful question is not which is harder but which your target degrees name. Check the published entry requirements for three or four universities before treating the choice as a difficulty decision.

faqs.question: Can my child switch from AA Higher to Standard Level partway through?
faqs.answer: Within the same route, schools in the Khalifa City corridor usually allow a move from Higher to Standard Level, most often at the end of the first Diploma year, though the decision belongs to the school and depends on timetabling. Moving between AA and AI after teaching has begun is much harder, because the courses diverge in content rather than depth. If a change is being considered, raise it with the coordinator early in the first year; the same conversation in Year 13 rarely has a good outcome.

faqs.question: How many exploration marks sit outside the mathematics itself?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent, in all four courses, marked out of twenty across five criteria. Criterion A presentation carries four marks, B mathematical communication four, C personal engagement three, D reflection three, and E use of mathematics six. Only criterion E rewards the mathematics being correct, so fourteen of the twenty marks depend on how the work is structured, explained, owned and interrogated. That is why students who are strong in class still lose marks here, and why reading the criteria is the highest-value hour in the whole project.

faqs.question: Where exactly must a tutor stop on my child's maths exploration?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor may teach what each criterion credits, stress-test whether a topic can carry mathematics at the right level, question a method until the student finds its weakness, mark drafts against the descriptors, and check referencing. A tutor may not draft, write or edit any part of the submission. One provider advertising in this market sells completed Internal Assessments; that is malpractice under IB rules and the student bears the consequence, not the seller. Ask any provider directly what they will refuse to do.

faqs.question: What is Paper 3 and why do Higher Level students underperform on it?
faqs.answer: Paper 3 is sat only by Higher Level candidates: two long structured investigations in one hour, worth twenty per cent of the final grade. Students underperform because the skill is unfamiliar. The parts build on each other, so an early slip contaminates later answers, and nothing in the rest of the course demands sustained reasoning across a single problem for thirty minutes. It is trainable, but it needs its own practice on past investigations in a longer session, not general revision in the week before the examinations.

faqs.question: My child gets the right answers in Paper 2 but loses marks. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the method is invisible. Paper 2 permits the calculator, so a student solves an equation on the screen and writes the answer. The examiner can award the answer mark and nothing else, and on a multi-part question the method marks are often the larger share. Writing down the equation being solved, or the integral being evaluated, before producing the value takes a few seconds and protects several marks across the paper. Premature rounding is the second cause: round once, at the end, to the accuracy the question asks for.

faqs.question: Which IB maths course do UAE universities expect?
faqs.answer: It depends on the programme, and it must be checked rather than assumed. Engineering, mathematics, physics and many economics degrees commonly name Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level. Business, design, social science and several life science programmes frequently accept either route. Read the published entry requirements on each university's own admissions pages, including the UAE institutions on your child's list, and treat a requirement that names AA Higher Level as non-negotiable, because strong AI performance does not substitute for it.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a Khalifa City Diploma student need?
faqs.answer: One reliable hour a week suits most students across the two years, with density added in two short bursts: before the school's internal exploration deadline, and in the eight to ten weeks before the session. Two sessions a week sounds more decisive and often produces two tired hours instead of one alert one, because a Diploma student is already carrying three to four hours of work a night across six subjects. Set the frequency against what the week genuinely holds, then increase it when there is something concrete to practise on.

faqs.question: Are IB maths tutors available in Khalifa City for Higher Level?
faqs.answer: In-home, the local pool for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level is thin, and it does not improve much by widening the search to Al Raha Gardens or Al Reef. Online, availability is a question of the course rather than the postcode: AI SL and AA SL are usually matched within a few days, AA HL can take a week or more, especially near exploration deadlines. Where a specialist is based outside the UAE, that is stated before the trial and the session is timed to Gulf Standard Time.

faqs.question: Does my child need a graphic display calculator for every paper?
faqs.answer: No, and the exception matters. In Analysis and Approaches, Paper 1 is sat without a calculator at both levels, which is why exact-value and manipulation work is central to AA preparation. Every Applications and Interpretation paper permits the calculator, and AA Paper 2 and Paper 3 permit it too. Knowing which functions answer which question types, and how to show working that earns method marks when the value came from a screen, is a short piece of training that pays back across every calculator paper.

faqs.question: We are moving from MYP maths into the Diploma. What should we fix first?
faqs.answer: Algebraic fluency, before anything else. MYP credits mathematical reasoning and investigation more heavily than fast, accurate manipulation, so students arrive able to think about unfamiliar problems and slow at indices, surds, rearrangement and algebraic fractions. Analysis and Approaches assumes that fluency from the first week. The summer before Year 12 is the cheapest time to close it, alongside the trigonometric identities the course uses constantly. The investigation habits MYP builds are an advantage later, particularly for the exploration and for Paper 3.

faqs.question: Is Additional Mathematics 0606 worth taking before the Diploma?
faqs.answer: If the school offers it and your child is heading for Analysis and Approaches, yes. 0606 introduces calculus and advanced algebra a year early, so students arrive in Year 12 with most of the AA entry gap already closed and spend the first term consolidating rather than catching up. It is not a requirement, and students who did not take it can close the gap in a focused summer. Taking it purely for the certificate, without a maths-heavy Diploma route in mind, is less obviously worth the Year 11 workload.

faqs.question: Will the weekly maths slot survive Ramadan in Khalifa City?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is better arranged before the month than during it. Household rhythms shift substantially, and a slot that worked at 17:00 often works better after Iftar, when students are alert and the house is settled. Because nobody is travelling to a Khalifa City address, moving a session later costs nothing and does not require anybody to redraw a route across the emirate. Agreeing the Ramadan pattern in advance also protects continuity through a month that otherwise tends to produce several cancelled weeks in a row.

faqs.question: What do you do if no AA Higher Level specialist is free?
faqs.answer: You are told, which no competitor page studied for this search does at all. The options are a short wait for the right tutor, a narrower piece of work with a second tutor in the meantime such as Paper 1 manipulation or exploration criteria coaching, or a referral elsewhere if the wait is unreasonable. A fast general match is the option that costs the most, because the first few sessions of diagnosis get repeated once the specialist becomes available, and the family pays for that work twice.

If the explanation lands, book a weekly slot that survives a bad week. If it does not, the next match costs nothing either, which is how it should work.

intro.heading: What an IB maths tutor in Madinat Zayed actually costs, and what the money buys
paragraphs: Start with the number, because that is what most parents in Madinat Zayed want before anything else. Researched in October 2026, the market for IB Mathematics tuition in Abu Dhabi runs from roughly AED 150 an hour for a graduate tutor working online, through AED 200 to AED 320 for a qualified Diploma Programme subject teacher, to AED 400 and above for a Higher Level specialist in an exam year. One agency, BartyED, publishes AED 650 an hour for its premium named tier. Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Those are the published figures of other providers, quoted so you can see the shape of the market; they are not an IB Gram price list.

The second number matters more and almost nobody shows it. An in-home visit in Abu Dhabi is quoted by Bestimate's 2026 rate table at AED 180 to 350 an hour, and independent home tutors in the emirate advertise AED 200 to 500. The premium over an online session is not a quality premium. It pays for a car, a parking search near the Madinat Zayed shopping district, and a commute that is charged to you either in money or in the tutor's flagging attention at 19:00. A family paying AED 320 for a home visit is often buying AED 220 of teaching and AED 100 of traffic.

The third number is the one that decides whether the first two were worth anything. The IB mathematics exploration is 20% of the final grade at both Standard and Higher Level. Paper 3 at Higher Level is another 20%, and it is a single hour of extended problem-solving that rewards a skill most school teaching has no time to build. A family who spends twelve weeks of tuition revising algebra, and none of it on the exploration or on Paper 3 technique, has spent money on the cheapest 60% of the grade and ignored the 40% where the marks were actually available.

That is the argument for matching on route and level before anything else. Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation are different courses with different papers, different calculator rules and different university consequences, and a tutor who is fluent in one is not automatically useful in the other. Madinat Zayed sits close enough to the Corniche, Al Bateen and the island's older school corridor that a family here has a reasonable choice of in-home candidates — but the choice is drawn from whoever happens to be free and within driving distance, which is a very different pool from every Diploma Programme maths specialist available at 17:00 Gulf Standard Time.

IB Gram delivers IB maths tuition to Madinat Zayed as one-to-one lessons over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. What that removes is travel cost and travel risk. What it adds is a tutor chosen for your child's route, level and weakest paper — a Higher Level Analysis and Approaches specialist who has taught Paper 3 to a dozen cohorts, rather than a competent generalist whose car can reach your building by five.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-madinat-zaye.programmesIntro: Madinat Zayed families sit across three IB programmes, and the cost conversation is different in each. Below is what each programme asks of a maths student, and what tuition at that stage is realistically for.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Maths in the PYP is taught inside transdisciplinary units rather than as a standalone subject with a textbook sequence. There is no external examination, and no mark that follows the child. What does follow them is number fluency, and that is where tuition at this stage earns its keep: place value, the four operations without a calculator, fractions as quantities rather than as notation, and the habit of writing a method down. A PYP student who leaves Year 6 slow at arithmetic will be slow in MYP algebra.
programmes.countryNote: Across Abu Dhabi, private schools licensed by ADEK run the PYP alongside the mandatory UAE subjects — Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies — which take real curriculum time out of the week. For a Madinat Zayed family, that is the honest reason a Year 5 maths gap is common and not a sign of anything wrong: the timetable is genuinely fuller than a UK or Indian equivalent. Tuition at PYP level is usually one 45-minute session a week, and the market rate is the lowest band on the page.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP mathematics is assessed against four criteria — knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts — each marked out of eight. Most students lose marks in investigating patterns and communicating rather than in knowing and understanding, because both reward written reasoning rather than a correct final answer. Years 9 to 11 also split into standard and extended mathematics, and that split is the first real decision about whether Higher Level is available later.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi the MYP-to-DP transition is where most tuition spending in this area actually begins, and it often begins a year late. A Madinat Zayed student in MYP Year 11 extended mathematics who is comfortable with functions and sequences has a realistic path to Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. One who has never been required to show an algebraic argument in writing will meet that requirement for the first time in DP1, in a class of twenty, with an exploration deadline already on the wall.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: DP mathematics splits into Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, each available at Standard and Higher Level — four distinct courses. Standard Level sits two papers of 90 minutes, each worth 40%, plus the exploration at 20%. Higher Level sits two papers of 120 minutes at 30% each, Paper 3 of 60 minutes at 20%, and the exploration at 20%. Analysis and Approaches Paper 1 is sat without a graphic display calculator; every other paper in either route allows one.
programmes.countryNote: For a Madinat Zayed family this is where the money concentrates, and where it is most often misallocated. UAE and international universities increasingly specify the route rather than just the subject: engineering and most economics programmes expect Analysis and Approaches, frequently at Higher Level, while Applications and Interpretation suits design, business and some life-science pathways. Switching route in DP1 is possible but costly in time, and the decision is easier to make well in MYP Year 11 than to repair in Year 12.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme pairs DP courses with a career-related study and a reflective project. Where a CP student takes a DP mathematics course, the assessment is identical to the Diploma version — same papers, same exploration, same weightings. What differs is the surrounding load, which is lighter on breadth and heavier on applied work, so a CP maths student often has more capacity for sustained exploration work than a full Diploma candidate juggling six subjects.
programmes.countryNote: The CP is offered by a small number of Abu Dhabi schools rather than most of them, so a Madinat Zayed family considering it should confirm availability directly with the school before planning around it. For tuition purposes the practical point is that CP maths costs the same per hour as DP maths, because it is the same course; any provider quoting it as a cheaper tier is pricing on the programme label rather than on the paper your child sits.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-madinat-zaye.subjectsIntro: Maths is the page, but almost no Madinat Zayed family buys one subject in isolation. These are the IB courses most often added alongside DP mathematics, with the specific place each one leaks marks.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebraic route. Proof, calculus and functions carry the weight, and Paper 1 is sat without a graphic display calculator, which exposes any student who has been leaning on one. Higher Level adds Paper 3, an hour of extended, scaffolded investigation worth 20%, where marks are lost to abandoned working rather than to wrong answers.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The modelling route. Statistics, regression, financial mathematics and graph theory at Higher Level, with calculator use permitted throughout. Students underestimate it: the arithmetic is lighter but the interpretation is heavier, and marks go missing where a correct calculation is reported without saying what it means in context.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The subject most tightly coupled to maths ability. A student weak on rearranging equations and on logarithmic scales will read as weak at physics when the problem is algebraic. Paper 2 extended response and the internal assessment both reward uncertainty handling, which is where Abu Dhabi cohorts most often lose a grade.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mole calculations, equilibrium constants and energetics are arithmetic problems wearing chemistry clothing. Organic mechanisms are the other common wall. The internal assessment is marked on a genuine research question and on error analysis, not on a tidy write-up of a recipe the class already performed.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three internal assessment commentaries built on recent news articles, each capped at 800 words. Higher Level adds a quantitative paper that frightens students who chose economics to avoid maths. Diagram accuracy — correctly labelled axes, shifts drawn rather than described — is a reliable source of recoverable marks.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume is the problem, not difficulty. Students who revise by rereading plateau early; those who answer past-paper questions under time improve faster. Statistical treatment of data in the internal assessment is where the mark is made or lost, which brings maths back into a subject chosen to avoid it.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Paper 1 and Paper 2 reward precise pseudocode and a working grasp of data structures. The solution development on the internal assessment must be the student's own, documented against criteria, and tutoring here is code review and design questioning rather than any form of co-authoring.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen textual analysis and it is where unprepared candidates drop a grade. The individual oral requires a global issue traced across one literary and one non-literary extract, prepared in advance and delivered without a script, which is a rehearsal problem as much as a writing one.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: An exhibition of three objects against one of thirty-five prescribed prompts, plus a 1,600-word essay on a prescribed title. The common failure is description where the rubric wants knowledge questions. Support is Socratic questioning about the student's own chosen objects and claims.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: A 4,000-word independent piece in a chosen subject, with a supervisor at school and a reflection record. A maths extended essay needs a question narrow enough to answer and broad enough to sustain. Outside support means teaching method and asking hard questions, never drafting the text.

sections.heading: What an hour of IB maths tuition costs in Abu Dhabi, and who publishes what
paragraphs: An IB maths tutor working online with an Abu Dhabi family sits in a market band of roughly AED 200 to AED 400 an hour for Diploma Programme work, as researched across published provider pages in October 2026. Below that, AED 45 to AED 150 buys a university-student or graduate tutor; EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Above it, AED 500 to 650 buys a premium named tier, of which BartyED's published AED 650 is the clearest example. The middle band is where almost every DP family ends up, and it is the band where the difference between providers is hardest to see from the outside.

In-home rates are structurally higher and the reason is mechanical rather than qualitative. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai and Abu Dhabi rate table puts home visits at AED 180 to 350 an hour, and independent home tutors advertise AED 200 to 500. A tutor who spends 50 minutes driving to Madinat Zayed and 50 minutes driving back has committed nearly three hours to deliver one, and that arithmetic is priced in whether or not anyone itemises it. Monthly packages seen in this market run around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits.

What none of those figures tells you is the thing worth paying for. A rate is an input. The output is whether the hour was spent on the component carrying the marks. Bestimate's monthly estimates for one weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000-plus for specialist exam-year support. A family at the top of that range who never opens a Paper 3 past paper has bought the expensive version of the wrong lesson, and a family at the bottom who drills Paper 3 weekly from January onward has not.

IB Gram does not publish a rate card on this page, and that is deliberate rather than coy. The sensible first step is a free trial lesson with a matched tutor, after which a figure for your child's route, level and session length means something. sections.heading: Five ways Madinat Zayed families waste money on maths tuition
paragraphs: The first is buying hours before buying a diagnosis. A tutor who starts teaching in session one, without having watched the student attempt a past paper under time, is teaching the syllabus rather than the student. Six weeks later the family has paid for twelve hours of competent coverage and the original gap — usually algebraic manipulation, occasionally a misread of function notation — is still there, because nobody looked for it. A diagnostic costs one session and saves five.

The second is paying a Higher Level rate for Standard Level teaching, or the reverse. These are different courses with different papers, and the difference is not a matter of difficulty dialled up. A Standard Level Applications and Interpretation student being taught by a Higher Level Analysis and Approaches specialist will be walked through proof technique they will never be examined on, while the regression and financial mathematics that will appear on their papers goes untouched. The hourly rate was fine. The match was not.

The third is spending the exploration window on revision. The mathematics exploration is 20% of the final grade, it is marked against published criteria including mathematical presentation and personal engagement, and it is the only part of the grade a student can work on calmly months ahead of any exam. Families routinely spend DP1 on topic revision and then discover the exploration in DP2 with six weeks to go. The marks were there for the taking and the clock took them.

The fourth is the cross-area in-home booking. A tutor who lives in Khalifa City and takes a 16:30 slot in Madinat Zayed will arrive late, leave early, or both, and will do it increasingly often as the term wears on. Nothing about that is dishonest; it is simply what the Abu Dhabi afternoon does to a schedule. The fifth is buying a single long session instead of two shorter ones. Mathematics is a practice subject, and two 45-minute sessions with homework between them beats one two-hour block almost every time, at the same cost.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation: the route decision that changes the bill
paragraphs: Route choice is the single largest determinant of what maths tuition will cost a Madinat Zayed family across two years, and it is usually made on a Thursday in Year 11 with very little information. Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic course: proof, calculus, functions, and a Paper 1 sat with no graphic display calculator. Applications and Interpretation is the modelling course: statistics, regression, financial mathematics, and at Higher Level graph theory and matrices, with calculator access on every paper.

The difficulty comparison parents expect does not survive contact with the courses. Analysis and Approaches demands more algebraic fluency, and the no-calculator paper punishes any student who has been quietly outsourcing arithmetic to a device since Year 8. Applications and Interpretation demands more interpretation: a correct statistical calculation reported without an explanation of what it means in the context of the data earns part of the available mark and no more. Students who choose Applications and Interpretation to escape difficulty tend to find it harder to score well, because the examiner is marking reasoning in prose.

University expectations are the part that actually drives the decision, and they are getting more specific rather than less. Engineering, physics, mathematics and most economics programmes in the UAE, the UK and North America expect Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level. Design, business, psychology and several life-science routes accept or prefer Applications and Interpretation. A student who takes Applications and Interpretation and then applies to engineering has a conversation with an admissions office that no amount of tuition fixes afterwards.

Practically, the tuition consequence is this: route first, level second, tutor third. A family that gets the order wrong pays twice — once for the mismatched teaching and again for the catch-up when the mismatch surfaces. Confirm which course your child's school actually offers at which level, because not every Abu Dhabi school runs all four combinations, and a school that runs Analysis and Approaches Standard Level but not Higher Level has already narrowed the decision for you.

sections.heading: The assessment structure you are paying to improve
paragraphs: Before buying a single hour, know where the marks are. At Standard Level, both routes sit two papers of 90 minutes, each worth 40% of the final grade, plus the mathematical exploration at 20%. At Higher Level, both routes sit two papers of 120 minutes at 30% each, a third paper of 60 minutes at 20%, and the exploration at 20%. There is no coursework beyond the exploration, and no component that can be dropped.

The weighting pattern has a direct consequence for how tuition money should be spent. At Higher Level, Paper 3 and the exploration together carry 40% of the grade, and both are the components school teaching has the least time for. Paper 3 is a single extended investigation across one or two contexts, scaffolded in parts, and it rewards a student who keeps writing when they are unsure — because the later parts carry method marks that are reachable even when the earlier answer went wrong. Most students stop. That is a trainable habit and it is worth more per hour than another pass through differentiation.

The exploration is marked against five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection, and the use of mathematics. The last of these is where the grade separates, and it rewards mathematics that is appropriate to the level and correctly deployed rather than mathematics that looks impressive. A Higher Level exploration built on Standard Level content is capped by the criteria no matter how neatly it is written. Equally, a borrowed advanced technique the student cannot explain reads immediately as borrowed.

Paper 1 and Paper 2 reward different things and are often revised as though they reward the same thing. For Analysis and Approaches, Paper 1 is the no-calculator paper, so exact values, surds, algebraic manipulation and trigonometric identities have to be secure in hand. Paper 2 allows the graphic display calculator and asks questions designed around it, which means the examinable skill is partly knowing which calculator function answers the question and reading the output correctly. Practising only one of those two modes leaves a predictable hole in the result.

sections.heading: Where Abu Dhabi students actually lose marks in IB Maths
paragraphs: Algebraic fragility is the first and largest. A student who is slow or unreliable at rearranging an equation, handling indices or clearing a fraction will appear to be failing at calculus, when the calculus is fine and the algebra underneath it is not. This is diagnosable in one session with three questions and it is the single most common finding across Abu Dhabi cohorts. It is also the cheapest thing on this list to fix, which is why a diagnostic before a package matters so much.

Second is calculator dependence meeting Analysis and Approaches Paper 1. Students who have had a graphic display calculator in hand since MYP arrive in DP1 unable to evaluate a trigonometric value exactly, simplify a surd, or sketch a cubic from its factorised form. The paper is specifically designed to find that out. Rebuilding by-hand fluency takes about eight weeks of short weekly practice and it cannot be done in the fortnight before a mock.

Third is unexplained method. The IB mark scheme awards method marks generously and students throw them away by writing only answers. A line of working that shows which rule was applied earns marks even when the arithmetic that follows is wrong. Training a student to narrate their working on paper is partly a maths intervention and partly a behavioural one, and it shows up in a mock result faster than almost anything else a tutor can do.

Fourth is the exploration treated as an essay. Students who are strong at written subjects produce a beautifully presented exploration with no mathematical depth and are surprised by the mark. Fifth is context-free statistics in Applications and Interpretation: the regression is computed, the correlation coefficient is quoted, and nothing is said about what either means for the data in question. Sixth, and specific to Abu Dhabi timetables, is a thin November and December caused by the mandatory UAE subject load competing with DP coursework deadlines in the same weeks.

sections.heading: Online maths tuition versus an in-home tutor in Madinat Zayed: the arithmetic
paragraphs: Set the two options side by side honestly. An in-home maths tutor in Madinat Zayed has one real advantage: physical presence, which some younger students genuinely respond to and which makes a parent's oversight easier. Against that sit a higher rate, a tutor pool limited to whoever can reach your building in an afternoon, a schedule exposed to the island's traffic, and no recording of the session afterwards. Market quotes for in-home work in the emirate run AED 180 to 500 an hour, against roughly AED 200 to 400 online for comparable Diploma Programme experience.

The pool argument is the one that decides it for most Diploma families. Madinat Zayed is well placed for in-home tutoring by Abu Dhabi standards, with the Corniche, Al Bateen and the central grid all close. Even so, the set of maths tutors who can physically reach a given building between 16:00 and 19:00 on a Tuesday is small, and the subset of those who have taught Higher Level Analysis and Approaches Paper 3 to multiple cohorts is smaller again. Online, the constraint disappears: the match is made on route, level and component experience, and Gulf Standard Time is the only scheduling variable left.

Mathematics also happens to be the subject where the online format gives up the least. A shared digital whiteboard shows a student's working line by line as they produce it, which is exactly what a maths tutor needs to see, and screen-shared past papers can be annotated by both parties at once. The session recording means a method can be revisited at 21:00 rather than re-asked next week. For a practical subject with apparatus this would be a real compromise; for algebra on a whiteboard it is not.

IB Gram delivers to Madinat Zayed online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not provide home visits in the UAE — that service exists only in India — and no page here will promise otherwise. sections.heading: The IB maths year counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: UAE Diploma Programme students sit the May examination session, and schools in Abu Dhabi plan the whole two years around it. The IB publishes the exact window and the results dates each cycle, and those should be confirmed with your child's Diploma Programme coordinator rather than taken from any tutoring website, including this one. What can be planned without a date is the sequence, and the sequence is where most families lose time.

Counting backwards from the examination window, the last eight weeks belong to timed papers under examination conditions, marked against the real mark scheme. Before that sits the mock window, usually in the second half of DP2, which is the most useful diagnostic a family will ever get for free. Before that, the exploration must be finished and submitted to the school's internal deadline, which almost always falls earlier than students expect and earlier than the IB's own upload deadline for the school.

The implication for tuition spending is that the useful work happens early and the expensive work happens late. An exploration supported properly in DP1, when there is no time pressure, costs a handful of sessions. The same exploration rescued six weeks before a school deadline costs twice as much and scores less, because the mathematics has to be whatever the student can learn quickly rather than whatever suits the question. Paper 3 drilling at Higher Level works the same way: started in January of DP2 it is a weekly habit, started in April it is a scramble.

For students sitting Cambridge IGCSE maths before the Diploma, the parallel calendar is worth knowing: Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for UAE candidates, and the February/March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Entry deadlines sit months before the papers, which is why a family that decides in April to enter a private candidate for a summer paper has usually already missed the window.

sections.heading: Academic honesty and the mathematics exploration: what a tutor may and may not do
paragraphs: This is the boundary that matters most and the one the UAE market is worst at respecting. The mathematical exploration is 20% of your child's grade and it must be their own work. One provider found in the research for this page sells completed Internal Assessments outright at AED 3,750. That is an academic-integrity breach, it triggers the IB's malpractice procedures, and the consequence falls on the student rather than on the seller. A family offered that should walk away from the provider entirely.

What a tutor may legitimately do is substantial. They may teach the mathematics the exploration needs. They may interrogate the research question until it is answerable at the right level. They may ask why a method was chosen and whether the assumptions hold. They may read the student's own draft and give feedback against each published criterion. They may point at a section and say that the reflection is thin or the notation inconsistent. All of that is teaching, and all of it is recorded as support in the normal way.

What a tutor may not do is write, redraft to completion, supply the mathematics for the student to transcribe, or produce any portion of the text. The line is not about how much help was given; it is about whose work the submitted document is. The practical test is simple and worth applying at home: if your child cannot explain, unprompted, why each step of their exploration is there, then the exploration is not theirs and the mark is not safe. That test costs nothing and it is the best quality check a parent has.

The same boundary applies to the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay and every other assessed component. IB Gram's tutors give feedback on work the student has written and teach the content the student needs. They do not produce assessed work, and no page on this site offers to. Nor will any tutor supply IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes as downloads — those are the boards' copyright, and the correct route is the official site or the school.

sections.heading: ADEK, Madinat Zayed schools and what a school report is actually telling you
paragraphs: Private schools in Abu Dhabi, including those serving Madinat Zayed, are licensed and inspected by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. That is a different authority from Dubai's Knowledge and Human Development Authority, from Sharjah's Private Education Authority, and from the federal Ministry of Education that supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. A tutoring page that treats the UAE as one regulatory space is not describing your child's school.

Inspection bands are published per school and they describe a whole institution, not a department. A school rated strongly overall can still be short of specialist Higher Level maths teaching in a particular year, usually because one experienced teacher left and the timetable absorbed the gap. That is the most common real reason a Madinat Zayed family starts looking for an IB maths tutor, and it is worth naming because it changes what you should ask for: not general maths support, but cover for the specific route and level the school is thin in.

A school report tells you less than parents assume. A grade on a report is a teacher's prediction against a cohort, converted through internal assessment that may or may not have been sat under examination conditions. A mock sat under real timing and marked against the published scheme tells you considerably more, and it is free. Before buying tuition, ask the school for the mock paper breakdown by component — Paper 1 against Paper 2 — because a student strong on Paper 2 and weak on Paper 1 has a calculator-dependence problem, and that is a different intervention from a content gap.

On credentials, there is a rule worth knowing in Abu Dhabi specifically. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and a tutor working privately needs the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. That permit is granted free of charge for two years. IB Gram holds no regulator accreditation of any kind, claims none, and is not approved or endorsed by ADEK, the Ministry of Education or the IB.

If Paper 1 has not moved in twelve weeks, the plan is wrong and should change. This review is also when a family decides whether to keep paying, which is as it should be.

process.description: Exploration support belongs in DP1 and early DP2, while there is time for the mathematics to be chosen rather than scrambled. whyPoints.title: A diagnostic before a package, every time
whyPoints.description: The first session finds the gap. Algebraic fragility, calculator dependence and missing method lines account for most of what looks like difficulty with calculus in Abu Dhabi cohorts, and all three are visible in three questions. Selling twelve hours before anyone has looked is how families overspend.

faqs.question: How much does an IB maths tutor in Madinat Zayed cost per hour?
faqs.answer: Researched in October 2026, the market for Diploma Programme maths tuition online in Abu Dhabi runs about AED 200 to AED 400 an hour, with AED 45 to 150 buying a graduate or university-student tutor and AED 500 to 650 buying a premium named tier — BartyED publishes AED 650. In-home visits are quoted higher: Bestimate's rate table puts them at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors advertise AED 200 to 500. Those are other providers' published figures, not an IB Gram price list. We quote after a free trial lesson, once the route, level and session length are known.

faqs.question: Is an in-home maths tutor in Madinat Zayed worth the extra money?
faqs.answer: It depends on the age of the student. For a younger child who needs an adult physically present, the premium can be justified. For a Diploma Programme candidate it usually is not, because the extra AED 100 or so an hour pays for a car and a parking search rather than for better teaching, and it narrows the tutor pool to whoever can reach your building between 16:00 and 19:00. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE in any case — that service runs only in India — so lessons here are one-to-one over live video, and the fee buys teaching time rather than travel time.

faqs.question: AA or AI — which maths route should a Madinat Zayed student choose?
faqs.answer: Work backwards from the degree. Engineering, physics, mathematics and most economics programmes expect Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level; business, design, psychology and several life-science routes accept or prefer Applications and Interpretation. Then check fit: Analysis and Approaches rewards algebraic fluency and includes a no-calculator Paper 1, while Applications and Interpretation rewards written interpretation of data and allows a calculator throughout. Students who pick Applications and Interpretation to avoid difficulty often score less well, because the marks sit in explanation rather than calculation. Confirm which combinations your child's Abu Dhabi school actually runs before deciding.

faqs.question: What is Paper 3 and why does it need separate tutoring at Higher Level?
faqs.answer: Paper 3 is sat only by Higher Level candidates. It is one hour, worth 20% of the final grade, and consists of extended scaffolded investigation across one or two contexts rather than short independent questions. School teaching rarely has time for it, and the technique it rewards is unusual: keep writing through the later parts even after an early answer has gone wrong, because method marks remain reachable. Most students stop instead, and lose marks that were available. Drilled weekly from January of DP2 it becomes a habit; attempted for the first time in April it is a scramble.

faqs.question: Is the mathematical exploration worth spending tuition money on?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent, at both Standard and Higher Level. It is an independent investigation marked against five criteria covering presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics. The last of those is where grades separate, and it rewards mathematics appropriate to the level sat and correctly used rather than mathematics that looks impressive. A Higher Level exploration built on Standard Level content is capped by the criteria however well it is written. It is also the only part of the grade that can be worked on calmly, months before any examination, which makes it the best-value thing to support early.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the maths exploration without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the boundary is clear. A tutor may teach the mathematics the exploration needs, interrogate the research question until it is answerable at the right level, challenge the assumptions, and give feedback on the student's own draft against each published criterion. A tutor may not write any of it, redraft it to completion, or supply mathematics for the student to transcribe. One provider in this market sells completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; that is a malpractice trigger and the consequence falls on the student. The home test: can your child explain every step unprompted?

faqs.question: My child is in MYP Year 11 in Abu Dhabi — when should maths tutoring start?
faqs.answer: Before the route decision rather than after it, which in practice means during Year 11. The MYP-to-Diploma step is where Abu Dhabi families most often start spending, and it is usually a year late. A student comfortable with extended mathematics and with writing an algebraic argument has a realistic path to Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. A student who has never been required to show reasoning in writing meets that requirement for the first time in DP1, in a full class, with an exploration deadline already set. A few sessions in Year 11 cost less than a term of repair in Year 12.

faqs.question: Why is my child good at maths in class but weak in the exam?
faqs.answer: Three causes account for most of it. First, answers written without the method line that carries the marks — the IB scheme awards method generously and students throw it away. Second, calculator dependence meeting Analysis and Approaches Paper 1, where exact values, surds and by-hand sketching are required and a graphic display calculator is not allowed. Third, timing: classwork is untimed and papers are not. All three are visible in one diagnostic session using three questions, and all three respond faster to short weekly practice than to additional content teaching.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does a Diploma maths student in Madinat Zayed need?
faqs.answer: One 60 or 90-minute session a week is the normal starting point for maintenance and gap-closing. Two shorter sessions beat one long block for most students, because mathematics is a practice subject and the homework between sessions is where fluency is built. During an exploration window or a Paper 3 push at Higher Level, two or three sessions a week for six to ten weeks is common and then it drops back. A provider recommending a fixed package before anyone has watched your child work through a timed paper is guessing.

faqs.question: Which schools near Madinat Zayed offer the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Diploma provision in Abu Dhabi is spread between the central island corridor and the newer off-island communities. Within a short drive of Madinat Zayed sit schools including Abu Dhabi International School, Al Bateen Academy and the American Community School of Abu Dhabi; the Saadiyat, Al Raha and Khalifa City corridor adds Cranleigh Abu Dhabi, Raha International School, GEMS American Academy Abu Dhabi and Al Yasmina Academy. All are licensed and inspected by ADEK, and the programmes offered change between intakes. Confirm current provision with the school. IB Gram has no affiliation with any school named here.

faqs.question: Does a maths tutor working with a Madinat Zayed family need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE requires the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered at government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Operating without one exposes the tutor to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published. Ask a tutor directly whether they hold the permit, and note that ADEK ethics rules bar school staff from tutoring students enrolled at their own school.

faqs.question: Does the Cambridge February/March exam series apply to my child in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge International offers the February/March series to India only. UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series, and the November route is the usual resit path. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Entry deadlines fall months ahead of the papers, which is why a decision made in April about a summer sitting is usually already too late. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that the correct zone timetable must be used, so take dates from the school's exams officer rather than from a tutoring site.

faqs.question: Can sessions work around Abu Dhabi school hours and Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is where the online format earns its place rather than merely coping. Slots run from 16:00 Gulf Standard Time, which suits students finishing on the central island, with later options for those travelling back from Saadiyat, Yas or Khalifa City. During Ramadan sessions move to post-Iftar timing, and families travelling over the summer or between terms keep the same tutor on the same clock. A tutor driving across the island at 16:30 cannot offer that flexibility, because their schedule is set by traffic rather than by your child's day.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free for my child's exact route and level?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than fill the slot. Higher Level Analysis and Approaches with Paper 3 experience is the narrowest pool on this page, and in a busy term the honest answer is sometimes a two to three week wait for the right tutor or an interim tutor for general algebra while the specialist slot opens. Neither option is hidden, and neither is charged as though it were the match you asked for. None of the competitor pages researched for this page discloses a coverage limit at all, and several route UAE families to non-UAE phone numbers without saying where delivery happens.

faqs.question: Is online maths tutoring really as effective for an IB student as sitting in the same room?
faqs.answer: For mathematics specifically, the format gives up very little. A shared digital whiteboard shows the student's working line by line as it is produced, which is precisely what a maths tutor needs to see; past papers can be annotated by both parties at once; and the recording lets a method be revisited later rather than re-asked next week. What the format gains is the match — the tutor is chosen for route, level and weakest component rather than for proximity. For a practical subject with apparatus the trade-off would be real. For algebra on a whiteboard it is not.

intro.heading: Masdar City has plenty of mathematicians and very few IB maths teachers
paragraphs: Masdar City sits near Abu Dhabi International Airport and was built as a clean-technology and research district: a university campus at its centre, the International Renewable Energy Agency headquarters, engineering and energy firms, a pedestrian-first street plan and a residential population that is small and skews towards researchers, postgraduates and professionals. It is, statistically, one of the most mathematically literate square kilometres in the emirate.

That produces a specific false comfort. A parent here can reasonably think the problem is solved locally. There is an engineer in the next apartment, a doctoral researcher on the floor above, a lecturer two buildings over. Any of them can differentiate a composite function, and several of them will offer to help. Then the first marked paper comes back from school and the grade has not moved, because the student was never confused about the mathematics.

The reason is worth stating precisely. An IB maths grade is not awarded for getting the right answer. It is awarded against a mark scheme that pays for visible method, for a stated model before a calculator result, for conclusions phrased in the context of the question, and for a particular structure in Paper 3 investigations. A practising engineer solves the problem in three mental steps and writes the answer, which is exactly the behaviour that loses method marks. They are not wrong about the maths. They are unfamiliar with how it is paid for.

Then there is the exploration, which carries roughly a fifth of the grade and is marked on five published criteria including personal engagement and reflection. Those criteria reward things no research career trains you to produce in a school assessment, and a student handed excellent technical advice on an exploration that is scoring badly on reflection has been helped in the wrong direction.

So the honest answer to "is there an IB maths tutor in Masdar City" is that there are capable mathematicians here and a very thin supply of people who teach the IB courses and read the mark schemes. IB Gram closes that gap online. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE — that is an India-only service — and the lessons are live one-to-one video in Gulf Standard Time, with the tutor chosen for the route and level your child sits.

There is a practical point too. Masdar City has no school inside it, so every family here commutes, most often towards the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor. That corridor is close enough that an afternoon session is genuinely possible, which is not true of much of this part of the emirate, and it is worth knowing before you assume lessons have to run late.

What follows is the detail: the route decision between the two courses, what a marked script reveals that a conversation cannot, the Paper 3 structure problem at Higher Level, what makes an exploration topic workable rather than merely ambitious, what the Abu Dhabi market charges for each kind of purchase in AED, and what we do when nobody suitable is free. Read it and you will know what to ask any maths tutor here before paying for an hour.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-masdar-city.subjectsIntro: These are the parts of IB mathematics Masdar City families ask about, with where marks actually go in each. Both routes, both levels.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL
subjects.description: Algebra, functions, trigonometry, calculus and proof at depth, plus Paper 3's two extended investigations. Technically strong students lose marks here to compressed working rather than to the mathematics itself.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches SL
subjects.description: The analytical spine with less breadth across two papers. Differentiation and integration applied in context are the usual losses, along with answers presented without the steps a marker needs to see.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation HL
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics, graph theory and technology-led problem solving, with Paper 3 built on extended data tasks. The calculator is examined, and unexplained calculator output earns a fraction of the marks offered.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation SL
subjects.description: Statistics, financial maths, functions and modelling across two papers. Marks go on reporting a statistical result without interpreting it in the context the question set up.

subjects.name: The maths exploration
subjects.description: Twelve to twenty pages of independent mathematical writing, marked on presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the use of mathematics. Technically impressive explorations routinely score poorly on reflection.

subjects.name: Calculus
subjects.description: Limits, differentiation, integration, kinematics and differential equations at HL. The reliable loss is rules used in combination, and integration attempted without first naming the substitution being used.

subjects.name: Statistics and inference
subjects.description: Distributions, hypothesis testing, correlation and regression, with more advanced inference at AI HL. Marks go on choosing the right test and reporting hypotheses and conclusions in context rather than generically.

subjects.name: Proof and reasoning
subjects.description: Direct proof, contradiction, induction and counterexample. Induction is highly structured: students score nearly everything or nearly nothing, and the fix is learning the required structure rather than understanding induction better.

subjects.name: Modelling and justification
subjects.description: Fitting a model to data and defending the choice. Technology finds a model in seconds; the marks are for saying why that model and not another, which is the step confident students skip.

subjects.name: Graphic display calculator technique
subjects.description: Mode settings, commands, statistical functions, and recording enough that a correct display earns full credit. One session here routinely returns more marks than a topic re-teach, and almost nobody sells it.

sections.heading: Is there an IB maths specialist in Masdar City? The honest answer
paragraphs: No, in any meaningful sense, and the reason is structural rather than reflecting badly on the district. Masdar City was built as a research and clean-technology hub around a university campus, with a small residential population and no school inside its boundary. Teaching the IB Diploma for a living is a specific occupation, and it clusters where schools are — in the Khalifa City belt, in the island school districts, in Mohammed Bin Zayed City.

What Masdar City does have in unusual density is mathematical competence. Engineers, energy researchers, postgraduate students and lecturers, many of whom will happily help a neighbour's child with calculus and most of whom have never seen an IB mark scheme. That is a genuinely useful resource for understanding a concept and a poor one for recovering a grade, and the distinction is the single most useful thing on this page.

Apply the filter stack honestly and the arithmetic is quick. Take the residential population. Take the fraction who teach school mathematics as their job. Take the fraction of those teaching the IB Diploma rather than another curriculum. Take the fraction covering your child's route at your child's level with a free slot after the school run. Four filters on a small base returns close to zero.

Widening the search to Abu Dhabi returns a real but thin pool, mostly resident in the Khalifa City corridor and pricing their journey into any in-home rate. Widening it to an online pool returns a comfortable number of route specialists. That is the trade this page is about, and the table sets it out.

sections.heading: Knowing maths and knowing IB maths are different jobs
paragraphs: This is the section worth reading twice if you live in a research district. An IB maths mark is not paid for the right answer. It is paid against a published mark scheme, and the scheme pays separately for method, for the model that produced a calculator result, for conclusions phrased in the context the question established, and in Paper 3 for sustaining a structured argument across many parts.

A practising engineer or researcher has spent years optimising in the opposite direction. They compress steps, trust the machine, state the result and move on, because in professional work the result is the product. Transfer that habit to an IB script and the student loses method marks on almost every multi-step question while being completely correct. The help was real and it was aimed at a problem the student did not have.

The same mismatch shows on the exploration, more expensively. It is marked on five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection, and the use of mathematics. Technical advice improves the last one, which is already the strength of a student in this household. The marks are being lost on reflection — genuine commentary on what the mathematics showed and where it broke down — and on notation consistency. A researcher's instinct is to make the mathematics more impressive, which raises nothing and sometimes pushes the topic past what the student can explain.
None of this makes local help worthless. Use it for understanding and use a route specialist for the grade. They are complementary, and knowing which is which saves a term.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation
paragraphs: The route decision matters more in a household oriented towards engineering and science, because the default assumption is Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level and that assumption is sometimes wrong. AA is algebraic and proof-oriented, built on calculus and manipulation. AI is modelling and statistical, built on using technology to make sense of real data. AI at Higher Level is demanding and many students find it harder than AA at Standard Level.

Decide on two inputs. Aptitude: a student who enjoys a clean algebraic argument belongs in AA; one who reasons well about real quantities and finds abstract manipulation thankless belongs in AI. And destination: engineering, physics, mathematics and economics courses frequently specify AA at Higher Level and some will not accept AI for them. Business, social science, design and many life-science courses accept either.

University requirements vary by institution and change over time, so the only reliable action is to read the admissions pages for the specific universities on the student's list. That includes the universities in this country, which publish their own entry requirements. No tutoring page, including this one, should be the source for an admissions rule.

If the route is fixed and wrong, raise it early. A change in DP1 is a manageable piece of work. The same change in DP2 is not, and the alternative — a student grinding through two years of mathematics they dislike for a grade that does not match their ability — is a worse outcome than the switch would have been.

sections.heading: What a marked script tells you that a conversation cannot
paragraphs: The first thing we ask Masdar City families for is not a description of the problem. It is the last two marked maths assessments with the teacher's annotations. The reason is that parents and students describe maths difficulty in terms of topics, and marked scripts show something different and much more actionable: a short list of repeating, nameable behaviours.

A typical list runs to four or five items and looks nothing like a syllabus. Three steps done mentally and one line written. A calculator left in the wrong angle mode for an entire paper. A statistical conclusion stated correctly in general terms and never tied to the context of the question. A diagram not drawn on a bearings question. A model produced by technology with no sentence explaining why that model. Each of those is specific, each is fixable, and none of them is "weak at trigonometry".

This is also the fastest way to judge a tutor. Give any prospective maths tutor a marked script and an hour. A route specialist comes out of it naming the four behaviours and what each costs. A capable mathematician who does not teach the course comes out of it explaining the trigonometry, which the student already understood. You will have learned which you are buying before you commit to anything.

The free trial lesson is structured to produce exactly that output, and some families take the list, hand it to the school, and spend nothing further. That is a legitimate result and we would rather it happened than sell a term of hours against a problem nobody has named.

sections.heading: Paper 3 and the Higher Level structure problem
paragraphs: Higher Level students sit a third paper that behaves unlike anything else in the course: two long, heavily scaffolded investigations rather than a set of questions. What it examines is the ability to sustain a line of reasoning across many parts, where part (f) depends on having set up part (b) in a usable form. Topic knowledge alone does not carry it.

The failure mode is consistent and it is not about mathematics. A student answers the early parts correctly, in a compressed form that was fine for a short question, and then cannot use their own earlier work when the later parts ask them to extend it. They lose the thread around part (c) or (d) and never recover it, having been entirely capable of every individual step.

This is a structural skill and it is learned by practising whole papers under timing, with the specific discipline of writing early parts in a form the later parts can build on. Three or four complete attempts, marked properly and discussed, changes it. Doing Paper 3 questions in isolation does not, because the thing being examined is the connection between them rather than any one of them.

For Standard Level students none of this applies — there is no Paper 3 — and the time is better spent on calculator discipline and on presenting method. Knowing which of these two situations your child is in is a precondition for spending money sensibly.

sections.heading: Choosing an exploration topic that can actually score
paragraphs: Exploration topics in households like these tend to be ambitious, and ambition is the commonest cause of a poor mark. The exploration is twelve to twenty pages marked on five criteria, and the heaviest of them rewards mathematics appropriate to the level, used correctly. A topic whose mathematics is above the course is as damaging as one below it, because the student cannot explain it and reflection collapses.

The topics that score well are narrow, personal and tractable. One phenomenon, one mathematical treatment, data the student can genuinely obtain or generate, and enough depth to reach the level of the course without exceeding what the student can discuss. A topic that can be stated in a sentence and investigated in fifteen pages is a good sign. A topic that needs a paragraph of background before anyone understands the question is usually too large.

The topics that fail are recognisable too. Anything requiring university mathematics the student has not met. Anything with a data set so large the analysis becomes a software exercise. Anything where the mathematics is a decoration on a topic the student chose for interest rather than for mathematical content. And anything where the student cannot answer the question "what did the mathematics tell you that you did not know before?", because that question is the reflection criterion in plain words.

What a tutor may do here is question the topic's viability, explain what each criterion rewards, read the student's own draft and name the criterion it undersells, and teach notation and citation. What a tutor may not do is choose the topic and hand it over, write or rewrite any part of the text, edit to completion, supply data the student did not generate, or produce a model exploration for adaptation. The student signs the authenticity declaration.

sections.heading: What the market charges, and what "near me" costs
paragraphs: Published rates in this market, read in October 2026, run as follows. Budget online tutoring, typically a university student, sits at AED 45 to 150 an hour. A qualified subject tutor working online sits at AED 150 to 300. An in-home one-to-one visit sits at AED 180 to 500 with the journey inside the fee. A named IB or A-Level specialist sits at AED 200 to 450 and above, and premium examiner-led provision reaches AED 650. On a monthly basis Bestimate's 2026 estimates put mid-range weekly sessions at AED 600 to 1,200.

The interesting figure for Masdar City is the in-home premium, because of where the tutors are. A resident tutor in the Khalifa City corridor driving to Masdar City is covering a real distance on the airport road, and that journey sits inside the quoted rate. The gap between the online and in-home bands is roughly AED 30 to 200 an hour, and in this part of the emirate that gap is paying for the drive rather than for teaching.

A budget tutor in a district like this is a particular false economy. The thing the student needs is mark-scheme fluency, which is precisely what the cheapest tier does not have, and the district already supplies conceptual help for free. Paying AED 60 an hour for a university student to explain calculus to a child of engineers is the one purchase in this market with no plausible return.

sections.heading: Online into a Masdar City apartment, and the honest fallback
paragraphs: Stated plainly, since this page targets a local search: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. No tutor will travel to a Masdar City address. In-home tutoring is a service we run in India only. Lessons are live one-to-one video with a route specialist, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time.

For maths that holds up well on one condition: the tutor must see handwritten working as it happens, through a camera angled at paper or a tablet and stylus. We set that up in the first session. With it, video has real advantages — a shared whiteboard retains every derivation so last week's integration can be reopened rather than reconstructed, the exact past-paper question is pasted onto the board, and the student works on their own paper in their own handwriting, which is what the exam asks for.

On coverage, the honest position. The common routes and levels are well covered and a trial is usually arranged within a week. Narrow Higher Level combinations are thinner. If the right specialist is not free we say so before you pay, and set out the options: wait for a slot, start on the exploration with a specialist in that component, or take a tutor based outside the UAE who teaches the same syllabus and works to your evening. If a tutor is not UAE-based you are told before the trial lesson rather than after.

That disclosure matters because several providers in this market route UAE parents to numbers outside the country without saying where the teaching comes from. We would rather lose a booking than have a parent discover it in week three.
