faqs.question: Are there any IB maths tutors actually living in Masdar City?
faqs.answer: Very few, and the reason is structural. Masdar City was built as a research and clean-technology district around a university campus, with a small residential population and no school inside its boundary. People who teach the IB Diploma for a living cluster where schools are, mainly the Khalifa City corridor and the island school districts. What Masdar City has in abundance is mathematical ability — engineers, researchers, postgraduates — which is a different thing from IB teaching, and the distinction is what this page exists to make.

faqs.question: Our neighbour is an engineer. Why would we pay for a maths tutor?
faqs.answer: Because an IB maths mark is not awarded for the right answer. It is awarded against a mark scheme that pays separately for visible method, for the model behind a calculator result, and for conclusions phrased in the question's context. Professional practice trains the opposite habit: compress the steps, trust the machine, state the result. Transfer that to an IB script and the student loses method marks while being entirely correct. Use the neighbour for understanding a concept; use a route specialist when the grade is not matching the ability.

faqs.question: Why does my child understand the maths but still score badly?
faqs.answer: Almost always presentation rather than understanding. Marked scripts from conceptually strong students show the same short list: several steps done mentally with one line written, a calculator left in the wrong mode, a statistical conclusion stated generically rather than tied to the context given, a model produced by technology with no sentence justifying the choice. Each loses marks the student had earned. Two or three sessions of a tutor refusing to accept compressed working changes it, and the gain shows on the next marked paper rather than months later.

faqs.question: Is Analysis and Approaches the right default for an engineering household?
faqs.answer: Often, but not automatically. AA is algebraic and proof-oriented; Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistical, and AI at Higher Level is demanding enough that many students find it harder than AA at Standard Level. Decide on the student's aptitude and on what their intended degrees require: engineering, physics, mathematics and economics courses frequently specify AA at Higher Level, while business, social sciences and many life sciences accept either. Requirements vary by institution and change, so read the admissions pages for the universities actually on the list.

faqs.question: What makes Paper 3 at Higher Level different from the other two papers?
faqs.answer: It is two long, heavily scaffolded investigations rather than a set of questions, and it examines the ability to sustain reasoning across many parts, where a later part depends on having set up an earlier one usably. Topic knowledge alone does not carry it: students answer the early parts correctly in a compressed form, then cannot build on their own work and lose the thread around part (c). Three or four complete attempts under timing, marked and discussed, fixes it. Isolated Paper 3 questions do not, because the connection is the thing examined.

faqs.question: How should a Masdar City student choose an exploration topic?
faqs.answer: Narrow, personal and tractable. One phenomenon, one mathematical treatment, data the student can genuinely obtain or generate, and depth that reaches the course level without exceeding what they can discuss. A topic statable in one sentence is a good sign. Ambition is the commonest cause of a poor mark here: mathematics above the course caps the heaviest criterion because the student cannot explain it, and reflection then collapses. Test any candidate topic against one question — what did the mathematics tell you that you did not know? — before committing to it.

faqs.question: How far can a tutor go in helping with the maths exploration?
faqs.answer: A tutor may question whether the topic can carry mathematics at the right level, explain what each of the five criteria rewards, read the student's own draft and name the criterion it undersells, teach notation and citation, and discuss the mathematics as mathematics. A tutor may not choose the topic and hand it over, write or rewrite any part of the text, edit a draft to completion, supply data the student did not generate, or produce a model exploration for adaptation. The student signs the authenticity declaration, so the boundary protects them.

faqs.question: Will an IB maths tutor come to a Masdar City address?
faqs.answer: Not from us. IB Gram runs no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Lessons are live one-to-one video in Gulf Standard Time. For maths the format works provided the tutor can see handwritten working as it happens, via a camera on paper or a tablet and stylus, which we set up in the first session. The practical gain is that the tutor is chosen for the IB route and level rather than for willingness to drive the airport road after the school run.

faqs.question: What does an IB maths tutor cost in this part of Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Published market figures read in October 2026: budget online tutoring at AED 45 to 150 an hour, a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150 to 300, an in-home visit at AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the rate, a named IB or A-Level specialist at AED 200 to 450 and above, and premium examiner-led provision reaching AED 650. Monthly, Bestimate's 2026 estimates give AED 600 to 1,200 for mid-range weekly sessions. Those are the market's numbers; ours follow a free trial and a consultation.

faqs.question: Is a budget online tutor worth trying first in a district like this?
faqs.answer: It is the one purchase here with least plausible return. The thing a conceptually strong student needs is mark-scheme fluency, and the cheapest tier is the tier least likely to have it. Meanwhile the conceptual help a budget tutor does provide is already available locally for nothing, from engineers and researchers who will gladly explain calculus. Paying AED 60 an hour to duplicate the free resource while leaving the actual gap untouched is the specific trap this neighbourhood falls into.

faqs.question: Which schools do Masdar City families usually commute to?
faqs.answer: The nearest belt is the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor, which is short enough that an afternoon session remains realistic — unusual in this part of the emirate. Families wanting a particular programme rather than a short journey enrol further out, on the islands or across the city, which pushes any tutoring slot into the evening. Because our lessons are online the commute direction does not affect which tutor is available, only which slot is. We ask for the arrival time rather than the school finish time when planning it.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor covers my child's exact route and level?
faqs.answer: You are told before you pay. Standard Level AA and AI are well covered and a trial is usually arranged within a few days. Higher Level is in demand and can take up to a week. Specialist Paper 3 work is narrower, and we say so rather than offering a near miss. The alternatives are named: wait for a slot, begin on exploration coaching or technique work with a specialist in that component, or take a tutor based outside the UAE who teaches the same syllabus and works to your evening, disclosed before the trial.

faqs.question: My child came from MYP maths and is slow under exam timing. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: It is extremely common, and it is a change of assessment model rather than a weakness. MYP maths is marked against four criteria through extended investigations, with no timed external papers unless the school enters eAssessment. A student can be conceptually excellent and genuinely inexperienced at speed and at presenting method for a marker. The Diploma asks for both immediately. Six to eight sessions on timed work and mark-scheme presentation bridge it, and placed in the spring of Year 11 they cost less and arrive earlier than the same work in DP1.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram have any approval from ADEK or the IB?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and operates no office or centre in the UAE. ADEK is named on this page because it licenses and inspects the private schools Masdar City children attend, and parents should know who the regulator is. Any provider describing its tutors as approved by a regulator is claiming a permit issued to institutions with premises; ask for the permit number and check it.

faqs.question: What should we send before the free trial lesson?
faqs.answer: The route and level — AA or AI, Higher or Standard — the school name, the last two marked maths assessments with the teacher's comments, and a draft exploration if one exists. Also the time your child is actually home, since that decides which slots are real rather than aspirational. With those in hand the trial hour works on a real script, and at the end you can ask the tutor to name the four behaviours costing marks. Whether they can is the most useful thing you will learn that week.

intro.heading: What it means for a tutor to actually know Diploma mathematics
paragraphs: Knowing mathematics and knowing a mathematics course are different qualifications, and the gap costs families money. There are four Diploma mathematics courses: Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, each at Higher and Standard Level. All four cover the same five topic areas, to sharply different depths, with different calculator rules and different paper structures. A capable graduate who has never taught one of them will handle the content and misread the examination.

Three abilities separate somebody who teaches the course from somebody who merely knows the subject. The first is knowing what each paper rewards and what it withholds, which is not obvious from the syllabus. The second is being able to look at a marked script and say whether a mark was lost to content, to invisible method, or to the clock, because each needs a different remedy. The third is being able to read a draft exploration against the five assessment criteria and name which criterion is about to cost the student marks.

Mohammed Bin Zayed City sits on the mainland with a large and curriculum-mixed population, and the Diploma cohort here is spread thin across several schools. The practical effect is that the number of local people who have taught Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level to an examination, in any given term, is small. Widening the search to Khalifa City or across to the island adds generalists and travel time. It does not reliably add anybody who has marked a Paper 3 investigation.

This page is organised to be useful whoever you hire. It maps how deep each of the four courses goes into each topic area, so a tutoring plan can be checked against the right syllabus. It sets out the calculator marks that disappear quietly in Paper 2. It counts the exploration backwards from a school internal deadline rather than forwards from a good intention. And it states what a tutor may and may not do with that exploration, because one provider visible in this market sells completed Internal Assessments and the consequence of buying one falls on the student.

On delivery there is no ambiguity. IB Gram does not operate home visits in Abu Dhabi, and visiting tutors are a service offered only in India. Every lesson for an MBZ City household is one-to-one over live video, on a shared whiteboard, timed to Gulf Standard Time so it fits around journeys that can run over an hour each way from the island schools. No IB examination or results dates appear here, because the IB's own site blocks automated verification and a wrong date acted on by a parent is worse than no date at all. Where a date matters, the school's IB coordinator is the source that governs, and this page points you there rather than guessing.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme mathematics
programmes.description: One mathematics course from four, taken over two years, with number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus running through all of them. Higher Level carries roughly 240 taught hours against 150 at Standard Level, adds a third paper, and goes considerably further into every topic area rather than only into the obvious ones.
programmes.countryNote: The school's internal deadline calendar is the document that governs a Diploma student's year, and it usually sits a full term ahead of what families assume. Ask the IB coordinator at your child's school for it in writing. It determines when exploration drafts are due, which is the constraint that most often turns an unhurried plan into an emergency in Year 13.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Criterion-referenced assessment graded 1 to 8, with extended and standard streams in the upper years. Students arrive in the Diploma comfortable with investigation and unfamiliar with the speed of manipulation that Analysis and Approaches assumes, because MYP credits the quality of reasoning more heavily than fluency under time pressure.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP cohorts in this corridor are smaller than the British-track ones, so a student arriving in Year 12 from MYP is often the only one in their class with that background and their specific gap goes unnoticed in a room where most students have a different one. Naming it early is most of the work.

programmes.name: IGCSE and International GCSE mathematics
programmes.description: The most common feeder in these communities, taught as Cambridge 0580 Extended or Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 Higher, with Additional Mathematics 0606 available in some schools as a bridge. Extended or Higher tier is the realistic minimum for Analysis and Approaches at either level.
programmes.countryNote: Students who completed 0606 arrive with most of the Analysis and Approaches entry gap already closed, which is the best single argument for taking it in Year 11 where a school offers it. Students who sat Core tier need honest advice rather than encouragement, and Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level is usually the realistic route.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-mohammed-bin.subjectsIntro: Diploma mathematics is five bodies of content plus two skills that sit outside them. Tutoring is organised by whichever of these seven is failing, because work on one does nothing for the others.

subjects.name: Number and algebra
subjects.description: Sequences, series, exponents and logarithms at every level, extending at Analysis and Approaches Higher Level into proof by induction and complex numbers. The topic where a weak IGCSE foundation surfaces first, usually as correct manipulation performed too slowly to finish a question.

subjects.name: Functions
subjects.description: Transformations, composite and inverse functions, and graph interpretation. Marks go when a sketch was required before a calculation and the student calculated first, or when a domain restriction is ignored and a technically correct answer becomes invalid.

subjects.name: Geometry and trigonometry
subjects.description: Identities, non-right-angled triangles and radian measure, extending to three-dimensional vectors at Analysis and Approaches Higher Level. Students memorise the identities and then cannot recognise which one a question is steering them towards, which is a pattern-recognition problem rather than a memory one.

subjects.name: Statistics and probability
subjects.description: Central to Applications and Interpretation and lighter in Analysis and Approaches, covering distributions, correlation and regression, with hypothesis testing at Higher Level. Calculator competence matters more here than anywhere, and marks are withheld when output is reported without justification.

subjects.name: Calculus
subjects.description: Differentiation and integration with applications, extending at Analysis and Approaches Higher Level into implicit differentiation, differential equations and series expansion. The heaviest content block in that course and the usual reason a capable student stalls in Year 13.

subjects.name: Paper 3 investigation technique
subjects.description: Two long structured problems in one hour at Higher Level, where an early slip contaminates later parts and nothing else in the course demands sustained reasoning on a single problem. Trainable, and almost universally under-practised before the examination itself.

subjects.name: The mathematical exploration
subjects.description: Independent mathematical writing marked out of twenty against five criteria, with only six of those marks awarded for the mathematics being correct. Fourteen marks depend on presentation, communication, engagement and reflection, which is why strong mathematicians underperform here.

subjects.name: Calculator and toolkit fluency
subjects.description: Knowing which function answers which question type, how to store and reuse values without transcription error, and how to show working that earns method marks when the value came from a screen. Quick to teach and worth several marks across every calculator paper.

subjects.name: Command terms and notation
subjects.description: The difference between show that, find, justify and hence, and the notation conventions an examiner expects. Students lose marks for answering a different question from the one asked, which is a reading problem that responds to a few focused sessions.

subjects.name: Timing and question selection
subjects.description: Deciding in the first minute whether a question is worth starting, and knowing when to abandon one and return. The most under-taught skill in the whole course, and the one that most often separates two students with identical knowledge.

sections.heading: Three checks before you hire anybody
paragraphs: A credential tells you what somebody has studied. These three checks tell you whether they have taught the course your child is sitting, and each takes a few minutes. Run them on every provider you speak to, including this one, because a family who applies the same test three times gets a ranking instead of three sales pitches.

The first check is the script test. Send a marked mathematics paper and ask one question: which of these lost marks are content, which are method not shown, and which are the clock? Somebody who teaches the course will answer within a minute and name specific questions. Somebody who does not will talk about carelessness and concentration. The distinction matters because content gaps need teaching, invisible method needs a four-second habit, and timing needs question-selection practice, and the three remedies have almost nothing in common.

The second check is the course test. Ask which paper is sat without a calculator and in which of the four courses, then ask what Paper 3 is, who sits it and what it is worth. The third is the criteria test: ask them to name criterion E of the exploration and its mark allocation, and to say which criterion students most often lose marks on. Any Diploma mathematics teacher answers all three instantly. A tutor who assembles the answers in front of you is learning the course on your money, and that is a reasonable thing to decline.

sections.heading: How deep each course goes into each topic
paragraphs: All four Diploma mathematics courses cover the same five topic areas, which is why a syllabus comparison at the heading level looks almost identical and tells you nothing. The depth is where they separate, and a tutoring plan built on the wrong depth either wastes hours on content that will not be assessed or leaves a gap that surfaces in the paper. Checking the plan against the right level is a ten-minute job at the start of an arrangement and saves a term.

The broad pattern is this. Analysis and Approaches goes deepest in calculus and algebra, adding proof, complex numbers and vectors at Higher Level, while keeping statistics relatively contained. Applications and Interpretation goes deepest in statistics and modelling, adding matrices and graph theory at Higher Level, and treats calculus more lightly and more applied. Both Standard Level courses are genuinely narrower rather than merely easier, which matters when a tutor arrives with Higher Level material and the student is not sitting it.

The practical test for a parent is to ask a tutor to name one topic their plan deliberately excludes, and why. Somebody working from the correct syllabus will give you a specific answer: no induction because that is Higher Level Analysis and Approaches only, no graph theory because that is Applications and Interpretation Higher Level. Somebody working from a general idea of Diploma mathematics will not be able to exclude anything, which is the clearest sign that the plan has not been built against your child's actual course.

sections.heading: The calculator marks that disappear quietly
paragraphs: Of all the mark losses on a Diploma mathematics paper, the cheapest to fix are the ones where the answer was right. They happen in calculator papers, which means every Applications and Interpretation paper and Analysis and Approaches Papers 2 and 3. A student solves something on screen, writes the result, and collects the answer mark while the method marks go unawarded because the examiner cannot see what was done. On a multi-part question the method marks are often the larger share.

The remedy is a habit rather than knowledge: write the equation being solved, or the integral being evaluated, before producing the value. It takes a few seconds and it is the single highest-return change available to most candidates. Alongside it sit three more mechanical disciplines. Round once, at the end, to the accuracy the question specifies. Store intermediate values in the calculator rather than retyping them, because transcription is where silent errors enter. And check that the calculator is in the right angle mode before a trigonometry question, not after it.

This block of work takes four to six sessions and is routinely skipped in favour of more content, which is why it stays available as an easy gain for so long. It is also measurable: take a marked script, count the marks withheld on questions where the final answer was correct, and that number is the ceiling on what technique work can recover. For many students it is larger than the number of marks lost to genuinely unknown content, and nobody has ever mentioned it to them.

sections.heading: The exploration, counted backwards from the school's deadline
paragraphs: The exploration fails on timing far more often than on mathematics. It is worth twenty per cent of the grade in all four courses, marked out of twenty across five criteria, and the deadline that governs it is set by the school rather than by the board. Families who plan from the examination window are planning from the wrong end, and they discover the school's internal draft date several weeks after it would have been useful to know it.

Counted backwards, the sequence is reasonably stable. Submission to the school sits at the end. Before that, a final draft the student has revised after feedback. Before that, a first complete draft, which is the version a tutor can usefully mark against the descriptors. Before that, the mathematics has to be done, which usually takes longer than expected because the first approach frequently fails. Before that, the data or the mathematical context has to be secured. And at the start, the topic has to be chosen and tested for whether it can carry mathematics at the course level.

That last step is where most of the eventual grade is decided and where almost no time is spent. A topic that cannot generate mathematics at the right level caps criterion E regardless of how well the piece is written, and no amount of later coaching rescues it. Asking a tutor to stress-test a topic before any work starts is cheap, fast and the highest-value hour in the whole project. Get the school's internal dates in writing from the coordinator first, because everything else is scheduled from them.

sections.heading: Higher Level when Standard would have served
paragraphs: A recurring and expensive decision in this corridor is taking mathematics at Higher Level for a degree that never required it. Higher Level carries roughly 240 taught hours against 150 at Standard, adds a third paper worth twenty per cent of the grade, and goes substantially further into every topic area. For a student heading into engineering, mathematics or physics, that is the correct and necessary load. For a student heading into business, design or most social sciences, it is a large tax on five other subjects.

The symptom appears in Year 13 and looks like a mathematics problem. The student's grades fall across several subjects at once, because the Higher Level mathematics workload is absorbing the time the other five subjects needed, and the exploration is late because there was never a free fortnight to do it properly. Tutoring at that point is firefighting, and a tutor who tells you the honest answer, which is that the level is wrong rather than the teaching, is more useful than one who sells more hours.

The decision point is at course selection and again, in most schools, at the end of the first Diploma year, when a move from Higher to Standard within the same route is usually possible. The test is to read the published entry requirements for three or four target universities, including UAE institutions, and see what they actually name. Where a programme requires Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, the load is unavoidable. Where it does not, Standard Level plus five properly supported subjects almost always produces a better total score.

sections.heading: Who is permitted to tutor your child here
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE requires a permit, and a near-me search returns names rather than permissions. Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced the MoHRE private tuition work permit, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Anyone tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

No fine schedule is published, so no amount appears on this page; a figure circulating online could not be verified against an official source and has been deliberately left out. MoHRE's own service page for the permit lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through its smart app, website or e-services system. The permit attaches to the individual, which means no platform can hold it on a tutor's behalf, and a tutor who holds one can simply say so when asked.

There is a second rule specific to this emirate. ADEK's professional-ethics requirements for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. That is press-reported rather than quoted from the policy document, so verify it against the current ADEK text. The principle holds either way: the person who marks your child's school assessment should not be paid privately to prepare them for it.

sections.heading: What a tutor may never do with an exploration
paragraphs: The exploration must be the student's own work, and that is not a formality. It is submitted with a declaration, schools in this corridor run originality checks as routine, and a piece that reads nothing like a student's class work is noticed. Malpractice findings fall on the candidate rather than on whoever sold them the document. At least one provider visible in UAE search results advertises completed Internal Assessments at a stated price, and the honest description of that transaction is that the student carries all of the risk.

No tutor may write, draft, rewrite or edit to submission any part of an exploration, an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay or any assessed coursework. That restriction holds regardless of deadline pressure, regardless of what a family is willing to pay, and regardless of how small the requested contribution sounds. A paragraph written by somebody else is still work that is not the student's own.

What remains is substantial and is the thing worth buying. Teaching what each criterion credits and how many marks it carries. Stress-testing a topic before weeks are invested in it. Questioning a method until the student finds the weakness themselves. Modelling an analytical technique on entirely different data so it transfers rather than being copied. Marking a draft against the descriptors and naming the criterion at risk. Checking that referencing and data provenance will survive scrutiny. All of that moves marks legitimately, and all of it leaves the work demonstrably the student's.

Those words decide which tutors are candidates and which syllabus depth the plan should be built against, and getting them wrong is the most common cause of a wasted first month.

process.description: The exploration is scheduled from the school's draft deadlines rather than the examination window. Ask the IB coordinator for the calendar, because every sensible plan for Year 12 and 13 is counted backwards from those dates.

whyPoints.description: The plan is built for one of four courses, and a tutor can name which topics it deliberately excludes and why. A plan that excludes nothing has not been built against your child's actual course, which is the quickest way to tell a real plan from a generic one.

whyPoints.description: Marks lost on questions where the answer was right are the cheapest to recover: write the equation before the screen value, round once, store rather than retype. Four to six sessions of this usually beats the same hours spent on further content.

faqs.question: How can I check that a maths tutor really knows the Diploma course?
faqs.answer: Run three quick tests. Send a marked paper and ask which lost marks are content, which are method not shown, and which are the clock; a course teacher answers in a minute and names questions. Ask which paper is sat without a calculator and in which of the four courses, and what Paper 3 is worth. Ask them to name criterion E of the exploration and its mark allocation. All three answers arrive instantly from somebody who teaches the course and get assembled in front of you by somebody who does not.

faqs.question: Why does it matter which of the four maths courses my child takes?
faqs.answer: Because they share five topic headings and diverge underneath them. Analysis and Approaches goes deepest in algebra and calculus, adding proof, complex numbers and vectors at Higher Level, and keeps statistics contained. Applications and Interpretation is built on statistics and modelling, adding matrices and graph theory at Higher Level. Calculator rules differ too: AA Paper 1 is sat without one. A tutor working from the wrong course either teaches content that will not be assessed or leaves a gap that surfaces in the paper.

faqs.question: What are the easiest marks to recover in Diploma mathematics?
faqs.answer: The ones already nearly earned. Take a marked calculator paper and count the marks withheld on questions where the final answer was correct: that number is what technique work can recover. The usual causes are writing an answer straight from the calculator screen with no visible method, rounding at an intermediate step, retyping a previous result instead of storing it, and answering to the wrong accuracy. Four to six sessions on those habits typically returns more than the same hours spent on new content.

faqs.question: How early does exploration work have to begin to stay calm?
faqs.answer: Ten to fourteen weeks before the school's internal submission deadline, starting with topic choice rather than with mathematics. Get the school's draft dates in writing from the IB coordinator first, because the exploration is governed by those rather than by the examination window. The topic has to be tested for whether it can generate mathematics at the course level, since a topic that cannot caps criterion E permanently. Securing data, completing the mathematics, a first full draft and a revised draft then fill the remaining weeks.

faqs.question: Which part of the exploration costs MBZ City students most?
faqs.answer: Reflection and personal engagement, between them, because both are assumed to be decorative. Criterion D rewards genuine critical interrogation of method and results, and most students supply one paragraph at the end saying the work was interesting. Criterion C rewards evidence of real individual involvement, which a topic chosen from a list cannot demonstrate. Criterion E, use of mathematics, carries six of the twenty marks and is the only one about the mathematics being right, so fourteen marks sit elsewhere entirely.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level mathematics worth the extra workload?
faqs.answer: Only if a target programme requires it. Higher Level carries roughly 240 taught hours against 150 at Standard, adds a third paper worth twenty per cent, and goes deeper in every topic. For engineering, mathematics or physics that is necessary. For business, design and most social sciences it is ninety hours taken from five other subjects, and the usual symptom is grades falling across several subjects in Year 13. Read the published entry requirements for three or four universities before treating the level as settled.

faqs.question: Can my child move down from Higher to Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Within the same route, most schools allow it, commonly at the end of the first Diploma year, though the decision belongs to the school and depends on timetabling. Moving between Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation after teaching has started is considerably harder, because the courses differ in content rather than depth. Raise it early with the coordinator if it is being considered. The same conversation in the second year, with an exploration outstanding, rarely ends well for anybody.

faqs.question: What is the honest reason a local Higher Level tutor is hard to find?
faqs.answer: Numbers. Mohammed Bin Zayed City has a large, curriculum-mixed population, so the Diploma cohort is spread thinly across several schools, and the subset of local people who have taught Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level to an examination in any given term is small. Widening the search to Khalifa City or the island adds generalists and travel time rather than course depth. Online delivery changes the filter to who has taught the course, which is the thing that was actually scarce.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need a permit to teach my child in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged fifteen to eighteen. Tutoring without one brings fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no figure appears here. Ask the tutor directly, because the permit belongs to the individual and no platform can hold it for them.

faqs.question: How many hours a week should a Diploma maths student have?
faqs.answer: One reliable hour, for most students, across both years, with short bursts of density before the school's internal exploration deadline and in the weeks before the session. A Diploma student is already carrying several hours of work a night across six subjects plus the core, and two sessions a week usually produces two tired hours rather than one alert one. Increase the frequency when there is something concrete to work on, such as a marked mock or a draft, rather than as a general precaution.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover Higher Level maths and physics together?
faqs.answer: It is a sensible pairing and worth asking about, because weak algebra usually appears in physics before anybody connects the two. A tutor holding both can tell you whether a physics problem failed on the physics or on the rearrangement, which saves a diagnostic session. Ask which of the two they have taught most recently to an examination rather than which they are comfortable with. Pairings that rarely work are a science with a language, where the teaching skill is genuinely different.

faqs.question: What happens to lessons during school examination weeks?
faqs.answer: A short review beats a pause, usually. Examination weeks produce the most immediate evidence of what is failing, and thirty minutes going over a paper that was sat yesterday is worth more than a full hour of new content. There is no rolling term to exit and no fee attached to a break if you prefer one, and because nobody is travelling to an MBZ City address the slot can be resumed in its original place without anybody rearranging a journey across the mainland.

faqs.question: How long does a Higher Level match take from these communities?
faqs.answer: Applications and Interpretation at either level and Analysis and Approaches at Standard Level usually match within a few days. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level can take a week or more, and it tightens sharply around school internal deadlines when every Diploma cohort in the corridor needs the same help at once. Where the specialist is based outside the UAE that is said before the trial, and the session is scheduled to Gulf Standard Time so it fits a mainland evening rather than somebody else's working day.

faqs.question: Can a tutor tell me what score my child will get?
faqs.answer: No, and an answer to that question is a reason for caution. Nobody can guarantee a grade, and no page here publishes one. What a tutor can do is tell you, from a marked script, which specific marks are recoverable and roughly how much work each one represents, which is a more useful answer than a predicted number. No tutor and no platform can promise a score, an improvement or a refund tied to a result, so a provider offering one is describing an outcome outside their control.

faqs.question: Does the exploration have to use real data?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, and this is a common misconception that narrows topic choice unhelpfully. A purely theoretical exploration can reach the top of criterion E if the mathematics is at the course level and genuinely explored rather than recited. What matters is whether the topic can generate mathematics at the right depth and whether the student can demonstrate real engagement with it. Where data is used, its provenance has to be clear and the analysis has to be the student's own, which is worth settling before weeks are spent collecting anything.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-mussafah.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Mathematics — Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, Higher and Standard Level — to students living in Mussafah and the Shabiya districts. Each session is scheduled around the school bus and the school's own homework load.

intro.heading: The school run decides the plan before the maths does
paragraphs: A Diploma student living in Mussafah has a long day. There is no IB school in the Shabiya districts, so the bus leaves early and heads north towards Khalifa City, Al Raha or the island, and comes back somewhere between 15:30 and 16:15. By the time a student has eaten and changed it is past five, and maths homework from that day is already waiting. Any tutoring plan that ignores this timetable gets abandoned in week three.

That matters more for mathematics than for most subjects, because maths is the subject schools set work in most consistently. A DP student will usually have a problem set from the day's lesson, and a tutor arriving on top of that competes with it rather than supporting it. The plans that survive do one of two things: they take the school's own problem set as the session material, or they sit far enough ahead of the class that the session makes the homework easier instead of adding to it.

The second constraint is energy. A session at 16:00, straight off the bus, is not the same hour as a session at 18:30. For algebraic manipulation and non-calculator work — the part of Paper 1 that rewards fluency — the difference is visible within a fortnight. Most Mussafah families end up with a weekday slot between 17:30 and 20:00 and a longer weekend slot when a full paper has to be sat to time, because a past paper needs two uninterrupted hours and a weekday evening does not have them.

The third is which course the student is actually on. Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation are different courses rather than harder and easier versions of the same one. AA rewards algebraic fluency, proof and calculus; AI rewards modelling, statistics and quick, confident use of a graphical calculator. A tutor who treats them as interchangeable will drill the wrong skill for two years, and a student placed in the wrong course will fight it rather than learn it.

IB Gram matches tutors by subject and level and delivers every lesson for UAE families one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the Emirates — home visits are offered only in India — which is what makes a 17:30 start actually a 17:30 start from a Shabiya address rather than an estimate dependent on the mainland road.

One more thing shapes the plan here, and it is easy to miss. Mathematics rewards frequency over length more than any other Diploma subject, because the skills that carry a paper are habits rather than facts. Three shorter sessions a week build algebraic fluency better than one long weekend block, and a Mussafah timetable that can only accommodate a single long session is better used for timed paper work than for teaching. Saying honestly which of those two your week has room for is the most useful thing a parent can do in a first enquiry, because it determines what the whole arrangement can achieve.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-mussafah.programmesIntro: Mathematics in the IB arrives in three stages for a Mussafah student, and each stage has its own place in the week. The programmes below are the ones that actually generate maths tutoring requests from this district.

programmes.name: MYP Mathematics
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria — knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts — marked against band descriptors rather than percentages. Standard and extended routes diverge in MYP 4 and 5, and that divergence is what determines whether Higher Level is realistic later.
programmes.countryNote: For a Mussafah family this is the cheap, quiet window. A single weekly session through MYP 4 and 5 fits easily into the evening and removes most of the pressure that would otherwise land in DP1, when the week is far more crowded.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
programmes.description: Algebra, functions, trigonometry, calculus and proof, with Higher Level adding complex numbers, more demanding calculus and a deeper proof expectation. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, so manipulation has to be automatic rather than merely possible. The exploration is marked against published criteria.
programmes.countryNote: AA is the route most Mussafah students heading for engineering, physics or economics at a competitive university are pointed towards. The cost of getting it wrong is two years of fighting non-calculator algebra, which is why the choice deserves a conversation before it is submitted.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
programmes.description: Statistics, probability, modelling and the use of technology, with Higher Level extending into more demanding statistical and modelling work. Every paper assumes a graphical calculator is used quickly and correctly, and students who learned mathematics entirely by hand lose time rather than knowledge.
programmes.countryNote: AI suits students heading into business, social sciences, design or medicine-adjacent routes, but UAE and overseas universities differ in which course they expect for which degree. Check the specific prerequisite rather than assuming, because the two are not interchangeable on an admissions page.

programmes.name: The IGCSE or MYP to Diploma bridge
programmes.description: The step from international GCSE or MYP mathematics into either Diploma course is the sharpest content jump in the programme. Algebraic fluency assumed at the start of DP1 is well beyond what a comfortable IGCSE grade requires, and the gap shows in the first term.
programmes.countryNote: Mussafah students arriving at the Diploma from an Indian-curriculum or British-curriculum school nearby often meet this jump without warning. A short bridging block in the summer term costs less than a term of catching up in DP1 and prevents the habit of falling behind from forming.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-mussafah.subjectsIntro: Mathematics is the subject on this page, but a maths tutor in the Diploma is drawn into neighbouring subjects constantly, because the mathematics in them is where students stall. The notes below cover the maths-adjacent requests that come from this district.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Paper 1 without a calculator exposes manipulation weaknesses that a calculator has masked since MYP. Higher Level marks concentrate in proof, complex numbers and harder calculus. Many candidates lose marks to presentation rather than method, because the scheme rewards a visible line of working.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, regression, probability distributions and modelling. The common loss is calculator speed: candidates know the method, use the machine slowly, and run out of time on the last two questions of the paper rather than on the hard ones.

subjects.name: The Mathematics exploration
subjects.description: An individual piece of mathematical writing marked against published criteria including presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the mathematics itself. The commonest failure is correct mathematics that is too shallow for the level being claimed.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The mathematics inside physics is where many Diploma students actually struggle: rearranging formulae under time pressure, handling logarithms in the astrophysics and nuclear topics, and reading a gradient correctly from a graph in the data-analysis questions.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles, concentration and equilibrium calculations stop students who can do the chemistry. Marks are lost on significant figures, unit conversion and on the multi-step problems where two quantities must be linked before anything is substituted.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Higher Level calculation questions are arithmetically simple and verbally tricky. Candidates lose marks reading the question rather than doing the maths, and diagram work rewards precision in labelling far more than extra prose.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Investment appraisal, break-even analysis and ratio work are the quantitative parts where students who are strong on theory come unstuck. The marks come from interpreting the figure produced, not from producing it.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Algorithm analysis, number bases and logic are closer to mathematics than to programming, and candidates who code confidently often lose marks in exactly these written sections.

subjects.name: MYP Mathematics, standard and extended
subjects.description: The criterion structure confuses families: a student can produce competent work and score mid-band because the task asked for investigation of a pattern and the answer offered a calculation. Reading the criterion wording is half the skill.

sections.heading: Where the Shabiya bus goes, and what that does to the evening
paragraphs: Mussafah has no IB school, so every Diploma student here commutes. The three realistic destinations are the Khalifa City cluster, the Al Raha corridor and the island, in roughly ascending order of journey time, and the choice a family made years ago at primary level is still shaping when maths homework can be done.

A Khalifa City run typically gets a student home before 16:00. An island run can land closer to 16:30 or later in heavier traffic. That forty-minute difference sounds trivial and is not, because the useful study evening in a Mussafah household runs to about 21:00. A student with four hours of evening has room for school homework and a tutoring session; a student with three has room for one of them.

The practical consequence is that the tutoring session has to either replace part of the homework load or make it faster. Working a fortnight ahead of the class does the second: the student meets a topic in the session, sees it again in school, and the problem set that used to take ninety minutes takes forty. Families who instead add a session on top of an unchanged workload usually stop within a month, and conclude that tutoring did not work.

This is also why the weekend matters more here than in communities closer to the schools. A full past paper under timed conditions needs two uninterrupted hours and genuine concentration, and there is no weekday evening in Shabiya that reliably contains both. Putting paper practice at the weekend and teaching on weekday evenings is the pattern that holds together across a full term.

sections.heading: AA or AI: the decision that shapes the next two years
paragraphs: The commonest avoidable problem in IB mathematics is a student in the wrong course. Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation are separate syllabuses with separate aims, and the choice is usually made in a single conversation at the end of the year before DP1, often on the basis of which one sounds more academic.

AA is built on algebra, functions, trigonometry, calculus and proof. It assumes manipulation is automatic, and Paper 1 is sat without a calculator in both courses, which means an AA student has to be fluent rather than merely capable. A student who relies on a calculator for routine algebra will find AA relentless, and the relentlessness arrives in the first term rather than in the exam year.

AI is built on statistics, probability, modelling and technology. It is not an easier course; it is a different one, and Higher Level AI is demanding. What it rewards is confident, fast use of a graphical calculator and the ability to interpret a model rather than derive it. Students who think clearly about data and dislike abstract proof often do markedly better here than they would in AA.

The deciding factor should be the course ahead, not the course beside. Universities differ in which route they expect for which degree, including inside the UAE, so the honest advice is to read the specific prerequisite for the specific programme rather than to assume AA is universally preferred. Where a student is already in the wrong course and it is too late to move, the tutoring plan changes shape entirely and should be explicit about that.

sections.heading: Where IB maths marks actually go missing
paragraphs: Report cards describe topics; mark schemes describe behaviours. A student who scores four across two papers is rarely failing at mathematics in general, and the useful first step with a Mussafah student is to take a marked paper and sort every lost mark into three groups: did not know it, knew it and presented it badly, knew it and ran out of time.

The second group is the one families underestimate. IB mark schemes award method marks for working that is visible and followable, and a student who computes in their head or on a calculator and writes only an answer throws away marks on questions they answered correctly. Teaching a student to write one line showing the method before any arithmetic is among the fastest mark gains available in this subject, and it takes a few weeks rather than a term.

The third group is about paper craft. Running out of time is almost never caused by slow thinking; it is caused by spending eight minutes on a four-mark question early in the paper. Rehearsing a paper order — attempt in sequence, mark the hard ones, come back — is a learnable skill that is rarely taught in class because class time goes on content.

Only the first group needs re-teaching, and in a Mussafah evening there is rarely time to re-teach broadly. Triage is the realistic approach: identify the topics with the highest mark density on the papers actually being sat, secure those properly, and be honest about which ones are being left.

Separate Paper 1 and Paper 2 practice; they fail for different reasons

sections.heading: The exploration, and the clock the school puts it on
paragraphs: Every Diploma mathematics student produces an exploration, an individual piece of mathematical writing marked against published criteria that include presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and the mathematics itself. It is internally assessed and the deadlines are set by the school, not by the board, which is why two Mussafah students at different schools can be on completely different timetables for it.

The failure mode is predictable. A student picks a topic they find interesting, writes competently about it, and scores mid-band because the mathematics is below the level being claimed. An exploration at Higher Level that uses only Standard Level techniques cannot score at the top of the mathematics criterion however well it is written. Choosing a topic with enough mathematical room in it is most of the work, and it happens at the start.

A tutor's role here is bounded and should be stated before any money is spent. A tutor may teach the mathematics the exploration needs, explain each criterion in ordinary language, read the student's own draft and say where it does not meet the criterion, teach how to present mathematical writing, and ask questions that make the student find the weakness. A tutor may not write, rewrite or supply any part of it, may not invent or supply data, and may not edit a draft into work the student could not have produced.

The test is simple and schools apply it: can the student explain every step and every choice unaided. One operator in this market advertises completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750, and buying one is academic malpractice under IB rules with consequences that fall on the student who signs the authenticity declaration.

sections.heading: What a specialist maths tutor costs around Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: Published market rates give a useful frame, and the maths-specific point is that this subject sits at the specialist end rather than the generalist end, because fewer tutors can teach either Diploma course properly to the mark scheme. Specialist IB, IGCSE and A-Level tutors are quoted from about AED 200 to 450 an hour and above; TutorChase lists AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more. Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150.

Below that band, online tuition from generalist or university-student tutors is advertised from roughly AED 33 to 150 — Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. For MYP mathematics and homework structure that can be the right purchase. For Higher Level AA in the final year it generally is not, because the value is in knowing how the paper rewards working, and that is not knowledge a strong undergraduate necessarily has.

In-home visiting rates run higher again — Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors in the Emirates at AED 200 to 500 including travel, with monthly packages quoted around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits. From Shabiya the travel share of that is substantial, because a tutor crossing from the school corridor at 17:00 spends the better part of ninety minutes on the road. None of these are IB Gram's prices; they are the market as published in October 2026.

What this means in practice for a Mussafah family is that the specialist rate buys mark-scheme knowledge and the travel premium buys presence. For a subject where the losses are presentation and timing rather than motivation, the first is the better purchase.

sections.heading: Permits, school staff and who you should not hire
paragraphs: Private tuition in the UAE is permitted work. Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 introduced the private tuition work permit, administered by MoHRE, granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including teachers registered at government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen.

Individuals offering private tuition without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published — Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the amounts or detail the penalties — so figures circulating online are unverified and should not be repeated. The official route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service, listed with no fee and a two-working-day completion time through the smart app, website or e-services system.

The rule that matters most when choosing a maths tutor in Abu Dhabi concerns school staff. Professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff in the emirate prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. This is press-reported and worth verifying against the current ADEK policy document, but the direction is clear.

There is an academic reason as well as a regulatory one. A tutor who also sets and marks your child's school assessments cannot give independent feedback on them, which removes the main value of a second pair of eyes. Private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are regulated by ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate; IB Gram holds no licence, accreditation or partnership from ADEK or from any board.

sections.heading: Ramadan, school breaks and when maths practice actually lands
paragraphs: Mathematics rewards frequency more than length, which makes the UAE calendar unusually important to plan around. Three shorter sessions a week beat one long one for building fluency, and that pattern is exactly the one a disrupted term breaks first.

During Ramadan school hours shorten and household evenings reorganise around iftar. The sessions that work move to after iftar, often between 20:30 and 22:00, where a fasting student is measurably sharper than in the late afternoon. Length usually drops and frequency holds, which keeps the compounding that fluency work depends on. Pausing for the month and resuming later is the pattern that costs the most, especially for a DP2 student whose papers follow soon after.

The winter and spring breaks are the only stretches in the year without competing school homework, which makes them the right place for foundation repair — index laws, algebraic fractions, trigonometric identities, the things that should be automatic and are not. Doing that work in a break is far cheaper than doing it in the exam term, and it leaves the final weeks free for paper technique.

Travel is the other factor. Many Mussafah households spend part of the summer or winter abroad, and a lesson over live video follows the student wherever they are, which a visiting arrangement cannot. A slot that works in Gulf Standard Time needs re-agreeing for another timezone rather than cancelling, and for mathematics specifically a four-week gap at the wrong point in DP1 is expensive to recover from.

faqs.question: What time can an IB maths session realistically start for a Mussafah student?
faqs.answer: Most families here settle between 17:30 and 20:00 on weekdays. Secondary students in the Shabiya districts travel north to Khalifa City, Al Raha or the island, and the bus usually returns between 15:30 and 16:15, later for island schools in heavy traffic. A session straight off the bus runs at noticeably lower productivity than the same hour after food and a break, and for non-calculator algebra that difference shows within a fortnight. Full past papers belong at the weekend, because they need two uninterrupted hours that a Mussafah weekday evening rarely contains.

faqs.question: Should my child in Mussafah take Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation?
faqs.answer: It depends on the degree ahead, not on which sounds harder. Analysis and Approaches rewards algebraic fluency, calculus and proof, and assumes manipulation is automatic because Paper 1 is sat without a calculator. Applications and Interpretation rewards statistics, modelling and fast, accurate use of a graphical calculator. Neither is the easy option, and Higher Level AI is demanding. Universities differ in which they expect for which programme, including in the UAE, so read the named prerequisite for the named degree rather than assuming AA is always preferred. Getting this wrong costs two years of friction.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a maths tutor to a home in the Shabiya districts?
faqs.answer: No. Home visits are a service offered only in India, not anywhere in the UAE. Every maths lesson for a Mussafah family runs one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, including the free trial. For this district that is the practical choice rather than a compromise: the specialist pool for Diploma mathematics sits near the schools well to the north, so a visiting arrangement would mean choosing from whoever travels south rather than from whoever teaches the course. It also means a 17:30 start happens at 17:30 instead of depending on the mainland road.

faqs.question: My child has maths homework every night. Will a tutor add to the load?
faqs.answer: Not if the session is positioned correctly. The arrangement that works in a Mussafah evening either takes the school's own problem set as the session material or sits a fortnight ahead of the class, so the student meets a topic in the session, sees it again in school, and finds the homework faster rather than heavier. Adding a tutoring session on top of an unchanged workload is why families abandon tuition in week three and conclude it does not work. Say what the nightly load actually is when you enquire, and the plan is built around it.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks on questions they can clearly do?
faqs.answer: Almost always presentation or timing. IB mark schemes award method marks for working that is visible and followable, so a student who calculates mentally or on a calculator and writes only the answer loses marks on questions they answered correctly. The other cause is paper craft: spending eight minutes on a four-mark question early in the paper and running out of time at the end. Both are learnable in weeks rather than terms, which is why a marked script in the first session is worth more than any amount of discussion about which topics feel weak.

faqs.question: How far ahead of DP1 should a Mussafah student prepare for IB maths?
faqs.answer: The summer term before DP1 is the useful window. The step from international GCSE or MYP mathematics into either Diploma course is the sharpest content jump in the programme, because the algebraic fluency assumed at the start of DP1 is well beyond what a comfortable IGCSE grade requires. A short bridging block then costs less than a term of catching up later and, more importantly, prevents the habit of being behind from setting in. Students arriving at an IB school from an Indian- or British-curriculum school near Mussafah meet this jump most sharply.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the maths exploration without crossing a line?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor may teach the mathematics the exploration needs, explain each assessment criterion in plain language, read the draft your child wrote and say where it does not yet meet the criterion, teach how mathematical writing is presented, and ask the questions that make your child find the weakness. A tutor may not write, rewrite or supply any part of it, may not invent or provide data, and may not edit a draft into work your child could not have produced. The test schools apply is whether the student can explain every step and choice unaided.

faqs.question: Why do explorations score mid-band even when they read well?
faqs.answer: Usually because the mathematics is below the level being claimed. An exploration at Higher Level that uses only Standard Level techniques cannot reach the top of the mathematics criterion however clearly it is written, and the problem is created at the topic-choice stage rather than at the writing stage. Choosing a question with enough mathematical room in it is most of the work. The other common cause is thin personal engagement and reflection, which are separate criteria and are frequently treated as decoration rather than as marks to be earned deliberately.

faqs.question: What does a specialist IB maths tutor cost in the Abu Dhabi market?
faqs.answer: Published rates put specialist IB, IGCSE and A-Level tutors at roughly AED 200 to 450 an hour and above: TutorChase lists AED 270, Bestimate's Dubai table gives AED 200 to 450 or more, and Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200. Generalist or university-student online tutors are advertised far lower, from about AED 33 to 150, which can suit MYP mathematics but rarely suits Higher Level work in the final year. In-home visiting rates run AED 180 to 500 including travel. These are market figures read in October 2026, not IB Gram's prices.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper tutor enough for MYP maths in Mussafah?
faqs.answer: Often, yes, and it is the sensible place to spend less. MYP mathematics is assessed against four criteria rather than by external paper, so the job is usually consistency and criterion awareness rather than mark-scheme expertise. A capable generalist at the lower published rates can do that well. The caveat is MYP 4 and 5, where the standard and extended routes diverge and that divergence decides whether Higher Level is realistic later. At that point the conversation becomes about Diploma preparation, and the value of a specialist rises sharply.

faqs.question: Can sessions run after iftar during Ramadan for a Shabiya student?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is usually the better slot. School hours shorten during Ramadan and household evenings reorganise around iftar, so a session that ran at 17:30 typically moves to between 20:30 and 22:00, when a fasting student is sharper than mid-afternoon. For mathematics the thing to protect is frequency rather than length: three shorter sessions a week build fluency better than one long one, so shortening sessions and keeping the rhythm is better than pausing. A month off and a resumption close to papers is the most expensive option available.

faqs.question: Which schools do Mussafah IB students usually travel to?
faqs.answer: Three clusters, because there is no IB school inside Mussafah itself. The Khalifa City group is the shortest run and the most common choice; the Al Raha corridor is next; the island and Saadiyat schools are the longest journey and tend to push sessions to the back of the evening. Named schools in these clusters are listed on this page as context for families comparing options, with no affiliation implied. Which cluster your child travels to is worth stating when you enquire, because it changes the realistic session window by up to an hour.

faqs.question: Can a Mussafah student be tutored by a teacher from their own school?
faqs.answer: You should avoid it. Professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi prohibit teachers from providing paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. That is press-reported and worth verifying against the current ADEK policy document. There is also an academic reason: a tutor who sets and marks your child's school assessments cannot give independent feedback on them, which removes most of the point of having a second opinion on the work.

faqs.question: How quickly should we expect to see maths marks move?
faqs.answer: Presentation and timing gains show in four to six weeks, because they are habits rather than knowledge. Writing a visible method line and rehearsing paper order recover marks on questions the student could already answer, and a timed paper will show it. Content gains take longer and depend on how deep the gap runs; a missing foundation two years old does not close in a term. No tutor can promise a specific grade, and anyone who does is describing a sales position rather than how assessment works. What a plan can commit to is a measurable check on a marked paper every few weeks.

faqs.question: What if the tutor we start with is not the right match?
faqs.answer: You say so and another is proposed, without an argument about the rest of the block. Most mismatches are visible in the free trial, which is why it is run as a working session on a marked paper rather than as a conversation, and why it is best run in the slot you intend to keep. Occasionally a match looks right and then does not survive contact with a real term — a clash of pace, or a tutor whose strength turns out to be AI when your child is on AA. Saying so early costs nothing.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-mussafah.closingHeading: Fit IB maths into the Mussafah evening you actually have
abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-mussafah.closingBody: Tell us the course and level, which school cluster the bus serves, and how much maths homework comes home on a normal night. Attach a recent marked paper if you can. The free trial lesson runs in the slot you intend to keep, so the diagnosis and the timing are both tested before anything is agreed, and the tutor will say plainly what the coming weeks will drill and what they cannot change. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with no travel inside the rate and no session shortened by the mainland road.

Each works in one of the four routes rather than all of them, because AA HL and AI SL are different courses with different papers and different calculator rules.

intro.heading: What two years of IB maths tutoring actually costs a Saadiyat Island family
paragraphs: Price the whole course, not the hour. A Diploma Programme mathematics course runs from the start of DP1 to the May session at the end of DP2. A weekly sixty-minute session across that span, allowing for holidays and exam leave, comes to somewhere between seventy and eighty paid hours. At the budget end of the Abu Dhabi market that is a few thousand dirhams. At the specialist end it is a five-figure commitment. Families on Saadiyat Island regularly sign up to the second without having priced the first.

The published bands are these, and each is attributed. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts weekly one-hour tutoring at roughly AED 240-600 a month at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. On an hourly basis, Tutopiya advertises from AED 33-52 and EdFlik from AED 45-65 at the entry level. Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate puts the IB and A Level specialist band at AED 200-450 and upwards. BartyED publishes AED 650 for a premium named tutor. In-home one-to-one with travel included runs AED 180-500.

Those ranges overlap, which is the first thing worth noticing. A tutor charging AED 200 an hour and one charging AED 450 can both be described as IB specialists, and the price difference does not reliably predict which one can teach the Paper 3 problem-solving questions in Analysis and Approaches at higher level. What does predict it is whether the tutor works in that route habitually. A tutor who teaches AI SL most weeks and takes an AA HL student because the booking came in is the most expensive mistake in this market regardless of the hourly figure attached.

The second thing worth noticing is where the money leaks. It leaks into hours spent on content the student already has, because nobody diagnosed first. It leaks into a tutor covering the wrong route's syllabus. It leaks into general maths help in DP1 when the exploration deadline in DP2 is the thing that will actually cost twenty per cent of the grade. And it leaks into the travel premium, which on an island reached by a single bridge is larger than it looks, and which buys no additional teaching at all.

What follows is the costing. A monthly ladder rather than an hourly one, the route decision that determines what you are paying a tutor to do, the paper weightings so you can see which component your money is buying marks in, the exploration criteria with their mark allocations, and the cost of the course set against school fees and exam entry. All AED figures are market figures with their sources named. IB Gram publishes no price list here; tuition starts with a free trial lesson and a conversation.

Mathematics is compulsory, which is why maths tutoring demand in the Diploma is structurally higher than in any other subject group. Every student picks one of four maths routes and that choice is difficult to reverse after the first term.
