programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The five years before the Diploma in a continuum school. MYP mathematics is assessed against four criteria rather than by terminal paper, which means a student can arrive in DP1 with strong MYP grades and no experience of a timed, non-calculator paper. That gap is the single most common reason a Saadiyat Island family books maths tutoring in the first term of DP1.
programmes.countryNote: Not every Abu Dhabi school running the Diploma runs MYP beneath it, so a DP1 cohort in this emirate often mixes MYP leavers with IGCSE leavers. The two groups need different first months of tutoring, and paying for the wrong one is a waste that shows up in February.

programmes.name: The IGCSE route into DP mathematics
programmes.description: Many students in Abu Dhabi reach the Diploma from Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE. An Extended or Higher tier pass with secure algebra is a workable foundation for Analysis and Approaches at standard level. Additional Mathematics 0606, where a school offers it, is the best preparation available for AA higher level because it introduces calculus a year early.
programmes.countryNote: If your child is in Year 11 in Abu Dhabi now and the Diploma is the plan, the cheapest maths tutoring you will ever buy is the block that closes algebraic fluency gaps before DP1 begins. Remediation in DP2 costs several times as much and happens under deadline pressure.

programmes.name: IB Career-related Programme and other routes
programmes.description: A smaller presence in Abu Dhabi, where students combine IB core elements with a career-related study. Mathematics support here is usually about quantitative confidence for the career strand rather than about Diploma papers, and it is correspondingly shorter and cheaper. Worth naming because families sometimes assume the Diploma is the only IB option available.
programmes.countryNote: Where a Saadiyat Island student is on a non-Diploma route, we say so before quoting anything, because the hour count and therefore the total cost are completely different from a two-year DP maths plan.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-saadiyat-isl.subjectsIntro: Mathematics is the page's subject, but families almost always add a second. These are the DP subjects Abu Dhabi households most often pair with maths support, with what each one assesses so you can judge whether an extra weekly hour is worth buying.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebraic, proof-oriented route. Standard level sits two papers at 40% each with the exploration at 20%; higher level sits three, weighted 30, 30 and 20 with the exploration at 20%. Paper 1 at both levels is taken without a calculator, which is where most marks are lost by students who learned maths with a screen in front of them.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The modelling and statistics route, with a graphical display calculator permitted on every paper. Lighter on proof, heavier on interpretation, regression, and reading a context correctly. Students lose marks here for giving a number without saying what it means in the situation the question described.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The most common pairing with AA at higher level, and the subject whose mathematical demand catches students out. Mechanics and fields reward exactly the algebraic fluency Paper 1 in maths requires, so a single tutor's work in one subject often shows up in the other.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and kinetics carry the quantitative load. Students who are comfortable with logarithms and rearrangement find the higher-level calculations routine; those who are not lose marks on questions they understand conceptually, which is a maths problem wearing a chemistry label.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Higher level adds quantitative work that an AI student finds straightforward and an under-prepared AA student sometimes does not, because the arithmetic is applied rather than abstract. Diagram accuracy and explicit evaluation decide the top band.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The statistical content, including standard deviation, correlation and significance testing, is where maths and biology meet. The internal assessment also rewards competent data handling, which is a transferable gain from maths tutoring rather than a separate purchase.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Algorithmic thinking, complexity and the higher-level case study. Students arriving from a strong AA background find the reasoning familiar; the gap is usually in the formal notation and in the discipline of tracing an algorithm by hand rather than running it.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Included because it is the subject most often paired with maths in a two-subject plan. Marks sit in the guided textual analysis and the individual oral, both of which are taught techniques. A student can be articulate and still score mid-band for not addressing the assessment criteria.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Arabic runs alongside the Diploma in Abu Dhabi private schools under federal requirements for Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies. The language B and ab initio routes are different courses, and a student placed in the wrong one struggles for reasons unrelated to ability.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge
subjects.description: Assessed by exhibition and essay, and worth real points in combination with the Extended Essay. Support here is process coaching against published criteria. The written work must be the student's own, and no tutor should supply text for it.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-saadiyat-isl.regionsTitle: Abu Dhabi areas where the same maths cohort lives
abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-saadiyat-isl.regionsIntro: Saadiyat Island students share their Diploma classrooms with families from across the emirate, and the rate a tutor quotes often depends on which of these areas they themselves live in. Useful context when you are reading a price.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Cultural-district and beach-district housing with a single bridge route to the mainland. Secondary provision on the island is limited, so most Diploma students commute, and in-home tutors price the crossing into the hour.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Dense tower living reached through the mainland rather than directly from Saadiyat. Reem households often share Diploma cohorts with Saadiyat, and the cheapest in-home quotes a Saadiyat family receives often come from tutors based here.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: Further east and reached inland, which makes a tutor's round trip from Yas to Saadiyat long enough to appear in the rate. A clear illustration of why an online hour and an in-home hour are not the same product.

regions.name: Al Raha Beach
regions.note: Coastal mainland strip close to several of the schools Saadiyat Diploma students attend. A tutor living here can reach the Khalifa City campuses quickly and Saadiyat slowly, which is why their two quotes differ.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: The largest block of Diploma places in Abu Dhabi and the base for a large share of the emirate's experienced maths teachers. Most of the mid-band AED quotes in this market originate here.

regions.name: Al Bateen
regions.note: Close-in district with long-established international provision, including Diploma schools. Shorter run to Saadiyat than the Khalifa City corridor, and in-home quotes from here are correspondingly lower.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City
regions.note: Inland and further out, with its own school cluster. Families relocating here from Saadiyat frequently change schools, and a mid-Diploma school change is the most expensive maths tutoring scenario there is.

regions.name: The Corniche and Al Khalidiyah
regions.note: Where tuition centres concentrate. A group class here is cheaper per hour than one-to-one and costs a Saadiyat family a second evening commute, which is the trade-off to weigh rather than ignore.

schoolClusters.city: Saadiyat Island and central Abu Dhabi
schoolClusters.note: Students we support in this cluster sit Diploma mathematics across all four routes, and the mix of AA and AI varies sharply by campus. That matters for cost, because an AA higher level specialist is a scarcer and therefore dearer tutor than an AI standard level one.
schools: American Community School of Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City and the Al Raha corridor
schoolClusters.note: The corridor where most Saadiyat Island Diploma students actually study. School-day finishes here cluster closely enough that a single evening slot works across campuses, which is what makes a weekly fixed-time arrangement survive a term.
schools: The British International School Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: Yas Island and Al Reem Island
schoolClusters.note: Growing provision on both islands. Students moving between these campuses and Saadiyat mid-Diploma are the group most likely to change maths route, and a route change is a content purchase rather than a scheduling one.

sections.heading: The monthly ladder: what Abu Dhabi families actually pay for DP maths
paragraphs: Hourly rates mislead because nobody buys one hour. Bestimate's 2026 estimates for weekly one-hour sessions are AED 240-600 a month at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Package pricing seen in this market includes around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Read that ladder cheapest first, because that is how a decision actually gets made. At the bottom sits homework supervision from a university student: useful for a DP1 student who is coping but disorganised, and inadequate for anyone sitting Paper 3. In the middle sits a qualified subject tutor working online, which is where most DP maths work belongs. At the top sits a named specialist, which is worth paying for in one specific situation: a higher level student in the final two terms whose paper scores have stalled and who needs technique rather than content.

The jump from the middle band to the top band is roughly double. Ask what the doubling buys before paying it. If the answer is reputation and scarcity, that is a legitimate thing to buy in the run-in to a session and a poor thing to buy in the first term of DP1, when the work is content coverage and the middle band does it just as well. Spending top-band money for two years is the most common overspend in this market.

sections.heading: Where the money is wasted in DP maths tutoring
paragraphs: The largest single waste is undiagnosed hours. A tutor who begins by re-teaching the current chapter is being paid to repeat school. A tutor who begins by marking a recent test and naming the three topics that cost the most marks is being paid to find the problem. The first costs the same per hour as the second and produces a fraction of the movement, and a family can run a full term on it without noticing, because the sessions feel productive.

The second waste is route mismatch. Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation are separate courses with separate calculator rules and separate paper structures. A tutor who habitually teaches one and takes a student in the other will cover material at the wrong depth in both directions, and will miss the specific demands that decide grades, such as non-calculator fluency in AA Paper 1 or contextual interpretation in AI. The hourly rate tells you nothing about this. The question does: ask which route the tutor teaches most weeks.

The third waste is timing. Twenty per cent of the grade sits in the exploration, and the exploration has an internal deadline inside DP2 that arrives earlier than most families expect. Money spent on general maths help in DP1 while the exploration goes unplanned is money spent on the eighty per cent while the twenty per cent is left to chance. A short block on the criteria, taken at the right moment, moves more marks per dirham than any other intervention in the course.

The fourth is the travel premium. In-home rates run AED 180-500 against AED 150-300 online for a qualified tutor, and that gap pays for a journey rather than for teaching. On Saadiyat Island, reached by one bridge, the premium is structurally higher. IB Gram does not sell in-home visits in the UAE at all, so the question does not arise with us, but it is worth checking in any quote you receive: ask what share of the rate is travel.

sections.heading: AA or AI: the route choice that decides what you are paying for
paragraphs: Every Diploma student takes mathematics, and every one picks a route. Analysis and Approaches is the algebraic and proof-oriented course; Applications and Interpretation is the modelling, statistics and interpretation course with a graphical display calculator permitted on every paper. Both exist at higher and standard level, giving four courses in total, and the choice is normally made at the end of Year 11 and is awkward to reverse after the first term.

For tutoring cost, the route matters in two ways. Tutors who work habitually in AA at higher level are scarcer than tutors who work in AI at standard level, which moves the rate. And the teaching itself is different work: AA higher level needs non-calculator fluency, proof technique and the problem-solving extension of Paper 3, while AI needs modelling judgement, regression and the discipline of interpreting a number back into its context.

For university choice the route matters more. Many engineering, mathematics, physics and economics programmes expect Analysis and Approaches, often at higher level, and some state it explicitly. Courses in social sciences, business, design and the life sciences more often accept either. The honest instruction here is to read the entry requirements of the specific universities your child is considering, because the pattern varies by country and by faculty, and a tutoring page is the wrong place to take that from.

What a tutor can do is tell you, from a marked paper, whether your child is in the right route. A student who is accurate but slow without a calculator is often misplaced in AI. A student who models well and freezes on an algebraic identity is often misplaced in AA. Finding that out in the first term costs a few sessions. Finding it out in DP2 costs considerably more.

sections.heading: Paper weightings: which component your money is buying marks in
paragraphs: Before you decide how many hours to buy, look at where the marks are. At standard level the two papers carry forty per cent each and the exploration carries twenty. At higher level the three papers carry thirty, thirty and twenty, with the exploration again at twenty. A family paying for weekly content tutoring across two years and nothing else is spending on the papers and leaving a fifth of the grade to whatever happens in class.

Paper 1 in Analysis and Approaches is sat without a calculator, and it is the component where Abu Dhabi students most often underperform relative to their classwork. The reason is habit: a student who has done every exercise with a screen in front of them has never built the arithmetic and algebraic fluency the paper assumes. That is a trainable gap, it responds to short repeated drills rather than long explanations, and it is cheap to fix if it is identified in DP1.

Paper 3 at higher level is a different animal again: an extended problem-solving investigation where the mathematics is familiar and the structure is not. Students who can do every topic still lose marks here for not following the thread of a multi-part question. Of all the components, this is the one where a specialist rate is most defensible, and it is also the one most often left untouched until the final weeks.

The table sets out the components with what each actually tests and where marks go missing. Use it to decide which component a block of tutoring is aimed at, and ask the tutor to say which one they are working on. A tutor who cannot answer that question is working on everything, which in practice means working on nothing in particular.

sections.heading: The exploration: twenty marks, five criteria, and the line a tutor cannot cross
paragraphs: The internal assessment in Diploma mathematics is an exploration: an independent piece of mathematical writing worth twenty per cent of the grade. It is marked against five criteria totalling twenty marks, and the allocation is public. Presentation carries four marks, mathematical communication four, personal engagement three, reflection three, and use of mathematics six. Most students lose marks in criteria they have never read rather than in mathematics they cannot do.

Reflection is the clearest example. Three marks are available for genuine reflection on the mathematics, and a very large number of explorations treat the reflection as a summary of what the student did. Personal engagement is the second: three marks for a real relationship between the student and the topic, which a generic topic chosen from a list cannot produce. Use of mathematics, worth six, rewards mathematics that is correct, relevant and at a level commensurate with the course, which means an elegant piece of work pitched below the course cannot reach the top band.

A tutor's legitimate role here is substantial and bounded. They can explain each criterion and what the marks are awarded for, discuss candidate topics and test whether a topic has enough mathematics in it, teach the techniques the student has chosen to use, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. That is genuinely valuable and it is where the exploration block earns its cost.

What no tutor may do is produce the work. No tutor should write the exploration, rewrite a draft into its final form, or supply text for submission. The IB's academic-honesty rules make authorship the student's responsibility, and a malpractice finding is a far worse outcome than a middling mark. One page competing for these searches sells completed internal assessments outright at a published price. We state our position instead of leaving it implied.

sections.heading: Costing the course in context: fees, tutoring and exam entry
paragraphs: Tutoring never sits alone in a household budget. Set it against the other education costs and the decision becomes clearer. Dubai's regulator confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in that emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. Abu Dhabi fee rules are set by ADEK rather than KHDA, so confirm your own school's position with the school.

Against a school fee, a mid-band weekly maths session at AED 600-1,200 a month is a visible but modest addition. A top-band specialist across two years is not; it is a second significant education line in the budget. That is the comparison worth making before signing a two-year arrangement, and it is the comparison no competing page in this market invites you to make, because three of the six pages we examined publish no price at all and the two that do quote in US dollars.

There is also a timing point. Spending in DP1 and spending in DP2 are not equivalent. Content coverage in DP1 is work the school is also doing, so the marginal value of a paid hour is lower. Technique work in the final two terms is work the school has limited time for, so the marginal value is higher. A family with a fixed budget generally gets more for it by spending less in DP1 and more in the run-in, with one exception: a diagnosed, specific gap in DP1 should be closed immediately, because it compounds.

sections.heading: How to verify the person you are about to pay
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and this is the cheapest piece of due diligence available to a parent. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time.

Because it is free and quick, there is no good reason for an independent tutor not to hold one, and individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you by anyone, including us. A tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal animal and needs an educational services permit for a training institute from the relevant authority.

There is an Abu Dhabi-specific point as well. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the permit-holder's own school. We treat that as press-reported rather than as ADEK's exact wording, and we do not arrange for a child to be tutored privately by a teacher at their own school.

The last piece of verification concerns claims. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB or Cambridge, and has no office or centre in the UAE. Any tutoring page that tells you otherwise about itself is making a claim you can check, and should. We name regulators to explain what they govern, not to borrow standing we do not have.

sections.heading: Buying the first month well
paragraphs: A first month that costs the same as any other month can produce a very different return, and the difference is almost entirely about sequence. Send one piece of marked work before the first session. A returned test, a mock paper, a marked exploration draft: anything with a teacher's annotations on it. That single document lets a tutor arrive with a hypothesis instead of a questionnaire, and it converts the first paid hour from an interview into teaching.

Then take the free trial lesson and judge three things. Whether your child talks to this person, because a student who will not admit confusion to a tutor is paying for silence. Whether the tutor named specific topics rather than general weaknesses, because "needs to work on algebra" is not a diagnosis. And whether the tutor asked which maths route and which level, which is the question that separates a subject specialist from a generalist.

Fix the weekly slot against your child's actual school day rather than against your own calendar. For a Saadiyat Island household whose child attends a Khalifa City or Al Raha campus, the honest earliest start is about 17:30 once the commute and a break are accounted for, and the most durable slots in an exam term sit at 18:00 or 18:30 Gulf Standard Time. A slot that only works on an untroubled week will break inside a fortnight.

Review at the half term against two measurable things: whether the named topic list is shrinking, and whether timed paper scores are moving. Feel is not evidence. If neither has changed after six weeks, change the plan or the tutor rather than continuing out of momentum, which is how families end up with two years of comfortable sessions and a grade that never moved.

faqs.question: How much should a Saadiyat Island family budget for IB maths tutoring across the whole Diploma?
faqs.answer: Price the course rather than the hour. A weekly sixty-minute session from the start of DP1 to the May session at the end of DP2 comes to roughly seventy to eighty paid hours once holidays and exam leave are removed. At the mid-market monthly band of AED 600-1,200 quoted by Bestimate's 2026 estimates, that is a substantial but predictable line in a household budget. At the specialist band of AED 1,000-2,000 or more a month in an exam year, it becomes a second major education cost. Decide which band each phase of the course deserves rather than paying one rate throughout.

faqs.question: Is an AED 450 IB maths tutor better than an AED 200 one?
faqs.answer: Not reliably, and that is the uncomfortable part. Published bands overlap: Unitors lists IB tuition from AED 200, TutorChase quotes AED 270, and Bestimate puts the specialist band at AED 200-450 and upwards. All of those describe themselves as IB specialists. What predicts teaching quality in Diploma mathematics is whether the tutor works habitually in your child's route and level, not the figure attached. Ask which route they teach most weeks. A higher-rate tutor outside your route is worse value than a mid-band tutor inside it.

faqs.question: Is in-home maths tutoring on Saadiyat Island something IB Gram sells?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Diploma mathematics support for Abu Dhabi families is delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time. For a cost-focused decision that matters directly: the published in-home band runs AED 180-500 an hour against AED 150-300 for a qualified online tutor, and the gap pays for a journey rather than for teaching. On an island reached by a single bridge, that gap is structurally wider.

faqs.question: Which maths route should my child take for a UAE or overseas university?
faqs.answer: Read the stated entry requirements of the specific universities and faculties your child is considering, because the pattern varies. Many engineering, mathematics, physics and economics programmes expect Analysis and Approaches, often at higher level, and some say so explicitly. Social sciences, business, design and several life-science courses more often accept either route. A tutoring page is the wrong source for a decision this consequential. What a tutor can tell you, from a marked paper, is whether your child is suited to the route they are currently in.

faqs.question: How much of the IB maths grade does the exploration actually carry?
faqs.answer: Twenty per cent, at both standard and higher level, marked out of twenty across five criteria. Presentation carries four marks, mathematical communication four, personal engagement three, reflection three, and use of mathematics six. The practical consequence is that a family paying for weekly content tutoring and nothing else is spending on eighty per cent of the grade and leaving a fifth of it to whatever happens in class. A short block aimed at the criteria usually moves more marks per dirham than any other intervention in the course.

faqs.question: What can a tutor legitimately do on a Saadiyat Island student's maths exploration?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor can explain each criterion and what its marks are awarded for, test whether a topic the student has proposed contains enough mathematics, teach the techniques the student has chosen to use, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. No tutor may write the exploration, rewrite a draft into its final form, or supply text for submission. Authorship is the student's responsibility under IB academic-honesty rules, and a malpractice finding is far worse than a middling mark.

faqs.question: Why does Paper 1 cause problems for students who are fine in class?
faqs.answer: In Analysis and Approaches, Paper 1 is sat without a calculator and carries forty per cent of the grade at standard level and thirty at higher level. Students who have done every exercise with a screen in front of them have never built the arithmetic and algebraic fluency the paper assumes, so classwork and paper performance diverge. It is a habit problem rather than an understanding problem, it responds to short repeated drills rather than long explanations, and it is inexpensive to fix if it is caught in DP1 rather than in the final term.

faqs.question: What is Paper 3 and does it justify paying a specialist rate?
faqs.answer: Paper 3 is sat only at higher level, carries twenty per cent of the grade, and is an extended problem-solving investigation. The mathematics in it is familiar; the structure is not, and students who can do every topic still lose marks for losing the thread of a multi-part question. Of all the components in Diploma mathematics, this is the one where a specialist rate is easiest to defend, and it is also the one most often left untouched until the final weeks. Buying specialist hours here and mid-band hours elsewhere is a defensible split.

faqs.question: Where do Saadiyat Island families most often waste money on maths tutoring?
faqs.answer: On undiagnosed hours. A tutor who opens by re-teaching the current chapter is being paid to repeat school; a tutor who opens by marking a recent test and naming three costly topics is being paid to find the problem. Both charge the same. The second waste is route mismatch, where a tutor who habitually teaches one maths route takes a student in the other. The third is spending heavily in DP1 on content the school is also covering while the exploration, worth a fifth of the grade, goes unplanned.

faqs.question: When is the best time to start paying for IB maths support?
faqs.answer: It depends on what you are buying. A diagnosed, specific gap should be closed immediately, in DP1, because it compounds through the course. General content support in DP1 has lower marginal value, because the school is covering the same material at the same time. Technique work in the final two terms has higher marginal value, because the school has limited time for it. A family with a fixed budget usually gets more by spending modestly in DP1 and concentrating the spend on the exploration block and the run-in.

faqs.question: Can sessions fit around a Saadiyat Island school run and Abu Dhabi traffic?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is where online delivery earns its place rather than merely saving money. Most campuses serving the island finish their taught day between 14:45 and 15:30, and a child at a Khalifa City or Al Raha school is often not home before 16:15. Allowing time to eat and change, the honest earliest start is around 17:30, and the most durable slots in an exam term sit at 18:00 or 18:30 Gulf Standard Time. Because there is no journey on either side, a late finish moves the session rather than cancelling it.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram publish an hourly rate for Saadiyat Island?
faqs.answer: Not on this page. Every AED figure here is a published market rate attributed to the competitor page or rate survey that produced it, and it is included so that you can test any quote you receive. Our own arrangement starts with a free trial lesson and a conversation about route, level, how many weeks remain before the session your child is entered for, and whether a bounded block or a weekly arrangement fits. Those variables change the answer enough that a single headline number would mislead rather than help.

faqs.question: My child moved from MYP into DP1 and is suddenly struggling in maths. Why?
faqs.answer: Middle Years Programme mathematics is assessed against criteria rather than by terminal paper, so a student can arrive in DP1 with strong MYP grades and no experience of a timed, non-calculator paper. The gap is usually exam behaviour and algebraic fluency rather than understanding, and it is the most common reason an Abu Dhabi family books maths support in the first term. It is also one of the cheaper problems to fix, because it responds to short repeated practice rather than to re-teaching the content.

faqs.question: How do I check that an independent maths tutor in Abu Dhabi is permitted to work?
faqs.answer: Ask whether they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents and university students. Because it costs nothing, there is no good reason for a tutor not to hold one. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: What should I see after six weeks to know the money is working?
faqs.answer: Two measurable things. The named topic list should be shorter than it was, which means the tutor identified specific topics rather than general weaknesses in the first place. And timed paper scores should be moving, which means papers are being sat under conditions and marked against the published scheme. Feel is not evidence, and comfortable sessions are the easiest thing in this market to keep paying for. If neither measure has shifted after six weeks, change the plan or the tutor instead of continuing from momentum.

Then choose a tutor who works in your child's maths route every week rather than one who can. intro.heading: You are comparing the wrong two things
paragraphs: Shakhbout City is a mainland villa community in the Khalifa City corridor, between Khalifa City and Mohammed Bin Zayed City. Families here and in the communities either side are close enough that a tutor's weekly route covers several of them, and when a parent compares tutoring availability across those addresses they usually find much the same list of names. The comparison looks like a decision and is not one.

In maths specifically, the comparison that does matter is which course your child is taking. The Diploma offers two: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, which is algebraic, calculus-led and proof-oriented, and Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation, which is modelling, statistical and technology-led. They are not harder and easier versions of one subject. They are different mathematics, examined differently, and taught well by different people.

That makes the geography comparison actively misleading. A tutor who lives three streets from your villa in Shakhbout City and whose main course is Applications and Interpretation is, for an Analysis and Approaches Higher Level student, a worse option than a specialist who happens to be on a screen. They will teach competently around the edges of the course and avoid the parts they do not own, and parents usually notice around the fourth session, when the Higher Level Paper 3 questions stop appearing.

The second variable that matters, and which no amount of proximity solves, is what your child is actually losing marks for. Marked scripts from Diploma maths students resolve into a short list of repeating behaviours — compressed working, an unset calculator mode, a statistical conclusion stated generically, a model produced without justification. None of those are topics, and none of them can be diagnosed from a conversation. A specialist reads a script and names them; a generalist re-teaches the topic the student already understood.

So this page does the comparison properly. It sets Shakhbout City against the communities either side on the things that genuinely differ, then moves on to what actually determines whether a maths hour works: the route, the level, the failing component, and six questions you can ask any tutor before paying them anything.

On delivery, plainly, since the search is local. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. In-home tutoring is a service we run in India only, and no tutor will travel to a Shakhbout City address or to any other in this corridor. Lessons are live one-to-one video in Gulf Standard Time, with the tutor chosen for the route and level in front of them.

What follows is the detail: the two communities compared, the route decision, where revision belongs by level, the questions that separate a specialist from a generalist, the marks nobody teaches, and what a maths hour costs on either side of the corridor.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Assessed against four criteria — knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts — each marked out of 8 and converted to a 1 to 7 grade on school-set boundaries, with no timed external papers unless the school enters eAssessment. Students become strong at investigation and inexperienced at speed.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools across this corridor run MYP into the Diploma within the same institution, which makes the step look like a continuation and conceals a real change in assessment model. A student fluent in criterion-marked investigation meets timed papers with a formula booklet in DP1 and finds out in October. Six to eight sessions in the spring of Year 11 handles it earlier and cheaper.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme mathematics
programmes.description: One Group 5 course per student: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, at Higher or Standard Level. Standard Level sits two papers, Higher Level three, with the third consisting of extended multi-part investigations. An individual exploration carries roughly a fifth of the final grade in every combination.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi schools enter the May session. IB exam and results dates are set and revised by the IB, and we publish none here — confirm them with your school's IB coordinator. What governs a maths term in practice is the school's internal deadline for the exploration, which usually falls well before anything external and is set by the department rather than the IB.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme with a DP maths course
programmes.description: At least two Diploma courses alongside a career-related study, with maths commonly among them. The course and its assessment are identical to the full Diploma version, including the exploration, so the teaching requirement does not change at all.
programmes.countryNote: A narrower need — one maths course taken to a defensible grade, usually Applications and Interpretation at Standard Level, plus structural help on the reflective project. One course a week is not enough work to interest a resident generalist in this corridor, which is exactly the case where a wider online pool is the practical answer.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-shakhbout-ci.subjectsIntro: These are the parts of IB mathematics families in this corridor ask about, with where the marks actually go. Both routes, both levels.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL
subjects.description: Algebra, functions, trigonometry, calculus and proof at depth, plus Paper 3's two long investigations. Marks go to structure: a student who has practised only short questions loses the thread by part (c).

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches SL
subjects.description: The analytical spine with less breadth across two papers. Differentiation and integration applied in context are the usual losses, together with working presented too compactly for the mark scheme.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation HL
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics, graph theory and technology-led problem solving, with Paper 3 built on extended data tasks. A correct calculator result with no stated model behind it earns a fraction of the credit.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation SL
subjects.description: Statistics, financial maths, functions and modelling across two papers. Students lose marks reporting a statistical result without interpreting it in the context the question established.

subjects.name: The maths exploration
subjects.description: Twelve to twenty pages of independent mathematical writing marked on five published criteria, with the use of mathematics carrying the most. Topic viability decides the mark long before the writing does.

subjects.name: Calculus
subjects.description: Limits, differentiation, integration, kinematics and differential equations at Higher Level. The reliable loss is rules in combination, and integrations attempted without naming the substitution first.

subjects.name: Statistics and inference
subjects.description: Distributions, hypothesis testing, correlation and regression, with harder inference at AI Higher Level. Marks go on choosing the right test and reporting hypotheses and conclusions in context.

subjects.name: Proof and reasoning
subjects.description: Direct proof, contradiction, induction and counterexample. Induction is highly structured, so students score nearly everything or nearly nothing, and learning the structure is the fix.

subjects.name: Modelling and justification
subjects.description: Fitting a model to data and defending the choice. Technology finds a model instantly; the marks are for explaining why that model rather than another, which is the step confident students skip.

subjects.name: Graphic display calculator technique
subjects.description: Modes, commands, statistical functions, and recording enough that a correct display earns full credit. One session here often returns more marks than a topic block and almost nobody offers it.

sections.heading: Shakhbout City against Mohammed Bin Zayed City, for maths
paragraphs: Set the two side by side and the differences are real but not educational. Shakhbout City is villa housing on compound streets with corridor schools ten to fifteen minutes away. Mohammed Bin Zayed City is a dense mainland grid with the broadest curriculum mix in the emirate, including Indian and Arab curriculum schools alongside British and IB ones. More schools, more families, more teachers in residence.

The instinct is that more teachers means better odds of finding a maths tutor, and in a raw sense that is true. It does not follow that your odds of finding an Analysis and Approaches Higher Level specialist with a free Tuesday improve proportionally, because the extra supply is spread across every curriculum that grid serves. A larger pool of maths teachers, most of whom teach a national curriculum or IGCSE, does not thicken the specific slice you need.

Meanwhile the two communities are fifteen to twenty-five minutes apart, so tutors serve both. A tutor living in Mohammed Bin Zayed City will take a Shakhbout City booking and price the drive into the rate; a Khalifa City tutor will take bookings in both. The practical supply is one corridor-wide pool allocated by who asked first.

Which leaves one genuine difference worth acting on: the school you choose, and therefore the time your child is home. From either community, a corridor school means a student at a desk before four and a real afternoon slot. A school on Yas or Saadiyat means an evening one. That is a decision about the school, made once, rather than a tutoring variable you keep revisiting.

sections.heading: The variable that actually matters: AA or AI
paragraphs: Analysis and Approaches is algebraic and proof-oriented, built on calculus and manipulation. Applications and Interpretation is modelling and statistical, built on using technology to make sense of real data. Both run at Higher and Standard Level, and Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level is a demanding course that many students find harder than Analysis and Approaches at Standard Level.

They reward different teaching. An AA specialist works on algebraic fluency, the structure of a proof, and calculus rules used in combination. An AI specialist works on choosing and justifying a model, running the right statistical test, and reporting a conclusion in the context the question set up. A tutor can do both adequately. Almost nobody does both well, and the one you want is whoever owns your child's course.

The route decision itself should rest on two inputs. Aptitude: a student who enjoys a clean algebraic argument belongs in AA, one who reasons well about real quantities and finds abstract manipulation thankless belongs in AI. And destination: engineering, physics, mathematics and economics courses frequently specify AA at Higher Level and some will not accept AI for them, while business, social sciences, design and many life sciences accept either.

Requirements vary by institution and change over time, so read the admissions pages for the universities actually on the student's list, including the universities in this country, which publish their own entry requirements. No tutoring page should be the source for an admissions rule. And if the route is already fixed and wrong, raise it in DP1 rather than DP2 — the switch is manageable in the first year and not in the second.

sections.heading: Six questions to ask any maths tutor before you pay
paragraphs: If the postcode is not the filter, something has to be. These six questions take ten minutes, cost nothing, and separate a route specialist from a capable generalist faster than any credential list. Ask them of anyone, including us.

First: which route and level is your main teaching, and how many students of that course do you currently have? A specialist answers immediately and specifically. Second: give them the marked script and ask what the four repeating errors are. A specialist names behaviours; a generalist describes the topic. Third, for a Higher Level student: how do you teach Paper 3, and how many complete papers will my child sit before the exam? If the answer is "we do Paper 3 questions", the structural skill is not being taught.

Fourth: what will you do about the exploration, and what will you not do? The right answer includes a clear refusal — they will not choose the topic, write, rewrite or edit to completion. Fifth: how will we know in six weeks whether this is working? A specialist names an external measure: the next school assessment, a timed paper, a marked draft. Sixth: what happens if you cannot help? Someone willing to say a subject or component is outside their strength is telling you something valuable about everything else they claim.

Those answers are more informative than years of experience, a list of schools, or any self-reported statistic. They are also the reason a family in this corridor should stop comparing communities: once you have asked them, the person's address has become the least interesting thing about them.

sections.heading: Where revision belongs, by level
paragraphs: Students revise as though all marks weigh the same. They do not, and the structure differs between the levels in a way that should drive the plan. Standard Level sits two papers plus the exploration. Higher Level sits three, and the third behaves unlike anything else in the course: two long, heavily scaffolded investigations where a later part depends on having set up an earlier one in a usable form.

For a Higher Level student that makes complete Paper 3 attempts non-optional. The skill is sustaining a line of reasoning across many parts, and it cannot be built by doing Paper 3 questions in isolation, because the thing examined is the connection between them. Three or four whole attempts under timing, marked and discussed, changes it. Topic knowledge alone does not.

For a Standard Level student none of that applies, and the time released should go to calculator discipline and to presenting method. Those two together usually recover more marks for an SL student than any topic block, because the losses are habitual rather than conceptual.

The exploration is the underweighted component at both levels. Roughly a fifth of the grade, marked internally against five published criteria and moderated by the IB, and the only part of the course where a student has months rather than hours. Marks lost there were entirely within the student's control. Confirm current weightings and components through your school, since the IB revises its subject guides on a cycle.

sections.heading: The marks nobody teaches, in either community
paragraphs: Three sources of lost marks appear on almost every Diploma maths script and are taught by almost nobody, in any community, at any price point. They are worth naming because they are cheap to fix and they are the reason a student can understand the mathematics and still score below their ability.

The first is working the marker cannot see. A student performs three steps mentally, writes one line, reaches the correct answer, and collects a fraction of the available method marks. It is a habit rather than a knowledge gap, and roughly three weeks of a tutor refusing to accept compressed steps changes it permanently. The gain appears on the very next marked paper, which makes it the fastest return available.

The second is the calculator. Angle modes left unset for a whole paper, fraction entry producing decimals, statistical functions used without recording the inputs, and correct displayed answers written down with nothing to support them. One session on calculator discipline regularly returns more marks than a topic block. Nobody sells it because it does not sound like teaching.

The third is the formula booklet. It is provided, which students take to mean it requires no preparation. A student who does not know roughly where things are loses a minute per question hunting, and a minute per question is a grade. Working with the booklet open from the start of DP1, rather than discovering it in the final term, costs nothing and is almost never suggested.

sections.heading: What a maths hour costs on either side of the corridor
paragraphs: Published market rates for this emirate, read in October 2026, are these. Budget online tutoring, typically a university student, at AED 45 to 150 an hour. A qualified subject tutor working online at AED 150 to 300. An in-home one-to-one visit at AED 180 to 500, with the journey inside the fee. A named IB or A-Level specialist at AED 200 to 450 and above. Premium examiner-led provision reaching AED 650.

Monthly, Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 estimates for weekly one-hour sessions come out at AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Those figures do not vary between Shakhbout City and Mohammed Bin Zayed City in any meaningful way, because the market is the corridor rather than the community.

What does vary slightly is the in-home premium, and it is smaller here than on the islands because the drives are shorter. It is honest to say that, and it is still a premium: somewhere between AED 30 and AED 200 an hour depending on where the tutor starts from, paid to a journey rather than to a mark scheme. Over a school year of weekly sessions that is a real figure, and it is the one line in a maths budget that can be removed without losing a minute of instruction.

IB Gram publishes no hourly price on this page. There is a free trial lesson and a consultation, and the number follows once the route, level and frequency are known. The figures above are the market's, included so you can price any quote you receive.

sections.heading: A specialist on a screen, or a generalist three streets away
paragraphs: Stated plainly, since the search is local: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. No tutor will travel to a Shakhbout City address. In-home tutoring is a service we run in India only. Lessons are live one-to-one video in Gulf Standard Time.

For maths the format needs one thing, and it is worth setting up in the first session rather than discovering later: the tutor must see handwritten working as it happens, through a camera angled at paper or a tablet and stylus. Without that the session becomes dictation and the student's own method — the thing that needed watching — is invisible.

With it, video has real maths advantages over a visitor. A shared whiteboard retains every worked line, so last week's integration can be reopened rather than reconstructed from a notebook. The exact past-paper question is pasted onto the board instantly. Two methods can sit side by side. And the student writes on their own paper in their own hand, which is precisely what the exam asks of them.

The comparison, then, is not convenience against inconvenience. It is a route specialist who can read your child's script against a competent generalist who lives nearby, with a shared whiteboard on one side and a notebook on the other. In this corridor, where the in-home travel premium is genuinely modest, that remains the argument — and it is an argument about the mathematics rather than about the drive.

sections.heading: Coverage, and the honest answer on availability
paragraphs: Since this page argues against the proximity filter, it should be honest about the filter we do apply. Standard Level in both routes is well covered and a trial lesson is usually arranged within a few days. Higher Level is in demand and can take up to a week. Specialist Paper 3 work is narrower, and some combinations are genuinely thin.

When the right specialist is not free, we say so before you pay and name the alternatives: wait for a slot, begin on exploration coaching or technique work with a specialist in that component, or take a tutor based outside the UAE who teaches the same syllabus and works to your evening in Gulf Standard Time. If a tutor is not UAE-based you are told before the trial lesson rather than after.

That disclosure is deliberate. Several providers in this market route UAE parents to contact numbers outside the country without stating where the teaching comes from, and no competitor researched for this market publishes a coverage limit at all. We would rather lose a booking than have a parent find out in week three.

On timing: Higher Level slots tighten in the second term as Diploma families across this corridor and the wider Gulf reach the same point in the calendar. The quickest route to a good maths tutor in February is to have asked in October, and if you are reading this in the autumn with a known weakness, that is the most useful line here.

faqs.question: Will I find a better IB maths tutor in Mohammed Bin Zayed City than in Shakhbout City?
faqs.answer: A larger pool of maths teachers, not a thicker slice of the one you need. Mohammed Bin Zayed City has the broadest curriculum mix in the emirate, so its extra supply is spread across national curricula, IGCSE and IB rather than concentrated in Diploma maths. The two communities are fifteen to twenty-five minutes apart, so tutors serve both and the practical pool is corridor-wide. What changes your odds is filtering on the route and level instead of the address, which is what online delivery allows.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether a maths tutor teaches AA or AI?
faqs.answer: More than anything else about them. Analysis and Approaches is algebraic, calculus-led and proof-oriented; Applications and Interpretation is modelling, statistical and technology-led. They reward different teaching: algebraic fluency and proof structure on one side, model justification and correct statistical reporting on the other. A tutor can cover both adequately and almost nobody covers both well. A tutor three streets away whose main course is the other route is a worse option than a specialist on a screen.

faqs.question: How do I tell a route specialist from a capable generalist?
faqs.answer: Give them your child's marked script and ask what the four repeating errors are. A specialist names behaviours — compressed working, an unset calculator mode, a conclusion stated without the question's context, a model used without justification — and says what each costs. A generalist explains the topic, which your child already understood. Then ask how they teach Paper 3 at Higher Level: if the answer is "we do Paper 3 questions" rather than complete papers under timing, the structural skill is not being taught.

faqs.question: What makes Paper 3 at Higher Level different, and how should it be practised?
faqs.answer: It is two long, heavily scaffolded investigations rather than a set of questions, and it examines the ability to sustain reasoning across many parts where a later part depends on an earlier one being set up usably. Students answer the early parts correctly in compressed form, then cannot build on their own work and lose the thread around part (c). Three or four complete attempts under timing, marked and discussed, fixes it. Isolated Paper 3 questions do not, because the connection between parts is the thing examined.

faqs.question: My child understands the maths but the grade will not move. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost always one of three habits rather than a knowledge gap. Working the marker cannot see: three steps done mentally, one line written, a fraction of the method marks awarded. A calculator left in the wrong mode or used without recording the commands, so a correct display earns little. And unfamiliarity with the formula booklet, which costs a minute per question hunting for what is already provided. Each is cheap to fix, each shows on the next marked paper, and none of them is taught by anyone.

faqs.question: Which single maths session returns the most marks?
faqs.answer: Calculator discipline, closely followed by working presentation. Modes, fraction and surd entry, statistical functions, and recording enough alongside a display that the mark scheme can award full credit. One hour, visible on the next paper. It is never offered because it sounds unimpressive next to a topic block on calculus. The expensive mistake is funding a year of general maths hours when the actual problem was a calculator setting and a habit of compressing three steps into one written line.

faqs.question: How do we choose between AA and AI if the school has not decided yet?
faqs.answer: On two inputs. Aptitude: a student who enjoys a clean algebraic argument belongs in Analysis and Approaches; one who reasons well about real quantities and finds abstract manipulation thankless belongs in Applications and Interpretation. And destination: engineering, physics, mathematics and economics courses frequently specify AA at Higher Level and some will not accept AI, while business, social sciences, design and many life sciences accept either. Read the admissions pages for the universities actually on the list, since requirements vary and change.

faqs.question: Is AI Higher Level easier than AA Standard Level?
faqs.answer: No, and many students find the opposite. Applications and Interpretation at Higher Level is a demanding course: advanced inference, graph theory, model justification and a Paper 3 built on extended data tasks. A student placed there because the name sounded gentler, who then has to defend a regression model every other question, is not in an easier position than an AA Standard Level student working on calculus. Choose on the mathematics the student is good at rather than on the perceived prestige or difficulty of the label.

faqs.question: What does an IB maths tutor cost around Shakhbout City?
faqs.answer: Published market figures read in October 2026: budget online tutoring at AED 45 to 150 an hour, a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150 to 300, an in-home visit at AED 180 to 500 with the drive inside the rate, a named IB specialist at AED 200 to 450 and above, and premium examiner-led provision reaching AED 650. Monthly, Bestimate's 2026 estimates give AED 600 to 1,200 for mid-range weekly sessions. Those figures do not differ meaningfully between the communities in this corridor.

faqs.question: Is the in-home premium worth paying in this corridor specifically?
faqs.answer: It is smaller here than on the islands, because the drives are ten to twenty-five minutes rather than cross-city, and it would be dishonest not to say so. But it is still a premium of roughly AED 30 to 200 an hour paid to a journey rather than to a mark scheme, and it buys you a generalist from the local pool rather than a route specialist. For a younger child who needs physical presence that may be the right trade. For a Higher Level Diploma student with a Paper 3 problem it is not.

faqs.question: Will an IB maths tutor come to our Shakhbout City villa?
faqs.answer: Not one of ours. IB Gram runs no home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we offer only in India. Lessons are live one-to-one video in Gulf Standard Time. For maths the format works provided the tutor can see handwritten working as it happens, via a camera on paper or a tablet and stylus, which we set up in the first session. The gain is a route specialist who can read a marked script rather than whoever in the corridor had a free Tuesday.

faqs.question: Where exactly is the line on exploration help?
faqs.answer: A tutor may test whether the topic can carry mathematics at the course level, explain what each of the five criteria rewards, read the student's own draft and name the criterion it undersells, teach notation and citation, and discuss the mathematics as mathematics. A tutor may not choose the topic and hand it over, write or rewrite any part of the text, edit a draft to completion, supply data the student did not generate, or produce a model exploration for adaptation. The student signs the authenticity declaration.

faqs.question: How quickly can we get a Higher Level maths specialist?
faqs.answer: Standard Level in either route is usually a few days to a trial lesson. Higher Level is in demand and can take up to a week, and specialist Paper 3 work is thinner again. If nobody suitable is free we say so before you pay and name the alternatives: wait for a slot, start on exploration coaching or technique work with a specialist in that component, or take a tutor based outside the UAE who teaches the same syllabus and works to your evening. Non-UAE delivery is disclosed before the trial, not afterwards.

faqs.question: When should a Shakhbout City family start looking for maths help?
faqs.answer: The autumn term, for two reasons. Academically it is the cheap window: foundations are being laid, habits can still be changed rather than patched, and there is no immovable deadline competing for the hours. Operationally, Higher Level slots tighten in the second term as Diploma families across this corridor and the wider Gulf reach the same point in the calendar. The fastest route to a good maths tutor in February is to have asked in October, which is advice that costs nothing to follow.

faqs.question: What should we send before a free IB maths trial in this corridor?
faqs.answer: The route and level, the school name, the last two marked maths assessments with the teacher's comments, and a draft exploration if one exists. Plus the time your child is actually home — from a corridor school that is usually before four, and from a school on Yas or Saadiyat considerably later. With that in hand the trial works on a real script, and at the end you can put the six questions to the tutor and judge the answers rather than the credentials.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-yas-island.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma mathematics to Abu Dhabi students, including Yas Island families. Each works habitually in one of the four routes, because Analysis and Approaches at higher level and Applications and Interpretation at standard level share a topic list and almost nothing else.

intro.heading: The five topic areas, and why the route changes all of them
paragraphs: Both Diploma mathematics courses are built on the same five topic areas: number and algebra, functions, geometry and trigonometry, statistics and probability, and calculus. That shared structure is why families assume the two routes are variants of one subject. Inside each topic area the content diverges sharply, and in several places the divergence is the difference between a proof course and a modelling course.

Take number and algebra. Analysis and Approaches at higher level includes proof by induction and proof by contradiction, complex numbers in Cartesian, polar and exponential form, and the binomial theorem extended to fractional and negative indices. Applications and Interpretation at higher level takes the same topic area somewhere else entirely: matrices and their eigenvalues, graph theory, adjacency matrices and Markov chains. A tutor who teaches one of those every week and takes a student in the other is not slightly out of position. They are teaching a different syllabus.

Calculus diverges in the same way. Analysis and Approaches at higher level carries implicit differentiation, related rates, integration by substitution and by parts, Maclaurin series and differential equations solved by separation of variables and by Euler's method. Applications and Interpretation at higher level does calculus through modelling and numerical methods, with the emphasis on setting up and interpreting rather than on technique for its own sake.

Statistics runs the other way. Applications and Interpretation carries considerably more of it: linear and non-linear regression, the chi-squared test for independence, the t-test, and at standard level Voronoi diagrams as a genuinely distinctive piece of applied geometry. Analysis and Approaches keeps statistics lighter and more conventional, which is why an Analysis and Approaches student asked to interpret a correlation coefficient sometimes produces a correct number and no meaning.

The practical consequence for a Yas Island family is that the first useful question is not about mathematics at all. It is which of the four courses your child is in, and whether the person you are about to pay teaches it as their main work. That question costs nothing to ask, and in this market nothing else reliably filters a specialist from a generalist, because the published hourly bands overlap completely. A tutor who answers that question with a yes and no detail has told you something; a tutor who answers it with the name of the route and the strand they find students struggle with most has told you considerably more.

The second half of this page is about the examination rather than the content: what each paper demands, why the non-calculator paper separates classwork from performance, what the graphical display calculator must be used for and recorded, and the anatomy of Paper 3 at higher level. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. No IB session or results date appears here, because none has been confirmed from the IB's own site.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-yas-island.programmesIntro: Four courses, not two, and a tutor should be matched to one of them. These are the Diploma mathematics routes a Yas Island household will be choosing between or already in.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, higher level
programmes.description: The most demanding of the four. Three papers weighted 30, 30 and 20 per cent with the exploration at 20. Adds proof by induction and contradiction, complex numbers in all three forms, de Moivre's theorem, vectors, Maclaurin series, implicit differentiation, integration by substitution and parts, and differential equations. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator.
programmes.countryNote: Often the expected route for engineering, mathematics and physics applications, though requirements vary by university and faculty and should be read from each institution's own statement. Abu Dhabi Diploma schools do not all offer it to the same cohort size, so a Yas Island student may be in a very small class.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches, standard level
programmes.description: Two papers weighted 40 per cent each with the exploration at 20. Covers functions, the binomial theorem, trigonometric identities and equations, differentiation and integration including kinematics, and conventional statistics with the binomial and normal distributions. Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, which is where most of the separation between students appears.
programmes.countryNote: The most commonly taken of the four in Abu Dhabi, and the route where a late switch from higher level most often lands. A student arriving from Analysis and Approaches at higher level mid-course has content to drop rather than acquire, which is a different and much easier adjustment.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation, higher level
programmes.description: Three papers weighted 30, 30 and 20 with the exploration at 20, and a calculator permitted throughout. Adds matrices including eigenvalues and eigenvectors, graph theory with adjacency matrices, Markov chains, non-linear regression, the t-test, and calculus approached through modelling and numerical methods including Euler's method.
programmes.countryNote: A genuinely distinctive course rather than an easier higher level, and the route where a tutor mismatch does the most damage, because the content a generalist expects to find is largely absent and the content that is there is unfamiliar to most Analysis and Approaches teachers.

programmes.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation, standard level
programmes.description: Two papers weighted 40 per cent each with the exploration at 20, calculator permitted on both. Covers financial applications of sequences including loans and annuities, Voronoi diagrams, linear regression and correlation, the chi-squared test for independence, the normal and binomial distributions, trigonometry in context and introductory differentiation.
programmes.countryNote: Frequently chosen by students heading for business, design, social sciences and several life-science courses, and the route where marks are most often lost not to mathematics but to giving a number without saying what it means in the situation the question described.

abu-dhabi/ib-maths-tutor-in-yas-island.subjectsIntro: These are the strands a Diploma mathematics tutor is actually asked to teach, written as a specialist would diagnose them: what the strand contains in each route and what the examiner rewards inside it.

subjects.name: Proof: induction and contradiction
subjects.description: Proof by mathematical induction follows a fixed four-part structure, and marks are awarded for the structure as much as for the algebra: base case, inductive assumption stated explicitly, inductive step, conclusion. Students who do the algebra and omit the assumption statement lose marks they had already earned.

subjects.name: Complex numbers
subjects.description: Cartesian, modulus-argument and exponential forms, de Moivre's theorem, roots of unity and loci in the complex plane. The recurring loss is argument conventions: giving an argument outside the required range, or omitting the general solution when all roots are wanted.

subjects.name: Matrices, graph theory and Markov chains
subjects.description: Matrix multiplication, determinants, inverses, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, adjacency matrices, transition matrices and steady states. Entirely absent from Analysis and Approaches, which is why a tutor mismatch in this direction is so costly.

subjects.name: Functions and their transformations
subjects.description: Composite and inverse functions, domain and range, rational functions, asymptotes and the effect of each transformation on a graph. The sign of a horizontal translation remains the single most reliable trap in the topic, in every route and at both levels.

subjects.name: Trigonometry and identities
subjects.description: Radian measure, the unit circle, compound and double angle identities, and trigonometric equations over a stated interval. Marks are lost for giving one solution where the interval contains several, and for not stating which identity a proof started from.

subjects.name: Voronoi diagrams and applied geometry
subjects.description: Perpendicular bisectors, cells, the nearest-neighbour interpolation and the toxic waste dump problem. A distinctive strand with no Analysis and Approaches equivalent, and one that rewards careful construction and a clearly stated interpretation of what a cell means.

subjects.name: Regression and correlation
subjects.description: Linear regression, the correlation coefficient, and at higher level non-linear models. The discriminating skill is interpretation: stating what the gradient means in the context, and whether extrapolation beyond the data is reasonable. A bare coefficient earns little.

subjects.name: Statistical tests
subjects.description: The chi-squared test for independence and goodness of fit, and at higher level the t-test. Marks follow the structure: stating the hypotheses, the degrees of freedom, the critical value or probability, and a conclusion in context rather than a bare reject or accept.

subjects.name: Differentiation and its applications
subjects.levels: All four routes, at very different depths
subjects.description: From introductory rates of change in Applications and Interpretation at standard level to implicit differentiation and related rates in Analysis and Approaches at higher level. In every route the recurring loss is a stationary point found and its nature never determined.

subjects.name: Integration techniques
subjects.description: Definite and indefinite integration, areas and volumes of revolution, and at higher level substitution and integration by parts. Students lose marks for omitting the constant, for not changing limits after a substitution, and for treating an area below the axis as negative when the question wanted magnitude.

subjects.name: Differential equations and series
subjects.description: Separation of variables, Euler's method, slope fields, and Maclaurin series including their use in approximation. The most technically demanding strand in any of the four routes, and the one most often reached last and practised least.

subjects.name: Financial applications of sequences
subjects.description: Compound interest, depreciation, loans, annuities and amortisation, usually handled on the calculator's finance application. The method mark depends on recording which values were entered, because a bare final figure shows the examiner nothing about how it was obtained.

sections.heading: What Analysis and Approaches has that Applications and Interpretation does not, and the reverse
paragraphs: This is the comparison that decides whether a tutor is the right tutor, and it is more concrete than the usual description of one route as algebraic and the other as applied. Inside the five shared topic areas, each route carries substantial content the other does not touch at all, and a generalist will be fluent in half of it.

Analysis and Approaches at higher level carries proof by induction and contradiction, complex numbers in all three forms with de Moivre's theorem, vectors and vector geometry, Maclaurin series, implicit differentiation and related rates, integration by substitution and by parts, and differential equations solved by separation of variables and by Euler's method. None of that appears in Applications and Interpretation, where a student will never be asked to prove anything by induction.

Applications and Interpretation at higher level carries matrices with eigenvalues and eigenvectors, graph theory with adjacency and transition matrices, Markov chains and steady states, non-linear regression, and the t-test. At standard level it adds Voronoi diagrams and the financial applications of sequences including loans and annuities. None of that appears in Analysis and Approaches, where a student will never construct a Voronoi cell.

The overlap, which is real, sits in functions, basic trigonometry, descriptive statistics, the binomial and normal distributions and introductory differentiation. A tutor can be competent across the overlap and useless at the edges, and it is the edges that separate grades. The table below sets the divergence out so that a parent can ask a specific question rather than a general one.

sections.heading: The papers, and what each one actually tests
paragraphs: At standard level there are two papers carrying forty per cent each, with the exploration at twenty. At higher level there are three carrying thirty, thirty and twenty, again with the exploration at twenty. Those weightings are the reason a run-in should be allocated deliberately rather than spent on whatever feels hardest.

In Analysis and Approaches, Paper 1 is sat without a calculator. That single constraint changes what the paper can ask and therefore what it tests: exact values, algebraic manipulation carried through by hand, trigonometric values from the unit circle, and integration that resolves cleanly. It is the component where classwork and examination performance diverge most sharply, because a student who has worked with a screen in front of them has never built the fluency it assumes.

Paper 2 permits the graphical display calculator, and the trap is the opposite one. A student can produce a correct value in a single keystroke sequence, write the number, collect the accuracy mark and forfeit every method mark that was available for showing the set-up. On a long question that is the difference between full marks and two out of six, and it is purely a recording habit.

Paper 3 exists only at higher level, carries twenty per cent, and is an extended problem-solving investigation. Students who can do every topic still lose marks here, because the difficulty is structural: a multi-part investigation requires reading a long stem accurately, carrying an early result forward correctly, and not abandoning the thread when one part resists. It is a practised skill, and it is the component most often left untouched until the final weeks.

sections.heading: The non-calculator paper, in detail
paragraphs: For an Analysis and Approaches student, Paper 1 is the component that most often explains a grade a family did not expect. The mechanism is simple and it is a habit rather than a deficiency. A student who has done every exercise with a calculator available has never been required to hold a fraction in their head, simplify a surd, recall an exact trigonometric value, or carry an algebraic expression through four lines without arithmetic support.

What the paper assumes is specific and listable. Exact values of sine, cosine and tangent at the standard angles. Fluent manipulation of surds and rational expressions. Logarithm laws applied without a calculator check. Differentiation and integration of standard forms recognised on sight. Factorisation of quadratics and cubics by inspection. None of that is conceptually hard, and all of it decays without use.

The remedy is unglamorous and works: short, frequent, deliberately non-calculator practice, started early. Ten minutes of exact-value drill four times a week will do more over a term than a single long session will do in a month. That is why this belongs in the first Diploma year rather than in the final term, and why a family deciding when to spend on mathematics should put some of it early rather than all of it late.

What can be fixed late is timing. A student who has never sat the paper under conditions does not know how long it takes them without a calculator, which means they do not know whether to attempt questions in order or to skip. Measuring that, and then deciding an order deliberately, is worth real marks and takes two sessions. It does not substitute for fluency, but it is the available gain when fluency work has been left too late.

Short frequent drills beat long occasional sessions for this specifically
