sections.heading: The calculator: what must be used and what must be written
paragraphs: On every paper where a graphical display calculator is permitted, it is both the most useful tool in the room and the most reliable way to lose method marks. The marks exist for showing the mathematics; the calculator produces the answer without showing anything. A student who does not bridge that gap on paper gives away marks on questions they answered correctly.

The discipline has three parts and all three have to be automatic before the examination. Write the rule, formula or equation being solved. Write what is being entered, including which function is being used and with what values, so that a reader can see the set-up. Then give the result, keeping full precision in the calculator and rounding only on the final line to whatever form the question demanded.

There is a second category of calculator work that is explicitly expected rather than optional, particularly in Applications and Interpretation. Regression lines and correlation coefficients, chi-squared and t-test outputs, normal and binomial probabilities, numerical solutions to equations, and financial calculations involving loans and annuities are all intended to be produced on the calculator. The marks attach to stating the model, the hypotheses, the degrees of freedom or the entered values, and then to interpreting the output in context.

That interpretation step is where Applications and Interpretation students most often fall short. The calculator gives a correlation coefficient; the question wanted to know what the relationship means for the situation described and whether extrapolation is reasonable. The calculator gives a probability; the question wanted a conclusion about the hypotheses stated in context. A number with no sentence attached collects part of the marks at best, and that pattern is visible immediately on a marked script.

sections.heading: Paper 3 at higher level: anatomy of a long investigation
paragraphs: Paper 3 is worth twenty per cent of the higher level grade, exists in both routes, and is structurally unlike anything else in the Diploma mathematics course. It presents one or two extended investigations, each built from a long stem that introduces a situation or a piece of mathematics, followed by parts that develop it progressively. The mathematics is drawn from the course. The demand is sustained reasoning under time pressure.

Three failure modes dominate. The first is not reading the stem properly: a student skims the introduction, starts part (a), and discovers in part (d) that a definition they skipped was the whole point. The second is mis-carrying a result: part (b) produces an expression that parts (c) and (d) rely on, and an error there propagates, which is survivable if method is visible and fatal if only answers are written. The third is abandonment: a part resists, the student stops, and the remaining parts that did not depend on it go unanswered.

All three are addressed by the same practice, which is why Paper 3 needs its own block rather than being folded into general revision. Sit a past investigation under timed conditions. Mark it together. Then work specifically on the transitions: what the stem established, which result each part depends on, and what to do when one part will not come out. Students who do this four or five times stop treating the paper as unpredictable.

In Applications and Interpretation, Paper 3 investigations lean towards modelling and data contexts, which rewards the interpretation discipline described above. In Analysis and Approaches they lean towards developing a piece of pure mathematics step by step, which rewards algebraic care and willingness to keep going. Different content, identical structural demand, and in both cases a component that is routinely left until there is no time left for it.
bullets: Read and annotate the stem before attempting part (a)
Keep method visible so a mis-carried result does not cost every later mark
Move on when a part resists; later parts may not depend on it

sections.heading: Where a tutor's role ends on the exploration
paragraphs: The exploration carries twenty per cent of the grade in all four routes and is marked out of twenty across five criteria. A tutor's role in it is real, bounded and worth stating in writing, because in this market it is not universally observed.

What a tutor may do: explain each criterion and what its marks are awarded for, so the student knows that presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics are each marked separately. Test whether a topic the student has proposed contains enough mathematics to reach the top band, and whether it is pitched at the level of their own course rather than below it. Teach the techniques the student has chosen to use. Read a draft the student has written and say where it does not yet meet a criterion.

What no tutor may do: write the exploration, rewrite a draft into its final form, edit it to completion, or supply text for submission. The IB's academic-honesty framework makes authorship the student's responsibility, and a malpractice finding costs the student their Diploma rather than costing a provider a sale. One page competing for these searches sells completed internal assessments outright at a published price.

The same limit applies to materials. We do not reproduce or distribute IB, Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides. They belong to the boards, are published through the boards' own channels, and reach students through their school. A tutor's job is to teach a student to use them, which is a skill that outlasts any file they could be handed.

sections.heading: Reading a Diploma maths script like a specialist
paragraphs: A parent can do a useful first pass on a marked paper in fifteen minutes, and the exercise is worth more than a reported grade. Start by separating the losses into mathematics the student could not do and mathematics they could do but did not write down in a form the scheme could reward. In most mid-band scripts the second pile is larger, and it is the cheaper one to fix.

Then look for specific patterns. Bare final answers on multi-step questions are forfeited method marks: count them. Stationary points found with their nature never determined is a recurring loss in every route. Values rounded at an intermediate step and carried forward drift away from the accuracy mark. Calculator results given with no recorded set-up collect the answer mark and nothing else. Each of those is a habit, not a gap in knowledge.

Next look at the end of the paper. Blank final questions alongside heavily worked earlier ones is a timing problem, and timing is fixed by practising allocation and order rather than by learning more content. Final questions attempted and scoring poorly is a content problem in the strands they came from, which is what a strand repair block exists for.

Finally, in Applications and Interpretation specifically, look for numbers without sentences. A correlation coefficient stated and not interpreted, a test statistic produced and no conclusion drawn in context, a gradient calculated and never explained. That pattern is the single most common and most correctable failure in that route, and it is invisible in a grade.
bullets: Separate losses into cannot-do and did-not-write-down

sections.heading: Fitting a maths session around the Yas Island day
paragraphs: Campuses serving Yas Island finish their taught day between about 14:45 and 15:30, with co-curricular sessions running later on some days. A student at a campus on the island itself is often home by 15:45. A student travelling to the Khalifa City or Al Raha corridor is typically not home before 16:15, and later still on an activity day.

Allowing three quarters of an hour at home, the honest earliest start is 16:30 for an island campus and 17:30 for a mainland commute. Our Abu Dhabi scheduling range runs from 16:30 to 21:00 Gulf Standard Time, and the slots that survive a full Diploma year are the ones at 18:00 and 18:30. The island's event calendar, including the Grand Prix weekend at the end of the first term, changes access and road conditions for residents, which is a factor for an in-home arrangement and not for a lesson delivered over live video.

Session length should follow the component. Paper work needs ninety minutes, because the working unit is a paper sat under conditions plus the marking afterwards and the marking is where the learning happens. Exploration coaching works in sixty, since the material is the student's own draft. Non-calculator fluency drills work best in forty-five minutes, frequently, rather than ninety minutes occasionally.

For context on cost, published market bands put in-home one-to-one at AED 180-500 an hour with travel included against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. Bestimate quotes AED 180-350 for in-home, Unitors lists IB tuition from AED 200, TutorChase quotes AED 270 and Bestimate puts the specialist band at AED 200-450 and upwards. Those are attributed market figures rather than our prices, and IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE.

faqs.question: Do the two IB maths routes really teach different content?
faqs.answer: Yes, substantially, inside the same five topic area names. Analysis and Approaches at higher level carries proof by induction and contradiction, complex numbers with de Moivre's theorem, Maclaurin series and differential equations. Applications and Interpretation at higher level carries matrices with eigenvalues, graph theory, Markov chains and the t-test, none of which appears in Analysis and Approaches. The overlap is real but sits in the easier material, and it is the edges that separate grades.

faqs.question: What should I ask to check a tutor knows my child's route?
faqs.answer: Ask which route and level they teach most weeks, then ask something specific to it. For Analysis and Approaches at higher level: how a proof by induction is structured and where the marks sit. For Applications and Interpretation at higher level: what a steady state in a Markov chain means and how it is found. For Applications and Interpretation at standard level: what a Voronoi cell represents. A specialist answers immediately; a generalist talks about topics in general.

faqs.question: Why does my child score well in class and badly on Paper 1?
faqs.answer: Because in Analysis and Approaches Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, and a student who has done every exercise with one available has never built the fluency the paper assumes: exact trigonometric values, surd manipulation, logarithm laws applied by hand, standard derivatives and integrals recognised on sight. It is a habit rather than a deficiency. Short frequent non-calculator drills fix it over a term, which is why the work belongs in the first Diploma year.

faqs.question: How do calculator-permitted papers cost marks?
faqs.answer: By letting a student produce a correct value without showing anything. The accuracy mark is collected and every method mark available for the set-up is forfeited, which on a long question is the difference between full marks and a fraction of them. The discipline is to write the rule or equation, write what is being entered and with which values, then give the result, keeping full precision and rounding only on the final line to the form the question required.

faqs.question: What exactly is Paper 3 and how should it be prepared?
faqs.answer: An extended problem-solving paper sat only at higher level, worth twenty per cent of the grade, presenting one or two long investigations built from a stem followed by progressively developing parts. The mathematics is from the course; the demand is sustained reasoning under time pressure. Prepare it by sitting four or five past investigations under conditions and marking them together, with specific work on reading the stem, carrying results forward, and moving on when a part resists.

faqs.question: Which strands cost Applications and Interpretation students the most marks?
faqs.answer: Interpretation, consistently. The calculator produces a correlation coefficient, a test statistic or a probability, and the question wanted to know what it means for the situation described, whether extrapolation is reasonable, or what conclusion follows about the stated hypotheses. A number with no sentence attached collects part of the marks at best. After that come degrees of freedom in a chi-squared test and recording the values entered in a financial calculation.

faqs.question: Which strands cost Analysis and Approaches students the most marks?
faqs.answer: In higher level, integration techniques and differential equations, which are reached last in most schemes of work and practised least. Specific traps: not changing the limits after a substitution, omitting the constant of integration, and treating an area below the axis as negative when magnitude was wanted. In complex numbers, giving an argument outside the required range. In proof by induction, doing the algebra and omitting the explicit statement of the inductive assumption.

faqs.question: Is a stationary point question really worth a separate lesson?
faqs.answer: It recurs in every route and at both levels, and the loss pattern is identical: the student differentiates correctly, solves for the coordinates and never determines the nature of the point. The marks for determining nature, by the second derivative or a sign change, are separately available and routinely unclaimed. It is a two-minute correction that pays across two years of papers, which makes it a good example of why method work outperforms content work for a mid-band student.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send maths tutors to Yas Island homes?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, including Yas Island; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Abu Dhabi families are taught one-to-one over live video, scheduled to Gulf Standard Time. On this island there is a practical bonus: large-scale event weekends, including the Grand Prix weekend at the end of the first term, change access and road conditions, and a lesson over video is unaffected by either.

faqs.question: My child is in a very small Applications and Interpretation class. Does that matter?
faqs.answer: It can. Diploma class sizes on the island's campuses vary, and a student in a route with few classmates has less peer support, fewer worked examples discussed in the room, and sometimes a teacher covering the route alongside another. That is not a criticism of the school; it is a consequence of cohort size. It does mean a tutor who teaches that exact route weekly adds more than they would for a student in a large standard level cohort.

faqs.question: How long should a Diploma maths session be?
faqs.answer: Let the component decide. Paper work needs ninety minutes, because the unit is a paper sat under conditions plus the marking, and the marking is where the learning happens. Exploration coaching works in sixty, since the material is the student's own draft. Non-calculator fluency drills work better in forty-five minutes frequently than ninety minutes occasionally, because fluency is built by repetition rather than by duration.

faqs.question: What can a tutor do on the maths exploration?
faqs.answer: Explain each of the five criteria and what its marks are awarded for, test whether a topic the student has proposed contains enough mathematics to reach the top band and is pitched at the level of their own course, teach the techniques the student has chosen to use, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. No tutor may write it, rewrite it into its final form, edit it to completion or supply text for submission. Authorship is the student's responsibility under IB rules.

faqs.question: Can a tutor give us past IB papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: No, and be wary of anyone offering a downloadable library of them. IB, Cambridge and Pearson syllabus guides, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the boards, are published through the boards' own channels, and reach students through their school. We cite and link them. What is worth teaching is how to read a mark scheme critically, which is a skill a student keeps and a file is not.

faqs.question: What time can a ninety-minute session start for a Yas Island student?
faqs.answer: A student at a campus on the island itself is often home by about 15:45, which makes a 16:30 start workable with room for ninety minutes before dinner. A student commuting to the Khalifa City or Al Raha corridor is typically not home before 16:15, so 17:30 is the honest earliest and 18:00 is more durable across a full Diploma year. Our Abu Dhabi range runs 16:30 to 21:00 Gulf Standard Time.

faqs.question: What is the fastest improvement available to a mid-band Diploma maths student?
faqs.answer: Writing the method down. A mid-band script typically contains a substantial number of bare final answers on multi-step questions, calculator results given with no recorded set-up, stationary points with no nature determined, and intermediate rounding carried forward. Each of those forfeits marks on mathematics the student already knew. Three sessions of work on the student's own scripts fixes the habits, adds no new content, and shows up on the next paper rather than next term.

intro.heading: The same plan costs different amounts depending on when you ask
paragraphs: Every Diploma family in Abu Dhabi becomes aware of the May session at roughly the same moment, and that moment is late. The consequence is a market where identical work carries two prices. Published rates in this emirate, read in October 2026, put a qualified online subject tutor at AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors listing IB tuition from AED 200 and TutorChase quoting AED 270 for specialist work; the Bestimate survey puts IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200-450 and above, and premium named listings reach AED 650 at BartyED. A family booking early transacts in the lower half of that spread with a choice of tutor. A family booking in the final weeks transacts at the top with whoever remains.

That is not a discount structure; it is supply. Higher Level mathematics, Higher Level physics and the scarcer Diploma options have a limited number of tutors in or serving this emirate, and demand for them concentrates into the same eight weeks every year. Booking early does not only cost less per hour. It buys the specific person who has taught the component that is failing, which in a final-term plan is the variable that actually determines whether anything moves.

The second thing the calendar changes is what the money can buy at all. At twenty weeks out, a genuine content gap in two subjects is addressable: there is time to teach, test, and re-test. At eight weeks, content teaching competes with technique work and technique usually wins on return. At three weeks, almost nothing that requires learning new material is purchasable, and the honest offer narrows to paper technique, timing, and the two or three repairs that are habits rather than knowledge.

The third is triage, which is the part families resist. With six subjects, three core components and a finite number of weeks, spreading effort evenly produces six marginal improvements and no change in the points total. Picking the two subjects closest to a grade boundary, and inside each the component carrying the most weight, is how a bounded budget changes a result. A plan that declines to name what it is leaving alone has not triaged; it has just promised everything.

Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. The cost argument runs in the family's favour and sharpens in the final weeks, because the in-home premium is a travel cost paid at the worst time of day. The Bestimate survey puts qualified in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 an hour, with independent home tutors quoted at AED 200-500, against AED 150-300 for comparable work online — and in a scarce-subject scramble the online pool is the only one with any depth left.

programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi Diploma programmes set internal Internal Assessment and Extended Essay deadlines through Year 1 and into Year 2. Ask the IB coordinator for the whole schedule in writing at the start of Year 1, because the collisions that produce a final-term emergency are visible a year in advance.

programmes.name: The autumn of Diploma Year 2, twenty weeks and more out
programmes.description: The cheapest point at which to buy real preparation, because content is still purchasable and the independent components are still open. Rates sit in the middle of the published range and the scarce-subject specialists are still available. Most families do not call now, which is why those specialists are still available.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi school calendars put a long winter break in this stretch, and it is the most useful block in the final year: a short intensive inside it addresses a content gap in a way weekly sessions through a term cannot.

programmes.name: The spring, eight to twelve weeks out
programmes.description: The point at which most families call. Demand across the emirate concentrates here, scarce-subject availability thins, and the published bands harden toward their upper ends. Content teaching now competes with technique work, and technique usually wins on return per hour because the habits move faster than the knowledge.
programmes.countryNote: Ramadan moves earlier in the Gregorian calendar each year, so its position relative to the final revision period shifts between examination years. Check where it falls for your child's cohort, because it changes when sessions can be held and how much output a week realistically contains.

programmes.name: The final three weeks and study leave
programmes.description: The point at which the honest offer narrows sharply. Timing, question-order strategy, command-term discipline and two or three specific repairs are purchasable. Learning a topic from nothing is not, and a provider selling it is selling reassurance. Most of what a student does in these weeks they do alone, which is a scheduling problem rather than a tutoring one.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session. No specific IB examination or results date appears on this page, because the IB's own site blocks automated checking and no date here has been confirmed from the IB directly. Confirm every date with the school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org.

abu-dhabi/ib-may-session-exam-preparatio.subjectsIntro: Final-term rates move by subject because supply does. These are the Diploma subjects Abu Dhabi families most often request for May session preparation, with where each sits in the published bands and why.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The most requested and least supplied Higher Level subject in this emirate, which puts it at the top of the qualified band and frequently into the specialist band of AED 200-450. Higher Level Paper 3 is the component most often booked alone, and a single-component booking is usually the cheapest useful purchase.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Better supplied than the Analysis route and priced mid-band. Statistics and modelling work suits a shared screen and a spreadsheet, so there is no quality argument for paying a travel premium on top.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Scarce at Higher Level and therefore priced near the top of the qualified band or above. Much of the final-term loss is mathematical rather than conceptual, which means an hour of algebra and graph linearisation often buys more marks than an hour of content at the same rate.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Reasonably supplied at both levels and mid-band. Mole fluency is the highest-return final-term repair because a weakness there costs marks across energetics, equilibrium, electrochemistry and organic yield simultaneously.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The best supplied of the sciences and most likely to be available at the lower end of the qualified band. The final-term work is command-term discipline and data-question technique, both of which respond to marking rather than to teaching hours.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Mid-band and well supplied. Diagram accuracy is the cheapest grade movement available in the subject, and Higher Level adds a third paper whose question style is worth practising separately from the other two.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Widely supplied and mid-band, and often the subject where a family can safely use fewer hours. Paper 1 guided analysis technique is the most coachable element available in the final weeks.

subjects.name: History and the human sciences
subjects.description: Variable supply by subject and mid-band generally. Essay-planning discipline under time is the final-term gain here: a plan written in three minutes changes the structure of an answer more than additional content recall does.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: By the final term these are usually submitted, which means they are no longer purchasable. Up to three Diploma points sat in them and the window closed earlier in the year. That is the clearest illustration on this page of what late booking costs.

subjects.name: Scarce Higher Level options
subjects.levels: Further Mathematics, Global Politics, Music, Film, ab initio languages
subjects.description: Where supply is genuinely thin, availability rather than rate becomes the constraint in the final term. The honest answer is sometimes a wait with a date, a tutor outside the UAE on the same platform, or a referral elsewhere.

abu-dhabi/ib-may-session-exam-preparatio.regionsIntro: Online delivery means the rate does not move with the postcode. What the area changes is the in-home quote a family is weighing and how much of the final weeks disappears into travel.

regions.name: Khalifa City and Al Raha
regions.note: Villa communities where the in-home premium is largest because of driving distance, and where a student loses an hour each way to the school run. In the final weeks that hour is the scarcest thing a family has, which makes the online comparison starker here than anywhere else.

regions.name: Al Reem Island and Al Maryah
regions.note: Short commutes and a denser in-home market, so the travel premium is narrower. Even so the published in-home band sits above the online one, and tower access adds unbilled time at both ends of a session.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: A small number of schools with mature Diploma programmes, which means local demand for the same specialists spikes in the same fortnight. Booking in the autumn saves more here in availability terms than in rate terms.

regions.name: Yas Island and Al Zeina
regions.note: Growing communities with substantial internal travel to school. Study leave changes the arithmetic in these areas more than most, because once a student is home all day the constraint becomes structure rather than time.

regions.name: Al Bateen, Al Mushrif and the Corniche
regions.note: Established schools with long-running Diploma cohorts and well-published study leave arrangements. Families here usually know the school's final-term calendar, which makes a backwards plan straightforward to build.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Shakhbout City
regions.note: Longer commutes and a wide curricular mix. Travel quotes to this corridor sit at the higher end of the in-home range, which in a final term where every hour counts is a poor trade.

regions.name: Al Reef, Al Shamkha and Al Ain
regions.note: Greater distances and, in Al Ain, a separate school ecosystem under the same emirate regulator. For scarce Higher Level subjects the local pool is effectively nil, which makes online delivery the only route rather than the cheaper one.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi island and Saadiyat Diploma provision
schoolClusters.note: Mature programmes with full Higher Level offerings and established final-term revision programmes. Families here are usually buying one or two scarce subjects for a small number of hours rather than broad support.
schools: American Community School of Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City, Al Raha and the eastern communities
schoolClusters.note: International schools with Diploma cohorts of varying size. Where a cohort is small, a subject may run at one level only or share a teacher across levels, which changes what independent marking is worth in the final term.
schools: The British International School Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: Schools running A Levels alongside or instead of the Diploma
schoolClusters.note: Where both programmes exist, final-term demand splits across two examination calendars and the school's study leave arrangements may differ by programme. Worth confirming rather than assuming, because it changes when sessions can be held.

abu-dhabi/ib-may-session-exam-preparatio.modesIntro: Three shapes of final-term purchase, costed by what they actually require rather than sold as a package. Which one fits depends on the weeks remaining and on what a marked script says.

modes.title: Independent re-mark and triage report
modes.description: A single piece of work rather than a plan. The student's most recent mock script re-marked against the published criteria, with every lost mark assigned to content, misapplication, command term or timing, and a written report naming the two subjects worth the remaining weeks and the components to leave alone. Some families stop here.
bullets: Existing mock script re-marked; no new paper required
Loss distribution reported rather than a total
Two-subject shortlist with the marks behind the choice
One fixed piece of work with nothing continuing

modes.title: Weekly component clinic in one or two subjects
modes.description: Sixty minutes a week per subject on a single named component, with a timed question set between sessions and marked before the next. The hour count is stated at the outset and reviewed at the halfway point, because the point of an hour count rather than a subscription is that it can be reduced.
bullets: 60 minutes weekly per subject, one named component per slot
Timed component marked before the session, never during it
Stated hour count, reviewed and reducible at the midpoint
Published band: AED 150-300 qualified, 200-450 for a named specialist

modes.title: Final-fortnight technique block
modes.description: Two or three short sessions in the last weeks on the things that are still purchasable: question-order strategy, timing across a long paper, command-term discipline, and calculator or formula-booklet fluency. Explicitly not content teaching, because at that range content teaching is reassurance rather than preparation.
bullets: Two or three short sessions, no content teaching

sections.heading: What May session preparation costs, by weeks remaining
paragraphs: The useful way to price final-term preparation is not per hour but per week remaining, because the weeks determine both the rate a family will meet and what the hours can accomplish. At twenty weeks out a Diploma family in Abu Dhabi is dealing with a market that has spare capacity: the scarce-subject specialists are uncommitted, the published bands sit where they sit, and a request for Higher Level mathematics on a Tuesday evening is likely to be met.

At eight to twelve weeks the picture changes because the whole emirate's Diploma cohort arrives at once. Availability in the scarce subjects thins first, which means a family either takes a less well-matched tutor at the same rate or pays toward the upper end for one who has actually taught the component. Both of those are worse outcomes than the same booking made in the autumn, and neither is a pricing decision anybody made.

At three weeks the constraint is no longer money. A family with a generous budget and three weeks cannot buy a Higher Level physics specialist who has already committed their final-term hours, and cannot buy the time required to learn a topic from nothing. What is available is technique: question order, timing, command terms, and the specific habits that move marks within a fortnight. That is a real and worthwhile purchase, and it is a small one.

The table below prices the plan by weeks rather than by subject. Every AED figure belongs to the provider or survey that published it, read in October 2026, and none of them is an IB Gram price: a plan here is quoted against a stated hour count so that it can be held against the published bands.

sections.heading: The May session counted backwards
paragraphs: A backwards plan is more useful than a revision timetable, because it attaches an action to a milestone rather than a subject to a week. The milestones are the school's rather than the board's in most cases, which is why the first act is administrative: ask the IB coordinator in writing for the internal deadline schedule, the mock window, the study leave dates and the school's own revision programme.

No specific IB examination or results date appears on this page, and the reason matters. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. Secondary sources circulate dates and some of them are wrong. UAE schools sit the May session; confirm the actual dates with the coordinator or on ibo.org, and treat any date on a tutoring page, including the absence of one here, as a reason to check rather than to assume.

What belongs on the backwards plan is a sequence of things that must already be done. Before study leave: the independent components submitted, the mock re-marked, the triage decision made. Before the mock: the specification content complete enough that the mock measures something. Before the final fortnight: the two chosen subjects' components identified and the technique work underway. Each of those has a date derived from the school's calendar rather than from a preference.

The planning error that recurs is reversing the order of cheap and expensive work. Independent-component work is early and cheap; examination technique is late and expensive. Families who do it the other way round pay weekly rates through the autumn for paper practice on content that is not finished, then discover in the spring that an Internal Assessment needs rescuing and buy that at the top of the market. Done in sequence, the autumn is a handful of block-booked core sessions and the spring is focused component work.

sections.heading: What money cannot buy in the final fortnight
paragraphs: This section exists because the market does not generally publish it. In the last two or three weeks before the May session, a number of things are not purchasable at any price, and a family with a budget and anxiety is the most likely customer for them. Saying so plainly is more useful than another paragraph about intensive revision programmes.

A topic learned from nothing is not purchasable. Learning requires exposure, retrieval and time between repetitions, and three weeks shared across six subjects does not contain it. A student who has not met a Higher Level topic will not meet it usefully now, and the hour spent trying is an hour not spent on the three or four topics they half know, which are the ones where marks are actually available.

A submitted component is not purchasable. Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay are gone, and with them up to three Diploma points that were available for work already on the timetable. This is the single clearest cost of late booking anywhere in the Diploma, and it is invisible because nothing announces it.

A committed specialist is not purchasable. In scarce subjects the final-term hours of the tutors who have actually taught the failing component are allocated by the spring, and a generous budget does not create more of them. What a family can buy late is a competent tutor who has not taught that specific paper, which is a different and lesser product and should be described as such. What is purchasable late, and worth buying, is technique: question order, timing across a long paper, command-term discipline, formula-booklet and calculator fluency, and two or three named habit repairs.
bullets: A topic from nothing: not purchasable, and the attempt costs better hours
A submitted component: gone, along with the points that sat in it
A committed scarce-subject specialist: not created by a bigger budget
Purchasable and worthwhile: question order, timing, command terms, fluency

sections.heading: Triage: two subjects, and the ones you name as left alone
paragraphs: A Diploma student has six subjects and a finite number of final-term hours, and the arithmetic of spreading those hours is unforgiving. Twelve hours divided across six subjects is two hours each, which changes nothing anywhere. Twelve hours divided across two subjects, aimed at the component carrying the most weight in each, can move two grades. The second plan is better and it requires saying out loud which four subjects are not getting hours.

The selection rule is weight times distance from the boundary, not perceived weakness. A subject the student dislikes but is comfortably passing at the target grade does not need hours. A subject they are confident in but sitting a mark below a boundary does. The marked mock, re-marked against the published criteria and broken down by component, is what produces that ranking, and a school report cannot because it compresses the components into one number.

The second rule is within-subject. Having chosen two subjects, choose one component in each. A paper carrying forty-four per cent of a science grade is worth more attention than one carrying thirty-six, and a Higher Level third paper carrying twenty per cent is worth a dedicated block if it is the component being abandoned mid-question. Working across a whole subject in the final term is a diluted version of the same spreading error, one level down.

The uncomfortable part is that triage sometimes identifies a subject as beyond reach in the time available, and the honest plan accepts that and reallocates. A student thirty marks below a boundary in one subject and two marks below in another should be spending their hours on the second. Saying so is not pessimism; it is the difference between a plan and a wish, and a provider unwilling to say it is selling hours rather than advice.

sections.heading: Abu Dhabi specifics: study leave, Ramadan and who may be paid
paragraphs: Three local variables change a final-term plan in this emirate and none of them appears on a generic revision page. The first is study leave. Abu Dhabi schools set their own arrangements and they differ, and the structure of a student's day changes completely once it begins: the constraint shifts from available hours to the ability to use them without a timetable. Ask the coordinator for the study leave dates early, because a plan built on school-day evenings stops fitting on the first day of leave.

The second is Ramadan. Its position in the Gregorian calendar moves earlier each year, so where it falls relative to the final revision period differs between examination cohorts. Check where it falls for your child's year rather than assuming. Where it overlaps revision, sessions move to post-Iftar times, written output per week drops, and a plan that assumed a constant weekly rate will not hold. That is manageable when it is planned and disruptive when it is discovered.

The third is who may be paid to help. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and teachers tutoring outside school hours must hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, whose code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with their own school. That is press-reported rather than read from ADEK's current policy document, so verify it against the authority's own publication; the practical point is that the most convenient arrangement a parent might imagine may not be permitted.

Abu Dhabi's private schools are regulated by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK is named by none of the competitor pages found in this research. Separately, private tutoring in the UAE requires the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years through MoHRE's own 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing' service with a stated two-working-day completion time; because it is free, no provider can justify a charge on licensing grounds, and tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws with no published fine schedule.

sections.heading: Online against in-home in a final term
paragraphs: The published numbers in this market run one way and the final term sharpens the argument rather than softening it. The Bestimate survey puts qualified in-home one-to-one in Abu Dhabi at AED 180-350 an hour, with independent home tutors quoted at AED 200-500 and monthly in-home packages advertised at AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour visits, against AED 150-300 for comparable work online. The gap pays for a commute.

In the final weeks that commute costs twice. It costs the premium, and it costs the student's own time at the point in the year when their hours are scarcest: a tutor arriving at six who leaves at seven-thirty has consumed more of the evening than the lesson used. Families in Khalifa City, Al Reef or Al Shamkha pay the largest version of both costs, because distance from the central tutoring clusters sets the premium.

The second final-term argument is depth of pool. In a scramble for Higher Level mathematics or Higher Level physics in the spring, the local in-home pool is the smallest version of the market available, and restricting a search to drivable distance at precisely the moment supply is tightest is the decision most likely to produce a mismatched tutor. Online widens the pool across the region, which in scarce subjects is the only thing that matters.

What in-home genuinely buys is presence for a student who cannot stay on task alone, and in study leave that is a real consideration rather than a marketing line. The honest version is that attention management is a scheduling and supervision problem a family can solve more cheaply than at AED 350 an hour, and that it is worth separating from the question of who teaches the component. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service, and UAE lessons run one-to-one on live video.
bullets: Published in-home band AED 180-500 against AED 150-300 online
The commute costs the premium and the student's scarcest hours
In a spring scramble the local pool is the smallest version of the market
Presence for a distractible student is a supervision problem, priced separately

sections.heading: What to refuse in the final term
paragraphs: A promised points total. Grade boundaries are determined after a session on the basis of candidate performance across the whole cohort, so the mark needed for a given grade is not knowable while the teaching is happening. Any provider offering a specific points total, a specific lift, or money back on a result is describing a sales position rather than how awarding works. What can honestly be committed to is a marked component after every session and a stated hour count that can be reduced.

Anything involving submitted work. Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay are finished by the final term, and an offer to improve or revisit one is either useless or a route to a malpractice finding. The market in this region sells written coursework: one UAE-facing site advertises completed Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. In the final term that purchase has no upside at all and the downside is the Diploma.

Unevidenced examiner claims at a premium. 'Examiner' is used loosely in this market and it sells well in the final weeks. Ask for evidence of current status, and note that examiner experience provides no access to marking in progress, to grade boundaries or to unseen paper content; a provider implying otherwise is describing something that would be a serious problem rather than a benefit. What an experienced marker genuinely offers is calibration against the published criteria, available well below the premium band.

An intensive package sold by the week. The honest final-term purchase is a stated number of hours aimed at named components, reviewable and reducible. A package priced by week has an incentive to fill the weeks, and in the last fortnight filling the weeks means content teaching that cannot work. Ask for the hour count, the components it addresses, and what the provider says is not worth buying at this range. The answer to the last question is the most informative thing in any final-term quote.

sections.heading: Results, remarks and the November question
paragraphs: A final-term plan should include the decision that follows the session, written before it. When results arrive, three routes exist and the criteria for each should already be on paper: accept the result, request a remark where a grade sits narrowly below a boundary and the marked evidence suggests technique rather than content loss, or consider a retake. Deciding criteria in advance converts an emotional week into an arithmetic question.

Remarks and retakes both have deadlines close behind results, and both are administered through the school rather than by a family or a tutor. A remark is a route worth considering for a borderline grade, because it can move a result without another term of work, but it is a review of marking rather than a second chance at the paper. Ask the coordinator what the school's process and timing are, before results rather than after.

The November session exists as a retake route, and the honest framing is that it suits a specific case: one subject, missed narrowly, where the loss was in a component that responds to a short block of work, and where the grade actually matters for the next step. Retaking a subject not required for the intended destination is a term spent for a better-looking certificate. No specific IB session or results date appears here because none has been confirmed from the IB; the coordinator holds the dates.

Costing the decision is simple and worth doing in advance. A single consultation reading the marked evidence and advising on remark against retake is one or two hours at the published qualified band of AED 150-300. A retake block is six to eight weeks on one subject, roughly twelve to sixteen hours. Both are small purchases. What makes them cheap is having decided the criteria in the spring rather than in the week the results arrive.

process.title: Say how many weeks remain, and send the mock script
process.description: The weeks determine what is purchasable and the script determines where the marks are. A photograph of the most recent marked mock plus the subject list with levels is enough to produce an honest answer, including the answer that a request is unrealistic at this range.

process.title: Free 30-minute trial lesson, one per family
process.description: Live video with the matched tutor, no card details taken, no obligation. In the final term it is spent on the script rather than on introductions: one question re-marked live against the published criteria so the standard being applied is visible before any figure is agreed.

process.title: Independent re-mark and the triage report
process.description: The mock re-marked to the published criteria with every lost mark assigned to content, misapplication, command term or timing, and a written report naming the two subjects worth the remaining weeks and the four that are not. Some families stop at this report, which is a reasonable outcome.

process.title: A plan with a stated hour count
process.description: The plan names the components, the number of sessions on each, the total hours and the total cost, so it can be held against the published bands on this page. It also names what is being left alone, because a plan that covers everything covers nothing properly.

process.title: Review and reduce at the halfway point
process.description: Mid-plan the marked evidence is re-read. Where a component has stabilised the sessions stop rather than continuing by default. An hour count exists so that it can be cut; a monthly subscription is designed so that it cannot.

process.title: Write the results-day criteria before the session
process.description: Which subjects would justify a remark request, which would justify a November retake, and which would justify neither — decided in the spring from marked evidence. One or two hours of consultation then, and an arithmetic decision instead of a panic in August.

whyPoints.title: Priced by weeks, not just by hour
whyPoints.description: The same plan costs differently at twenty weeks and at three, and the difference is supply rather than policy. Stating that lets a family capture the largest saving available in the final year, which costs nothing but a calendar.

whyPoints.title: What cannot be bought late is named
whyPoints.description: A topic from nothing, a submitted component, a committed specialist. A family with a budget and three weeks is the most likely customer for all three, and no page in this market publishes the limitation. Naming it is more useful than another intensive programme.

whyPoints.title: Triage names what is left alone
whyPoints.description: Two subjects, one component in each, and four subjects explicitly not getting hours. Spreading twelve hours across six subjects changes nothing anywhere, and a plan unwilling to say which four are excluded has not triaged.

whyPoints.title: Hours are stated and reducible
whyPoints.description: A quote attaches to a number of sessions and a total, reviewed at the halfway point and cut where the evidence says the hours are no longer needed. That is a different product from a package priced by the week with an incentive to fill them.

whyPoints.title: Local variables built in
whyPoints.description: Study leave changes the structure of a student's day, Ramadan's position shifts between cohorts and changes weekly output, and ADEK's ethics rules restrict who may be paid to help. None of those appears on a generic revision page.

whyPoints.title: The results decision written in advance
whyPoints.description: Remark criteria and retake criteria decided in the spring from marked evidence, so August is arithmetic rather than panic. One or two hours of consultation then is cheaper and better than a decision made in the week the results land.

faqs.question: How much does May session preparation cost in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: It depends more on when you ask than on what you buy. Published rates read in October 2026 put a qualified online subject tutor at AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors listing IB tuition from AED 200 and TutorChase quoting AED 270 for specialist work; the Bestimate survey puts IB and IGCSE specialists at AED 200-450 and above, and premium named listings reach AED 650. A family booking in the autumn transacts in the lower half of that spread with a choice of tutor. A family booking in the final weeks transacts at the top with whoever is free, which is supply rather than a pricing policy.

faqs.question: Why does booking late cost more for Diploma revision?
faqs.answer: Because the whole emirate's Diploma cohort becomes aware of the session at roughly the same moment. Higher Level mathematics, Higher Level physics and the scarcer options have a limited number of tutors serving this emirate, and demand for them concentrates into the same eight weeks every year. By the spring the specialists who have actually taught a failing component have committed their final-term hours. A later booking therefore costs more per hour and buys a less well-matched person, and neither of those is a decision anybody made deliberately.

faqs.question: What can a tutor not fix three weeks before IB exams?
faqs.answer: Three things, and a family with a budget and anxiety is the most likely customer for all of them. A topic learned from nothing, because learning needs exposure, retrieval and time between repetitions that three weeks across six subjects does not contain. A submitted component — Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay, the Theory of Knowledge essay — which is gone along with the points that sat in it. And a committed specialist in a scarce subject, whose final-term hours a larger budget does not create. What is purchasable is technique, and it is worth buying.

faqs.question: What is worth buying in the last fortnight before the May session?
faqs.answer: Technique, in a small block. Question-order strategy, so a student does not spend twenty minutes on a question worth four marks. Timing across a long paper, which is untested until a full paper has been sat under conditions. Command-term discipline, which recovers marks across several subjects simultaneously because the habit is subject-independent. Formula-booklet and calculator fluency, which is pure mechanics. Two or three short sessions covers it. Anything sold as intensive content teaching at this range is reassurance rather than preparation, and it displaces the work that could still move marks.

faqs.question: Should final-term hours be spread across all six Diploma subjects?
faqs.answer: No, and the arithmetic is unforgiving. Twelve hours divided across six subjects is two hours each, which changes nothing anywhere. Twelve hours divided across two subjects, aimed at the component carrying the most weight in each, can move two grades and therefore the points total. The selection rule is weight times distance from a boundary rather than perceived weakness: a disliked subject comfortably at target needs nothing, while a confident subject sitting a mark below a boundary needs attention. A plan unwilling to name the four subjects it excludes has not triaged.

faqs.question: How do I decide which two subjects get the hours?
faqs.answer: From a mock script re-marked against the published criteria and broken down by component, not from a school report. The report compresses components into one number and therefore cannot rank anything. The re-mark produces the two numbers that matter: how far each subject sits from the target boundary, and which component within it is carrying the loss. Then apply the honest rule, including the uncomfortable part — a subject thirty marks below a boundary should lose its hours to one sitting two marks below, however unfair that feels.

faqs.question: Does study leave change how an Abu Dhabi student should use a tutor?
faqs.answer: Yes, substantially, and it is worth planning for before it begins. Once study leave starts the constraint shifts from available hours to the ability to use them without a timetable, and a plan built on school-day evenings stops fitting on the first day. Sessions can move to mornings, which is generally better for timed-paper work, and the useful function of a tutor changes toward external structure and measurement. Ask the IB coordinator for the study leave dates early, because they differ between schools in the emirate.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan affect May session revision in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Its position in the Gregorian calendar moves earlier each year, so where it falls relative to the final revision period differs between examination cohorts. Check where it falls for your child's year rather than assuming. Where it overlaps revision, sessions move to post-Iftar times, written output per week drops, and a plan that assumed a constant weekly rate will not hold. That is entirely manageable when it has been planned for and disruptive when it is discovered mid-plan, which is the only real argument for building the calendar first.

faqs.question: Is a home tutor better than online for final-term Diploma revision?
faqs.answer: The published numbers run one way and the final term sharpens the argument. The Bestimate survey puts qualified in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 an hour, with independent home tutors quoted at AED 200-500, against AED 150-300 online. The commute costs the premium and also the student's scarcest hours, since a tutor arriving at six and leaving at seven-thirty has consumed more than the lesson used. In a spring scramble for a scarce subject, the local in-home pool is also the smallest version of the market. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; that is an India-only service.

faqs.question: Can anyone promise a Diploma points total for the May session?
faqs.answer: No, and the reason is structural rather than cautious. Grade boundaries are determined after a session on the basis of candidate performance across the whole cohort, so the mark required for a given grade is not knowable while the teaching is happening. A provider offering a specific points total, a specific lift in marks or money back on a result is describing a sales position. What can honestly be committed to is a marked component after every session, written feedback on the student's own work, and a stated hour count that can be reduced if the evidence says so.

faqs.question: Is a premium examiner-badged tutor worth it close to the exams?
faqs.answer: Only with evidence, and not for the reason it is usually sold. 'Examiner' is applied loosely across this market and it sells particularly well in the final weeks. Ask for demonstrable current status, and note that examiner experience provides no access to marking in progress, to grade boundaries or to unseen paper content — a provider implying otherwise is describing something that would be a serious problem rather than a benefit. What an experienced marker genuinely offers is calibration against the published criteria, which is available well below the premium band.

faqs.question: What should a Diploma family have done by the autumn of Year 13?
faqs.answer: Four things, and all of them are cheaper in the autumn than later. The independent components either submitted or on track, because those carry up to three points and close permanently. A mock or timed paper re-marked so the triage decision has evidence behind it. The two chosen subjects identified with their components. And the scarce-subject tutor booked, because that booking is the one that cannot be made later at any price. Together those cost a handful of hours and they determine the price and the usefulness of everything in the spring.

faqs.question: What are the options when results do not match expectations?
faqs.answer: Three, and the criteria for each should be written down in the spring rather than decided in the week they arrive. Accept the result. Request a remark, which is worth considering where a grade sits narrowly below a boundary and the marked evidence pointed to technique rather than content loss — though a remark reviews the marking rather than offering a second attempt at the paper. Or consider a retake in the November session. All three are administered through the school, with deadlines close behind results, so ask the coordinator for the process before results rather than after.

faqs.question: When is a November retake worth the cost?
faqs.answer: In a specific case: one subject, missed narrowly, where the loss sat in a component that responds to a short block of work, and where the grade actually matters for the next step. Retaking a subject not required for the intended destination is a term spent for a better-looking certificate. Costed, a retake block is six to eight weeks on one subject, roughly twelve to sixteen hours at the published qualified band of AED 150-300. The decision itself is one or two hours of consultation, and it is cheapest when the criteria were agreed months earlier.

faqs.question: What if no tutor is free for our subject this close to the May session?
faqs.answer: You should be told, with the options named rather than a substitute quietly supplied. Scarce requests concentrate in the spring: Higher Level Further Mathematics, a specific third paper, a minority language at ab initio level. The honest choices are a wait with a date attached, a tutor based outside the UAE delivering on the same live video platform and on Gulf Standard Time, or a referral elsewhere. A specialist rate charged for someone who has not taught the component is the thing to refuse. No competitor page found in this market discloses a coverage limit at all.

abu-dhabi/ib-may-session-exam-preparatio.closingHeading: Count the weeks before you compare the rates
abu-dhabi/ib-may-session-exam-preparatio.closingBody: An hourly rate means little in a final term without the number of weeks beside it. Twenty weeks out, a content gap in two subjects is addressable at the middle of the published range with a choice of tutor. Three weeks out, the honest offer is a short technique block and nothing more, whatever the budget. Send the subject list, the weeks remaining and the most recent marked mock, take the free 30-minute trial lesson, and ask for a plan with a stated hour count plus a written list of what the provider says is not worth buying at your range.

intro.heading: A mock is evidence, and most of it gets thrown away
paragraphs: Mock exams in an Abu Dhabi IB school are written, sat and marked internally. The school chooses the papers, often from previous sessions, sets its own window, applies the published assessment criteria as its teachers read them, and then uses the result for two purposes: telling a student where they stand and justifying a predicted grade to universities. That makes a mock the single richest piece of evidence a Diploma candidate generates before the real session, and in most households it is read once, as a number, and then filed.

The number is the least useful part. A 4 in Chemistry HL tells you nothing actionable. The same script, read question by question, tells you that eleven marks were lost on command terms where the candidate described instead of explaining, that six went on a data-analysis question where uncertainty was never propagated, and that four were simply unattempted because the paper ran out of time. Those are three different problems with three different fixes and three different costs in hours. One is a vocabulary job, one is a technique job, one is a pacing job.

This page is built around that reading, because the brief for it was evidence rather than reassurance. What follows is what a marked mock script actually yields, how it connects to a predicted grade and how it does not, what the weeks between mocks and the May session should produce in writing, and where mock marks go missing in each subject group. The AED figures are here too, quoted as market rates with their sources, but they sit behind the diagnostic argument rather than in front of it.

There is a limit to state at the outset. A tutor does not set a predicted grade and cannot change one. That belongs to the subject teacher and the school, which hold the full picture including classwork, internal assessment progress and attendance. What marked work can do is give a teacher better evidence to look at, and give a student a countable list of repairs between a mock mark and the next grade band. Any page promising a grade movement is selling something nobody owns.

Delivery is one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address; home visits are a service we offer only in India. During mock season that matters practically rather than philosophically: a script marked on Tuesday needs reading with the student on Wednesday, and the scheduling flexibility to do that is easier online than it is around the Abu Dhabi school run. It also widens the pool. A candidate in Al Ain or Al Shamkha wanting an HL Chemistry specialist to read a mock paper is otherwise choosing from whoever can drive to the address inside a reasonable window, which is a constraint about geography rather than about teaching. Live video removes it and leaves only the question of who can mark the paper to the criteria, which is the question the family meant to ask.

abu-dhabi/ib-mock-exam-preparation.programmesIntro: Mocks exist at more than one stage, and they mean different things at each. These are the IB programmes running in Abu Dhabi schools and what an internal assessment week signifies in each one.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: There are no mock exams in the PYP, and any school presenting them as such has imported a structure the programme does not use. Assessment is continuous, with the exhibition at the end of the programme as the summative piece. Where families look for support here, the useful work is in written explanation and mathematical reasoning rather than in examination technique.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi PYP schools report against the programme's own framework rather than against examination grades, which can be disorienting for parents arriving from systems that test annually. Ask the school how it will evidence readiness for MYP, because that is the transition where examination habits begin to matter.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP assessment runs on criteria A to D in each subject, each with its own mark band and descriptors, and schools increasingly run formal internal assessment weeks in MYP 4 and 5 that function as mocks. Reading those papers against the criterion descriptors is genuinely useful preparation, because the criterion language reappears in Diploma internal assessment.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi schools offer MYP through Year 11 with eAssessment as an option, and others switch students to IGCSE at Year 10. A family whose child is in MYP 5 should know which route the school has chosen, because it changes what a mock week is rehearsing for.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The programme where mocks carry real weight. DP mocks usually sit in the winter of the second year, use past papers, and feed the predicted grades that go to universities. The grade is school-issued; the papers are externally written in origin. That combination makes a mock script unusually close to the real article and therefore unusually informative.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi DP candidates normally sit the May session. Mock windows vary between schools in the emirate and are usually set against university application deadlines rather than against the exam calendar, which is why two schools a few kilometres apart can mock six weeks apart.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: CP students take DP courses alongside a career-related study, so they sit mocks in their DP subjects on the same timetable as DP candidates. The reflective project runs in parallel and has its own internal deadlines, which in practice collide with the mock window more often than schools plan for.
programmes.countryNote: The CP is offered by a small number of schools in the emirate, and CP candidates often find mock-season support harder to buy because tutors default to assuming a full Diploma. Stating the programme at the outset avoids a plan built for the wrong course load.

abu-dhabi/ib-mock-exam-preparation.subjectsIntro: Where mock marks actually go, by subject. Each note names the component and the behaviour rather than the topic, because that is the level at which a marked script is useful.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: HL mock losses concentrate in Paper 3, where the extended investigative questions reward sustained reasoning rather than recall, and in proof. Across both levels, marks go on unjustified steps in method-marked questions and on calculator papers where an exact form was required.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistical interpretation is the heaviest mark sink: tests chosen correctly and then conclusions written without reference to the significance level or the context. Modelling questions lose marks where parameters are found and never interpreted in the terms the question set.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Mock scripts typically show losses in energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms, plus a consistent band of marks lost on data questions where uncertainty is calculated but not propagated or discussed. Command-term discipline between state, outline and explain costs more than content gaps.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Marks go on fields and circular motion at HL, and across both levels on the long-answer questions where a correct equation is applied without the reasoning line the mark scheme credits. Graph questions lose marks on gradient interpretation rather than on plotting.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The most command-term sensitive subject in the group. Mock answers are routinely accurate and uncredited because they describe where they were asked to explain, or outline where the question asked for an evaluation. Data-based questions reward reading the axes before the prose.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and labelled axes carry marks that are lost casually, and evaluation marks go unclaimed because candidates stop after analysis. HL quantitative questions lose marks on units and on interpretation rather than on calculation.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 marks turn on close reading of the specific text rather than on general technique spotting, and Paper 2 on sustained comparison. Mock scripts commonly show strong knowledge of works and weak control of the comparative structure the criteria reward.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Marks are lost where tools are named and not applied to the stimulus, and in the extended-response questions where a judgement is required and only a summary is given. The case-study paper rewards familiarity with the pre-release material that mocks often simulate imperfectly.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source-based questions lose marks on provenance and on the compare-and-contrast structure rather than on content. Essay marks go on argument maintained across the response, and mock scripts often show a strong first paragraph followed by narrative.

subjects.name: Arabic and UAE social studies alongside the Diploma
subjects.description: Private schools in the UAE teach Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies alongside the licensed international curriculum, and those lessons continue through mock season. For a DP candidate in a mock window this is fixed timetable load that a revision plan has to accommodate rather than wish away.

abu-dhabi/ib-mock-exam-preparation.regionsIntro: Mock windows and school runs do not coordinate, and in Abu Dhabi the second of those varies sharply by community. These notes are about when a session can realistically sit during a mock fortnight.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Short school runs and a small DP cohort, so a 4pm session the day after a mock paper is workable. That proximity to the mock itself is the single biggest factor in whether a script gets read while the candidate still remembers writing it.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Mushrif
regions.note: Established island communities feeding several Diploma schools, with manageable commutes and a high concentration of HL science candidates. Mock weeks here often coincide with university application deadlines, which doubles the week's load.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: A long school run in term time, which pushes sessions to 5pm or later and makes weekend script reviews the practical option. Families here benefit most from marking turned around overnight rather than at the next lesson.

regions.name: Al Raha and Al Bandar
regions.note: Close to the Khalifa City cluster and generating heavy demand for HL Chemistry and Physics support in the winter mock window. Two shorter weekday sessions tend to survive mock fortnight better than one long block.

regions.name: Yas Island and West Yas
regions.note: A newer and growing DP population with a slow afternoon commute. Candidates here often want a session between the last mock paper and the first internal assessment deadline, which lands in the same fortnight.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Dense apartment living with short travel and the easiest weekday scheduling in the emirate. The constraint is a quiet room rather than the clock, which matters when a session involves reading a script aloud.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: An hour inland with a small Diploma cohort and few HL subject specialists physically present. For an Al Ain candidate wanting a marked Physics HL paper read the day after a mock, live video is the only route that exists.

schoolClusters.city: Island and Saadiyat Diploma schools
schoolClusters.note: Smaller DP cohorts where a single subject may run one HL class, so a candidate struggling in HL Chemistry has limited internal comparison. Mock scripts matter more here because there is less cohort data around them.

The output is a written list of marks lost grouped by cause: command term, method presentation, content gap, pacing. sections.heading: What an IB mock actually is, and who owns each part of it
paragraphs: A mock exam in an Abu Dhabi IB school is an internal exercise built from external material. The school selects papers, usually from previous sessions, decides when the window sits, invigilates it, and marks it using the published assessment criteria. No part of the process is run by the IB, and no mock result appears on any certificate. That matters because it changes who you can usefully ask about a mark: the subject teacher who marked the script owns the judgement, not an external body.

What the school does with the result is where the stakes come from. Mock marks are one of the main inputs to a predicted grade, and predicted grades go to universities. In Abu Dhabi, where mock windows are frequently set against application deadlines rather than against the exam calendar, a candidate can find a single fortnight in winter carrying both the mock papers and the point at which a predicted grade is finalised. That is a scheduling fact worth knowing before it arrives.

There is also variation that confuses families who compare notes across the emirate. Two Diploma schools a short drive apart can mock six weeks apart, use different past papers, and apply the criteria with different severity. A mock 5 at one school and a mock 5 at another are not the same statement about a candidate. The only way to read a mark is against the script and the mark scheme behind it, which is why this page keeps returning to the script.

The practical consequence is a short list of questions to ask the school: which session's papers were used, whether the marking was moderated across teachers, how the mark maps to a grade boundary, and when the predicted grade is finalised. Most schools answer all four readily. Very few parents ask.
