abu-dhabi/ib-myp-arts-tutor.programmesIntro: Arts runs through the IB programmes with the assessment model changing at each stage, and the cost profile changes with it. The map below is written around what each stage demands of a family's budget as well as of the student.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The programme in the URL. Arts is assessed against knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively, and responding - 8 marks each. Schools choose the discipline, so Arts may mean visual art, music, drama, dance or a rotation through several. The process journal is the spine of the evidence in every case, which is why the same support works across disciplines even though the technique does not.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi MYP schools vary widely in which Arts disciplines they run and for how long. A rotation model in MYP 1 to 3 followed by specialisation in MYP 4 and 5 is common, and families often start paying for instrumental coaching before knowing whether the school will offer music as the assessed Arts discipline at all. Confirm with the department before committing to a two-year instrument plan.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Visual Arts, Music, Theatre and Dance continue at SL and HL, assessed through externally submitted work - a comparative study and process portfolio in Visual Arts, recorded and documented work in Music. The documentation demand rises sharply, and students who kept a real MYP journal find the transition manageable where students who kept a tidy one do not. Costs rise too, because exhibition and recording requirements are more demanding.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma Arts cohorts in Abu Dhabi are small and a school may not run every discipline in a given year. That is worth checking before an MYP 5 student builds an option plan around Visual Arts HL, because the alternative of switching discipline late is both academically and financially expensive.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Arts in the PYP is taught inside transdisciplinary units with no criterion marking and no journal requirement. This is the cheapest stage by a wide margin: the useful spending is on an instrument if a child shows sustained interest, and on nothing else. Formal tutoring here buys very little that a good school programme is not already providing.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi primary sections run instrumental programmes from Year 3 or 4, sometimes with instruments supplied. Families who take that route reach MYP with an instrument and some grounding at no cost, which is the single largest saving available anywhere in this subject.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Where offered, the Career-related Programme can pair a Diploma Arts course with a career-related study in a creative field, evidenced through portfolio work and a reflective project. The cost profile resembles a portfolio-based course rather than an examined one: lower per-hour coaching, higher material and production costs concentrated at the end.
programmes.countryNote: Very few Abu Dhabi schools run the Career-related Programme. It is mentioned because families exploring creative routes after MYP occasionally encounter it and should know that its evidence model, and therefore its cost shape, is different from Diploma Arts.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-arts-tutor.subjectsIntro: Arts support is most often booked alongside another subject, and the pairing affects the total bill. The grid below sets out the subjects most commonly booked with Arts in Abu Dhabi and what each is actually assessed on.

subjects.name: Arts - visual art
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively, responding, with the process journal as the evidence base. The usual cause of a stuck grade is a strong final piece documented thinly, which is a journal problem rather than a skill problem.

subjects.name: Arts - music
subjects.description: The same four criteria applied to performing, composing and listening. Technical coaching on an instrument is a separate purchase from MYP support, and families frequently buy the first believing it covers the second.

subjects.name: Arts - drama and theatre
subjects.description: Marked on process and reflection as much as performance. Rehearsal records, directorial decisions and responses to live or recorded work are journal evidence, and they are what distinguishes a 6 from a 4.

subjects.name: Arts - dance
subjects.description: Choreographic process, skill development and response to repertoire. Video documentation is the practical journal format here, and students who film their rehearsals systematically are the ones whose criterion B evidence holds up.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, evaluating. The folder works like an Arts journal, so a student who learns documentation discipline in one subject usually gains a band in the other.

subjects.name: English - Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysing, organising, producing text, using language. Arts criterion D responses are written analysis, and students weak at analysing a text are usually weak at analysing an artwork for the same reason.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Investigating, communicating and thinking critically. Arts criterion A research on context, movement and influence is the same research skill, and the two subjects' investigation marks tend to move together.

subjects.name: Arabic and Islamic Education
subjects.description: Mandatory subjects in UAE private schools with set school material. They compete with Arts for weekly study hours, which is the main reason Arts support is often better bought as a short block than as a year-long commitment.

subjects.name: Mathematics - Standard and Extended
subjects.description: Included because families budgeting across subjects usually have maths support in the same month. Arts is the cheaper and more quickly improvable of the two, which affects the order in which money is best spent.

subjects.name: Personal Project
subjects.description: Investigating, planning, taking action, reflecting, evidenced in a process journal. An arts-based Personal Project is common and doubles the value of journal discipline learned in MYP 3 and 4.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-arts-tutor.regionsIntro: In Arts, where you live changes what the student can make and what it costs to make it - studio space, instrument noise, and proximity to the galleries that make criterion A research free. The notes below are about that rather than about travel, since lessons are online.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Walking or short driving distance to the island's museums and cultural venues, which turns primary research for criteria A and D into an afternoon rather than a paid session. The cheapest Arts postcode in the emirate for that reason alone.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Apartment living constrains large-format work and makes instrument practice a neighbour question. Sketchbook-scale media, digital work and headphone-compatible instruments are the practical choices and the cheaper ones.

regions.name: Al Raha Gardens and Al Raha Beach
regions.note: Villa space for messy media and a room where a drum kit or piano is viable. Families here spend more on materials and less on studio access than apartment households do.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: Mixed housing and the emirate's largest MYP cohorts, so school Arts facilities are well used and after-school studio time is competitive. Home working space becomes the determining factor for coursework in MYP 4 and 5.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Mushrif
regions.note: Close to the Cultural Foundation and the older city venues, with established school Arts departments that run to higher criterion B expectations. Instrument teaching supply is deepest here, which keeps in-person music rates lower.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: Newer schools with facilities still expanding and a strong events programme nearby. Performance opportunities are easier to come by than studio space, which suits drama and music students more than visual arts students.

regions.name: Al Shamkha and Al Falah
regions.note: Mainland communities where in-person instrumental teaching is thinly covered and a weekly drive to the island is the usual alternative. This is where online coaching for theory, journal and composition work saves the most money.

schoolClusters.city: Saadiyat, the Corniche and Al Bateen
schoolClusters.note: Schools within reach of the emirate's main cultural venues, where gallery-based research is a routine part of Arts teaching rather than an excursion. Arts departments here are long-established and mark to higher criterion B expectations.

sections.heading: Two markets: what Arts support actually costs in Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: The published rates in this market are for academic subject tutoring, and MYP Arts support - journal work, criterion-referenced critique, written responses - sits inside those bands. A qualified online subject tutor runs roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour as of October 2026. Entry-level online tuition is advertised from AED 33 to 65 by Tutopiya and EdFlik. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes about AED 270. BartyED sits at AED 650 for a premium named tutor. Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and specialist exam-year support at AED 200 to 450 and above.

Instrumental and vocal coaching is a different market and is not covered by those figures. It is priced per lesson, usually for a 30- or 45-minute slot rather than an hour, and the rate is set by the teacher's own standing rather than by curriculum specialism. Families regularly compare an instrumental lesson price against an academic tutoring price and conclude one is overpriced; they are buying different things, and a student needing MYP journal support will not get it from an instrumental teacher who has never seen the criteria.

The practical consequence is a two-question triage before any money is spent. Is the problem technical - the student cannot yet do the thing - or is it evidential, meaning the student can do it and the folder does not show the thinking? Technical problems need discipline coaching, which may be local, in person, and priced per short lesson. Evidential problems need criterion-referenced review, which is an academic tutoring purchase and works perfectly well over video. The second is cheaper and, in MYP Arts, far more commonly the real issue.

Every figure in the table below is the provider's own published rate, read in October 2026. It is a market map rather than an IB Gram price list - our own number follows the free trial lesson, once the triage above has established which of the two purchases your child actually needs.

sections.heading: The budget nobody itemises: materials, instruments and entry fees
paragraphs: Tutoring is frequently the smallest line in an Arts budget and the only one anybody quotes. The others arrive unannounced: a specialist media list in MYP 4, an instrument that has to be bought rather than borrowed once a child outgrows the school's loan stock, an accompanist for a recital, entry fees for graded music examinations that have nothing to do with the IB but fall in the same term.

The honest position on figures here is that most of these are school-specific or retailer-specific and should not be guessed at. ADEK publishes approved fee levels for private schools in the emirate, so school costs are checkable at source. Graded music examination fees are set and published annually by the awarding bodies and should be read from the current schedule rather than from a tutoring page. Materials lists come from the department. What a page like this can usefully do is tell you which lines exist, when they arrive, and which of them are avoidable.

Three of them are genuinely avoidable. Instrument purchase can often be deferred by a year through a school loan or a rental arrangement, and for a child on a rotation model in MYP 1 to 3 it should be, because the assessed discipline may not be music. Specialist media can usually be substituted - criterion B rewards skill development in a medium, not an expensive medium, and a student working seriously in graphite and ink is not disadvantaged against one working in oils. And studio access is free at school for students who ask the department rather than buying space.

One line is not avoidable and is worth paying: documentation. A sketchbook or journal that holds up, and a way to photograph or film work consistently. A phone is sufficient. Students lose criterion B and C marks every year to work that was good and was never recorded, and that is the cheapest preventable loss in the subject.

sections.heading: What your money is buying: the four criteria and the journal
paragraphs: MYP Arts is assessed against four criteria at 8 marks each: knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively, and responding. A parent who knows which of the four is weak can buy four useful hours. A parent who does not buys a term of pleasant studio chat, and the grade does not move.

Criterion A, knowing and understanding, is about context, vocabulary and informed connections - the artist, movement, period or repertoire behind the work, used rather than listed. Students lose marks here by naming influences without showing how they changed a decision. Criterion B, developing skills, is the acquisition and application of technique, evidenced through practice and experiment over time. This is the criterion a thin journal destroys, because a finished piece on its own shows a skill but not its development.

Criterion C, thinking creatively, asks for an articulated intention, a willingness to take risks, and evidence of exploration - including the experiments that failed. Students systematically under-record failure because it feels like weakness, and it is the single most reliable source of criterion C marks. Criterion D, responding, is reflection and critique: on their own work, on others' work, and on the relationship between the two. It is written, and it is where students with strong practical ability and weak written analysis lose the grade they earned at the easel.

The journal is where three of those four live. That is why the cheapest effective intervention in MYP Arts is a journal review rather than a course of lessons: a tutor reads it, states the band each criterion sits in, names what is missing, and the student fills the gaps with work they have already done but never recorded. Four sessions frequently move a grade. Twenty sessions of technique will not, if the journal stays thin.
bullets: Criterion A - knowing and understanding: context used to change a decision, not listed
Criterion B - developing skills: evidence of technique over time, not one finished piece
Criterion C - thinking creatively: intention, risk, and the experiments that failed
Criterion D - responding: written reflection and critique of own and others' work
Three of the four live in the journal, which is why a journal review is the cheapest fix

sections.heading: What video can and cannot do for a practical subject
paragraphs: A fair question from any Abu Dhabi parent: how does an Arts tutor work over a screen? The honest answer separates the subject into parts, because some of it transfers to video intact, some transfers well enough, and some does not transfer at all - and knowing which is which is what stops you paying for the wrong hour.

Transfers intact: journal review, criterion banding, research and context work, written response and critique, composition analysis, music theory, rehearsal and performance review from recordings, and portfolio selection. These are reading, talking and writing tasks, and a shared screen is as good as a shared table. For most MYP Arts students these are also where the lost marks are.

Transfers well enough: technique critique from photographs and video, and process coaching. A tutor can see a drawing clearly on a camera, can watch a student's hand position on an instrument, can tell from a filmed rehearsal that a transition is being rushed. What they lose is the ability to step in physically, which matters more for a beginner than for a student with a grade to move.

Does not transfer: the practical making itself, physical demonstration of a medium in the student's hands, ensemble work, and anything requiring a kiln, a press or a studio the student does not have. Nobody should pretend otherwise. The practical work happens in the student's own space with their own materials, at school in the department's studio, or in an ensemble locally. What an online session adds is the criterion-referenced layer around it, which no amount of practice supplies on its own. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE - home visits are a service we offer only in India - so where a student genuinely needs hands-on instrumental teaching, the honest advice is to find that locally and use online support for the journal, theory and response work.

sections.heading: Abu Dhabi's cultural sector is free research, and almost nobody uses it
paragraphs: This is the section that should save an Abu Dhabi family the most money, and no competing tutoring page in this market mentions it. Criterion A rewards informed understanding of context, and criterion D rewards reflection and critique of others' work. Both are best evidenced from primary encounters with real work, and the emirate is unusually well supplied with those.

Saadiyat Island's museums and galleries, the Cultural Foundation in the old city, the emirate's festival and concert programme, and the temporary exhibitions that rotate through all of them constitute a standing research resource. A student who visits one, documents a specific work properly - what it is, what it does, how it was made, what decision it suggests for their own practice - and writes a reasoned response in the journal has produced exactly the evidence two criteria ask for. Entry costs are modest, student concessions are common, and several venues run free programming.

The method matters more than the venue. A gallery visit that produces a photograph and the sentence 'it was interesting' is worth nothing. A visit that produces three annotated observations, one technical question, and a journal entry explaining how it changed the student's next experiment is worth a band. That discipline is teachable in a single session and then costs nothing to repeat, which is the opposite of the economics of a standing tutoring arrangement.

The same logic applies to performing arts. A concert or theatre performance attended with a specific observational brief produces criterion D evidence that no online lesson can manufacture. Families who build two or three such visits into a school year, each documented properly, generally need fewer paid hours - not more - because the journal fills with real primary material instead of secondhand summaries.

sections.heading: When paying for Arts support is the wrong decision
paragraphs: A tutoring page that cannot name the cases where it should not be hired is not being straight with you. In MYP Arts there are four, and they are common enough that saying so is more useful than another argument for booking.

The first is a student who is behind because they have not done the work. No tutor fixes volume. If the journal is empty because three units' worth of practice never happened, the required intervention is time and a schedule, not money, and an hour a week with a specialist simply relocates the problem. The second is a rotation year. A student rotating through three disciplines in MYP 2 is not being assessed on specialist technique, and paid coaching in one of the three is a bet on which discipline the school will specialise in later.

The third is a technical problem misdiagnosed as an academic one. A beginner who cannot yet hold a bow or control a wash needs hands-on teaching in a room, which is not what online academic support provides, and buying it anyway produces a frustrated child and a reasonable invoice for nothing. The fourth is a student already scoring 6s and 7s whose family wants a 7 across all four criteria. The remaining marks in MYP Arts are usually in criterion C risk-taking, which is a disposition built by making more work with permission to fail, and which a tutor cannot buy for them.

In each of those cases the honest recommendation after a trial lesson is no purchase, or a smaller one than was expected. A four-session journal block that ends is a better outcome for a family than a standing arrangement that never does, and if the trial establishes that your child needs nothing, the written note says so.

A rotation year: specialist coaching is a bet on a discipline not yet chosen
Beginner physical technique: needs hands-on teaching in a room
Already at 6 and 7: the remaining marks are risk-taking, which is built by making work

sections.heading: Graded music examinations alongside the MYP, and how the two calendars collide
paragraphs: A large share of Abu Dhabi music students are working towards graded practical examinations run by external awarding bodies at the same time as their MYP Arts assessment. The two are unrelated. A graded music certificate is not an IB qualification, it carries no MYP marks, and the MYP criteria do not reward it. It is worth doing on its own terms, and it is worth understanding as a separate cost and a separate calendar.

The collision is practical rather than academic. Graded examination sessions, school concerts, MYP unit deadlines and - in MYP 5 - the Personal Project all draw on the same evenings, and families routinely discover in February that three of them fall in the same month. The entry fees are set and published annually by the awarding bodies, so the dates and the amounts are both checkable in advance from the board's own current schedule. Reading that schedule in September is a cheaper exercise than rearranging in March.

There is a genuine academic use for the graded work, though, and most students miss it. The repertoire studied for a graded examination is legitimate criterion A and B material: a student who documents how they learned a piece, what the technical obstacle was, what they tried, and how the interpretation changed has produced journal evidence for MYP Arts out of practice they were doing anyway. That is the single most efficient overlap available in this subject.

What it does not do is substitute for the MYP work. A certificate in the folder is not evidence of skill development; the documented process of earning it is. Families paying for instrumental coaching and expecting the MYP grade to follow are missing precisely that step, and it is the step an online journal session supplies cheaply.

sections.heading: What the first session establishes, and the honest version of availability
paragraphs: The first session is free: one trial lesson per student, booked without card details, nothing payable before or after it, no obligation to continue. In Arts it is used as a triage rather than a lesson, because the two possible purchases are so different that guessing wastes a term.

The tutor looks at two things together: a piece of finished work and the journal pages behind it. That pairing answers the question that matters. If the work is strong and the journal is thin, the problem is evidential and four to six sessions of journal and criterion work will move the grade. If the work itself is below the level the student is being marked at, the problem is technical, and the honest recommendation may be local hands-on teaching for the practical side with online support reserved for journal, theory and written response work.

What you receive afterwards is a written note: a band judgement for each criterion that has evidence, the specific gaps in priority order, a recommended number of sessions with an end point, and - where it applies - a plain statement that no paid support is needed. The note is written to be shown to the Arts teacher, because the department sets the units and marks the work, and a student arriving with named gaps gets a specific answer where a student asking for general feedback gets a general one.

Where no MYP Arts specialist in the right discipline is free for the slot a family needs, we say so. The options offered are a different slot with the right tutor, a tutor from an adjacent discipline with the limitation stated plainly, or a referral back when availability opens. Several providers in this market conceal a coverage gap behind a premium rate; a disclosed gap costs a family less, because it does not waste a term discovering it.

process.title: Send one finished piece and five journal pages
process.description: Photographs or scans are fine, and the journal pages should be the real ones rather than the tidiest. That pairing is what separates a technical problem from an evidential one, and it decides which of the two purchases your child actually needs.

process.title: Free trial lesson used as a triage
process.description: One lesson, one student, no card details and nothing payable. The tutor reads the journal against the four criteria and looks at the work against the level it is being marked at, then says which of the two is holding the grade.

process.title: A written note with an end point in it
process.description: You receive a band judgement per criterion, the gaps ranked by how many marks they cost, a recommended number of sessions, and a stated finish. Where the answer is that no paid support is needed, the note says that instead.

process.title: Short block, not a standing arrangement
process.description: Most MYP Arts work is a four to six session journal block rather than a year of lessons. Sessions run on Gulf Standard Time around the school run, with the student's own work photographed or filmed and reviewed between them.

process.title: Close the block and hand over a note for the school
process.description: When the journal holds what the criteria require, the block ends with a short written summary the student can show their Arts teacher. A documented subject can define what finished looks like, and this one does.

whyPoints.title: The triage happens before the invoice
whyPoints.description: Visual arts support and instrumental coaching are different purchases at different rates. The free trial lesson exists to establish which one your child needs, including the answer that the practical teaching should be found locally.

whyPoints.title: Rate bands published with their sources
whyPoints.description: Three of the six most visible pages in this market publish no price at all, and two quote in US dollars. This page publishes the AED bands, names the providers they came from, and dates them - then keeps them separate from what IB Gram quotes.

whyPoints.title: The costs around the tutoring line are itemised
whyPoints.description: Materials, instrument hire, documentation and graded examination entries all arrive on their own schedule. We name which lines exist, when they land, where the real figure is published, and which three of them are genuinely avoidable.

whyPoints.title: Journal first, because that is where the marks are
whyPoints.description: Three of the four Arts criteria are evidenced in the process journal. A four-session journal block frequently moves a grade where twenty sessions of technique will not, and we recommend the cheaper one when it is the right one.

whyPoints.title: Blocks that end
whyPoints.description: Each arrangement is quoted with a number of sessions and a finish point. An Arts journal either holds the required evidence or it does not, which makes this one of the few subjects where a tutor can state when the work is done.

whyPoints.title: Delivery and limits stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE - home visits are a service we offer only in India - and where no specialist in the right discipline is free, we say so.

faqs.question: What does an MYP Arts tutor charge per hour in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Journal and criterion work sits inside the general academic tutoring bands: roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour for a qualified online subject tutor as of October 2026, with entry-level online tuition advertised from AED 33 to 65 by Tutopiya and EdFlik, around AED 270 by TutorChase, and AED 650 at BartyED's premium tier. In-home academic tutoring runs AED 180 to 500 because travel sits inside the fee. Instrumental and vocal coaching is a separate market priced per short lesson rather than per hour. Those are the providers' published figures, not an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: Why is an instrumental teacher priced differently from an Arts tutor?
faqs.answer: Because they are selling different things. An instrumental or vocal teacher is priced per 30- or 45-minute lesson on the strength of their performing and teaching standing, and they teach technique hands-on. An MYP Arts tutor is priced per hour as an academic subject specialist and works on the four criteria, the process journal and written responses. A student with a journal problem will not get it solved by an instrumental teacher who has never read the criteria, and a beginner needing physical correction will not get it from an online academic session. Establish which problem you have before comparing prices.

faqs.question: What should we budget for MYP Arts materials in an Abu Dhabi school?
faqs.answer: Ask the department, because it is school-specific and most schools supply core media. The avoidable line is specialist media in MYP 4 and 5: criterion B rewards skill development in a medium rather than an expensive medium, so a student working seriously in graphite and ink is not disadvantaged against one working in oils. The unavoidable and cheapest line is documentation - a journal that holds up and a consistent way to photograph work. Students lose criterion B and C marks every year to good work that was never recorded, and a phone camera prevents it.

faqs.question: Do graded music exams count towards the MYP Arts grade?
faqs.answer: No. A graded practical music certificate is awarded by an external body, is not an IB qualification, and carries no MYP marks. It is worth doing on its own terms. What does count is the documented process of earning it: how the repertoire was learned, what the technical obstacle was, what was tried, and how the interpretation changed. That is legitimate criterion A and B journal evidence drawn from practice the student was doing anyway, and it is the most efficient overlap available in the subject. Entry fees and session dates are published annually by the awarding body.

faqs.question: Can visual art really be taught over video?
faqs.answer: Parts of it, and usefully. Journal review, criterion banding, context and research work, written response and critique, and portfolio selection all transfer intact, because they are reading and writing tasks on a shared screen - and for most MYP students that is where the lost marks are. Technique critique from photographs and film works well for intermediate students. What does not transfer is beginner physical correction and anything needing a kiln, press or shared studio. The practical making happens in the student's own space or at school; the online session supplies the criterion-referenced layer around it.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to use the school art room than to buy materials at home?
faqs.answer: Usually, and more students should ask. Departments hold core media, equipment and often studio time that is free to students who request it, and in apartment households on Al Reem Island or similar the school studio solves both the space and the cost problem at once. The limitation is access hours, which in the large Khalifa City cohorts can be competitive. The practical approach is to do messy and equipment-dependent work at school and keep home work to sketchbook-scale media and documentation, which costs very little and protects the marks that depend on consistent recording.

faqs.question: Does a process journal need paid support, or can a student keep one alone?
faqs.answer: Most students can keep one alone once somebody has shown them what counts. The useful intervention is short: a tutor reads the journal, states the band each criterion sits in, and models what a research entry, an experiment record and a reflection have to contain. Four to six sessions is a typical block, and it frequently moves a grade because the student usually has the underlying work and has never recorded it. What keeps journals thin is not inability but under-recording of failed experiments, which is the most reliable source of criterion C marks.

faqs.question: Can Abu Dhabi museums and galleries be used as free Arts research?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is the largest saving available in the subject. Criterion A rewards informed context and criterion D rewards critique of others' work, and both are best evidenced from primary encounters. Saadiyat Island's museums, the Cultural Foundation and the emirate's festival programme give a student real work to document, with student concessions common and some free programming. The method matters: three annotated observations, one technical question, and a journal entry explaining how the visit changed the next experiment is worth a band. A photograph and the word 'interesting' is worth nothing.

faqs.question: When is paying for MYP Arts support the wrong decision?
faqs.answer: Four cases. When the journal is empty because the work was never done - that needs a schedule, not a tutor. During a rotation year, when specialist coaching is a bet on which discipline the school will later assess. When a beginner needs hands-on physical technique, which online academic support does not provide and should not pretend to. And when a student is already scoring 6s and 7s, because the remaining marks are usually in criterion C risk-taking, a disposition built by making more work with permission to fail. In all four, the honest recommendation after a trial is a smaller purchase or none.

faqs.question: Does instrument hire or purchase count as an MYP Arts cost?
faqs.answer: It is a real cost and it is often deferrable, which matters more. School loan stock covers many students through the early MYP years, and rental is widely available after that, so purchase can usually be postponed by a year. That postponement is worth taking during a rotation model in MYP 1 to 3, because the assessed Arts discipline may not turn out to be music at all. Families who commit to buying an instrument before the school has confirmed the specialisation route are making the most expensive avoidable decision in this subject.

faqs.question: How many hours of Arts support does a term usually take?
faqs.answer: Less than in most subjects. The common and effective shape is a four to six session journal block - roughly four to six hours in total - aimed at a single criterion profile, after which the student maintains the journal themselves. Weekly year-long arrangements are occasionally right for a student whose criterion B skill development or criterion D written responses are genuinely behind, but they are the exception. Any provider recommending a standing arrangement before reading the journal has not established what the problem is, and in this subject the problem is usually evidential and quickly fixed.

faqs.question: Does MYP Arts affect Diploma options enough to justify the spend?
faqs.answer: It affects readiness rather than eligibility. Diploma Visual Arts, Music, Theatre and Dance are assessed through externally submitted work with a much heavier documentation demand, and students who kept a genuine MYP journal - including failed experiments - find the transition manageable where students who kept a tidy one do not. Abu Dhabi Diploma Arts cohorts are small and a school may not run every discipline in a given year, so check at option-choice time. The spend that genuinely pays forward is journal discipline in MYP 3 and 4, which is the cheapest part.

faqs.question: Will a practising artist without IB experience be good enough as a tutor?
faqs.answer: For technique, often yes. For the grade, frequently not. The marks in MYP Arts are distributed across knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively and responding, with three of those four evidenced in the journal - and a tutor who has never read the criteria cannot band a journal or tell a student which descriptor their reflection falls short of. A practising artist at a lower rate is good value for hands-on skill work. For criterion-referenced review, ask directly whether the tutor has marked MYP Arts work before paying for it.

faqs.question: Does an Arts tutor need a MoHRE permit, and who pays for it?
faqs.answer: A permit is required of the tutor and costs nothing. The UAE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Anyone tutoring privately without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. A provider adding a licensing charge to your bill is charging you for a free document.

faqs.question: Do Arts tutoring rates rise before an exhibition or performance deadline?
faqs.answer: Advertised rates generally hold; availability does not. Demand concentrates in the weeks before a school exhibition, recital or portfolio submission, and the first thing to disappear is a specialist in the right discipline at a usable hour. Families who wait until that point commonly pay an upper-band rate for a third-choice tutor, or find nothing at all in a narrow discipline like dance or theatre. Because the useful work here is a short journal block rather than a long course, booking it early in the term is both cheaper and more effective than booking it late at any price.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-arts-tutor.closingHeading: Work out which purchase you need before you make one
abu-dhabi/ib-myp-arts-tutor.closingBody: Arts is the MYP subject where the wrong purchase is easiest to make and the right one is often the smallest. Send one finished piece and five real journal pages, and the free trial lesson - one lesson, one student, no card details, nothing payable - will establish whether the problem is technical or evidential, give you a band judgement per criterion, and recommend a number of sessions with a stated finish. Where the answer is that no paid support is needed, the written note says so. Sessions run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-biology-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors here teach the biology strand of MYP Sciences, integrated in MYP 1 to 3 and discrete where an Abu Dhabi school offers it in MYP 4 and 5. Each marks practice work against the published criterion rubric, writes the note that follows a session, and will show you a baseline before asking you to commit to a term.

intro.heading: How you will know whether biology tutoring is working
paragraphs: Most tutoring is bought on impression and abandoned on impression. A parent feels that sessions are going well because the student is calmer about biology, or feels that they are not because a grade has not moved, and in neither case is there anything on the table to look at. MYP biology is unusually well suited to a different approach, because the assessment model already produces the evidence. Four criteria, each marked out of eight, applied to tasks your child's school writes. That gives you four numbers to take a baseline from and four numbers to compare against later, strand by strand, instead of one blurred grade.

So the arrangement on this page starts with a baseline before any money changes hands. Send one marked biology task with the teacher's comments and the current report showing criterion levels. The tutor records where each criterion sits, which strand inside each criterion lost the level, and what the task was actually asking for. That record is written down and sent to you. It is the thing every later claim about progress gets measured against, and without it nobody can honestly say whether eight weeks of sessions achieved anything.

The second part is the fortnightly artefact. After two weeks there should be a piece of practice work marked against the rubric. After four weeks there should be an annotated draft of a biology write-up in the student's own words, with the tutor's marks visible as questions rather than corrections. After six weeks there should be a second marked task comparable to the baseline. If those three things do not exist, no amount of positive feeling is evidence, and you are entitled to say so.

The third part is the honest reading of what the evidence means. A criterion C level that moves from 3 to 5 across six weeks is a real result. A biology grade that moves from 4 to 5 in the same period may be a real result or may be a different unit with an easier task, and we will say which we think it is. Grades in the MYP are produced from tasks of varying difficulty set by the school, so a grade on its own is a weaker signal than a criterion level on a comparable task. Parents are rarely told this, and it changes how you should read a report.

All of it happens online. Lessons are one to one, live over video, in Gulf Standard Time, and IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi; visiting tutors are a service we run only in India. For an evidence-led arrangement the online format helps directly: every annotated draft, marked task and session note is a file that already exists in a shared place, rather than ink on a page in a school bag that nobody can find in six weeks' time.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-biology-tutor.programmesIntro: Biology shows up differently in each part of the IB continuum, and so does the evidence it produces. The record you can build in the MYP is better than most families realise and worse than the external record the Diploma generates, which is why what you do with it matters.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Biology is one strand of the Sciences subject group. MYP 1 to 3 is typically integrated, with cells, nutrition and ecology units alongside chemistry and physics. MYP 4 and 5 may split into discrete biology. All work is marked internally against criteria A to D, each out of eight, on tasks the school writes. That internal model is what makes a private baseline worth keeping.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi the schools licensed by ADEK report criterion levels directly, so the raw material for an evidence ledger is already in your household. ADEK also inspects these schools and publishes ratings, which gives a second reference point: a department rated well where your child is scoring poorly points towards a student-specific gap rather than a teaching one. That distinction decides whether tutoring is the right purchase at all.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Biology becomes a named Standard or Higher Level course with external papers and an Internal Assessment. The evidence changes character completely: marks come from outside the school, past papers exist, and progress can be measured against published assessment criteria on work that an examiner will eventually see.
programmes.countryNote: What an Abu Dhabi family keeps from the MYP is a record of which criteria were weak, and that predicts Diploma difficulty better than the MYP grade does. A student who left MYP 5 with a solid criterion A and a persistent criterion C problem will struggle with the Internal Assessment two years later, because the Internal Assessment is criterion C with the scaffolding removed. Families who kept the ledger know to spend DP 1 money on data handling rather than on content revision.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led science with no criterion grading. Children observe living things, record what they see and describe change. There is no biology mark, no rubric and therefore no evidence to baseline, which is the honest reason paid biology tutoring has nothing to work with at this stage.
programmes.countryNote: In continuum schools in this emirate a child moves from PYP 5 straight into MYP 1 and meets criterion marking for the first time. The transferable habit is recording: a child who writes down what they observed, with a unit and a date, arrives in MYP 1 already doing the thing criterion C will reward. That costs nothing and we would rather recommend it than sell a biology course to a ten-year-old.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-biology-tutor.subjectsIntro: A biology request usually arrives attached to something else, because the Sciences criteria are shared and the skills travel. These are the courses Abu Dhabi families most often combine with biology, and what evidence each one generates.

subjects.name: Sciences: the biology strand
subjects.description: Cells and microscopy, transport across membranes, nutrition and digestion, gas exchange, homeostasis, inheritance, evolution and ecology. The clearest evidence of progress here is a labelled diagram and an ecology sampling write-up, both of which show criterion C work plainly.

subjects.name: Sciences: the chemistry strand
subjects.description: Particles, bonding, reactions and quantitative work. Shares criteria C and D with biology, so a data-processing fix made in biology is visible in the next chemistry write-up without being taught twice.

subjects.name: Sciences: the physics strand
subjects.description: Forces, energy, waves and electricity. Its graph work is the most demanding of the three strands, which makes it a useful place to practise a criterion C skill that biology will then reuse on a growth curve or a transect.

subjects.name: Integrated Sciences
subjects.description: One grade covering all three strands, which averages away exactly the signal a parent needs. Ask for criterion levels per unit instead; a biology unit at 6, 3, 4, 5 next to a physics unit at 5, 5, 5, 5 tells you something the overall grade hides.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Standard)
subjects.description: Scale, ratio, percentages and simple statistics. Biology is quietly numerical: magnification calculations, rates of reaction in enzyme work, percentage change in growth data and means from sampling all sit inside criterion C levels.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, evaluating. Produces a process journal, which is the closest thing in the MYP to the fortnightly record this page argues for, and students who keep one well transfer the habit to Sciences.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Investigation, source handling and critical thinking. Directly useful for criterion D in biology, where implications of applying science must be discussed with specific consequences rather than general concern about the environment.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysis, organisation, text production and language use. Biology write-ups are extended prose, and a student who cannot structure a paragraph will lose Sciences levels for reasons a biology tutor alone cannot fix.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first or additional language
subjects.description: Required alongside the licensed curriculum in UAE private schools, with its own homework load. It is the main reason an Abu Dhabi biology plan has fewer workable evenings than a plan written for a student elsewhere.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Separately assessed units pairing Sciences with another subject group. Ecology and sustainability pairings are common in this emirate, and they carry their own criteria and their own grade, which parents often discover only when the report arrives.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-biology-tutor.regionsTitle: Abu Dhabi communities and the biology records that come out of them
abu-dhabi/ib-myp-biology-tutor.regionsIntro: Delivery is online, so no tutor is driving anywhere. What varies between communities is the school day, the hour at which a student can still write carefully, and which biology artefacts families arrive holding when they first make contact.

regions.name: Eastern Mangroves
regions.note: The one community where criterion D and ecology fieldwork are on the doorstep. Students here can write a sampling investigation about a habitat they can walk to, which produces visibly stronger evidence than a generic food-web task.

regions.note: Early returns from island school runs make four o'clock sessions workable, which matters for biology because annotating a draft takes patience. Al Reem families usually arrive with a marked task already in hand.

sections.heading: The baseline: what gets written down before the first paid session
paragraphs: A baseline in MYP biology takes one marked task, the current criterion levels and about twenty minutes of a specialist's reading. What comes out of it is a short document naming four things: where each criterion currently sits, which strand inside the weakest criterion lost the level, what the task's command terms asked for, and which single criterion the term will target. That document is sent to you before anything is paid for, and every later claim about progress is measured against it.

Specificity is what makes it useful. 'Criterion C is weak' is not a baseline. 'Criterion C sits at 3; the data table had units in the cells rather than the headings, no mean was calculated from the three repeats, the graph used a line where the variable was categoric, and the evaluation named no limitation of the method' is a baseline, because each of those four statements can be checked against the same student's work six weeks later. It also tells you what the sessions are supposed to be doing, which means you can tell when they are not doing it.

Parents sometimes ask why a report card is not enough. Because a report gives you an average of tasks of different difficulty, written by different teachers, at different points in a unit. It tells you roughly where a student stands and almost nothing about why. A marked task tells you why, and the why is the only thing a tutor can act on. If the school has not sent marked work home this term, ask for it; schools in this emirate are generally willing, and the request itself tends to produce a useful conversation with the subject teacher.

sections.heading: Reading a marked biology task when you are not a biologist
paragraphs: A parent with no biology background can extract a surprising amount from a marked task in ten minutes, and the method does not require knowing the answers. Start with the command terms. Find each one in the question and read whether the answer did what it asked. If a question says 'explain' and the answer contains no 'because' and no mechanism, that is a lost mark you can see without understanding the biology at all.

Next, look at the diagrams. MYP biology rewards accurate labelled diagrams, and they fail in predictable ways: labels with lines that touch nothing in particular, structures drawn freehand where the shape carries meaning, no title, no magnification stated where a microscope was used. All of that is visible to anyone. A student who draws well and labels carelessly is losing criterion A marks for reasons that take one session to fix.

Then look at the data. In any biology write-up, check whether the table has units in the headings, whether repeats appear, whether a mean was calculated, and whether the graph type matches the kind of variable. A bar chart for a continuous variable or a line joining the dots instead of a line of best fit are the two errors that recur most, and both are mechanical. Finally, read the last paragraph. If it says 'there may have been human error' and stops, criterion C's evaluation strand has been left on the table, and that is worth one or two levels in itself.

What you cannot assess yourself is whether the biology content is right, and that is fine, because it is usually not the problem. Across requests from this emirate, content-only failures are the minority. The majority are command terms, diagram discipline, data presentation and evaluation, all of which a parent can audit directly. Doing that audit before buying tutoring often reveals that one focused term, not an open-ended arrangement, is what is actually needed.

sections.heading: What moves a biology criterion level, and how long each takes
paragraphs: Criterion levels do not move at the same speed, and knowing the rates stops families from abandoning an arrangement that is working or continuing one that is not. Criterion A, knowing and understanding, is the quickest: two to four sessions of focused work on explanation rather than description will usually move it a level, because the underlying knowledge is often already there and being presented wrongly.

Criterion B, inquiring and designing, is the slowest. A student has to produce a testable research question, identify and control variables, justify a method and plan something that would actually work. Four to eight sessions is a realistic expectation for one level, and the work is largely transferable: a student who can plan an osmosis investigation can plan an enzyme one. Criterion C, processing and evaluating, sits in similar territory, although the presentation half of it can move fast while the evaluation half takes longer.

Criterion D, reflecting on the impacts of science, is the one where a specific local context produces the fastest movement. Students write generically about environmental harm and score in the middle. Given a real habitat, a real trade-off and a citable source, the same student writes something specific and moves two levels. That is why the Abu Dhabi ecology context is treated as a tool on this page rather than as decoration. The table sets out each criterion with the strand that most often costs the level and a realistic number of sessions.

sections.heading: Diagrams, systems and the biology that produces checkable evidence
paragraphs: Biology content divides into parts that generate good evidence quickly and parts that do not. Cells and microscopy generate it immediately: a labelled diagram with a stated magnification is either accurate or it is not, and a student's second attempt sits next to their first. Transport across membranes is similarly legible, because osmosis and diffusion investigations produce numbers, and numbers produce the tables and graphs that criterion C is marked on.

Systems content, meaning digestion, circulation, gas exchange and homeostasis, generates evidence through explanation. These topics are where the gap between describing and explaining is widest: a student can list the parts of the digestive system and still be unable to explain why surface area matters to absorption. A tutor's intervention here is to keep asking why until structure and function are linked, and the evidence is a cold answer to a question the student has not seen, before and after.

Inheritance produces the cleanest evidence of all, because it is partly procedural. A student either sets out a genetic cross correctly, with parental genotypes, gametes, offspring genotypes and the phenotype ratio, or they do not. That is checkable by a parent in thirty seconds and improves in two or three sessions. Evolution and natural selection are the opposite: they reward precise reasoning about variation, selection and inheritance over generations, and loose phrasing about animals adapting because they needed to is penalised heavily. Ecology sits between the two, generating sampling data and the opportunity for a genuinely local criterion D discussion.

sections.heading: The Abu Dhabi habitat on your doorstep, used as criterion D evidence
paragraphs: Criterion D asks a student to apply science to address a problem and to discuss the implications of doing so. Most students answer it with generalities about pollution, and most scripts look identical as a result. Abu Dhabi students have access to specific local material that almost none of them use, and specificity is exactly what separates a middling level from a strong one.

The mangrove stands along the eastern edge of the island are a working example. They are a real habitat with a named dominant species, a measurable role in sediment stabilisation and carbon storage, a nursery function for fish, and a direct conflict with coastal development. A student can visit, photograph a transect, note the zonation from the water's edge inland, and write about a trade-off that exists rather than one imagined. The Environment Agency for the emirate publishes material on coastal and marine habitats that can be cited properly, which turns an assertion into a referenced claim.

Other contexts work the same way. Desert ecology supports a discussion of water conservation and grazing pressure. Species reintroduction programmes in this emirate raise questions about captive breeding, genetic diversity and the cost of conservation in money terms. Wetland reserves inland support a discussion of migratory birds and habitat protection against land use. Each of those has published local material behind it, which is the difference between a criterion D paragraph that could have been written anywhere and one that could only have been written here. The second scores better and takes no longer to write.

sections.heading: The academic-honesty line, and why the evidence depends on it
paragraphs: An evidence-led arrangement only works if the evidence is the student's. The IB's position is unambiguous: submitted work must be the student's own, and a tutor who supplies text has destroyed both the student's position and the only record worth keeping. A tutor may teach biology, question reasoning, mark practice work, name an unaddressed strand of the rubric and explain in general terms what a limitation or an implication is. A tutor may not provide sentences for a submission, correct a draft into a finished state, or supply answers to the task being assessed.

The question-led method is what makes this practical rather than merely principled. A tutor who annotates a draft with 'what was the smallest division on the instrument you used, and could you see the difference you are claiming?' has taught the evaluation strand without writing a word of it. The student answers in their own language, and the answer survives a teacher asking about it later. A tutor who writes 'the thermometer's precision limited the result' has handed over a sentence that the student cannot defend and that has taught nothing.

This matters commercially as well, because the same search results that brought you here contain providers selling completed assessed work. That is a malpractice trigger for the student, and the student bears the consequence. It is also why the annotated draft and its rewrite are both kept in this arrangement: two versions in the student's own voice, with the tutor's questions visible between them, are evidence of teaching. A single polished document with no history behind it is evidence of nothing, and in a dispute it is worse than nothing.

sections.heading: When the record says stop, and what to do about it
paragraphs: A six-week review has three honest outcomes, and two of them are not 'continue'. If the targeted criterion moved and the artefacts are in place, continuing is straightforward. If nothing moved, the question is why, and there are only a few real answers. The diagnosis may have been wrong, in which case the baseline gets rewritten and the target changes. The tutor may be the wrong match, in which case changing tutor rather than stopping is usually right. Or the obstacle may sit outside biology entirely.

That third case is more common than families expect. A student whose criterion C problem is really a mathematics problem will not improve with biology sessions, however good they are, because every data-processing task will keep failing at the same arithmetic step. A student whose write-ups fail on structure needs writing support, not biology support. A student whose sessions keep landing at half past seven after a long bus journey and two other homework subjects is not failing to learn; they are too tired to. The record usually shows which of these it is, because session notes that say 'ran out of time again' six weeks in a row are telling you something about the timetable rather than about the biology.

The fourth possibility is that tutoring is not needed. If the evidence shows a student at 6 or 7 across the criteria who is anxious rather than behind, more sessions will not help and may make it worse. We would rather say that at the six-week review and stop than keep selling hours into a problem that is not academic. Saying it is only possible because the baseline exists; without a record, every arrangement defaults to continuing indefinitely, which is precisely why so many of them do.

sections.heading: What the MYP biology record predicts about the Diploma
paragraphs: The most valuable thing a family takes out of MYP biology is not the grade. It is knowing which criteria were weak, because the Diploma reuses them with the scaffolding removed. The Internal Assessment in Diploma biology is essentially criteria B and C combined and extended: a student designs an investigation, collects and processes data, and evaluates the method, largely unaided. A student who left MYP 5 with a persistent criterion C weakness will meet that weakness again two years later with far higher stakes.

Criterion A translates less directly, because Diploma content is far broader and recall demands are higher. What does translate is the explanation habit. Students who learned in MYP 4 to answer 'explain' with a mechanism rather than a description arrive able to write Diploma answers that earn marks, and students who never learned it spend DP 1 being told the same thing their MYP teacher told them. Criterion D has the loosest mapping of the four, although the discipline of citing a source and naming a specific consequence is exactly what Diploma extended responses reward.

For an Abu Dhabi family choosing whether to spend in MYP 5, that is the practical frame. You are not buying a middle-years number that no university will ever see. You are buying the criterion B and C skills that the Internal Assessment will assume are already in place, at a market rate well below what Diploma support costs, in a year when the student has more time than they will have in DP 1. The record from MYP 5 then tells your DP 1 tutor exactly where to start, which is itself worth several sessions.

process.title: Send one marked biology task
process.description: With the teacher's comments on it, plus the current report showing criterion levels. These two documents support a real diagnosis; a phone conversation about how biology is going does not, because students and parents are usually wrong about which criterion is the problem.

process.title: Receive the written baseline
process.description: Before any payment, you get a short document naming where each criterion sits, which strand lost the level, what the command terms asked, and the single criterion a term would target. It is written so that it can be proved wrong later, which is the point of it.

process.title: One session at no charge on the same work
process.description: A fifty-minute session with an MYP Sciences specialist at no charge, one per family, no card details taken. It tests the baseline's diagnosis against the student cold. Occasionally it disproves the diagnosis, which is more useful than confirming it.

process.title: Agree target, count and terms in writing
process.description: One criterion, a number of sessions, the rate in AED, whether preparation time is charged, and the reschedule window. Chasing all four criteria at once produces a busy term with nothing to show at the end of it.

process.title: Review at six weeks against the baseline
process.description: Second marked task next to the first, same criterion, read strand by strand. Continue, change tutor, change target, or stop. All four are real outcomes, and the review is where we say which one the evidence supports rather than which one sells more hours.

whyPoints.title: A baseline you can hold us to
whyPoints.description: The target criterion and the failing strand are written down and sent to you before the first paid session. That document is specific enough to be proved wrong, which is the only kind of promise worth making about tutoring.

whyPoints.title: Artefacts, not impressions
whyPoints.description: A marked practice task every fortnight, an annotated draft with the student's rewrite beside it, and a comparable second task at six weeks. Each is a thing you can look at. None of them is a score we invented or a dashboard built to look like progress.

whyPoints.title: Honest reading of a grade
whyPoints.description: A grade that rises may reflect an easier task rather than a better student, and we will say so when that is the likelier explanation. A criterion level on comparable work is the stronger signal, and treating the two as equivalent is how families get told good news that is not true.

whyPoints.title: Questions instead of answers
whyPoints.description: Drafts are annotated with questions. The student answers them and rewrites in their own language, which is both the honest route and the one that produces defensible work. No sentence for a submission is ever supplied by a tutor here.

whyPoints.title: Local context used properly
whyPoints.description: Criterion D rewards specificity, and this emirate has mangrove stands, desert ecology, reintroduction programmes and wetland reserves with published material behind them. A referenced paragraph about a habitat your child can visit outscores a general one about the environment.

whyPoints.title: A review that can say stop
whyPoints.description: At six weeks the evidence decides, and sometimes it decides against continuing. If the obstacle is mathematics, writing or an exhausted eight o'clock session, we will say that rather than sell another term into a problem biology tutoring cannot reach.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether my child's biology tutoring is actually working?
faqs.answer: By comparing a marked task from week one with a comparable one from week six, on the same criterion, strand by strand. That is the only comparison that means anything, because MYP tasks vary in difficulty and an overall grade averages them. Alongside it you should have a marked practice task every fortnight, an annotated draft with the student's rewrite beside it, and a short written note after each session. If those artefacts do not exist after six weeks, you have no evidence of progress regardless of how the sessions felt, and you are entitled to say so.

faqs.question: How can I check a marked biology task if I have no biology background?
faqs.answer: Four checks, none of which need subject knowledge. Find each command term and read whether the answer did what it asked, so an 'explain' question with no 'because' in the answer is a visible lost mark. Look at the diagrams for labels that point at nothing, missing titles and absent magnification. Check the data table for units in the headings, repeats and a mean. Read the final paragraph: if it says there may have been human error and stops, the evaluation strand has been left unwritten. Those four cover most lost marks in this emirate.

faqs.question: My daughter's biology criterion levels are 6, 3, 4, 5. What does that tell us?
faqs.answer: That the biology knowledge is in good shape and the investigation work is not. A 6 on criterion A means she can explain and apply content. A 3 on criterion B means inquiring and designing is the problem: the research question, the variables, the justification of the method. The 4 on criterion C says data processing and evaluation are mediocre, which usually travels with a weak B. A term aimed squarely at B, with C following, is the right purchase. A term of content revision would raise the 6 slightly and change nothing else.

faqs.question: How long does it take for a biology criterion level to move?
faqs.answer: It depends on which one. Criterion A usually moves in two to four focused sessions, because the knowledge is often present and being presented wrongly. Criterion B takes four to eight, as designing a controlled investigation is a composite skill that has to be built. Criterion C is similar, with presentation improving faster than evaluation. Criterion D can move in two to five sessions if the student is given a specific local context and a citable source instead of writing generally about the environment. Anyone promising a level in a fortnight is describing a sale.

faqs.question: Can we see evidence of the approach before committing to a term?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is the sequence we prefer. Send one marked task and the current criterion levels, and you receive a written baseline naming where each criterion sits and which strand lost the level, before any payment. Then one fifty-minute session at no charge, one per family, with no card details taken, which tests that diagnosis against your child cold. You keep the baseline document either way. If the session disproves the diagnosis, that is a useful outcome rather than an embarrassing one, and it changes what gets bought.

faqs.question: What should exist after four weeks of biology sessions?
faqs.answer: Three things. A marked practice task from around week two, scored against the published criterion rubric rather than given a percentage. An annotated draft of a biology write-up, with the tutor's marks appearing as questions rather than as corrections, plus the student's own rewrite of it so the change is visible side by side. And four short session notes, one paragraph each, naming which criterion strand was worked on and what to practise. If any of those is missing at four weeks, ask why before week six.

faqs.question: Is a rising biology grade proof that the tutoring worked?
faqs.answer: Not on its own. MYP grades come from tasks of varying difficulty, written and marked by your child's own school, so a move from 4 to 5 could reflect a kinder task rather than a better student. The stronger signal is a criterion level on comparable work, which is why the baseline records the strand rather than the grade. We will tell you when we think a rise is task difficulty rather than progress. A provider that treats every improvement as proof of its own value is not measuring anything.

faqs.question: How do we evidence criterion B when the practical happens at school?
faqs.answer: By working on the plan rather than the apparatus. Criterion B is assessed on the research question, the variables identified and controlled, the justification of the method and the plan's workability, all of which are written documents. A tutor can set an investigation planning task on a biology topic the school is not currently assessing, mark it against the rubric, and repeat it a fortnight later on a different topic. Two plans, two marked levels, same criterion. That is clean evidence, and it does not touch the work being submitted at school.

faqs.question: What counts as strong evidence for criterion D in biology?
faqs.answer: A paragraph that names a specific application, a specific consequence and a source. Writing that pollution harms ecosystems earns a middling level because it is true of everywhere. Writing about the mangrove stands at the eastern edge of Abu Dhabi, their role in stabilising sediment and sheltering juvenile fish, and the direct conflict with coastal development, with an emirate environment-agency publication cited, earns considerably more. The evidence of progress here is simple: the earlier paragraph next to the later one, with the citation and the named trade-off present in the second.

faqs.question: Does my child have to do fieldwork for MYP biology?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, as it depends entirely on what your school's units require, and the IB prescribes concepts and criteria for Sciences rather than a content list. Where ecology appears, fieldwork is common because sampling produces data a student can process. Even where the school does not run a trip, a student can practise the whole cycle informally: a transect along a public shoreline or a quadrat on a patch of ground generates real numbers to tabulate, mean and plot. The marks live in the processing and evaluation, not in the location.

faqs.question: Can we use the Abu Dhabi mangroves in a biology investigation write-up?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the better options available in this emirate. The stands along the eastern coast have a named dominant species, visible zonation from the water inland, and a documented role in sediment stabilisation and as a fish nursery. A student can photograph a transect, record zonation, and build a criterion D discussion about coastal development trade-offs with an emirate environment-agency publication as the source. Two cautions: check access rules for the specific site, and keep the write-up entirely in the student's own words.

faqs.question: What should we do if six weeks of sessions show no movement?
faqs.answer: Work through four explanations in order. The diagnosis may have been wrong, so rewrite the baseline and change the target. The tutor may be a poor match, in which case change tutor rather than stopping. The obstacle may sit outside biology: a criterion C problem that is really a ratio problem, or write-ups failing on paragraph structure. Or the schedule may be the issue, which session notes repeatedly mentioning lost time will reveal. If none of those applies and the student is already at 6 or 7, the honest answer may be that tutoring is not the right purchase.

faqs.question: Do labelled diagrams really earn marks in MYP biology?
faqs.answer: They do, and they are the most frequently wasted marks we see. Criterion A rewards accurate representation of biological knowledge, and diagrams fail predictably: label lines that end near a structure rather than on it, freehand shapes where proportion carries meaning, no title, and no magnification stated where a microscope was used. None of that is a biology failure, which is why it is fixable in one or two sessions. It is also the easiest thing for a parent to audit in a marked task without knowing any biology at all.

faqs.question: How well does an MYP biology record predict Diploma biology?
faqs.answer: Better than the grade does. The Diploma Internal Assessment is largely criteria B and C extended with the scaffolding removed: the student designs an investigation, processes the data and evaluates the method with far less support. A persistent criterion C weakness in MYP 5 reappears there with much higher stakes. Criterion A translates as the habit of explaining rather than describing, which earns Diploma marks immediately. Keeping the MYP record means a DP 1 tutor can start where the gap actually is instead of spending three sessions finding it.

faqs.question: Will a biology tutor come to our address in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, and visiting tutors are a service we provide only in India. UAE lessons are one to one, live over video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. For an evidence-led arrangement that is an advantage: annotated drafts, marked practice tasks and session notes are files in a shared place rather than paper in a school bag, so a six-week comparison is actually possible. The tutor is also chosen for how well they mark MYP Sciences criteria rather than for where they live.

faqs.question: Should we record the biology sessions to keep our own record?
faqs.answer: The session notes and marked artefacts are the record that matters, and they are easier to use than video. A one-paragraph note naming the criterion strand worked on, plus a marked task every fortnight, can be read in two minutes at the six-week review. An hour of video cannot. If you do want recordings, agree it in writing with the tutor in advance, keep them private to the household, and remember that recordings of a minor are personal data under the UAE's data-protection law and should be stored and deleted accordingly.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-biology-tutor.closingHeading: Start with a baseline, not with a booking
abu-dhabi/ib-myp-biology-tutor.closingBody: The useful first step costs nothing and takes a day. Send one marked biology task with the teacher's comments and the report showing criterion levels. You will get back a written baseline naming where each criterion sits, which strand is costing the level and what a term would target, followed by one fifty-minute session at no charge that tests that reading against your child cold. From there you can decide with a document in front of you rather than a feeling, and six weeks later you can check whether the document turned out to be true.
