abu-dhabi/ib-myp-eassessment-preparation.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach MYP subject groups at Year 5 level and mark against the criterion descriptors the student's own school uses. Each profile names the subject groups covered, the on-screen components they prepare, and the ePortfolio work they can give process feedback on.

intro.heading: A Year 5 report tells you the grade; it rarely tells you what moved
paragraphs: Most Abu Dhabi parents arrive at this page holding a Year 5 report card with four criterion levels on it and no idea which of them is fixable before the May session. The report says 5, 4, 5, 3. It does not say that the 3 is the criterion where the student describes when the task asked them to explain, and that this is a question-shape problem rather than a knowledge problem, and that it is the single cheapest level to move. IB MYP eassessment preparation in Abu Dhabi is useful exactly to the extent that it makes that distinction visible, in writing, in the first fortnight.

So this page is built around evidence rather than reassurance. It sets out what a marked on-screen task should look like when it comes back, what the four criterion bands actually reward at levels 1-2, 3-4, 5-6 and 7-8, what the process journal has to contain for an ePortfolio subject, and what the file of dated drafts does for a Personal Project supervisor who has to sign an authenticity declaration. It also sets out the numbers: what MYP-level support costs across the Abu Dhabi market, who publishes those figures, and what the hour does and does not include.

There is a practical reason to be this specific. MYP eAssessment is not a paper examination sat on a laptop. The on-screen components are built around stimulus material the student reads inside the interface, and a student who revises content but never practises the interface loses marks to navigation and clock management rather than to physics or history. The ePortfolio subjects are won in term one, because what is submitted is a record of process compiled over months. By March, an ePortfolio either exists or it does not, and no amount of weekly tutoring conjures one up.

Abu Dhabi adds its own constraints. ADEK licenses and inspects the private schools here and publishes its own inspection ratings, so a parent comparing two schools is reading an ADEK judgement rather than a Dubai one. School runs along the Sheikh Zayed and Al Maqta corridors put many Khalifa City and Al Raha students home closer to a quarter to five than four o'clock, which decides whether a weekday session is realistically a five-thirty or an eight o'clock. Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies sit on the timetable alongside the MYP in every private school in the emirate, which is minutes a revision plan has to work around rather than wish away.

Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video with a shared whiteboard and the student's own work on screen. IB Gram does not run home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere else in the UAE; that is a service offered only in India. The reason to prefer the online route here is not cost, it is supply: a Year 5 student who needs a design teacher who has moderated ePortfolios gets that person rather than whoever can reach Al Reef by half past five.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-eassessment-preparation.programmesIntro: Four IB programmes run in Abu Dhabi schools, and a Year 5 family is usually looking at two of them at once: the MYP their child is finishing and the Diploma the same school will offer in Year 12. Here is what each one assesses and what it means in this emirate specifically.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria marked out of 8, with the criterion totals converted to a 1-7 grade using published boundaries. The criteria are named differently in different subject groups, but the mark allocation does not change. Assessment is continuous and internal for MYP 1-4, which is why a Year 5 family often meets external marking for the first time in the eAssessment year and finds the standard unfamiliar.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi has a smaller MYP cohort than Dubai, concentrated in the IB continuum schools on the island and in the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor. That matters for supply: a family needing a Year 5 design or arts specialist is drawing on a thin local pool, and the subject groups least covered by in-emirate tutors are usually design, arts and language acquisition at phase 4 or above.

programmes.name: The eAssessment year
programmes.description: The final MYP year is where on-screen examinations and ePortfolios are externally marked and moderated, and where the Personal Project is externally moderated against its own criteria. Schools choose how far to go: some enter candidates for the full IB MYP Certificate, others for individual course results. The two routes carry different requirements, and a parent should know which one their school has chosen before buying a single hour of support.
programmes.countryNote: Ask the MYP coordinator at your Abu Dhabi school, in writing, which components your child is entered for and on what date each is due. Entry decisions are made by the school, not the family, and the registration window closes months before the session. Several Abu Dhabi schools enter course results in two or three subject groups rather than the full certificate, and the preparation plan is materially different in each case.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at Higher or Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Internal assessment carries roughly a fifth to a third of the grade depending on the subject, and the external papers carry the rest. The step up from MYP Year 5 is less about content than about the length of the written answer and the amount of independent reading a Higher Level subject assumes.
programmes.countryNote: Most Abu Dhabi MYP students continue into the Diploma at the same school, which makes Year 5 criterion data genuinely predictive. A student sitting at 4s in the analysis-and-evaluation criterion in a science subject group will meet the same demand again in a Diploma Paper 2 extended response. Fixing the question-shape problem in Year 5 is cheaper than meeting it again in Year 12 with a Higher Level syllabus on top.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units of inquiry with no external examinations, finishing with the Year 6 exhibition. Reporting is against learning outcomes rather than numerical criteria, so the first time most families see a criterion level out of 8 is in MYP 1. That jump in reporting style, not a jump in difficulty, is what unsettles parents of a Year 7 student in their first MYP term.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi IB continuum schools run PYP through to MYP on one campus, so a Year 5 student may have been in the same building since FS1. That continuity is useful: the school holds years of internal evidence. Ask for it. A portfolio of Year 9 and Year 10 work tells a tutor more in twenty minutes than a diagnostic test does in an hour.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-eassessment-preparation.subjectsIntro: MYP subject groups are assessed against four criteria each, and the criterion that is weak is usually the same one across several subjects. These are the groups we cover at Year 5, with the specific place marks go missing in each.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Marks go on analysing how a text produces its effect, not on summarising what happens in it. The commonest Year 5 pattern is a student who can identify a technique and name it correctly but never links it to the reader's response, which caps the analysing criterion at the 3-4 band however much terminology appears.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Four criteria across listening, reading, speaking and writing, with the phase deciding the standard. Students lose marks by writing at the right level in the wrong register: an informal reply where the task set a formal letter scores badly on the criterion that rewards appropriate conventions, regardless of grammatical accuracy.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: The on-screen component hands the student source material and asks for use of it. Answers that could have been written without opening the source lose the investigating and communicating marks. The fix is mechanical: every paragraph must cite a line, a figure or a date from the stimulus provided.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: The criterion that rewards processing and evaluating is where Year 5 science marks disappear. Students calculate correctly, then stop, where the descriptor asks them to evaluate the method's limitations and suggest an improvement that follows from the data rather than a generic one about repeating the experiment.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Standard and extended, on-screen examination at Year 5
subjects.description: Two things cost marks: unjustified steps in the criterion that rewards communication, and real-life application questions where the model is set up but never interpreted back into context. Extended mathematics adds proof-style reasoning that standard students have usually never been asked to write out.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: An ePortfolio subject, so the submission is a documented design cycle rather than a product. Marks sit in the inquiring and analysing stage and in the evaluating stage, both of which demand evidence collected months earlier. A beautiful final artefact with no research record scores in the lower bands.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.levels: Visual arts, music, drama; ePortfolio at Year 5
subjects.description: Assessed on the developmental record as much as the outcome: investigation, process, presentation and reflection. The process journal is the evidence, and it cannot be reconstructed in April. Students who photograph and annotate as they work score in bands their finished pieces alone would not reach.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: The criteria reward planning for performance and reflecting on it, which means written and video evidence rather than athletic ability. A strong athlete with no plan, no data and no reflection sits lower than a moderate performer who documented a training cycle properly.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary learning
subjects.description: Assesses whether a student can bring two disciplines together and say what the combination reveals that neither would alone. Answers that run the two subjects in parallel paragraphs without integrating them score in the middle bands at best, which surprises strong single-subject students.

subjects.name: Personal Project
subjects.description: Marked on planning, applying skills and reflecting, with the process journal and the report as the evidence. The product itself carries no marks of its own. Students lose bands by leaving the journal until the end, which makes the reflection generic and the planning criterion impossible to evidence.

sections.heading: What an on-screen MYP component actually produces as evidence
paragraphs: An MYP on-screen examination is a timed component sat inside a software interface that presents stimulus material alongside the questions. That one structural fact changes what preparation means. A student revising from a textbook is practising recall. A student sitting an on-screen task is being asked to read unfamiliar material under time pressure, work out which criterion a question is testing, and produce a response of the right shape inside a box that does not scroll the way a page does.

The evidence this produces is unusually good, because every task comes back with a criterion level and a reason. After one timed task you can see three separate things: whether the content is known, whether the question shape was recognised, and whether the clock ran out. Those are three different problems with three different fixes, and a report card that says 4 collapses all of them into a single number. This is why the first lesson is spent generating a marked script rather than talking about study habits.

Which subject groups are examined on screen and which are submitted as an ePortfolio is a decision set out in the current MYP assessment arrangements and chosen in part by the school. Confirm it with your child's MYP coordinator in writing before planning anything, because the preparation for a two-hour timed component and the preparation for a portfolio compiled across two terms have almost nothing in common. Getting that wrong in October is the single most expensive planning error available to a Year 5 family.
bullets: A marked script separates missing content from a missed command word
Time-per-question data shows where the clock, not the knowledge, failed
Stimulus-use can be counted: how many paragraphs cite the source
Interface handling improves with practice and is worth real marks

sections.heading: The evidence file: what you should be able to see after four weeks
paragraphs: A month of weekly sessions should leave a file, not a feeling. By the end of week four an Abu Dhabi parent should be able to open a folder and find a dated starting criterion level for each criterion in the target subject group, the descriptor sentence that level came from, at least four marked tasks, and one full-length timed attempt with notes on where the clock ran out. If that file does not exist, there is nothing to judge progress against and the next three months are being bought on trust.

The second thing the file should show is the student marking their own work. A Year 5 student who can mark their own script against the published descriptors and land within one level of the tutor has internalised the standard, and that single skill is worth more in the examination than any individual topic. Disagreement of two or more levels tells you the student does not yet know what the criterion rewards, which is a diagnosable and fixable problem rather than a vague lack of effort.

The table below is the shape of the file we keep, week by week. It is deliberately dull. The point of writing it down is that a plan which is not working becomes visible in week five or six, while there is still time to change the subject group, the criterion or the tutor, rather than in March when the only remaining option is to hope.

sections.heading: Criterion levels one to eight, read as bands rather than as marks
paragraphs: MYP criteria are marked out of 8 and the descriptors come in pairs of bands: 1-2, 3-4, 5-6, 7-8. Treating the number as a score out of eight is the most common parental misreading in Abu Dhabi and elsewhere, because it suggests a 4 is halfway to full marks. It is not. A 4 means the response described where the descriptor at 5-6 asks for explanation with reasoning, and the jump between those two bands is a change in the kind of sentence written, not an increase in the amount of content known.

That reframing is what makes the number useful. Each band has a characteristic missing move, and the missing move is teachable in a known number of sessions. Moving from the 3-4 band to the 5-6 band in a science or humanities subject group is mostly a matter of carrying reasoning through to a judgement and tying every paragraph to the stimulus. Moving from 5-6 to 7-8 is a different order of work: it needs evaluation of limitations and counter-cases offered without prompting, and that depends on reading the student does alone.

The table sets out the four bands, what each descriptor rewards, the move usually missing at that band, and a realistic amount of work to shift one band. The session counts are a planning tool rather than a promise; they come from what the work actually involves at each band, and a student arriving in February with a 3 in two criteria has a materially different plan from one arriving in October.

sections.heading: ePortfolio subjects are judged on the record, and the record is built in term one
paragraphs: In design, arts, physical and health education and language acquisition, the Year 5 submission is an ePortfolio: a compiled record of work with the student's development visible across it. The grade rests on evidence of process. For design that means the inquiring and analysing stage, the research that justified the specification, and an evaluation that tests the outcome against criteria set before it was made. For arts it means the developmental workbook. For physical and health education it means a plan, the data collected while following it, and an honest reflection on what the data showed.

The operational consequence is brutal and worth stating plainly in October rather than March. A process record cannot be assembled retrospectively. A student who photographs and annotates a design iteration in November has evidence; the same student reconstructing that iteration in April has a paragraph of recollection that a moderator will read as exactly that. Every term one session that produces two annotated journal pages is worth more to the final band than a term three session spent polishing the artefact.

What a tutor does here is narrow and it matters that it stays narrow. The tutor reads the journal, asks the questions a moderator would ask, names the stage with no evidence behind it, and sends the student back to collect it. The tutor supplies no text, suggests no wording for the submission and edits nothing. We keep a dated note of each session so the school supervisor can see the sequence of work and confirm it is the student's own.
bullets: Journal pages dated as they are made, not compiled at the end

sections.heading: The Personal Project, the supervisor's record and the line a tutor stays behind
paragraphs: The Personal Project is externally moderated against criteria covering planning, applying skills and reflecting, and the product carries no marks of its own. Students and parents find this counter-intuitive: a genuinely impressive outcome with a thin process journal sits in a lower band than a modest outcome documented properly. The report and the journal are the assessed artefacts. A tutor who understands that spends the sessions on the record of thinking rather than on the thing being made.

There is a hard boundary around this component and it protects the student rather than us. The work must be the student's own, the school supervisor signs an authenticity declaration, and a breach is an academic-honesty matter with consequences that reach the certificate. So the support offered is process coaching: planning the stages, choosing a realistic goal, interrogating the reflection, checking that the journal evidences what the criteria ask for. No sentence of the submission comes from a tutor, and nothing is edited into it.

That boundary is also a differentiator in this market. There are operators in the Gulf selling finished coursework, including completed assessed pieces at prices that imply the work is done for the student. Buying one of those is an academic-honesty breach for the student and a malpractice trigger for the school, and no price makes that a sensible purchase. Saying so explicitly on a page like this is deliberate: it is the position a parent should insist on from anyone they pay.

sections.heading: ADEK, the inspection report and what an Abu Dhabi MYP school's grades tell you
paragraphs: In Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, private schools are the responsibility of the Department of Education and Knowledge, which the UAE government's own portal describes as supervising the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Dubai schools answer to KHDA, Sharjah to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah to its Department of Knowledge, and schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah to the federal Ministry of Education. A parent moving from Dubai to Khalifa City is reading a different regulator's judgements on arrival, not a differently formatted version of the same ones.

What an inspection rating does and does not predict is worth being honest about. A rating describes a school's provision at the time of inspection across a basket of measures. It does not forecast one student's criterion levels in one subject group, and it says nothing about whether the Year 5 design teacher has moderated an ePortfolio before. Parents comparing two Abu Dhabi schools on their published ratings are comparing institutions; parents trying to explain one child's 3 in one criterion need the child's own marked work instead.

The regulator matters to tutoring in a second way. Press reporting of ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff describes a prohibition on teachers giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, with the MoHRE private tuition work permit required for teachers tutoring outside school hours. Treat that as press-reported and verify it against the current ADEK policy document, but the practical advice holds: do not arrange paid tuition with your child's own class teacher in this emirate.

Our own model is a free trial lesson first and a consultation that quotes against the actual subject group, criterion target and number of weeks remaining.

Two things move the number more than anything else at MYP level. The first is whether marked work comes back. An hour of conversation and an hour that returns a criterion-level mark with the descriptor quoted are priced similarly in this market and are not the same product, and the difference is invisible until you ask to see a sample marked script. Ask for one before paying. The second is travel: a tutor driving to Al Reef or Al Shamkha in late afternoon traffic is charging for the drive inside the hourly rate, whether or not the invoice itemises it.

Read the table as a map of what exists rather than as a recommendation. The lower bands are typically university students or generalists; the upper bands are advertised as specialists. Nothing about a price confirms that the person holds a MoHRE private tuition work permit, has marked at Year 5 standard, or has seen an ePortfolio moderated. Those are separate questions, and they are the ones worth asking.

sections.heading: The Abu Dhabi school-run clock and when a Year 5 session can realistically start
paragraphs: A tutoring plan that ignores the commute collapses in week three. Abu Dhabi spreads its international enrolment across the island, the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor and the mainland communities, and bus routes from Al Reef, Al Shamkha and Al Falah can put a Year 5 student through the door after five. A session booked for half past four looks fine on a calendar in October and becomes a weekly argument by November, which is how good plans die.

The honest version is that most Abu Dhabi weekday sessions work at one of two times: shortly after the student is home and fed, or after eight when homework is done. Timed on-screen practice is a different problem again, because a two-hour component cannot be rehearsed in a forty-minute weekday slot. Families who take timed work seriously put it at the weekend and keep the weekday slot for single-criterion work on shorter tasks. Two hours on a Friday or Saturday morning costs a family less in friction than four interrupted weekday evenings, and it produces a comparable script.

Ramadan reorganises all of it. Sessions move to post-Iftar timing, concentration in the late afternoon drops, and schools shorten the day. Planning around it rather than pretending it will not happen is the difference between losing four weeks and losing one. The table below lists the areas our Year 5 families contact us from, the school clusters they typically use, when students are actually home, and the slots that hold up across a full term.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies inside a Year 5 week
paragraphs: Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific national curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, and must otherwise adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That federal rule is why your child's Abu Dhabi school teaches those subjects alongside the MYP rather than instead of it, and why a revision plan built as though the week contains only eight MYP subject groups is already over-committed before it starts.

KHDA's published guidelines for Dubai schools give the clearest public picture of how the requirement is implemented, and they are worth reading even for an Abu Dhabi family because the underlying federal obligation is the same. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit, advises that no mandatory subject lesson runs shorter than twenty-five minutes, requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and social studies, and prohibits additional or different content without prior Ministry permission.

For planning purposes the arithmetic is simple. Those lessons occupy real timetable minutes, they carry their own assessments and homework, and in Year 5 they land in the same weeks as ePortfolio submissions. A family choosing between a second MYP subject group and Arabic support should make that choice deliberately in October, not discover in February that both were needed. Where Arabic is the pressure point, it is worth asking the school which stream the student sits in before arranging anything, because the content and language of instruction differ between the streams.

process.title: Tell us the subject group and the criterion
process.description: Send the Year 5 report, the subject group that is weakest, and the criterion levels as written. If you have a marked piece of work, send that too. A photograph of a marked script tells us more than a paragraph of description, and it means the free lesson starts from the actual problem rather than from a diagnostic test.

process.title: A free trial lesson that produces a marked task
process.description: One lesson, free, one per student, no card details taken. You finish with a starting criterion level and the descriptor sentence it came from, whether or not you continue.

process.title: Agree the target and the weeks available
process.description: We count the weeks left before the school's own submission and entry deadlines, not before the session, because the ePortfolio dates come first. From that we set which criterion is the target, how many sessions it realistically needs, and what the fortnightly written summary will report. The plan is written down so it can be checked.

process.title: Weekly sessions in a fixed Gulf Standard Time slot
process.description: A fixed weekly slot chosen around your area's school run, with longer weekend blocks when timed on-screen practice is due. Each session produces a marked task and a logged criterion level, and Ramadan timings move to post-Iftar slots by arrangement rather than by cancellation.

process.title: Review the evidence at week six
process.description: At week six we look at the chart of criterion levels together. If it has not moved, we change something concrete: the criterion, the task type, the session length or the tutor. Continuing unchanged because everyone is being polite is the failure mode this review exists to prevent.

whyPoints.title: The marking comes back, every time
whyPoints.description: Every session returns a marked task with a criterion level and the descriptor sentence that level came from. You are not buying an hour of conversation; you are buying a piece of marked evidence that either shows movement or does not. Ask any provider for a sample marked script before you pay them, including us.

whyPoints.title: Specialist supply rather than local radius
whyPoints.description: Online delivery means a Year 5 student in Al Shamkha can work with a design or arts specialist who has seen ePortfolios moderated, instead of whoever is free within a thirty-minute drive. In a thin market like Abu Dhabi's MYP cohort, that is the whole argument, and it has nothing to do with saving money.

whyPoints.title: A boundary around assessed work that protects the student
whyPoints.description: Process coaching on the Personal Project and ePortfolio components, with nothing supplied, drafted or edited into a submission. The student's work stays the student's, the supervisor's declaration stays true, and the dated session record is there if the school asks what support was given.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling built for this emirate
whyPoints.description: Slots set in Gulf Standard Time around the school runs that actually exist here, including later starts for bus routes from Al Reef and Al Shamkha, weekend blocks for timed components, and post-Iftar sessions during Ramadan. A plan that fits the week survives the term.

whyPoints.title: Figures that carry a source
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page names the provider that published it and the month it was read, and every regulatory statement points at the authority that issued it. Where something is not verifiable, including specific IB session and results dates, the page says so instead of printing a number that might be wrong.

whyPoints.title: A six-week review with teeth
whyPoints.description: A fortnightly written summary and a formal review at week six, where the criterion chart decides what happens next. Changing tutor or target at week six costs nothing. Discovering in March that nothing moved since October costs the session.

faqs.question: How do we tell whether MYP eassessment preparation is actually working, week by week?
faqs.answer: Ask for three things in writing. First, a dated starting level for each criterion in the target subject group, with the descriptor sentence it came from. Second, a marked task from every session, so you can see the mark rather than hear about the lesson. Third, a fortnightly summary naming the criterion being worked on and what changed. By week six those three items either show a criterion level moving or they show it flat. Flat is useful information at week six and useless in March, which is why the review date matters as much as the lessons.

faqs.question: What should a marked on-screen practice task look like when it comes back?
faqs.answer: It should carry a criterion level, the quoted descriptor sentence that justifies it, annotations on the script itself showing where marks were gained or lost, and a time note against each question. The annotations matter most. A student who sees that paragraph three never referred to the stimulus material learns something repeatable; a student who sees only a number learns nothing. If a provider cannot show you a sample marked script before you book, that is the most informative answer you will get from them.

faqs.question: My daughter's Year 5 report shows 5, 4, 5 and 3. What does that actually mean?
faqs.answer: Those are four criterion levels out of 8, and they are band positions rather than scores. A 3 sits in the 3-4 band, where the descriptor rewards description with limited use of the material provided. A 5 sits in the band that rewards explanation with reasoning. So the 3 is not a little below the 5; it is a different kind of answer. In practice the 3 is usually the cheapest level to move, because the missing move is tying each paragraph to a line in the stimulus rather than learning new content.

faqs.question: Which Abu Dhabi schools enter candidates for MYP eassessment?
faqs.answer: The IB continuum schools in the emirate do, and they are concentrated on the island and in the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor, with newer campuses on Saadiyat, Yas and the mainland adding cohorts. Rather than trusting any list, ask your own school's MYP coordinator two questions in writing: which components my child is entered for, and whether the entry is for the full MYP Certificate or for individual course results. Schools choose differently, the deadlines sit months before the session, and the preparation plan is materially different for each route.

faqs.question: Can a tutor look at my son's Personal Project journal without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor may read the journal, ask the questions a moderator would ask, point at a stage with no evidence behind it, and discuss structure and planning. A tutor may not supply text, suggest wording for the submission, or edit anything the student submits. The work has to be the student's own because the school supervisor signs an authenticity declaration. We keep a dated record of what each session covered, so if the school asks what support was given there is an honest answer available.

faqs.question: How many criterion levels can realistically move between October and the May session?
faqs.answer: Enough to matter, with no promise attached. Moving one band in a criterion where the missing move is question shape or stimulus use is ordinary work over six to eight weekly sessions. Moving into the 7-8 band is slower, because it depends on independent reading as much as on teaching. Across a Year 5 year starting in October, families typically target one or two criteria in one or two subject groups rather than everything at once. Anyone offering a specific grade outcome is selling something nobody can deliver.

faqs.question: What does the process journal have to show for a design or arts ePortfolio?
faqs.answer: Evidence of the stages, dated as they happened. For design that means the inquiry and research that justified the specification, the iterations with annotations, testing against criteria written before the outcome existed, and an evaluation that refers to the data collected. For arts it means a developmental record: investigation, experiments that failed, and reflection on what changed. A journal assembled in April reads as recollection rather than process, and moderators are experienced at telling the difference between the two.

faqs.question: Does practising on paper prepare a child for an on-screen examination?
faqs.answer: Partly, and the gap is where marks go. Content revision transfers fine. What does not transfer is reading stimulus material inside an interface, moving between tasks without losing your place, typing an extended response in a box that behaves unlike a page, and managing a two-hour clock on screen. Those are learnable skills worth real marks, and they need rehearsal in a comparable environment. Practising them is why we put full-length timed work in weekend blocks rather than trying to squeeze it into a weekday slot.

faqs.question: Does the MYP certificate matter for entry to the Diploma at an Abu Dhabi school?
faqs.answer: Ask the school, because entry requirements are set by the school rather than by the IB, and Abu Dhabi schools differ. What is consistently true is that Year 5 criterion data is read as a signal about readiness, especially in the subject groups a student wants to take at Higher Level. A pattern of 3s in the criterion that rewards analysis and evaluation in a science subject group is the same demand that reappears in a Diploma extended response, so it is worth addressing in Year 5 regardless of what the certificate route turns out to be.

faqs.question: What does MYP-level support cost per hour in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Market rates read in October 2026 run from roughly AED 45-150 an hour for university-student and generalist tutors online, AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor one-to-one online, AED 180-500 for a tutor travelling to an address, and AED 200-650 at the specialist and premium tiers advertised by agencies. Those are other providers' published figures with their names attached, not our prices. IB Gram starts with a free trial lesson and quotes against the subject group, the criterion target and the weeks remaining.

faqs.question: We live in Khalifa City and my son is home at half past four. When can a session start?
faqs.answer: Half past five or eight o'clock, in practice. The Sheikh Zayed corridor run commonly lands Khalifa City and Al Raha students home between four and a quarter to five, and a session scheduled before the student has eaten becomes a weekly argument by November. Shorter single-criterion work fits the earlier slot; full-length timed components do not fit either and belong in a weekend block. During Ramadan the slot moves after Iftar, which is an arrangement rather than a cancellation.

faqs.question: Is my child's own MYP teacher allowed to tutor him privately in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Press reporting of ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff describes a prohibition on teachers giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct described in the same terms. Verify the current wording against the ADEK policy document before relying on it, but the practical advice is settled: do not arrange paid tuition with your child's own class teacher here. Choosing an independent tutor avoids placing the teacher in that position at all.

faqs.question: How do Arabic and Islamic Education fit into a Year 5 revision week in this emirate?
faqs.answer: They sit on top of the MYP timetable rather than instead of it. The federal position is that private schools must teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies and otherwise adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. KHDA's published Dubai guidelines show how this is implemented in practice, calculating mandatory-subject time on a forty-minute lesson unit and requiring separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. Those lessons carry their own assessments, so decide in October whether Arabic support competes with a second MYP subject group.

faqs.question: What happens if the evidence shows no movement after six weeks?
faqs.answer: We change something concrete rather than carry on politely. The options are narrow and all of them are specific: a different criterion as the target, a different task type, a longer session, or a different tutor. Occasionally the honest answer is that the problem is not the subject group at all but a submission deadline being missed at school, which is a conversation with the coordinator rather than more hours. A six-week review exists so that this decision gets made in November instead of March.

faqs.question: Can we see how the marking works before committing to a block of hours?
faqs.answer: That is what the free trial lesson is for: one lesson per student, no card details taken. The student sits a short timed task in the relevant format, and the tutor marks it against the published criterion descriptors and gives you the level plus the descriptor sentence behind it. You keep the marked script either way. Judging a provider on a marked piece of your own child's work is a far better test than any claim on a website, including the claims on this page.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our home in Abu Dhabi, or are all lessons online?
faqs.answer: All lessons are online, one-to-one, over live video with a shared whiteboard and the student's own work on screen. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi or anywhere else in the UAE, and we never send anyone to a UAE address; the in-home service exists only in India. For a Year 5 MYP family the online route is usually the stronger option anyway, because the specialist who has marked your child's subject group at this level is unlikely to also live within driving distance of your community.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-eassessment-preparation.closingHeading: Start with one marked task, not a twelve-week commitment
abu-dhabi/ib-myp-eassessment-preparation.closingBody: The useful first step is small. Send the Year 5 report, name the subject group that worries you, and take the free trial lesson: one per student, no card details taken. Your child sits a short timed task, a specialist marks it against the published criterion descriptors, and you keep the marked script and the starting level whether or not anything follows. From there the decision is an informed one, made on your own child's work rather than on a provider's description of itself. If no specialist in that subject group is free at a workable Gulf Standard Time slot, we will say so rather than book the nearest available alternative.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-eassessment-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below work at MYP 4 and MYP 5 level with Abu Dhabi families. Each is matched to a subject group and to the form that group is assessed in, because on-screen examination practice and ePortfolio feedback are two different jobs with two different sets of rules.

intro.heading: Eight graded components, one keyboard, and a tutor who has to know which is which
paragraphs: Most parents who search for an IB MYP eassessment tutor in Abu Dhabi are a few weeks past a report that said less than they hoped. The grades arrived as single digits against subject groups, the school explained criteria A to D, and nobody said which of the eight graded components behind the certificate that digit belonged to. So the first thing a session establishes is factual rather than academic: what your child is entered for, in which form, and who marks it. Until that sits on one page, hours get spent on the wrong half of a subject while the half that carries the grade goes untouched.

The split matters more than anything else on this page. Some components are sat as on-screen examinations, written into a browser under timed conditions and marked externally against published criteria. The rest are ePortfolios: coursework your child builds across the year, marked by the teacher and moderated externally. The Personal Project sits in its own category, with a supervisor record attached to it. A tutor who treats all eight the same way will give you revision when what you needed was a process journal that stands up, or feedback on a draft when what you needed was timed practice against unseen stimulus material.

Abu Dhabi adds its own layer. Private schools in the emirate are licensed and inspected by ADEK, the Department of Education and Knowledge, which publishes its own inspection ratings, and only some of those schools run the Middle Years Programme at all. Enrolment is spread between the island, the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor, Yas and Saadiyat, and the newer mainland communities, so two MYP 5 students a short drive apart can be following different school calendars and different internal deadlines. The practical consequence is scheduling: a session that works for a family in Al Bateen rarely works unchanged for one in Al Shamkha.

Every lesson IB Gram arranges for a family in the emirate runs online, one-to-one, over live video with a shared screen. IB Gram does not make home visits in Abu Dhabi; that is a service offered only in India, and no page here will tell you otherwise. The reason is not cost. It is supply. There are perhaps a handful of people in the country who have taught the interdisciplinary learning component properly, and your child should be taught by one of them rather than by whoever can reach Al Reem Island by half past five on a Tuesday.

What you should be able to see, week by week, is evidence. A marked task with criterion levels against each strand. A list of which of the eight components has been looked at and which has not. A note of what changed between the first attempt and the third. We also tell you where the line is: a tutor may teach, question, model on a different example and give feedback on the student's own work, and may not write, rewrite or complete any part of an ePortfolio or a Personal Project. That boundary is in the IB's academic-honesty rules, and crossing it puts your child's whole programme at risk.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-eassessment-tutor.programmesIntro: Four programme stages matter to a family at this point: the earlier MYP years where the habits are set, the two years that end in eAssessment, the Diploma that follows for most Abu Dhabi candidates, and the International GCSE route some schools offer instead.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: No external assessment runs in these years, which is exactly why they get neglected. Everything the on-screen papers later reward is built here: reading an unseen source without panicking, writing a paragraph that answers the command term, laying out mathematical working so a marker can follow it. One-to-one hours at this stage are short and diagnostic rather than remedial, and six to eight sessions on a single weakness usually beat a standing weekly slot.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi these are also the years when Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies settle into a weekly pattern alongside the programme. A child who arrived mid-year with no Arabic script is behind on the alphabet before anything else, and that gap is far cheaper to close in Year 7 than in Year 11. Families moving between ADEK-inspected schools often find the MYP subject group names match while the internal assessment calendars do not.

programmes.name: The eAssessment years
programmes.description: These two years produce the eight graded components. MYP 4 is where the ePortfolio record starts accumulating, because a moderator judges the record rather than the last fortnight of it. MYP 5 is where on-screen examination practice has to become routine, including practice using the tools inside the examination rather than on paper beside it. Starting in MYP 4 is not an upsell; it is where the ePortfolio half of the certificate is actually won or lost.
programmes.countryNote: Not every Abu Dhabi school that teaches the programme enters candidates for the certificate, and some enter for selected components only. Ask the MYP coordinator for the entry list in writing. It is a two-minute question that changes what a tutor should be doing for the next eight months, and we have had families discover in February that the component they had been revising was never on the entry.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Most MYP 5 candidates in the emirate continue into the Diploma at the same school. The handoff that causes trouble is mathematics: a candidate who sat the standard on-screen paper and then selects Analysis and Approaches is taking on algebraic fluency that the standard route never demanded. Sciences behave similarly, where the MYP integrated science paper covers less discipline-specific depth than a DP Chemistry or Physics course assumes in its first term.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi DP cohorts sit the May session, and the schools build internal coursework deadlines backwards from it. For a family deciding in MYP 5, the useful question to the school is not whether your child can enter the Diploma but which subjects at which level, and what evidence from the MYP components the school uses to decide. Ask for that rule before results, not after.

programmes.name: International GCSE, the alternative route at 14 to 16
programmes.description: Several Abu Dhabi schools run Cambridge or Pearson International GCSE across Years 10 and 11 instead of MYP 4 and 5, and a few run both in parallel. The assessment model is almost the opposite: syllabus codes, published past papers, terminal written examinations and tiering decisions, rather than criteria and portfolios. Families moving between the two mid-course need a subject-by-subject map rather than a general reassurance.
programmes.countryNote: The route also has consequences for a Ministry of Education equivalency file later, because that process asks for accredited subjects with grades. The British-track rule published in July 2026 is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus an Advanced Level pass. Verify current requirements on the ministry's own channel before you rely on them.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-eassessment-tutor.subjectsIntro: MYP eAssessment is organised by subject group rather than by subject name, and each group is assessed in one particular form. This grid is the one to put next to your child's entry list, because the form decides what a session can usefully do.

subjects.name: Language and literature
subjects.description: Sat on unseen stimulus material, so content revision helps very little and reading technique helps a great deal. Marks go missing when a candidate summarises a text instead of analysing how it produces an effect, and when the comparison task is answered as two separate descriptions with no point of contact between them.

subjects.name: Individuals and societies
subjects.description: Source handling under time pressure. The published criteria reward using a source as evidence and evaluating its origin and purpose; candidates lose marks by paraphrasing the source back and by answering an evaluate question as a describe question. Practice is about command terms and about structuring an answer before typing it.

subjects.name: Mathematics, standard
subjects.description: Covers the standard content of the framework and is entered as a separate level from extended. Working typed into an answer field is where most marks leak, because a candidate who does the algebra on scrap paper and types only the result has nothing for a method mark to attach to.

subjects.name: Mathematics, extended
subjects.description: Adds the extended framework content and expects multi-step reasoning on unfamiliar problems. It is the right entry for a candidate heading towards Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and the wrong one for a candidate whose algebra still breaks when the unknown appears on both sides of an equation.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Integrated rather than split into three disciplines, and built around data, graphs and experimental scenarios. The recurring loss is in explanation: a candidate names the correct variable but never links cause to effect in a sentence a marker can credit, or reads a gradient without units.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary learning
subjects.description: The component that cannot be revised as a topic. It asks a candidate to bring two disciplines to bear on one unfamiliar problem and to show awareness of what each discipline contributes. Strong single-subject students often score lowest here because they answer from one discipline and stop.

subjects.name: Language acquisition
subjects.description: Arabic, French and Spanish are the common ones in Abu Dhabi schools. Assessed as a portfolio of coursework in the phase the school has entered, which means the task sheet matters as much as the language. A tutor can teach the structure and the register, then give feedback on what the student has written.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Judged on a documented process: investigating, developing specifications, creating and evaluating against those specifications. The product rarely costs the marks. The missing dated process journal entries, the specification that was never tested against, and the evaluation written as an apology are what cost the marks.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Visual arts, music and drama all submit a process record alongside the outcome. Moderators look for development over time rather than a strong finished piece delivered from nowhere, so a journal that starts in October is worth more than a brilliant fortnight in March.

subjects.name: Physical and health education
subjects.description: Includes planning, performance and reflection on a personal programme. Candidates underplay the written strands and over-rely on being good at the sport. The achievable marks sit in the planning and evaluation strands, which are the ones a one-to-one session can genuinely move.

subjects.name: Personal Project
subjects.description: The one component every certificate candidate completes. It carries a supervisor record of meetings, and the report has to show how the goal, the research and the product connect. A tutor may ask questions about the plan and the writing and may not contribute content to either the report or the product.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-eassessment-tutor.regionsTitle: Where in the emirate the MYP 5 families we work with live
abu-dhabi/ib-myp-eassessment-tutor.regionsIntro: Session timing is the practical constraint, not distance, because every lesson is online. What differs by community is when a MYP 5 student is actually home, settled and able to work for sixty uninterrupted minutes.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Apartment living with school runs onto the island and off it twice a day. Families here typically land on a 5.30pm or 6pm start, and the 4pm slot that suits a villa community rarely works. Several MYP households here have siblings on different school buses.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Short runs to the island schools mean an earlier start is realistic, often 4.30pm. The constraint here is activity schedules rather than traffic, with swimming and music filling the early evening on two or three weekdays.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Khalidiyah
regions.note: Central and close to several long-established schools, so the commute is short but the roads are slow between 3pm and 4pm. A 5pm start with a hard stop at 6pm is the pattern that holds through a term here.

regions.name: Khalifa City and Al Raha
regions.note: The corridor where most of the emirate's newer international schools sit. Buses can run forty minutes in each direction, which pushes a weekday session to 5.30pm and makes a Saturday morning block the more reliable option for timed on-screen practice.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: Compact, with short school runs, but weekend traffic onto the island is its own event. Families here often prefer two shorter weekday sessions to one long weekend block, and that suits ePortfolio feedback better than it suits timed papers.

regions.name: Al Shamkha and Al Falah
regions.note: Longer bus routes and larger households. A MYP 5 student here is frequently home after 4.30pm with younger siblings around, so sessions work best after 6pm once the house has settled, or on Friday mornings.

regions.name: Mussafah and Mohammed Bin Zayed City
regions.note: Mixed residential and industrial, with school runs that depend heavily on the route rather than the distance. Parents here most often ask for fortnightly ePortfolio review slots rather than a weekly commitment.

regions.name: Al Reef
regions.note: Villa community near the airport road with a long bus run to the island schools. The practical window is 6pm to 7.30pm on weekdays, and that is long enough for a full on-screen paper under timed conditions once a week.

schoolClusters.city: The island, Saadiyat and Al Bateen
schoolClusters.note: The older and more central cluster, where the schools we see most often in MYP 5 enquiries sit. Programme offerings differ school by school and change over time, so check the school's own prospectus and the regulator's listing rather than assuming a continuum.
schools: American Community School of Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City, Al Raha and Yas
schoolClusters.note: The corridor with the heaviest concentration of newer international schools and the longest bus runs. Students we support here are the ones most likely to need a 5.30pm or later start during term.

schoolClusters.city: The mainland and southern communities
schoolClusters.note: Al Shamkha, Al Falah, Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Al Reef. Fewer programme schools and longer journeys, which is the clearest case for online delivery rather than a search for someone local.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-eassessment-tutor.schoolDisclaimer: Schools are named here as context for the education ecosystem families ask us about; no affiliation, partnership or endorsement is implied, and programme details should be confirmed with each school and with ADEK.
abu-dhabi/ib-myp-eassessment-tutor.modesIntro: Three formats cover almost every MYP 5 enquiry we take from the emirate. The one that fits depends on which half of the certificate you are worried about, and on how many weeks are left before the school's internal deadlines bite.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one on a named component
modes.description: Sixty minutes a week against one component, with a marked task returned between sessions. This is the format for an on-screen examination subject, because the skill being built is timed performance under the examination's own tools and that needs repetition rather than explanation.
bullets: One component per block, named in writing before the first lesson
A timed task set every second week and returned marked
Criterion levels recorded so movement is visible rather than asserted
Progress reviewed against the evidence at six weeks, not at the end

modes.title: Fortnightly ePortfolio feedback
modes.description: A review slot for language acquisition, design, arts or physical and health education work. The student brings the task sheet, the teacher's criterion comments and their own draft. The tutor questions, models the structure on a different example and gives feedback. Nothing is written, rewritten or supplied by the tutor.
bullets: Task sheet and teacher comments read before the session, not during it
Process journal checked for dated entries rather than polish
Feedback given against the criterion strands the school is using
A written note of what the student will change, in the student's own words

modes.title: Pre-session intensive block
modes.description: A short, dense run of sessions in the weeks before the on-screen session, usually two a week. Suited to a candidate who knows the content but has never sat the papers under proper conditions, including with the on-screen tools, a running clock and no scrap-paper habit to fall back on.
bullets: Full papers sat under timed conditions in the examination interface
One session to sit it, one to mark it against published criteria
Typing and on-screen working audited in the first week, not the last
A stop rule agreed in advance so revision does not run into the session itself

sections.heading: What the search usually means, and the one question that answers it
paragraphs: An IB MYP eassessment tutor in Abu Dhabi is someone who can prepare a MYP 5 candidate for the specific component they are entered for, in the form it is assessed in, and who can show you marked work as proof it is working. That is the whole definition, and it is narrower than it sounds. A general maths tutor can teach the content of the standard mathematics framework. Rather fewer can tell you what a method mark looks like when the working has to be typed into a browser rather than written on paper.

So the first question is not about tutoring at all. Ask the school's MYP coordinator for the entry list in writing: which components your child is entered for, which level for mathematics, and which phase for language acquisition. Three lines of email. Everything a tutor plans afterwards depends on it, and the number of families who discover in February that they had been preparing for something not on the entry is higher than it should be.

The second question is about form. On-screen components are externally marked against published criteria, and the preparation is timed practice plus technique. ePortfolio components are teacher-marked and externally moderated, and the preparation is a record built over months. If someone quotes you a package of ten sessions before asking which of those two you need, they are selling hours rather than diagnosing a problem.

What we do first is free, which keeps this honest. One trial lesson, one real task your child has already attempted, marked in front of you against the criteria the school is using. You will learn more about whether a tutor is any good from watching that than from any amount of description, and you will learn whether the problem is content, technique or simply that nobody has told your child what the marker is looking for.
bullets: Get the entry list in writing from the MYP coordinator before booking anything
Separate on-screen components from ePortfolio components on the same page
Mathematics has a level decision attached to the entry; ask which one was submitted
Judge a tutor on one marked task, not on a plan

sections.heading: The eight components, and the evidence each one leaves behind
paragraphs: The certificate is built from eight graded components, and they are not graded in the same way. Five are sat as on-screen examinations and marked externally by the IB against published criteria. The rest are ePortfolios, assembled by the student across the year, marked by the teacher and then moderated externally. The Personal Project sits with the second group and carries a supervisor record of meetings alongside the report and the product.

This matters because each form leaves a different trail, and the trail is what a parent can actually inspect. For an on-screen component you should be able to see a marked practice script with criterion levels against each task. For an ePortfolio you should be able to see the task sheet, the dated process entries and the teacher's criterion comments. If a tutor cannot produce either after a month, there is nothing to review and no basis for deciding whether to continue.

The table below is the one to print and keep next to the entry list. It is also the one that settles most arguments about what a tutor should be doing. A family worried about design does not need revision sessions; they need the process journal to have dated entries in it from October rather than a sprint in March. A family worried about individuals and societies does not need more content; they need source-evaluation answers marked against the criteria until the shape is automatic.

Confirm the detail of your child's entry with the school. Component availability, levels and phases are set by the IB and chosen by the school, they do change, and this page is not a substitute for the coordinator's own list.

sections.heading: On screen is a different skill: the tools inside the examination
paragraphs: A candidate who has spent five years writing by hand and then sits a two-hour paper in a browser is being asked to do two things at once. The content is familiar. The medium is not. Candidates read long stimulus material by scrolling rather than by flicking back, they type extended answers at whatever speed they type, they enter mathematical working through an interface rather than writing it, and they cannot annotate a page in the margin the way they have always done.

None of that is hard to fix, and almost nobody practises it. The fix is to do MYP on-screen examination practice in the actual medium from the start. That means typing full answers rather than planning them aloud. It means entering algebra through the tools provided until it stops being slow. It means reading a source on a screen and learning a method for holding its structure in mind without a highlighter, because the highlighter is not there. Two or three sessions spent on the medium alone usually buy back more marks than the same hours spent on content, especially for a strong candidate whose only real problem is that the clock beats them.

The second habit worth auditing early is scrap paper. In mathematics, a candidate who works a problem out beside the machine and types only the final answer has nothing for a method mark to attach to. We check that in the first week rather than the last, because it is a habit, and habits take a month to shift. Typing speed is worth measuring once too: not to worry a child, but to tell you whether the issue in a long answer is thinking time or keyboard time. Those two have opposite remedies.

The last piece is nerves about the machine itself. Knowing what the interface looks like, where the time shows, how to move between tasks and what happens if the connection drops is worth a quiet session of its own. Your child's school will run through the mechanics, and a tutor who has watched candidates do it before can tell you which parts of the mechanics actually eat time.

sections.heading: Standard or extended mathematics on screen, and what the choice costs later
paragraphs: Mathematics is the one on-screen component entered at a level, and the entry is submitted months before the paper. Standard covers the standard framework content. Extended mathematics on screen adds the extended content and asks for multi-step reasoning on problems a candidate has not seen before. The decision is usually taken by the school on the strength of MYP 4 performance, and parents are often told the outcome rather than consulted on it.

The honest test is not confidence, it is algebra. A candidate whose rearranging holds when the unknown appears on both sides, who can work with indices without reaching for a rule sheet, and who can read a problem and decide which tool it needs, belongs on extended. A candidate who still loses the thread in a two-step equation after a full year of teaching does not, and putting them there buys a lower grade on a harder paper rather than a higher ceiling.

What makes this a Diploma decision taken a year early is the handoff. A candidate heading for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level in DP1 at an Abu Dhabi school is going to meet algebraic fluency assumptions in the first term that the standard route never demanded. Applications and Interpretation is more forgiving on that front and less forgiving on modelling and technology use. Neither is a soft option, and the school's DP coordinator is the right person to tell you what evidence they use to place students.

If the level on the entry looks wrong to you, raise it early and raise it with evidence from a marked script rather than a general sense that your child is better than the grade. Entries are an administrative process with their own cut-offs, and a reasoned case in October is a different conversation from an appeal in March.
bullets: Algebraic fluency is the signal, not confidence or effort
Extended suits a candidate heading towards Higher Level Analysis and Approaches
Ask the DP coordinator what evidence they use to place students into maths routes
Challenge a level with a marked script, early, not with an opinion, late

sections.heading: Interdisciplinary learning: the component strong candidates underestimate
paragraphs: The interdisciplinary learning component is the one that reliably catches good students. It gives an unfamiliar problem and expects the candidate to bring two disciplines to it, to use each one for what it is actually good for, and to say something about what the combination produced that neither discipline would have produced alone. There is no topic list to revise. A student who has spent five years being excellent at one subject will often answer entirely from that subject and score in the middle.

Preparation for it looks nothing like preparation for a subject paper. It is practice at a move rather than at content: read the problem, name two disciplines that have purchase on it, state what each contributes, then integrate rather than alternate. Most weak answers alternate. They give a paragraph of science, a paragraph of history and no sentence anywhere that puts the two in contact with each other. The criteria reward the contact.

This is also the component where a tutor's own breadth shows. Someone who has only ever taught mathematics will struggle to model the move convincingly, which is why we match this component separately rather than bundling it with a subject. Expect two or three worked examples from different pairings before your child tries one alone, and expect the first solo attempt to be mediocre. That is normal and it is the point of doing it in October rather than April.

One practical note for Abu Dhabi families: this component rewards students who notice their own surroundings. Water, energy, construction, heritage conservation and public health all sit visibly in the emirate and all genuinely need two disciplines to discuss. A candidate who can reach for a local example speaks about the problem rather than reciting a textbook pairing, and markers can tell the difference.

sections.heading: Reading a grade from 1 to 7 as a plan rather than a verdict
paragraphs: Every MYP component is reported on a scale of 1 to 7, which looks reassuringly like the Diploma scale and behaves differently. The number comes from criterion levels, and two candidates with the same digit can have completely different profiles underneath it. A 4 built from even levels across four criteria is a different problem from a 4 built from a strong level in one criterion and a weak level in another. The first needs general consolidation. The second needs one strand fixed, which is usually faster and cheaper work.

So ask for the strand levels, not the grade. Most Abu Dhabi schools will give them if you ask the subject teacher directly, and some publish them in the reporting portal already. Once you have them, the planning question becomes specific: which criterion is costing the most, is it a knowledge problem or a communication problem, and what would a better answer on that strand actually look like? That is a question a tutor can answer in one session with a marked script in front of them.

Be careful with the arithmetic of the certificate itself. The IB publishes the rules for how component grades combine into the award, including a minimum total and minimum per-component requirements, and schools interpret the implications for their own progression decisions. Ask your coordinator what the current rules are and what your school does if a candidate falls short. We will not print a threshold here that we cannot cite from the IB, and you should be wary of any page that does.

What movement is realistic? Enough to be worth doing, and less than the internet implies. A criterion strand that is weak because nobody has explained the expectation can move quickly. A strand that is weak because the underlying content was never learned moves at the speed of learning that content. A tutor who promises a specific number of grades in a specific number of weeks is guessing, and a grade guarantee is not something any honest provider sells.
bullets: Ask for criterion strand levels, not just the reported 1 to 7
An uneven profile is usually faster to fix than a flat weak one
Get the certificate rules and your school's progression policy from the coordinator in writing
Treat any promised grade jump as a reason for scepticism rather than reassurance

sections.heading: What MYP-level one-to-one costs in the Abu Dhabi market
paragraphs: Three of the six provider pages that rank for this kind of search publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, which is not the currency any family here transacts in. So here are the published market figures in dirhams, with the source attached to each band. These are market rates, not an IB Gram price list: we quote after the free trial lesson, once we know which component and which form you actually need, because an hour of ePortfolio feedback and an hour of timed on-screen practice are not the same product.

Read the table by model rather than by number. A university-student tutor at the bottom of the range may be perfectly good at explaining standard framework content and will know nothing about how an on-screen script is marked. A premium examiner-badged rate at the top buys a claim that is hard for a parent to verify, and we do not describe anyone as a current examiner because we cannot evidence that status for individuals. The middle of the market is where component-specific experience usually sits.

Watch the exclusions column more closely than the rate. The cost that surprises families is not the hourly figure, it is what the hour does not include: marked work returned between sessions, written feedback a parent can read, a replacement if the match is wrong, or availability at the hour your child is actually home. An AED 150 hour with no marked work attached is more expensive than an AED 250 hour that comes with a script, because the first one leaves you with nothing to inspect.

On value in context: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for 2026-27, and Abu Dhabi fee decisions sit with ADEK rather than with KHDA. Either way, tutoring is a discretionary add-on to a fee you are already paying, and the sensible way to size it is by component and by weeks remaining, not by buying the largest package available.

sections.heading: ADEK, the permit, and whether the person teaching your child is allowed to
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories are wider than most parents expect: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no figure appears on this page.

In Abu Dhabi there is a second rule that matters to families directly. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. This is press-reported rather than quoted from the policy document here, so verify it against the current ADEK publication. The practical effect is clear enough: your child's own MYP teacher is not the route, however appealing it sounds.

ADEK itself supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, publishes inspection outcomes, and is the body to consult about a school rather than about a tutor. A tutoring business with premises and staff is a different legal animal again, needing an educational services permit from the emirate's education authority. IB Gram holds no regulator permit of that kind, operates no office or centre in the UAE, and does not describe itself or its tutors as approved by any authority or examination board. Anyone who tells you otherwise about themselves has given you a reason to check.

The application route for an individual permit is MoHRE's own service, applied for through the ministry's app, website and e-services system, with no fee listed. That is the link worth keeping. For a parent, the checkable version of all this is short: ask to see the permit, ask which school the person teaches at, and ask who verified them.
