abu-dhabi/ib-myp-online-tutor.programmesIntro: Price tracks programme more than it tracks subject, because the specialisation required and the size of the available tutor pool both change at each transition. The four rows below are the ones that matter for budgeting in an Abu Dhabi household.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: No external examination, progress evidenced through portfolios, observation and whatever standardised measures a school runs. Sessions are short and the skills being built are reading fluency, number facts and written structure. The widest tutor pool of any programme, which is reflected in price.
programmes.countryNote: Primary support is the cheapest hour available in Abu Dhabi and also the one with the highest variance in quality, because a wide pool means little filtering. Buying the budget band here is defensible in a way it is not higher up, provided somebody is checking that reading and number work is actually progressing.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, four published criteria per subject, each scored 0-8 by best fit against descriptors. Assessment is task-based rather than examination-based until the final year, where some schools add on-screen eAssessment or ePortfolios alongside the Personal Project.
programmes.countryNote: The middle of the price range in Abu Dhabi and the band with the sharpest internal spread. MYP Mathematics draws a wide pool and prices near the qualified-teacher band; Design, a specific Language Acquisition phase, or Personal Project supervision support draw a narrow one and price closer to specialist rates.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects with three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. External papers plus an internally marked, externally moderated component in each subject, against published criteria and boundaries.
programmes.countryNote: The most expensive band, and the gap is real rather than a mark-up. A Higher Level subject with a moderated internal assessment needs a tutor who has taught that exact course through a final session, and in Abu Dhabi the pool for several Higher Level subjects is thin enough that scarcity alone sets the price.

programmes.name: IGCSE after MYP 3
programmes.description: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel courses that several Abu Dhabi schools run in place of MYP 4 and 5. Externally examined with syllabus codes, tiering decisions and published series dates, which makes preparation more standardised and the tutor pool larger.
programmes.countryNote: Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 against IB from AED 200, and that gap is a reasonable guide to the difference across the market. If your Abu Dhabi school moves students into IGCSE in Year 10, budget on the lower band from that point and on more predictable session counts.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: Within the Middle Years Programme the price differences are driven by how many tutors genuinely cover a subject group at the year you need. The notes below say where each one sits and why.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: The widest pool in the programme and therefore the most competitive rate. Plenty of tutors can teach the content; far fewer work in criterion terms, and investigating patterns and communicating are where levels are lost. Pay for the second kind, which still sits inside the qualified-teacher band.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: A wide pool for content and a narrow one for the investigation criteria, which is where the marks sit. Expect the qualified-teacher band for general support and the upper part of it for somebody who has actually marked inquiring and designing against the descriptors.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Mid-band and plentiful, with the caveat that general English tutors are not the same as MYP Language and Literature tutors. Analysing is assessed as comment on how a text works, not as summary, and that distinction is what you are paying for.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: The least predictable price in the programme, because the pool depends on the language and the phase. French and Spanish at lower phases are straightforward; a less common language at a higher phase is a scarcity purchase and will be quoted accordingly, if it can be quoted at all.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Mid-band. The useful spend here is on thinking critically and investigating, which is essay structure and research process rather than content. A tutor from a history or geography background covers it; one from a general humanities background may not know the criteria.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Surprisingly scarce and therefore priced above what families expect from a subject they think of as practical. The assessed work is the design folder, so you are buying documentation coaching, and few tutors in this market have marked it.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Narrow pool, and most of the usable work is on the process journal rather than the practical piece. Worth buying as a short block before a unit deadline rather than as a weekly commitment, which keeps the cost proportionate to what can actually be changed.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Rarely tutored and rarely needed, with one exception: the written planning and reflection criteria, where capable athletes lose levels. A short block of two or three sessions is almost always the right purchase here rather than anything ongoing.

subjects.name: Arabic and the federally required subjects
subjects.description: Priced separately from the MYP language subjects and quoted according to the stream. Confirm which stream your child is registered in before asking for a rate, because booking the wrong one buys teaching against material your child is not assessed on.

subjects.name: Personal Project support
subjects.description: The narrowest pool and the highest band inside the MYP, because the work is supervision-adjacent and the honesty boundary is strict. Usually bought as a short block of three or four sessions around scope and journal habits rather than as a weekly arrangement.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-online-tutor.regionsTitle: What changes the number by community in Abu Dhabi
abu-dhabi/ib-myp-online-tutor.regionsIntro: Location does not change an online rate directly, and it changes several things that feed into it: which schools a community feeds, which subject groups come up, and what time of day a session has to happen. The notes below are about the cost consequences rather than the academics.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: The highest MYP volume in the emirate and the most competitive quotes, because tutors who teach these subject groups are already working in this corridor. The cost pressure here is the evening slot: a 17:30 start is in demand and the earliest slots get taken first.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: MYP 5 and Personal Project enquiries dominate, which sits in the narrowest and dearest part of the Middle Years market. A short block of three or four sessions is the proportionate purchase, not a weekly commitment through the year.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Frequent mid-year arrivals, which means diagnostic sessions rather than long programmes. Budget for two or three sessions to establish which criteria the new school is actually marking before committing to a term.

regions.name: Al Raha Beach and Al Raha Gardens
regions.note: Households with children in two programmes at once, so the real budgeting question is allocation between an MYP child and a Diploma one. The Diploma hour costs more and the MYP hour buys a longer-lasting habit.

regions.name: Al Shamkha and Al Falah
regions.note: Larger families and tighter budgets, where the fortnightly cycle with set tasks between sessions is usually the best value available. It halves the cost per child while preserving most of the assessment opportunities.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: Younger cohorts and activity-heavy weeks. The weekend morning slot is the one that survives here, and a 45-minute session rather than a full hour keeps both the attention and the cost proportionate for MYP 1 and 2.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City
regions.note: Mixed-curriculum neighbourhood where parents compare MYP tutoring quotes against IGCSE ones and find the IGCSE band lower. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 against IB from AED 200, which explains most of the gap.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Mushrif
regions.note: Bilingual households managing the Arabic stream alongside MYP language subjects, which is effectively two purchases. Sequencing them across terms rather than running both at once is what keeps the total manageable.

schoolClusters.city: Island and Saadiyat IB schools
schoolClusters.note: These schools generate the MYP 4 and 5 enquiries, including Personal Project work, which sits at the upper end of the Middle Years range. Students we support attend schools in this cluster; no affiliation with any of them exists.

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City, Al Raha and mainland schools
schoolClusters.note: A cluster where IB and British-curriculum schools sit side by side, so families here are often pricing MYP tutoring against IGCSE tutoring for a child of the same age. The published gap between the two bands is a reasonable guide.

sections.heading: What an MYP hour costs, and why it is not a Diploma hour
paragraphs: An online Middle Years hour in this market sits below an online Diploma hour, and the published rates show the shape of it. Unitors advertises IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB tuition from AED 200, a gap that roughly tracks the difference between externally examined secondary work and the Diploma. Bestimate's 2026 survey puts IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above. At the budget end, Tutopiya publishes from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 for online tutoring generally, without distinguishing programme. All figures were read in October 2026.

The reason a Middle Years hour prices lower is supply rather than quality. MYP content in most subject groups is within reach of any competent subject teacher, so the available pool is wide, and a wide pool pushes rates down. A Higher Level Diploma subject with a moderated internal assessment needs somebody who has taught that specific course to a final session, and in several subjects that pool is small enough that scarcity alone sets the number.

Three cases reverse this inside the MYP, and they are where Abu Dhabi families get an unexpected quote. Language Acquisition in a specific language and phase can be scarcer than any Diploma subject. Design is assessed through the folder rather than the artefact, and very few tutors in this market have marked that folder against the criteria. Personal Project support is supervision-adjacent work with a strict honesty boundary and the narrowest pool in the programme. For those three, expect a figure closer to the specialist band and treat a very low quote as a signal that the person has not done the work before.

sections.heading: The five things that move an MYP quote in this emirate
paragraphs: Abu Dhabi has its own cost drivers, and they are not the ones a generic tutoring price guide lists. The first is the subject group rather than the subject: a Mathematics request and a Design request at the same year level sit in different bands because the pools are different sizes, and a parent who assumes a single MYP rate will be surprised by the second quote.

The second is the Arabic requirement. Private schools in the UAE teach Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies alongside their licensed curriculum, and the Arab and non-Arab streams are genuinely different subjects with different material and different languages of instruction. A household needing Arabic support alongside the MYP subjects is making two purchases, not one, and the honest planning move is to sequence them across terms rather than run both at once. The third is the final-year assessment model: where a school enters students for on-screen MYP eAssessment or ePortfolios, final-year support becomes more specialised and prices accordingly, so establish with the coordinator whether your school does.

The fourth is timing within the term. Abu Dhabi schools cluster their assessment, and demand for tutors rises sharply in the weeks before a reporting round, which is also the point at which the least progress can be bought. The fifth is the evening slot. Nothing about an online rate depends on distance, but the early-evening slots that a mainland household can actually use are finite, and they fill first. Booking in August for an October start costs nothing and secures the slot that makes the whole arrangement survivable.

sections.heading: Cost per criterion level, which is the only unit that matters
paragraphs: AED per hour is the wrong unit for the Middle Years Programme, and it is why parents feel they cannot tell whether tutoring is good value. The programme is marked in criterion levels: four criteria per subject, each from 0 to 8, awarded by best fit against published descriptors. A level changes when the school next marks a task assessing that criterion, which in some subject groups happens twice a term. So the hard ceiling on progress is the assessment calendar, not the number of hours a family buys.

Reframed properly, the question becomes how much it costs to shift one named criterion, and the answer is usually fewer sessions than parents expect for process criteria and more than they expect for content ones. Communicating in Mathematics, which marks whether reasoning is presented so a reader can follow it, is often two or three sessions of habit work. Inquiring and designing in Sciences, which requires a documented investigation process, is a term. Knowing and understanding, where the gap is content, depends entirely on how much content is missing and is the only one where more hours genuinely buy more progress.

The practical use of this framing is that it stops a household buying hours against the wrong target. A student sitting at 7 on knowing and understanding and 3 on investigating does not need more teaching; they need a process habit, and three sessions plus consistent task practice will do more than a term of content revision costing five times as much. Ask any tutor to name the target criterion and estimate the sessions before you agree a rate. The estimate is the useful number.

sections.heading: Five years of the MYP, costed as a whole
paragraphs: Middle Years support is usually bought as a reaction to one report, and priced one term at a time. Looked at across the five years the programme runs, the arithmetic changes the decision. A household that buys one weekly session for the whole of MYP 1 to 5 is making a very large commitment; one that buys a short targeted block in three of those five years is making a modest one, and in most cases it buys more.

Bestimate's published monthly estimates give a usable frame for the sums: AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end for a weekly one-hour session, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work. A school year of roughly nine teaching months at the mid-market estimate is therefore a five-figure annual commitment per subject. Across five MYP years, continuously, that is a sum most families would want to see justified against a specific target rather than against a general sense of support.

The alternative pattern that works is targeted and cheaper. Three or four sessions in MYP 1 or 2 to establish habits and written structure, while they are cheap to change. Nothing in MYP 3 unless a specific criterion stalls. A term in MYP 4 on the process criteria that the next programme will rely on. A short block in MYP 5 on the Personal Project and the route decision. That shape costs a fraction of continuous tutoring and front-loads the spend where the habit returns compound, which is the genuine argument for acting early rather than a sales line about getting ahead.

sections.heading: The costs around the tuition that nobody quotes you
paragraphs: The hourly rate is rarely the whole number. Several real costs attach to Middle Years support in Abu Dhabi, and none of them appears in a tutoring quote. The first is equipment, and it is small but genuinely necessary: headphones with a microphone rather than laptop speakers, and for mathematics a second device or a phone propped over the page so the tutor can see written working. A tutor who cannot see the working cannot diagnose anything, which turns a paid hour into a conversation.

The second is school-side charges in the final year. Where a school enters students for on-screen MYP eAssessment or ePortfolio submission, there may be an entry charge, and the amount is set by the school rather than published centrally. Ask the coordinator what the entry arrangements and costs are for your child's subjects rather than assuming. The same applies to any resource the school requires for the Personal Project, which varies enormously with what the student chooses to do.

The third is the cost of the wrong purchase, which is the largest hidden number in this market. A term of content revision bought for a student whose problem is a process criterion produces no report movement and roughly a five-figure sense of grievance. A tutor booked for the wrong Arabic stream teaches material the child is not assessed on. A weekly commitment bought for a subject the school assesses twice a term spends most of its hours in the gaps between assessments. Each of those is avoidable with one diagnostic session, which is the cheapest hour on this page.
bullets: Headphones with a microphone, and a second camera view for mathematics

sections.heading: Where online delivery actually changes the number
paragraphs: Comparing an online quote with a visiting quote on the hourly rate alone misses most of the difference, because the two have different cost structures rather than different prices for the same thing. Travel is the obvious element: a visiting tutor's week is built around journeys, and whether or not the drive is itemised, it is paid for in the rate and in the inflexibility of the slot. Published figures bear this out, with in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and home tutors at AED 200 to 500 in Bestimate's 2026 survey against online rates starting far lower.

Three less obvious elements matter more for a Middle Years budget. Minimum session length is one: a 45-minute online session is a normal unit and for an MYP 1 or 2 student it is the right one, whereas almost nobody drives across Abu Dhabi for 45 minutes. Cancellation loss is another: a child home ill loses a session either way, but a visiting arrangement loses the tutor's travel time too and the policy reflects that. The third is the fortnightly option, which only really works online, because marked work can move between tutor and student without anybody travelling.

The element that does not change is the one families assume will. Online delivery does not reduce what a scarce specialist charges. A tutor who has marked MYP Design folders or teaches a rare Language Acquisition phase is scarce in absolute terms, and removing the drive does not add anybody to that pool. What online delivery does is give an Abu Dhabi household access to that person at all, which for several subject groups in this programme is the difference between a specialist and whoever was available nearby.

sections.heading: Buying the cheap hour: when it is sensible and when it is waste
paragraphs: The budget band is real and it has a legitimate use. Tutopiya publishes online tutoring from AED 33 to 52 per hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, and at those rates a household can buy regular supervised homework time for a younger Middle Years student. For an MYP 1 or 2 child whose problem is starting work rather than understanding it, a reliable adult presence four times a week at the budget rate may do more than a single specialist hour costing the same in total.

Where the cheap hour is wasted is any criterion that is marked against descriptors the tutor has never read. A budget tutor can teach content accurately and still produce no change in a report, because the levels being lost are in investigating, communicating or reflecting, and those require somebody who knows what the descriptor band above actually asks for. Paying a low rate for work against a process criterion is not a slower route to the same place; it is usually no route at all.

The test is simple enough to apply before booking. Ask the tutor which criterion they would target and what the band above requires. A tutor at any price point who answers in terms of topics and revision is being honest about what they do, and that is fine for homework supervision. A tutor who answers in terms of a named criterion and a descriptor strand is doing the other job. Buy the first cheaply and the second properly, and do not expect the first to deliver the second at any number of hours.

sections.heading: VAT, invoices and what to settle before the first payment
paragraphs: Before any money moves, three things are worth having in writing, and none of them is controversial enough to cause friction with a reasonable provider. The first is what the rate covers: session length, whether marking between sessions is included, who sets the between-session task, and what written record you receive. A quote of AED 250 an hour that includes marked work between sessions is a different purchase from the same number for contact time only.

The second is tax treatment, stated as a question rather than an assumption. Ask whether the quoted rate includes value added tax and whether the provider holds a tax registration number. This page does not state how UAE VAT applies to tuition fees, because that treatment is set by the Federal Tax Authority and should be read from its own guidance rather than from a tutoring website. What a parent needs is simply to know whether the number they were quoted is the number they will pay.

The third is the cancellation, pause and replacement position. What notice is required, what happens if a child is ill, whether a block can be paused over a school holiday or during Ramadan, and what happens if the match is wrong after two sessions. Ask also whether the tutor holds the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, and whether they teach at your child's school, since ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid tutoring of their own enrolled students. Those two questions cost nothing to ask and are the ones most families never think of.
bullets: Confirm what the rate includes: marking, tasks, notes, session length
Ask whether the quoted figure includes VAT and whether a TRN is held

Ask about the MoHRE permit and about your child's own school

sections.heading: If you only have one term's budget, spend it here
paragraphs: A household with one term of tutoring money and a child somewhere in the Middle Years Programme has a genuine allocation problem, and the default answer, the weakest subject, is usually wrong. The weakest subject on a report is often weak for a content reason that will be retaught anyway. The expensive problem is a process criterion sitting at 3 or 4 across several subjects at once, because that pattern will follow the student into the next programme and get more expensive every year.

The order that produces most value from a single term is this. Start with one diagnostic session that reads the report and the last two marked tasks and names the criterion pattern. Then spend the bulk of the term on one process criterion in one subject, with marked work between sessions, because process habits transfer across subjects in a way content does not. Reserve two sessions at the end for the written review, which is what you take into the school consultation.

What not to do with a single term's budget is spread it across three subjects, buy the final weeks before a report, or put it on the subject the child dislikes most. Thin coverage produces no marked evidence in any subject. The final weeks before a report arrive after the assessments that set it. And a disliked subject usually needs a conversation with the school rather than a tutor. Each of those is an easy mistake because each feels responsible, which is exactly why it is worth writing the allocation down before the first session rather than after the third.

process.title: Say what you want to change, not which subject
process.description: Send the report, the last two marked tasks and their clarifications. A tutor who reads them can name the criterion that is costing levels, which is what makes an estimate meaningful. A subject name on its own produces a generic rate and a generic plan.

process.title: Ask for an estimate in sessions, then in AED
process.description: Any competent tutor can say roughly how many sessions a named criterion needs: two or three for a habit, a term for a documented investigation process. Multiply that out yourself. A rate without a session estimate is a number you cannot evaluate.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One lesson at no charge, no card required. It should end with a target criterion, a reason and an honest session estimate. If it ends with enthusiasm and no diagnosis, you have learnt something useful about the tutor at no cost.

process.title: Settle the terms in writing
process.description: Session length, whether marking between sessions is included, notice and pause policy, what happens if the match is wrong, whether the quoted figure includes VAT, and whether the tutor holds the MoHRE private tuition permit. Five minutes, before any payment.

process.title: Review on the evidence at week eight
process.description: Read the session notes, the tutor-marked tasks and the first school-marked task on the target criterion. Continue, change target, change tutor or stop. Buying another term because the sessions felt productive is how a modest budget becomes a large one.

whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here names the provider who published it or the survey it came from, with October 2026 as the read month. Three of the best-ranked pages in this market publish no price at all and two quote in dollars.

whyPoints.description: The bands on this page are what other providers advertise. What IB Gram charges comes out of a consultation after the free trial, because the honest figure depends on subject group, year, frequency and whether marked work between sessions is included.

whyPoints.title: Priced against the criterion, not the hour
whyPoints.description: Tutors give a session estimate for a named criterion before a rate is agreed, because the assessment calendar caps how fast a level can move. That makes the spend evaluable rather than open-ended.

whyPoints.title: Cheaper units genuinely available
whyPoints.description: Forty-five-minute sessions for younger Middle Years students, and a fortnightly cycle with marked work in between for households running two children on one budget. Both are hard to buy from a visiting tutor and straightforward online.

whyPoints.title: Honest about where a low rate works
whyPoints.description: The budget band is useful for homework supervision at MYP 1 and 2 and ineffective against a process criterion, and we say which is which. Paying a low rate for descriptor-level work is usually no route to the result rather than a slower one.

whyPoints.title: No claimed approvals and no UAE office
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education or the IB, occupies no UAE premises, and publishes no statistic it cannot evidence. Regulators are explained here only where they affect your decision.

faqs.question: What does an online MYP tutor charge per hour in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Published market rates, read in October 2026, run from AED 33 to 65 at the budget end, where Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. In the qualified-teacher band Unitors publishes IB tuition from AED 200 and IGCSE from AED 150, and TutorChase quotes around AED 270. Bestimate's 2026 survey puts specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above. Common MYP subjects usually sit between AED 150 and 300; Design, Arts, scarce language phases and Personal Project work sit higher because the pool is far smaller.

faqs.question: Why is Middle Years tutoring cheaper than Diploma tutoring?
faqs.answer: Supply, not quality. Most MYP content is within reach of any competent subject teacher, so the pool is wide and rates fall. A Higher Level Diploma subject with an externally moderated internal assessment needs somebody who has taught that exact course through to a final session, and for several subjects that pool is small enough that scarcity sets the price. The published gap is visible in Unitors' own rates, IGCSE from AED 150 against IB from AED 200. Three MYP areas reverse the logic: Design, scarce Language Acquisition phases and Personal Project support.

faqs.question: Is a tutor at AED 50 an hour ever a sensible purchase?
faqs.answer: Yes, for one specific job. For an MYP 1 or 2 student whose problem is starting work rather than understanding it, regular supervised homework time at the budget rate can do more than one specialist hour costing the same in total. Where it fails is any criterion marked against descriptors the tutor has never read. A budget tutor can teach content accurately and produce no report movement, because the lost levels sit in investigating, communicating or reflecting. Ask which criterion they would target; the answer tells you which job they are doing.

faqs.question: How many sessions does it take to move one criterion level?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on which criterion. Communicating in Mathematics, which marks whether reasoning is written out so a reader can follow it, is often two or three sessions of habit work. Analysing in Language and Literature is usually four to six. Inquiring and designing in Sciences is a term, because it needs a documented process and is only assessed when a formal investigation is set. Knowing and understanding depends on how much content is missing and is the only target where more hours reliably buy more progress. Ask for the estimate before agreeing a rate.

faqs.question: Does a monthly package work out cheaper than paying by the hour?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the comparison is only fair if both quotes describe the same thing. Packages seen in this market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end and AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market. Before comparing, establish session length, whether marking between sessions is included, what happens to unused sessions, and the notice period. Those four answers usually matter more than the headline figure.

faqs.question: Do quoted tutoring rates in the UAE include VAT?
faqs.answer: Ask, every time, and get the answer in writing. This page does not state how UAE value added tax applies to tuition, because that treatment is set by the Federal Tax Authority and should be read from its own guidance rather than from a tutoring website. What you need as a parent is narrower: whether the figure you were quoted is the figure you will pay, and whether the provider holds a tax registration number. A provider who cannot answer either question clearly is telling you something about their invoicing generally.

faqs.question: Is it better value to start tutoring in MYP 2 or wait until MYP 5?
faqs.answer: Earlier is cheaper for process habits and later is cheaper for content. A process criterion sitting at 3 or 4 in MYP 2 is a habit, and three or four sessions can change it while it is still cheap. The same gap discovered in the second Diploma year costs several times as much, because the stakes are higher and the pool is dearer. Content gaps are different: much of what is weak in MYP 2 gets retaught anyway. The targeted pattern that works is short blocks in MYP 1 or 2, a term in MYP 4, and a project block in MYP 5.

faqs.question: Can we book 45-minute sessions instead of a full hour?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for MYP 1 and 2 students it is usually the better unit as well as the cheaper one. Attention at eleven or twelve does not reliably hold for sixty minutes after a long school run, and a session that ends while the student is still engaged produces more than one that ends when they have stopped. Forty-five minutes is a normal online unit; it is rarely available from a visiting tutor, because almost nobody drives across Abu Dhabi for three quarters of an hour.

faqs.question: Does my child need a separate tutor for each MYP subject?
faqs.answer: Usually not, and the reason is about criteria rather than about subjects. If the pattern on the report is a process criterion sitting low across several subjects, one tutor working on that habit in one subject will produce change in the others, because the habit transfers. Separate tutors make sense where two genuinely different content gaps exist, or where one subject group is specialised enough to need its own person, such as Design or a particular Language Acquisition phase. Spreading one budget across three subjects usually produces no marked evidence in any of them.

faqs.question: What does Personal Project support cost, and is it worth buying?
faqs.answer: It sits at the upper end of the Middle Years range, in Bestimate's specialist band of AED 200 to 450 and above, because the pool of tutors who have worked within the project's honesty boundary is small. It is worth buying as a short block of three or four sessions rather than as a weekly arrangement. Most stalled projects fail on scope rather than effort, and questioning a goal until the student narrows it themselves usually unblocks it in one session. No tutor may contribute any part of the work itself.

faqs.question: Are there extra costs for MYP eAssessment in the final year?
faqs.answer: Possibly, and the figure is set by your school rather than published centrally, so ask the MYP coordinator directly. Not every school enters students for on-screen eAssessment or ePortfolio submission, and the subjects entered vary, which means the first thing to establish is whether yours does and in which subjects. It matters for budgeting in two ways: any entry charge the school passes on, and the fact that final-year support for an assessed subject draws on a narrower and dearer pool of tutors than general MYP work.

faqs.question: Why would a Language Acquisition tutor cost more than a Mathematics one?
faqs.answer: Because the pool is smaller and the match is narrower. MYP Mathematics is taught by a very wide set of tutors, which keeps rates competitive. Language Acquisition is assessed in phases rather than year groups, and a request for a particular language at a particular phase can be scarcer than any Diploma subject. French and Spanish at lower phases are straightforward; a less commonly taught language at a higher phase is a scarcity purchase. A very low quote for one of those is usually a signal that the tutor has not worked in that phase before.

faqs.question: Is group tutoring cheaper for an MYP student?
faqs.answer: Per hour, yes, with centre and group packages advertised in this market from around AED 799 a month. Whether it is better value depends on what you are buying. Group work suits a confident student who wants structure and pace, and it works against the specific problem most Middle Years students have, which is a single criterion that needs individual diagnosis and marked work. A group cannot mark your child's investigation against the descriptors each fortnight. The honest middle option is a fortnightly one-to-one cycle with set work between sessions.

faqs.question: What should I settle in writing before the first payment?
faqs.answer: Five things. What the rate covers, including session length and whether marking between sessions is included. Whether the quoted figure includes VAT and whether a tax registration number is held. The notice, pause and replacement terms, including what happens if the match is wrong after two sessions. Whether the tutor holds the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. And whether they teach at your child's school, since ADEK ethics rules bar that arrangement.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest honest way to support an MYP student in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Ask the school first, because most Abu Dhabi schools already run departmental clinics and catch-up sessions inside the fees you pay. Then buy one diagnostic session to name the criterion pattern on the report. Then spend a single term on one process criterion in one subject, with marked work between sessions, because process habits transfer to the subjects you are not paying for. That sequence costs a fraction of continuous weekly tutoring across five years and, for most students, produces more durable change.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-online-tutor.closingHeading: Get the session estimate before you get the rate
abu-dhabi/ib-myp-online-tutor.closingBody: The AED bands on this page are the market's, published by named providers and read in October 2026, and they exist here because a parent cannot budget against silence. What turns a band into a decision is the session estimate for a named criterion, which any competent tutor can give you after reading a report and two marked tasks. Send those, take the free trial lesson, and ask what the target criterion is and how many sessions it needs. Lessons are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, with no home visits anywhere in the UAE.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-personal-project-help.tutorsIntro: The mentors below have supervised MYP personal projects from goal setting through the process journal to a marked report. Each works from the three criteria and their strands, and each knows the difference between helping a student plan and doing the work for them.

intro.heading: The product is what everyone looks at, and it is not what earns the marks
paragraphs: The MYP personal project is the culminating piece of the Middle Years Programme, completed in the final MYP year, which in most Abu Dhabi schools is Year 11. The student chooses a goal, selects one of the six global contexts to frame it, keeps a process journal as they work, creates a product or outcome, and writes a report. Assessment is against three criteria, each marked out of eight for a total of 24, and the 24 marks convert to a grade from 1 to 7 using published boundaries.

The single most useful thing a parent can know is that the product itself is not assessed. A student who builds a working prototype, films a documentary or organises an event is assessed on how they planned it, how they applied their skills, and how well they reflect on both. We have read reports from this emirate describing genuinely impressive outcomes that scored thirteen out of twenty-four, because the planning was retrospective, the journal was assembled in a weekend, and the reflection described feelings rather than learning.

The second thing to know is that the process journal is evidence, not a diary. It is the raw material the report draws on, and a report that cannot point to dated entries showing decisions, difficulties and changes of direction has nothing to put under criterion A or criterion C. Students who keep the journal badly are not being lazy; they have usually been told to keep a journal without being told what it is for. Ten minutes a week with three specific prompts fixes it entirely.

The third is the goal. Criterion A rewards a goal that is appropriately challenging for this particular student, with criteria for the product specified in advance so success can be judged. Students in Abu Dhabi tend to err in both directions: a goal so ambitious that nothing can be finished, or a goal so safe that it demonstrates no new learning. The fix is a conversation early in the year, before the product is chosen, which is the cheapest intervention in the whole task.

We work one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. The project happens wherever the student makes it, and our sessions are planning and review conversations with the journal and the report on a shared screen. ADEK licenses and inspects the emirate's private schools, and every school runs the project to its own timetable with its own supervisor arrangements, so the school's handbook always takes precedence over anything here. Three sessions across two terms is the shape we recommend to most families here, starting with the free one.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-personal-project-help.programmesIntro: The personal project sits at the end of the MYP, and what comes next changes how a family should think about it. Here is how the programmes relate in this emirate.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The personal project is completed in the final MYP year and is the programme's culminating independent work. It is assessed against three criteria out of eight each, and where a school registers for MYP eAssessment it is externally moderated and required for the MYP certificate. Students work with a supervisor from their school.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi the project usually runs across the first two terms of Year 11, finishing well before the end of the year. That places it alongside the heaviest MYP subject assessment of the whole programme, which is the real source of the pressure families feel.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: For students continuing into the Diploma, the personal project is the closest preparation available for the Extended Essay and for subject internal assessments. The habits it builds, keeping evidence, planning against criteria and reflecting with specifics, are exactly the ones DP1 demands immediately.
programmes.countryNote: Students who kept a usable process journal in Year 11 arrive in DP1 able to draft an Extended Essay research proposal without help. Students who assembled a journal in a weekend arrive having learned the wrong lesson about how coursework works.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP ends with its own exhibition, a collaborative inquiry presented to the school community. It is a different task from the personal project and shares its spirit: a student-directed inquiry with a public outcome.
programmes.countryNote: Families with children in both programmes in one Abu Dhabi school often receive project emails for both in the same term and conflate them. The PYP exhibition is collaborative and unmarked; the personal project is individual and assessed out of 24.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: For students taking a career-related route after the MYP, the personal project is often the first substantial piece of independent, self-directed work they have produced, and it is the piece a sixth form or college admissions conversation can refer to.
programmes.countryNote: CP provision in the emirate is limited, but the point holds for any post-16 route: a well-documented personal project is something a Year 11 student can actually talk about in an interview.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-personal-project-help.subjectsIntro: A personal project is framed by one of six global contexts and built with the approaches to learning skills. These are the territories we plan against, and what each one does to a project.

subjects.name: Identities and relationships
subjects.description: Health, wellbeing, community, belonging. The most chosen context in UAE schools and the easiest in which to produce something vague. A project here needs a specific group of people and a specific question, not a theme about identity.

subjects.name: Orientation in space and time
subjects.description: History, migration, journeys, turning points. Strong for research-led projects and well suited to students in this emirate with family histories across several countries, which gives genuinely original material.

subjects.name: Personal and cultural expression
subjects.description: Art, music, writing, performance, design. The context that most often produces an excellent product and a mediocre report, because the making absorbs all the student's attention and the planning criteria go unserved.

subjects.name: Scientific and technical innovation
subjects.description: Engineering, coding, environmental technology, data. Attracts students who want to build something, and rewards them if they treat the build as a series of documented decisions rather than a weekend of work.

subjects.name: Globalization and sustainability
subjects.description: Resources, interconnection, environmental impact. Abundant local material in the UAE, from water and energy to construction and logistics, and the context in which a student can most easily find a real audience for an outcome.

subjects.name: Fairness and development
subjects.description: Access, equity, opportunity, rights. Serious territory that can produce the strongest projects and needs the most careful handling, particularly where a student proposes to work with a community they are not part of.

subjects.name: The process journal
subjects.description: Not a context but the backbone of the marks. Dated entries recording decisions, obstacles, changes of plan, sources consulted and skills practised. It is the evidence both the planning and reflecting criteria are judged against.

subjects.name: Approaches to learning skills
subjects.description: Research, communication, self-management, thinking and social skills. Criterion B is explicitly about applying these, so a report that names which skills were used, where, and how they developed scores better than one describing activity.

subjects.name: Product criteria and success measures
subjects.description: The student specifies in advance what a successful outcome would look like, in terms specific enough to be judged afterwards. Projects that skip this step cannot reflect properly at the end, because there is no standard to reflect against.

subjects.name: Report format choice
subjects.description: The report may be written or electronic at 1,500 to 3,500 words, or oral or visual at 13 to 15 minutes. The choice should follow the student's strengths and their school's permitted formats, and it changes how the evidence is presented.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-personal-project-help.regionsIntro: Where a family lives in the emirate shapes what a Year 11 student can realistically build, reach or research. These are the areas we work across.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi island and Al Khalidiyah
regions.note: Short distances to institutions, organisations and specialists a student might interview. Island projects often have the strongest primary research simply because an interview is a bus ride rather than an expedition.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: Apartment living limits making and building, so projects here tend towards digital products, writing, film and research. That is no disadvantage: the criteria reward process, not workshop space.

regions.name: Khalifa City and Al Raha
regions.note: Villa households with space to build, and the longest school runs. Sessions start at 5pm or later, and project deadlines across these schools tend to fall in the same weeks of the second term.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Cultural institutions nearby, which makes personal and cultural expression projects unusually well resourced. Students can often arrange a conversation with a practitioner, which is strong criterion B evidence.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: Sport, events and leisure dominate, and many Year 11 students here travel for fixtures. Project planning has to account for that, which is a self-management point the report can legitimately reflect on.

regions.name: Mohammed Bin Zayed City and Shakhbout City
regions.note: Large, mixed communities with strong neighbourhood networks, which gives projects a ready audience and a genuine recipient for an outcome. MoE-mandated subjects sit alongside MYP courses here, so time is tight.

regions.name: Al Shamkha and Al Reef
regions.note: Longer distances to organised provision, so projects built around the immediate community or around digital outcomes work better than ones requiring regular travel.

regions.name: Al Ain

sections.heading: What MYP personal project help in Abu Dhabi involves
paragraphs: It involves three criteria and a journal. Planning, applying skills and reflecting carry eight marks each, and every useful hour of support is traceable to one of them. Nothing we do touches the product, which is the student's own work and is not assessed in any case, and nothing we do replaces the school supervisor, who is the person who knows the school's timetable, format rules and expectations.

The first task in a first session is to find out what stage the student is at and what their school has already issued. Schools in this emirate publish their own project handbooks with internal deadlines, supervisor meeting schedules and permitted report formats, and those documents govern. A student working from general advice found online frequently misses a school-specific requirement, such as a proposal form or a mandatory number of supervisor meetings recorded in the journal.

The second task is the goal, if it is not yet fixed. A good goal for this task is one the student cannot already do, stated precisely enough that a reader knows what finished looks like. Learning to play the guitar is not a goal; performing a specific three-piece set at a specific event, having started from no instrumental experience, is. The precision matters because criterion A asks for a challenging goal and criterion C asks whether it was met.

The third is the journal, which is the task's only source of evidence. We set up three prompts, which take ten minutes a week, and check in the following session that they have been used. Students who adopt the habit need very little further support. Students who do not will reach the report with nothing to cite, and that is the point at which the marks become hard to retrieve.
bullets: Three criteria of eight marks: planning, applying skills, reflecting
The school's own project handbook governs formats, deadlines and meetings
A goal precise enough that both challenge and success can be judged
A ten-minute weekly journal habit, checked in the following session

sections.heading: Twenty-four marks across three criteria
paragraphs: Each criterion is marked out of eight in bands, and each has strands that must all be addressed. Planning covers the goal, the global context and the product criteria. Applying skills covers the use of approaches to learning and of subject-specific knowledge in service of the goal. Reflecting covers the evaluation of the product against the criteria the student set, and reflection on the learning and on their development as a learner.

The pattern in Abu Dhabi reports is consistent. Applying skills usually scores reasonably, because students genuinely do apply skills and describe doing so. Planning scores lower than it should because the plan is written retrospectively and the product criteria were never specified in advance. Reflecting scores lowest because the student evaluates how they felt rather than evaluating the product against a standard.

The practical consequence is that the two criteria most often lost are also the two most fixable at the start and the least fixable at the end. Specifying product criteria takes twenty minutes in week one and cannot be done honestly in week twenty. Reflecting against a standard requires that a standard exists. This is why we push families towards an early session even when nothing appears to be wrong.

The table below is our reading diagnostic, not the official rubric. Read the criterion descriptors in your child's own copy of the school's project handbook or the MYP projects guide their school works from, and treat the supervisor as the authority on how their school applies them. We do not reproduce or supply IB documents or exemplar projects.

A plan written after the fact; criteria too vague to judge against

sections.heading: Choosing the global context on purpose
paragraphs: The global context is a framing decision, and students make it carelessly because it feels like a label rather than a choice. In fact it determines what the project has to engage with and what the report has to justify. Criterion A asks for the context to be identified and the choice explained, so a context picked because it sounded impressive produces a paragraph the student cannot write convincingly.

The useful question is what the context adds. A project to build a water-saving device sits comfortably in globalization and sustainability and could sit in scientific and technical innovation; the first pushes the student towards the resource question and the second towards the engineering. Both are legitimate and they produce different projects, different research and different reflections. Deciding deliberately is worth a mark or two and costs ten minutes.

The table below sets out the six contexts with what each pushes a project towards and the pitfall each carries. Students in Abu Dhabi have genuinely good access to material in all six, and the two that are over-chosen here are identities and relationships and personal and cultural expression, which is worth knowing if a student wants their report to stand out to a reader who has seen thirty from the same cohort.

One caution about fairness and development, which produces the strongest projects we see and needs the most care. A Year 11 student proposing to work with a community they are not part of has an ethical dimension to think through, including whether the intended beneficiaries actually want what is being offered. That thinking, documented in the journal, is excellent criterion C material, and skipping it produces a project that reads as well-meaning rather than considered.

columns: What it pushes the project towards

sections.heading: The process journal: ten minutes a week, or nothing to cite
paragraphs: The journal is where personal projects are won and lost, and students consistently misunderstand it. It is not a diary of feelings and it is not a log of hours. It is a working record of decisions, obstacles, sources, attempts that failed and skills practised, dated as they happen. Both criterion A and criterion C are judged partly on what the report can show from it, so a thin journal caps two criteria at once.

The habit we set up has three prompts, used once a week. What did I decide this week, and why that rather than the alternative? What went wrong or took longer than expected, and what did I do about it? What skill did I have to use or learn, and how well did it go? Three answers, two sentences each, ten minutes. A student who does this for twelve weeks arrives at the report with thirty-six specific, dated, citable pieces of evidence.

Entries do not have to be prose. A photograph of a failed prototype with a caption explaining what failed, a screenshot of a message arranging an interview, a sketch with a date and a note about why the design changed: all of these are stronger evidence than a paragraph written from memory, and all are faster to produce. Where a school's platform permits it, mixed-format journals are usually the best ones.

The honest position on a thin journal is worth stating, because families ask. Entries cannot be invented. What a student can do is record accurately now what genuinely happened earlier, noting that the entry is written retrospectively, which is far better than fabricating dated entries and is something supervisors can work with. The report then reflects honestly on the journal's own weakness, which is itself a creditable piece of reflection.
bullets: Three prompts, once a week, ten minutes: decisions, obstacles, skills
Photographs, screenshots, sketches and voice notes all count as entries
Date entries as they happen; retrospective entries should say they are retrospective
A thin journal caps both the planning and reflecting criteria at once

sections.heading: Report format and length: pick the one that suits the student
paragraphs: The report can be delivered in several formats, and students default to written prose without realising they had a choice. A written or electronic report runs to between 1,500 and 3,500 words. An oral or visual report runs for 13 to 15 minutes. Schools may restrict which formats they accept, so the handbook decides, but where there is a choice it should be made on the student's strengths rather than by habit.

The format changes how evidence is presented rather than how much is needed. A 15-minute recorded presentation still has to evidence all three criteria, and students who choose it because it feels easier than writing often find the opposite: fifteen minutes of structured speech with evidence on screen takes real preparation, and there is nowhere to hide a weak plan. A student who speaks fluently and writes laboriously will still do better in the oral format, provided they script it.

Length discipline matters in both directions. A written report at 1,400 words has almost certainly skipped a criterion. One at 4,000 has usually described the product at length, which earns nothing, while leaving the reflection thin. The allocation that works is roughly a third to planning, a third to applying skills and a third to reflecting, which is also how the marks are distributed.

The table below sets out the formats with their limits and who each suits. Confirm what your child's school accepts before planning around one, because a format the school does not permit is not a format.

sections.heading: Why capable students score thirteen out of twenty-four
paragraphs: The most common disappointing outcome in this task is a strong student with an impressive product and a middling mark. It happens for a specific and avoidable reason: the student optimised for the product, which carries no marks, and treated the planning and reflection as paperwork to be completed afterwards. The report then reads as a description of something good rather than as evidence of a documented process.

The second cause is a goal that was never specified tightly enough to evaluate. If the goal was to make a film about sustainability, the reflection cannot assess whether it succeeded, because there is no standard. If the goal was to make a six-minute film that explains three household water-saving measures clearly enough that a Year 7 audience can list them afterwards, the reflection has something to measure and the measurement is interesting whether or not it succeeded.

The third is reflection that reports satisfaction. A student writes that they are proud of the result and learned a lot about time management. Both may be true and neither is assessable. Criterion C wants the product judged against the stated criteria, the learning named specifically, and the student's development as a learner assessed with evidence from the journal. Three sentences of that kind out-score a page of warm summary.

The encouraging part is that all three faults are cheap to prevent and expensive to repair, which means a Year 11 student who gets one session in the first month is in a materially better position than one who gets four in the last. We say this to every family who asks, and the families who act on it rarely need us again.
bullets: The product is not marked; stop optimising for it
Specify success criteria precisely enough to be judged afterwards
Reflect against the standard you set, not on how the project felt
One session in month one beats four in the final month

sections.heading: Where the supervisor's job ends and ours begins
paragraphs: Every MYP student has a school supervisor, and that person is the authority on this task. They know the school's internal deadlines, which report formats are accepted, how many meetings have to be recorded, and what their school expects at each stage. Nothing we do substitutes for them, and the first thing we tell a student is to take their questions about requirements to their supervisor rather than to us.

What a mentor adds is time and attention of a kind a supervisor managing twenty projects cannot give. A supervisor meeting is often fifteen minutes. An hour spent narrowing a goal, specifying product criteria and setting up journal prompts is a different kind of conversation, and it is the one most students never have. Marking a draft report cold, strand by strand, is also something a supervisor who has watched the project develop cannot easily do.

The integrity line is firm and specific to this task. The project is the student's own, and that includes the product, the journal and the report. We do not make any part of a product, write journal entries, draft report sections or supply text for pasting. Where a student needs a skill to make their product, the honest routes are to learn it, to document the attempt to learn it, or to adjust the goal, and all three are creditable under the criteria.

One further point parents raise: how much parental help is acceptable. Practical support such as transport, buying materials or being interviewed is normal and should simply be recorded in the journal. A parent who makes part of a product has removed the student's evidence of applying skills, which costs marks under criterion B directly. Recording help accurately is both honest and in the student's interest.
bullets: The school supervisor is the authority on requirements, deadlines and formats
No part of the product, journal or report is ever produced by us
Learning a skill and documenting the attempt is creditable; outsourcing it is not
Record parental and other help in the journal rather than hiding it

sections.heading: Timing in the Abu Dhabi school year, and what mentoring costs
paragraphs: Schools in the emirate typically run the personal project across the first two terms of Year 11, with a proposal early in the autumn, supervisor meetings through the winter, and the report due in the spring, well before the end of the year. Counted backwards from the school's report deadline: goal and product criteria fixed in the first month, the bulk of the making done by the midpoint, journal complete throughout, draft report written a month before the deadline, and the final weeks spent on reflection and format rather than on the product.

The project runs alongside the heaviest subject assessment of the whole MYP, which is why it is the thing that gets dropped. Students in this emirate also meet the Ramadan shift in the middle of the year: school days shorten, evenings reorganise around iftar, and our sessions move to post-iftar slots rather than pausing. Making and interviewing both slow down in that month, so the sensible plan front-loads the product work before it.

On cost, the relevant framing for this task is that it is mentoring rather than subject tuition and should be a small purchase. Published UAE rates read in October 2026 run from AED 33 to 65 an hour at the budget online tier, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 200 to 450 and above for IB specialists, AED 180 to 500 for in-home visits where travel is priced in, and AED 650 at one provider for a named tutor. Those are the providers' own figures, not ours.

Our recommendation to Abu Dhabi families is almost always the same: one session early, one at the midpoint and one on the draft report. Three sessions across two terms, with the free trial as the first of them. A family being sold a weekly arrangement for a Year 11 project should ask what the weekly hour is for, because for most students the answer is nothing that the journal prompts do not already cover.
bullets: Goal and product criteria fixed in the first month of the project

faqs.question: How is the MYP personal project assessed?
faqs.answer: Against three criteria, each marked out of eight for a total of 24: planning, applying skills, and reflecting. The marks convert to a grade from 1 to 7 using published boundaries. Where a school registers for MYP eAssessment the project is externally moderated and required for the MYP certificate. The important point for families is what is not assessed: the product itself carries no marks. A student is judged on how they planned, how they applied their skills, and how well they reflect.

faqs.question: Does the product itself earn marks?
faqs.answer: No, and this is the single most useful thing to know about the task. The product or outcome is the vehicle, not the assessment. We regularly read reports from this emirate describing genuinely impressive outcomes that scored in the middle band, because the plan was written retrospectively, the journal was assembled in a weekend and the reflection described satisfaction rather than learning. The practical consequence is that a student should spend less of their term perfecting the product and more of it documenting decisions as they make them.

faqs.question: What should go in the process journal?
faqs.answer: Decisions and the reasoning behind them, obstacles and what was done about them, sources consulted, attempts that failed, and skills that had to be learned, all dated as they happen. It is not a diary of feelings or a log of hours. Three prompts used once a week for ten minutes will produce everything needed: what did I decide and why, what went wrong and what did I do, what skill did I use and how did it go. Photographs, screenshots and sketches with captions all count as entries.

faqs.question: How long should the personal project report be?
faqs.answer: A written or electronic report runs to between 1,500 and 3,500 words; an oral or visual report runs for 13 to 15 minutes. Check which formats your child's school accepts before planning around one. A written report coming in under 1,500 words has usually skipped a criterion, and one running well over 3,500 has usually described the product at length while leaving reflection thin. Roughly a third of the space to each criterion matches how the marks are distributed.

faqs.question: How should my child choose a global context?
faqs.answer: Deliberately, by asking what the context adds rather than what it sounds like. The same project can often sit in two contexts and they produce different work: a water-saving device framed by globalization and sustainability pushes towards the resource question, while scientific and technical innovation pushes towards the engineering. Criterion A asks for the choice to be explained, so a context picked for appearances produces a paragraph the student cannot write convincingly. Ten minutes of thought here is worth a mark or two.

faqs.question: What makes a goal appropriately challenging?
faqs.answer: It should be something the student cannot already do, stated precisely enough that a reader knows what finished looks like. Learning the guitar is not a goal. Performing a specific three-piece set at a specific event, starting from no instrumental experience, is. Precision does two jobs: it lets criterion A judge the challenge, and it gives criterion C something to evaluate the product against. Goals that are either unachievable or entirely safe are the two ways students lose marks here, and both are visible in week one.

faqs.question: Why did a strong project score only thirteen out of twenty-four?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the student optimised for the product and treated the planning and reflection as paperwork. The report then describes something good rather than evidencing a documented process. The three usual faults are a retrospective plan, product criteria that were never specified tightly enough to evaluate, and reflection that reports satisfaction instead of assessing learning. All three are cheap to prevent at the start of the project and expensive to repair at the end, which is why early support matters more here than late support.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help make the product?
faqs.answer: No. The project is the student's own work, including the product, the journal and the report, and criterion B is explicitly about the student applying their own skills. If someone else makes part of the product, the evidence for that criterion disappears along with the marks. Where a student lacks a skill the product needs, the creditable routes are to learn it, to document the attempt honestly, or to adjust the goal. All three are legitimate and all three give the reflection something real to work with.

faqs.question: How much can parents help with the personal project?
faqs.answer: Practical help such as transport, buying materials, being interviewed or giving access to a contact is normal and should simply be recorded in the journal. What costs marks is a parent making part of the product or writing part of the report, because that removes the student's own evidence of applying skills. Recording help accurately is both honest and in the student's interest: a journal entry noting who helped and with what demonstrates exactly the self-awareness the reflecting criterion rewards.

faqs.question: Is personal project help delivered online in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Yes, one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. The project happens wherever the student makes it, and the sessions are planning and review conversations with the journal and the draft report on a shared screen. That works better than a visit for a Year 11 student whose product may be a film, a website or a series of workshops rather than something on a table.

faqs.question: When in Year 11 should a student start?
faqs.answer: The goal and product criteria should be fixed within the first month of the project, which in most Abu Dhabi schools means early in the autumn term. The bulk of the making should be done by the midpoint, with the journal running throughout and the draft report written a month before the school's deadline. Front-load the product work before Ramadan, when making and interviewing both slow down. A student who gets one session in the first month is in a far better position than one who gets four in the last.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the MYP personal project and the PYP exhibition?
faqs.answer: They share the spirit of student-directed inquiry and almost nothing else. The PYP exhibition at the end of Year 6 is collaborative, presented to the school community and not graded by the IB. The personal project in the final MYP year is individual, assessed against three criteria out of eight each, and required for the MYP certificate where a school registers for eAssessment. Abu Dhabi families with children in both programmes regularly receive emails about both in the same term, which is where the confusion comes from.

faqs.question: Can the report be a presentation instead of an essay?
faqs.answer: Where the school permits it, yes: an oral or visual report runs for 13 to 15 minutes instead of 1,500 to 3,500 words. Students who speak fluently and write slowly often do better this way, but it is not an easier option. Fifteen minutes of structured speech still has to evidence all three criteria, there is nowhere to hide a weak plan, and it needs scripting. Confirm with the supervisor first, because a format the school does not accept is not available however well it suits the student.

faqs.question: My child's journal is nearly empty and the deadline is close. What can be done?
faqs.answer: Record accurately now what genuinely happened earlier, and say in the entries that they are written retrospectively. That is honest, supervisors can work with it, and it is far better than fabricating dated entries, which is a declaration about work that is not true. The report can then reflect on the journal's own weakness and on what the student would do differently, which is itself creditable reflection. What cannot be recovered is detail nobody remembers, which is the real cost of a thin journal.

faqs.question: Does the personal project help with the Diploma later?
faqs.answer: More than any other MYP assessment, for students continuing into the DP. The habits it builds are the ones DP1 demands immediately: keeping dated evidence, planning against stated criteria, and reflecting with specifics rather than sentiment. A student who kept a usable process journal in Year 11 can draft an Extended Essay proposal without help. One who assembled a journal in a weekend has learned that coursework can be reconstructed at the end, which is an expensive lesson to unlearn in DP2.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-personal-project-help.closingBody: If your child has just been given their personal project, the useful hour is now and not in the spring. Send us whatever their school has issued and a sentence about what they are thinking of making, and the free session will turn that into a goal precise enough to be judged, a global context chosen on purpose, product criteria written in advance, and three journal prompts that take ten minutes a week. Most Abu Dhabi families we work with need that session, one review at the midpoint and one cold mark on the draft report. Three in total, across two terms.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-personal-project-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below have supervised and marked MYP personal projects. Each can read a learning goal, a set of success criteria and a handful of journal entries and tell you which strand is underfed - which is a different conversation from asking whether the project idea is good.

intro.heading: The grade is usually lost in week one, not week twenty
paragraphs: The MYP personal project produces more anxiety in Abu Dhabi households than any other piece of MYP work, and it is assessed on less than families imagine. The current projects guide marks it against three criteria of 8 marks each - planning, applying skills, and reflecting - giving 24 criterion marks that the school converts into a 1-7 grade. Older versions of the guide used four criteria and required a global context, so if an older framework is being described to you, ask your MYP coordinator which version your school is working to. That single question saves a great deal of confusion.

Within those three criteria the work is strand-based, and that is the detail almost nobody tells students. Criterion A asks for a stated learning goal with an explanation of the personal interest behind it, an intended product, success criteria for that product, and a clear detailed plan. Criterion B asks the student to explain how approaches to learning skills were applied to achieve the learning goal and, separately, how they were applied to achieve the product. Criterion C asks them to explain the impact of the project on themselves or their learning, and to evaluate the product against their own success criteria. Each of those is a separate thing to evidence, and a report that addresses five of the seven cannot score in the upper bands no matter how good the project was.

The consequence is that the grade is largely determined in the first fortnight. A learning goal that is too broad produces success criteria that cannot be measured, which makes the criterion C evaluation impossible to do well eight months later. A student who sets out to learn about photography has no way of evaluating whether they achieved it. A student who sets out to produce a twelve-image documentary sequence on a specific subject, with stated criteria about lighting consistency, sequencing and caption quality, has handed themselves a criterion C structure for free.

The second high-value moment is the report. By then the project is what it is, and the marks available are in how the work is explained. Students write narratives - first I did this, then this went wrong, then I finished - and narratives bury the strands. A report organised around the strands scores higher than a better project described chronologically, which feels unfair to students and is simply how criterion-referenced marking works.

Abu Dhabi adds a calendar problem rather than an academic one. The personal project runs through MYP 5, the same year as the heaviest subject assessment load, and the supervisor is a teacher with a full timetable rather than a dedicated mentor. Families in the emirate's larger schools often find supervisor meetings are brief and widely spaced. This page is written to fill that gap honestly: what each strand needs, where marks are lost, and what a tutor may and may not do, because the project must be the student's own work and the consequence of anything else falls on the student. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, and IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE - home visits are a service we offer only in India.
