abu-dhabi/ib-myp-personal-project-tutor.programmesIntro: The personal project sits at the end of a sequence of self-directed work that starts earlier in the MYP and continues into the Diploma. Reading it as one stage of that sequence makes the point of it clearer than treating it as a one-off hurdle.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The personal project is completed in the final year of the programme and is the capstone piece of independent work. Students set a learning goal, produce a product, keep a process journal throughout, and submit a report with an academic honesty form signed by both student and supervisor. Schools registered for the MYP certificate submit it for external moderation, which is why the form and the journal matter as much as the product.
programmes.countryNote: In Abu Dhabi's larger MYP schools, particularly in the Khalifa City and Al Raha corridor, supervisors carry several students alongside a full teaching timetable, and formal meetings can be brief and widely spaced. Students who keep their journal between meetings get far more from each one. Those who arrive with nothing to show spend the meeting explaining instead of being advised.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma's extended essay and CAS portfolio are the direct descendants of the personal project: a self-directed piece with a supervisor, a process requirement and a reflective component. Students who learned to keep a real journal and to evaluate against stated criteria arrive able to handle both. Students who produced a good product and a thin report repeat the same pattern two years later at higher stakes.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi students moving from MYP 5 into DP1 often do so inside the same school, which means the habits formed in the personal project are visible to the teachers who will supervise the extended essay. That continuity is an argument for doing the process properly rather than surviving it.

programmes.name: MYP community project
programmes.description: Where a school runs it, the community project is a group or individual piece completed earlier in the programme, assessed against the same three-criterion structure with a service focus. It is the rehearsal: a student who has written success criteria once before writes much better ones for the personal project. Where a school does not run it, the personal project is the student's first experience of the format.
programmes.countryNote: Not every Abu Dhabi MYP school runs the community project, and that single difference shows up clearly in the quality of MYP 5 learning goals. Students meeting the format for the first time in their final year need more support at the goal-setting stage, not less, and it is worth asking the coordinator whether your child has done one.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP exhibition in the final primary year is the earliest version of the same idea: a student-led inquiry with a presented outcome and a reflective element. There is no criterion marking, but students who did one arrive in the MYP already familiar with the shape of self-directed work, which is a real advantage five years later.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi primary sections run a substantial exhibition in Year 6, and students who transfer into the emirate after that point often have no equivalent experience. It is a small gap and worth naming, because it explains why some MYP 5 students find the personal project structurally unfamiliar rather than difficult.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-personal-project-tutor.subjectsIntro: A personal project draws on subject knowledge the student already has, and the strongest projects are the ones anchored in a subject the student is competent in. The grid below names subjects commonly used as the base for a project and what each contributes.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: The closest subject in logic: inquiring, developing ideas, creating and evaluating. A student with two years of Design folders already knows how to write measurable criteria and keep a change log, which covers most of criterion A and B evidence.

subjects.name: Arts - visual, music, drama, dance
subjects.description: A frequent base for a product, and the process journal habit transfers directly. The risk is a project that becomes a performance or exhibition with no stated success criteria, which caps criterion C.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating. Science-based projects produce the most measurable success criteria of any discipline, which makes criterion C straightforward, but students often over-scope the investigation.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Investigating and communicating. Research-heavy projects based here score well on criterion A planning, and lose marks when the product turns out to be a report about the research rather than a product in its own right.

subjects.name: Mathematics - Standard and Extended
subjects.description: Useful for projects involving data, modelling, finance or measurement. A student who can handle the arithmetic of their own product writes success criteria with numbers in them, which is exactly what criterion C needs.

subjects.name: English - Language and Literature
subjects.description: Organising and producing text is what the report is marked on in practice. Students with weak written organisation lose personal project marks for reports that contain the right thinking in an order a moderator cannot follow.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition - French, Spanish, Arabic
subjects.description: A language-based learning goal is viable and often strong, provided the product is not simply 'becoming better at the language'. A measurable artefact - a translated collection, a recorded interview series - makes it assessable.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Planning for performance and reflecting on it are already criterion-shaped. Training-based projects work well when the success criteria are about a programme's design rather than about a personal result the student cannot control.

subjects.name: Arabic and Islamic Education
subjects.description: Mandatory subjects in UAE private schools with set school material. They run through MYP 5 alongside the project and compete for the same hours, which is the main scheduling constraint on an Abu Dhabi student's project year.

subjects.name: Approaches to learning skills
subjects.description: Not a subject but the thing criterion B is explicitly about. Research, communication, social, self-management and thinking skills - the student has to explain which they applied and how, for the goal and for the product separately.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-personal-project-tutor.regionsIntro: What varies across Abu Dhabi is not the project but the support around it: how many students a supervisor carries, how the school runs its exhibition, and how early the deadlines fall. The notes below reflect that.

regions.name: Khalifa City
regions.note: The emirate's largest MYP cohorts, which means supervisors carry more students and formal meetings are shorter. Keeping a journal between meetings matters more here than anywhere else in Abu Dhabi.

regions.name: Al Raha Gardens and Al Raha Beach
regions.note: Settled cohorts with established project calendars, so deadlines are predictable and published early. Students here lose marks to complacency about the report rather than to running out of time.

regions.name: Al Reem Island
regions.note: High mid-year transfer rates. A student arriving in MYP 5 may have missed the goal-setting phase entirely and has to compress eight months of process into fewer, which changes what a realistic product looks like.

regions.name: Saadiyat Island
regions.note: Smaller cohorts and closer supervision, with cultural institutions nearby that make certain products genuinely viable - exhibitions, guided materials, documentation projects with a real audience.

regions.name: Al Bateen and Al Mushrif
regions.note: Long-established schools with mature project processes, formal exhibitions and earlier internal deadlines. Expectations for the report are correspondingly higher because departments have seen many of them.

regions.name: Yas Island
regions.note: Newer schools where project calendars are still settling, so internal deadlines move more often. Students here should confirm dates in writing rather than relying on what was said in September.

regions.name: Al Shamkha and Al Falah
regions.note: Longer commutes compress the evenings available for project work in a year that is already full. Products that can be made at home, rather than ones needing school facilities after hours, are the realistic choice.

schoolClusters.city: Khalifa City, Al Raha and Yas
schoolClusters.note: Large year groups where a supervisor may carry a dozen or more projects. Internal deadlines are firm and exhibition slots limited, so students who miss a milestone have little room to recover it.

schoolClusters.note: Established schools with mature personal project processes, formal exhibitions and earlier internal deadlines. Reports are read by staff with years of moderation experience, and the strand-based expectations are explicit.

modes.title: Goal and criteria session, at the start
modes.description: One or two sessions in the first fortnight, aimed at narrowing the learning goal until it is achievable and writing success criteria that can actually be evaluated. This is the highest-value hour in the whole project and the one families most often skip.

modes.title: Mid-project journal and skills review
modes.description: A single session around the halfway point, reading the process journal against criterion B. Students almost always have applied approaches to learning skills and almost never named them, which is the difference between a 4 and a 6 on that criterion.

modes.title: Report structure block, before writing
modes.description: Two or three sessions before the report is drafted, spent mapping the strands onto a structure. The student writes every word; the session is about what has to be addressed and in what order so that a moderator can find it.

sections.heading: What the personal project is actually assessed on
paragraphs: Three criteria, 8 marks each, 24 marks in total, converted by the school into a 1-7 grade. Within them sit seven strands, and the strands are what a moderator looks for. The table below sets them out, names the evidence each requires, and identifies where Abu Dhabi students most often lose the marks.

The most useful thing a parent can do with this table is check it against the report in draft. Each strand should be findable - not implied, not spread across three paragraphs, but addressed. Students who have never seen the strands written down tend to produce a report that answers four or five of the seven thoroughly and leaves the rest to inference, which costs bands rather than marks.

Note what is not assessed. The ambition of the project is not a criterion. Neither is the quality of the product in any absolute sense - criterion C evaluates the product against the student's own success criteria, which is why those criteria are the hinge of the whole thing. A modest product honestly evaluated against well-written criteria outscores an impressive product measured against nothing, every time, and students find this genuinely hard to believe until they see the descriptors.

Confirm the version of the guide your school is using before planning around any of this. Earlier guides used four criteria and required the project to be framed by a global context; the current structure centres the learning goal and the product. Your MYP coordinator can answer that in one line, and the answer changes what the report has to contain.

sections.heading: The learning goal: why most of them are too big
paragraphs: A learning goal does two jobs. It states what the student intends to learn, and it sets the boundary within which everything else is judged. Students write them in the first week, before they understand what the criteria will later ask, and they write them too broad because broad feels ambitious. Eight months later the breadth makes criterion C unanswerable.

The test is simple: could somebody else tell whether the goal was achieved? 'Learn about marine conservation' fails - there is no state of the world in which that is finished. 'Learn how to identify and document the common reef fish of the Abu Dhabi coast well enough to produce an identification guide for a school audience' passes, because achievement is checkable and the product is implied by the goal rather than bolted on.

Narrowing is the work of a single session and it is the cheapest intervention available in the subject. The method is to ask three questions in order. What will exist at the end that does not exist now? Who is it for? What would make it good, in terms someone else could verify? The answers to those three are the intended product, the audience, and the success criteria - which is most of criterion A produced in twenty minutes of interrogation.

The scope question is separate and equally important in an Abu Dhabi MYP 5 year. The project runs alongside the heaviest subject assessment load of the programme, and students regularly set goals that would need a free summer. A product that can be made in the evenings across two terms, with mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education and the full subject timetable continuing, is the realistic unit. Over-scoping does not lose marks for ambition; it loses them because the plan, the journal and the evaluation all end up thin.

sections.heading: Success criteria are the hinge between criterion A and criterion C
paragraphs: This is the part of the personal project that students most reliably get wrong, and it is worth understanding mechanically. Criterion A asks the student to develop success criteria for their product. Criterion C asks them to evaluate the product against those criteria. The second is therefore only as good as the first. Criteria written vaguely in October make a strong evaluation in May arithmetically impossible, and nobody notices the connection at the time.

A usable success criterion has three properties. It describes the product rather than the student - 'the guide identifies twenty species' not 'I work hard'. It can be checked by somebody who was not involved. And it is specific enough to fail: a criterion that the product obviously meets tells a moderator nothing. Four or five criteria of that kind is a better set than ten aspirational ones.

The evaluation that follows is then a short, honest exercise rather than an essay. Take each criterion, state the evidence, and judge it - met, partly met, not met - with the reason. A product that misses two of five criteria, evaluated honestly with specific evidence, scores well on criterion C. A product that met everything, evaluated in general praise, does not. Students resist recording failure because it reads to them as a confession; in criterion-referenced marking it reads as evidence of judgement.

The practical sequence is therefore: narrow the goal, name the product, write criteria that could fail, then build. Students who do it in that order find the report largely writes itself, because every claim has a stated criterion and a piece of journal evidence behind it. Students who build first and write criteria afterwards produce a document that looks complete and reads as retrospective, which moderators recognise immediately.
bullets: A criterion describes the product, not the student's effort
It must be checkable by somebody who was not involved
It must be specific enough that the product could fail it
Four or five sharp criteria beat ten aspirational ones
Evaluate each one as met, partly met or not met, with the evidence

sections.heading: Criterion B is about skills, not about the product
paragraphs: Criterion B is the most misread of the three. It does not ask what the student made or how well. It asks them to explain how approaches to learning skills were applied - once in service of the learning goal, and separately in service of the product. Two explanations, two strands, 8 marks between them.

The approaches to learning skill clusters are research, communication, social, self-management and thinking. Every student uses several of them across a project year. Almost none of them name any. A student writes that they made a schedule and stuck to it; what criterion B wanted was that they applied an organisation skill within self-management, how specifically they applied it, and what evidence in the journal shows it working or failing. The underlying work is identical. The explanation is what is marked.

The separation of goal and product trips students up almost as often. Learning how to sequence documentary photographs is a research and thinking exercise; producing the twelve-image series on a deadline is a self-management and communication exercise. A student who answers the question once, generally, has addressed one strand and left the other to inference. Reading criterion B as two questions rather than one is worth a band on its own.

What a mid-project session does here is mechanical. The tutor reads the journal, asks the student which skill a given entry demonstrates, and makes them answer. The skills were applied - the student lived the project - so this is recall and labelling rather than invention. Done at the halfway point it also reveals which weeks have no record at all, while there is still time to keep one properly.
bullets: ATL clusters: research, communication, social, self-management, thinking
Criterion B is two questions - skills for the goal, and skills for the product
Describing the action is not explaining the skill

sections.heading: The process journal: evidence, not a diary
paragraphs: The process journal is where criterion B lives and where criterion C finds its material, and it is the single most commonly mishandled requirement in the personal project. Students treat it as a diary - what I did today, how I felt about it - and produce a document with no assessable content. Or they ignore it for seven months and write twenty entries in a weekend, which is visible to anyone who reads them.

What belongs in it is narrower and easier than a diary. A decision and the reason for it. A thing that was tried and did not work, with what was learned. A source, cited, with a note on what was taken from it. A skill applied, named, with what happened. A change to the plan and why it was necessary. Five categories, a couple of entries a week, three or four sentences each. That is perhaps ten minutes a week and it produces everything criterion B and C need.

Format is flexible and should suit the student. Written notes, voice memos, photographs with annotations, a running document, a notebook. The requirement is a record maintained throughout rather than a particular medium, so a student who thinks better aloud should record audio. What does not work is a format so elaborate that it does not get kept - an over-designed journal is an abandoned journal by December.

For an Abu Dhabi MYP 5 student the practical difficulty is the competing calendar. Subject assessment, mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education, and in many schools a graded music examination or a sports commitment all run through the same months. The journal survives that only if it is small and habitual. Two entries a week of four sentences, attached to an existing routine, is the version that still exists in March.
bullets: A decision and its reason; something tried that failed; a cited source; a skill named; a plan change
Two short entries a week is enough - roughly ten minutes
Any format: written, audio, annotated photographs, a running document
An elaborate journal is an abandoned journal by December
A journal written retrospectively in the final fortnight reads as exactly that

sections.heading: The report: structure the strands rather than tell the story
paragraphs: By report-writing time the project is finished and the remaining marks are entirely in how it is explained. This is the second moment where a session earns its fee, and the gain is usually larger than families expect, because most students default to chronology and chronology hides the strands.

The structural principle is one section per strand, in the order the criteria run. State the learning goal and the personal interest behind it. State the intended product and list the success criteria as they were written at the start. Present the plan and what changed in it. Explain the ATL skills applied to the goal, with journal evidence. Explain the ATL skills applied to the product, with journal evidence. Explain the impact of the project on the student or their learning. Evaluate the product against each success criterion in turn. A moderator reading that finds everything they are looking for, in the order they are looking for it.

Length is set by format in the guide - a written report, an oral presentation and a multimedia submission have different limits - and the figures are the kind of detail that is revised between guide versions, so take them from your school's own current brief rather than from any tutoring page. What is constant is that the limit is generous enough for the strands and tight enough to punish narrative padding. Students who tell the story run out of room before they evaluate anything, and the evaluation is a whole criterion.

The academic honesty requirement sits here too. Sources must be cited, the form is signed by both student and supervisor, and the work must be the student's own. A tutor reading a draft comments on whether a strand is addressed, whether a claim has evidence, and whether the evaluation refers to the stated criteria. A tutor never writes any part of it, and never supplies the evidence, because the consequence of misrepresented authorship falls on the student and it is severe.

sections.heading: Counting back from the deadline in an Abu Dhabi MYP 5 year
paragraphs: The personal project fails on scheduling more often than on substance. It is the only major piece of MYP work with no weekly lesson attached to it, which means nothing in the timetable forces progress, and the internal deadlines in Abu Dhabi's larger schools arrive earlier than families assume. The table below counts backwards from submission, which is a more useful way to see the year than counting forwards from September.

Two features of the emirate's school year shape it. The first is that MYP 5 subject assessment and the project compete directly for evenings, and the subject work always wins in the short term because it has a teacher chasing it. The second is Ramadan, which shortens school days and moves family routines later - and in most years falls close enough to the project deadline to matter. Students who have banked progress before it are comfortable; students who planned to work through it are not.

Supervisor meetings are the other fixed point and they are limited. In a large cohort a supervisor may carry a dozen projects, so meetings are short and widely spaced. The way to get value from them is to arrive with something specific: a draft criterion set, three journal entries, a structural question. A student who arrives with nothing spends the meeting describing the project to a teacher who then has nothing to advise on.

Treat the table as a template against your school's own published dates. Ask for those dates in writing early, particularly in the newer schools where project calendars are still settling, and work backwards from the earliest one rather than from the final submission. The commonest avoidable failure is discovering in February that the internal draft deadline was January.

sections.heading: What a session fixes, what the supervisor does, and where the line is
paragraphs: A supervisor and a tutor are different roles and it is worth being precise about both. The supervisor is a member of school staff who meets the student periodically, signs the academic honesty form, and confirms that the work is the student's own. They are accountable to the school and the IB, and they are the authority on the school's own deadlines and expectations. Nothing on this page substitutes for them.

A tutor adds time and criterion literacy - two things a supervisor carrying a dozen projects does not have in quantity. What that looks like in practice is narrow and specific. Interrogating a learning goal until it is evaluable. Rewriting success criteria with the student until each one could fail. Reading a journal and asking which skill an entry demonstrates. Reading a draft report and saying which strand is missing. Checking that the evaluation refers to the criteria as written rather than to how the student feels about the product.

What a tutor must not do is equally specific. Not choose the goal or the product. Not write any part of the report, the journal or the criteria. Not supply research, sources or content. Not make the product or any component of it. The project must be the student's own work, the academic honesty form attests to that, and the consequence of a breach falls on the student under IB rules. We say this plainly because the market this page sits in contains providers who sell completed assessed work, and that is an exposure for the student rather than a shortcut.

The first session is free - one trial lesson per student, no card details, nothing payable, no obligation to continue - and it is used to find out which of the two useful moments you are at. If the goal is still open, that is the session to have. If the product is done and the report is not written, that is the other one. If the project is in good order and the student needs nothing, the written note says so. Where no personal project specialist is free for the slot you need, we say that too rather than putting a generalist in front of a strand-based report.

process.title: Send the goal, the criteria and three journal entries
process.description: Whatever exists. A one-line goal and nothing else is useful information. Those three items together show which of the seven strands currently has evidence behind it and which is being left to inference.

process.title: Free trial lesson to locate the real problem
process.description: One lesson, one student, no card details and nothing payable. Most projects need help at one of two moments - goal-setting or report structure - and the session establishes which, rather than assuming a standing arrangement is needed.

process.title: Narrow the goal and rewrite the criteria
process.description: Where the project is early, this is the work: three questions that produce the product, the audience and a set of success criteria that could fail. It is twenty minutes of interrogation and it determines the criterion C mark eight months later.

process.title: Mid-project journal and skills labelling
process.description: One session reading the journal against criterion B, with the student naming which approaches to learning skill each entry demonstrates. It also exposes the weeks with no record while they can still be kept properly.

process.title: Report structure, then the student writes it
process.description: The strands are mapped to sections and the evidence for each claim is selected from the journal. The student writes every word; feedback says which strand is thin, not what to put in it.

whyPoints.title: The goal is interrogated before anything is built
whyPoints.description: A learning goal that cannot be evaluated makes a strong criterion C mark impossible months before anyone notices. Narrowing it is the cheapest and highest-value hour in the project, and it is where a first session goes.

whyPoints.title: Success criteria written to be failable
whyPoints.description: Criterion C evaluates the product against the student's own criteria, so criteria that the product obviously meets earn nothing. We write four or five that could fail, which turns the evaluation into a short honest exercise instead of an essay.

whyPoints.title: Criterion B read as two questions
whyPoints.description: Skills applied to the learning goal and skills applied to the product are separate strands. Students answer once, generally, and lose a band. Labelling skills from an existing journal is recall rather than invention, and it is quick.

whyPoints.title: A report organised by strand
whyPoints.description: Chronology hides the strands and runs out of room before the evaluation. One section per strand in criteria order means a moderator finds everything where they look for it, which is worth more than a better project told as a story.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line is explicit
whyPoints.description: The project must be the student's own work. A tutor comments on whether a strand is addressed and whether a claim has evidence - never writes, supplies or makes any part of it. The academic honesty form is signed by the student and their school supervisor.

whyPoints.title: Two sessions is often the right answer
whyPoints.description: Most personal projects need help at goal-setting and again before the report, not weekly across a year. If the trial lesson finds the project in good order, the written note says no purchase is needed.

faqs.question: How many criteria does the MYP personal project have now?
faqs.answer: Three in the current projects guide - planning, applying skills and reflecting - each worth 8 marks, giving 24 that the school converts into a 1-7 grade. Earlier guides used four criteria and required the project to be framed by a global context, which is why families sometimes receive conflicting descriptions. Ask your MYP coordinator which version your school is working to, because it changes what the report must contain. Within the three criteria sit seven strands, and the strands are what a moderator actually looks for - a report that addresses five of them thoroughly cannot reach the upper bands.

faqs.question: How specific does the learning goal have to be?
faqs.answer: Specific enough that somebody else could tell whether it was achieved. 'Learn about marine conservation' fails that test, because there is no state in which it is finished. 'Learn to identify and document common reef fish of the Abu Dhabi coast well enough to produce an identification guide for a school audience' passes, because achievement is checkable and the product follows from the goal rather than being bolted on. The narrowing method is three questions: what will exist at the end that does not now, who is it for, and what would make it good in terms a stranger could verify.

faqs.question: Why do the success criteria decide the reflection mark?
faqs.answer: Because criterion C evaluates the product against the student's own success criteria rather than against any external standard. Criteria written vaguely in the first weeks make a strong evaluation arithmetically impossible eight months later, and nobody notices the connection at the time. A usable criterion describes the product rather than the student's effort, can be checked by somebody who was not involved, and is specific enough that the product could fail it. Four or five of that kind beat ten aspirational ones, and they turn the final evaluation into a short honest exercise.

faqs.question: What is the difference between my child's supervisor and a tutor?
faqs.answer: The supervisor is school staff. They meet the student periodically, sign the academic honesty form, confirm the work is the student's own, and are the authority on the school's internal deadlines. A tutor adds two things a supervisor carrying a dozen projects does not have much of: time, and fluency in what the criteria ask for. A tutor interrogates the goal, helps rewrite criteria, reads the journal for criterion B evidence and says which strand a draft report is missing. A tutor does not choose the goal, write any part of the work, or supply content.

faqs.question: Does the process journal get submitted with the report?
faqs.answer: Schools handle this differently and your coordinator will confirm the local requirement, but the journal is a required part of the process in every case and extracts from it are normally used as evidence inside the report. What matters practically is that it is maintained throughout rather than reconstructed - twenty entries written in one weekend read exactly like twenty entries written in one weekend. What belongs in it is narrow: a decision and its reason, something tried that failed, a cited source, a named skill applied, a change to the plan. Two short entries a week is sufficient.

faqs.question: How long is the personal project report supposed to be?
faqs.answer: The guide sets limits by format - a written report, an oral presentation and a multimedia submission are treated differently - and those figures are the kind of detail revised between guide versions, so take them from your school's own current brief rather than from any tutoring page. What is constant is that the limit is generous enough to address all seven strands and tight enough to punish narrative padding. Students who tell the project as a story run out of room before they evaluate the product, and the evaluation is a whole criterion rather than a closing paragraph.

faqs.question: Is the personal project marked outside the school?
faqs.answer: Schools registered for the MYP certificate submit personal projects for external moderation, which is why the academic honesty form and the journal carry real weight alongside the report. Where a school is not registered, the project is assessed internally against the same criteria. Your MYP coordinator can confirm which applies. Either way the criteria and the strands are identical, so a project built properly serves both routes. The practical difference is in deadlines: external moderation brings fixed submission dates that the school works backwards from, often earlier than families expect.

faqs.question: Which approaches to learning skills does criterion B expect?
faqs.answer: Any of the five clusters - research, communication, social, self-management and thinking - but the criterion is about explanation rather than selection. The student must explain how skills were applied to achieve the learning goal, and separately how they were applied to achieve the product. Two strands, two answers. Describing the action is not explaining the skill: writing that they made a schedule and stuck to it is description, where naming the organisation skill within self-management, saying how it was applied and pointing to journal evidence is what the criterion asks for.

faqs.question: Does the personal project still need a global context?
faqs.answer: Earlier versions of the guide required the project to be framed by one of the global contexts. The current structure centres the learning goal and the product instead, which is one of the reasons families receive contradictory advice about this piece of work. Confirm with your MYP coordinator which guide your school is working to before planning the report, because a global context section in a report assessed under the current criteria uses space the evaluation needs, and its absence in a school still using the older framework would be a gap.

faqs.question: When should an Abu Dhabi student start the personal project?
faqs.answer: Earlier than the school's first deadline suggests, and the reason is local. MYP 5 carries the heaviest subject assessment load of the programme, and subject work always wins the competition for evenings because it has a teacher chasing it. Ramadan shortens school days and in most years falls close enough to the project deadline to matter, so progress banked before it is worth more than plans made around it. Ask for the school's internal dates in writing early, particularly in the newer schools where project calendars are still settling, and work backwards from the earliest one.

faqs.question: Can the product be a performance, an event or something sold?
faqs.answer: A performance or an event is a perfectly good product, provided the success criteria describe it in checkable terms and there is documentation - recordings, photographs, audience response - to evaluate against them. The difficulty with anything sold is that commercial success depends on factors the student does not control, so criteria about revenue make the criterion C evaluation a matter of luck. Write criteria about what the student produced and how well it met a defined need, and treat any commercial outcome as context in the reflection rather than as a criterion.

faqs.question: What happens if the product does not work?
faqs.answer: It costs far less than students fear, because criterion C rewards honest evaluation against the stated criteria rather than a successful product. A product that misses two of five criteria, evaluated with specific evidence and a clear explanation of why, scores well. A product that met everything, evaluated in general praise, does not. What does cost marks is concealing the failure, rewriting the criteria afterwards so the product passes, or leaving the evaluation vague. The journal entries recording what went wrong are among the most valuable evidence in the whole project.

faqs.question: Does the personal project grade matter for Diploma entry?
faqs.answer: It matters as preparation far more than as a gatekeeper, and schools set their own progression requirements - ask yours directly rather than assuming. What is reliably true is that the extended essay and CAS portfolio in the Diploma are the direct descendants of this piece of work: a self-directed project with a supervisor, a process requirement and a reflective component. Students who learned to keep a real journal and evaluate against stated criteria handle both. Students who produced a good product and a thin report repeat the pattern two years later with higher stakes attached.

faqs.question: Who signs the academic honesty form and what does it cover?
faqs.answer: Both the student and the school supervisor sign it, and it attests that the work submitted is the student's own and that sources have been acknowledged. That is the formal reason the boundaries around outside help matter: a tutor may teach, question and give feedback on the student's own work, and may not write, supply or make any part of it. Under IB rules the consequence of misrepresented authorship falls on the student. Any provider offering to produce assessed work is offering the student a risk, not a shortcut, and this market contains some that do.

faqs.question: Can a tutor read the report in draft before it is submitted?
faqs.answer: Yes, and reviewing a draft is one of the two moments where outside help is genuinely worth paying for. The boundary is what the feedback consists of: which strand is not addressed, which claim has no journal evidence behind it, whether the evaluation refers to the success criteria as they were originally written, and whether sources are cited. That is commentary on the student's own work. Rewriting sentences, restructuring sections on the student's behalf or supplying content is not, and it would make the signed honesty form inaccurate.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-personal-project-tutor.closingHeading: Fix the goal early or fix the report late - both work, one is cheaper
abu-dhabi/ib-myp-personal-project-tutor.closingBody: The personal project rewards two short interventions far more than a year of weekly sessions. Send the learning goal, the success criteria and three journal entries, and the free trial lesson - one lesson, one student, no card details, nothing payable - will establish which of the two moments you are at and what the strands currently lack. Where the project is in good order, the written note says no support is needed. Sessions run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and everything submitted remains the student's own work.

intro.heading: What an MYP physics tutor in Abu Dhabi costs, and what sets the number
paragraphs: Start with the only honest answer: the published range for private tutoring in the UAE runs from AED 45 an hour at the budget online end to AED 650 an hour for a named premium tutor, and MYP physics sits in the lower middle of that spread. EdFlik advertises online tutoring from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Unitors publishes IGCSE tutoring from AED 150 and IB tutoring from AED 200. Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 350 and exam-year specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more. BartyED quotes AED 650 for a premium named tutor. Those are their figures, read in October 2026, not ours.

MYP physics is cheaper per hour than Diploma physics for a structural reason, not a marketing one. There is no external examination hanging over MYP 1 to 4, no Internal Assessment to supervise, and the assessment is criterion-referenced coursework set by your child's own school. A tutor working in MYP 4 is not preparing a candidate for a terminal paper; they are moving criterion levels on tasks the subject teacher has written. That is skilled work, and it is less specialised work than coaching a Paper 3 option at Higher Level, so the market prices it lower.

What pushes an Abu Dhabi quote up is not the emirate's cost of living. It is three things. First, discrete versus integrated: a tutor asked to cover physics as a separate MYP 5 course is being asked for subject depth, and depth costs more than general science coverage. Second, criterion B and C work: designing a controlled investigation and processing data properly takes longer to teach than recalling definitions, so a term aimed at those criteria needs more hours than a term aimed at criterion A. Third, timing. A request that lands two weeks before an end-of-unit task competes with every other family in the same school for the same evening slot, and scarce evening slots are the only part of this market that behaves like a commodity.

The second cost nobody quotes you is unseen preparation. The MYP does not publish a content syllabus for physics. The IB Sciences guide sets out key concepts, related concepts, global contexts and the four assessment criteria; your child's school then writes its own units and its own tasks. So before lesson one a tutor has to read the unit planner, the task sheet, the criterion rubric and the last marked piece of work. Providers handle that differently: some absorb it, some bill it, some skip it and then teach the wrong thing for a fortnight. Ask which, in writing, before you pay anything.

Lessons from IB Gram are delivered live online, one to one, over video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi; home visits are a service we run only in India. For a physics family that is the cheaper and the better arrangement at the same time, because the screen is where the work already lives. Graphs get drawn on a shared whiteboard, a photographed lab book is annotated in real time, and a logger-recorded data set can be opened and reprocessed in front of the student instead of being described from memory.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-physics-tutor.programmesIntro: Abu Dhabi families usually arrive on this page in MYP 3 or MYP 4, when Sciences splits into recognisable physics content and the report card suddenly reads 4, 5, 3, 5 instead of a percentage. Here is where the Middle Years Programme sits either side of that moment, and what the physics workload looks like in each phase.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years in which Sciences is one subject group rather than three subjects. In MYP 1 to 3 most Abu Dhabi schools teach integrated Sciences, so physics appears as units on forces, energy and waves alongside chemistry and biology content. In MYP 4 and 5 many schools let students take discrete physics. Assessment is against four criteria, each marked out of eight, set and marked internally by the school.
programmes.countryNote: In this emirate the schools licensed by ADEK publish criterion levels on their reports, and parents routinely see four numbers with no percentage anywhere. ADEK also inspects these schools and publishes ratings, so a weak Sciences department usually appears in the inspection narrative before it appears in your child's grade. A physics tutor here reads the school's own unit planner, because no two Abu Dhabi MYP schools teach the same physics in the same term.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The two years after MYP 5, where physics becomes Standard or Higher Level with external papers and an Internal Assessment. The jump that catches students is quantitative: DP physics assumes fluent algebra, confident unit work and uncertainty handling that the MYP introduces but does not drill. Hourly rates for Diploma physics support run visibly higher than MYP rates in every published UAE price list.
programmes.countryNote: Abu Dhabi students choosing physics at Higher Level after MYP 5 are the ones who benefit most from MYP money spent early. Nothing about MYP physics is externally examined, so a thin MYP 4 and 5 leaves no trace on a transcript and a large hole in DP 1. Families who spend on criterion B and C skills in MYP 4 typically buy fewer catch-up hours in DP 1, which is the clearest return-on-cost argument this page can make.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The programme that feeds the MYP in continuum schools. Science in the PYP is inquiry-led and not graded on criteria, so there is no physics mark to compare. What carries forward is measurement, recording and the habit of explaining a result rather than stating it, all of which reappear in MYP criterion C.
programmes.countryNote: Several Abu Dhabi schools run the full IB continuum, which means a child can move from PYP 5 into MYP 1 without changing campus. Parents of those children rarely need paid physics support, and we say so plainly rather than selling it. The sensible spend at this stage, if any, is on number fluency, because unit conversion and rearranging a formula are where MYP 3 physics first goes wrong.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-physics-tutor.subjectsIntro: A physics request in the MYP is almost never only physics. Sciences is a single subject group, maths sits underneath every calculation, and the criteria are shared across the group. These are the courses Abu Dhabi families most often book alongside or instead of physics, with what each one actually assesses.

subjects.name: Sciences: the physics strand
subjects.description: Forces and motion, energy transfer, waves, electricity and magnetism, taught through the school's own units. Marks are lost less on recall than on rearranging a relationship, converting a unit and reading a gradient off a graph with its units attached.

subjects.name: Sciences: the chemistry strand
subjects.description: Particle model, bonding, reactions and quantitative work. Shares criteria C and D with physics, so a student who processes data badly in chemistry is almost always processing it badly in physics, and one set of sessions can fix both.

subjects.name: Sciences: the biology strand
subjects.description: Cells, systems, genetics and ecology. Criterion B investigation design is identical in structure to physics, which is why a tutor who teaches variables and controls well in biology transfers straight into a physics practical.

subjects.name: Integrated Sciences
subjects.description: The single course most Abu Dhabi MYP schools run for the first three years. One teacher, one grade, three sciences inside it. A physics problem at this stage usually shows up as a low criterion A on one unit and a solid level on the next.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Standard)
subjects.description: Number, algebra, geometry and statistics. Rearranging a formula, handling indices and plotting a line of best fit are maths skills marked inside physics, so weak standard maths caps a physics level regardless of how well the concept is understood.

subjects.name: Extended Mathematics
subjects.description: The faster route for students heading to Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. Covers algebraic manipulation and functions at a depth that makes DP physics readable. Often the better purchase for a student whose physics problem is arithmetic, not physics.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, evaluating. The criteria mirror the Sciences investigation cycle closely enough that a student who can plan a Design project can usually plan a physics investigation once the vocabulary is swapped.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Investigation, source handling and critical thinking. Shares criterion D ground with Sciences, where students must discuss the impacts of science on people and the environment, and that is the criterion Abu Dhabi students most often leave half-written.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysis, organisation, text production and language use. Relevant to physics because criterion D asks for a written discussion, and a student who cannot structure a paragraph loses science levels for writing reasons.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Separately assessed units combining two subject groups, often Sciences with Individuals and Societies in Abu Dhabi schools. They carry their own criteria and their own grade, and parents are frequently surprised to find a second mark on the report with no obvious lesson behind it.

sections.heading: There is no MYP physics syllabus to buy, and that shapes the first invoice
paragraphs: Parents arriving from a CBSE, Cambridge or American background look for the MYP physics syllabus and cannot find it, because it does not exist. The IB publishes a Sciences subject guide that sets out key concepts, related concepts, global contexts and the four assessment criteria. It does not prescribe a content list. Your child's school writes the units, chooses the contexts, sets the tasks and marks them against the published criteria. Two MYP 4 students at two Abu Dhabi schools can both be studying physics and be studying completely different physics.

That single fact changes what you are buying. A tutor who walks in with a generic Year 9 physics scheme of work will teach content your child's school is not assessing this term, and the criterion levels will not move. A tutor who reads the unit planner first will know that this term's unit is marked on criteria B and C through a controlled investigation on energy transfer, and will spend the hours on variables and graph work instead of on definitions. The difference between those two tutors is not talent. It is forty minutes of reading before the first lesson.

So ask every provider in Abu Dhabi the same three questions before paying. Who reads the unit planner, and is that time charged? What happens if the school changes the task mid-unit? And will I get a written note after each session saying which criterion was worked on? A provider that cannot answer those is selling hours, not physics. sections.heading: What physics support costs in Abu Dhabi, and who published each figure
paragraphs: Three of the six most visible tutoring pages in this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars. So here is the AED picture, assembled from what providers themselves publish and read in October 2026. Treat every row as that provider's claim about its own service, not as a quote from IB Gram, and treat the spread as information about market segmentation rather than about quality.

The budget online band sits at AED 33 to 65 an hour and is populated by university students and generalist tutors. For MYP physics that band can work for a student who needs company while doing homework and cannot work for a student whose criterion B planning is weak, because planning an investigation is a taught skill that a generalist has usually never been marked on. The qualified subject band at AED 150 to 300 is where most MYP Sciences work genuinely lives. Above that, AED 200 to 450 and beyond buys Diploma and A-Level specialism that an MYP 3 student does not need and should not be sold.

In-home visiting rates are the outlier. Bestimate's Dubai table puts home visits at AED 180 to 350 an hour, and independent home tutors advertise AED 200 to 500, with monthly in-home packages seen at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. A meaningful part of that premium is the tutor's travel, which buys your child nothing. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, so that premium does not appear in our model at all; the one-to-one hour runs live online instead, and the money that would have paid for a drive across Khalifa City pays for a Sciences specialist instead of whoever lives nearby.

sections.heading: Where the physics money goes: criteria B and C, not criterion A
paragraphs: MYP Sciences is marked on four criteria, each out of eight, and your child's single 1-7 subject grade is produced by adding those four levels and converting the total through a boundary table the IB publishes in its programme documentation. Ask your MYP coordinator for the version your school applies; it is not something to take from a tutoring page. What matters for spending decisions is that the four criteria are not equally expensive to teach.

Criterion A, knowing and understanding, is the cheap one. It rewards explaining scientific knowledge, applying it to solve problems and analysing information. A student who revises will move on criterion A, and a tutor adds least here. Criterion B, inquiring and designing, and criterion C, processing and evaluating, are where hours disappear and where levels stall for years. These ask a thirteen-year-old to write a testable research question, identify and control variables, justify a method, process raw data into something interpretable, present it correctly and then evaluate the method honestly. None of that is physics knowledge. All of it is taught.

Criterion D, reflecting on the impacts of science, is the one Abu Dhabi students most often leave half-finished, because it is a writing task hiding inside a science course. It asks for the application of science to address a specific problem, the implications of using science, and accurate use of scientific language. A physics student who can calculate the efficiency of a solar panel and cannot discuss the consequences of deploying it loses two levels for reasons that have nothing to do with physics. The table sets out where a Year 9 physics student in this emirate typically loses ground, criterion by criterion, and how many sessions it usually takes to move one level.

sections.heading: Online lessons against a visiting tutor, with Abu Dhabi travel costed honestly
paragraphs: The comparison most Abu Dhabi families are actually making is not between tutors. It is between a visiting tutor and a screen. So compare them on the things that differ: the published rate, what the travel does to a weekday evening, how deep the tutor pool goes for a specific subject, and what is included when the hour ends.

Travel is not a small factor in this emirate. A tutor living on the island and teaching in Khalifa City at five o'clock is committing to the bridge in both directions, which in practice means the family pays for ninety minutes of the tutor's time to receive fifty minutes of physics. Rearrange the session to six o'clock and the traffic improves but the student is tired. Cancel at short notice because a sibling has a fixture and the tutor has still spent the drive. None of those costs appear on an advertised hourly rate, and all of them are real.

Depth of pool is the argument that matters more. MYP physics taught as a discrete MYP 5 course is a narrow specialism. The number of tutors who can confidently teach it and mark against criterion C is small anywhere, and the number who can do that and live within a twenty-minute drive of Al Raha Gardens is smaller still. Online delivery replaces the geographic filter with a subject filter. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, which is precisely why the match can be made on the physics rather than on the postcode.

sections.heading: Equations, units and gradients: the line items that repeat every single term
paragraphs: Across MYP physics requests from this emirate the same three technical failures recur, regardless of school or year group. The first is algebraic rearrangement. A student who understands that resistance relates voltage to current, and who cannot make current the subject of the equation without guessing, will lose criterion A marks on a topic they genuinely understand. The fix is not physics teaching. It is twenty minutes a week of rearrangement practice until it stops being a thinking task.

The second is units, and specifically the conversions that MYP tasks quietly require: centimetres into metres before a density calculation, grams into kilograms before anything involving mass, minutes into seconds before a speed. Students lose levels not for failing to convert but for converting inconsistently inside the same calculation, which produces an answer that is numerically wrong and dimensionally meaningless. A tutor who insists on units written at every line of working, every time, removes a whole class of lost marks without teaching any new content.

The third is graph work, which is where criterion C is won and lost. Plotting points is rarely the problem. The problems are choosing a scale that uses the paper, drawing a line of best fit rather than joining the dots, calculating a gradient from two points on the line rather than two data points, and then stating what the gradient physically means with its units attached. A gradient of 9.8 is not an answer; 9.8 metres per second squared, interpreted as the acceleration of free fall, is. That distinction is worth two criterion C levels and takes about three sessions to make automatic.

None of these three are advanced physics. They are the mechanical skills that MYP tasks assume and MYP lessons rarely have time to drill. If a household has budget for one term of physics support and nothing more, spending it on rearrangement, units and gradients will return more criterion levels than spending it on the content of the current unit.

sections.heading: The Abu Dhabi evening, and the hour you are actually buying
paragraphs: An Abu Dhabi weekday leaves a narrow window for serious physics. School buses on the island routes return students between half past two and half past three; buses serving Khalifa City, Al Raha and the mainland communities regularly land later. Add a prayer time, a sibling's activity and a meal, and the first realistic start for focused work is somewhere between four and six o'clock depending on which community you live in. The window closes earlier than parents expect, because a tired fourteen-year-old does not plan an investigation well at eight in the evening.

This is where online delivery stops being a compromise and starts being the reason the session happens at all. A fifty-minute slot at five o'clock from a bedroom desk is attainable four weeks out of four. The same slot with a tutor driving in from the island is attainable until the first accident on the bridge. Fixed weekly timing also matters more than most families realise: a session at an unpredictable hour becomes the thing that gets cancelled, and cancelled sessions are how a term of planned criterion work turns into four random hours.

Ramadan reorganises everything, and it is worth planning for rather than pausing through. School days shorten, energy in the afternoon drops, and post-iftar evenings are genuinely productive for many students. Sessions can be moved to a late slot for the month and moved back afterwards. Summer is the opposite case: with no school deadlines, it is the only period in the year when criterion B and C skills can be taught slowly, out of context, without a task breathing down the student's neck. Families who buy their investigation clinic in July rather than in February get noticeably more out of the same hours.

sections.heading: Who may legally charge you for private physics lessons in this emirate
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and the position is clearer than most tutoring pages admit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and it is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service page, 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system. Anyone offering private tutoring without that permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no amount is quoted here or anywhere else on this site.

Eligibility is broad. Teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen can all apply. That breadth is why the AED 33 to 65 band exists: a university student with a permit is operating entirely legally at that price. It is also why asking about the permit tells you about legality, not about teaching quality. Both questions need asking separately.

Abu Dhabi adds a condition worth knowing. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported as prohibiting teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's own code of conduct has been reported as barring the same arrangement. Verify the current wording against ADEK's published policy before relying on it, but treat the principle as settled: your child's own Sciences teacher is not the right person to hire privately, however convenient it looks. No part of our model depends on that arrangement.

sections.heading: Five years of MYP Sciences, and the terms when physics money is worth spending
paragraphs: Spending the same amount in different years produces very different returns. In MYP 1 and 2, Sciences is integrated, the units are short and the criteria are being introduced rather than enforced. Paid physics support here is usually premature. The exception is a student who cannot handle number work, because every subsequent physics problem will be an arithmetic problem wearing a physics costume, and that is worth fixing at eleven rather than at fifteen.

MYP 3 is where the first honest signal arrives. Criterion levels start separating, and a pattern of 5, 3, 3, 4 across the four criteria tells you something specific: knowledge is adequate, investigation and data work are not. A term of targeted criterion B and C support at this point costs the same as a term of general science help and does considerably more, because the skill it builds is used in every Sciences unit for the next three years and again throughout the Diploma.

MYP 4 and 5 are the expensive years, and the ones where families most often overpay for the wrong thing. Here Sciences may split into discrete physics, tasks get longer, and MYP 5 adds the Personal Project and, in some Abu Dhabi schools, on-screen eAssessment. The temptation is to buy an intensive block two weeks before a task. The arithmetic argues against it: three sessions of polish on top of weak criterion C will shift one level, while twelve weekly sessions spread across a term will usually shift two or three and leave the student able to do it unaided. If the budget is one term, buy the term early rather than buying a panic fortnight late.

process.title: Send the three documents
process.description: Email the current Sciences unit planner, the most recent marked task with the teacher's comments, and the latest report card showing criterion levels. Those three tell a tutor more in ten minutes than a phone call does in an hour, and they determine whether the sessions aim at criterion A or at criteria B and C.

process.title: Trial lesson at no charge
process.description: One fifty-minute session with an MYP Sciences specialist, at no charge, one per family, with no card details taken and nothing to cancel afterwards. The tutor works on a real task from your school's current unit, not a demonstration topic, so what you see is what the paid sessions look like.

process.title: Agree the target and the price in writing
process.description: Before any payment you receive which criterion the term is aimed at, how many sessions, the rate per session in AED, whether preparation time is charged, and the reschedule terms. Anything a provider will not put in writing is something you will argue about in week six.

process.title: Run the weekly cycle
process.description: Teach, set a task, mark it against the published criterion rubric, teach into the result. A short written note after each session records which criterion strand was worked on and what the student should practise before the next one, so a parent can follow the work without being a physics teacher.

process.title: Review at six weeks on evidence
process.description: Compare marked tasks from week one and week six, strand by strand, and decide whether to continue, change tutor or stop. If the evidence shows no movement we say so and look at why, which is sometimes a tutoring problem and sometimes a timetable problem.

whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is attributed to the provider or rate table that published it, with the month it was read. For a narrow specialism like discrete MYP 5 physics that difference is the difference between a specialist and whoever was available.

whyPoints.title: The school's own unit, not a generic scheme
whyPoints.description: The MYP prescribes no physics content, so a tutor who ignores your school's unit planner teaches the wrong material. Ours read the planner, the task sheet and the rubric before the first lesson, and the sessions follow the sequence your child's teacher is actually assessing.

whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, question, review and give feedback on the student's own work. They do not supply submissions, and they do not touch the wording of a Personal Project report or an investigation write-up. That boundary is stated to the student in the first session, because it protects them and nobody else benefits from blurring it.

whyPoints.description: Criterion levels, a marked task from week one against a marked task from week six, and a one-paragraph note after each session. No dashboards, no scores we invented. A parent with no physics background can see which strand moved and which did not.

whyPoints.description: If no MYP Sciences specialist is free in your preferred slot we tell you the earliest one that is, rather than filling the hour with a generalist. For discrete MYP 5 physics that sometimes means waiting a week, and we would rather say so than sell the wrong tutor.

faqs.question: What does an MYP Sciences tutor charge per hour for physics in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.answer: Published UAE rates read in October 2026 put budget online tutoring at AED 33 to 65 an hour, qualified subject tutors at AED 150 to 300, exam-level specialists at AED 200 to 450 or more, and premium named tutors as high as AED 650. MYP physics generally sits in the AED 150 to 300 band, below Diploma physics, because the assessment is internally set coursework rather than external papers. Those figures are the providers' own published claims, not an IB Gram price list. For our own pricing, ask on the consultation; the bands above are here so you can judge any quote you receive against the market.

faqs.question: Is there an MYP physics syllabus I can buy for my child?
faqs.answer: No, and this surprises most families. The IB publishes a Sciences subject guide covering key concepts, related concepts, global contexts and the four assessment criteria, but it prescribes no content list. Your child's Abu Dhabi school writes its own units, chooses its own contexts and sets its own tasks. That is why a tutor needs your school's unit planner rather than a textbook: two MYP 4 students at two schools in the same emirate can be studying genuinely different physics in the same term. Ask your MYP coordinator for the current planner, and ask any prospective tutor whether they will read it.

faqs.question: My son is in MYP 3 and his report says Sciences, not physics. Why?
faqs.answer: Because in the MYP, Sciences is one subject group rather than three subjects. Most Abu Dhabi schools teach it as an integrated course in MYP 1 to 3, so physics content appears as units on forces, energy or electricity alongside chemistry and biology units, all marked against the same four criteria and reported as a single Sciences grade. From MYP 4 many schools offer discrete physics. If you want to know how the physics units specifically went, ask for the criterion levels from each unit rather than the overall grade, which averages the lot and hides exactly what you are looking for.

faqs.question: How many hours does a criterion B investigation task usually take to teach?
faqs.answer: Moving one level on criterion B generally takes four to eight sessions, which is more than most parents expect and less than the whole term. The reason is that inquiring and designing is a composite skill: writing a testable question, identifying and controlling variables, justifying a range and a number of repeats, and planning something that could actually be carried out. A student rarely fails all four at once, so the first session is diagnostic. Criterion C, processing and evaluating, runs on a similar timescale. Criterion A moves faster, in two to four sessions, because revision does much of the work.

faqs.question: Why would a first invoice include preparation time?
faqs.answer: Because a competent first lesson requires reading. The unit planner takes twenty to forty minutes, the task sheet and criterion rubric fifteen to thirty, the last marked task twenty to thirty, and the report card around fifteen. Providers handle that cost in different ways: some absorb it into the hourly rate, some bill it separately and openly, and some skip it entirely and then teach material your school is not assessing. None of those is dishonest except the last. Ask which model you are buying before you pay, and get the answer in writing with the rest of the terms.

faqs.question: Is a visiting physics tutor in Abu Dhabi worth the extra AED per hour?
faqs.answer: The published premium for in-home tutoring in this market runs from AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for qualified online work, and a real share of that gap is travel. An island-based tutor teaching in Khalifa City at five o'clock spends forty to eighty minutes on the road each way. Your child receives none of that time. The bigger cost is the narrowing of the pool: insisting on a short drive means choosing from tutors who live nearby rather than tutors who teach MYP Sciences well. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi for exactly that reason.

faqs.question: Does my child need a laboratory to do MYP physics investigations properly?
faqs.answer: For the school's assessed practical work, no, because that happens in the school laboratory with the subject teacher. What a tutor works on is everything around the apparatus: the research question, the variables, the method, the data table, the graph and the evaluation. Those are paper and screen tasks, and they are where the criterion levels are won. Where home practicals are genuinely useful, physics is unusually generous: a ruler, a stopwatch, a phone sensor app and a kitchen scale cover motion, period and density work convincingly enough to practise the full inquiry cycle.

faqs.question: How do online physics lessons handle practical data and graph work?
faqs.answer: The student photographs or scans the lab book and sends it before the session, and it goes on the shared screen where the tutor annotates it live. Data gets typed into a spreadsheet and replotted during the lesson, so a student watches a badly scaled axis become a usable graph rather than being told about it. Gradients are calculated on the screen with units attached at every step. In practice this is closer to how physics is actually done than a tutor reading over a shoulder at a kitchen table, because the working is visible to both people at once and is saved afterwards.

faqs.question: What does physics help cost if we only want support before one end-of-unit test?
faqs.answer: A pre-task block is usually three or four sessions in the fortnight before the assessment, so at market rates for a qualified subject tutor you are looking at the equivalent of three to four hours rather than a term. It is the most expensive way to buy criterion levels, because polish can only improve what already exists. It works well for a student whose understanding is sound and whose technique under time pressure is not. It will not build mechanics from nothing in two weeks, and any provider suggesting otherwise is selling you something that does not exist.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover physics, chemistry and biology inside MYP Sciences?
faqs.answer: In MYP 1 to 3, usually yes, and often that is the better arrangement. Integrated Sciences is marked against four criteria that are identical across the three strands, so a tutor who teaches investigation design and data processing well improves all three at once. From MYP 4, where schools offer discrete courses, the content depth starts to matter and a physics specialist pulls ahead for physics. A practical rule: buy one tutor for criteria B and C across Sciences, and buy subject depth separately once your child is sitting a discrete physics course.

faqs.question: Does a private physics tutor in Abu Dhabi need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Teachers, public and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged fifteen to eighteen can all apply. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so treat any specific amount you read elsewhere with suspicion. Ask a prospective tutor directly whether they hold one.

faqs.question: My daughter is strong at maths but weak at physics. Will tutoring fix that?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and faster than the reverse case, because the harder half is already in place. A student who is fluent in algebra and poor at physics is typically losing marks on modelling rather than on calculation: choosing which relationship applies, deciding what the question is actually asking, and interpreting an answer physically. Those are teachable in a handful of sessions. The reverse profile, confident with concepts and shaky with rearrangement, takes longer, because every physics problem then carries an arithmetic risk. Send a marked task and the diagnosis takes one session rather than guesswork.

faqs.question: Should we wait until MYP 5 before paying for physics support?
faqs.answer: Waiting is usually the more expensive choice. MYP 3 is where criterion levels first separate clearly, and a pattern like 5, 3, 3, 4 tells you knowledge is fine and investigation work is not. Fixing that at thirteen costs the same per hour as fixing it at fifteen and buys three more years of use, because criteria B and C reappear in every Sciences unit and again throughout the Diploma. MYP 5 is also the busiest year, with the Personal Project and on-screen components in some Abu Dhabi schools competing for the same evenings. Early is cheaper here.

faqs.question: Do quoted MYP physics tutoring rates in Abu Dhabi include VAT?
faqs.answer: Treat it as unresolved until the provider states it. We do not publish a position on the UAE VAT treatment of tuition fees, because that requires a Federal Tax Authority citation we are not going to approximate. What you should insist on is simpler: ask whether the AED figure you have been quoted is the amount that will be charged, and get that confirmed in writing alongside the reschedule terms and the cancellation window. A quote that becomes a different number on the invoice is a commercial problem regardless of how the tax question is answered.

faqs.question: How do we fit physics sessions around the Abu Dhabi school run and Ramadan?
faqs.answer: School buses on the island routes typically return students between half past two and half past three, while Khalifa City, Al Raha and mainland runs land later, so realistic start times range from four o'clock to six depending on your community. A fixed weekly slot survives better than a flexible one. During Ramadan, shorter school days and low afternoon energy make post-iftar sessions genuinely productive, and the slot can move for the month and move back afterwards. Summer is the best window for criterion B and C work, because the skills can be taught without a task deadline pressing.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come to our villa in Abu Dhabi for physics lessons?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Abu Dhabi, and home visits are a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one to one, live over video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. For physics specifically that is an advantage rather than a concession: the lab book is annotated on a shared screen, data is replotted live, and the match is made on who teaches MYP Sciences criterion C well rather than on who lives within a short drive of your community. Anyone promising a tutor at an Abu Dhabi address is describing a different service.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-physics-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the numbers, then with one marked task
abu-dhabi/ib-myp-physics-tutor.closingBody: If you have read this far you already know more about MYP physics pricing in this emirate than most of the pages ranking above it. The next step is small: send the current Sciences unit planner, the last marked task with the teacher's comments, and the report card showing criterion levels. A specialist will read the three, tell you in plain language which criterion is actually costing your child levels, and run one fifty-minute session at no charge on a real task from your school's own unit. After that you will have a written note, a quoted rate in AED and a decision to make, rather than a sales conversation.
