sections.heading: The Personal Project, and keeping authorship visible
paragraphs: In MYP 5 the Personal Project becomes the dominant piece of work and the most delicate one to buy help with. It is supervised inside the school, assessed against its own criteria, and judged substantially on the process journal rather than on the finished outcome. Families often engage a tutor at the point where the journal has stalled, which is also the point where the temptation to contribute material is highest. The honest position is narrow and worth stating before any session: a tutor may ask questions, explain what a criterion rewards, and comment on the student's own entries. A tutor may not supply content, restructure the journal, or contribute any part of the report.

A tutor can be genuinely useful inside those limits. Most stalled projects fail on scope rather than on effort: the goal is too broad to evidence, or the success criteria were written so vaguely that nothing can be measured against them. Questioning a goal until the student narrows it themselves is legitimate supervision support and usually unblocks the project in one session. Likewise, asking what the journal entry for last week actually shows prompts the student to document a process they did complete but never recorded.

Keep authorship visible while you are at it. Dated entries in the student's own account, written as they happen rather than reconstructed in the final fortnight, are the clearest evidence of authorship if a question is ever raised, and they are also the thing the criteria reward. IB academic-honesty rules make a breach here a serious matter for the student rather than a service complaint about the tutor, which is why the boundary is stated at the first session and not negotiated later.

sections.heading: MYP 5 to the Diploma: what the evidence actually says about readiness
paragraphs: The decision at the end of MYP 5 is usually made on the overall grades, which is the least informative data available. A grade of 6 in MYP Sciences tells you the sum of four levels; it does not tell you whether the student can design an investigation, which is what a Diploma internal assessment will ask them to do unaided across a longer timescale. The criterion profile is the useful evidence, and most Abu Dhabi families have had it on a report card for two years without being told what it predicts.

The patterns are reasonably stable. Strong knowing and understanding with weak investigating predicts a comfortable first Diploma year and a difficult internal assessment season in the second. Strong communicating in Mathematics predicts a reasonable fit with Analysis and Approaches, while strength in applying mathematics in real-life contexts points towards Applications and Interpretation. Low levels on the reflection criteria predict trouble in Theory of Knowledge and in the Extended Essay, both of which are reflective pieces of work in a way nothing in MYP 1 to 3 prepares students for.

None of this is deterministic, and the point of surfacing it in MYP 5 is that there is still a year in which to close a gap. A student who wants Higher Level sciences and sits at 3 on inquiring and designing has a specific, nameable, fixable problem and twelve months in which to fix it. The same student discovering this in the second Diploma year has an expensive problem instead. That is the strongest argument for MYP tutoring over waiting: the gaps are cheaper to close before the stakes arrive.

sections.heading: Approaches to learning, interdisciplinary units and service as action
paragraphs: Three parts of the MYP sit outside the subject grid and cause a disproportionate amount of family confusion. Approaches to learning are the skills clusters the programme teaches explicitly: thinking, research, communication, social and self-management skills. They are not separately graded in most schools, but they are the mechanism through which the investigation and reflection criteria are supposed to be taught, and a student weak on self-management will present as weak on several criteria at once.

Interdisciplinary units are assessed against their own criteria and reported separately in many Abu Dhabi schools, which is why a parent occasionally finds an extra grade on the report with no obvious subject attached. These units reward the connection between two disciplines rather than performance in either, so a student who is strong in both contributing subjects can still land on a 4. Preparation is specific: practise stating what one subject explains that the other cannot, which is the move the criteria are looking for.

Service as action is a requirement rather than a graded subject, documented by the student and reviewed by the school. A tutor has no legitimate role in it beyond helping a student write a clear reflection on something they actually did. It is worth mentioning here only because families sometimes assume it carries marks, deprioritise it, and then face a documentation scramble in MYP 5 alongside the Personal Project. Keeping a rolling record through the year costs an hour a term and removes that problem entirely.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies alongside the MYP
paragraphs: Every private school in the UAE teaches Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies alongside its licensed curriculum. Federal rules are explicit that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond those subjects while adhering to the Ministry's general regulations, so an MYP student in Abu Dhabi carries them in addition to the eight MYP subject groups. Families moving from overseas are regularly surprised by this in the first term, and it is a real workload factor when deciding where the weekly tutoring hour goes.

The detailed published requirements worth reading are KHDA's, which apply to Dubai schools and set out the position clearly enough to be informative anywhere in the country. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and social studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, and schools are advised that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes.

For an Abu Dhabi family the practical points are these. Check which stream your child is registered in, because the Arab and non-Arab routes are different subjects with different expectations, and a tutor booked for the wrong one will teach material your child is not assessed on. Use of different or additional content for these subjects without prior Ministry permission is not permitted, so a tutor works with the school's material rather than importing their own scheme. And confirm the position with your own school and with ADEK rather than assuming Dubai's published detail applies identically in this emirate.

process.title: Send the report card and two marked tasks
process.description: The report card gives the criterion profile and the marked tasks give the reason behind it. Include the task-specific clarifications if your child still has them. Those three documents let a tutor name a target criterion in the first session instead of spending a fortnight finding one.

process.title: We match on the criterion, not the subject
process.description: An MYP Sciences brief about inquiring and designing is a different job from one about knowing and understanding, and we match accordingly. If no tutor covers the exact combination you need, you are told at first contact rather than after a trial lesson.

process.title: A free trial lesson, one per student
process.description: One lesson at no charge, no card required. Your child attempts a task unaided while the tutor watches, which is how the real stopping point gets found. You should finish the hour with a named target criterion and a stated reason for it.

process.title: Fix the slot and the between-session task
process.description: A weekly time in Gulf Standard Time around the school run, plus a short task each week assessing the same criterion. The between-session task is what produces something to mark before the school's next formal assessment arrives, which is usually weeks away.

process.title: Review in week seven or eight
process.description: Look at the lost-level log, the tutor-marked tasks and the first school-marked task on the target criterion. Decide to continue, name the next criterion, change tutor or stop. Agree this date at the start, while it is still an easy thing to agree to.

whyPoints.title: Criterion-referenced, not percentage-referenced
whyPoints.description: Tutors work in the descriptors your child's school marks with, and name a target criterion rather than a target grade. A criterion is a thing work can shift; a grade is the arithmetic that follows four of them being shifted.

whyPoints.title: A record that survives the term
whyPoints.description: Dated session notes, a lost-level log sorted by cause, tutor-marked tasks with strand-level comments, and dated drafts in your child's own account. Four artefacts, reviewed in week eight, which is what makes a renewal decision evidence-based.

whyPoints.title: Matched on who has taught the criterion
whyPoints.description: Online delivery means your child works with somebody who has taught that subject group in the Middle Years Programme, rather than with the nearest available tutor who mostly teaches the Diploma and will treat an MYP report as a percentage sheet.

whyPoints.title: Honest about the Personal Project boundary
whyPoints.description: A tutor asks questions, explains what a criterion rewards and comments on the student's own journal entries. No content is supplied and no part of the report is contributed. The boundary is stated before the first session rather than discovered during one.

whyPoints.title: Timing explained rather than promised around
whyPoints.description: A criterion level moves when a task assessing it is next marked, which can be weeks away. We say that at the start, because the alternative is a promise about grade movement that the school's assessment calendar does not permit.

whyPoints.title: No claimed approvals, because none are held
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or partnership from ADEK, KHDA, the Ministry of Education or the IB, and occupies no UAE office. Regulators and federal subject rules are explained here because they affect your planning, not because any of them endorses us.

faqs.question: Why does my child's MYP report show letters instead of percentages?
faqs.answer: Because the Middle Years Programme assesses against published criteria rather than against a fixed body of examinable content. Each subject has four criteria, each scored from 0 to 8 by best fit against descriptors, and a given task is marked only against the criteria it was designed to assess. A percentage would average competences that are not comparable. The four levels are summed and converted to a grade from 1 to 7 using boundaries published in each subject guide, and your child's MYP coordinator can give you the exact conversion table the school applies.

faqs.question: What do criteria A, B, C and D mean in MYP Sciences?
faqs.answer: In Sciences they are knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Each is scored from 0 to 8 on its own descriptor. The letters are not transferable between subject groups: criterion A in Design is inquiring and analysing and criterion A in Language Acquisition is listening, so comparing letters across subjects on a report card compares unlike things. Most lost levels in Sciences sit in the two middle criteria, which reward a documented investigation process rather than knowing the right answer quickly.

faqs.question: My child has a 5 in MYP Mathematics. What does that actually mean?
faqs.answer: It means the sum of four criterion levels fell into the band the subject guide maps to a 5, and on its own it tells you very little. Two children can both hold a 5 with opposite profiles: balanced levels around 5 across all four criteria, or two 7s alongside two 3s. Those two children need completely different work. Ask for the four underlying levels, which the school records, and look at investigating patterns and communicating in particular. Strong arithmetic students very often sit low on both while holding a high level on knowing and understanding.

faqs.question: How far can an MYP tutor go on the Personal Project before it stops being my child's work?
faqs.answer: Within clear limits, yes. A tutor may ask questions about the goal and the success criteria, explain what each criterion rewards, and comment on journal entries the student has written themselves. A tutor may not supply content, restructure the journal or contribute any part of the report. Most stalled projects fail on scope rather than effort, and questioning a goal until the student narrows it themselves usually unblocks it in one session. Keep dated journal entries in your child's own account: the criteria reward them and they evidence authorship if a question is raised.

faqs.question: Which MYP year is the right one to start tutoring in?
faqs.answer: It depends on what the report shows rather than on the year. MYP 1 and 2 requests are usually about writing structure and the transition out of inquiry-led primary work into criterion-marked tasks with deadlines. MYP 3 is the year to act if a process criterion has been sitting at 3 or 4 for two terms, because the habit is still cheap to change. MYP 4 and 5 bring the Personal Project and the route decision, so the brief widens. The expensive version is waiting until the Diploma, when the same gap costs far more to close.

faqs.question: How is MYP eAssessment different from a school exam?
faqs.answer: Where a school enters students for it, MYP eAssessment is externally set and marked, taken on screen, and designed to assess the criteria rather than recall of a syllabus. Some subjects use ePortfolios of coursework instead of an on-screen examination. Not every school enters its students, so the first thing to establish is whether yours does and in which subjects, because it changes the final-year brief considerably. Ask the MYP coordinator directly; it is not something a tutor should assume from the school's curriculum listing.

faqs.question: Is the MYP good preparation for the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: For the reflective and investigative work, yes, and better than most alternatives. MYP students arrive in the Diploma already used to criterion-referenced marking, documented investigations and reflective writing, which are the three things that cause most trouble for students joining from other systems. The weaker side is examination technique under time pressure, since MYP assessment is largely task-based. The criterion profile is the honest predictor: strong knowing and understanding with weak investigating tends to produce a comfortable first year and a difficult internal assessment season in the second.

faqs.question: How do I know whether my child is ready for Higher Level after MYP 5?
faqs.answer: Look at the criterion profile rather than the grade. For Higher Level sciences you want consistent high levels on processing and evaluating as well as on knowing and understanding; a 3 or 4 on inquiring and designing predicts a hard internal assessment year regardless of the overall grade. For Analysis and Approaches, strong communicating and investigating patterns matter more than arithmetic speed. The useful thing about doing this in MYP 5 is that a nameable gap still has twelve months in which to close, which it will not have later.

faqs.question: What should an MYP tutor be able to show me after a month?
faqs.answer: Four things. Dated session notes saying what each lesson addressed. A log of lost levels sorted by cause rather than by topic. At least two short tasks the tutor has set and marked against the published descriptors, with comments at strand level. And a written statement of the target criterion with the reason for choosing it. What you should not expect inside a month is a changed report grade, because a criterion level only moves when the school next marks a task assessing it.

faqs.question: Does MYP Mathematics prepare a student for Analysis and Approaches?
faqs.answer: The extended route does, if the right criteria are strong. Analysis and Approaches rewards algebraic manipulation, written justification and proof, and includes a paper sat without a calculator. The MYP criteria that predict comfort there are communicating, which marks whether reasoning is presented so a reader can follow it, and investigating patterns, which requires generalising and justifying. A student who reliably gets correct answers without writing the steps will find the transition harder than their grade suggests, and that is a fixable habit rather than a limit.

faqs.question: What are approaches to learning skills, and can a tutor teach them?
faqs.answer: They are the skill clusters the programme teaches explicitly: thinking, research, communication, social and self-management skills. Most schools do not grade them separately, but they are the mechanism through which the investigation and reflection criteria are meant to be taught. A tutor can absolutely work on them, and self-management is often the highest-value target: a student who plans a task and checks it against each descriptor strand before submitting gains levels across several subjects at once without learning new content.

faqs.question: Do MYP students in Abu Dhabi have to study Arabic as well?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private schools in the UAE teach Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies alongside their licensed curriculum, under federal rules that leave the rest of the curriculum to the school. So an MYP student carries these in addition to the eight MYP subject groups. Published requirements in Dubai also set out that Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and social studies run in separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs. Check with your own school and with ADEK which stream your child sits in, because the two routes are genuinely different subjects.

faqs.question: What is an interdisciplinary unit and why is it graded separately?
faqs.answer: It is a unit taught across two or more subjects and assessed against its own criteria, usually around evaluating, synthesising and reflecting, which is why many Abu Dhabi schools report a separate grade for it. Students strong in both contributing subjects still land on a 4 fairly often, because the task rewards the connection between disciplines rather than performance in either. Preparation is specific and quick: practise stating what one subject explains that the other cannot, which is the move the criteria are built to reward.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does an MYP student actually need?
faqs.answer: One, in most cases, with a short task between sessions. The limiting factor in the Middle Years Programme is not teaching time but assessment opportunity: a criterion level changes when a task assessing it is next marked, so buying three hours a week rarely moves a report faster than buying one. Two sessions a week make sense in a specific case, where a student is carrying a process problem in two different subject groups and the two briefs genuinely do not overlap. Otherwise the second hour is better spent next term.

faqs.question: Are MYP sessions held at our home in Abu Dhabi or online?
faqs.answer: Online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. For Middle Years work that is a practical advantage rather than a limitation, because the match can be made on who has actually taught that subject group and criterion rather than on who is willing to drive to Khalifa City or Al Reem Island at 17:00. Sessions run in Gulf Standard Time and are fixed around your school run.

abu-dhabi/ib-myp-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the report card, not the subject
abu-dhabi/ib-myp-tutor.closingBody: Send the latest MYP report, two recent marked tasks and their task-specific clarifications. Those three documents are enough to name the criterion that is costing your child levels, which is a far more useful starting point than the subject label. Then take the free trial lesson and judge it on whether you finish the hour with a target criterion and a reason. Sessions are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, with no in-home visits anywhere in the UAE, and a written review in week eight where continuing, changing or stopping is an honest choice.
